articles.title: ‘Doctor Who’: Multiple BBC Studios Labels Likely To Apply For Tender
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Doctor Who’: Multiple BBC Studios Labels Likely To Apply For Tender Callum Scott Howells & Gabrielle Creevy Leading Adaptation Of Vanessa Savage Thriller ‘The Night They Vanished’ For BBC Studios & Channel 4 BBC Studios Scripted Boss Spotlights Strategy Behind Indie & Talent Deals: “We’re Not Going To Spend Millions Buying A Production Company” View All September 30, 2026 2:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Doctor Who' BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon EXCLUSIVE: At least one BBC Studios indie will be throwing its hat in the ring to become the next producer of Doctor Who , with scripted boss Jamie Hall telling Deadline he “firmly believes” the entire BBC group should “reap the rewards” of the iconic sci-fi series. Hall said “we’ve probably got one, potentially two companies” going for the multi-million pound tender, which if successful would bring the show back in house following two seasons made by Sony-owned Bad Wolf, starring Ncuti Gatwa. His comments followed BBC Studios CEO Tom Fussell recently saying BBC Studios would be applying “with gusto.” Related Stories News BBC Studios Scripted Boss Spotlights Strategy Behind Indie & Talent Deals: "We're Not Going To Spend Millions Buying A Production Company" News Graham Norton Says It's Getting Harder To Launch Talk Shows: "I Feel Like We Might End Up Being The Last Chat Show On Planet Earth" Hall wouldn’t reveal the names of the indies but said he would “100%” be happy for more than one to enter the race. Watch on Deadline BBC Studios runs an in-house drama label, which made Doctor Who before Bad Wolf, while it also owns several scripted indies outright including Baby Reindeer maker Clerkenwell Films, Happy Valley producer Lookout Point and Sherwood indie House Productions. While he hasn’t seen his labels’ proposals, Hall said he has been “very open” and honest with those keen to go for the tender because the process is “quite an onerous undertaking and costs quite a bit of money.” “I have to make sure that it doesn’t become a distraction from the day job,” he added. If two BBC Studios labels enter, they will likely join Line of Duty producer World Productions, whose boss Simon Heath has previously indicated his ITV Studios-owned outfit is interested. More thoughts from producers can be found in our future Doctor Who analysis from over the summer. Published a fortnight ago, the tender calls for a “relevant, surprising, brave and inspiring” new vision for the show that should premiere in 2028-29. Notably, it said it is happy for indies to pitch a series using “episodic writers” rather than a “showrunner model,” which would do away with how Doctor Who has been made in recent years. After several years with Bad Wolf and after the termination of the just-ended Disney+ co-pro deal , Hall was adamant that Doctor Who “should sit within the BBC and the whole group should reap the rewards of it.” Questioned on what he would want to see from a revamped Doctor Who, Hall harked back to the days when Matt Smith and David Tennant were playing the Doctor. “It feels to me that there is an opportunity to get back to what the core offering was in that time,” he added. “It will be off screen for two or three years and that gives the audience a great chance to have a break then rediscover, while also bringing a new audience.” CA Gov Candidate Steve Hilton On Federal Tax Credits, ParaBros Merger, More Red Carpet Premiere Photo Gallery, Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson, Review BBC Studios Scripted Boss Jamie Hall On Talent Deal Strategy Paramount Streaming Boss Cindy Holland Exiting Ahead Of WBD Merger Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Netflix Renews Indian Reality Breakout ‘Lock Upp’ For Second Season
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Fremantle International Commercial Strategy VP Jill Kellie Exits After Four Years ‘Joseph’s Machines’, ‘Triple Charm’ & ‘What’s Up Moms’ Among Volt Factor Shows Rolling Out On Future Today Channels Hearst Networks UK Buys ‘American Chopper’ Revival Series ‘Orange County Choppers Original’ View All September 30, 2026 2:32am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Lock Upp' Netflix Netflix is returning the inmates to the Lock Upp jail. A second season of the ‘captive reality’ series, whose full title is Lock Upp: Sach Yaa Sazaa has been ordered following Season 1’s breakout summer, where it placed number one of Netflix’s TV shows list within two days of the premiere and remained in the top ten for seven straight weeks. The response to the show was so strong that five weekly episodes were expanded to six to satisfy demand, Netflix has said. It eventually amassed 50 million hours viewed in a month. Related Stories Books Everything We Know About Netflix's 'Icebreaker' Adaptation So Far News Netflix Scores Ratings Hit With 'Wonka's The Golden Ticket' The show sees Indian celebrities thrown together in a jail cell, where they compete in challenges. What broke through with audiences was some of the more divisive characters discussing their public perception and confronting narratives that have surrounded them. Watch on Deadline Netflix said Season 2 “build on that world, bringing audiences back inside the jail for another chapter where personalities collide, dynamics shift, and every secret has the potential to change the game.” Riteish Deshmukh and Farah Khan return as hosts, with Balaji Telefilms producing. Show creator Ekta Kapoor is producing alongside Shobha Kapoor and Manisha Sharma, with Malaya Pradhan the showrunner. “ Lock Upp: Sach Yaa Sazaa became appointment viewing overnight,” said Monika Shergill, VP of Content at Netflix India. “Viewers invested, debated, and kept coming back. It captured the zeitgeist — not just as entertainment, but also as a space where celebrities talked about topics they rarely do, owned their choices and confronted past trauma. “Ekta’s bold homegrown idea and the scaled adaptation on Netflix led to entertainment maxxing. Season 2 will be about recreating the same Netflix effect with many new surprises for our audiences.” Ekta Kapoor, Jjoint Managing Director at Balaji, added: “ Lock Upp: Sach Ya Sazaa on Netflix went far beyond what we imagined. The conversations, the inmates, and their most memorable moments continued to live with audiences even after the finale. That’s what makes the return of Lock Upp so exciting. “The next season will take audiences back into a world they know, but with an entirely new set of stories, personalities, and surprises. And Farah and Riteish will continue to helm the Lock Upp as the formidable jailer duo, bringing their own energy, unpredictability, and dynamic to the next chapter.” Lock Upp originally launched on ALTBalaji and MX Player in 2022, but was rebooted for Netflix. articles.title: European Film Academy To Honor Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz & Sandra den Hamer With New Community Award
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie European Film Academy To Honor Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz & Sandra den Hamer With New Community Award Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea Fund Gets Behind Projects From Tarzan & Arab Nasser, Sofia Alaoui & Amanda Nell Eu Lauren Cohan & Jake Epstein To Co-Star In Eric Stoltz-Directed Rom-Com ‘Both Sides Now’ View All September 30, 2026 3:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz, Sandra den Hamer Getty Images The European Film Academy has named Beki Probst , Marin Karmitz and Sandra den Hamer as the first recipients of its new Community Award for an Outstanding Contribution to European Film Culture. The award, paying tribute to “a decisive and continuous contribution over many years to the development and expansion of European film culture”, will be presented during the European Film Awards weekend in Athens in January 2027. The trio will be presented with the award on January 15, on the eve of the main ceremony at the traditional Welcome Night gala dinner, taking place this edition at the Acropolis Museum housing some 4,000 artefacts dating as far back as 1,200 BCE. Related Stories News Netflix Renews Indian Reality Breakout 'Lock Upp' For Second Season News 'Doctor Who': Multiple BBC Studios Labels Likely To Apply For Tender Probst is best known internationally as the founder of the Berlinale’s European Film Market, having entered the cinema world as the founder with her Swiss husband of the Queenie Cinemas in Berne in the 1960s, which grew into a successful chain of arthouse cinemas still existing today. Watch on Deadline Born into a Sephardic Jewish family in Istanbul, Probst studied Law and Journalism and worked briefly as a film journalist. From 1981 to 1988, she was the Berlinale delegate for Turkey and Greece and after initiating Locarno’s industry program, she was asked by Berlinale Director Moritz de Hadeln to start the European Film Market in 1988 in its current form. Under her management, which continued into 2014, the EFM became one of the largest and most important international film market in Europe. She has previously been feted with the Berlinale Camera, the Prix du cinéma Suisse , the French Chevalier des Arts et des Lettres and the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany. Karmitz is known as the founder of France’s independent exhibitor, producer, film financier and sales agent mk2 film. Born in Romania in 1938, Karmitz arrived in France as a refugee with his family in 1947. After studies at the IDHEC film school in Paris, he worked as assistant director to the filmmakers Jean-Luc Godard, Agnès Varda, Jacques Rozier, Yannick Bellon and Pierre Kast. before directing his first short film, Nuit Noir, Calcutta, based on a screenplay by Marguerite Duras, in 1964. In 1965, he worked with Samuel Beckett on the adaptation of Comédie . In the same year, the feature was selected to open the Venice International Film Festival and shocked audiences with its avant-garde material. He launched mk2 Productions in 1967 and made his feature-length directorial debut with Seven Days Somewhere Else (1968), followed by Comrades (1970) and Blow for Blow (1972), which were screened at international festivals. He opened his first cinema in Paris in 1974 in response to Blow for Blow , about a group of textiles workers who take their factory boss hostage in protest at the work conditions, being shut out of mainstream circuits. In 40 years, he would produce 108 films and distribute over 350 in theatres, among them Krzysztof Kieslowski’s Three Colours trilogy, for which he received a nomination for the European Film Awards 1994, twelve films by Claude Chabrol, Alain Resnais, Louis Malle, the Taviani brothers, Theo Angelopoulos, Lucian Pintilié, Gus Van Sant, Ken Loach, Abbas Kiarostami, Hong Sang-Soo, Michael Haneke, Walter Salles and Xavier Dolan. Den Hamer has an extensive track record in the Dutch film industry. From 2007 to 2023, she was the director of the Netherlands Filmmuseum in Amsterdam. Under her leadership, the re-named Eye Filmmuseum opened a brand-new museum building and a new collection centre in Amsterdam. Its eclectic programming includes large retrospectives, international conferences and as well as exhibitions, exploring the work and careers of filmmakers such as Bela Tarr, Apichatpong Weerasethakul and Alex van Warmerdam among many others. Before that, Sandra den Hamer worked for 23 years at the International Film Festival Rotterdam, including roles as co-ordinator of CineMart and the Hubert Bals Fund. From 1996 to 2007, she directed the festival. She also served as President of the Board of the Association of European Cinematheques (A.C.E.). From 2023 to 2026. she was appointed interim executive director at the Netherlands Film Fund. Today she chairs the Board of the IDFA Institute and the Gerrit Rietveld Academy in Amsterdam. Gathering 5,700 members from more than 50 countries across Europe, the European Film Academy oversees the annual European Film Awards, which alternates taking place in its home city of Berlin and another European city, which is Athens this year. The 39th ceremony marks the second time it is unfolding in its new January slot, after the academy decided to shift it from a long-running December slot to integrate the awards more fully into the wider awards season. articles.title: Hearst Networks UK Buys ‘American Chopper’ Revival Series ‘Orange County Choppers Original’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Fremantle International Commercial Strategy VP Jill Kellie Exits After Four Years ‘Joseph’s Machines’, ‘Triple Charm’ & ‘What’s Up Moms’ Among Volt Factor Shows Rolling Out On Future Today Channels Hearst Networks UK Buys ‘American Chopper’ Revival Series ‘Orange County Choppers Original’ View All September 30, 2026 3:11am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Orange County Choppers' EXCLUSIVE: Orange County Choppers Originals is headed out of the garage and travelling to Europe. Hearst Networks has bought UK rights to the ‘reborn’ ob doc series from Off The Fence , which has boarded the show after striking an agreement to represent it worldwide (excluding the U.S.). The new series – which aired in the U.S. on Discovery Channel, Discovery Turbo TV, Discovery+, and Discovery GO after launching in February – is the latest chapter in the motorbikes franchise that began in 2002 with American Chopper and is bases around the Orange County Choppers custom bikes business. A second season has been ordered, with the number of eps doubling to 12. Related Stories News Dori Media Hitting Cannes With Unscripted Shows Like 'You Show Know' & 'New Love' Executives V10 Entertainment Gears Up For MIPCOM By Tieing With Former Paramount, Amazon MGM Studios & Vision Plus Execs Prior to Orange County Choppers Originals ‘ launch, there had been no new American Chopper episodes since 2020’s finale, American Chopper: The Last Ride . At one point, there had been a six-year gap due to legal problems between Paul Teutul Sr. and his son, Paul Teutul Jr., the father and son at the center of the series, but they were ultimately settled and the pair reunited on-screen. Watch on Deadline The Hearst agreement, brokered by OTF’s SVP North America and Global Networks, Sam Thompson and Hearst Networks’ Acquisitions Manager, Hannah Gray, marks a first international deal for the revival. Orange County Choppers Originals is based around Teutul Sr., founder and CEO of Orange County Choppers, who has spent over 30 years crafting custom motorcycles for major corporations and sports teams. The series shifts the focus to his workshop in Florida, where he reunites with some of the original team while introducing fresh talent. It also delves into his personal life, highlighting his charity work and passion for animal welfare and rescue on his hobby farm. Hearst’s Gray said: “ Orange County Choppers has everything we look for in great factual entertainment: big builds, strong characters and plenty of heart. With Paul Sr. back at the centre of the story, we’re excited to bring this new chapter to UK audiences.” Orange County Choppers Original sees Teutul Sr.’s team design and build one-of-a-kind motorcycles for charitable causes, with each episode following them through engineering challenges, tight deadlines, and unexpected setbacks, culminating in auctions or raffles to raise funds and awareness. Joan Kay, co-CEO of OCC said: “Everyone loves a comeback story and this one comes with the rebirth of an iconic brand and frankly, Paul Sr. is kicking ass. We’re very excited to partner with OTF on the global revival of the show as the company shares our values of working with entertainment with purpose and has an enviable reach and network of partners around the world across all platforms. “This show isn’t just television, it has proved itself as a cultural phenomenon with the power to ignite fans and enthusiasts and turbocharge bike culture – we can’t wait for you all to see it.” OTF’s Thompson said: “We’ve seized this opportunity wholeheartedly because the facts speak for themselves. There’s an existing fanbase hungry for more, with proven ratings, engagement, sponsorship and merchandising potential. We’re especially excited to have Hearst Networks on board as a quality broadcast partner and look forward to sharing the rollout of this rare gem.” The American Chopper franchise has previously broadcasted in 160 territories in 35 languages worldwide, and OTF’s acquisition offers a new opportunity for buyers at MIPCOM in just under two weeks’ time in Cannes, France. articles.title: London Film Festival: Sam Pollard To Lead Official Competition Jury
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Ascent Creatives International Launches After DDA Talent & Worldwide Production Merger AI Short Film ‘The Gifted’ Wins Inaugural Future Vision XPRIZE Backed By Range Media Partners & Google SXSW Teen Comedy ‘Edie Arnold Is A Loser’ Lands International Sales Rep View All September 30, 2026 4:29am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sam Pollard Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images for Tribeca Festival. Legendary documentary filmmaker Sam Pollard will lead the Official Competition jury at this year’s London Film Festival . Pollard will be joined by Argentine filmmaker and writer Mariano Llinás ( The Life of Jorge Luis Borges ) and Julie La Bassiere, Chief Strategy Officer at DDA Global. The ten films in Competition at LFF this year are: • 7 Miles Out — Carol Morley • Act 3 — Christine Molloy and Joe Lawlor • Glaxo — Benjamín Naishtat Related Stories News Paul Thomas Anderson's Cameron Winter Concert Film Joins London Film Festival Lineup As Mubi Acquires World Rights News London Film Festival Lineup: Ava DuVernay's '14th' & Boots Riley's 'I Love Boosters' Among Headline Titles -- Full List • Imperium — Sergei Loznitsa Watch on Deadline • Ketticè — Giovanni Tortorici • Look Back — Hirokazu Koreeda • My Notes on Mars — Lili Horvát • The Difficult Bride — Rubaiyat Hossain • The Idiot(s) — Małgorzata Szumowska and Michal Englert • Woman Unknown — May el-Toukhy The First Feature Competition (Sutherland Award) jury will be led by British Egyptian actor and producer Amir El-Masry. El-Masry won a Scottish BAFTA for his performance in Limbo and was named a 2020 BAFTA Breakthrough Brit. His recent screen work includes the Naseem Hamed biopic Giant and 100 Nights of Hero . Sandhya Suri will lead the Documentary Competition jury. Suri’s Hindi-language narrative fiction debut, Santosh , premiered at Cannes in 2024, won the BIFA for Best Screenplay, was nominated for an Outstanding British Debut BAFTA, and was shortlisted for the Oscars. Suri, who originally made her debut with the 2005 documentary I For India , is now working with BBC Film on a JG Ballard adaptation. T The Short Film Competition jury is led by producer, writer and Erebus Pictures co-founder Helen Simmons. Her producing credits include the BAFTA-nominated Hoard , the 2025 LFF Closing Gala film 100 Nights of Hero , and Berlinale Crystal Bear winner Last Swim . She also co-wrote and co-directed the Méliès Award-winning short Measure . The 2026 London Film Festival runs from October 7 to October 18. articles.title: Fremantle International Commercial Strategy VP Jill Kellie Exits After Four Years
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Fremantle International Commercial Strategy VP Jill Kellie Exits After Four Years ‘Joseph’s Machines’, ‘Triple Charm’ & ‘What’s Up Moms’ Among Volt Factor Shows Rolling Out On Future Today Channels Hearst Networks UK Buys ‘American Chopper’ Revival Series ‘Orange County Choppers Original’ View All September 30, 2026 6:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jill Kellie Fremantle EXCLUSIVE: Jill Kellie, Fremantle ‘s VP of Commercial Strategy, Commercial and International, has left the Kill Jackie and Baywatch company. Fremantle confirmed her exit to Deadline, with the departure coming more than four years after she had joined , initially in a Director of Acquisitions, Scripted Content role. She took on her current role in 2024 and was notable for pushing Fremantle’s digital distribution business, and working on content deals on YouTube, FAST channels and ad-supported streaming. Further back, she worked in commercially-focused roles at BBC Studios and ITV Studios, and also had earlier spells at BBC-backed 2Entertain and Universal Pictures International. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'American Idol's Luke Bryan, Lionel Richie, Carrie Underwood & Ryan Seacrest Return For Season 25 News 'America's Got Talent' Is Latest Reality Show To Eye California Exit Jens Richter, Fremantle’s CEO of Commercial and International, said in a statement to Deadline today: “Jill has been an integral member of the team driving the commercial growth strategy across Fremantle’s global content business. “She played a key role in shaping Fremantle’s content portfolio and driving Fremantle’s expansion in digital-first content distribution, scaling the company’s commercial impact across YouTube, FAST, and AVOD. It has been a pleasure to work with Jill, and we would like to thank her for all her achievements as we wish her every success for the future.” Kellie added: “I’m really proud of my time within Fremantle’s Commercial and International division and of helping build its success. I am excited to see where the business goes next.” Her exit from Fremantle follows that of Vasha Wallace and long-serving Commercial and International COO Bob McCourt . The company, which posted half-yearly revenues of €835M ($948M) in August, is heading to MIPCOM Cannes with the likes of Kill Jackie and Baywatch . articles.title: Ahead Of Tonight’s CNN Gubernatorial Debate, Steve Hilton On No Federal Tax Credits This Year, ParaBros Politics, L.A.’s Next Mayor & California’s Spirit
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Trump “Very Close” To Unveiling AI Czar, Praises Techlords Inking “Morally Binding” Self-Regulation Pact As Tech Rebranded Blue State AGs Side With Paramount, Scolding Sen. Cory Booker Over Settlement Opposition: “A Negotiated Agreement …Includes Compromises On Behalf Of All Of The Parties Involved” ParaBros Foes Urge Court To Reject Settlement In Midnight Filings: “This Merger Lessens Competition” View All September 30, 2026 6:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source David Ellison, Donald Trump and Steve Hilton Getty Images “People actually want to be in California and in L.A. particularly, and so I think we don’t have to go crazy,” says gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton on the need for greater film and TV tax incentives in the Golden State and from the federal government. Related Stories News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Warn That Trump Will “Reinstitute A Complete Ban” Without Judge’s Injunction: “An Injury On All News Media” News Film Execs Ponder Federal Film Tax Credit Impact, Timeline & Potential Price Rises — Zurich Summit “We just have to match the best, and we have to be as good as the best,” the Brit-born ex-host of Fox News’ The Next Revolution adds of the lucrative jurisdictions of the UK, Canada and Europe. “Once we’ve done that everyone will want to be here because it’s better here. We just got to take the tax argument off the table for the production decision, and then we’ll win.” Talking to politicians from both parties, there’s always a need in interviews to navigate around their talking points and stump lines. It’s a dance: They want to stay on message, and you want to have a conversation and get some news out of it. Watch on Deadline A seasoned veteran of UK elections for Britain’s Conservative Party, Hilton is trying to sell his MAGA-lite approach out here on the very blue West Coast. Yet, unlike many of his fellow Trump-following brethren, Hilton is prepared to engage. He’s also open to saying he doesn’t know when he doesn’t have an answer, something you hear very rarely on the American campaign hustle. Perhaps that’s just a tactic of a contender behind in the polls and scratching away to be the first Republican to lead California since Arnold Schwarzenegger. Perhaps, with an eye on the next prize beyond Sacramento, it’s also a consummate operative in action. Perhaps, and most likely, it’s both and more. With a head-to-head debate coming up Wednesday night at 6 p.m. PT on CNN with his Democratic rival Xavier Becerra , Hilton took time away from the campaign trail to talk about the race and his plans. We discussed how ailing Hollywood can grow strong again, AI, the role and the reach of Trump and ICE. Hilton offered opinions on his opponent and the L.A. Mayor’s race between incumbent Karen Bass and current poll-topper Nithya Raman. Of course, this being Hollywood, the well-connected candidate also addressed the $111 billion ParaBros merger, the sudden settlement and (with a cameo by Spencer Pratt) the moves in DC toward a bipartisan federal film and TV tax credit. Getty Images DEADLINE : The first thing Steve I want to talk about is the proposed federal film and TV tax credit. This is seen, at least right now, as a bipartisan measure. Trump is obviously behind it . His arch foe Adam Schiff’s also behind it. So, strange bedfellows. California will clearly be a great beneficiary of this. With all that hype, is it possible to get this passed by the end of the year? STEVE HILTON: I think it’s very unlikely. DEADLINE : Full points for honesty. HILTON: I’d love it to get passed. I’ve been in close conversation with Jon Voight and Steven Paul, for example, and Spencer Pratt. We’re all behind it, no question. But I just don’t see the votes for it in Congress, frankly. Now I’d love it to pass. I hope I’m wrong. I sincerely hope I’m wrong, but I think that it’s unlikely to get the votes. DEADLINE: Is it unlikely to get the votes because of the strange bedfellows, or do you just think because of the calendar with the midterms and then the lame duck Congress? Is it just simply there’s just no time? HILTON: It’s mainly the calendar. DEADLINE : Really? HILTON: Also, the incorrect assumption among those who either are ignorant of the real economic realities or just don’t care and just want to pander to their own districts. DEADLINE: What do you mean by that? HILTON: I mean those who say, “Why on Earth should we be bailing out Hollywood celebrities?” I just think that’s a simple, totally false argument. But I think that it’s powerful. If you’re representing some district somewhere that has had zero connection with the entertainment industry, and that’s most districts, why would you vote for this tax credit? Why would you risk any political capital for this? Sadly, I just think it’s very unlikely. DEADLINE: I disagree, but I know that argument… HILTON: Absolutely. Which is exactly why I’ve put so much effort into making developing a really strong California package because I don’t think we can rely on the feds to come to our rescue. I don’t think we can, and so we have to save ourselves here. That’s the starting point for me. Second point is that I feel very strongly, and I say this everywhere I go, like the other week, we had a number of entertainment industry events here in L.A., roundtables with unions and others, and of course I said it to them: The mission as the next governor to me is turning around California’s business climate. DEADLINE: Why? HILTON: Because Dominic, everything is too hostile to business. All businesses, right? The litigation that you face, the energy cost, you know, all of those things: taxes, regulations, insane red tape driving business away. That’s my argument. However, I always say there are two specific industries that need emergency help right now because they are collapsing. One of them is agriculture, and the other is entertainment. They’re iconic industries for California. We have to save them. I say that to every audience, not just when I’m in L.A. County. DEADLINE: On both of those, but the entertainment industry specifically, can they be saved as we know them? HILTON: Let me say this, broadly, I agree with the argument that we shouldn’t be doing what is sometimes called a race to the bottom with tax incentives. I agree with that as an economic theory, right? But we don’t live in a world of economic theory. We live in the real world, and in the real world, that’s what’s happening. I may not love the fact that UK and Hungary and now New Jersey are doing these incredible …what you could call bribes, right, or tax incentives. But they are doing them, and so we got to compete. Xavier Becerra Getty Images DEADLINE: Secretary Becerra has not pledged he will uncap the tax credits , as you have, but everyone acknowledges that even with the state’s tax credits already at $750 million, there’s more to be done. HILTON: Agree. DEADLINE: We’ve already seen that in the last session with the post-production credit. But you’ve also talked about in your policy papers, and I read them, as this is an investment, not a handout. But to go to your earlier point, do you not worry that a federal tax incentive will lead to a race to the bottom with the UK, Canada and other countries? HILTON: I think that the difference is that we have an inherent advantage here. DEADLINE : How so? HILTON: Because people want to be here, so you have to be bribed to go elsewhere. People actually want to be in California and in L.A. particularly, and so I think we don’t have to go crazy. We just have to match the best, and we have to be as good as the best. Once we’ve done that everyone will want to be here because it’s better here. We just got to take the tax argument off the table for the production decision, and then we’ll win. DEADLINE: Speaking of winning, even though a federal judge has yet to sign off on the antitrust settlement, it looks like David Ellison will get his mega-merger. With all it took to get him and us here, what’s your stand on that, and what’s your concerns about job losses? HILTON: I see it as a long-term growth story. I mean, I haven’t particularly weighed in on it, honestly, and I’ve consciously done that because I think it’s already been politicized too much. What I do want is I want to see the industry grow, and I want to see jobs not just protected but increased. So, I do think that that means successful, profitable companies. In that sense, I trust the market process here. This should, long term, guarantee the health of the industry. That’s my sense of it. That’s why I certainly haven’t weighed in to oppose it. I’m not a cheerleader for it, but I think that it’s certainly not something that I would want to weigh in on and encourage or discourage either way. California Attorney General Rob Bonta , left, and Paramount CEO David Ellison Getty Images DEADLINE: Something or someone you have weighed in on many times in the past is California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who I believe you once called a hack. He took the lead in going after Paramount and WBD with that antitrust suit in July. He was also the one who struck a deal with Ellison earlier this month, tossing a lot of his antitrust concerns aside. HILTON: Indeed. DEADLINE: Was it political pressure from Gavin Newsom and others that caused him to back off everything? HILTON: I think the whole case was entirely political driven. I think that the substance of his case just wasn’t there. That’s why I always sensed that it was totally driven by politics, by wanting to look as if he’s sticking it to a Trump-supporting billionaire. That’s what I think this was motivated by. I mean, look at what Rob Bonta, you know, what’s his main message in his campaign for re-election? I sued the Trump administration, whatever many times. That’s his message. It’s not I’ve cracked down on crime, or I’ve made our communities safer. It’s not I’ve cracked down on the cartels or any of these other things that he could have been focusing on. It’s I sued the Trump administration. So, this is to me a proxy for that: I’m suing a Trump-supporting billionaire. DEADLINE: Were you surprised he and the 11 other blue state AGs came to a settlement with Ellison after the leaked threats that Paramount would leave LA? HILTON: No, I’m not surprised that it collapsed. Because they cobbled together some case, which was laughable when it was actually tested, in a way. I feel sorry for the other AGs that went along with it. They saw political opportunity as well, and were hoodwinked by him, I think. DEADLINE: You would be involved to some degree in all this if you win in November. There have been a lot of criticisms about the settlement. Obviously, there’s a judge in Oakland, a Biden-appointed judge, who has some very serious questions about the deal and hasn’t signed off on it yet. There’s also been an intervention by Cory Booker…. HILTON: Dominic, these people don’t know what they’re talking about. Honestly, it’s so frustrating to me. They’re just performative idiots. DEADLINE: Bonta? The judge? Booker? HILTON: David Ellison is a guy who loves this industry. David Ellison is someone who loves movies and loves this industry and loves California and loves Los Angeles. Now, I’m not sort of cheerleading for this. DEADLINE: It does sound like you are … HILTON: No, as I say, I do love Spencer and think he’s fantastic. Spencer’s been cheerleading for this, and I think that’s great, and I love that he’s done that. I’m focusing my campaign on reducing costs and get California back on track. DEADLINE: So, you don’t think you don’t think Ellison was serious when it was leaked and later confirmed that he was going to leave? You think that was negotiation? HILTON: I don’t know. I can’t see into his mind. But I know that most of the people, businesses who’ve left California, love California. They’ve just been driven out by crazy policies and hostility from the government. This was another case of that. I mean, again, it’s just obvious to me that David Ellison is someone who loves this industry and wants to make it thrive in California, and that’s great, and I agree with that. DEADLINE: Let’s see into your mind for a sec: You are behind in the polls, let’s just be honest. And with the lead Becerra has, he’s running a ghost campaign, but you are going to be with him on stage later Wednesday… HILTON: Yeah. DEADLINE: He is running a very traditional, “do no harm” campaign and you, like Andy Burnham and Trump, are taking a different way to run for office and then to govern now. HILTON: Well, I think that after all my political work, moving to America, teaching at Stanford, being involved with start-ups and then offered a new career in the media hosting on Fox News, I really feel very conscious of who I am and the working-class background I came from. And so, going to the election campaign, the parts of this that I most I most feel at home in when I’m with regular people, like really, I really like I love doing our townhalls… DEADLINE: Yes, but you are so far behind right now. There isn’t a single poll that has you even, let alone ahead. HILTON: I did Mark Halperin’s show the other day, and I made the argument to him that the polls are flawed. He kind of amplified it. He said, “Look, any you can’t do a good poll unless you have a good model of who the likely electorate is.” So, paraphrasing, right now with everything that’s going on in California, the level of dissatisfaction and turmoil, and the fact that you’re both kind of new candidates, I don’t know how you would you could predict what the electorate is in California today. That’s actually reflected in the differences in the polls. So, you have a traditional series that don’t change their assumptions about who’s going to show up and vote. Big gap, 20-points, 25-point gap, of course. Other polls that are just a bit more fine-tuned in terms of likely voters. It’s a much smaller gap, but we’re still behind. Yeah, like eight points behind, not 30 or 25. DEADLINE: To that, trying to expand your base, you have an immigrant story, but there was a blowback earlier this week to your English only in California schools remark, especially here in L.A. County, which obviously is a majority Latino county. How do you how do you factor that, knowing perfectly well that that’s going to be thrown at you in the debate? HILTON: I think it’s completely uncontroversial. Reed Hastings, for example, who is you know he’s a Democrat, he’s a great supporter of Democrats, had exactly the same position when he was chairman of the state board of education. How is anyone supposed to succeed and climb the ladder of opportunity in in California or America, for that matter, if you don’t speak English? DEADLINE: I’ll play devil’s advocate here. How could you expect to climb the ladder of opportunity in L.A. County if you don’t speak Spanish? Or to use your own words on Fox: “This is our country. We speak English here.” HILTON: In America, how are you’re going to be a startup founder if you don’t speak English? How are you going raise money on Silicon Valley’s Sand Hill Road? It’s insulting and it’s patronizing, and it’s exactly why right now you have a total crisis of literacy with huge numbers not proficient in English. It’s a total disaster. Anti-ICE protests during “National Shutdown” on January 30, 2026 in Los Angeles DEADLINE: You have been very clear that you are you are a supporter of Donald Trump. So, do you feel that what we have seen with the immigration raids and abductions – especially with American citizens have been plucked off the street and kids plucked off the streets, put in detention centers, sent to overseas – how do you factor that into your campaign, and how do you factor that into being governor? HILTON: It’s nothing compared to what Xavier Becerra did when he was Secretary of Health and Human Services under Biden sending thousands and thousands of Latino children directly into the hands of child sex and labor traffickers. DEADLINE: Whoa… HILTON: As a result of his personal decisions, in order to try and launder his reputation, because he didn’t like the TV pictures of kids in camps that he was responsible for, because he was so utterly incompetent. So instead of actually dealing with the problem, he dismantled the checks and the vetting for where these children should be sent, That was his job, because he was responsible for the Office of Refugee Resettlement. That’s under HHS. Today, there are still over 300,000 missing, unaccounted for. Some of them may have aged out of the system. They may have returned to the country they came from. We don’t know. What we do know is that of that number, because their ages are recorded when they came across the border, 100,000 are under 10 today. DEADLINE: The numbers of lost and abandoned children may differ, but what happened at HHS under Becerra is undeniably heartbreaking. It’s also a big part of this campaign. But, in the context of two wrongs don’t make a right, I feel like you’re dodging my question about Trump and ICE in California. HILTON: Well, I’m very happy to talk about it. Let’s break it down. First of all, a lot of this is their refusal to just engage in normal legal cooperation under California’s sanctuary state law. There’s no reason for this this confrontational attitude with immigration enforcement. It’s entirely political and performative. All of this drama and confrontation and rage has been created entirely by Democrat politicians. DEADLINE: Steve, you can’t honestly say that you don’t think that the administration has taken a very confrontational approach. If you just take them on their initial word that they were going to arrest criminals, and what they are doing is hauling children, families of service members and legal American citizens into detention camps … HILTON: If they, well, if you look, what they say about that is, and first of all… DEADLINE: I’m asking what you say as the Republican candidate for governor about that. What you would say to the people of L.A. who live in fear, who have seen family members taken? HILTON: (PAUSES) I’ll tell you what I would do, which is lower the temperature on this whole issue. As governor, I know all the people involved, and I will get on the phone, meet in person, and say, right, we need to sort this out. I don’t want to see any of this going on in California. Let’s focus on what the priorities are and work together calmly and cooperatively to make that happen, which is to focus on the people that, where there’s a broad consensus, should be removed from the country. DEADLINE Which are? HILTON: Illegal immigrants who’ve committed some other kind of crime, especially violent crime. Let’s work on that together. That’s what I would do. So, I’m not really interested in so much in you know commenting on what’s happened in the past, I’m just telling you what I would actually do as governor, which is to lower the temperature, work together within the sanctuary state law to focus on removing the people who most Californians would agree shouldn’t be here. All the time you’re hearing these stories of crimes committed by people who everyone agrees should not be here, but judges are releasing them. Local law enforcement is releasing them, not notifying immigration enforcement, and they go back into the community, and that’s happening all the time. This whole argument is broken as far as I’m concerned. Gavin Newsom Getty Images DEADLINE: On a much less human scale, at least for now, another argument that some people feel is broken is artificial intelligence or superintelligence, as Trump likes to call it. There are a lot of concerns, especially because the hub of AI in this country is here in California. This is what we have created in many ways. Newsom has put in what he says are various safeguards and guardrails that are going to protect people and institutions. If they’re even effective, they only go as far as the state line. With all the doom and gloom, even from the CEOs themselves, what do you think needs to be done with AI?. HILTON: Yeah, I think it’s a huge question, and we got to take it very seriously. I think that we’re leading, and I want us to continue to lead. That’s the first point. I want us to continue to lead this incredible industry, just as we’ve led so many others. I want to keep it here in California, not drive it away, which is what current policies would do. So that’s the first point. And the second point, I actually want to see more of it here? DEADLINE: More AI? HILTON: Pretty much all the job creation from this new wave of technology is happening in other states. The high-end manufacturing, construction, infrastructure, all in Texas, Nevada, Arizona, elsewhere. You saw Nvidia, fantastic Bay Area success story last year announced a half trillion-dollar investment in America, none of it in California. Like, can we please have the jobs and investment from this industry here rather than chasing it out to other states? That’s a very important point. On that question of regulation, I think there’s some easier and harder questions here. One of them is protecting children. I don’t think we’re doing enough at the moment. It’s all very haphazard and random. It’s being rolled out in ways that are just, I think, very dangerous. You know, 11 years ago, I wrote a book, More Human, arguing that children shouldn’t have smartphones. I think the Australia ban is a waste of time because it’s not aiming at the real target, which is the device. It’s not the apps. It’s the device, the smartphone. That’s the problem. We’ve got to get smartphones out of kids’ lives. Also, there’s way too much involvement of the tech companies in in core academic processes like setting curriculum and so on. That’s been really corrupt and that’s got to end. Secondly, I think we had we need an immediate pause on AI in the classroom. Immediate. I think that L.A. Unified has done that, and I agree with that. And I want to see that statewide. Not for long, right? Just a pause while we actually evaluate how and if, if and how we want AI to be used in education. There’s very concerning reporting of what what’s being described as cognitive stunting, where you have the introduction of AI too early, and it’s actually changing kids’ ability to think. So I think that shouldn’t be a difficult thing to get agreement on. DEADLINE : Except if you are a tech company… HILTON: Yes DEADLINE: On Wednesday night you’re going to be meeting your opponent, Secretary Beccera. It might be the only time you actually get face to face with him before November. CNN are hosting this with Jake Tapper and Dana Bash moderating. There’s going to be a lot of topics that we’ve discussed here coming up like the film industry, tax credits, and Paramount Warner Bros merger. You’re a seasoned television performer, how did you prepare for this debate? HILTON: What I’ve been doing the last year and a half, honestly. Traveling the state, meeting people, understanding what’s going on, and responding to their questions. That’s the true answer. I’ve been preparing for five years for this debate with the work I‘ve been doing is what I would say to that. DEADLINE: I’m not throwing any shade on you at all but let’s assume the polls are correct, and you don’t win. What are you going to do next? HILTON: I don’t know. I really haven’t thought about it. I really haven’t. DEADLINE: Steve? HILTON: I swear, all my thought process is, “How are we going to start?” You know what comes first? I’m thinking its very important to establish a good relationship with the leaders of the legislature. That’s going to be crucial. I want to make, you know, phone them straight away. Let’s get together, the mayors of the big cities. You know we got to work together. We got to solve some problems… Los Angeles City Councilmember Nithya Raman, left, and Mayor Karen Bass Apu Gomes / JC Olivera / David McNew / Getty Images DEADLINE: Let me ask you then, because you brought up big cities, who’s going to be the next mayor of L.A.? HILTON: It’s hard to tell, but it seems to me like the momentum is with Nithya, doesn’t it? I think that there’s some justice in that. DEADLINE: Why? HILTON: Whatever one may think of Nithya Raman or Karen Bass, and I haven’t met either of them, so I’m really not judging, and I’m not weighing in. I don’t have a vote in LA. But I do think that there’s something about rewarding the level of failure that Karen Bass has presided over that’s very hard for voters to do that. My attitude is also I’m going to have to work with either of them, and I’m looking forward to working with either of them, you know, to make things happen. Especially in L.A., it’s a hugely important relationship because we got the Olympics coming up. I mean, it’s just like an absolutely central thing that we got to get right. DEADLINE : Is to get things right why you are running? HILTON : (LAUGHS) Truly I’m running because I love California. The reason I felt so at home here, as soon as we got here, and wanted to stay here and be here and be part of the story of California, is that I love it. It’s not just the physical beauty and the weather and all those things we can see and touch, but there’s the soul and a spirit of California that is just so precious. DEADLINE: I hear a stump speech starting… HILTON: Truly, I think that’s what’s being crushed by what’s happened over 16 years of this one-party rule. The spirit of California is the rebel spirit, I often call it, and we got this government that’s just so weighing us down. We’ve got so much potential, and we can, you know, do anything, build anything, make anything, grow anything. We don’t. You just need the government to get its basic things right, and then Californians will do the rest. I don’t want to tell people how to live their life. DEADLINE: All politicians do, especially the ones who say they don’t. HILTON: I really don’t. I want everyone to have the chance to live the life they want in a way that’s affordable and safe and secure. Go about their business and have a fantastic time in this incredible state of ours. That’s all I’m here to do. Believe it or not, this interview has been edited for length and clarity. articles.title: Condé Nast CEO Roger Lynch Jumps To Top Job At Mattel, Succeeding Ynon Kreiz
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Disney Hit By Layoffs, A Couple Hundred Workers Cut Broadcast To Hit A Double, Peacock Going Deep In NBC Sports Coverage Of MLB Wild Card Playoffs Paramount To Move Its Class B Shares From Nasdaq To New York Stock Exchange In Early October View All September 30, 2026 6:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Roger Lynch, left, is stepping down as CEO of Condé Nast to take the top exec job at Mattel, replacing Ynon Kreiz. Getty Images/Teri Weber Condé Nast CEO Roger Lynch has stepped down in order to take the top job at Mattel . Ynon Kreiz , who steered the toymaker through its Barbie movie breakthrough, is poised to take “a senior leadership position at another public company,” an announcement by Mattel said Wednesday. Lynch, whose appointment as CEO takes effect on November 2, will become chairman on October 2. He has been a member of Mattel’s board of directors since 2018. Lynch took over Condé Nast as CEO in 2019, helping the publishing giant navigate declines in print readership and advertising along with Covid. He will remain on the company’s board of directors. Related Stories Executives Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch's Total Pay Declines To $31M In Fiscal 2026 From $33M In Prior Year News Mattel Studios Boss Says "We All Want To See The 'Barbie' Sequel" But Timing Remains Unclear The move follows what Mattel described as a “comprehensive succession planning process” after Kreiz spent eight years running the company. Board member Judy Olian, who led the succession process, called Lynch “a visionary leader with a track record of growing global companies at the forefront of changing industry and consumer trends.” Watch on Deadline Before leading the parent company of Vogue and the New Yorker, Lynch was CEO of music streamer Pandora and the founding chief exec of Sling TV, the streaming pay-TV provider launched a decade ago by Dish Network. Along with the inherent complexities of running a media company born in the 20th century as it reckoned with the consumer habits and tech innovations of the 21st, artificial intelligence was a major challenge. Condé Nast, like other publishers, has seen its web traffic decline as AI chatbots aggregate information that readers would previously have sought out on media platforms. Mike Perlis, lead independent board member for Condé Nast who has previously run media companies Forbes and Ziff Davis, will become interim CEO while a search for a permanent top exec is conducted. Kreiz, who previously had CEO stints at Endemol Group, Fox Kids Europe and Maker Studios before its acquisition by Disney, turned Mattel toward Hollywood during his eight years at the helm. The main fruit of that effort was Barbie , which became a global phenomenon in 2023, grossing $1.4 billion and netting multiple Oscar nominations. Efforts to make a Barbie sequel have run aground on budget issues, however. A Hot Wheels movie project is in development, but the flow of entertainment adaptations has been erratic. Mattel stock has fallen 31% over the past five years. “It has been a privilege to lead Mattel, with a global team dedicated to its mission and purpose, and I am proud of all we have achieved together,” Kreiz said in a statement. “I have every confidence the company will continue to thrive under Roger’s leadership.” Lynch said during his time on Mattel’s board, he came to admire its “brands, its talented people, and unique culture. I am especially grateful to Ynon for his many years of outstanding leadership and service to the company.” CA Gov Candidate Steve Hilton On Federal Tax Credits, ParaBros Merger & More ‘Ted Lasso’ Shocker: Actor Reflects On Death Of OG Character BBC Studios Scripted Boss Jamie Hall On Talent Deal Strategy Review & Red Carpet Premiere Photos With Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.title: ‘The Night Agent’s Curtis Lum To Topline Ensemble Horror-Comedy ‘New Diamond Restaurant’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Lucien Laviscount & Taylour Paige To Topline Netflix Thriller ‘Tyler Perry’s Confabulation’ CAA Signs Actress Sadie Stanley Famke Janssen Inks With Buchwald View All September 30, 2026 7:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Curtis Lum Phil Sharp EXCLUSIVE: Curtis Lum , a Canadian actor with credits like The Night Agent and The Audacity , is in production in British Columbia on New Diamond Restaurant , an indie genre-bender from writer-director Milton Ng , who makes his feature debut. Blending zombie horror, action and family comedy, New Diamond Restaurant follows Aaron Chan (Lum) as he returns home to tell his father he no longer wants to take over the family restaurant. But before he can, a zombie outbreak traps his fractured family inside. Forced to fight for survival together, the family must confront threats outside the restaurant, old resentments and cultural expectations. With its setting in the fictional prairie town of Saint-Legal, the film takes inspiration from Ng’s small-town Alberta upbringing. Related Stories Executives Condé Nast CEO Roger Lynch Jumps To Top Job At Mattel, Succeeding Ynon Kreiz Executives Fremantle International Commercial Strategy VP Jill Kellie Exits After Four Years Other members of the Chan clan are played by Vincent Cheng, Phoebe Miu, filmmaker Ng and Alannah Ong. The film also stars Aleks Paunovic, Morgan Taylor Campbell and Lochlyn Munro. Watch on Deadline In addition to writing, directing and starring, Ng is producing New Diamond Restaurant alongside Mike Morrison. Lum is exec producing the film, with Jessica Ally, Jared Cheer, Natasha Jung and Paolo Valdes serving as co-producers through Dear Hero Studios / New Diamond Film Inc. The production is supported by Telefilm Canada and Creative BC, with Canadian distribution through Photon Films. This year, Lum returned for the third season of Netflix’s The Night Agent before appearing in Jonathan Glatzer’s dark Silicon Valley comedy The Audacity for AMC/AMC+. Past credits include Apple TV’s Invasion , The Agency: Central Intelligence for Paramount+ and the Freeform drama Siren . Next year, the actor will be seen on ABC’s The Rookie: North and Season 3 of Prime Video’s Cross , also appearing alongside Cynthia Erivo, Teo Yoo and more in the Lionsgate action thriller Karoshi . He is repped by Artium Talent and Trisko Talent in Canada. Ng is repped by The Characters Talent Agency. articles.title: Tribeca Festival Sets 2027 Dates, Opens For Submissions
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Tribeca Festival Sets 2027 Dates, Opens For Submissions Paramount Woos Investors With Mega $44 Billion Debt Offer To Fund WBD Deal As Judge Weighs Settlement NYFF Turns Up The Heat As ‘Godzilla’, ‘Artificial’, ‘NAZA’, ‘You Can See Everything’ Spark Festival Buzz View All September 30, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Earth, Wind & Fire and The Roots perform at The Beacon Theatre at Tribeca Festival 2026 Getty Tribeca Festival ’s 26 th edition will unspool June 3–12, 2027 in New York City. Submissions across signature programming categories are now open, and Festival passes are on sale today including the returning Under 25 Pass and a new Hudson Opening Weekend Pass. The fest, a destination for emerging and established artists to debut new work and connect with audiences, industry leaders, and a creative community, has been expanding each year and is a key stop on the indie film circuit. In 2026, it welcomed 57 first-time feature filmmakers, joining alumni community that includes Ryan Coogler, Damien Chazelle, Jon M. Chu, Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert, Alex Gibney, Jessica Kingdon and Nia DaCosta. Related Stories Acquisitions Antenna Releasing Acquires 'Lemonade Blessing' After Letterboxd VOD Run Draws Fan Support News 'Unidentified' Director Haifaa Al Mansour On A New Era In Saudi Arabian Filmmaking, Especially For Women “Building on a record year at the box office, we cannot wait to welcome our passionate audiences back to New York City for our 26th year to discover and delight in the incredible stories, creativity, and cultural experiences that make Tribeca so special each June,” said Rebecca Glashow, CEO of Tribeca Enterprises. “At its heart, Tribeca has always been about bringing audiences and artists together to experience the new voices shaping our culture.” Watch on Deadline “Last year’s record-breaking submissions helped make our 25th anniversary one of the most remarkable editions in Tribeca’s history, and we can’t wait to see what comes next,” adds Cara Cusumano, fest director and SVP Programming. “Tribeca was built on the belief that the next great storyteller could come from anywhere, and we look forward to meeting the voices who will define the 2027 festival.” Submissions are now open across Features, Shorts & Music Videos, Tribeca TV, Tribeca Digital Creators, Tribeca Games, Tribeca Podcasts, and Tribeca X. Submissions for the Tribeca Works in Progress category opens January 5. The 2026 fest marked a milestone 25th anniversary with more than 240 live events and a record 104 world premieres. The festival was founded by Robert De Niro, Jane Rosenthal, and Craig Hatkoff in 2001 to spur the economic and cultural revitalization of lower Manhattan following the attacks on the World Trade Center on Sept. 11. articles.title: Dubai’s MForMedia & Arcana Labs Sign AI Production Pact For Middle East
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Fremantle International Commercial Strategy VP Jill Kellie Exits After Four Years ‘Joseph’s Machines’, ‘Triple Charm’ & ‘What’s Up Moms’ Among Volt Factor Shows Rolling Out On Future Today Channels Hearst Networks UK Buys ‘American Chopper’ Revival Series ‘Orange County Choppers Original’ View All September 30, 2026 8:20am Add us as a Google Preferred Source MForMedia MForMedia EXCLUSIVE: Dubai’s MForMedia will look to add AI workflows into its productions following a deal with Arcana Labs . The two companies have struck a strategic partnership to incorporate Arcana’s software into MForMedia’s production workflows, Arabic-language co-productions and staff training. The overaching goal is to build AI-native film and television production capabilities across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. Arcana Studios, the production arm of Arcana Labs, and MForMedia will also co-produce original content for MENA audiences, with unnamed titles already in development. MForMedia staff are also provided with a five-day training workshop on AI-native production this month. Related Stories News Trump "Very Close" To Unveiling AI Czar, Praises Techlords Inking "Morally Binding" Self-Regulation Pact As Tech Rebranded News BBC Boss Matt Brittin Says He Was Sent A 'Doctor Who' Episode Entirely Generated By AI: "It Was Pretty Good" “The Middle East and North Africa region is one of the most active production markets outside the United States, yet premium original Arabic-language content has struggled to keep pace with soaring demand,” said Arcana Labs CEO Jonathan Yunger. Watch on Deadline “With this model, we are embedding an AI-native pipeline inside a regional studio from day one. Content can now be created in Dubai, in Arabic, faster and more cost-effectively than ever before, ensuring Arabic-language production stays in the region.” MForMedia, led by co-founders and Managing Partners Ralph Matar and Khalil Homeissy, produces Arabic versions of Carpool Karaoke and The X Factor and also makes the likes of the Mahzooz Lottery Show , Eisha Sah , Celebrity Escape Room and Celebrity Advice Bureau . The news comes soon after MForMedia hired MENA television industry veteran Ziad Kebbi as Managing Director, as we revealed two weeks ago. At the same time, the company announced it was pivoting toward AI production, original content and IP ownership, as opposed to its more production services-focused past. “This collaboration marks a significant step in MForMedia’s evolution and reflects a shared ambition: to bring people, creativity and technology together to expand the possibilities of storytelling across the region,” said Matar and Homeissy in a statement. “At the heart of the collaboration is a commitment to empowering creative talent. With these tools, directors, producers, designers and storytellers will have greater freedom to experiment and move more efficiently from concept to production, while retaining creative control and artistic vision.” Arcana is represented by Paradigm Talent Agency. Inspired by the extraordinary world of Tor, this series has all the elements of a powerful HBO drama, and we are proud to support these creators in bringing it to life.” HBO Max has been building out European originals and recently greenlit a French medical drama inspired by The Pitt. articles.title: Canada’s Banger Films Tunes Up Animated Rock Comedy ‘Gone To Hell’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Fremantle International Commercial Strategy VP Jill Kellie Exits After Four Years ‘Joseph’s Machines’, ‘Triple Charm’ & ‘What’s Up Moms’ Among Volt Factor Shows Rolling Out On Future Today Channels Hearst Networks UK Buys ‘American Chopper’ Revival Series ‘Orange County Choppers Original’ View All September 30, 2026 8:42am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: Gone to Hell , a Canadian adult animation about a world-famous rock band who are sent to the underworld, will launch next month. The series, billed as “part supernatural adventure, part rock-and-roll sature, debuts on the BangerTV YouTube channel on October 30. Brian Peco and Craig Mailman are the co-creators and Banger Films is producing with support from the Independent Production Fund, Canada Media Fund and Ontario Creates. Robin Hatch comprised the music. Per the synopsis, the eight-episode series, set in 1994, follows Demon Destroyer, a world-famous rock band whose members are crushed by their own stage mascot during a live performance and sent straight to Hell. There’s just one complication: They aren’t actually dead. Related Stories Casting Lauren Cohan & Jake Epstein To Co-Star In Eric Stoltz-Directed Rom-Com 'Both Sides Now' News Canada's Precious Metal Productions & Black Fawn Distribution Strike Genre Slate Deal - TIFF Back on Earth, the band remain comatose and their predicament triggers an obscure rule of the underworld known as the Coma Clause, which keeps the Gates of Hell open to them for as long as their bodies remain alive. If they can reach the gates before their record label pulls the plug, they can return to Earth, or they will be stuck in this version of Hell, which isn’t particularly scary but populated by self-absorbed oddballs and ruled by the egomaniacal Dev, who has his own ambitions for fame. Watch on Deadline Voice cast includes Paul Spence ( FUBAR , Deaner 89’ ) as Demon Destroyer frontman Rick Fashun, Chris Locke as Dev Devilio, Derrick Beckles ( Hot Package , The Eric Andre Show ) as drummer Donnie, Jackie Pirico as bassist Jojo and Kevin Morgan as Derek, Dev’s assistant, and Deva, Dev’s sister. The show marks Banger Films’ first animated series. The company is best known for music and pop culture programs and films such as the Peabody and Emmy Award-winning Hip-Hop Evolution , Rush: Beyond the Lighted Stage and Metal: A Headbanger’s Journey . “Craig and I wanted to make something that captured the feeling of the cartoons we grew up watching every Saturday morning,” said Peco, the co-creator, writer, director and producer. “We created these hilarious characters, then we literally made Hell. The world is made up of miniature sets that I made and they became such an important part of the identity of the show. There’s an imperfection to it that makes this strange world feel real. The opposite of AI slop.” “ Gone To Hell started with this very simple idea of a rock band trying to escape Hell, but the more we developed it, the more it became a story about people who are never quite satisfied with what they have,” added Mailman, co-creator and producer. “It gave us a really funny foundation for the characters, but also a world that can keep getting bigger and stranger.” You can see a trailer above. articles.title: Mike Flanagan’s ‘Carrie’ Envisioned As Three Seasons In “Dream Scenario”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Recap: Yacht Rock Night Sees One Couple Eliminated In Week 3 ‘Vanderpump Rules: Lisa Las Vegas’ Trailer & Episode Release Guide Schedule Set At Bravo Dennis Haskins Dies: ‘Saved By The Bell’s Mr. Belding Was 75 View All September 30, 2026 8:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Summer H. Howell Prime Video Mike Flanagan adapted Stephen King ‘s Carrie into a series, and in a “dream scenario,” he would like it to run as a trilogy. Already counting on King’s approval of the adaptation, Flanagan has a specific vision for Carrie that could potentially go beyond the original story. “In my dream scenario,” Flanagan said in an interview with Collider . “I think it’s three seasons. In my dream scenario, I think Carrie has a wonderful three-step arc. It’s a trilogy, really.” Carrie follows misfit high‑schooler Carrie White (Howell) after having spent her life hidden away inside the walls of her home with her fiercely protective mother, Margaret (Samantha Sloyan). Following her father’s unexpected death, Carrie enters the public high school ecosystem and is forced to navigate a viral bullying scandal that tears through her community. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Books 'The Love Hypothesis' Author To Release Book Sequel, MRC Developing Film Adaptation For Amazon News Amazon's Kelly Day Says AI Will Unlock "Creative Risk" & Help Free Up Creatives Working On The Next Big Hit Carrie also faces the relentless pressure and casual cruelty of the social‑media age, and the awakening of mysterious telekinetic powers that rise alongside her adolescence. The supernatural horror miniseries premieres on October 7 on Prime Video with Summer H. Howell in the title role. Carrie was first adapted into a film in 1976, with Brian De Palma directing a screenplay written by Lawrence D. Cohen and Sissy Spacek as Carrie. A direct sequel, directed by Katt Shea, The Rage: Carrie 2 was released in 1999, with Emily Bergl playing Rachel Lang, Carrie’s younger half-sister. In 2002, a television film directed by David Carson and based on a screenplay by Bryan Fuller debuted on NBC, with Angela Bettis as Carrie. Before the new miniseries on Prime Video, Kimberly Peirce directed a 2013 remake starring Chloë Grace Moretz. articles.title: Amsterdam’s IDFA Adds Ava DuVernay’s ‘14th,’ Laura Poitras’ ‘They’re Here’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All September 29, 2026 6:00am Ava DuVernay with sitting Librarian of Congress Carla Hayden while making '14th.' Paul Garnes/Netflix The 2026 International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam ( IDFA ), which takes place Nov. 12-22, has added more than 100 films to its program, including in its IDFA Competition for Short Documentary. The Dutch doc fest has also added to its Best of Fests, Signed and Paradocs programs, while unveiling first projects for its new media program DocLab. The IDFA Competition for Short Documentary “celebrates the versatility of the form, with 15 films that use creativity and imagination to push the boundaries of short documentary,” organizers said on Tuesday. “Together, they form a mosaic of styles, themes, and perspectives, driven by ambitious directors with singular cinematic voices and strong artistic visions.” Related Stories Business Amazon MGM Execs Tout New Mercedes Ron Hit, How Spain's 'Apocalypse Z' Became a Hit That's Getting a Sequel: "Zombies Have No Nationality" TV Netflix's 'The Eternaut' Effect: Subscriber Impact Estimate Disclosed at Iberseries Among the titles are a tragicomic portrait of humanity and its fallibility, The Bus of Broken Hearts by Björn Carlberg and Johan Palmgren, which follows the world’s biggest cross-country ski race, where thousands of disheartened participants fail to make it to the finish line. Several titles turn their attention to the act of looking itself, including Perihan Incegöz’s Our Village From the Moon , set in the aftermath of an earthquake in southern Turkey, and PICNIC – In Light Invisible to the Human Eye by Jan Ijäs, which “follows Israeli tourists who travel to the border of Gaza to make a spectacle of the devastation of the Palestinian people.” ‘Our Village From the Moon,’ courtesy of IDFA IDFA DocLab, in its 20th anniversary edition, will feature two films that the Netherlands Film Fund and IDFA DocLab have selected for the 2026 Film Fund DocLab Interactive Grant: The Love Files by Sanne De Wilde and Samir Veen, which invites audiences to step inside and critically review a “love file” application for a residence permit, and All the Downtime by Ant Hampton, immersing audiences in an algorithm-led distribution center, just as a power outage disrupts the order and gives way for creative disorder. Also set for the IDFA DocLab and Tamara Shogaolu’s The Invisible Woman , a VR opera that recovers the story of Francisca de Angola, a 17th-century Black woman in Amsterdam, and Polymorf ’s Microbiome Restaurant, with two sensory experiences exploring the human body as an ecosystem. Other projects include Orgasmagoria and Archive Arcade . Signed “showcases the latest cinematic adventures of some of the most original filmmakers of our time,” and its selection of films “celebrates those with a unique artistic signature, beyond the canon,” IDFA highlighted. “The selection reflects on lives lost, those left behind, and what remains after upheaval.” Among this year’s Signed films are Michal Marczak’s Closure , following a father in search of his missing son along the Vistula River near Warsaw, Ava DuVernay’s 14th , tracing the legacy of the U.S. Constitution’s 14th Amendment, Guillaume Massart’s Detention , about a French prison officers’ training school, and They’re Here by Laura Poitras and Rachel Lauren Mueller, an account of the show of force by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in Minneapolis. And in Wild Asparagus , Avi Mograbi returns to his archives of a visit to Palestinian village Saffuriya with his friend Ali Al-Azhari, giving new meaning to decades-old footage. Meanwhile, IDFA’s Best of Fests section will present 59 titles spanning diverse styles and genres and engaging with some of the world’s most pressing topics. Among them are Pegah Ahangarani’s Rehearsals for a Revolution , Ahmed Hassouna’s Citizen Osama , Lukas Marxt’s >1.5°C: Pyropolitics and the New World , The Illusion of an Everlasting Summer by Alessandra Sanguinetti, and Concrete Land by Asmahan Bkerat. Paradocs, in which visual artists and filmmakers present their explorations in non-fiction filmmaking, will this year feature 16 titles exploring the world “through bold formal experimentation, genre-bending, and unexpected perspectives,” Amsterdam organizers said. “A hedonistic escape to a melting glacier is interrupted by apocalyptic climate change and existential anxiety in Susanne Regina Meures’s Eternity – adapting Florentina Holzinger’s performance art to the screen. In The Case Against Space , Graeme Arnfield offers a reconstruction of the first ‘strike’ in space, reframing the astronaut hero through a critical lens on capitalism and surveillance.” Also, Johann Lurf’s Forever…Forever presents a vision of the cosmos in motion, with an ever-accelerating timelapse of the sun’s path filmed over 22 months. Plus, Ãsheghetam by Filmsaaz blends computer animation, fiction, and documentary in a kaleidoscopic portrait of queer love in Tehran, while in Together , ecofeminist art collective Neozoon uses archival and social media footage to explore the tension between communal life and the desire for private property.
