articles.title: How Britney Spears and the ‘Cannibal Cop’ Left Erin Lee Carr Forever Changed
articles.full_text: Continue to Variety SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Sep 29, 2026 8:00am PT How Britney Spears and the ‘Cannibal Cop’ Left Erin Lee Carr Forever Changed By Marlow Stern Plus Icon Marlow Stern Chief Correspondent Latest How Britney Spears and the ‘Cannibal Cop’ Left Erin Lee Carr Forever Changed 33 minutes ago Mayor Zohran Mamdani Refuses Jimmy Kimmel’s Request to Text Trump a Selfie of Them 11 hours ago John Cho’s Odyssey From ‘MILF Guy #2’ to Porn-Hating Pastor in ‘Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’: ‘It Felt Very Lonesome at Times’ 4 days ago See All Getty Images/Netflix/Tribeca Few documentary filmmakers are as prolific as Erin Lee Carr . In the last five years alone, the in-demand director has helmed the controversial Netflix doc “Britney vs Spears,” “The Ringleader: The Case of the Bling Ring,” “Fanatical: The Catfishing of Tegan and Sara,” the docuseries “I Am Not a Monster: The Lois Riess Murders” and scripted series “Murdaugh: Death in the Family.” She’s also produced “Stormy,” a doc on embattled Trump accuser Stormy Daniels , “Trophy Wife: Murder on Safari” and “Perfect Wife: The Mysterious Disappearance of Sherri Papini.” If you see a throughline there — centering the stories of women — that is by design, and something Carr chalks up to a terrifying encounter with the “ Cannibal Cop ” Gilberto Valle, the subject of her 2015 film “Thought Crimes: The Case of the Cannibal Cop,” that turned her world upside down (more on that later). Related Stories Tilly Norwood Creator Says AI Actress Made 'Many People Realize That AI Is Coming' and 'That Was the Point' Glen Basner Says FilmNation Will Ramp Up Slate in 2027, Is Ready to ‘Raise His Fist’ for ‘I Play Rocky’ and Celebrate ‘Thoughtful’ and ‘Entertaining’ ‘Bunker’ Her latest is “The Swan: Behind the Mirror.” Premiering Sept. 29 on Hulu, the feature-length documentary explores Nely Galán’s notorious 2004 Fox reality-competition series “ The Swan ,” where 16 women — so-called “ugly ducklings” — subjected themselves to extreme plastic surgery, dentistry, training, dieting and a little bit of therapy to transform themselves into what a panel of experts deemed more “attractive” versions of themselves. They would then compete against one another in a beauty pageant, which had a lingerie portion for God knows what reason, for the ultimate prize of being crowned The Swan. It is considered one of the worst reality TV shows ever produced, and the doc features eye-opening testimonials for a dozen former contestants, many of whom were left traumatized by the experience , as well as series producers and even one of its plastic surgeons, who comes off particularly bad. Popular on Variety “On a personal level, I didn’t like my body and what I looked like and always wanted to look like somebody else,” Carr tells Variety about making the doc. “But in many ways, ‘The Swan’ was a harbinger of what was to come.” Carr, 38, is the daughter of late, great New York Times columnist David Carr, and managed to find a window in her packed schedule to fit in “The Swan: Behind the Mirror,” nestling it between “a feature for Netflix that I’m going to finish in the next couple of months” and some more “scripted things” she’s cooking up. But for now, we’re here to talk about “The Swan” — and her “ Britney vs Spears ” ordeal. Did you watch “The Swan” when it was on TV? I wasn’t allowed to watch TV on the weekdays — my father was very intense — but I ended up sneaking it and found out about the show. At the time, I was a huge Britney Spears person and I was like, OK, what am I trying to look like? I just remember seeing a clip of this really intense dentistry and plastic surgery that haunted me, and I don’t think I watched the rest of the show. When Hulu contacted me saying that Expectation TV, this U.K. production company, had this I was like, I gotta do it! I didn’t even have room in my schedule but figured it out. How long did the process take to make “The Swan: Behind the Mirror?” I was not given a lot of time. I will say it was under a year. Typically, the films that I make take 18 months, and I do it to protect the editorial process and develop access in a way that feels deeply meaningful. In this case, a lot of the access had been figured out. Some of the Swans were onboard, Dr. Terry [Dubrow] was a maybe, Dr. Haworth was a maybe, Nely [Galán] I’d had many conversations with. What I immediately knew at the beginning was: I’m not going to cast inside this documentary. Typically, you pick three people and that’s all a feature has room for; you don’t have 12 participants. But I wasn’t going to do the same thing that happened to these women where they got chosen whose story was best. I needed to interview everyone for 2-3 hours and we’d figure it out in the edit. What happened with trying to convince Terry Dubrow and Nely Galán to be in the doc? I’ll let you in on a little secret: Terry wanted a sum of money that would never make sense for a documentary expert. It was under $100,000 for one interview. And with Nely, it’s her show and it’s her footage so if anyone was going to do a “Swan” documentary, it was going to be her. Plus, she wanted to be an executive producer on it and that wasn’t going to work. So then we were in discussions about licensing the footage and we did not end up licensing the footage — it was fair use, so that had to be carefully constructed. When you see the iPad inside the interview scenes it was because they had to comment on the parts of the show. How do you feel about the Terry Dubrow of it all, who now features on “The Real Housewives of Orange County?” He’s had some harsh comments about the women who’ve expressed sadness over appearing on “The Swan.” He said it was “all a bunch of BS,” and I wrote back to him, and I was like, “I’m excited to hear what you think.” I think he’s a reasonable and rational man, and when he sees this, he’ll understand. Maybe his recollection was that he helped people, but that’s not the case. And I was actually really surprised that he was dismissing the experiences of the women so publicly. When I looked into the women and their time on the show, Dr. Dubrow was very well-liked. So, I think it’s puzzling that that is the stance he would take before even watching [the film]. One of the more startling revelations in the documentary concerns a nude photo shoot Dr. Haworth subjected the Season 2 contestants to that seemed incredibly sketchy. He ended up giving the photos to production to give back to the women, but there would be no agreement about deleting or destroying the photos. He said it was for an “art book” and I think the story checked out that it actually was for that, but the circumstances of the women not knowing why they were taking these photos and the fact that production people weren’t at the photo shoot, in a story about exploitation it’s important to include those details. There seemed to be a turning point in your career about a decade ago where you really started focusing on women’s stories. What changed? Do you want to know the craziest reason why that happened? I did “Thought Crimes: The Case of the Cannibal Cop,” and my male subject [Gilberto Valle] would not stop messaging me. I felt harassed and stalked, and I said, I’m never making a film about a man again . I’m not going to fear for my physical safety, I care about women and I’m a long-term feminist. I even advocated for Gil Valle in my film that it had been thought crimes! I ultimately found my path but it’s because this early thing happened to me. I later met an FBI officer in Manhattan who was like, “That guy was absolutely going to kill people so you shouldn’t live where you live.” So you moved because of the “Cannibal Cop?” Because of the “Cannibal Cop” and I had to move in with a cutie in Astoria. Another prominent documentary filmmaker, Alex Gibney, is dealing with legal threats right now from the richest man in the world over his “Musk” doc. How worried are you about legal risk? It’s a scary time to be a documentary filmmaker when it comes to legal risk. I did the “Stormy” film with Sarah Gibson and Judd Apatow, and there was Trump legal risk associated with it. Who I am before that and who I am after makes me feel differently about risk. They tried to file an injunction, the Southern District of New York didn’t want the film coming out, we got legal letters while we were making it and it was a painful experience on all sides. I also got legal letters while I was making the Britney Spears doc and pressure from somebody at an agency saying not to do it. And Stormy Daniels lives as a hunted person. We premiered the film at South by Southwest and there had to be a bomb sweep before the film by security. So, all the hats I have off to Alex Gibney for saying, “I’m going to take on the richest and most litigious person in the world.” You mentioned your Britney Spears doc “Britney vs Spears,” and it did receive a good amount of pushback. There were critics who found it exploitive. Yes. I would say the Britney Spears thing was a very punishing experience in my life because I spent two years where every single moment of my life was dedicated to this person and trying to get her out of this unlawful conservatorship. Ultimately, she disavowed the film and said that people were exploiting her. There were very intense tactics taken by the filmmaking team to not do that. There was no showing of those photos that every doc that’s ever been about her has shown of the incident with the umbrella and her own mental health crisis. So, what I decided was: What other people think of my work can’t be a part of my opinion because then it will ruin how I make films. A part of me was extremely hurt by the process and the accusations, and it was dark days. Now, when I think about the work I am making and want to make, it’s about enthusiastic participation — people who want to do this and want their story to be out. That has been extremely healing for me as it relates to doing this with Hulu and the Swans. But Britney Spears is out of the conservatorship. Certain people think Britney’s not doing well, but she’s not being financially taken advantage of by her father anymore, so that’s a win. Given the work that you do now shining a light on women’s stories, how do you feel about starting your filmmaking career at a place like Vice that had an awful culture when it came to its treatment of women? I was a very strange kid in a bedroom shooting things that no one saw, and then I was a strange kid at an organization shooting things that people saw. I got to have a launchpad to my career. I made this film called “Click. Print. Gun.” about a guy who was printing AR-15s, and that got Andrew Rossi to notice me, and then I got into a room with Sheila Nevins. Would I be here sitting and talking to you and making films about the empowerment of women if that didn’t happen? No. Is it lost on me that the themes and values that I hold dear are incongruent [with Vice]? During one of the last fights I had with my father before he died, he said, “You are incredibly ungrateful when it comes to Vice. They made you a part of who you are.” He ended up really liking Vice. And I said, “Try being a woman working there.” We couldn’t see eye to eye on that. articles.title: Steven Knight on Making the Leap From ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?’ to ‘Dirty Pretty Things’ to, Eventually, James Bond
articles.full_text: Continue to Variety SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Sep 29, 2026 8:08am PT Steven Knight on Making the Leap From ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?’ to ‘Dirty Pretty Things’ to, Eventually, James Bond By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest Daniel Webber, Dermot Mulroney and Katheryn Winnick to Lead Psychological Thriller ‘Compound 9’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Jeremy Clarkson Is Already Thinking About What Comes After ‘Clarkson’s Farm’: ‘It Has to Be Unbelievably Ambitious’ 3 hours ago Should the BBC and Channel 4 Merge? Sony Pictures Television’s International Production Boss Wayne Garvie Thinks So 5 hours ago See All Getty Images One of the most prolific writers and creators working today, Steven Knight ‘s body of work includes the likes of “Peaky Blinders,” “SAS: Rogue Heroes,” “House of Guinness,” “A Thousand Blows” and, most famously (even though it’s not even started filming), the next James Bond film. But, as many might not be aware, his first major breakthrough in the industry was as one of the creators of global smash hit TV game show “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?” in the late 1990s. Related Stories 'Avengers: Doomsday' Star Alan Cumming Says 'I Don't Fully Understand the Plot' and Only Acted With Florence Pugh's Stunt Double ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Co-Director Explains It’s ‘Very Difficult’ to Evolve Marvel Characters, but ‘We Need to Surprise Ourselves’ and ‘Audiences’ This seemingly wild shift from quiz show phenomenons to hit dramas was discussed in a special conversation with Knight at the RTS London Convention on Tuesday, where he revealed that his secret at the time was having “two computers.” Popular on Variety While “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?” was starting to make a splash, Knight said he was also writing radio and radio commercials, writing comedy for stand-ups (including British icons such as Frankie Howard, Ken Dodd and Jasper Carrot), and also writing novels. “I’d had a couple of novels published, and at the time of ‘Millionaire’ I was writing a fourth novel, and it was going to be ‘Dirty Pretty Things,'” he said. “It was going to be a novel, but I was writing it in present tense, which is how you write a script. So I thought, ‘Well, I might as well do the script.” That script wound up getting into the hands of Stephen Frears and turned into the acclaimed 2002 film starring Chiwetel Ejiofor and Audrey Tautou. “And then I was in. I went to Hollywood on the back of that,” Knight said, but noted that he was still “introduced in every meeting I went to as the man who helped make ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?” Nearly a quarter-century on and Knight is one of the most in-demand writers around, having recently been hired by Noel and Liam Gallagher to shape the Oasis tour documentary “Don’t Look Back in Anger” and by Amazon MGM to pen the long-awaited 26th James Bond film and 007 franchise reboot. While Bond wasn’t outwardly discussed in Knight’s RTS talk, it was referenced as “the unmentionable thing,” with host Gaby Roslin asking him if it felt like a “heavy weight” on his shoulder. “Not at all…. articles.title: Sylvester Stallone Says Superhero Movie Bodies Aren’t ‘Natural’ and Taking Steroids to Bulk Up Is Like ‘Putting on Part of a Costume’
articles.full_text: Continue to Variety SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Sep 29, 2026 8:22am PT Sylvester Stallone Says Superhero Movie Bodies Aren’t ‘Natural’ and Taking Steroids to Bulk Up Is Like ‘Putting on Part of a Costume’ By Antonio Ferme Plus Icon Antonio Ferme Latest Chris Rock Says Infidelity and Struggling to ‘Make It’ Aren’t Just Hollywood Problems: ‘If You Got No Love, You’re Broke as F—k’ 2 days ago ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Sets Sights on Best Picture Oscar Nomination: ‘If the Possibility Is Not Zero, It’s Hard Not to Have a Little Bit of Hope’ 2 days ago ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Director Champions Franchise’s First R Rating as Sequel Rocks NYFF at World Premiere: ‘Censoring’ the Action ‘Was Not an Option’ 3 days ago See All Getty Images Sylvester Stallone is sharing the story of how “ Rocky ” got made 50 years after its release in his new tell-all memoir, “Steps,” which hits shelves today. Part of the Oscar winner’s press tour brought him to New York 92nd Street Y for a 50-minute conversation with journalist Tracy Smith about his early career struggles, the legacy of the “Rocky” franchise and the physical toll of his action roles. After making headlines for telling The New York Times that he was “bulimic” while filming “Rocky III” and discussing the “terrible toll” steroids took on his body, Stallone explained to Smith that he rationalized his drug use with his desire to push the Rocky Balboa character in a new direction. Related Stories 'Obsession,' 'Backrooms' Ushering in Shift Similar to 'Easy Rider' in 1970s, Sony Pictures Classics Co-Chief Says Matthew McConaughey Exposed Himself to Jimmy Kimmel in the Emmys Bathroom and Woody Harrelson Saw the Whole Thing “By the time they did ‘Rocky III,’ you’ve lost the element of surprise. Everyone knows what this guy is all about,” Stallone said. “I wanted him to develop serious narcissism. I wanted him to get his scars removed and be a totally different guy. That would be a story point. He became protected, he’s shielded and vain. And when he finally met Mr. T, or Clubber Lang, that’s where reality hit him. But to do that, I had to do a total body metamorphosis. So I went from like 50% body fat to 2.6%. I did it literally by eating tuna fish and [drinking] maybe 30 cups of coffee a day. And, of course, there’s steroids.” Popular on Variety When the audience responded with audible gasps, Stallone made light of the fact that he’s hardly the first and only Hollywood action star to use steroids and go to extreme lengths to achieve a certain bulked-up physique. “Guys … you really think these guys are natural?” Stallone quipped. “If you’re trying to play a sort of superhero or a person that is above and beyond a normal guy, you can’t do it. It’s almost like putting on part of a costume. For six to eight weeks, you manifest that book. And then you shed it.” When Smith asked when Stallone realized he could no longer continue using steroids and maintaining such an arduous workout routine, the actor recalled experiencing “a wake-up call” after having a heart valve replaced. His wife, Jennifer Flavin Stallone, insisted he get checked out after he appeared unwell. Stallone believes the examination “absolutely” saved his life. “And I thought I was okay. I was lucky that my wife said, ‘I don’t like the way you look.’ [I said], ‘Oh, come on. I’m just getting old over here. Relax,’” he recalled. “Women have an extra sense. They really do.” The live interview with Stallone marked the first installment of “ CBS Sunday Morning at 92NY,” a new series of conversations featuring prominent figures from the worlds of arts, politics and culture before a live audience. The series serves as an extension of “CBS Sunday Morning,” the network’s long-running Sunday morning news program. “For over 150 years, the 92nd Street Y has been a world-class beacon for culture, deep conversation and intellectual curiosity,” said 92NY CEO Seth Pinsky. “We are honored to work with ‘CBS Sunday Morning’ on this incredible new programming series. By bringing two great American institutions together, we are creating the kind of deeply engaging experiences our communities crave and expect.” Stallone and Smith’s live conversation will begin streaming on CBSSundayMorning.com, YouTube and Paramount+ later this week. articles.title: JioStar’s Kevin Vaz Urges Indian Government to Restore BARC TV Audience Ratings as Media Sector Hits $28.9 Billion
articles.full_text: Continue to Variety SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Sep 29, 2026 8:24am PT JioStar’s Kevin Vaz Urges Indian Government to Restore BARC TV Audience Ratings as Media Sector Hits $28.9 Billion By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Tops U.K., Ireland Box Office 12 hours ago ‘Hirayasumi’ Anime Unveils Footage, Key Visual and Lead Voice Cast Ahead of NHK Debut 15 hours ago Mohammad Rasoulof, O Mipo to Receive Tokyo Film Festival’s Kurosawa Akira Award 16 hours ago See All FICCI Frames Leading Indian streamer JioStar ‘s Kevin Vaz has called on India’s government to immediately restore BARC audience ratings, using the inaugural address at the FICCI-Frames conference to warn that the data gap is leaving broadcasters, advertisers and agencies without dependable numbers heading into the festive season. Vaz is the CEO of entertainment at JioStar and chair of the FICCI Media & Entertainment Committee. He thanked India’s Ministry of Information & Broadcasting for scrapping the 10+2 advertising cap, describing the move as a step toward rules that fit how linear TV and the wider media business now operate. Related Stories Glen Basner Says FilmNation Will Ramp Up Slate in 2027, Is Ready to ‘Raise His Fist’ for ‘I Play Rocky’ and Celebrate ‘Thoughtful’ and ‘Entertaining’ ‘Bunker’ Martin McDonagh Jokes About His Past – as a Hitman – and Calls ‘Wild Horse Nine’ His Most Political Film: ‘There’s Too Much Artistic Neutrality and Too Much Saying Nothing’ The ministry first ordered BARC to stop publishing news channel ratings on March 6, citing sensationalist coverage of the Israel-Iran conflict, and extended that pause several times. In early July, it widened the freeze to all genres until BARC secures registration under the Television Ratings Policy 2026, which took effect in March. BARC applied on April 29 and has expanded its panel to 70,876 homes against the policy’s 80,000-home target, but ratings remain suspended. Popular on Variety “At a time of global economic uncertainty, reliable audience measurement is critical to keeping this ecosystem efficient, supporting advertisers and broadcasters, and keeping domestic economic activity moving,” Vaz said. He also pressed for a concrete roadmap to strip away the regulatory load and costs that weigh on linear broadcasting. Forbearance has been a long-standing demand from the sector, he said, and self-regulation backed by solid industry standards should sit at the core of its next phase. The appeal comes as the sector continues to grow. Indian media and entertainment expanded 9% in 2025 to INR2.78 trillion ($28.9 billion), Vaz said. Digital passed INR1.1 trillion ($11.5 billion), while live events jumped 47%. Through much of its history, Vaz said, the hard limit on Indian media was distribution, with too few channels and screens for stories to reach viewers. “Attention is the new currency, and in an era where content and ideas seem endless, the magic lies in creating something that makes the ‘thumb stop!'” he said. He pointed to Connected TV as a case where older and newer screens are converging rather than displacing each other. Citing industry estimates, Vaz put India’s CTV audience at more than 200 million viewers, with over 80% of that viewing done together with family or friends. Linear TV streaming, he added, lets viewers watch live channels on any screen and connection while opening up new options for measurement and advertising. The 2026 Indian Premier League (IPL) cricket tournament, which reached more than 1.2 billion viewers, was “perhaps the clearest expression” of that convergence, he said. Microdrama was worth INR6.5 billion ($68 million) in 2025, and the category is expected to grow at more than 50% a year by 2028, Vaz said. JioStar has entered the format through Tadka and is working with over 50 production houses, which he said was helping to bring more creators into the business. JioHotstar also let viewers find and buy products inside the app while they watched the IPL and a live stream of blockbuster “Dhurandhar The Revenge.” Vaz called content commerce a third “value pool” for the industry, next to advertising and subscriptions. On AI, Vaz said the technology is reshaping production, storytelling, workflows, analytics and personalization. “But even as technology expands what is possible, the human being must remain at the center of the creative ecosystem,” he said. He called for clear rules on copyright, consent, attribution and a fair return for creators, so that technology and creativity move forward together. Before turning to the industry’s numbers, Vaz asked the room to pause in silence for the late Leena Jaisani, FICCI’s deputy secretary general and head of media and entertainment, who helped found its Media & Entertainment Committee. This year’s edition, held under the theme “India’s Media Moment: Creating Value in an Age of Infinite Content,” marks 26 years of the committee’s work through FICCI Frames. Vaz closed by urging the industry to judge itself on the value it creates rather than on output or reach. “Did we build intellectual property that could travel from India to the world?” he asked. articles.title: Broadway-Bound ‘Beat Street’ Musical From Grammy-Winning Rapper Nas Assembles Creative Team
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘The One About Matthew Perry’ Intimate Docuseries Gets Netflix Premiere Date, Trailer Broadway-Bound ‘Beat Street’ Musical From Grammy-Winning Rapper Nas Assembles Creative Team Taylor Swift’s “Patient Zero” Music Video Drops: Watch It On Apple Music, Amazon Music Or Spotify View All September 29, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Nas, Schele Williams, Kristoffer Diaz, Jason Michael Webb Production EXCLUSIVE: Beat Street , the Broadway -bound musical based on the groundbreaking 1984 film, has assembled its principal creative team, with The Wiz ‘s Schele Williams , Hell’s Kitchen ‘s Kristoffer Diaz and music supervisor Jason Michael Webb joining the previously announced Nas on the project. Nas, the Grammy-winning, multi-platinum rapper, is creating new material for the production and expanding the film’s soundtrack. Beat Street was one of the first films to depict hip-hop culture, including breakdancing, mixing, scratching, and graffiti art. The film has been cited for its influence by such artists as Ice-T, Ice Cube, LL Cool J and Lin-Manuel Miranda, among many others. Related Stories News 'School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play' Broadway Review: When Escape Is Just A Clique Away Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Williams will direct the musical, with Diaz writing the show’s book, based upon the MGM Motion Picture. Webb (Broadway’s Choir Boy, MJ: The Musical and the upcoming Purple Rain ) joins the team as music supervisor, arranger, and orchestrator. Watch on Deadline Last month, Nas, Williams, Diaz and Webb collaborated on a 29-hour workshop to develop the stage adaptation. Further details concerning casting and production timeline will be announced in the coming months. Set in the early 1980s, Beat Street revolves around a group of aspiring young talents in the South Bronx, including a graffiti artist, a DJ, and a break-dancer, as they pursue their dreams in the emerging hip-hop scene while facing the challenges of urban life. The film was also notable for appearances by major artists of the era, including Doug E. Fresh, DJ Kool Herc, Afrika Bambataa & The Sonic Force, Us Girls, The Treacherous Three, Magnificent Force, The New York City Breakers, Rock Steady Crew, and Grandmaster Melle Mel & The Furious Five, among others. It was produced by Harry Belafonte and David V. Picker, with music by Belafonte and Arthur Baker, story by Steven Hager, screenplay by Andrew Davis, David Gilbert & Paul Golding, and directed by Stan Lathan, Beat Street starred Rae Dawn Chong, Gus Davis, and Jon Chardiet. Beat Street on Broadway will be produced by Richard Fearn, Arthur Baker, Michael Holman, and Peter Bittenbender, in association with Mass Appeal. Baker and Holman were producers on the original 1984 film. The wildly successful Beat Street soundtrack, released in two volumes, was produced by Baker, with Volume One cited as one of the first rap albums to be certified gold. ShowTown Theatricals will serve as General Managers. Nathan Gehan and Jamison Scott of ShowTown Productions are executive producers of Beat Street. articles.title: Oscar Nominee Michael Shannon & Jason Narducy Reveal 2027 Tour Dates, Playing R.E.M. Classic ‘Document’ In Full
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Erik Pedersen Erik Pedersen Managing Editor More Stories By Erik Oscar Nominee Michael Shannon & Jason Narducy Reveal 2027 Tour Dates, Playing R.E.M. Classic ‘Document’ In Full ASIFA-Showcase Set For November, New FYC Event From Annie Awards Group 2026 Premiere Dates For New & Returning Series On Broadcast, Streaming & Cable View All September 29, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Michael Shannon, left, and Jason Narducy onstage Hard to believe it was 15 years ago last week that R.E.M. called it a career, but fans can re-live the group’s pre-breakout fifth album played in its entirety next year. Oscar nominee Michael Shannon , Jason Narducy and their band are hitting the road again in 2027 to track one of the revered American group’s albums all the way through for its 40th anniversary. Next year’s model is Document, which featured the breakthrough single “The One I Love” and iconoclastic classic “It’s the End of the World as We Know It (And I Feel Fine).” Related Stories News R.E.M. Plays First Public Performance In Years At Songwriters Hall Of Fame Induction MTV VMAs 2026 Red Carpet: Taylor Swift, Lisa, Sombr, Charli XCX & More Running from February 3-May 15, the 2027 jaunt spans 27 dates — five more than last year — across 23 cities. Check out the tour schedule below. After running through Murmurs in 2023 and Fables of the Reconstruction and Lifes Rich Pageant the past two years, Shannon, Narducy and company are tackling the first R.E.M. to make the Top 10 and to be certified platinum. Along with its aforementioned two most famous cuts, Document features such often-overlooked gems as “Finest Worksong,” “Oddfellows Local 151,” “Disturbance at the Heron House” and the ever-relevant “Welcome to the Occupation” and “Exhuming McCarthy.” Watch on Deadline The group also will perform many other R.E.M. songs, usually close to 30 each night. “This is the album that introduced me to the band,” Shannon said of Document aka R.E.M. No. 5 , which made Rolling Stone ‘s 2003 list of 500 Greatest Albums of All Time. “If you had told me when I was a kid that some day Iʼd get up on stage and perform it, I wouldnʼt be able to comprehend, probably even believe, that. … Feels like it was recorded yesterday to address the calamity of tomorrow.” Shannon has scored two Supporting Actor Oscar nominations — for 2016’s Nocturnal Animals and 2008’s Revolutionary Road — and a 2023 Emmy nom for his lead role as George Jones in George & Tammy. He also won a pair of Actor Awards (then SAG Awards) for HBO’s Boardwalk Empire. His acting chops are on display when he inhabits R.E.M. frontman Michael Stipe onstage, replicating his singular voice and captivating mannerisms and quirks. Narducy has played with such acts as Bob Mould, Supoerchunk and Sunny Day Real Estate. They’ll be joined on tour by Jon Wurster (drums), John Stirratt (bass), Dag Juhlin (guitar) and Vijay Tellis-Nayak (keyboards). The 2026 tour saw Stipe sing with Shannon and Narducy’s group in Brooklyn and guitarist Peter Buck and bassist Mike Mills join for two shows in R.E.M.’s hometown of Athens, GA. articles.title: ‘The One About Matthew Perry’ Intimate Docuseries Gets Netflix Premiere Date, Trailer
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘The One About Matthew Perry’ Intimate Docuseries Gets Netflix Premiere Date, Trailer Broadway-Bound ‘Beat Street’ Musical From Grammy-Winning Rapper Nas Assembles Creative Team ‘School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play’ Broadway Review: When Escape Is Just A Clique Away View All September 29, 2026 7:12am Add us as a Google Preferred Source In the new trailer for Netflix The One About Matthew Perry , the late Friends star reflects on his TV success and the toll it took. In a voiceover early in the clip, Perry says, “I said God, you can do anything you want to me just please make me famous.” When fame arrived, Perry reflected, “God did not forget the other part.” The three-episode series, described by Netflix as “an intimate documentary series exploring the life and legacy of Matthew Perry,” premieres globally on the streamer October 27. Check out the trailer above. Directed by Mary Robertson, the docuseries features interviews with Perry’s family and friends, including sister Mia Perry Bowick, close friends David Pressman and Roger Castillo, former NBC President Warren Littlefield and others who knew or worked with the late Friends star. Related Stories Casting Netflix's 'Women Like Us' Adds Nine To Cast Casting Lindsay Lohan & Henry Golding To Lead Netflix Romantic Feature 'Return To You' From Director Mark Waters The two-minute trailer chronicles Perry’s experience with fame and the realization that it was not actually everything he wanted. Using testimonies from his sister Mia Perry Bowick, several other close friends and unreleased photos and videos from the Perry family’s private archive, the three-part series explores his career as a beloved actor and comedian while also revealing details about his long-term struggle with drug use and his attempts to get sober (he spent more than $7 million in those efforts, the doc says). Watch on Deadline The release of the film comes on the third anniversary of Perry’s death. In a statement accompanying the Netflix premiere date announcement, Perry’s sister said, “It’s taken time for me to feel ready to share these memories and what it was like to love Matthew through all the complexity of his life—to see him as a whole person, not just as Chandler, and not just as someone who struggled with addiction. As his sister, he shaped who I am today, the person I strive to be, and the work to which I’ve devoted my life. “Matthew had a beautiful heart,” she continues, “and a generous spirit, and even in his darkest moments, he could still make you laugh and feel loved. I hope this series gives everyone who loved him, whether personally or from afar, a deeper appreciation for who he truly was, and the legacy he leaves behind.” “Matthew Perry was one of the comedic geniuses of our time,” said director Robertson. “Through his many films, TV and stage performances, and his unforgettable portrayal of Chandler Bing, he made millions of us laugh, connect, and feel a little less alone. He also gave us so much more by bravely speaking about addiction. Yet the public only knew part of his story. That’s why we set out to make this film: to let the people who knew and loved Matthew reveal the person behind the public figure.” Netflix’s The One About Matthew Perry is executive produced by Mary Robertson, Lisa Kalikow, Eli Holzman and Aaron Saidman; co-executive produced by Lora Moftah; and produced by Jessica Call. Maxine Productions, a part of Sony Pictures Television, is the production company. Check out the trailer above. articles.title: ABC News’ Will Reeve Shares Story Of Undergoing Treatment For Testicular Cancer
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted CNN, MS NOW And Politico Warn That Trump Will “Reinstitute A Complete Ban” Without Judge’s Injunction: “An Injury On All News Media” Federal Film & TV Tax Credit Bill Adds Eight New Senate Co-Sponsors White House Defends Using Taxpayer Money To Run Trump Ad — Even Though It’s Nearly The Same As 2024 Campaign Spot View All September 29, 2026 7:18am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Will Reeve Photo by Maya Dehlin Spach/Getty Images ABC News correspondent Will Reeve said that he was diagnosed with testicular cancer earlier this year and undergoing treatment through the summer. Reeve, 34, and his wife Amanda appeared on Good Morning America on Tuesday to talk about what happened. “Right off the top, I need everyone to know, I am okay,” Reeve said, surrounded by the show’s co-hosts and other contributors. He said that the diagnosis was a “shock,” and the treatments were a “slog,” but “today, I am relieved to announce that we have arrived at our destination, and this cancer is in the rearview mirror.” Related Stories News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Say White House Continues To Deny Access To Some Staffers Even After Judge's Order; Outlets Seek New Hearing News Trump Ban Temporarily Blocked By Judge, Who Orders CNN, Politico & MS NOW Credentials Restored Reeve is the son of Christopher Reeve and Dana Reeve. His father died in 2004, nearly ten years after he was paralyzed in an equestrian accident. His mother died of lung cancer in 2006. Watch on Deadline On GMA , Reeve shared a segment where he detailed diagnosis and treatment, including a conversation with his oncologist. After he discovered a lump in his left testicle, he sought a doctor’s evaluation, and it was removed in a surgery in early May. He was later diagnosed with an aggressive form of testicular cancer. He underwent a second surgery and then two cycles of chemotherapy at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York. In July, he rang the bell at the cancer center to mark the end of his treatment. “I can proudly say that at this moment, I don’t currently have any cancer,” he said. He said that he shared his story to raise awareness. He said, “Don’t be scared. This is not an epidemic. It is a rare cancer, but you should go get yourself checked. If you feel something wrong, say something about it. Go to the doctor, report your change and you will end up okay, almost always.” At UK Event, Bosses At Amazon & BBC Back Artificial Intelligence Woos Investors With $44B Debt Offer To Fund Merger; Dems Vs. articles.title: Sister Boss Predicts “Premium” TV Talent & Drama Will “End Up On YouTube Or TikTok”

Featherstone, whose credits include Black Doves, The Split and Chernobyl, said the funding model for premium drama on TV isn’t going anywhere for the time being, but she anticipates big changes in the medium to long term. “Talent is like water, they will find the shortest way to the audience past all obstacles and our job is to make sure we’re on top of where audiences are,” Featherstone told the RTS London Convention. “Talent wants legitimacy and audience on main channels. She was speaking to one of the biggest talking points in the TV industry today on a panel at the RTS Convention alongside the likes of Expectation CEO Tim Hincks, whose firm makes Clarkson’s Farm. Also looking to the future, Hincks predicted the UK TV industry’s terms of trade, which have been a financial bedrock for UK production companies for more than two decades, are “not long for this world.” He stressed that indies will survive, adding: “There are lots of great independently minded people who have authority issues and have a burning desire to not be in a meeting for three hours where at the end of it someone says, ‘Shall we have a meeting about this?’.” The producers were speaking at the same event as head honchos from Amazon, the BBC and Channel 4, along with talent like Jeremy Clarkson. articles.title: Lauren Cohan & Jake Epstein To Co-Star In Eric Stoltz-Directed Rom-Com ‘Both Sides Now’
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow , Andreas Wiseman September 29, 2026 7:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lauren Cohan, Jake Epstein Sam Jones, Elana Emer EXCLUSIVE: The Walking Dead star Lauren Cohan and Jake Epstein ( Degrassi: The Next Generation ) are set to lead the ensemble cast of working-titled indie romantic comedy Both Sides Now . Actor and director Eric Stoltz ( Madam Secretary , Nashville ) is directing from a screenplay by Hailey Lustig, founder of Three Birds Landing Productions, and composer Robbie Roth, which takes inspiration from their real lives. The ensemble cast also features Erich Bergen ( Love Story ), Justin Chatwin ( Shameless ) and Brian Norris ( The Cleaning Lady ). Related Stories News Canada's Precious Metal Productions & Black Fawn Distribution Strike Genre Slate Deal - TIFF News Quiver Distribution Takes U.S. For Jérémy Comte's Ghana & Canada-Set Drama 'Paradise' Both Sides Now follows a group of lifelong friends nearing 40 who return to the Jewish summer camp where they came of age to celebrate the impending wedding of Eddie (Epstein). Watch on Deadline But when his best friend Lloyd (Bergen) invites Eddie’s first love and former camp sweetheart Erin (Cohan) to the bachelor weekend, the reunion becomes a reckoning with old relationships, unresolved love and the question of what might have been. Co-writers Lustig and Roth were born in the same Toronto maternity ward on either side of midnight and grew up together at summer camp and have been best friends for decades. Their friendship and shared experience of summer camp helped inspire the characters, relationships and world of the film. The romantic comedy also features six original songs written by Roth and performed by the cast. “We’ve been making each other laugh and sharing music and stories for as long as we can remember. Writing this film together feels wonderfully full circle,” said Lustig and Roth. “We share a history and a shorthand that made the process incredibly natural, and seeing these characters come to life, with original music woven through the story, has been thrilling.” Stoltz said: “This script made me laugh, made me a bit nostalgic, and then caught me off guard emotionally – which is exactly what I love in a film. Hailey and Robbie have written something funny and deeply personal about friendship, first love, and the lives we choose for ourselves. Robbie’s songs are woven beautifully through that world.” Both Sides Now is independently financed by Three Birds Landing Productions and marks the company’s debut feature film. The film is produced by Lustig, Carrie Mudd and Erin Berry, in association with Peacock Alley Entertainment. Production began September 19 in Muskoka, Ontario, and is scheduled to wrap October 20. Maridueña will assume the role of Juan De Marcos through Sunday, January 3, 2027, at Broadway’s Schoenfeld Theatre. “I’m honored to be making my Broadway debut with the incredibly talented team at Buena Vista Social Club ,” said Maridueña. “Broadway has always been a dream, but getting to make that dream come true while being part of such an important and beautiful story feels like hitting the lottery twice. L.A.’s V10 Entertainment is gearing up for the TV content confab by adding a trio of veteran sellers to its ranks. Michelle Payne, Matt Vassallo and Poh Lin Ho will be in Cannes with the America’s Funniest Home Videos seller in strategic partner roles. Payne is based out of London and will lead sales in EMEA. With decades of experience in TV sales, she was most recently a consultant for Fox while it was building its international distribution arm. Prior to that, was a Senior VP at Paramount predecessor ViacomCBS, where she oversaw sales in EMEA. Related Stories News Tony Robinson 'Rewrites History' With Debuting Radar Studios Executives Noel Hedges Joins Boat Rocker Studios In Global Acquisitions Role Vassallo, who works out of L.A., has been in TV distribution, acquisitions and co-production for 15 years. He was most recently Head of Series Acquisitions & Distribution Strategy at Amazon MGM Studios Distribution, leading series acquisitions and developing the go-to-market strategy for Amazon MGM Studios content. He also worked as EVP of International Distribution at MGM Studios, prior to its acquisition by Amazon. Watch on Deadline Ho has worked as a senior media exec for more than 35 years in areas such as acquisition, regional syndication, and media investment. She was at Malaysian content group Vision Plus Entertainment for well over three decades before exiting her CEO post in 2023. Since then, she has operated independently. V10 will be in Cannes with the likes of America’s Funniest Videos , America’s Funniest People , Hooligans: The ARCH Racing Project with Keanu Reeves and Gard Hollinger and MotoAmerica’s live races. Samantha Cooper and Josh Vodnoy, V10’s co-Heads of Global Licensing and Distribution continue to lead the sales operation. “As V10 continues to expand its footprint across every major market, we’re bringing on world-class executives who understand the nuances of local audiences and platforms,” said Cooper. “This global buildout allows us to maximize the reach of our flagship properties like Hooligans with Keanu Reeves and Gard Hollinger, to live MotoAmerica races, to AFV with Alfonso Ribiero — all while unlocking new territories for our clip show formats.” Vodnoy added the hires “accelerate” V10’s efforts ahead of MIPCOM, which begins in under two weeks. “We look forward to leveraging our strategic partners to champion our IP internationally, expand our reach into new territories, and build lasting opportunities for our content in key markets,” he said. Having been founded in 2022, V10 comprises companies such as Venture 10 Studio Group, Fishbowl Media, America’s Funniest Home Videos maker Vin Di Bona Productions and Clip Tiger. It has a comedy content library of more than 3.1 million digital assets and produces over 250 hours a year for 44 owned and operated FAST and digital channels. In April last year, V10 acquired the digital rights management and production company, Towerhouse. articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Creator Business Motion Society Hires Ex-Spotify, Meta & Fullscreen Exec Chanel Simmons To Lead U.S. Operation V10 Entertainment Gears Up For MIPCOM By Tieing With Former Paramount, Amazon MGM Studios & Vision Plus Execs Paramount+ Buys British A24 Series ‘It Gets Worse’, ‘Major Players’ & ‘The Ministry Of Time’ View All September 29, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Chanel Simmons Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Creator economy business Motion Society has named former Spotify, Meta and Fullscreen exec Chanel Simmons as its new U.S. boss. She will become Managing Director, U.S., at the company, which works with around 650 creators and distributes more than 30,000 videos on streaming and digital platforms each month for the likes of Jesser, Stephen Sharer and Lizzy Capri. Simmons has worked in the creator economy for more than a decade at the likes of digital channels business Fullscreen, Meta and Spotify. At the former, she led on YouTube syndication and then worked on FaZe Clan’s owned channels business and 50-strong creator roster. Related Stories News Samsung TV Plus Strikes Creator Channel Deals With Fearne Cotton & More; Expands Mark Rober Reach Agencies The Sidemen Rep Arcade Signs Max Fosh, Friends From Work & More Ahead Of Europe's First Creator Upfront She later moved to Meta and then to Spotify, where she worked on digital culture content partnerships, onboarding creators and helping creator service providers to expand their YouTube video programming to Spotify. Watch on Deadline At Motion Society, she’ll be overseeing business growth in the U.S. for an operation that tests ideas to determine where a piece of content has the best opportunity to cut through. It uses a proprietary operating system to speed up workflows for its 50+ staff. This, in theory, gives them more time to work on creative and strategic plans for Motion Society’s creator partners. The company uses performance data from platforms to inform its OS, allowing staff to see how thousands of videos have performed on each platform. “During my time at Spotify, Motion Society consistently stood out,” said Simmons. “The team understood the needs of both creators and platforms and came to us with a deeply informed point of view on how creator content could succeed on Spotify. What impressed me most was the combination of strong creatives, platform expertise and the technology they built that allows their team to focus more time on strategy and the content itself.” Motion Society was founded in 2022 by Martin Belotti, the creator of LADB Restoration; Thomas Subra, who is CEO; COO Jean-Loup Fraudin; and CPO and engineer Lucas Falga. Subra, Fraudin and Falga left careers in finance and engineering to build the company with Belotti, and together they later raised seed funding to develop the proprietary operating system that has underpinned their business. “Motion Society was inspired by a problem I ran into while growing my own channel,” said Belotti. “Even as I reached more than one million subscribers, I was still mostly operating it on my own. I could see more value in the content I had already made, but expanding it across platforms required the time and expertise I didn’t have. I wasn’t willing to give up quality and control of the content just to grow. So we set out to build the partner I had been looking for.” At UK Event, Bosses At Amazon & BBC Back Artificial Intelligence Woos Investors With $44B Debt Offer To Fund Merger; Dems Vs. articles.title: Sky Confirms Plans To Showcase Series Like ‘The Day Of The Jackal’ On ITV After Takeover
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Jeremy Clarkson Working On “Unbelievably Ambitious” Show Amid Uncertainty Over ‘Clarkson’s Farm’ Future Channel 4 CEO Priya Dogra Open To Putting Shows On BBC iPlayer — Just Don’t Mention A Merger Sony Chief Wayne Garvie: “It’s Very Difficult To See How Channel 4 Survives In Present Form” View All September 29, 2026 8:23am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Day of the Jackal' SkyShowtime The Day of the Jackal and Brassic could be coming to free-to-air television in the UK after Sky completes its £1.6 billion ($2.1 billion) takeover of ITV ‘s network operations. Cécile Frot-Coutaz, Sky’s content chief and the CEO of Sky Studios , has said that the Comcast-owned company wants to experiment with windowing its original series on ITV over the coming years. Frot-Coutaz’s comments, which were made at the Royal Television Society London Convention on Tuesday, confirm Deadline’s report in July about Sky’s plans to give original series airtime on its new asset . Related Stories News Sister Boss Predicts "Premium" TV Talent & Drama Will "End Up On YouTube Or TikTok" News Jeremy Clarkson Working On "Unbelievably Ambitious" Show Amid Uncertainty Over 'Clarkson's Farm' Future Frot-Coutaz said Sky would look at showcasing old seasons of a show like The Day of the Jackal on ITV ahead of a new season launching. “There’s various permutations,” she said. Watch on Deadline The former Fremantle executive said Sky previously experimented with a similar windowing strategy when it put the first four seasons of Brassic on Netflix. “We saw that we had been able to find some new headroom [in viewing] because we’d exposed the show to an audience that we didn’t have,” she said. Frot-Coutaz added that Sky will also look closely at putting sport on ITV, opening up the possibility that Premier League football could get free-to-air exposure. She explained: “We have 40,000 hours of sports. So within that, there’s also huge opportunities in terms of putting more sports on free-to-air. We think everybody wins from that. The viewer wins, but also the leagues win.” Earlier in the day, ITV CEO Carolyn McCall said the company had little choice but to sell to Sky because the “competition is ferocious.” As part of the takeover, Sky has agreed a £2.1 billion output deal with ITV Studios, which will guarantee that shows like Love Island and Coronation Street will remain on ITV until 2032. Asked if Sky could rip up this deal in six years, McCall responded: “Good luck.” She added that, if anything, Sky will start commissioning more from ITV Studios, which will remain independent and listed on the London Stock Exchange. articles.title: ‘Rose’ Trailer: Watch a First Look at Sandra Hüller’s Next Must-See Performance (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By David Canfield Plus Icon David Canfield Senior Entertainment Writer View All September 28, 2026 5:00am 'Rose' The Match Factory/Courtesy Everett Collection In their conversations leading up to the making of Rose , star Sandra Hüller and director Markus Schleinzer worked hard at fine-tuning their eponymous 17th-century hero. Hüller was to play a woman disguising herself as a male soldier in the aftermath of the Thirty Years’ War, ingratiating herself in a small Protestant village. She considered preparation routines like strength training, before setting them aside as anachronistic; she agonized over keeping things as believable as possible. “She was wondering, ‘What should I do with my voice — should I lower it?’” Schleinzer recalls. “Then we started to laugh because then we found out that my voice, as a man, is higher than her voice as a woman. It would be a weird thing for her, to lower her voice to pretend to be a man, for a male director who has a much higher voice than hers.” Related Stories Movies 'Avengers: Endgame' Powers $26M Return at Crowded Box Office Movies Phil Lord and Chris Miller Tapped as Guest Artistic Directors for AFI Fest 2026 The anecdote offers some amusing insight into the dynamic between Schleinzer and Hüller, which remained deeply playful and collaborative over the years it took to get Rose made. Yet it also speaks to the ultimate mastery of Hüller’s portrayal here, which never goes for the easy or obvious choice. In a career full of decorated performances, this ranks among Hüller’s very best, a moving, wondrously strange embodiment of a survivor in constant, subtle hiding. Below, you can watch the exclusive trailer for the film for a first look. Rose premiered at the Berlin Film Festival in February, where Hüller won the Silver Bear for best lead performance. The star then went on to receive a Tribute Medallion in Telluride earlier this month, where the movie made its North American premiere; now, it’s making the rounds in New York. “ Rose is another extraordinary showcase for her gifts and a master class in the art of acting with rigor, honesty, physicality and zero showiness,” wrote THR chief film critic David Rooney of Hüller in his review . Schleinzer first had the idea for Rose on his birthday, when a friend told him that 250 years ago to the day, a woman had been executed for being caught living her life as a man. The Austrian filmmaker and former casting director, who came up under the legendary Michael Haneke, became obsessed with the story and researched hundreds of other examples, from decades before and after. He saw them speaking to the current climate of fear felt by various marginalized communities. “Every life, every day is a political act — so we cannot hide,” says Schleinzer, who is queer. “We have to change things if we want to have a better life as a community.” Already at work on the script, Schleinzer then met Hüller on the set of the 2023 German black comedy Sisi & I — as her co-star. “I was really bad in this movie because I was so keen to watch Sandra firsthand — I already had started writing Rose and started stalking her, watching all the things she was ever in, even the tiny television spots she had at the beginning of her career.” He later sent her the script, which was written in prose, more akin to a novel; she jumped at the challenge. Sandra Hüller in Rose . The Match Factory/Courtesy Everett Collection When asked what surprised him about Hüller’s approach to the role, Schleinzer points to a viral red-carpet clip of the star describing her process in straightforward terms — “I really have to disappoint you, it’s not so much: I learned the lines” — in noting that what results from that is anything but simple. “I was a casting director for 17 years and I always had the feeling that my main job was to get people out of being afraid, of having fear or discomfort — there is this type of actor who loves to talk, because talking means that they do not have to act, they can just talk, talk, talk, talk,” the director says. “Sandra is the complete opposite. She is someone who gets easily bored, so no take is the same: ‘Now I’ll become a little more boyish,’ ‘Now I’m the soldier.’ I had the big problem of choosing how to build up a character for the audience, then — but this was surprising, to see such life come alive in front of your eyes on the set every day.” Shot on location near the East German border with original sets, scouted by Schleinzer through hours of hiking, the film boasts a handmade quality in Gerald Kerkletz’s black-and-white cinematography, the exacting makeup and costume work and the dry humor that allows the absurdity of certain situations to breathe — even as Rose hurtles toward profound tragedy. “My intention was to make something more about these days we are in than just a museum piece with some nostalgic images,” Schleinzer says. Rose premiered this past weekend to more raves at the New York Film Festival, and will be released in North American theaters by Mubi on Dec. 11. The project started shooting less than two weeks after the end of Hüller’s campaign for Anatomy of a Fall , which netted her a best-actress Oscar nomination — and shot in small increments over many months from there. This could be the project that brings her back to the Oscars, although her greatest competition may be herself: She’s also terrific as the lead of Cannes -winner Fatherland , also a Mubi release, and plays key supporting roles in Project Hail Mary and Digger . But within the scope of Hüller’s filmography — really, any actor’s — Rose feels special. “Sandra said I should not threaten people, but I have watched her career for the last 20 years and I’ve seen so many prizes taken away from her,” Schleinzer says with a grin. “If she’s not going to be nominated for this one, I’m going berserk.” Check out the official poster below.
