articles.title: Streaming & Local Film Propel Major Asian Markets To $15B Content Spend This Year – MPA
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Streaming & Local Film Propel Major Asian Markets To $15B Content Spend This Year – MPA Samsung TV Plus Strikes Creator Channel Deals With Fearne Cotton & More; Expand Mark Rober Reach Independent Talent Group Buys Into Sports Agency Tongue Tied Management View All September 24, 2026 2:03am 'Paatal Lok' Prime Video Streaming and local film are set to send spend on content in seven major Asian markets over the $15B mark this year, according to a study. Media Partners Asia (MPA) reports that content investment will rise from $14.8B in 2025 to $15.1B this year and on to $15.4B in 2031. While TV currently accounting for 60% of the spend, followed by online video at 30% and film at 10%, MPA’s ‘Asia Video Content Dynamics 2026’ report noted “virtually all incremental growth comes from streaming and film as television budgets decline.” Related Stories News Korean Bestselling Thriller 'The Kidnapping Day' Set For Arabic-Language Movie Adaptation News Audiences Flocking To Anime On Netflix At 10 Times The Rate Of Other Genres, Report Reveals The report assessed spend in India , Indonesia , Korea , Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam , with key findings being that while Asian video industries command large audiences and have valuable brands, this is not always “converting into attractive financial returns” and many “established media companies” are trading “well below equity book value.” MPA is predicting those that spend wisely, rationalize costs and protect “genuine content advantages” will “increasingly separate” those that don’t. Watch on Deadline Within the $14.8B figure from 2025, Korea accounts for $6.9B, with India second at $5B, which is approximately 80% of the total. MPA noted streaming has overtaken TV in India with online video accounting for 46% of content investment in 2025, compared to 42% in television. Indian audiences streamed 420 billion hours last year, with JioHotstar leading the way with a 58% of the premium VOD viewing. Sports is driving demand, with JioHotstar experiencing a boost in reach during the IPL cricket season. In Korea, Netflix leads the way with domestic streamer TVING a clear second, while Indonesia’s Vidio, which has been profitable since the fourth quarter of last year, leading that market with six million paying subs. TVING’s extensive baseball rights helped expand its subs base from 5.3 million to 6.5 million, according to MPA. Local film represents “the region’s clearest growth opportunity,” MPA added. This was evidenced by Vietnam’s box office rising 20% to $213M in 2025 with local titles accounting for 69%. There were similar figures in Indonesia, while India posted a record box office total of $1.41B, and local titles were attributed for a “substantial theatrical recovery” in Korea this year. TV advertising, on the other hand, fell, with MPA suggesting “several television industries still carry more legacy capacity than their advertising economics can support.” Stephen Laslocky, Vice President, MPA, said: “Asia’s video industries are not short of audiences or creative capability. They are short of structures that convert both into sustainable returns. As the margin for error narrows, management quality will become decisive. Companies that rationalise legacy costs through restructuring and the adoption of new technologies such as AI, collaborate where independent investment no longer makes sense and protect the content that gives viewers a reason to stay will increasingly outperform, and the valuation gap between winners and losers will widen.” Another MPA analyst Myat Pan Phyu (May), added: “The viewership data shows demand is intact. Premium VOD engagement continues to grow across India, Korea and Southeast Asia, streaming now leads content investment in India, and local stories are winning at the box office from Hanoi to Jakarta and Mumbai. This is a story of reallocation rather than retreat as capital moves toward streaming and local film, where both audiences and returns are growing.” 150 Tech Roles Set To Go; TV & Radio Network Closures Expected Next Week Trump Ban Temporarily Blocked; CNN Credentials Restored Key Asian Markets Set For $15B Content Spend In 2026 – Study HBO’s Bloys, Par’s Cheeks Fuel Merger Intrigue With Joint Appearance At ‘War’ Premiere Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Paramount UK’s 5 Launches Linear Drama Network With ‘All Creatures Great And Small’, ‘Gilmore Girls’ & ‘Home And Away’ Plus BBC Drama ‘Waterloo Road’

Replacing the 5Select channel, 5Drama will launch October 21 with a collection of 5 originals, American imports and Australian series including popular soap Home and Away. British drama will air at peak times in the evening including originals like 5’s smash All Creatures Great and Small reboot, which airs on PBS Masterpiece in the U.S., while weekday afternoons will be dedicated to U.S. shows like Gilmore Girls , Columbo and ABC’s A Million Little Things . Home and Away will start from ep 1 in the afternoons. Related Stories Executives Sturm Und Drang At Warner Bros Amid Paramount Merger Has Insiders Wondering If The Brand Survives Executives HBO's Casey Bloys & Par's George Cheeks Go To 'War' Together: Execs' Joint Premiere Appearance Creates Intrigue With WBD Merger Closing Intriguingly, the new channel also has rights to the first 10 seasons of long-running BBC school series Waterloo Road , seasons that aired between 2006 and 2014 before it was rebooted in 2023. Watch on Deadline 5Drama joins a Paramount UK linear roster including the main 5 channel, 5Action, 5Star and 5USA. Launching a linear channel may feel anachronistic and comes at a time when the BBC is set to close at least one but under maverick content chief Ben Frow, 5 has leaned in to linear. It is the only network to have grown linear share over the past few years and regularly beats rivals Channel 4 and BBC Two in the overnights. The news comes in the week that Paramount-Warner’s $110B deal terms included divestiture targets for American linear networks like BET, VH1 and Comedy Central. In the UK, David Ellison recently committed to £80M ($105M) of additional 5 investment over three years as a means of getting the deal past the regulators, along with committing to 5’s public broadcasting remit. 5 boss Reemah Sakaan said: “Award winning drama is increasingly at the heart of what 5 offers viewers, so it’s the right time to give it a dedicated home. articles.title: The Guardian To Offer ‘NAZA’ For Free On Website After Theatrical Run & Is Exploring Ways To Show Doc In Israel & Palestinian Territories
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie The Guardian To Offer ‘NAZA’ For Free On Website After Theatrical Run & Is Exploring Ways To Show Doc In Israel & Palestinian Territories ‘Maserati: The Brothers’ Actress Maya Talem Signs With MAD Celebrity ‘Ray Gunn’ Trailer: Netflix Adds Limited Theatrical Release For Brad Bird’s Sam Rockwell & Scarlett Johansson-Voiced Animated Sci-Fi View All September 24, 2026 3:34am Filmmaker Yuval Abraham (right) interviews a source in 'NAZA' The Guardian/JW Films The Guardian and mk2 films have announced global release plans for Israeli directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor ’s bombshell documentary NAZA . The partners said that The Guardian-produced documentary will be released theatrically from September 28 onwards in more than 50 territories, having secured theatrical distributors in 56 territories since its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival on September 10, where it went on to win the Special Jury Prize. In an unprecedented move, The Guardian will make NAZA available for global audiences for free on its website, after the theatrical run later this fall. The partners said the move was due to the “worldwide interest” in the documentary as well as The Guardian’s “commitment to fearless, independent journalism”. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'On Standby' Renewed For Season 2 At Israel's Yes News 'Thirteen In Gaza' Trailer: Father & Daughter Tale Shot In Devastated Palestinian Territory Won NETPAC Award At TIFF The investigative documentary, exposing the Israeli military ‘s calculated targeting of civilians in Gaza in missile strikes through the testimony of intelligence personnel and soldiers involved in the killing, has caused a sensation since its Venice debut. It landed a record 25-minute ovation its Venice premiere Film , but has since been attacked by Israeli politicians including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has threatened to strip the directors of their Israeli citizenship even though he has no power to do this under the country’s laws. The Guardian and mk2 said the film has been offered to a number of distributors and cinemas in Israel , and they will be exploring other ways to enable the film to be seen in the occupied Palestinian territories. They added that, as previously announced, the film will receive its North American premiere on 26 September at New York Film Festival, and will open in U.S. theaters on September 30, launching exclusively at the IFC Center in New York City. It will expand to Los Angeles and other key markets on October 9, ahead of a national roll out in the weeks to follow. NAZA is produced by The Guardian and James Wilson (JW Films); and executive produced by Oscar-winning filmmaker Jonathan Glazer. The documentary builds on a series of revelations first published by the Guardian, +972 Magazine, a Israeli-Palestinian publication, and Hebrew-language outlet, Local Call between 2023-2025, including groundbreaking investigations into how Israel uses AI to identify targets in Gaza. It follows Abraham and Szor’s No Other Land , winner of the Best Documentary Academy Award in 2025. Co-directed with Palestinian filmmakers Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal, it documented Israeli army-backed efforts to erase the West Bank Palestinian villages of Masafer Yatta, while painting a wider picture of Israeli occupation. “We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israelis to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible,” said Abraham and Szor in a joint statement as the NAZA release plans were unveiled. “The threats from the Israeli government to revoke our citizenship and the death threats do not change that and will not stop the film. We thank our colleagues for the solidarity and look forward to sharing NAZA all over the world very soon.” Harry Davies, a Guardian investigations correspondent and one of NAZA’s producers, added: “ NAZA is grounded in rigorous journalism published over the past three years, but it is also a powerful piece of cinema that will soon be available on screens, large and small, around the world.” “The initial response from those who’ve seen it shows audiences are engaging deeply with the urgent questions the film raises. We’re working with MK2 and international partners to bring the film to global audiences as soon as possible.” The 56 territories sold by Paris-based mk2 film, which boarded international sales on the documentary ahead of its Venice premiere, include France, UK, Italy, Spain, Germany, Belgium, Netherlands, Austria, Switzerland, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Greece, Portugal, Poland, Lithuania, Romania, Bulgaria, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Thailand, Canada, Brazil, Turkey, Central America, and the Middle East. 150 Tech Roles Set To Go; TV & Radio Network Closures Expected Next Week Trump Ban Temporarily Blocked; CNN Credentials Restored Key Asian Markets Set For $15B Content Spend In 2026 – Study HBO’s Bloys, Par’s Cheeks Fuel Merger Intrigue With Joint Appearance At ‘War’ Premiere Read More About: Comments

articles.title: BBC Cuts Latest: Around 150 Tech Staff Expected To Take Voluntary Redundancy, Saving Millions
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BBC Cuts Latest: Around 150 Tech Staff Expected To Take Voluntary Redundancy, Saving Millions BBC Expected To Announce TV & Radio Network Closures Next Week ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Writer Defends Amazon Movie Amid Outcry Over Sacha Baron Cohen’s Character Reinforcing “Harmful” Racial Stereotypes View All September 24, 2026 4:41am BBC iPlayer BBC EXCLUSIVE : The drumbeat of BBC cuts continues, with Deadline hearing that roughly 4% of the British broadcaster’s technology unit is expected to take voluntary redundancy. Around 151 employees are set to exit BBC Media Tech, the unit that helps power online services including iPlayer and BBC Sounds. The voluntary redundancies are expected to deliver savings of £14.5 million ($19.8M) over the coming years. Deadline understands that 11% of staff in BBC Media Tech applied for voluntary redundancy, but only 40% (the 151 figure) can be accepted. The department is set to announce other changes over the coming days, as the BBC reveals further details about its plan to cut 2,000 jobs and save £500M amid a funding crisis. Related Stories News On Eve Of Her First Convention, Royal Television Society Boss Sophie Jones Wants To Shout Louder About The "Powerhouse" UK Industry News BBC Expected To Announce TV & Radio Network Closures Next Week Deadline revealed on Wednesday that the BBC is expected to announce TV and radio network closures early next week, with speculation that BBC Three could be shut. Also on Wednesday, the BBC Sport unit told employees about plans to make redundancies and cut sports bulletins on its news channel. Watch on Deadline The BBC will also consider “bumping” roles in BBC Media Tech, meaning an employee can take voluntary redundancy, but another staff member facing compulsory redundancy can backfill the role. BBC technology teams have faced uncertainty over the past year amid the corporation drawing up radical plans to outsource thousands of non-content jobs to the private sector. The proposals, codenamed Project Ada , explored spinning off Media Tech into a potential commercial unit. Discussion about Project Ada has gone quiet since the arrival of Matt Brittin , the BBC’s new director general, and the exit of chief operating officer Leigh Tavaziva . The BBC’s £500M savings target expands on a previous goal worth £1.5 billion. The bigger picture behind the cuts is that 94% of the UK population use the BBC every month, but fewer than 80% pay the £180 annual licence fee. The BBC is attempting to bridge this gap. articles.title: CAPA Deputy Director Unveils Sean Connery Doc; Talks Mission To Expand French Company’s International Reach
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie The Guardian To Offer ‘NAZA’ For Free On Website After Theatrical Run & Is Exploring Ways To Show Doc In Israel & Palestinian Territories ‘Maserati: The Brothers’ Actress Maya Talem Signs With MAD Celebrity ‘Ray Gunn’ Trailer: Netflix Adds Limited Theatrical Release For Brad Bird’s Sam Rockwell & Scarlett Johansson-Voiced Animated Sci-Fi View All September 24, 2026 5:04am Sally Blake/Sean Connery with his wife artist Micheline Roquebrune at The Metropolitan Opera in 2006 Courtesy.Getty Images for The Metropolitan Opera EXCLUSIVE: A documentary promising unprecedented behind-the-scenes insight into the life of late Scottish star Sean Connery is in the works at Paris-based factual film and TV production company CAPA . Titled Sean Connery: The Untold Story , it is being developed and directed by French journalist and TV presenter Stéphanie Renouvin, who is the granddaughter of the James Bond star and his second wife, the French Moroccan painter Micheline Roquebrune. It follows Renouvin’s 2022 mini-series Mme Sean Connery , which focused on her grandmother and was made primarily for a French audience. Related Stories News French Film & TV Sectors Sound Alarm Over Cuts To State Broadcaster Budget; Say They Are At Odds With Macron's Lumière Summit Pledges Acquisitions Disney+ Seals EMEA Deal For Season 1 Of TF1 Hit 'Cat's Eyes' As Season 2 Gets October Launch Date Sean Connery: The Untold Story is one of the upcoming titles currently being developed by Sally Blake , the newly appointed Deputy Director of CAPA, which is part of the Studio TFI group. Watch on Deadline “We developed it here. It’s a coproduction with Canal Plus and Sky has come onboard in the UK,” says Blake, also citing London-based Embankment and Glasgow-based Boy 313 as coproducers. Blake, who was appointed to her new role in early September, will work closely with CAPA MD Patrice Lorton, with a mission to “internationalize” the company’s activities and specific goals to connect it with new territories and sources of funding. She says the upcoming Sean Connery documentary ticks the box of appealing to the company’s home audience in France as well as having wider international resonance. “Sean Connery is definitely universal while Stéphanie’s connection to the subject gives it a good anchor in France. That’s a perfect example of something that can speak across audiences,” she says, talking to Deadline just days after the announcement of her appointment. Career highlights & international mission The Canadian French documentary veteran has been working as a producer with CAPA since 2017. Documentary feature credits across her 20-year career include Su Rynard’s 2015 work The Messenger , exploring environmental threats to songbirds around the world, which she co-wrote, produced and edited. It premiered at Canada’s Hot Docs festival and was then acquired by Kino Lorber for the U.S. Under the CAPA umbrella, she was a producer on Ron Chapman’s Revival69: The Concert That Rocked the World, as well as Anastasia Trofimova’s Russians at War , which world premiered at the Venice Film Festival in 2024. More recent credits include the 2025 natural history two-parter 13 Hours to Survive , about how sea creatures tackle the challenge of being left high and dry by the tide, which played on Arte and Blue Ant Studio’s Love Nature platform; 2025 six-part, docu-series Marie Antoinette Confidential , coproduced with Banijay Studios France for Canal Plus, and TV docu-movie Tardigrade, the Indestructible Animal , which she also co-wrote. “I’ve been a producer with CAPA for a few years and was an independent producer previously, both in Canada and in France, so I have built up a big network for making international coproductions… the main reasons that they’ve given me this job is to push the international angle,” says Blake of her new role. “CAPA is the largest documentary production company in France. It’s really well known, really well established and producing for all the platforms and all the channels,” she continues. Blake cites true-crime series From Rock Star to Killer, about rock singer Bertrand Cantat, who killed his partner actress Marie Trintignant in 2003, and 2025 docu-drama November 13, Sonia’s Choice as examples of recent CAPA productions that have moved the dial in France. “ From a Rock Star to a Killer was a Netflix series which did really, really well. It was definitely in the top 10 of Netflix documentary series,” she says of the first title, which was released on the platform on March 2025. The two-part November 13, Sonia’s Choice recounts the true story of a woman at the heart of the hunt for the culprits of the Paris terror attacks on November 13, 2015, who is now living in hiding. It was broadcast in a primetime slot by state broadcaster France Télévisions on November 13, 2025, as part of its programming to mark the 10th anniversary of the attacks in which terrorists killed 130 people and injured many more across the French capital. “It was really interesting because it was an innovative hybrid film.” Blake says of the docu-drama, directed by David André and starring Carima Amarouche in the titular role. “Docu-drama is definitively one of the interesting areas we want to do more in. They’re working really well right now.” Blake believes strongly that the CAPA has the content, no-how and connections to expand its international footprint. “I think that the quality of the CAPA programming is something that could travel even more than it does now, and that’s something that I really, really want to make happen,” she says, adding that working with international partners is also becoming a necessity. “It’s something we all have to do right now when the industry is so difficult. We have to really, really look for those international partnerships and those ‘sneaky’ ways of financing things. You also need a sense of what’s out there, what the trends are, which is something I have, because I travel to all these markets quite a bit.” Alongside Sean Connery: The Untold Story, other upcoming CAPA productions that Blake feels have strong international potential include Compost . Being developed as a hybrid for the French market, it delves into the ecosystem and “drama” of a compost heap, exploring its inhabitants and the roles they play in breaking down food leftovers and garden refuse. “I have a long-standing experience in science, the environment and the natural world and of course that’s something that lends itself to international,” says Blake, citing titles such as 13 Hours to Survive. “I am currently working on a film, which is going to be primetime feature documentary for France Télévisions. The entire thing is going to be filmed in a compost heap… it will version and adapt very easily to other markets because composting, technically speaking, is something everyone can do,” she says. “It’s literally about the drama that happens inside a compost heap. Imagine the wooden boxes at the end of gardens, you open them up and it’s absolutely fascinating. It’s like a jungle in there with these tiny, tiny creatures. In the French version, the compost heap is in the back garden of a fictional family to give a human side to it, but the natural history part of the film can travel anywhere.” In the backdrop, Blake acknowledges it is a complex time for the documentary sector, with the genre making waves on the festival and awards circuit at the same as it faces funding squeezes. “There have been different waves. There was a contraction of the North American documentary market a few years ago that seems to have settled in the sense we know where we’re at right now. But recently, we’re seeing more and more crisis within public broadcasters in Europe. We’re definitely feeling that in France, but I think that’s happening all over,” she says. In spite of the challenges, Blake remains confident in the genre. “People are always looking for keys to decrypt the world, and the world is just getting scarier and more confusing, so I think there’s always going to be an interest in documentary.” 150 Tech Roles Set To Go; TV & Radio Network Closures Expected Next Week Trump Ban Temporarily Blocked; CNN Credentials Restored Key Asian Markets Set For $15B Content Spend In 2026 – Study HBO’s Bloys, Par’s Cheeks Fuel Merger Intrigue With Joint Appearance At ‘War’ Premiere Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Terence Winter To Adapt Jay Stratton’s ‘Out Of The Shadows’ Memoir About Investigating Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena As TV Series
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Terence Winter To Adapt Jay Stratton’s ‘Out Of The Shadows’ Memoir About Investigating Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena As TV Series HBO’s Casey Bloys & Par’s George Cheeks Go To ‘War’ Together: Execs’ Joint Premiere Appearance Creates Intrigue With WBD Merger Closing ‘A Man On The Inside’ To End With Season 3; Netflix Comedy Starring Ted Danson Sets Returning Cast, Guest Stars & New Mystery As Production Starts View All September 24, 2026 6:00am Terence Winter ( Boardwalk Empire, Tulsa King ) is set to develop a TV series based on the upcoming memoir by former senior U.S. intelligence official Jay Stratton , the central figure in the U.S. Government’s modern investigation of unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) and non-human intelligent life. Winter has partnered on the project with Dan Farah , director/producer of the recent UAP documentary The Age of Disclosure, who had acquired the film and TV rights to the book. As the Chief of Air & Space Warfare in the Defense Warning Office of the Defense Intelligence Agency, Stratton specialized in emerging and disruptive aerospace technologies, ultimately focusing on investigating UAP. Related Stories Books Jay Stratton, Former Director Of U.S Government's Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force, Unveils Title & Release Date For William Morrow Memoir Documentary Oscar-Contending Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Doc 'The Age Of Disclosure' Becomes VOD Phenomenon, Outperforming 'One Battle After Another' & More “In the early days of my investigation into UAP and non-human intelligent life, my work was so classified I couldn’t even tell my wife and kids that I had learned we are not alone in the universe or about any of the paradigm shift information I was learning,” Stratton said. “I had to live a double life, where the front door to my house served as a boundary between two distinct identities… but that all changed when we started having UAP activity and encounters with non-human intelligent life at our house and my wife and kids saw it with their own eyes.” Watch on Deadline Winter, who executive produces via his Cold Front Productions, noted that Stratton’s story has elements of some of his favorite shows and movies, Homeland, The Americans, The Hunt for Red October, All The President’s Men, Spotlight, and The Big Short. “For all of human history, mankind has wondered whether we are the only intelligent life in the universe,” Winter said. “Jay Stratton’s shocking true story answers that question and more as it delves into the world of the U.S. Government’s investigation of UAP and non-human intelligent life. It’s a riveting journey into a world the public knows little about.” Stratton’s memoir Out of the Shadows will be published in the U.S. by HarperCollins imprint William Morrow on Oct. 13. “ Out of the Shadows has the propulsive storytelling of a high-stakes political thriller,” Farah said. “It brings you behind the scenes of the U.S. Government’s investigation of the biggest mystery of all time. At the center of the story is the deeply personal, harrowing toll Jay’s pursuit of the truth had on him and his family. We intend to fully explore that in our show.” Winter, an Oscar nominee for The Wolf of Wall Street, won four Emmys for his work on The Sopranos . He created and executive produced HBO’s Boardwalk Empire and most recently served as executive producer/showrunner on Taylor Sheridan’s Paramount+ series Tulsa King. Winter is repped by CAA. articles.title: Andra Day To Play Wrongly Convicted Army Veteran In ‘Don’t Go Gentle’ From Deborah Riley Draper
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Andra Day To Play Wrongly Convicted Army Veteran In ‘Don’t Go Gentle’ From Deborah Riley Draper MIP London Comes To An End After Two Years; Organizers Launching New Event Alongside London Book Fair Liz Murdoch & Jane Featherstone’s Sister Group Takes Stake In Common Interest View All September 24, 2026 6:32am L-R: Andra Day, Len Cariou, Lonnie Chavis, Teyonah Parris, Alexandra Daddario, Finn Wittrock To Star In ‘Don’t Go Gentle’ From Deborah Riley Draper Emilynn Rose, Andrew Walker, Getty, Najah Chavis, Jacob Webster, Storm Santos, PMC EXCLUSIVE: Andra Day will star as a U.S. Army veteran trying to clear her name after being convicted of a crime she did not commit in Don’t Go Gentle . Len Cariou will play a retired judge who becomes involved with her case in the film, which Deborah Riley Draper writes and directs. Lonnie Chavis, Alexandra Daddario, Finn Wittrock and Teyonah Parris also star in the movie, which Draper has reworked from Stephen Belber’s play of the same name. Gerard Butler is a producer under his G-BASE banner, alongside Alan Siegel and Dan Kaslow. Crystine Zhang produces for Oval-5. Related Stories Festivals 'Is This Thing On?' Review: Bradley Cooper's Comedic Dissection Of A Marriage On The Rocks Is Indeed Right On - New York Film Festival Casting 'Percy Jackson': Andra Day Cast As Athena In Season 2 Of Disney+ Series Set in modern-day Buffalo, Don’t Go Gentle follows Tanya Jenkins, a mother and Army medic who was honorably discharged. She refuses to let a wrongful conviction become the final word on her life and ends up being pulled into the privileged but strained world of a former judge and his family. Watch on Deadline Cariou ( Blue Bloods ) is the retired judge, Lawrence Driver, whose history and sense of authority are challenged by Tanya’s presence. Chavis ( This Is Us ) plays Rasheed, Tanya’s teenage son, and Parris ( WandaVision ) is Ellen, Tanya’s half-sister. Daddario ( The White Lotus ) is Amelia, Lawrence’s architect daughter. Wittrock ( American Horror Story ) plays Ben, his troubled son. This marks Draper’s move into writing and directing narrative features. She is known for making award-winning docs including A&E’s James Brown: Say It Loud and OWN/Discovery+’s The Legacy of Black Wall Street . Speaking to Deadline from the Toronto set of the movie, Draper said: “ Don’t Go Gentle is completely reimagined from the play, but this is still a story about place, belonging and identity. In her quest to vindicate herself after being wrongly convicted, Tanya crosses paths with a retired judge who’s dying and ultimately her family moves in with him. There is a dynamic of these families understanding who they are, their place in America, understanding what home is, what legacy is and what entitlement is.” Day earned an Academy Award nom and won a Golden Globe for Best Actress for her portrayal of Billie Holiday in Lee Daniels’ The United States vs. Billie Holiday . “ Don’t Go Gentle challenges the idea that strength means suffering in silence,” she said. “What we accepted yesterday does not have to be what we accept today and Tanya exemplifies that. She is resilient and a healer. For her, every new environment and every obstacle is an opportunity to grow and improve conditions for herself, her son and her community.” Draper added that stories about what happens to women after military service are thin on the ground. “Women veterans in America are one of the most overlooked groups because the military system wasn’t necessarily set up for them,” she said. “They come home and often they are poorly served. Andra has embodied this character in so many ways. She’s done so much research about female veterans and African American female veterans.” Draper’s Atlanta-based label Coffee Bluff Pictures produces alongside G-BASE and Oval-5. articles.title: Thriller ‘Sender’, Starring Britt Lower, Rhea Seehorn, David Dastmalchian & Jamie Lee Curtis, Gets U.S. Deal
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Thriller ‘Sender’, Starring Britt Lower, Rhea Seehorn, David Dastmalchian & Jamie Lee Curtis, Gets U.S. Deal Andy Serkis To Narrate Adrian Tchaikovsky’s Sci-Fi Adaptation Of ‘The Odyssey’ For Audible ‘My Darling California’: Evans, Chastain, Pine, Madison & Cheadle Begin Shoot On L.A. Noir As Financiers Join Project View All September 24, 2026 6:38am Sender Dark Sky Films EXCLUSIVE : Dark Sky Films has acquired U.S. distribution rights to Sender , the psychological thriller from writer-director Russell Goldman, starring Britt Lower, Rhea Seehorn, Anna Baryshnikov, David Dastmalchian, Utkarsh Ambudkar, and Jamie Lee Curtis, who also produces. Following a festival run that began with its world premiere in Narrative Feature Competition at SXSW, Dark Sky Films will release the film nationwide in spring 2027. The acquisition comes ahead of Senders ’s Los Angeles premiere at Beyond Fest and European premiere at the 59th Sitges International Fantastic Film Festival. Following its SXSW debut, the film was selected as a Marquee Presentation at the San Francisco International Film Festival and won jury prizes for Best Feature at the Sidewalk Film Festival and Chattanooga Film Festival. Related Stories Reviews 'Sender' Review: Britt Lower Stars In Mesmerizing Psychological Thriller Even More Twisted Than 'Severance' - SXSW Casting 'Severance's Britt Lower To Topline Psychological Horror Film 'Sender' Produced By Jamie Lee Curtis The distribution agreement was negotiated by Greg Newman, Executive Vice President of Dark Sky Films, with producers Jake Katofsky and Molly Hallam and writer-director Russell Goldman representing the filmmakers. Matt Shreder of Concourse Media is handling international sales. Watch on Deadline In Sender , Lower stars as Julia, “a recently sober and unemployed woman attempting to rebuild her life in a new suburban rental, one online order at a time. When unmarked packages she never purchased begin arriving at her home, their eerie specificity starts to feel like a message from someone who knows exactly who she used to be. As Julia becomes increasingly consumed with discovering who is behind the deliveries, she turns to delivery driver Charlie (David Dastmalchian), her sister Tatiana (Anna Baryshnikov), and Whitney (Rhea Seehorn), a woman from her recovery group, for help. Her search eventually leads her to Lisa Barr (Jamie Lee Curtis), who has been receiving disturbingly familiar packages of her own.” The film marks the debut feature from writer-director Goldman. His script first appeared in the 2023 Black List of unproduced screenplays. Curtis is a producer alongside Molly Hallam and Jake Katofsky. Executive producers include Russell Goldman, Britt Lower, Akshay Shah, Thomas Grabinski, Paris Jones, and Andre Ray. “The dream of any filmmaker is finding a distributor that understands your film and wants to put it in front of as many eyeballs as possible,” said Goldman. “ Sender isn’t the kind of film that fits neatly into a box, which makes it especially meaningful that the entire MPI and Dark Sky team has a real vision for its nationwide theatrical release. I’m grateful to JLC, Britt, Jake, Molly, Thomas and the entire cast and crew, and proud our film will be at the home as some of the most exciting films of the decade. To use one of JLC’s favorite phrases, “Let’s f–king go.” “What drew us to Sender was how confidently Russell takes a familiar anxiety and turns it into something completely unexpected,” said Greg Newman, Executive Vice President of Dark Sky Films. “It’s smart, unsettling and darkly funny, with an incredible cast that keeps you invested at every turn. “Russell has made the kind of bold, original thriller that immediately gets under your skin and stays there,” added Justin DiPietro, Executive Vice President of MPI Media Group. “With an extraordinary cast, Sender is exactly the kind of distinctive filmmaking we want to champion at Dark Sky. We believe this is a film audiences will want to experience together in a theater, and we’re excited to give it our biggest theatrical push yet.” 150 Tech Roles Set To Go; TV & Radio Network Closures Expected Next Week Trump Ban Temporarily Blocked; CNN Credentials Restored Key Asian Markets Set For $15B Content Spend In 2026 – Study HBO’s Bloys, Par’s Cheeks Fuel Merger Intrigue With Joint Appearance At ‘War’ Premiere Read More About: Comments

articles.title: CNN, MS NOW And Politico Say White House Continues To Deny Access To Some Staffers Even After Judge’s Order
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Trump Ban Temporarily Blocked By Judge, Who Orders CNN, Politico & MS NOW Credentials Restored Judge Says He’ll Rule “As Soon As I Can” On Trump’s Ban On CNN, Politico And MS NOW; Expresses Concern Over Due Process CNN CEO Mark Thompson Addresses Donald Trump’s White House Ban, Pending Paramount Merger In Town Hall View All September 24, 2026 6:54am Donald Trump Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images The White House has continued to deny access to reporters for CNN , Politico and MS NOW , even after a judge ruled against Donald Trump ‘s ban and that credentials must be restored. CNN’s Betsy Klein reported that she was still not being allowed access to the grounds, and did a standup from outside the White House gates. Politico reported that one of its correspondents was turned away and his press credentials were confiscated. Related Stories News Trump Ban Temporarily Blocked By Judge, Who Orders CNN, Politico & MS NOW Credentials Restored News Reporters Committee And Dozens Of Media Outlets File Legal Brief Urging Judge To End Trump’s Ban On CNN, Politico And MS Now U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, in a ruling issued overnight, issued a temporary restraining order that requires that access be restored. He concluded that the outlets were denied due process, but also indicated that the media plaintiffs were likely to succeed in their Fifth Amendment claims. The order lasts for 14 days as he considers further legal arguments.
