articles.title: ‘The Future of Spanish Cinema Is Not About Making More Films’: Atresmedia Unveils Broad Slate
articles.full_text: Sep 22, 2026 6:45am PT ‘The Future of Spanish Cinema Is Not About Making More Films’: Atresmedia Unveils Broad Slate From 'La Bola Negra' to 'La Roja,' Atresmedia Makes Its Case for Bigger, Bolder Spanish Cinema By Callum McLennan Plus Icon Callum McLennan Latest Inside the Basque Production Boom: Who Owns the Growth? 8 hours ago ‘The Harvester’ Star Antonio de la Torre: ‘Violence Has No Justification, but It Does Have an Explanation’ 9 hours ago San Sebastian Startup Challenge Puts AI, Immersive Tech and Green Production in Focus 9 hours ago See All 'La Bola Negra' Carla Oset/Netflix SAN SEBASTIAN, Spain — Spanish theatrical audiences are concentrating around fewer films, with nearly 75% of admissions this year going to just 10 local titles despite more than 275 Spanish films being released, according to Atresmedia Cine general manager Jaime Ortiz de Artiñano. “Audiences have become far more selective,” Ortiz de Artiñano told Variety ahead of Atresmedia’s San Sebastián presentation. “They are willing to leave home for films that feel like true cultural events.” Related Stories Steve Doocy, Brian Kilmeade Will Commemorate 9/11 on Fox News After Covering it 25 Years Ago Billy Bush to Join Fox News as Contributor Atresmedia Cine, which Ortiz de Artiñano says has led the Spanish box office for the past seven years with market shares ranging from around 30% to more than 50%, sees that concentration as reshaping what theatrical success requires. Popular on Variety “For me, this leads to a very clear conclusion: the future of Spanish cinema is not about making more films, but about making films that more people want to see,” he said. That thinking was on display at the Hotel Maria Cristina’s Salon Elcano in San Sebastián, where Atresmedia presented a slate spanning the return of Adriana Ugarte in “Sira,” thriller “Trazos ocultos” and Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s “ La Bola Negra ,” where it has partnered on the film, taking free-to-air TV rights. The event was Atresmedia Cine’s traditional annual industry presentation during the festival, moderated by journalist David Martos, with a host of actors among them Goya winners Eduard Fernández, and Javier Gutiérrez, both in good sprits, and filmmakers Roberto Bueso, Aritz Moreno, Álvaro Fernández Armero and Daniel Calparsoro with their projects. “Sira” brings Adriana Ugarte (“Julieta”) back with sequel to “The Time In Between Seams” as Sira Quiroga, moving the period drama into the aftermath of World War II and across Jerusalem, London, Madrid and Tangier. Produced by Buendía Estudios Bizkaia with the participation of Atresmedia and Netflix, it will premiere first on Atresplayer before moving to Antena 3 primetime, an increasingly important windowing model for the broadcaster. “Trazos ocultos,” starring Toni Acosta and Rodolfo Sancho, forms the other major series play presented at the festival, underscoring Atresmedia’s continuing bet on broad appeal premium fiction that can travel between subscription and linear television. On the film side, Spain’s Oscar submission “La Bola Negra” and TIFF People’s Choice Award winner, points to a more international model. The Lorca-inspired drama, directed by Calvo and Ambrossi and starring Guitarricadelafuente, Penélope Cruz, Miguel Bernardeau, Lola Dueñas and Glenn Close, is a Movistar Plus original produced with Suma Content Films, El Deseo and Le Pacte, with the participation of Atresmedia. For Ortiz de Artiñano, the film’s festival trajectory has gone beyond initial expectations. “In more than twenty-five years working in this industry, I have rarely seen a project gather this level of momentum,” he said, pointing to Cannes, Toronto and San Sebastián. That international reach sits alongside a more hard-headed reading of the Spanish theatrical market. Atresmedia says its films account for more than 50% of Spanish-film box office in 2026, with “Torrente Presidente” alone representing almost 40%. That logic also shapes financing. Ortiz de Artiñano argues that broadcasters, platforms, distributors and independent producers increasingly need to combine forces around ambitious projects. “No single player can consistently finance ambitious films on its own anymore,” he said. Atresmedia’s expanding 2027 slate, from “La Roja” and “El Confidente” to “Caza Mayor,” suggests the company sees its role increasingly as both producer and industrial catalyst: assembling partners, reducing risk and helping Spanish projects reach the scale needed to compete for attention at home and abroad. Below we profile the upcoming projects: “La Bola Negra” dir. Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi (Movistar Plus+, Suma Content Films, El Deseo, Le Pacte) Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi direct a multi-generational drama tracing the interconnected lives of three men across three different periods. Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau and Carlos González lead a cast that also includes Penélope Cruz, Lola Dueñas and Glenn Close. Written by Calvo, Ambrossi and Alberto Conejero, the film explores sexuality, desire, pain and inheritance through a three-part story linked to one of Federico García Lorca’s final unfinished works as well as the subject of his near last love poems. “ The Blind Ants “ ( “Las Ciegas Hormigas,” “Inurri Itsuak”) dir. Igor Legarreta (Lamia Producciones, Lamia Films, Lapona Zinema, Lazona Producciones, Bruja del Norte AIE, Buendía Estudios Bizkaia, Sideral Cinema, Caviar Antwerp B.V.) Igor Legarreta directs and co-writes this 1935-set Basque drama starring Urko Olazábal, Itziar Ituño, Josean Bengoetxea, Miren Gaztañaga and Carlos Santos. When a violent storm grounds an English ship carrying tons of coal off Algorta, Sabas Jauregui sees a chance to save his family from winter and drags his children into the dangerous salvage effort despite his wife Josefa’s fears. The struggle to protect the recovered “black gold” becomes a test of survival, desperation and family loyalty. “Karateka” dir. Aritz Moreno (Atresmedia Cine, Sr.&Sra., Karateka A.I.E., Wrong Men, Apaches Entertainment, Colosé Producciones) Aritz Moreno (“Advantages of Travelling by Train”) directs an inspirational sports drama chronicling Sandra Sánchez’s journey from Talavera de la Reina to Olympic gold in Tokyo at 39. Andrea Ros stars opposite Patrick Criado as Sánchez’s coach and partner Jesús del Moral. Shot across Spain and Japan, the film combines elite competition, romance and resilience in the true story of one of karate’s defining champions. “ El mal padre ” dir. Roberto Bueso (MOD Producciones, MOD Pictures, Misent Producciones, Atresmedia Cine) Eduard Fernández leads Roberto Bueso’s family drama as a celebrated writer who gathers his estranged children before Christmas at the coastal holiday home where they spent their childhood summers. Adam Jezierski, Francesco Carril, Meritxell Calvo and Cristina Plazas co-star. Selected for San Sebastián’s Official Selection, the film explores abandonment, resentment and impending parenthood as one fractured family is forced to confront the past. “The Confidant” (“El confidente”) dir. Daniel Calparsoro (Bowfinger International Pictures, Esto También Pasará, El Confidente Films AIE, Lionceau Films) Daniel Calparsoro directs a fact-inspired thriller starring Javier Gutiérrez and Miguel Herrán as a veteran policeman and his young informant, two men divided by principle but bound by loyalty and loneliness. Scripted by Fernando Navarro, the Spain-France production unfolds against a dangerous police operation and will world premiere in Seminci’s Official Selection, screening out of competition. “La Roja” dir. Marcel Barrena (Atresmedia Cine, Beta Fiction Spain, Vilaüt Films, La Roja AIE) Marcel Barrena directs and co-writes this fact-inspired underdog sports drama starring Paco León as a coach attempting to turn Spain into a competitive cricket nation. Carolina Yuste co-stars alongside Atul Vijayakumar and an ensemble including several debutants. Shot in Barcelona, the film uses cricket to explore integration, cultural difference, belonging and an evolving idea of what representing Spain can mean. “Big Game Hunt” (“Caza mayor”) dir. Daniel Sánchez Arévalo (Movistar Plus+, La Película del Tigre A.I.E., Estela Films, Tenampa Films, Cut One, Pólvora Films, Tinnitus) Daniel Sánchez Arévalo directs a rural thriller with black-comedy overtones starring Antonio de la Torre. He plays an Extremaduran pig herder who returns home covered in blood claiming to have seen a tiger, setting off an increasingly strange reckoning in Fregenal de la Sierra. Written by María Ballesteros and José Antonio de Pascual, the film turns an impossible sighting into a test of truth and desperation. “Caer de Pie” dir. Salvador Calvo (Atresmedia Cine, Fonte Films, LAZONA, Cómo Volé AIE) Salvador Calvo directs a fact-based drama starring Marina Salas as Ana, a 30-year-old woman admitted to psychiatric care after reaching breaking point and attempting suicide. Written by Alejandro Hernández, the film follows her 37-day hospitalization and gradual confrontation with vulnerability and recovery. Daniel Ibañez, Carmen Ruiz, Pedro Casablanc and Alicia Borrachero feature in the ensemble. “The Professor” (“El profesor”) dir. Daniel Castro (Atresmedia Cine, Gonita, 4 Cats Pictures, Una Nueva Comedia AIE, Vaya Films) Javier Gutiérrez headlines Daniel Castro’s Spain-Colombia production as a lonely university professor who falls for a Colombian model 20 years his junior despite her refusal to appear on video. Written and directed by Castro, the digital-age relationship story is in post-production, with Film Factory Entertainment handling international sales and A Contracorriente Films distributing in Spain. “Todo por la Casa” dir. María Togores (Atresmedia Cine, Beta Fiction Spain, Chef Sin Desperdicio 2022 AIE) Spain’s housing squeeze fuels María Togores’ romantic comedy starring Silvia Alonso and Alejandro García as desperate Madrid renters who pose as a conventional couple to secure an apartment from traditional-minded landlords. Written by Olatz Arroyo, the film turns an acute contemporary housing problem into the engine for a high-concept relationship comedy, with the deception complicated by the landlords living directly opposite. “Matar a Ramón” dir. Álvaro Fernández Armero (Atresmedia Cine, Un Pueblo Tranquilo AIE, La Terraza Films, True Crime Factory, Ikiru Films) Álvaro Fernández Armero directs a rural mystery-comedy about Ramón, a La Mancha contractor who survives a bizarre hit-and-run only to suffer a string of increasingly suspicious accidents. The ensemble includes Óscar de la Fuente, Carla Díaz, Yaël Belicha, Israel Elejalde and José Mota. Written by Daniel Castro and Diego Soto, the film pairs an attention-seeking Guardia Civil veteran with a socially awkward rookie investigating what may be their first “serial victim.” “Entre olas” dir. Chloé Wallace (Atresmedia Cine, Buendía Estudios Canarias, La Pepa Films, Basque Films, Xoelius and Veguchini, Ocean Love Story AIE) Chloé Wallace directs a romantic coming-of-age story starring Carla Tous, Nuno Gallego and Jan Buxaderas. Shot in Tenerife, the film centers on a summer love triangle in which surfing and environmental awareness become increasingly central. As an ecological threat emerges, Ali’s choice between stability and freedom expands into a larger reckoning with identity, belonging and the island’s future. “A morte nos teus ollos” dir. Guillermo de Oliveira (Atresmedia Cine, Sideral, Sétima) Guillermo de Oliveira makes his fiction feature debut with a fact-inspired Galician thriller starring Pepe Lorente and Iván Marcos. Developed through the Spanish Film Academy’s Residencies program and shot around Vigo and Pontevedra, the 1990s-set story follows two compromised policemen whose robbery scheme spirals into a tale of corruption, family, violence, greed, guilt and power. “La Dona Invisible” dir. Cristina Fernández Pintado (Atresmedia Cine, The Fly Hunter, La Terraza Films, Sucedió en Valverde AIE) Cristina Fernández Pintado directs a comic mystery starring Mona Martínez as Mihaela, a Romanian cleaner nearing retirement who discovers a dead civil servant in the government offices where she works. When police dismiss the death as accidental, the crime-fiction obsessive launches her own investigation alongside an eccentric young intern, probing both a possible murder and the opaque, rule-bound world of public bureaucracy. articles.title: BTS, Seventeen, Tomorrow X Together, Enhypen Anchor Trafalgar-HYBE Cine Fest’s Global Expansion
articles.full_text: Sep 22, 2026 6:51am PT BTS, Seventeen, Tomorrow X Together, Enhypen Anchor Trafalgar-HYBE Cine Fest’s Global Expansion By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Resident Evil’ Reboots at No. 1 as ‘Shaun the Sheep’ Bounds to No. 3 at U.K., Ireland Box Office 2 hours ago Juliet Stevenson, Olivia Williams Join Tim Crouch’s ‘An Oak Tree’ at the Other Palace (EXCLUSIVE) 5 hours ago Parvathy Thiruvothu on Playing a Police Officer in ‘Pradhama Drishtiya Kuttakkar’ and Speaking Out About Misogyny Despite Scrutiny: ‘I Enjoy Watching Patriarchy Fall Apart’ 6 hours ago See All HYBE Trafalgar Releasing and HYBE are expanding HYBE Cine Fest into a global event for the first time, bringing the week-long cinema festival to more than 60 territories from Oct. 24-31. The festival previously launched in Latin America in 2024 and expanded across Asia in 2025. This year’s lineup includes six presentations: two live broadcasts of the BTS World Tour “Arirang,” concert films from Seventeen , Tomorrow X Together and Enhypen, and the interactive “HYBE Cheering Party” in 3D. Related Stories Steve Doocy, Brian Kilmeade Will Commemorate 9/11 on Fox News After Covering it 25 Years Ago Maria Bartiromo Out at Fox News, Fox Business The BTS broadcasts will stream from Buenos Aires, marking the group’s first performance in Argentina, on Oct. 24 in the Americas and Oct. 25 in the rest of the world. A second BTS broadcast from São Paulo, the finale of the group’s Latin American tour, will screen Oct. 30 in the Americas and Oct. 31 elsewhere. Popular on Variety Seventeen’s film captures the group’s “New” world tour, while Tomorrow X Together’s entry documents “Act : Tomorrow,” its fourth global tour. Enhypen’s film revisits the Seoul concert that opened the “Blood Saga” tour. The “HYBE Cheering Party” screening lets audiences sing along to on-screen lyrics and wave light sticks to music videos from artists including BTS, Seventeen, Tomorrow X Together, Enhypen, Le Sserafim, &Team, Boynextdoor, TWS, Illit, Katseye, aoen, Cortis and Santos Bravos. Tickets go on sale Sept. 30. “Following the incredible response to HYBE Cine Fest across Latin America and Asia, we are scaling this festival format to global cinema audiences,” said Marc Allenby, chief executive officer of Trafalgar Releasing. “Bringing together major concert films, interactive 3D cheering parties, and landmark live broadcasts across a single week gives fans everywhere an unprecedented way to celebrate their favorite HYBE artists together in cinemas.” The festival’s Special Location program, which offers interactive fan zones, merchandise and pop-up stores at select cinemas, is expanding into North America and Europe this year after previously running in Latin America and Asia. Trafalgar Releasing operates in more than 15,000 cinemas across 132 countries and has distributed concert films for artists including Taylor Swift, Beyoncé and Metallica. HYBE’s roster spans labels including Bighit Music, Belift Lab, Source Music and Pledis Entertainment. articles.title: Former Cinecittà Chief Nicola Maccanico Appointed CEO of Rainbow Group’s Colorado Film
articles.full_text: Sep 22, 2026 6:52am PT Former Cinecittà Chief Nicola Maccanico Appointed CEO of Rainbow Group’s Colorado Film By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest Oscars: Egypt Selects Abu Bakr Shawky’s ‘The Stories’ for International Feature Race 5 hours ago Red Sea Film Festival Cancels 2026 Edition, Will Return Next Year 1 day ago Dubai Film Festival Revived With New Edition Set for December 2027 5 days ago See All Courtesy Colorado Films Former Cinecittà Studios chief Nicola Maccanico has been appointed CEO of Rome-based production shingle Colorado Film. The company is owned and operated by Italy’s Rainbow Group, led by Iginio Straffi , creator of the hit “Winx Club” animation franchise. Maccanico, who is a former Warner Bros. and Sky Italia senior exec, spearheaded the radical overhaul of Cinecittà’s Rome studios for three years. He stepped down in 2024 after Italy’s right-wing government decided to change the studios’ management team. Related Stories Billy Bush to Join Fox News as Contributor Steve Doocy, Brian Kilmeade Will Commemorate 9/11 on Fox News After Covering it 25 Years Ago Colorado Film is a commercially successful live-action movies shingle that in 2024 scored a hit with young adult romantic drama “The Tearsmith,” which became the first Netflix Italy original to reach the No. 1 slot on the streamer’s global movie chart in the non-English-language category. Besides “The Tearsmith,” Colorado’s top titles over the years comprise the smash-hit “Me Contro Te” comedy franchise, featuring two Sicilian YouTube sensations; blockbuster comedy “La Peggior Settimana della Mia Vita”; theatrical saga “Ten Days Without Mom”; and bestselling Italian mystery writer Donato Carrisi’s directorial debut “The Girl in the Fog.” Popular on Variety Colorado’s upcoming productions include English-language rom-com “Blame It on Rome,” directed by Francesco Carrozzini and starring Michele Morrone (“365 Days”) and Gabrielle Union (“Bad Boys II”). It’s co-produced by Colorado Film, Nebraska and Amazon MGM Studios as an original for Prime Video Italy. Maccanico will replace Colorado’s outgoing CEO Thomas J. Ciampa, who has just been appointed chief of Vision Distribution, the Italian theatrical distributor jointly operated by Sky Italia and five prominent Italian production companies. “Nicola Maccanico’s appointment is part of Rainbow Group’s ongoing growth strategy and is aimed at further strengthening Colorado Film’s position within the Italian and international audiovisual industry, building on its creative heritage and developing new production opportunities,” Rainbow Group said in a statement. “Nicola Maccanico’s arrival marks the driving force behind a new strategic phase for the future of Colorado Film,” said Straffi, Rainbow Group’s president. “His extensive expertise and ability to combine creative vision with industrial strategy will be crucial to the company’s expansion.” Straffi added, “We will continue to invest in talent and in Italian creative excellence, driven by the ambition to ensure these stories resonate powerfully with audiences both in Italy and internationally.” Commented Maccanico: “Contributing to the development of Colorado Film is an important challenge, and having the opportunity to do so alongside an entrepreneur with the visionary talent of Iginio Straffi is a privilege. The audiovisual market needs Italian production companies with an industrial mindset, capable of growing and becoming increasingly competitive. I am convinced that this is the role Colorado is meant to play, and it is the role we will strive to fulfill with ever greater impact.” Deauville American Film Festival Unveils Buzzy Lineup, Sets Honors for Brendan Fraser, Faye Dunaway, Ethan Hawke, Susan Sarandon, Sophie Thatcher and Patrick Schwarzenegger Susan Sarandon to Be Honored at Rome Film Festival Sidebar Where ‘The Accompanist’ Will Bow Internationally (EXCLUSIVE) Susan Sarandon Says She’s ‘Still Had Movies Taken Away Recently’ Over Palestine Support: ‘There Are Agencies That Are Telling People Not to Hire Me’ Martin Scorsese and Susan Sarandon Squash Their Children’s Internet Beef in New Jack Henry Robbins Sketch (EXCLUSIVE) Javier Bardem to Be Honored by Rome Film Festival With Lifetime Achievement Award Loading comments... articles.title: Top UK YouTubers Launch Alliance Pushing For Better Conditions For Content Creators
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘The Gentlemen’ Star Chanel Cresswell Boards Netflix’s ‘The Lords’ Day’ Top UK YouTubers Launch Alliance Pushing For Better Conditions For Content Creators ‘Lollipop Chainsaw’: Cult Japanese Video Game Getting The Live Action Feature Treatment View All September 21, 2026 4:01pm The Sidemen: repped by alliance member Jordan Schwarzenberger Netflix Top UK creators have banded together to launch an independent alliance championing their interests. YouTube UK is backing Creator Voices , which consists of The Sidemen ’s rep Jordan Schwarzenberger , DamienTalksMoney, Jade Beason, TLDR News, Grace Andrews and Brandon B. The alliance is being unveiled today at a YouTube Festival in London. Creator Voices said its members will “leverage their collective reach” and “advocate for institutional recognition and deeper integration with traditional creative bodies.” Related Stories News Adam Conover Dates New Stand-Up Special 'Big Divorce Energy' News 'Bling Empire' Star Dorothy Wang Launching Wedding Series On YouTube The move comes after thousands of creators including Amelia Dimoldenberg put their names to a first-of-its-kind report from YouTube that found its creator ecosystem contributed more than £2B ($2.67B) to the UK economy in 2023. That figure rose to £2.8B last year, according to a newer Oxford Economics Impact Report, which said the number could support more than 60,000 equivalent jobs. When the report came out, its authors said they wanted the job of content creator to be given government recognition along with better industry representation and access to finance. Since then, digital creators have become an even more crucial cog in the traditional entertainment machine. Dimoldenberg, for example, will host Saturday Night Live UK this weekend, just a fortnight after Hollywood superstar Jeff Goldblum. Watch on Deadline “The UK boasts one of the most dynamic creative ecosystems in the world, and digital creators are adding an extraordinary new dimension to that heritage,” said YouTube UK boss Alison Lomax. “While YouTube is proud to support the convening of this independent collective, the voice and vision belong entirely to them. Connecting digital talent with established creative leaders will unlock significant economic growth, foster fresh storytelling and showcase the best of modern British culture on a global stage.” Earlier this year, we told you how UK content creators like Dimoldenberg, Beason and Munya Chawawa were helping shape the TV industry behind the scenes. ‘Gangs Of London’ Producers Suing Vice, Claiming They Are Owed $20M Piers Morgan Wins Apology From Diana’s Brother Over Memoir Which Midnight Madness TIFF Pic Could Become The Next Box Office Obsession? ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $108M WW Read More About: 3 Comments

articles.title: ‘Forgotten Island’ Review: H.E.R. And Dave Franco Give Life To Gorgeously Animated And Frenetic ‘Toon
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Pete Hammond Pete Hammond Awards Columnist/Chief Film Critic @DeadlinePete More Stories By Pete ‘La Bola Negra’ Wins Oscar-Predictive Toronto Film Festival People’s Choice Award ‘Magazine’ Review: Lily McInerny And Bright Young Cast Give Flavor To Pre-Digital Vanishing Era Of NY’s Literary World – Toronto Film Festival Toronto Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline’s Reviews View All September 21, 2026 4:05pm Forgotten Island DreamWorks / Universal Pictures You have to give points to DreamWorks’ latest animated feature, Forgotten Island , just simply for being an original from a studio system that rewards familiarity. And it comes from writer/directors Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado who proved with their own sequel, 2022’s Puss In Boots: The Last Wish that you could find clever ways to renew and energize existing IP, rather than just settling for what the audience expects. I suspect this one though will have the most appeal to a teenage female audience as it is centered on the BFF relationship of two young girls, besties since grade school in the Phillipines, who have lived a life of memories (they have matching charm bracelets to prove it) since being little kids inseparable from each other. Now on the cusp of seeing life taking them down separate paths, they are about to embark on their greatest adventure together ever. But will they even be able to remember it? That is the hook here as the opening of the film introduces us to the wild and wacky Jo, and the more serious-minded Raissa with dreams of being a scientist one day. Related Stories Casting Jenny Slate Joins Dylan O'Brien In Hulu Comedy Pilot 'Lex' News Jo Koy Sets Sixth Netflix Comedy Special 'Blue In The Face' At home in Manila they both dream of a mythical place that in their minds absolutely exists. During their lives they have been fed epic stories by the beloved elder Lola (Dolly DeLeon) which are vividly shared with her class by Jo. The film jumps ahead to the end of their high school years where Jo (the older version voiced by singer H.E.R. ) and Raissa ( Liza Soberano ) are at that inflection point. Raissa is accepted into Caltech in America and is going to be leaving, while meanwhile Jo is stuck in a menial job at a fast food joint. This will be their last night and they are going to make the most of it when they come upon a magical portal on the beach, the portal it turns out to, Nakali, that Forgotten Island. Watch on Deadline Next thing you know they have landed there, with absolutely no idea of just how they got to the place of their imaginations. They are about to find out in this play on memory and the importance of it in all of our lives. With colorful new appearances (Raissa now has wings and half a head of hair) they have gone down the kind of rabbit hole that infamous characters like Alice and Dorothy have tread in literature and movies before, but this place is something else. In quick and whirring succession they meet some real doozies starting with Weredog, Raww (voiced with style and fun by Dave Franco ), who claims he had just spent the previous 12 hours with both of them. He is a bit of a mess, embarrassed by his ever-changing appearance from human to dog and back again, mostly dog though. He will be their self-appointed guide thorugh Nakali, but he has competition from another new acquaintance, Bungi ( Manny Jacinto ) a cycloptic giant blue baby still stuck (literally) to his mother after all these years. We also meet the more restrained cave dwelling Batiba (terrifically voiced by Jenny Slate ) who is agoraphobic to her core, but lives with a collection of knick knacks it turns out have been stolen from other peoples memories, just not her own since she is deathly afraid of venturing out into the world. She promises to help Jo and Raissa get back to their own world in return for their own memories. Along the way we meet Daju ( Jo Koy ) leader of a tree brigade; King Truffle Wuffle (Ronny Chieng) lording over his own feifdom; and the impossibly vain and slick Prince Mermahn (Kevin McCann). As in every single cartoon aimed at kids there is also a villainess, and here it is The Dreaded Manananggal ( Lea Solonga ) who can magically divide herself down the middle and other horrific talents. She’s the wicked witch and evil queen of the piece but of course there is a reason she got to be so bad and we will find out in due time. Jo and Raissa must navigate all of this in order to get back to where they came from in this uber frenetically-paced journey. Crawford and Mercado (who clearly has added the Filipino flavor to this story) pack way too much visually, especially in the first half perhaps sensing today’s younger moviegoers have a bit of attention deficit. I thought this thing, beautifully animated with different styles creeping in and out and as colorful as it could possibly be, would never slow down to take a breath. But finally in the second half when the girls’ own hopes and dreams come front and center, and the emotional elements take charge, it does cool its jets just enough to take it all in. The main theme of saving our memories, and keeping them close comes through loud and clear and there is nice resoloution to all of this. The busy soundtrack has lots of catchy tunes, old and new, including an original or two from H.E.R. herself. Is this an animated movie I will keep in my memories? Not likely, but I think its younger (much) target audience will indeed be the ones who will find some cool things to remember and some sharp life lessons about the value of friendship. Producer of the DreamWorks Animation production is Mark Swift. articles.title: Paramount-WBD Settlement Sets Up Editorial Independence Board For CNN And CBS News
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Donald Trump Vows To Appeal Ruling In Networks’ White House Ban Lawsuit, Even Though Judge Has Yet To Rule Paramount-WBD Settlement Sets Up Editorial Independence Board For CNN And CBS News Read The Proposed Consent Decree To Settle The Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger View All September 21, 2026 12:40pm Story Arc CNN; CBS News UPDATED: The potential ownership of CBS News and CNN under one corporate owner has generated months of fear, anxiety and loathing at both networks, but the Paramount – Warner Bros. Discovery settlement tries to resolve some of the issues with the establishment of an editorial independence board. Related Stories News WGA Gets No Writer Layoffs At CBS News, $17.5M For Health Fund As Guild Confirms Settlement Of Lawsuit Against Paramount-WBD Merger News Read The Proposed Consent Decree To Settle The Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger Per the terms of the consent decree reached with a dozen state attorneys general, the board will establish a set of guiding principles based on each network’s policies for “accuracy, independence, fairness and journalistic integrity.” The board will resolve any disputes between CBS News employees, CNN employees and management regarding any alleged violations of the principles. And it will monitor “adherence to ethical journalism as defined by journalism industry best practices and to editorial independence.” The decree also sets up who can serve on the body, made up of five retired or active journalists who have worked for a minimum of ten years, and who will be appointed by the combined Paramount-WB board. No more than two members may be affiliated with the same political party. Watch on Deadline “No member of any government or governmental entity, including federal, state, and local governments, may approve or have approval rights over members appointed to the Editorial Independence Board,” per the decree. Officers, directors or non-journalist employees of Paramount-WB also are restricted from serving on the board, whose members will have terms of three years. Paramount would have 180 days to establish the board. There is a designation of a monitoring trustee to oversee Paramount-WBD compliance with the entire consent decree, but that person will have “no role or authority” relating to news operations. A “force majeure” provision can be invoked for events including disasters, strikes, labor disruptions and economic recessions, among other things. A separate settlement with the Writers Guild of America includes a provision prohibiting writer layoffs at CBS News broadcast for five years, the guild said. What the AGs’ consent decree does not do is restrict a combination of CBS News and CNN. Nor does it give the board oversight over who runs the respective news entities, something that has been an issue as CEO David Ellison tapped Bari Weiss to lead CBS News after Skydance’s purchase of Paramount last year. That has raised concerns that the network would be steered rightward, or even in a direction more favorable to Donald Trump. Weiss previously worked as an opinion writer for The New York Times and founded The Free Press, the center-right opinion and analysis site that Paramount also purchased. As part of her changes, she ousted the executive producer of 60 Minutes , while some of the correspondents who were fired have alleged politically motivated interference. Weiss has defended her input to the show, saying it is part of the news process. As part of commitments to close its purchase of Paramount last year, Skydance said that it would install an ombudsman to take complaints over CBS News. The person they hired, Kenneth Weinstein, was not a journalist but the former head of the rightward Hudson Institute. Unlike the traditional role of an ombudsman at a news organization, none of the findings are made public. Other actions have triggered further suspicions, including that, like CBS News, changes would be afoot for CNN, including appointing Weiss to oversee that network as well. As he sought administration approval to purchase Warner Bros. Discovery this year, Ellison hosted a dinner for the Trump White House tied to the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, and he appeared at the president’s State of the Union address. Anna Gomez, the sole Democrat on the FCC, said that the “editorial independence protections included in this settlement remain untested, and there is good reason to be skeptical they will hold up once the ink is dry. Whether these commitments actually protect newsrooms inside CBS and CNN from political, financial, or regulatory pressure, or simply provide cover for further editorial interference, remains to be seen.” Seth Stern, chief of advocacy of the Freedom of the Press Foundation, called the consent decree’s oversight board “worthless.” He said in a statement, “It’s unclear how the attorneys general or courts can constitutionally hold Paramount accountable for the board’s actions or inaction without themselves interfering in content. The attorneys general might be fine with censorship when they’re the ones doing it, but what happens when successors with opposing political views inherit enforcement powers?” California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who led the state AG lawsuit, told reporters that the independent board would “ensure independent, objective, fact-based reporting at CBS News and at CNN.” An independent board is unusual, not not unprecedented. A special committee was set up in 2007 to oversee editorial integrity at the Wall Street Journal , as Rupert Murdoch’s News Corp was looking to acquire the news outlet from the Bancroft family trust. The committee, though, does have a say in major newsroom positions, as it has to grant approval for the appointments of an editor-in-chief and editorial page editor. Comcast committed to an ombudsman when it acquired NBC Universal, with concerns over corporate interference in the editorial process. David McCormick, vice president of standards at NBC News, had already been serving as ombudsman in 1993, and expanded his duties to other NBCU news properties. ‘Gangs Of London’ Producers Suing Vice, Claiming They Are Owed $20M Piers Morgan Wins Apology From Diana’s Brother Over Memoir Which Midnight Madness TIFF Pic Could Become The Next Box Office Obsession? ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $108M WW More from this Story Arc Paramount WB September 21, 2026 Paramount Settlement Protects Pluto TV, Sets BET & Comedy Central As Potential Divesture Targets While Omitting Premium Channels & TV Studios September 21, 2026 Paramount To Keep Headquarters In Los Angeles Post-Merger: “We Aren’t Going Anywhere” View All Story Arc Read More About: Comments

articles.title: The Final Stretch: California AG Rob Bonta On How Settlement On Paramount-WBD Merger Came Together…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva , Katie Campione September 21, 2026 1:25pm Story Arc Paramount, Rob Bontas Getty Images/Courtesy Paramount ‘s settlement with the 12 Democratic state attorneys general appeared to be a Yom Kippur affair, with the final signoff coming after sundown on Sunday. California Attorney General Rob Bonta was cagey when asked about the exact timeline for the agreement following his Monday morning press conference announcing the deal but when he was cheekily asked by a reporter whether he had brushed his teeth yet by the time all was said and done, he responded with, “I can affirmatively say yes.” Related Stories News David Ellison Hopes To Close Paramount-WBD Deal “In Approximately Two Weeks” As He Hails Legal Settlement In Company Memo News WGA Gets No Writer Layoffs At CBS News, $17.5M For Health Fund As Guild Confirms Settlement Of Lawsuit Against Paramount-WBD Merger “You get to a place in some of these negotiations where you get to 90% maybe 95%, maybe even 99%, and then the last part is often the hardest part,” Bonta added. “Something comes up, something unexpected; you make a lot of progress, then it goes slow, there’s a hiccup — and that was not proven wrong here either.” Watch on Deadline

articles.title: Paramount Shares Fall After Antitrust Deal, But Business Minds Marvel At Favorable Terms
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Paramount Shares Fall After Antitrust Deal, But Business Minds Marvel At Favorable Terms David Ellison Hopes To Close Paramount-WBD Deal “In Approximately Two Weeks” As He Hails Legal Settlement In Company Memo Paramount Settlement Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta, Who Says Deal Is “Not A Blessing” Of WBD Merger View All September 21, 2026 1:38pm Story Arc Paramount's corporate office in New York's Times Square Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images While Warner Bros. Discovery shares soared 11%, as is often the case of a company about to be acquired, while Paramount shares stumbled on news the companies’ merger will take another two weeks to complete. The stocks’ divergent movement came after news Monday morning of a settlement between Paramount and 12 state attorneys general. A parallel lawsuit filed by the Writers Guild of America was also settled. The agreements pave the way for the $111 billion deal to close, but Paramount CEO David Ellison told staffers in a memo that it would take about two weeks for that final step to occur. Related Stories News Paramount Settlement Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta, Who Says Deal Is “Not A Blessing” Of WBD Merger News David Ellison Hopes To Close Paramount-WBD Deal “In Approximately Two Weeks” As He Hails Legal Settlement In Company Memo While Paramount’s beleaguered stock jumped 10% earlier in the day, it slumped in the last two hours of the day, possibly on the news that more time is required before the transaction can be completed. Paramount is on the hook for a “ticking fee” of about $7 million a day, payable to WBD shareholders, for every day past October 1 that the deal is not closed. Paramount stock settled at $9.91, its lowest closing price in a month. Watch on Deadline Fears of the ticking fee adding up to around $650 million per quarter ahead of a scheduled March 2027 trial date – a not-inconsequential amount for a company worth about $11 billion – shadowed the legal process in recent weeks. The state AGs and the WGA filed suit in July after federal regulators had approved the deal, and gained surprising traction in a series of early court rulings, giving opponents of the merger hope it would be curtailed or even fully blocked.

articles.title: Paramount To Keep Headquarters In Los Angeles Post-Merger: “We Aren’t Going Anywhere&#8221…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Paramount Settlement Protects Pluto TV, Sets BET & Comedy Central As Potential Divesture Targets While Omitting Premium Channels & TV Studios Paramount To Keep Headquarters In Los Angeles Post-Merger: “We Aren’t Going Anywhere” The Final Stretch: California AG Rob Bonta On How Settlement On Paramount-WBD Merger Came Together After Stalemate View All September 21, 2026 3:03pm Story Arc Getty Images Paramount is not leaving California — at least not anytime soon — and that includes both the company’s studio lot(s) and headquarters. The settlement of the anti-trust lawsuit filed by 12 state attorneys general calls for the Paramount, which is set to acquire WBD shortly, to keep both the Paramount lot on Melrose and the Warner Bros. lot in Burbank for the next five years. Related Stories News David Ellison Hopes To Close Paramount-WBD Deal “In Approximately Two Weeks” As He Hails Legal Settlement In Company Memo News Paramount Settlement Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta, Who Says Deal Is “Not A Blessing” Of WBD Merger “We wanted those lots to be protected, they are part of the the broader solution, and I believe that the future of this merged company is in Los Angeles for many years to come for the foreseeable future,” California AG Rob Bonta said during his press conference about the settlement Monday morning. Bonta was asked about the status of the Paramount headquarters, currently located in Los Angeles. Watch on Deadline “I believe that will be the case, that they will have their headquarters in California for the foreseeable future,” he said, adding, “It’s not part of the deal, I believe there will be public statements.” There had been no public statements on the matter, and the fact that Paramount maintaining its headquarters in California was not part of the agreement raised a few eyebrows. Paramount Chairman and CEO David Ellison did not address it in his official reaction to the settlement or in his company memo Monday, the latter of which noted the combined company’s commitment to producing 30+ movies a year and expanding U.S. film production. Hours later, he stepped in to clear the confusion. “Let me be clear: the newly merged company will be headquartered in Los Angeles,” Ellison said in a new statement. “We aren’t going anywhere. Our history is here and this is where our future is being built.” This brings to an end weeks of tension that culminated in an alleged ultimatum that Paramount would move its headquarters to Tennessee, Texas or Georgia if the anti-trust lawsuit filed by the state AGs was not settled by October 1 when a costly ticking fee to WBD was set to kick in. Per the settlement’s consent decree , the bulked up post-merger Paramount “shall not sell or close the Paramount or Warner Bros. Lots and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to operate the Lots in a manner consistent with past practices, including leasing use to third parties and producing films and television shows.” ‘Gangs Of London’ Producers Suing Vice, Claiming They Are Owed $20M Piers Morgan Wins Apology From Diana’s Brother Over Memoir Which Midnight Madness TIFF Pic Could Become The Next Box Office Obsession? ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $108M WW More from this Story Arc Paramount WB September 21, 2026 Paramount Settlement Protects Pluto TV, Sets BET & Comedy Central As Potential Divesture Targets While Omitting Premium Channels & TV Studios September 21, 2026 Paramount Shares Fall After Antitrust Deal, But Business Minds Marvel At Favorable Terms View All Story Arc Read More About: 9 Comments

articles.title: Paramount Settlement Protects Pluto TV, Sets BET & Comedy Central As Potential Divesture Targets While Omitting Premium Channels & TV Studios
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Paramount Settlement Protects Pluto TV, Sets BET & Comedy Central As Potential Divesture Targets While Omitting Premium Channels & TV Studios Paramount To Keep Headquarters In Los Angeles Post-Merger: “We Aren’t Going Anywhere” The Final Stretch: California AG Rob Bonta On How Settlement On Paramount-WBD Merger Came Together After Stalemate View All September 21, 2026 5:27pm Story Arc Pluto TV Photo Illustration by Rafael Henrique/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images Here is a concession no one really asked for — the settlement of state attorneys generals’ anti-trust lawsuit over the proposed Paramount -Warner Bros. Discovery merger includes a provision ensuring that Paramount will keep Pluto TV or another free, ad-supported streaming service for the next five years. Related Stories News Read The Proposed Consent Decree To Settle The Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger News Paramount Settlement Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta, Who Says Deal Is “Not A Blessing” Of WBD Merger While Pluto TV is protected, the settlement spells out which cable brands Paramount will have to divest if it fails to keep carriage negotiations for the Paramount and Warner Bros. basic cable networks at arm’s length. The list includes two Par nets that already had been put on the block twice, BET (and its various sub-channels) and VH1 , as well as Comedy Central , with the company’s flagships MTV and Nickelodeon out of danger. Overall, television feels a little like an afterthought in the settlement, illustrated by California AG Rob Bonta’s opening remarks at his Monday morning press conference. He spent more than six minutes laying out the agreed-upon terms for film production and had only two lines about TV, one about the establishment of “a news editorial independence board to support CBS News’ and CNN’s continued editorial independence” and one that “Paramount and Warner Brothers are required to continue negotiating their cable packages separately.” Watch on Deadline With state AGs’ action focused on protecting jobs, there is nothing in the agreement that would prevent Paramount from combining some of its post-merger TV studios — Warner Bros. Television, Paramount TV Studios and CBS Studios — which will result in layoffs. Or any guardrails limiting the number of positions that will inevitably be cut when Paramount merges Paramount+ with HBO Max as the company had said. Movies and basic cable were the focus of AGs’ legal battle because those were the areas where there were strong anti-trust concerns. (The combined HBO Max-Paramount+ will become a major SVOD player but will not have dominance in the space.) Still, the complete omission of the TV (or film) studios is surprising, as is the lack of mention of Paramount’s pay cable network Showtime , which, like the basic cable nets, negotiates carriage agreements. That would allow Paramount to bundle it together with WBD ‘s market leader HBO in dealings with operators. Emphasizing that, the settlement’s statement about separate affiliation negotiations for Paramount and WBD’s basic cable channels carries the following disclaimer: “For the avoidance of doubt, this paragraph does not apply to other Combined Entity offerings (e.g., premium cable channels, streaming services, or broadcast)” The omissions are especially glaring given the attention Pluto TV got despite it not being considered in real danger and it having no counterpart on the WBD side. The Curious Case Of Pluto TV Over the past year, Paramount’s leadership has been bullish about Pluto TV, vowing to invest in the AVOD platform and grow it, which they have done in the form of a slew of library content acquisitions and making Pluto part of the company’s backend tech stack convergence alongside Paramount+ – a complex, lengthy process which has largely been completed. Long before the Ellisons arrived on the scene, Pluto’s star had started fading as rivals Tubi and Roku became more popular. Pluto, although it had been a pioneer of FAST when it was founded in 2014, fell back in the market-share race. Its co-founder, Tom Ryan, and other core staffers exited the company. Even so, the new regime has expressed optimism about aiding the potential of Pluto, which had been largely neglected for the previous couple of years. “I am a big believer in the FAST space,” Paramount Chairman and CEO David Ellison said on the company’s Q4 2025 earnings call. Pluto TV was talked up to advertisers at the Paramount upfront presentation in May as a key piece of the company’s ad strategy, with upgrades ongoing and more underway. Most recently, Paramount noted that “Paramount+ and Pluto TV remain at the center of how audiences discover and engage with our programming as we build an entertainment platform for the future” in its Q2 2026 letter to investors, with the company’s executives saying on the earnings call that “we do expect that Pluto will return to growth in back half of the year.” With Paramount making a substantial investment in Pluto TV over the past year, there has been no talk of shutting it down. That has now been put on paper for the next five years in the anti-trust settlement. Basic Cable Haves & Have Nots According to the settlement with the 12 state AGs, “Paramount and Warner Brothers are required to continue negotiating their cable packages separately — a negotiate-separately condition, preserving the competition that exists between them today,” Bonta said Monday, adding, “It will mimic them being separate companies, even post-merger.” As to how that separation will be ensured, the statement is a little vague, noting that there will be a “monitor” and a “state committee” that would assess any complaints. If Paramount is caught in a “material violation,” following a six-month cure period where the company can “come into compliance,” they will have to sell one or more of the following linear networks: BET (Black Entertainment Television, including BET, BET Gospel, BET Her, BET Hip-Hop, BET Jams, and BET Soul), VH1, Comedy Central, Smithsonian, Destination America, and Science. After Skydance’s acquisition of Paramount, the company’s new leadership has shared their intention to revitalize legacy cable brands such as MTV, Nickelodeon, Comedy Central and BET. The inclusion of two of the four on the potential divesture list is somewhat surprising but Paramount still has kept crown jewels MTV and Nickelodeon out of reach. Additionally, the company already has Comedy Central’s biggest program, South Park, locked into a Paramount+ streaming deal for the foreseeable future and just folded BET+ into Paramount+. The rest of the channels on the list are small and, amid linear TV’s continuing decline, Paramount likely won’t mind divesting them anyway. articles.title: Oscar Winner Barbara Kopple On ‘Union Town,’ Her Third Towering Film On American Labor – Camden Film Festival
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Camden Film Festival: ‘Dependence,’ ‘Revolutionaries Never Die,’ ‘Bucks Harbor’ Take Top Awards As Fall Approaches, Camden International Film Festival Spends Time With ‘The Illusion Of An Everlasting Summer’ ‘Once Upon A Time In Harlem’ Wins $200,000 Library Of Congress Lavine/Ken Burns Prize For Film View All September 21, 2026 5:50pm 'Union Town' Courtesy of Camden International Film Festival Fifty years ago, a young director named Barbara Kopple came out with her first film, a documentary she thought would be little seen. “When I started making the film, I thought, ‘Oh, my parents will see it and their friends and maybe a museum will show it,’” she recalls. That film was Harlan County U.S.A. , about a long running strike at a coal mine in southeast Kentucky, and it was immediately hailed as brilliant, earning Kopple an Academy Award. She would earn a second Oscar for her 1991 documentary American Dream , about a strike at a Hormel Foods plant in Minnesota. Related Stories Documentary Camden Film Festival: 'Dependence,' 'Revolutionaries Never Die,' 'Bucks Harbor' Take Top Awards Documentary As Fall Approaches, Camden International Film Festival Spends Time With 'The Illusion Of An Everlasting Summer' Kopple has made many other documentaries in intervening years – on actor Gregory Peck, singer Sharon Jones, and country band the Chicks (formerly the Dixie Chicks), among others. But she returns to the theme for which she is best known – working people in America — in her new documentary Union Town . It just held its U.S. premiere at the Camden International Film Festival in Maine after bowing at the Venice Film Festival earlier in September. Watch on Deadline UPS workers walk a ‘practice picket line’ on July 7, 2023, in New York City, ahead of a possible strike. TIMOTHY A. CLARY/AFP via Getty Images Union Town follows the battle for better wages and working conditions on three fronts in New York City — at UPS, at Amazon, and among “deliveristas” – that is, people who work for apps like DoorDash making food runs for customers. “I think that they [labor organizers] have a big fight on their hands, but I think that they’re road warriors and I feel an awful lot of hope,” Kopple tells Deadline in an interview at the Camden Opera House, where Union Town screened. “Each time they win something, it’s glorious. It’s wonderful. And they get a little closer and a little closer. And what else can you do? You have to keep fighting… Looking at the people that they work with who can hardly make a living or people who die in the plants because there’s no air conditioning [in summer] or no heat in the winter, it’s just a very human thing to do, so you can’t stop.” In the past four decades, union participation in America has dropped by about half. “[But] they’re still there. They’re still there,” Kopple says of unions. “And if you don’t have them, you don’t have anything.” Director Barbara Kopple with Antonio Rosario, a Teamsters union organizer, at the U.S. premiere of ‘Union Town’ at the Camden International Film Festival on Sept. 19, 2026 in Camden, Maine. Matthew Carey She points to Antonio Rosario, a veteran of a 1997 strike at UPS who serves as the Teamsters lead union organizer for Amazon workers in the northeast. At one moment in the film, Rosario is with his young sons at the dinner table and holds a bundle of sticks in his hands to illustrate the importance of worker solidarity. “Tony is trying to show them the difference that if you have a lot of people together, it takes too much to break it,” Kopple explains. “And if you just have one stick, you can break it. And that’s what it is. It’s people who have your back. It’s people who will help you and it gives you a sense of strength that you can change.” Of the three groups seen in the documentary, deliveristas face the worst conditions and pay – they work year-round in every kind of weather, driving their bikes through snow in winter, for instance. Kopple documents the case of Victor Hidalgo, a 24-year-old man who was working for a pharmacy delivery company in 2024 when a New York Fire Department vehicle hit his bicycle, killing him. At a Q&A following the U.S. premiere, Kopple said Hidalgo’s aunt urged her to put him in the documentary. “She said, ‘I don’t want anyone to ever forget Victor,’” Kopple recounted. “’Please come and film the funeral. Please come and let people know that these things really happen.’” A DoorDash delivery person prepares to bike in the snow in New York City. Noam Galai/Getty Images Deliveristas rely on tips as a major source of income, but customers often don’t give them much (one deliverista recalls a person opening his hand to deposit a tip and placing in his palm a piece of candy). What’s worse, the tips they receive through the app may not go to them; in 2025 DoorDash reached a nearly $17 million settlement in New York after being accused of effectively taking workers’ tips. (Per the New York Attorney General’s office, “Customers were misled into believing their tips would directly benefit Dashers. Instead, DoorDash would keep the tips meant for Dashers and take it out of their guaranteed pay. DoorDash would guarantee pay to a delivery worker, and then only actually pay them whatever the tip did not cover.”). “What it does if people get to see this film is maybe they’ll give big tips. Maybe they’ll talk to the people who deliver or at least understand them,” Kopple says. “Ever since UPS got their contract, every time I see a UPS truck, I stop and I talk to the driver and I say, ‘So how’s your contract? How’s work?’ And they’re looking at me like, ‘Who’s this crazy person?’ But it’s wonderful to do it… [It shows] somebody cares. Somebody’s out there who cares about them. They’re not invisible.” Producer Peter Palandjian, Teamsters union organizer Antonio Rosario, director Barbara Kopple, and producer Hannes Hosp attend the ‘Union Town’ photocall at the Venice Film Festival on September 9, 2026. Aurore Marechal/Getty Images Autlook is handling worldwide film sales for Union Town . The 2024 documentary Union , about the successful effort to organize workers at an Amazon facility in Staten Island, NY, struggled to find U.S. distribution (it was clear Prime Video wouldn’t touch it). That film by Stephen Maing and Brett Story is now streaming through Criterion. Kopple says it’s “too soon to tell” about potential distribution of Union Town . “This was the third time the film has ever shown, and I had just finished it maybe two weeks before Venice. So, it’s totally at the beginning. Acme’ Nears $100M WW – Global Box Office Update Post-Merger Paramount May Overdeliver On Settlement Terms With 36-Film 2027 Slate Amid Speculation About Duplication & WB Leadership Paramount-Warner Bros Penalty If Merger Fails To Release 30 Pics A Year: Divest Miramax View All September 21, 2026 7:17pm 'A Minecraft Movie'; 'A Quiet Place Part II'; 'Sonic the Hedgehog 2'; 'Superman' Warner Bros.; Jonny Cournoyer / Paramount Pictures; Paramount Pictures; Warner Bros.; all Courtesy Everett Collection California Attorney General Rob Bonta can rest easy: A merged Paramount Warner Bros. Discovery would already account for 36 movies on the release schedule for 2027. Note, that’s an organic number of theatrical releases which were always set to happen even before the union of the storied studios came together . As for 2028, the combined entity currently accounts for 25 theatrical releases, hence another five titles are needed to meet the state AGs’ agreed-upon settlement term of 30 films in the merger’s first two years of existence. That should be easy, it’s still early, and awards season fare often gets dated later rather than sooner. Related Stories News Paramount Settlement Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta, Who Says Deal Is “Not A Blessing” Of WBD Merger News Done! Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit, Set To Seal Deal For Warner Bros. Discovery Beyond 2029, the AGs’ demand from the merged entity is for 32 films annually over three years. It’s on Ellison to make sure this union isn’t a repeat of Disney-Fox. Missing the annual theatrical release quota could cost Paramount — per the pact with the AGs — its 49% investment in Miramax. In addition, per Bonta, “For each film that they fail to make, should they fail to make any, $30M is paid to be split three different ways, but 90% of it goes to workers.” Watch on Deadline Despite all the pom pom waving that the house of Harry Potter and Batman are now one with the house of Transformers, Star Trek and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, the question becomes, how will Ellison’s Paramount wrangle this beast? If merged today, both studios combined would count $838.3M at the YTD domestic box office (Jan. 1-Sept. 20) for an 11% market share, ranking fourth behind Universal ($1.78 billion), Sony ($1.22B) and Walt Disney ($1.03B) — global annual numbers were not available at the time of this report for Paramount or Warners. However, Universal leads all studios with around $5B WW, followed by Disney with $4B-plus WW. Rumors that both studios would have to operate separately were wrong. We hear that as Ellison eyes his early corporate structure that one or two executives would oversee overall theatrical and film strategy and likely one or two executives would oversee each film brand. Note that this is all fluid and still in the works. In addition, how the new conglomerate plans to deal with the duplication of marketing and distribution groups is in wait and see mode. Per the release breakdown below, there are plenty of weekends where the studios are dating against each other on the same weekend. In most instances, it’s a matter of counterprogramming — e.g. May 21, 2027, when family animated Warners pic Bad Fairies opens against a new James Wan Paranormal Activity film. However, it’s arguably unprecedented for a major studio to shell out on marketing for two big films from two big labels in the same weekend. Note: It hasn’t been uncommon of late for a big studio to face-off against its adult specialty label — e.g. Universal going up against a Focus Features title. The one glaring tentpole-on-top-of-a-tentpole frame is June 30, 2028 where Paramount’s feature take of video game Call of Duty is up against DC’s Dynamic Duo. Also, there’s the situation of some serious summer stacking. July 2027 has James Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow followed by Crawl 2 (granted, it’s a counterprogrammer) followed by Ocean’s Prequel and A Quiet Place III. Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani Warner Bros. On the bright side, before this year is over, the combined entity has a possible billion dollar hit and award contender in Warner Bros/Legendary’s Denis Villeneuve Dune: Part Three, which could create another Barbenheimer effect at the box office in its competition with Disney/Marvel Studio’s Avengers: Doomsday on Dec. 18. While the studios can operate separately, Bonta says when it comes to negotiating and creating a marketplace where there isn’t reduced competition, “We basically ensure the status quo competition with negotiations (remaining) separately. It’s as if the companies never merged. They can’t bundle their basic cable channel assets. They can’t use them together to reduce competition…They have to remain separate and independent in their negotiations, and when they’re working with the cable companies. Same with the theatrical release. “Usually, when you see [a deal that] reduces competition, you see people paying more for less. So you see less output, less quality. And you see higher prices. We address that by making sure that the fees remain flat, for the three years between the merch company and the exhibitors, the theaters. And then the requirement, this incredible, massive requirement for production output, cures for the less part, instead of paying more for less. You have the flat fee requirement with massive increase in production. So that’s how we address the concerns about reduced competition,” explained California’s AG this morning. The multi-billion dollar question as far as box office goes is whether Warner Bros. Motion Picture Chairs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy make the jump to the new entity. De Luca told us earlier this year that no matter which way the merger went (Netflix or Paramount), “We’re hoping to stay the course.” Last year was a banner year for the duo with $4.3 billion WW. This year, there haven’t been as many hits, but the longtime production partners are known for their excellent relationships with filmmakers like their recent Oscar winners Paul Thomas Anderson, Ryan Coolger as well as Alejandro Inarritu and Zach Cregger, to name a few. Rumors have swirled about DeLuca and Abdy heading over to Sony, or Netflix (that latter rumor fueled around town after their longtime comms chief Katie Martin Kelly departed Warners for the streamer). The reality is that the duo have a four-year extension on their contacts until 2030 to run Warners. A world where the pro-theatrical De Luca and Abdy continue to stay at the helm of their ship isn’t out of the question. Ellison said in a memo to Paramount staff today, “We are tentatively planning to close in approximately two weeks.” Get ready… Here’s how the release schedule looks at this point in time for mid-October 2026 through the end of 2028. Acme’ Nears $100M WW – Global Box Office Update Post-Merger Paramount May Overdeliver On Settlement Terms With 36-Film 2027 Slate Amid Speculation About Duplication & WB Leadership Paramount-Warner Bros Penalty If Merger Fails To Release 30 Pics A Year: Divest Miramax View All September 21, 2026 8:00pm RESIDENT EVIL, Austin Abrams, 2026. © Sony Pictures Releasing / Courtesy Everett Collection UPDATED: TriStar Pictures/Constantin Film/Davis Films’ Resident Evil rang up a massive $108.3M worldwide , not only the best start the franchise has ever seen, but also Zach Cregger ‘s biggest start as filmmaker surpassing the $70M WW reported opening of last year’s Weapons. What was the previous biggest opener in the Resident Evil franchise? We’re told it was 2012’s Resident Evil: Retribution which bowed to $70.6M WW (note that included Russia and Japan in its first suite at the time). The movie finaled at $240M WW. In addition, the opening alone for Resident Evil beats the global final of the original 2002 movie ($102.9M) as well as the last title, the failed reboot Welcome to Raccoon City ($41.9M). Currently, 2016’s Resident Evil: The Final Chapter stands as the highest grossing title in the series with $312M (51% of that coming from China or $159.5M). Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'Resident Evil' Scores $60M U.S. Opening: Best Ever For Zach Cregger & Franchise - Box Office Update News 'Resident Evil's Austin Abrams Recalls "Harrowing" Stunt Shoot For Zach Cregger's Video Game Adaptation: "You Don't Wanna F*ck Up" Also, get this but this zombie shoot-em up paced like Scream 7, in fact even better (that pic opened to a franchise best $63.5M and $97M worldwide. Comps to Scream 7 were iffy on Thursday night, until they became real. For a horror pic this year at the worldwide B.O., it’s the second best after Backrooms ‘ $118M. In terms of pure international debuts for a horror movie YTD, Resident Evil ‘s $48.3M is the best for the genre, higher than Backrooms ‘ $36.6M. Resident Evil is 66% over Weapons , 33% above A Quiet Place: Day One , and 18% ahead of Alien: Romulus on a like-for-like basis at current exchange rates. What’s impressive is that the movie expanded its audience beyond the Milla Jovovich movies. UK at $5.8M was the top territory (in reported, 2010’s 3D charged Afterlife bowed to $2.5M there). Mexico followed at $5.6M (higher than Afterlife ‘s reported $3.2M). Metropolitan had French speaking markets, while Constantin had Germany speaking markets. France did $2.6M (higher than Final Chapter ‘s reported $1M start). Germany counted $2.5M (higher than Final Chapter ‘s reported $1.3M), Other top markets were Australia ($2.6M), Spain ($2.3M), Brazil ($2.0M), Italy ($1.7M), Saudi Arabia ($1.6M), UAE ($1.4M), Indonesia ($1.4M), Malaysia ($1.3M), Taiwan ($1.2M), the Philippines ($1.2M), and India ($1.1M). And there’s 13% of foreign markets left to go, and they’re big territories for the franchise, i.e. Thailand (Sept. 24), Japan (Oct. 9) and China (still to be dated). South Africa is opening on Sept. 23 while Central Asia is Sept. 24. Final Chapter ‘s $159.5M in the Middle Kingdom is looked at as an anomaly: Just a perfect place in time and space for a Resident Evil in regards to the types of U.S. action movies that fared well in China, in addition to the game’s popularity. Japan was the second highest territory for Final Chapter at $36.4M. In addition, A24’s highest grossing movie ever, Backrooms , clicked past the $400M mark at the global box office. THE ODYSSEY, Cyclops, 2026. © Universal Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection Universal’s The Odyssey was second around the globe in its tenth frame with $21.3M WW in 85 territories ($4.95M domestic, $16.4M int’l) for a worldwide running total of $1.72B (Universal’s highest as we told you with $1.11B offshore, $609.8M domestic). Korea added $3.1M in first place for a $91.6M tally, sailing past Avengers: Endgame ‘s lifetime total and becoming the third biggest Hollywood movie of all-time in the territory behind Avatar 1 and 2. China’s sixth frame was $2M and a $107.7M running cume, yes, still Christopher Nolan’s second-highest grossing there behind Interstellar. Japan added $1.8M in Wknd 2, reaching $7.9M cume, performing well above Oppenheimer at the same point, as well as The Dark Knight Rises . The Odyssey clicked past Dune: Part Two ‘s lifetime total earlier this week. Germany grossed $1.2M in its tenth frame for a $64M cume. ‘Practical Magic 2’ Warner Bros./Courtesy Everett Collection Do you believe in magic, in an old studio’s heart? If so, then Warner Bros’ Practical Magic 2 ranked third on the global charts with $19.1M WW ($12.1M domestic, $7M offshore), $76.8M WW ($50M domestic, $26.8M foreign) for the net $75M production. Top five territory totals are UK ($7.5M), Australia ($3.6M), Mexico ($2.4M), Germany ($1.3M) and Spain ($1.2M). The first 1998 movie finaled at $94.4M WW. Fourth is the eighth session of Sony /Marvel’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day with $17.2M WW ($10.8M offshore, $6.4M domestic) and a running global cume of $2.478B ($944.4M all-time running stateside cume, $1.53B offshore). Pic is in play on 17,500 screens in 67 markets. ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Warner Bros. Stand-up and applaud Ketchup Entertainment’s rescue of Warner Bros Animation’s Coyote Vs. Acme as the movie is on the edge, on the edge of cracking $100M WW with $54.7M in U.S./Canada and $44.3M abroad in 46 territories. That adds up to $99M after a global fourth frame of $10.5M ($4.4M domestic, $6.1M abroad) in the No. 5 worldwide spot. Warner Bros wrote off for $30M on the $70M project which Ketchup acquired global on for $50M (and then sold off foreign on). Other notables: Angel Studio’s action movie Runner starring Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson minted $4.466M from 31 territories worldwide, of that $1.28M was from offshore and $3.1M domestic. Running global is $15.2M (with $11.9M from domestic). China’s Once Upon a Time in the Middle East from Muye Wen continued to lead the box office in China with a $4.3M weekend ahead of local film V and The Odyssey. Guess how much Middle East has made to date there? $323.8M. OBSESSION, from left: Inde Navarrette, Michael Johnston, 2025. © Focus Features /Courtesy Everett Collection Focus Features’ Obsession minted $2M from offshore this weekend with a current global running cume of $516.7M . That was largely driven by Korea’s third weekend was $1.4M, ranking third behind The Odyssey and local remake The Intern for a $5.6M cume, surpassing the lifetimes of It, Annabelle, Insidious, Five Nights at Freddy’s and A Quiet Place: Day One , in addition to having already overtaken a number of tentpole horrors earlier in the run. ‘Forgotten Island’ DreamWorks / © Universal Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection Universal/DreamWorks Animation’s Forgotten Island started its offshore rollout and know that it’s staggered. The Joel Crawford and Januel P. Mercado directed movie doesn’t hit our shores until Sept. 25. For now, it’s made $1.5M from Mexico, Australia and New Zealand. Mexico posted $900K for a No. 3 rank which includes $400K of previews from last weekend and Wednesday’s Independence Day public holiday. Audience reactions and sentiment are positive with crowds attracted to the pic’s beauty and emotion. Australia bowed to $500K, No. 7 in the territory on 285 screens. Business on Saturday and Sunday was impacted by warm and dry weather and football semi-finals for both the AFL (football) and NRL (rugby). Very good audience and critics reactions are teeing the pic up for a solid run during the upcoming school holidays, which began today across 50% of the country. articles.title: ‘Trump TV’ Promo Uses Clips From ‘The Simpsons,’ ‘Seinfeld,’ ‘Friends,’ ‘The Dark Knight’ & Many More
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Tom Tapp Tom Tapp Deputy Managing Editor More Stories By Tom ‘Trump TV’ Promo Uses Clips From ‘The Simpsons,’ ‘Seinfeld,’ ‘Friends,’ ‘The Dark Knight’ & Many More Presley Gerber Dies: Model, Son Of Cindy Crawford & Rande Gerber Was 27 Ke Huy Quan Reveals “Life Changing” Gesture From Spielberg & Lucas When He Was A Kid View All September 21, 2026 8:46pm YouTube Donald Trump has defied copyright complaints from Neil Young, Ariana Grande, Beyoncé and everyone in between for unauthorized use of their music. Today, it posted a promo video for Trump TV that made use of footage from Friends, The Simpsons, Family Guy, Home Alone, Modern Family, Breaking Bad, The Dark Knight , The Office, SpongeBob SquarePants, Parks and Recreation, That ’70s Show and more. Related Stories News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Journalists Denied White House Entry; Colleagues Condemn Trump’s Ban News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Sue Donald Trump Over His White House Ban Among the studios and networks whose IP is used in the promo are Warner Bros., Fox, Nickelodeon, Sony Pictures Television, Disney and NBCUniversal. It’s not a terribly unusual move for the president, who routinely posts AI videos that lift scenes from hit films like Top Gun . It is, however, somewhat unique in its breadth. And perhaps that is the point. Trump TV is a promotional effort launched after the president banned Politico, CNN and MS Now from the White House . The administration billed it “The Essentials Station.” Another (grammatically-challenged) administration pitch for the service was, “Not every big moment has made it on your tv, now it can.” The service provides a live feed of official events, seemingly without the razzle dazzle of which the president is so fond. The New York Times dubbed it “essentially a form of state television.” Watch on Deadline IT'S LIVE. 📺🦅 TRUMP TV IS STREAMING NOW. 24/7, updated in real time, with top past moments, announcements, and the latest and greatest from the administration all in one place. Not every big moment has made it on your tv, now it can. 📲 https://t.co/3KwWkBZ69m pic.twitter.com/g4v7n2J04s — The White House (@WhiteHouse) September 21, 2026 The advent of Trump TV comes after the president denied Politico, CNN and MS Now access to the White House over the weekend, prompting outcry from other media and a lawsuit from the trio . CNN had the White House pool assignment for Monday and was scheduled to be the primary network for coverage. The other TV networks declined to replace CNN in protest of the move, and as a result, there was no TV pool on a day when Trump is traveled to New York. The lack of network-level production is apparent. Video posted on the White House YouTube channel this weekend includes a long, very unTrumpy nine-minute recount of a ribbon cutting. It includes long takes of the president shaking hands with attendees before proceeding to make his remarks.
