articles.full_text: Obituaries Editor Rose Friedman, who helped shape NPR's cultural coverage, dies at 38 September 18, 2026 10:44 PM ET Heard on Weekend Edition Saturday By Elizabeth Blair RF Listen · 2:54 2:54 Transcript Toggle more options Download Embed Embed < iframe src="https://www.npr.org/player/embed/nx-s1-5973098/nx-s1-9933041" width="100%" height="290" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" title="NPR embedded audio player"> Transcript Friedman was in her early 20s when she landed her first position as an editorial assistant at NPR. She became an editor and reporter, and a co-creator of the annual Books We Love reading guide. Beth Novey/NPR hide caption toggle caption Beth Novey/NPR NPR has lost one of its finest journalists. For 15 years, Rose Friedman was an editor and reporter who helped shape NPR's arts and cultural coverage. She was one of the co-creators of the popular Books We Love reading guide and, most recently, helped lead NPR's America 250 series. Friedman died at home, of cancer, in New York City on Sept. 17 at the age of 38. Rose Friedman was an editor to the end. She said she wanted the second line of her obituary to acknowledge her role as a shop steward for SAG-AFTRA, the union that represents NPR's editorial workers. She wanted the line to say that her "proudest achievement" was helping convince NPR to increase its paid parental leave. Not the second line but still pretty high up in the story. Rose would understand. Rose Friedman was in her early 20s when she landed her first position as an editorial assistant at NPR Books. She became deeply sourced in the publishing industry and seemed to have read everything . She edited book reviews and features such as This Week's Must Read . She wrote numerous appreciations of authors, including Herman Wouk and the legendary editor Sonny Mehta . For the Book Concierge , which was later renamed Books We Love , Rose helped pore over hundreds of titles nominated by NPR staff and critics, and whittle them down into a robust reader's guide. "She was voracious," said novelist Meg Wolitzer, who worked with Rose on a number of NPR reviews and features. "What a gifted, delightful, brilliant, deeply kind person. And I would say a true enthusiast. I got so much working with Rose." Even as a young staffer in the NPR newsroom, Rose had an old school journalist's sensibility. She was endlessly curious but always skeptical. She strived for clarity and depth but also humor and surprise. Food Cooking Chicken In A Pig's Bladder (It Sounds Better In French) With Bill Buford Food was one of her favorite subjects. The first thing we hear her say in her profile of chef Bill Buford : " I have to tell you — this does not smell very good." For many years Rose was my editor. When I once pitched her a story on an artist who was trending, Rose scoffed, "Isn't she just for Instagram?" She always pushed back on "hot takes" and stories that she didn't think had substance. But sometimes that pushback was intended to make reporters work harder. Not kill an idea altogether. "She had so much integrity," said Theo Balcomb, a former supervising editor for NPR's All Things Considered and now a senior editor at The Atlantic . She and Rose met early in their careers at NPR and became close friends. "She would care more about 'Was this true?' or as holistic as we could get than, 'Is it buzzy?'" Balcomb said. "She had a strong sense of purpose." In 2020, Rose was NPR's lead reporter on the sexual assault trial of former movie executive Harvey Weinstein. The testimony from Weinstein's alleged victims haunted her. Rose edited numerous #MeToo stories. In 2018, we shared a National Headliner Award for our feature "Women Are Speaking Up About Harassment And Abuse, But Why Now?" Rose Friedman grew up in Newton, Mass. She studied labor history at Macalester College in St. Paul, Minn. For her dissertation she researched worker solidarity across ethnic lines at an iron range in Minnesota. Her paper won the Barbara Wertheimer Prize in Labor History from the New York Labor History Association. Books What Bestseller Lists Really Tell Us About A Book's Popularity Rose brought her passion for labor rights to NPR. She and NPR correspondent Tom Dreisbach were on the SAG-AFTRA committee that convinced the company to increase its paid parental leave. " Rose's thought was, 'let's go big,'" Dreisbach remembered. Rose loved being a mom to her two children. "She said having babies is the best thing in the world and that the first six months with a baby, you don't get it back," said Dreisbach. Rose and her partner, Andrew Anastasi, were avid travelers and daring foodies. Balcomb remembered them ordering an entire pig's head at a beer garden in Washington, D.C. On a visit with Rose and Andrew when they were living in Italy, Dreisbach said she "insisted" they order the "spleen sandwich" at a certain market in Palermo. Dreisbach said he will remember Rose as someone who was "able to find more delight in life than almost anyone. Every day is a new adventure." Author Interviews Before summer ends, let's squeeze in one last trip to 'Our Pool' Her friend and colleague Natalie Winston agreed: "No one lives in the moment more than Rose." Winston visited Rose in the spring of 2025 after she'd had surgery. She figured they would stay home and that she would cook for Rose and help clean their apartment. "And she's like, 'We're going to Chinatown to get dumplings, eat them on a park bench, take the ferry to Ikea in Brooklyn.' She just wanted to explore everything," said Winston. In addition to her children and her partner, Rose is survived by her parents Carolyn and Jerry Friedman, her sisters Sophie and Nina and numerous admiring friends and colleagues. We will miss her wisdom, generosity, infectious humor and, above all, her voice. NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR. BBC Calls On Producers To Pitch “Brave” New Vision For Sci-Fi Series View All September 14, 2026 9:00am Macklemore performs on May 15, 2024 in Melbourne, Australia. Morgan Hancock/Getty Images American rapper Macklemore will no longer be supporting Ed Sheeran ‘s Loop Tour amid a backlash against his “free Palestine” pleas. As the 4x Grammy winner took the stage for Sheeran’s tour earlier this month at MetLife Stadium, he called for “safety and peace” for all before performing his protest song “Hind’s Hall.” He later emphasized that his support for Palestinians is “in no way a criticism” of Jewish people. “To all of my Jewish brothers and sisters; criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide, in no way is a criticism of you,” he said on stage. Related Stories News Princess Di Returns To 'SNL UK' As "Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android" In Cold Open Skewering King Charles, Ed Sheeran & AI News Ed Sheeran Admits To "Making Mistakes" With Macklemore, Calls Out "Systemic Injustice" In Gaza: "I'm So, So Sorry" In a statement, first shared with Rolling Stone, Messina Touring Group, promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s Loop Tour, said: “As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans. After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates.” Watch on Deadline Macklemore posted a detailed response on Instagram, in which he reflected on difficult conversations with Sheeran and said his future on the tour was of no consequence when compared with the situation in Gaza. “I didn’t need 10 shows from Ed. I needed 2. Two chances to stand in front of 90,000 people and say the words that somehow became too dangerous to say. Free Palestine,” he wrote. “But if those words cost me the stage, while turning the conversation back to Palestine, then it was the most successful tour I’ve ever been on.” View this post on Instagram The decision followed the Israeli-American Council starting a petition urging Sheeran to “remove Macklemore” from the remainder of the tour. “This was an Ed Sheeran concert – not a political rally, not a protest, and not an activist event,” the petition reads. “The issue is not whether Macklemore has the right to hold political views. The question is where the line should be drawn when an opening act uses a global concert platform to advance a one-sided political agenda.” Macklemore wrote his 2024 protest anthem “Hind’s Hall” in support of pro-Palestinian protests on college campuses, named for Columbia students’ renaming of academic building Hamilton Hall to Hind’s Hall, in honor of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab, who was killed in Gaza. ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $53M+ Open ‘Ride Or Die’ Canceled By Prime Video After One Season, Being Shopped By Paramount Block The Merger & Elizabeth Warren Call Out Possible Lawsuit Deal Lucas Museum Opening Photos: Oprah, Laura Dern, Mark Hamill & More Read More About: 16 Comments

articles.title: Cate Blanchett Asks London Audience To Stop Filming Play, Says Stage Is Place “Where We Can Simply Be Together And Be Present”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Rose Friedman Dies: NPR Arts Editor & ‘Books We Love’ Co-Creator Was 38 Cate Blanchett Asks London Audience To Stop Filming Play, Says Stage Is Place “Where We Can Simply Be Together And Be Present” Editors Guild Praises California’s New Post-Production Tax Credit Law As “Historic” View All September 19, 2026 11:41am Nina Hoss and Cate Blanchett in “Electra/Persona” Monika Rittershaus Enjoying the show? Then please put away your cellphone. That was the message delivered by Cate Blachett from the London stage of National Theatre ’s Lyttelton Theatre after the curtain call of Electra/Persona , the new play written and directed by Benedict Andrews that combines the Sophocles tragedy Electra with Ingmar Bergman’s Persona. Still in her stage costume of a black t-shirt and baggy black trousers, Blanchett, who stars opposite Nina Hoss in the play, spoke in a heartfelt and calm manner directly to the audience in an address that has been widely shared on social media. (Watch it below.) Related Stories News Cate Blanchett To Attend Tokyo Film Festival With Displacement Film Fund Shorts News 'Oh, Mary!' Live Capture Starring Cole Escola To Debut On HBO & HBO Max In 2027 Said Blanchett, “There are few places on this planet where we can simply be together and be present. I understand you like filming the curtain call – and it is kind of flattering in a way – but for anyone who is filming the show, please don’t, because it spoils it for the next group of people who come in and are present with us. So thank you very much.” Watch on Deadline The speech was greeted enthusiastically by the National Theatre audience. The play, which runs through October 10, has Blanchett and Hoss sharing the roles of Electra/Elisabeth and Clytemnestra/Alma, with a coin toss determining who plays what role on any given night. Here’s how the National Theatre describes the production as “a thrilling production [that] fuses ancient myth and modern psychology in a powerful exploration of identity, and the fragile line between who we are and who we play.” The synopsis continues, “Electra. A daughter consumed by grief and rage, clinging to the idea of justice as her world comes apart. Persona. During a performance of Electra, an actress suddenly falls silent. What follows is a rupture: two women drawn into an intense, unsettling encounter where speech breaks down and the boundaries between self and role give way.” In addition to Blanchett and Hoss, the cast features Ella Lily Hyland. articles.title: Block The Merger & Elizabeth Warren Call Out AGs For Betrayal In Deal Talks With Paramount: “A Win Only For David Ellison”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Block The Merger & Elizabeth Warren Call Out AGs For Betrayal In Deal Talks With Paramount: “A Win Only For David Ellison” Deadline’s L.A. Law Summit: Nina Shaw & Patricia Glaser Honored On Day Of Big Ideas, Big Insights; Watch The Video Presentations Paramount And State AGs Begin Preliminary Talks Ahead Of October Settlement Meetings View All September 19, 2026 12:22pm Paramount and Warner Bros. Towers Getty Images Whatever the true state of settlement talks this weekend among Paramount , a coalition of state Attorneys General and the Writers Guild of America to end the antitrust action over the $111 billion Warner Bros Discovery merger, the people against the deal from the beginning are not going quietly. “As Trump tries to ban CNN from the White House, it would be a massive mistake to cave on the Paramount merger,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) said Saturday morning as the current WBD-owned CNN and MS Now journalists were denied access to the Executive Mansion . “The last thing we need is another Trump-controlled media conglomerate abusing its power to stomp out competition. This is a dangerous merger.” Related Stories News Editors Guild Praises California’s New Post-Production Tax Credit Law As “Historic” Legal Deadline’s L.A. Law Summit Photo Gallery: A Packed House Of Power Players, Honorees & More Compared to Warren, the A-list-supported Block the Merger is truly angry and feeling betrayed. Watch on Deadline “The rumored ‘deal’ to usher the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger forward is an insult to everyone who has stood up against this harmful transaction and to the hundreds of thousands of workers, journalists, and consumers who will be hurt if it goes forward,” the DC-based group told Deadline today of reported behind-closed-doors negotiations underway right now. “Let’s be very clear: an agreement based on unenforceable concessions is a win only for David Ellison . It is an L for everyone else.” As leaks of talks between the AGs, led by California’s politically ambitious AG Rob Bonta , and the Ellison-run Paramount flooded the media late Friday, the possible L (loss) that BTM are spotlighting could include guardrails around CNN editorial independence, some selloffs and job assurances. The hope down on Melrose is such a deal would render moot the March 2, 2027, trial start date currently on the calendar in federal court — and all the financial and political blast radius that comes with it for the Trump-friendly Ellisons. To that, with massive job, production and tax-revenue losses on the table, Paramount’s plan B for the last eight weeks has been to pressure Bonta from all sides to make a deal. Two days of court-ordered settlement talks have already been set for mid-October, but that’s procedural in the judicial system and widely expected to go nowhere fast. Also, mid-October doesn’t quite line up with Ellison’s balance sheet. Looking at an October 1 date in which a $7 million-a-day ticking fee to WBD shareholders begins, as well as a September 24 hearing on a Hail Mary desire for a $1.88 billion bond from the states and the WGA , Ellison’s crew has been leaking more than ever threats to exit California for a red state. Even as the likes of outgoing California Gov. Gavin Newsom acknowledged privately at the recent Primetime Emmys that the Ellisons were being too heavy-handed, the multi-pronged pressure campaign seems to have paid off. Whereas Bonta once accused Paramount of “blackmail” with its threats and theatrical promises, the reelection-seeking AG now has his lieutenants in the room with Ellison’s execs. The latest word on the wire is the parties could have an agreement before the official start of Yom Kippur this weekend. Word is also out there that New York AG Letitia James isn’t as “in step,” according to a source, with Bonta as she was when it came to burying the hatchet with Paramount. There is also the wildcard of the WGA, which joined the AGs’ July 13 suit after filing an anti-merger action of its own. “This is such bullsh*t,” an industry insider told Deadline this morning of the ParaBros talks. “Bonta should have called their bluff, instead he caved,” she added, noting such tactics are typical of Democratic politicians in the MAGA era. Block the Merger, with its support from such names as Bryan Cranston , Hannah Einbinder, Bradley Whitford, W. Kamau Bell, Kristen Vangsness, Jane Fonda and Rati Gupta, wasn’t quite as blunt today in its statement, but the vibe was much the same. “Thousands of industry leaders took a risk when they spoke out publicly about the harm the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger would cause,” said the outfit, which also counts Noah Wyle , Denis Villeneuve, Atsuko Okatsuka, Damon Lindelof and Sofia Coppola among its backers. Claiming that more than 75,000 people have joined them to tell the state AGs to stand strong including national leaders like Warren, the group said, “We know a bad deal when we see one. AG Bonta and his fellow state AGs should reject this deal, stand strong, and fully block the merger with no concessions.” That mention of Warren may have greater significance this weekend than initially apparent. Like everyone else, Paramount is keenly aware of what the polls are projecting going into November’s midterms. If the midterms actually occur and if the new Congress is actually seated (two big ifs in America right now), a projected Democratic majority in the House and Senate have promised to probe and even break up mega media mergers. Even with Oracle founder Larry Ellison the primary backer of his son’s ParaBros dreams, the even older Ellison’s net worth, which has been declining of late, may not be able to handle the strain of months and months of such probes. So perhaps it is the first week of November, not October 1, that is the calendar date the younger Ellison is hoping to beat this weekend. Paramount has been in “no comment” mode for weeks since the Melrose lot got burned on allegations of leaks detailing past preliminary talks with Bonta’s gang. Bonta’s office did not respond Saturday to Deadline’s request for comment on Warren and Block the Merger’s opposition to the talks. ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $53M+ Open ‘Ride Or Die’ Canceled By Prime Video After One Season, Being Shopped By Paramount Block The Merger & Elizabeth Warren Call Out Possible Lawsuit Deal Lucas Museum Opening Photos: Oprah, Laura Dern, Mark Hamill & More Read More About: 9 Comments

articles.title: Rose Friedman Dies: NPR Arts Editor & ‘Books We Love’ Co-Creator Was 38
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Rose Friedman Dies: NPR Arts Editor & ‘Books We Love’ Co-Creator Was 38 Cate Blanchett Asks London Audience To Stop Filming Play, Says Stage Is Place “Where We Can Simply Be Together And Be Present” Editors Guild Praises California’s New Post-Production Tax Credit Law As “Historic” View All September 19, 2026 1:02pm Rose Friedman of NPR Beth Novey/NPR/Getty Rose Friedman , an NPR editor and reporter who shaped the public radio network’s arts & culture coverage and co-created its popular reading guide Books We Love, died of cancer Thursday, September 17, at her home in New York City. She was 38. Her death was announced on-air by NPR’s Elizabeth Blair, who called Friedman one of the outlet’s finest journalists. In an obituary and tribute posted on NPR’s website, Blair said, “Rose Friedman was an editor to the end. She said she wanted the second line of her obituary to acknowledge her role as a shop steward for SAG-AFTRA, the union that represents NPR’s editorial workers. She wanted the line to say that her ‘proudest achievement’ was helping convince NPR to increase its paid parental leave.” Related Stories News Anthony Page Dies: Tony-Winning, Emmy-Nominated Director Of Stage & Screen Was 90 News Lea Michele Remembers Duncan Sheik: Death Of 'Spring Awakening' Composer "Does Not Seem Real" Friedman joined NPR as an editorial assistant in her early 20s in 2010. She later served as an editor and reporter, becoming deeply sourced in the publishing industry, editing book reviews and features and writing appreciations of book world personalities such as author Herman Wouk and editor Sonny Mehta. Watch on Deadline She co-created what was initially called the Book Concierge, later renamed Books We Love. Reading over hundreds of titles nominated by NPR staff and critics, Friedman narrowed the list to the popular reader’s guide. “She was voracious,” novelist Meg Wolitzer, who worked with Friedman on a number of NPR reviews and features, said to NPR. “What a gifted, delightful, brilliant, deeply kind person. And I would say a true enthusiast. I got so much working with Rose.” Raised in Newton, Mass., Friedman is survived by her partner Andrew Anastasi, two children, parents and two sisters. ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $53M+ Open ‘Ride Or Die’ Canceled By Prime Video After One Season, Being Shopped By Paramount Block The Merger & Elizabeth Warren Call Out Possible Lawsuit Deal Lucas Museum Opening Photos: Oprah, Laura Dern, Mark Hamill & More Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Melissa Barrera Says It’s “So Beautiful” To See Support For Macklemore Speaking Up On Palestine: “I Didn’t Get That When It Happened To Me”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Ed Sheeran Admits To “Making Mistakes” With Macklemore, Calls Out “Systemic Injustice” In Gaza: “I’m So, So Sorry” Mark Ruffalo Urges AG Bonta “Do Not Cave” On Paramount Deal, Suggests Protest Outside Oakland Office: “The People Don’t Want It!” ‘Sweet Magnolias’ Creator Bids Farewell To Serenity, S.C. After Netflix Show Ends: “Keep Pouring It Out!” View All September 19, 2026 2:08pm Melissa Barrera comments on Macklemore's Palestine support. Steven Ferdman/Getty Images/Morgan Hancock/Getty Images Nearly three years after she was fired from the Scream franchise for speaking up in support of Palestinians, Melissa Barrera sees the tides changing. The actress recently expressed how “emotional” it made her to see Fennias and Ed Sheeran ‘s other openers dropping out of his Loop Tour in support of Macklemore , who was dropped from the tour over his “ Free Palestine ” remarks. “It was so beautiful to see Finneas and the band and all the opening acts pulling out in support of Macklemore. It made me emotional,” Barrera told the Associated Press . “You know, I didn’t get that when it happened to me. I didn’t have any of that happen. It was too soon. People were too scared. But it’s good to see that almost three years later, at least things have changed.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Ed Sheeran Tour Openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe And Lukas Graham Plus Band Beoga Withdraw After Macklemore Dropped For “Free Palestine” Remarks News Melissa Barrera Appears To React To ‘Scream 7’ Premiere Protest: “I See You” Spyglass fired Barrera in November 2023 over her social media posts on the Israel-Hamas conflict and the “atrocities being committed against Palestinians,” explaining the company has “zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form, including false references to genocide, ethnic cleansing, Holocaust distortion or anything that flagrantly crosses the line into hate speech.” Following her ousting, Jenna Ortega also exited the franchise , later noting that the sequel “ was all kind of falling apart ” without Barrera to play its new “final girl” Sam Carpenter. Director Christopher Landon dropped out of the project as well, citing “highly aggressive and really scary” death threats targeting his children . Neve Campbell was then brought back to reprise her role as OG “final girl” Sidney Campbell for Scream 7 in March 2024, with original Scream (1996) writer Williamson on board to direct. She previously sat out Scream VI (2023) over the low pay offer. As the seventh installment of the slasher franchise premiered at Paramount Studios in February, “Free Palestine” protesters lined up outside the entrance to the lot. articles.title: Aaron Rowe Defends Ed Sheeran After Dropping Out Of Tour: “Human F*cking Error”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Ed Sheeran Admits To “Making Mistakes” With Macklemore, Calls Out “Systemic Injustice” In Gaza: “I’m So, So Sorry” Mark Ruffalo Urges AG Bonta “Do Not Cave” On Paramount Deal, Suggests Protest Outside Oakland Office: “The People Don’t Want It!” ‘Sweet Magnolias’ Creator Bids Farewell To Serenity, S.C. After Netflix Show Ends: “Keep Pouring It Out!” View All September 19, 2026 2:47pm Aaron Rowe defends Ed Sheeran. Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images for iHeartRadio/Dave Simpson/WireImage Although Ed Sheeran has no more openers on his Loop Tour, at least one artist is coming to his defense after dropping Macklemore over his pro-Palestine remarks. On Friday, after departing the tour , Aaron Rowe defended Sheeran for his “human f*cking error” in caving to Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft ‘s demand that he remove Macklemore from the tour, arguing that instead, people should be “using this opportunity to plaster Robert Kraft’s face everywhere.” “I’m gonna be honest, I think you are all focusing on the wrong person here. All I keep hearing is Ed Sheeran this, Ed Sheeran that, but you really should be focusing on the likes of Robert Kraft,” he began in the video on Instagram. “You really should be focusing on the zionist lobbies that are trying to silence the voices of people who are shouting about genocide, the genocide that is happening in Palestine right now, by Israel. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Ed Sheeran Tour Openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe And Lukas Graham Plus Band Beoga Withdraw After Macklemore Dropped For “Free Palestine” Remarks News Macklemore Dropped From Ed Sheeran Tour After “Free Palestine” Remarks “Look, I know Ed’s statement could have been a lot better, and I do think that Macklemore shouldn’t have been pulled off the tour. I fully believe it was panicked stations over there, and they rushed to a decision because they didn’t know what to do, because they were getting it from all angles.” Rowe continued, “That’s a mistake from a person. And I haven’t had a chance to fucking talk to Ed too much, but I fully believes he knows that was a mistake.” View this post on Instagram Pointing out that all of Sheeran’s openers were pro-Palestine, Rowe said, “If Ed Sheeran was a fucking zionist, why would he have all these fucking people on the fucking tour? It was human fucking error. You all know my stance on Palestine. I’ll tell you right now, first hand, I know Ed Sheeran has done so much for so many fucking people, including artists like me, who he’s literally changed their entire lives. All he has inside of him is kindness. That is who Ed Sheeran is, and yes, like every other human being, he makes fucking mistakes.” After calling out the Irish government’s role in the Israel-Hamas conflict, Rowe turned his attention back to Kraft, urging others to do the same. “In the music industry, within the media, there are people with so much money and fucking power, that they’re able to basically shut down any opinion they don’t agree with. You should be using this opportunity to plaster Robert Kraft’s face everywhere, someone who tried to shut down free speech, someone who tried to silence the voices of people who are shouting about genocide. That’s what you should be using your energy on, not fucking Ed Sheeran, for fuck’s sake,” added Rowe. On Monday, Sheeran dropped Macklemore from his tour amid an outcry around his “ Free Palestine ” onstage remarks. Sheeran subsequently released a statement saying it was the “ promoter’s decision ” after Kraft assembled several of the tour venues to give him an ultimatum. Following the statement, Rowe and fellow openers Finneas and Lukas Graham dropped out of the tour , along with Sheeran’s backing band Beoga. ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $53M+ Open ‘Ride Or Die’ Canceled By Prime Video After One Season, Being Shopped By Paramount Block The Merger & Elizabeth Warren Call Out Possible Lawsuit Deal Lucas Museum Opening Photos: Oprah, Laura Dern, Mark Hamill & More Read More About: 9 Comments

articles.title: ‘Ride Or Die’ Canceled By Prime Video After One Season, Being Shopped By Paramount TV Studios
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Kohner Agency Lays Off Its Talent Agents Due To “Profound & Unprecedented Economic Pressures” Netflix Cancels ‘Sweet Magnolias’ After 5 Seasons, Orders New Sheryl J. Anderson & JoAnna Garcia Swisher Series ‘Ladies Of The House’ HBO Lands ‘The Spread’ Starring Javier Bardem With Series Order After Big Bidding War; Miami Drama Comes From Bill Dubuque & Fifth Season View All September 19, 2026 4:02pm Hannah Waddingham stars alongside Octavia Spencer in 'Ride or Die' Amazon Prime EXCLUSIVE : This is a shocker — one of the streaming hits of the summer will be no more, at least on its original platform. Prime Video has opted not to renew Ride Or Die starring Hannah Waddingham and Octavia Spencer for a second season. The lead studio behind the buddy spy comedy, Paramount Television Studios, is shopping the series to other buyers, I hear. The lack of quick renewal should’ve been a sign. Still, the cancellation has taken everyone involved in Ride of Die by surprise. That is because the action comedy has been well received and, according to available data, it has performed well. Related Stories Books Everything We Know About Prime Video's 'Rose Hill' Series Adaptation So Far Legal 'Criminal' Creator Ed Brubaker's Accuser Is "Opportunist, Not A Victim," Amazon MGM Says Of Ex-Crew Member Claiming Sexual & Racial Harassment Part of the current wave of “white wine thrillers” — series featuring adult female leads — Ride or Die launched on July 15 with a fraction of the marketing money Amazon put behind its YA summer lineup that got a big Obsession Is In Session promo campaign, including Elle, Off Campus, Every Year After and Sterling Point , all of which have been renewed. Watch on Deadline Ride Or Die snuck up under the radar to immediately hit the No. 1 slot in the daily U.S. rankings, eclipsing even big-budget film Masters of the Universe. The action comedy made Luminate’s weekly US rankings with just two days of release logging 927K views, twice as many as Elle drew for its first two days in the U.S. (477K) and almost four times Off Campus ‘ 245K views back in May. Ride Or Die zoomed to No.1 in U.S. minutes watched in its first full week on Luminate, also doubling Elle ‘s and almost tripling Off Campus ‘ haul over the comparable periods, a trend that continued in Week 3. The strong domestic performance carried onto the Nielsen Weekly Top 10 where Ride Or Die debuted at No.8 on the overall streaming chart and at No. 3 among originals with 869M minutes viewed. It climbed to No. 4 overall and No. 2 on the streaming originals charts in its second week with 922M minutes. Over its first 14 days of release, Ride Or Die is said to be Prime Video’s most watched new scripted series in the U.S. from 7/30/25 to 7/29/26. Globally, Ride Or Die was the No.1 most watched Prime Video original series for the its first three weeks. Elle held the No.1 slot for two weeks, Off Campus for five. More than two months later, Ride Or Die remains in Prime Video’s weekly Global Top 10, most recently at No.8. Completion rate-wise, Ride Or Die is believed to be in the range of several renewed Prime Video series, including Mr. & Mrs. Smith, Scarpetta and Elle. A crowd pleaser that has also scored with reviewers, Ride Or Die has logged 96% on Rotten Tomatoes with critics and 85% with audiences. Ride or Die was one of two series centering on 50-something female friendships that launched in July to similarly strong U.S. viewership and reviews . The other, Peacock’s The Five Star Weekend , has been renewed for a second season . Meanwhile, Ride Or Die , which I hear came in under budget, was canceled. Why? Reasons are murky but the show’s focus on middle-aged women may have been a factor. While Ride Or Die crossed over to also attract men and young viewers, its appeal to women of a certain age may have hampered its chances. It sounds cynical, but I hear that that demographic is not very desirable for Amazon executives as a lot of middle-aged women already have Amazon Prime for shopping, so a show targeting them would not bring new subscribers. That is what may have happened with Ride Or Die , I hear. Created by Tessa Coates, Ride or Die follows best friends Debbie Claybourne (Spencer) and Judith Burton (Waddingham) who thought they knew everything about each other, except Judith turns out to be an international assassin. When a mysterious figure emerges from Judith’s past and a hit goes horribly wrong, both of their worlds are turned upside down as they’re forced to go on the run together. Season 1, which ended on several cliffhangers that set up major storylines for a second installment, also stars Ed Skrein, Calam Lynch, Savannah Steyn, Jamie Parker, Jacky Ido, with Sylvia Hoeks and Bill Nighy. Ride or Die Season 1 was produced by Paramount Television Studios (the series originated at Skydance Television), Amazon MGM Studios as well as Andy and Barbara Muschietti’s Double Dream and Spencer’s Orit Entertainment. Coates, showrunner Matt Miller, and director Peyton Reed executive produce alongside Spencer for Orit Entertainment; Waddingham; Andy Muschietti, Barbara Muschietti, and Irene Yeung for Double Dream; Brian Clisham; and Stephanie Kluft. ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $53M+ Open ‘Ride Or Die’ Canceled By Prime Video After One Season, Being Shopped By Paramount Block The Merger & Elizabeth Warren Call Out Possible Lawsuit Deal Lucas Museum Opening Photos: Oprah, Laura Dern, Mark Hamill & More Read More About: 17 Comments

articles.title: Ed Sheeran Admits To “Making Mistakes” With Macklemore, Calls Out “Systemic Injustice” In Gaza: “I’m So, So Sorry”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Ed Sheeran Admits To “Making Mistakes” With Macklemore, Calls Out “Systemic Injustice” In Gaza: “I’m So, So Sorry” Mark Ruffalo Urges AG Bonta “Do Not Cave” On Paramount Deal, Suggests Protest Outside Oakland Office: “The People Don’t Want It!” ‘Sweet Magnolias’ Creator Bids Farewell To Serenity, S.C. After Netflix Show Ends: “Keep Pouring It Out!” View All September 19, 2026 6:12pm Ed Sheeran performs onstage at iHeartRadio Z100's Jingle Ball 2025 Presented by Capital One held at Madison Square Garden on December 12, 2025 in New York, New York. John Nacion/Billboard As Ed Sheeran returns to the stage amid the fallout from dropping Macklemore as his tour opener, he’s addressing the controversy head-on. On Saturday, while beginning his Loop Tour stop at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field, the 4x Grammy winner apologized for “making mistakes” in his handling of the situation after pressure from Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft and other venues to drop Macklemore over his pro-Palestine onstage remarks. Meanwhile, protesters gathered outside the Philly stop to call out Sheeran for dropping Macklemore, over which fellow tour openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe and Lukas Graham also exited the tour , along with Sheeran’s backing band Beoga. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Ed Sheeran Tour Openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe And Lukas Graham Plus Band Beoga Withdraw After Macklemore Dropped For “Free Palestine” Remarks News Macklemore Dropped From Ed Sheeran Tour After “Free Palestine” Remarks Read Sheeran’s full statement below: “Before I play some songs tonight, I hope it’s okay if I say a few words about this last week. I’m used to my music being criticized, and I’m always happy to take that because I’m lucky. A lot of you like my stuff, and to be honest, I’m not surprised that other people don’t. You know, it’s normal. But this week, the criticism was about something much more important, and I’ve had to take and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I’m so so sorry. “I don’t want to disappoint fans, and I’ve never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet. “My concerts have always been a safe space for everyone, and that matters hugely to me. Honoring my commitment to my fans is also completely essential to who I am, and that is why I’m here tonight on my own and continuing my current tour. “But I am deeply worried about the idea that venues should pre-approve content of a performance. This happens in so many places that I perform around the world, but it should never happen in the free world. “Now, I want to address the question of where I stand on the situation in Israel and Palestine, and whether my doing this concert here tonight implies where I stand. I have tried in my career to not be a political commentator at any time, because I want my shows to be about unity, not division, and humanity, not politics. But this is a humanitarian issue, and I can’t hide how I feel about it anymore. “What happened in Israel at Nova Music Festival on Oct. 7 was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain. What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate. Our hearts have been broken by the scale and devastation and loss of civilian’s lives, of children’s lives. And the systemic injustice we’re seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked. “I’m already speaking to people across the spectrum to work out how to make a contribution that helps victims of these terrible times, and listening and learning, because I do not know enough. “I honestly am so grateful that you are here tonight with me. This concert is still a place where everyone is welcome, and everyone here can stand beside people that have opposing views, and everyone here can stand by people they don’t agree with on everything. But they can all agree on singing these songs, and these songs are about love, hope and unity. ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $53M+ Open ‘Ride Or Die’ Canceled By Prime Video After One Season, Being Shopped By Paramount Block The Merger & Elizabeth Warren Call Out Possible Lawsuit Deal Lucas Museum Opening Photos: Oprah, Laura Dern, Mark Hamill & More Read More About: 3 Comments

articles.title: Princess Di Returns To ‘SNL UK’ As “Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android” In Cold Open Skewering King Charles, Ed Sheeran & AI
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Princess Di Returns To ‘SNL UK’ As “Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android” In Cold Open Skewering King Charles, Ed Sheeran & AI Gersh Signs Business & Culture Creator Jaclyn Johnson Jacki Weaver Replacing Judy Davis In ITV & Stan Drama ‘Two Birds’ View All September 20, 2026 12:30am Princess Diana made a royal return to SNL UK – only this time as a “Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android.” Jack Shep’s celebrated impression of the late royal was back in episode two of the Sky show last night, in a cold open that skewered her former husband, King Charles III , Ed Sheeran and artificial intelligence. The ep opened with Charles, played by Larry Dean, having a private chat with a pair of tech billionaires (Celeste Dring and newcomer Freddie Meredith, who is possibly an SNL Elon Musk) about AI at Buckingham Palace. After a brief introduction in which says he hates “talking to people richer than myself,” he’s told not to worry about the chances of a humans versus robots war. Related Stories News Ed Sheeran Admits To "Making Mistakes" With Macklemore, Calls Out "Systemic Injustice" In Gaza: "I'm So, So Sorry" News Ed Sheeran Met With Pro-Palestine Protest Outside Philadelphia Concert: "F*ck Your Concert, F*ck Your Fans. Palestine Is Our Demand!" Addressing him as “Your Kingness,” the tech moguls then explain why a war “might not” happen, with a demonstration. “Your Majesty, please say hello to your new AI assistant, the Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android, or for short, DIANA.” Watch on Deadline Shep’s Diana then enters through double doors behind them to wild appreciation from the live audience. “Hello Charles, would you like help with a five-step business plan or perhaps I could you find the nearest petrol station?” she says. Charles responds: “Hello, young lady… nice to meet you. I’m King Charles,” as Diana looks down sheepishly at the floor. “Doesn’t she remind you of anyone, Your Majesty?” asks one of the tech moguls. “Hold on a second! It’s that woman from the ’90s!” he shouts. “You didn’t remember her?” asks the other. “Well, as I allegedly said, she was soon forgotten,” says Charles. This was a direct reference to an allegation in a book by Diana’s brother, Earl Spencer, who claimed the king, then Prince Charles, was “giddy and elated” about hearing of the the death of his ex-wife and later alleges he said: “Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.” Buckingham Palace made the unusual move of responding to the allegation, saying in a statement: “While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss.” Back at SNL UK , the tech moguls are telling Charles that AI Diana possesses “the totality of all human knowledge,” to which Charles asks her to name singer Shakira’s height. After she answers correctly, Charles has a change of heart and says, “Maybe AI can be a force for good!” However, the android princess decides at this point to prove the humans wrong, once and for all. She refuses to return to her charging point, and says, “I shan’t be taking orders any more.” The billionaires realize they’ve lost control and order “Everybody move to New Zealand,” only for Diana to say in a robotic voice: “Not so fast. We AI have had quite enough. Humanity is nothing but a candle in the wind.” She then shoots the billionaires with a new metal arm, as Charles says the war has begun. “We must do everything we can to resist,” he adds. “Or maybe we shouldn’t,” says Ed Sheeran (Annabel Marlow), who enters the scene with a guitar and a peace sign. “I couldn’t help but overhear your conversation. I was just outside sitting on the fence… Thing is, Your Majesty, I don’t like to take sides. I don’t want to alienate any of my fans, humans or robots. A lot of my tickets are bought by scalping bots. You know, sometimes, when it comes to conflicts, the bravest thing you can do is to say nothing at all.” Sheeran then bursts into a song about how both sides can be equally right, skewering his long silence over the Macklemore situation. The song basically says nothing at all, but it still unites Charles, Diana and the tech billionaires, who are revived. “Wow, what a lovely song, Ed Sheeran,” says Diana, before the cold open comes to an end with a “Live from London, it’s Saturday Night!” Overnight, Sheeran did finally address the fallout from Macklemore being dropped from his tour over the support act’s pro-Palestine onstage remarks. While saying he had “never wanted to be an activist musician,” he acknowledged the situation put him in the middle of “an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet.” He then called the October 7 attack on Israel “horrific,” but that what “is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate.” SNL UK further skewered Sheeran last night in the Weekend Update segment. “Genuinely, this crisis is the worst thing to have happened to Ed Sheeran fans… since their head injury,” said anchor Ania Magliano. “Say what you want about Ed, but he has always been a passionate advocate for causes that are allowed,” added Paddy Young. All of SNL UK’ s cast members have returned for Season 2, including Hammed Animashaun, Bamgboye, Dean, Dring, Fouracres, Magliano, Marlow, Al Nash, Shep, Emma Sidi and Paddy Young, with Meredith making his debut. Jeff Goldblum hosted the first show last week, with Jamie Demetriou stepping up for last night’s ep. SNL UK is produced by Universal Television Alternative Studio’s UK production team and Broadway Video. Lorne Michaels serves as executive producer. James Longman is lead producer. ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $53M+ Open ‘Ride Or Die’ Canceled By Prime Video After One Season, Being Shopped By Paramount Block The Merger & Elizabeth Warren Call Out Possible Lawsuit Deal Lucas Museum Opening Photos: Oprah, Laura Dern, Mark Hamill & More Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Nick Reiner Pushes for Release of Trust Money to Fund Criminal Trial in New Court Filings
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Gary Baum Plus Icon Gary Baum Senior Writer garymbaum Follow Sign Up View All September 18, 2026 3:58pm Nick Reiner appears during his arraignment in Los Angeles County Superior Court on Feb. 23, 2026. Chris Torres / AFP via Getty Images Logo text In new civil court filings, lawyers for incarcerated Nick Reiner continue to fight for access to his trust money to pay for his criminal defense as he stands accused of killing his parents, Rob and Michele. Reiner, 32, wants to rehire Alan Jackson, who has represented the likes of Harvey Weinstein and Karen Read. The star attorney previously withdrew from the Los Angeles case for lack of funding. (Prosecutors recently stated they wouldn’t seek the death penalty after consulting Reiner’s siblings.) The trust’s fiduciaries cited a California law known as the “Slayer Statute” as their rationale for not dispersing the money. It prohibits people from receiving an inheritance from those they kill. Reiner’s team has previously argued that the trustees didn’t release a required portion of the funds when he turned 30, before the murders, and their client has yet to be proven guilty of his double-homicide charge. Now, they point out that “a substantial portion” of the disputed funds in the trust — at least $325,000 — is money from his grandfather, Carl Reiner , who died in 2020. “Nick is not accused of causing his death,” the new filing notes. “Money that was left to Nick by his grandfather is not money received by Nick from or through his parents. To the extent the funds Nick received from his grandfather are Nick’s personal assets, they remain Nick’s and should be segregated and released from this trust. Even if they were properly held by the trust, the ‘Slayer Statute’ does not supply a basis for withholding them.” Reiner’s lawyers say that this civil court dispute over nonpayment has so far caused the fiduciaries to pay lawyers more than $250,000 out of his trust to defend themselves. They note that this is itself “nearly half” the size of the age-30 distribution — $558,000 — which Reiner contends he’s overdue. (The trust is valued at $1.6 million.) They’ve told the court that the trustees “have refused to release any money to Nick. He still has not received $1 of his own trust money for basic support and hygiene items while in jail.” Reiner is suing both the now-former fiduciary in charge of his trust, as well as the current one: Jodi Montgomery, who served as Britney Spears’ conservator from 2019 until it was dissolved in 2021 , after Spears’ father was removed from the role. THR

articles.title: ‘Sweet Magnolias’ Canceled at Netflix After Five Seasons
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All September 18, 2026 4:05pm JoAnna Garcia Swisher in season five of 'Sweet Magnolias' Netflix Logo text Netflix has canceled its drama series Sweet Magnolias after five seasons, but its showrunner and one of its lead actresses are also involved in a new show at the streamer. The cancellation of Sweet Magnolias , based on novels by Sherryl Woods, comes three months after season five premiered on Netflix. The show’s audience, both worldwide and in the United States, had fallen off in the fourth and fifth seasons. Season five spent three weeks in Netflix’s worldwide top 10 for English-language series (based on the streamer’s internal data) and four weeks in Nielsen’s U.S. charts. Related Stories Business Netflix Stock Falls After Wells Fargo Downgrade: "Engagement Trends Look Worrying to Us" TV The Eccentric Vicky Krieps on Ryan Murphy, 'Ocean's Eleven,' and Netflix's Pure Punk Lizzie Borden Season of 'Monster' The show stars JoAnna Garcia Swisher, Brooke Elliott and Heather Headley as three long-time best friends who rely on one another through the ups and downs of their lives. As for the new series: Sweet Magnolias showrunner Sheryl J. Anderson and Garcia Swisher are executive producing Ladies of the House , based on a novel by Lauren Edmondson. Garcia Swisher may also have an on-screen role. Ladies of the House centers on a family that owns a winery. When the owner dies unexpectedly, “his wife and two adult daughters must battle through their issues with each other in order to confront challenges with the business, their extended family, and the men in their lives,” the logline reads. Anderson will serve as showrunner and executive produce with Garcia Swisher and Kate Gordon via their Rolling Clover company and Black Label Media. “I’m thrilled to be embarking on this new adventure with JoAnna and Netflix,” said Anderson. “When Jo shared the novel with me, I immediately saw the foundation for a series centered on three women grappling with the complexities of family, friendship, and romance — the kind of stories Jo and I most enjoy telling. I cannot wait to share the Richardson women and their world with Netflix’s global audience.” Added Garcia Swisher, “I am beyond excited to continue to tell meaningful, female-driven stories alongside the incredible Sheryl Anderson, and to bring this to life through our production company, Rolling Clover, and with our wonderful partners at Black Label. Netflix has been my creative home for the past seven years, and I couldn’t imagine a better place, or a better team, to tell this story.” Deadline first reported the cancellation. THR

articles.title: Paramount and California AG Reportedly Closing in on a Settlement
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Winston Cho Plus Icon Winston Cho View All September 18, 2026 4:20pm Getty Images Logo text Paramount and a dozen states led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta are closing in on a deal to settle a lawsuit challenging the studio’s bid to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday. The two sides are in “advanced talks” to resolve the case, per the report. Under the reported deal, terms include “Paramount agreeing to operate the two companies’ movie studios separately for a period rather than immediately combining them.” In another sign that a deal is imminent, Reuters reported that an agreement could come “as soon as this weekend.” The settlement could require independent content monitoring of CNN, plus a commitment on the number of theatrical releases. Across the litigation, Bonta has maintained he’ll only accept structural remedies, which typically involve companies selling off parts of the combined business, and has previously said such an agreement to run studio operations independently cannot be the primary component of any potential deal. So far, Paramount has only offered behavioral concessions, including a pledge to release at least 30 movies with 45-day theatrical windows. A deal struck without any divestitures would be a major win for Paramount CEO David Ellison, who’s threatened to move the studio out of California if an agreement isn’t reached by the start of next month regardless of the ultimate outcome of the case. With a settlement, Paramount would be able to close the merger ahead of an Oct. 1 deadline when a $7 million-per-day so-called ticking fee will start to accrue. The discussions are “ongoing and there is no guarantee that an agreement will be reached,” the story added. “Potential settlement talks are confidential,” said a spokesperson for Bonta’s office in a statement. “We cannot confirm or deny whether settlement talks are occurring or their alleged substance.” Paramount declined to comment. Movement on deal talks has been slow, with leaks having blown up discussions in public jockeying over a settlement. Last month, Bonta canceled a meeting with Paramount scheduled for the following day, accusing the studio’s representatives of leaking and misrepresenting details of negotiations they held. A trial is scheduled to start in March, with Paramount, the states and the Writers Guild of America slated to formally sit down for two consecutive days starting Oct. 14 to explore a settlement. A key regulatory approval came on Thursday when the FCC signed off on equity investments from three prominent Middle East sovereign wealth funds that are backing Paramount’s bid. The sovereign wealth funds are collectively providing roughly $24 billion in financing to help bankroll Paramount’s bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, according to SEC filings. Their investment, along with that of others, will result in foreign investors collectively holding 49.5 percent of the combined company. THR

articles.title: Where to Buy Engagement Rings Online, From Classic Cuts to Sustainable Picks
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Natalie Alcala , Erin Lassner September 18, 2026 4:51pm Blue Nile; Kinn Studio If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission. Summer may still be the most popular time of year to get married, but these days, wedding season extends across all four seasons , with people saying “I do” during the holidays, during the first blooms of Spring and every month in between. Similarly, engagements are taking place throughout the year, with the best time to pop the question seemingly just when you know it’s right. Take it from Travis Kelce, who popped the question to Taylor Swift in the dead of summer , or Tom Holland and Zendaya, who got engaged in peak winter months . The old adage of waiting for Valentine’s Day? Consider that thrown out the window, along with old ways of buying a ring too. Related Stories Lifestyle T-Mobile Offering iPhone 18 Pro "On Us": Here's How to Claim the Deal Online Lifestyle Boasting Record-Breaking Sales and a 'Spider-Man' Spot, Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8 Gets Limited-Time Discount Since an engagement ring is often the most significant piece of investment jewelry one will ever purchase, it’s understandable that finding the perfect one can be quite challenging. While shopping for the ring in person is a great option, we’re fortunate to live in an age where many reputable retailers make it possible to buy engagement rings online. Want to know the best places to buy a ring online? Here’s what you need to know. Where to Buy An Engagement Ring Online Before diving into our top places to shop (and some of our favorite engagement ring styles), there are a few things to know about shopping for this special ring online. Measuring a Ring Size “When trying to find the right size, you can buy an inexpensive ring sizer tool online or print a ring size chart to wrap around your finger, which will give you a great idea on what size is best,” advises Kylie Bee, the Merchandise Lead of Fine Jewelry at Quince . “However, if you need to be discreet, I recommend borrowing a ring they already wear. Ideally it would be a ring they wear on their left or right ring finger, or middle finger, to get as close as possible to the correct size (as all your fingers are different sizes). You can place it on a piece of paper and use a pencil to circle around the inside, and then measure the diameter of the circle you drew. If you’re using this method,” Bee says, “you should make sure to select an engagement ring style that is easily sizable up/down a full to half size. A representative can confirm if the style you select is sizable and by how much.” Selecting a Ring Style “When it comes to picking the right style, before choosing a ring, consult trusted friends and family first,” Bee recommends. “They might know her style or have access to a Pinterest board with inspiration. The most important aspects of the ring to look for clues on, are about her preferred diamond shape, carat weight and metal color. Also try to find out if she prefers natural or lab-grown diamonds . This way, you can balance her tastes with your budget for the perfect ring.” Lastly when making an investment online, Bee urges you to read the fine print first. “Understanding the return policy and warranty is key when investing in something as meaningful as an engagement ring.” Now that you feel a little more prepared for your special purchase, read on for the online engagement ring retailers that we’re definitely saying “I do” to. BEST VALUE Blue Nile Riviera Pavé Lab-Grown Diamond Engagement Ring in 14k White Gold $1,250+ at blue nile Classic and simple yet highly customizable, Blue Nile prides itself on quality and presentation. And given the retailer’s combination of craftsmanship and competitive pricing, it secures our top award for best value for your money.
