articles.title: ‘Vintage Violence’ Review: Eugene Kotlyarenko’s Blood-Splattered Rom-Com Is A Fun Crime-Fueled Trip Through Japan’s Denim Trade — Toronto Film Festival
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Toronto Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline’s Reviews Hudson Williams Teases ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2, Worrying He’s “Doing An Impression” Of Shane: “It Was Surreal” Greta Gerwig On Why She Chose Meryl Streep To Voice Aslan In ‘Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew’ View All September 17, 2026 6:40pm Kiko Mizuhara and Cole Sprouse in 'Vintage Violence' WME Six years after his unhinged social media age horror Spree , writer/director Eugene Kotlyarenko takes a more optimistic approach with his action-packed rom-com out of Japan. In Vintage Violence , Carter ( Cole Sprouse ) is an urban explorer who finds a haul of rare denim in a mineshaft. When Izumi ( Kiko Mizuhara ) invites him to offload the merchandise in Tokyo, the pair ends up in the crosshairs of the yakuza in a twisty, high-octane trip through the country’s thriving denim market. Much how he used the found footage of a livestream in Spree to contribute to the social media atmosphere, Kotlyarenko similarly introduces this world with Carter’s urbex stream in Colorado, which Izumi watches on the other side of the world in Toyko. It’s an interesting use of modern tech to drive the narrative, painting a quick but thorough portrait of these two strangers before they even meet. Related Stories Reviews Toronto Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline's Reviews Festivals Curry Barker, Alex Gibney, Siân Heder, Rachel Morrison & Bassam Tariq On Taking Chances & Conquering Obstacles - Deadline & DGA's Art Of Directing At TIFF Kotlyarenko also cleverly uses the connectivity of an abandoned AirPod to provide an adrenaline-fueling soundtrack for an intense chase scene, which makes utilizes the skipping music to build the chaotic tension. Watch on Deadline Being as Vintage Violence explores the potential of human connection via the internet, sharing locations becomes the ultimate sign of trust and intimacy in this perpetually online rom-com. Sprouse and Mizuhara manage to establish a believable chemistry as they flirtatiously get to know each other in the virtual opening montage, bringing a playful infatuated quality to their dynamic before they’re even in the same room. While act one gets us invested in their budding romance, all hell breaks loose in act two with an entertaining ensemble of bad guys on their trail. Nijirô Murakami slips effortlessly into the role of Izumi’s shady boyfriend Hiro, who masterminds a shady plot involving Carter’s denim after he racks up debt with the yakuza. Hio Miyazawa channels his inner eccentric Bond villain as Edoga, a dangerous denim-obsessed yakuza boss. But it’s Pierre Taki as the disgraced gangster Ko who gives a devilishly fun performance, seeking vengeance years after his finger was taken as punishment. Using Tokyo as the film’s setting provides gritty, vibrant playground for Kotlyarenko to explore a twisty yakuza plot and shed light on Japan’s growing sex tourism industry, which has come to attracts unsavory visitors from the US. Meanwhile, the film uses the symbolism of denim to represent the old glory of America as a beacon of the West. Don’t let the title fool you. If Spree was Kotlyarenko’s cynical comedic take on horror in the social media age, Vintage Violence is an optimistic rom-com with an exciting action twist, that’s still not afraid of a little gross-out factor—not just in the form of the quintessential Japanese blood spray, but also a graphically detailed makeout scene that will have audiences losing it. Vintage Violence is an addictive fusion of genre set through Kotlyarenko’s hyper-stylized cinematic aesthetic, which is grounded seamlessly by charming performances from Sprouse and Mizuhara. articles.title: UTA Partner Josh Katz Exits Agency After 30-Year Run
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt UTA Partner Josh Katz Exits Agency After 30-Year Run Dana White’s Thrill Sports Signs With Independent Artist Group Emily Deschanel, Ryder Allen, Carrie Brownstein & Nick Thune Among New Additions To Coming-Of-Age Dramedy ‘Friend Thing’ View All September 17, 2026 7:21pm UTA UTA EXCLUSIVE: Josh Katz , a longtime UTA Partner and Motion Picture Talent Agent, has left the company after a 30-year run. Sources close to the agency indicated that Katz left of his own accord. The veteran rep himself declined to comment when contacted by Deadline. No next destination was given. It’s expected that Katz will remain in the industry — possibly as a manager — though whether or not he’ll bring clients with him to his next venture is not yet clear. During his time at UTA, he worked with talents such as Rhea Seehorn — the Better Call Saul star fresh off her first Emmy win for Pluribus — along with Rob Delaney, Josh Duhamel, SNL alums Bill Hader and Bobby Moynihan, Nicholas Braun, Nick Offerman, Jessica Biel, Emerald Fennell, Michael Showalter, and many more. Katz has been a partner at UTA since 2013. A homegrown talent who grew up loving movies, he joined the agency through the mailroom in 1996 — set on a path toward becoming an agent when he read an essay from its co-founder Jeremy Zimmer, who served as CEO for nearly 13 years, ending in June 2025. articles.title: Barbra Streisand Decries Trump’s “Unchecked Ego” Amid His Assertion That The Kennedy Center May Be Torn Down
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Tom Tapp Tom Tapp Deputy Managing Editor More Stories By Tom Barbra Streisand Decries Trump’s “Unchecked Ego” Amid His Assertion That The Kennedy Center May Be Torn Down Hollywood Sign Gets A ‘Fast & Furious’ Makeover Rodney Charters Dies: ‘24,’ ‘Shameless’ Cinematographer Was 80 View All September 17, 2026 7:23pm Barbra Streisand; Donald Trump Getty Images “You can easily imagine my indignation at seeing this revered institution become the subject of such a bitter struggle over one man’s name and unchecked ego,” wrote Kennedy Center honoree Barbra Streisand . She was referring to President Donald Trump ‘s attempts to close down or, in his words, issue a warning that the center would be “ripped down” unless a renovation plan is carried out and his administration gets recognition for it. Related Stories News Judge Says Kennedy Center Must Give Court 30 Days Notice Of Any Demolition Plans After Trump Floats Prospect It Could Be “Ripped Down” News Donald Trump’s Name Removed From Kennedy Center Facade Trump has long complained that the center is old and needs to be renovated. Congress included more than $250 million in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act last year for just that. But since Trump’s takeover of the center weeks into his second term, the institution has seen a drop in ticket sales and, after the president’s name was added to the complex in December, another wave of artist cancellations. What followed was a saga in which Trump’s name was added on the front of the building and then, when order by a judge, it was removed. But a tarp was then placed over the entire edifice as if to hide it. Watch on Deadline Trump posted on Truth Social earlier this week that the renovation will not take place unless courts lift a judge’s order that has prohibited his name from being enshrined on the facade of the complex. Then came the president’s threat on Wednesday that the center may be ripped down unless a renovation plan is carried out and his administration gets recognition for it. A federal judge today said that the Kennedy Center must give the court 30 days notice before proceeding on any demolition of the complex. Sharing a photo of herself and the late president, streisand noted that the center was renamed in the wake of Kennedy’s death as a memorial, and for good reason. “The Kennedy family and other American leaders wanted a meaningful way to preserve his legacy. Re-naming the Cultural Center in JFK’s honor was a fitting choice, because he was a true champion of the arts.” In fact, being honored by the center meant something greater that other awards. “In 2008, I was deeply honored to be included in the 31st annual class of Kennedy Center Honorees. For me, and for so many artists, that honor represented something larger than a career recognition. It represented a belief in the importance of art to the life of a democracy.” She continued, “That is why what is happening to the Kennedy Center is so galling and painful to witness.” Another reaction came from Kennedy’s niece, Maria Shriver, who wrote on Tuesday, “That a sitting president would not let any renovations to a public building go on unless he gets to first put his name in the said building… What a sad state of affairs. What a tragedy. Actually, how small minded, how narcissistic. Actually great men, devoted to public service and the public good do not act like this.” BBC Calls On Producers To Pitch “Brave” New Vision For ‘Doctor Who’ Adam Smith To Lead Unit, Joe Earley New Role; Eric Schrier To Producing Deal Edie Falco To Star In Legal Drama ‘Katie Greaves’ Ordered To Series By Fox ‘Resident Evil’ Franchise Record Previews $8M-$9M & Audience Score 91% Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Resident Evil’ Scaring Up Franchise Best Previews With $8M-$9M & Rotten Tomatoes 91% Audience Score
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Curry Barker, Alex Gibney, Siân Heder, Rachel Morrison & Bassam Tariq On Taking Chances & Conquering Obstacles – Deadline & DGA’s Art Of Directing At TIFF ‘Dark Winds’ Zahn McClarnon Receiving Santa Fe International Film Festival’s Visionary Award ‘Obsession’ Star Megan Lawless Boards Indie Romantic Comedy ‘Crushed’ View All September 17, 2026 10:28pm Austin Abrams in 'Resident Evil' Sony Buckle up your 4DX seat because it’s gonna be a fun weekend as out of the gate, Zach Cregger ‘s take on Resident Evil is already posting the best previews ever for the franchise with tonight north of $8M and maybe even north of $9M . The outlook going into the weekend was $40M-$50M. Those who are smart, inside the industry and study ticket sales believe the movie has a shot to go over $50M. Similar to how this Resident Evil is posting the series best critical score on Rotten Tomatoes (now at 96% certified fresh), so is it posting the best audience score as well at 91%. On Rotten Tomatoes, the previous best audience score belonged to the original 2002 film at 67%. Related Stories News Audiences Flocking To Anime On Netflix At 10 Times The Rate Of Other Genres, Report Reveals News 'Resident Evil' To Scorch The Earth With $80M Global Debut - Box Office Preview Previews for the Sony /Constantin R-rated feature adaptation of the Capcom video game began at 2PM stateside. Watch on Deadline Tonight’s estimated take easily decimates the franchise’s previous high (which wasn’t much), 2016’s Resident Evil: Final Chapter at $1M. That was the first time a Resident Evil movie posted seven digits in its previews. But get a load of this: Resident Evil ‘s previews even on the low-end of $8M scorch Cregger’s Weapons ($5.75M previews, $43.5M opening), Scream 7 (yes, $7.8M, $63.6M opening, but put a pin in that one), Mortal Kombat 2 ($5.2M, $38.5M, a Midway video game adapted into an R-rated franchise), Sonic the Hedgehog 3 ($6.5M, $60.1M; yes, we know that’s a family film, but it’s based on a video game. Calm down). Here’s the thing, the Friday/preview-to-Saturday holds for some previous Resident Evil movies are pretty good with The Final Chapter +1.4% between those two days, the original 2002 movie +1%, and Resident Evil: Afterlife -9%, that pic holding the series previous domestic opening record at $26.6M). The point is, because it’s horror, and because it’s a different iteration of Resident Evil from the previous Milla Jovovich films, the wait-and-see is just how front loaded this movie is. Scream 7 was a completely different animal in the return of Neve Campbell to the franchise and tracking sources tonight advise not to comp Resident Evil to that horror pic (at least not yet). It was Cregger’s vision here to make a more authentic adaptation of the games which he has avidly played. The net $75M Constantin/Sony production of Resident Evil is playing in PLFs and Imax, with the latter format’s 70MM still on a crusade with The Odyssey (about 35 auditoriums). Tonight’s figures come from distribution sources, not the studio, so take everything with a grain of salt. articles.title: ‘The Book Of Mormon’ Original Cast Members Nikki M. James & Rory O’Malley Set Broadway Return Engagement
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Tony-Winner J. Harrison Ghee Takes Two-Month Break From ‘Oh, Mary!’ Tour On Medical Advice Duncan Sheik Hospitalized In “Critical But Stable Condition” Weeks Before Two Major Off Broadway Musicals Set To Begin Billionaire Robert Kraft Doubles $1 Million Macklemore Donation To Aid “Humanitarian Crisis” View All September 18, 2026 5:00am Nikki M. James and Rory O’Malley Production EXCLUSIVE: The Book of Mormon original cast members Nikki M. James and Rory O’Malley will return to the Broadway production at the Eugene O’Neill Theatre for a strictly limited 12-week engagement. From October 27, 2026, through January 17, 2027, James will step back into her Tony Award-winning role as Nabulungi, and O’Malley will return in his Tony-nominated role of Elder McKinley. Both James and O’Malley performed selected scenes and songs during The Book of Mormon ’s “Magical Mormon Mystery Week” in June, but will play their entire original roles for the limited engagement. Related Stories News Broadway's 'Two Strangers (Carry A Cake Across New York)' Sets Closing Date News Rosie O'Donnell To Join Broadway's 'Rocky Horror Show' As Temporary Fill-In For Rachel Dratch “Returning to The Book of Mormon feels like a true homecoming,” James said in a statement. “Sharing the stage with Rory O’Malley again, in the role that completely changed my life, is a rare and beautiful gift. I am incredibly excited to step back into Nabulungi’s shoes for these 12 weeks and re-experience the brilliant humor and immense heart of this show alongside both old friends and a spectacular new company.” Watch on Deadline Said O’Malley, “Being in the original Broadway cast of The Book of Mormon has always been the thing I am most proud of as an artist. Getting to perform as Elder McKinley again is a dream come true. I can’t wait to share the stage with my mission companion, Nikki, and the brilliant current cast!” James won the 2011 Tony Award for Best Featured Actress/Musical for originating the role of Nabulungi. Her other Broadway credits include a Tony-nominated performance as Ida B. Wells in Suffs and Les Misérables, while Off Broadway credits include Little Shop of Horrors and Tony Kushner’s A Bright Room Called Day. She stars in Marvel’s Disney+ series Daredevil: Born Again and recurs in the Apple TV+ thriller Severance . O’Malley earned a Tony Award nomination for originating the role of Elder McKinley. He also starred as King George III in Hamilton , both on Broadway and on tour. He made his Broadway debut in The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee . Screen credits include Dreamgirls and TV’s Modern Family, Grace and Frankie and others. The Book of Mormon , with book, music and lyrics by Trey Parker, Robert Lopez and Matt Stone, choreographed by Casey Nicholaw and directed by Nicholaw and Parker, opened on Broadway March 24, 2011. In addition to James and O’Malley, the opening night cast included Josh Gad, Andrew Rannells and Michael Potts. The Book of Mormon is the longest running show in the 100-year history of the Eugene O’Neill Theatre and is the 10th longest running Broadway musical of all time. articles.title: Everything We Know About Prime Video’s ‘Rose Hill’ Series Adaptation So Far
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Everything We Know About The ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Movie So Far What To Expect For ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2: Everything We Know So Far All The Songs In ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 So Far View All September 18, 2026 6:00am Elsie Silver/Wild Love by Elsie Silver/Heidi Cole McAdams Getty One of Prime Video ’s next big book adaptation bets is that on Elsie Silver ’s Rose Hill series. The streamer is adapting the contemporary small-town romance into a TV show, which sounds like its in the vein of Netflix’s My Life With the Walter Boys and Ransom Canyon . The cast is currently being assembled with many lead roles already established. Related Stories Casting Jake Weary, Sean O’Pry, Hannah Galway & Sadie Dickerson To Lead Prime Video’s ‘Rose Hill’ Casting Prime Video’s ‘Rose Hill’ Adds 5 To Cast Read on for everything we know about Prime Video’s Rose Hill series adaptation so far: When will Prime Video’s Rose Hill TV series adaptation come out? A release date has not yet been set for the series’ arrival because it is in early stages of development with casting. Watch on Deadline Has Prime Video’s Rose Hill TV series started production? Not yet, but as stated above, a cast is being assembled. Who will be in the cast of Prime Video’s Rose Hill adaptation? Jake Weary ( The Waterfront, Animal Kingdom) , Sean O’Pry, Hannah Galway ( Under the Banner of Heaven ) and Sadie Dickerson ( Just In Time ) have been cast as West Belmont, Ford Grant, Rose and Skylar Stone. Jake Weary, Sean O’Pry, Hannah Galway and Sadie Dickerson Courtesy/Kate Kondratieva/Calyssa Lorraine/Arden Dickson American model O’Pry is well known for appearing in the music video for Taylor Swift’s single “Blank Space” off of her 1989 album. Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland, Gigi Zumbado, and Curtis Hamilton also recently joined the cast. McGroarty will play Cora, Reid-Gantzert will play Emmy Belmont, and Mulholland will play Oliver Belmont. In recurring guest roles, Zumbado will play Tabitha and Hamilton will portray Bash Rousseau. Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland, Gigi Zumbado and Curtis Hamilton Who else is behind the Rose Hill adaptation at Prime Video? Is Elsie Silver involved in the creation of the series? Heidi Cole McAdams will serve as showrunner, which was revealed when Amazon announced the news of the adaptation at its upfront presentation in May 2026. Marc Webb will direct the pilot and second episode, and Temple Hill is producing. Silver also serves as executive producer alongside Wyck Godfrey, Marty Bowen, and James Seidman for Temple Hill. Temple Hill’s Annika Patton will also serve as a co-executive producer. How many books are in Elsie Silver’s Rose Hill series? The series consists of four books — Wild Love, Wild Eyes, Wild Side , and Wild Card . What is Elsie Silver’s Rose Hill book series about? The story centers rancher with commitment issues West Belmont and brooding record label owner Ford Grant, who are best friends and neighbors. Grant, known as Forbes’ “World’s Hottest Billionaire” has long carried a torch for West’s sister, Rose. Country-pop star Skylar Stone’s entry into the rugged mountain town setting causes ripples in the romantic family drama.

articles.title: Matthew Lillard Says He’s “Embarrassed” About Returning for ‘Scream 7’ After Melissa Barrera’s Firing
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All September 16, 2026 7:24pm Matthew Lillard and Melissa Barrera Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures; Arturo Holmes/Getty Images Matthew Lillard has confessed that he’s “embarrassed” about returning for Scream 7 following Melissa Barrera’s firing from the slasher franchise. During a recent Q&A, via a video posted on TikTok , the actor said Barrera was “on the right side of history” when she expressed support for Palestinians in 2023 amid the Israel-Hamas war. “It’s just human, it’s like who we are… I don’t know what else to do,” Lillard said. “For me… I have queer kids; if I’m not standing up for queer kids or kids in the trans community, what the fuck am I doing?” Related Stories Movies Watermelon Pictures Acquires 'Thirteen in Gaza' Out of TIFF (Exclusive) Music Ed Sheeran on Dropping Macklemore From Tour Over Palestine Remarks: "The Promoter's Decision, Not Mine" The Five Nights at Freddy’s star continued, “Listen, I don’t think it’s easy all the time. Melissa Barrera , who’s a beautiful actor, was fired for what she said. … That’s really fucking bullshit and really hard, and she’s on the right side of history. And when they start coming after your job, sometimes things are worth it.” “But I’m just gonna say, what happened to Melissa, the whole world didn’t pipe up,” he added. “She was like a year early on what the fuck’s going on, but the whole world should have piped up and said, ‘She’s right,’ and they didn’t. And that’s brutal.” Lillard said he then “got called out” for reprising his role as Stu Macher in Scream 7 , which was released in February. He previously starred in the original 1996 Scream and 1997’s Scream 2 . “I’m like, ‘Oh fuck, that’s brutal.’ I feel bad about that, I feel shame about that,” he said. “Because in that moment, I was so excited to go back, I didn’t really think about Melissa and the journey, and I didn’t say ‘no.’ And I’m embarrassed, and that’s the truth.” Barrera was dropped from the seventh installment in the slasher franchise in November 2023 after she spoke out in support of Palestine on her social media after Hamas invaded Israel the month prior. Spyglass Media Group, the company behind the Scream franchise, said in a statement at the time, “Spyglass’ stance is unequivocally clear: We have zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form, including false references to genocide, ethnic cleansing, Holocaust distortion or anything that flagrantly crosses the line into hate speech.” Following the news, Jenna Ortega dropped out of Scream 7 , as did director Christopher Landon . Neve Campbell was later brought back to reprise her role as Sidney Campbell in the new film. THR

articles.title: Universal Is Getting Cold Feet on Releasing the Elon Musk Documentary (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Steven Zeitchik Plus Icon Steven Zeitchik Senior Editor, Technology and Politics View All September 16, 2026 7:44pm Elon Musk, founder and CEO of SpaceX, speaks via video before the ringing of opening bell at the Nasdaq Marketsite at the launch of the company's initial public offering (IPO) on June 12, 2026 in New York City. Musk is the subject of a hard-hitting documentary that Universal may back out of releasing. Spencer Platt/Getty Images When it screened at the Venice Film Festival earlier this month, Musk got the kind of reception every international distributor dreams about. Attendees applauded enthusiastically for five minutes and saluted director Alex Gibney , even shouting “thank you” inside the festival’s Sala Grande for his hard-hitting investigation into the world’s richest man. But despite that instant and reassuring focus group, Universal Pictures , which controls worldwide rights to the film outside of North America, now appears to be having second thoughts on a documentary it paid a significant sum to acquire. The company has not dated the movie, has not communicated with the filmmaking team about its plans, and generally appears to be rethinking the release of a project that it once showed high enthusiasm for but is now politically sensitive for parts of the Trump administration. Two people with knowledge of the dynamic who were not authorized to speak publicly tell The Hollywood Reporter that while a final decision has not been made and that several outcomes were possible, they believed that Universal would ultimately decide against releasing the film and return rights to the movie to filmmakers. When asked what its release plans were for the film, a Universal representative said it had no comment. The movie is set to premiere in U.S. theaters via the independent Bleecker Street as well as play the London Film Festival next month; both are media-rich affairs that a studio usually times with a release in the U.K. and even across the European continent. But Universal has made no such plans. Gibney did not immediately respond to a request seeking comment. If Universal opts against releasing the movie, it would mark an extraordinary reversal at a moment when media companies are already under scrutiny for bowing to various forms of political pressure. Amazon backed out of releasing Artificial as it got into business with Sam Altman’s OpenAI, while ABC News and Paramount/CBS News each paid millions to settle lawsuits with the Trump administration many legal experts felt would be quickly dismissed. Universal would be required to pay filmmakers a kill fee not to release the movie, according to a person familiar with the deal’s structure. The filmmakers would then be free to sell it anew, essentially allowing it to profit twice off the same rights sale. The film would not struggle to be seen around the world no matter what happens. Distributors in individual countries have been salivating over the film ever since the four-hour project began gaining buzz in recent weeks, first with a THR cover story and then with the Venice and Toronto festival premieres, but were of course told it was spoken for, and many would likely jump at a fresh chance to buy it. Still, the specter of yet another media giant paying a bounty to avoid angering people on the right while also shelving a project for no legitimate creative reason would surely raise questions about the ability of conglomerates to protect free speech in an era when it is already under assault. Musk is a politically explosive film that alleges, among other things, that its subject could be using data gathered during his DOGE period against Democrats in the upcoming U.S. election. In the film Gibney includes comments from Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel Prize-winning godfather of AI, describing how that could play out. “It’s fairly clear to me that Trump is hell-bent on corrupting the midterm elections,” he says onscreen. “If you wanted to corrupt those midterm elections and you wanted to use AI, all you needed to do was get detailed information on U.S. citizens. And what DOGE did looked like just what you would do.” While Donald Trump’s relationship with Musk has had his ups and downs, Musk has had a rock-solid relationship with FCC chair Brendan Carr, who had come to Musk’s defense when the Biden administration opened investigations into the mogul, has allegedly facilitated Starlink regulatory approvals and even posed for a praise-filled selfie with him. An FCC source who has worked closely with Carr said he privately reveres the tycoon. And Carr, of course, oversees an agency that wields enormous power over media companies and currently is conducting an investigation into Comcast’s DEI practices. Angering Carr with a Musk release could potentially bring more legal and regulatory headaches for the Brian Roberts-led conglomerate. Universal bought the rights to Musk three years ago, paying a multimillion dollar price tag to release the film around the world. But the climate was very different in 2023, with Musk not yet aligning formally with Donald Trump and the 45th president — and Carr — far from the apex of power. Musk has shown his disdain for Gibney’s film, repeatedly calling it a “hit piece” and saying it was “boring,” despite the fact that there are no indications he has seen it. His lawyer, Alex Spiro, has also sent a letter to Gibney’s production company putting it “on notice,” raising the temperature for potential distributors. HBO snapped up North American TV and streaming rights back in 2023 and pressed Gibney to continue shooting when Musk arrived in Washington at the start of the Trump administration, even dipping into its coffers to provide more financing. For now the company is plowing ahead, though a sale of Warner Bros Discovery to David Ellison could complicate the picture. Ellison’s father Larry, who is partly bankrolling the WBD acquisition, is briefly cited in the film in an unfavorable light. The earliest HBO could air the film is February given a four-month pay VOD window retained by the filmmakers. By February, Ellison could already control HBO and WBD. THR

articles.title: Bleachers Bring Out The Chicks to End Five Nights of Underplays at the Troubadour
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Rachel Head Plus Icon Rachel Head View All September 16, 2026 8:11pm Bleachers performed their fifth and final show at the Troubadour on Tuesday, Sept. 15. Rachel Head Bleachers ended a rare set of underplays in Los Angeles at West Hollywood’s Troubadour on Tuesday night, bringing out The Chicks to close out a full-circle moment marking the first time the New Jersey indie rockers have played the iconic venue since 2014. Led by Grammy-winning superproducer Jack Antonoff, Bleachers gave fans a much closer look than usual in the 500-cap room, with their nostalgic sound and deep-cut lyrics right at home with the Troubadour’s magic. The Troubadour gave a much more intimate vibe than the arenas and theaters they usually play, like Madison Square Garden back in June. With the smaller space, the band could engage directly with the audience more freely, with devotees in the front row feet away at the edge of the stage. Related Stories Music Ed Sheeran Openers Finneas, Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe Depart Tour in Solidarity With Macklemore TV Noah Kahan Performs "Bridge Over Troubled Water" During 2026 Emmy In Memoriam All five nights felt like a return to the start of the group, with the set list offering a blend of nostalgia from their first album, Strange Desire , and fresh cuts from everyone for ten minutes , the band’s fifth studio album they released in May. Showcasing old favorites and new material, concertgoers were given a compilation of cherished classics like “Don’t Take the Money” and “Good Morning” and new songs including “you and forever” and the everyone for ten minutes’ opening song “sideways,” which kicked off Tuesday’s show too. The inclusion of an acoustic set further heightened the intimacy, with Antonoff’s vocals shining. Past the midway point of their set, they’d brought up country icons The Chicks for a surprise guest appearance for a cover of “I Wanna Get Better,” which sent the audience into a frenzy. Carly Rae Jepsen performed the same song — originally released by Bleachers in 2014 on their debut album — with Antonoff on the first night. Tuesday’s show also featured Antonoff’s dad, Ricky Antonoff, who joined the band for “How Dare You Want More.” Despite the venue’s capacity of just 500, concertgoers radiated an electric energy, creating a vibrant and lively atmosphere. Some in the crowd brought bubbles to spray during a few songs, adding a funny extra dynamic during some of the slower, more emotional songs like “Merry Christmas, Please Don’t Call,” the band’s melancholy tune about setting emotional boundaries and asking a toxic person not to contact you during the holidays. Bleachers’ mini-residency served as a good reminder of the importance of connecting popular bands with intimate venues, championing not just the music but also the shared joy between the band and their fans. For some, this was their first Bleachers show, and others their 19th, 30th or, in one fan’s case, their 98th. Bleachers may have graduated from their time in these smaller rooms, but this past week’s stand at the Troubadour is a reminder that it’s still magical when artists make their way back to those intimate spaces they began their careers in. THR

articles.title: ‘South Park’ Returns as ‘South America’ as Plot Stays Local and Trump-Free
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Kevin Dolak Plus Icon Kevin Dolak View All September 16, 2026 9:50pm South Park on Comedy Central and streaming on Paramount+. Comedy Central Logo text South Park , one of the longest-running comedy series on television, returned to Comedy Central for its 29th season after making the unexpected move of changing the show’s name to “ South America ” — a gag that creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone announced as a possible marketing gimmick but is certainly also a jab at President Donald Trump. Wednesday night’s season premiere provided little explanation as to when and why the name change happened for the fictional Colorado town, but it does offer a vague metaphor for current U.S. politics around immigration. Seasons 27 and 28 of South Park had shifted from the show’s traditional stand-alone episodes to a season-long arc centered on fictionalized happenings within the White House, including President Trump’s clandestine affair with Satan. With the premiere, the show appears to be returning to its traditional format — stand-alone episodes that may still carry overarching themes. It’s not entirely clear whether we’ve seen the last of South Park ‘s satirical Trump character and the supporting cast of cabinet officials, hangers-on and vice-president-turned-lover J.D. Vance, but they’re absent from this one-off episode, which stays within the confines of the titular town. Related Stories TV When and Where to Stream 'South Park' Season 29 (AKA 'South America') TV South Park's 'South America' Rebrand Isn't Going Anywhere in Season 29 Premiere “Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of ‘South Park’ to ‘SOUTH AMERICA,'” Parker and Stone said in a Sept. 8 statement announcing the name change. One might have expected the season premiere to show Trump signing an executive order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America” before eventually getting to South Park. Instead, the season begins after the name change has already been accepted — essentially baking the joke into the show, as characters refer to their town as “South America” without question. Only once does a character allude to the name change itself, and it’s clear the moment was divisive for the town. What the episode offers is a straightforward plot that, as usual, hides a metaphor for a social issue beneath dialogue soaked in double entendres. It begins with Eric Cartman faking being bullied at school to trick his mother into buying him an e-bike — a vehicle clearly designed for adults that has become the one thing every kid in town must have. Ever the earnest pushover, Liane Cartman complies, and soon the boy is terrorizing the town on his new, dangerous ride. Eventually, more of the town’s children are wreaking havoc around South America, crashing through diner windows and scaring pedestrians — a clear metaphor for groups of immigrants moving into American towns. Early in the episode, Kyle tries his own version of Cartman’s ploy on his mother, but he has to go through his father, Randy, who arrives home in flashy spandex and sneakers, now a 10-speed cyclist commuting in the bike lane that’s being overtaken by kids on e-bikes. Randy soon forms a gang of 10-speed riders that begins roughing up anyone in their way. They’re not especially fast, though — one motorist bemoans the “old farts” blocking the road. Still, the gang feels like a stand-in for Immigration and Customs Enforcement as they comb the town trying to eradicate the e-bike kids. As the kids’ South American youth biker gang is hunted by Randy’s gang of adults, the episode piles on satire aimed at the companies and public figures who have fallen in line as Trump took a marker to traditional maps. Google is repeatedly used to search things like “how to get the laws changed in South America?” (the answer: bribing government officials) and “how can police respond to gang violence in South America?” (the answer: extreme violence). The episode also spoofs the massive cultural anticipation ahead of the release of Grand Theft Auto VI , the video game sequel slated to arrive in stores in November — making it a natural stand-in for the upcoming midterm elections, which “the libs” of Trump’s America are looking to for drastic change. “Hopefully, things will get better in November. That’s when Grand Theft Auto Six comes out,” one character says. Someone has to do something — we need to get these kids off the streets and back inside on their phones. Parker and Stone have packed these metaphors into the premiere, a style that marks a clear departure from last season’s grotesque White House storylines. The question now is whether they plan to run this metaphor across the season and carry on with the e-bikes plot or if they will bring a new issue into the foreground and subject it to their now more subtle satire. THR

articles.title: King Charles Makes Rare Statement Over Bombshell Memoir Claim He Told Diana’s Brother: “We’ll Forget Her Soon Enough”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All September 17, 2026 1:57am King Charles in September 2026 Courtesy of Getty King Charles has, as the British press put it, been dragged into a “war of words” this week with Charles Spencer, the younger brother of the late Princess Diana . Ahead of the release of Earl Spencer’s bombshell memoir about his sibling next week, titled Swan Song: Diana, My Sister , one particular claim from the book has seemingly thrown the Palace for a loop. Spencer writes that in the wake of Diana’s 1997 death in a Paris car crash, he recalls the then-Prince of Wales saying: “We’ll forget her soon enough.” The uproar among the British public and press has been fierce, and Charles has been criticized for allegedly making such a cruel comment about his ex-wife, who remains a beloved icon in the U.K. — no matter how unpopular other royals are. Related Stories Movies Zhang Yimou to Lead Busan Film Festival Competition Jury Movies Why Aura Entertainment Isn't Obsessed With Topping 'Obsession' Such is the backlash that the Palace has made a rare public statement over the matter, where the firm appears to cast doubt on Spencer’s recollection of the event: “While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss,” it said, per BBC News . The language, reporters have pointed out, is strikingly similar to Queen Elizabeth’s response to allegations of racism from Prince Harry and Meghan Markle in 2021, when she stated “recollections may vary,” in what was a surprisingly firm response from the monarch. The latest (and very public) quarrel between King Charles and his former brother-in-law has threatened to loom over a big day for the royal family , with Charles, Prince William and Kate Middleton attending events, as well as Prince Harry’s first major appearance since returning to Britain with Markle . Spencer’s book has unearthed a common public sentiment that the royal family is unwilling to show empathy in moments of hardship, especially surrounding the death of Diana. In the released excerpt from the memoir, Spencer claims that Charles unleashed “a stream of anger” over Spencer’s insistence that Diana would not have wanted 15-year-old Prince William and 12-year-old Prince Harry to walk in her funeral procession. Spencer writes: “[Charles] unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death. ‘Rest assured,’ he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough’.” According to the BBC, the Palace refute the claim. They see it as being “entirely out of character for a man with a deeply compassionate nature, who at the time was dealing with his own grief and that of their two sons.” THR

articles.title: Cary Joji Fukunaga, Sine Plambech Named Zurich Film Festival’s Feature and Documentary Jury Presidents
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All September 17, 2026 6:40am Cary Joji Fukunaga, Sine Plambech Zurich Film Festival has confirmed its feature film competition jury will be presided over by James Bond director Cary Joji Fukunaga , while filmmaker Sine Plambech will head up the documentary competition jury. American director and screenwriter Fukunaga ( No Time to Die ) will be joined on his jury by Swiss-French actress Ella Rumpf ( Love Letters ), Mexican director and screenwriter Fernando Eimbcke ( Moscas ), producer Julie Billy ( The Little Sister ), and Italian film editor and director Walter Fasano ( Nino – Un Film Su Nino Rota ). They will decide on the winner of the Golden Eye in the feature film competition. Related Stories News King Charles Makes Rare Statement Over Bombshell Memoir Claim He Told Diana's Brother: "We'll Forget Her Soon Enough" Movies Zhang Yimou to Lead Busan Film Festival Competition Jury Among the 14 movies vying for the Golden Eye is Rhys Marc Jones’ Black Church Bay , a mystery-thriller starring Tom Cullen and Joe Locke about a man whose world unravels after an intimate encounter with a younger man. Zou Jing’s A Girl Unknown , Blerta Basholli’s Dua and Pierre le Gall’s Flesh and Fuel are also included in the competition section, as are Andrina Mračnikar’s Mila / Marija , Manuela Martelli’s El Deshielo , Ramzi Bashour’s Hot Water , Fabian Stumm’s Die Ideen , Tareq Daoud’s Serife Tavsan , Arie Esiri and Chuko Esiri’s Clarissa , Mads Mengel Nielsen’s The Guest , Ghasideh Golmakani’s Head to Head , Andrius Blaževičius’s How to Divorce During the War and Ufuk Emiroglu’s Sevda . Meanwhile, Danish anthropologist and filmmaker Sine Plambech ( Heartbound ) will head up the doc competition jury with Spanish cinematographer Alfredo de Juan ( Edge of the Unknown ), Norwegian producer Anne Köhncke ( Pervert Park ), Swiss director Jela Hasler ( Les Nouvelles Eves ) and Austrian director and producer Nikolaus Geyrhalter ( Homo Sapiens ). Fourteen films are competing in the doc section, including Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco’s Cannes-premiering The Match , following the historic Argentina vs. England game at the 1986 FIFA World Cup, as well as Habiba Nosheen’s The Gymnasts of Fisherman Colony and Guillaume Massart’s Le Detention . Christian Bonke and Adam Bonke will present Perfect Road , chronicling a man living as a nomad on his bicycle for 10 years, and Elisabeth Rasmussen’s We Are Stardust , Erik Shirai’s Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing , Gar O’Rourke’s The Siege of Paradise , Simon David’s Shreckschraube and Lucas Paleocrassas’ Bugboy . Pete Muller will compete with Bucks Harbor , as will Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes’ One In a Million , Khoroldorj Choijoovanchig’s Colors of White Rock , Patrick Wally’s My Home of Wind and Sand and Arnaud Alain’s La Face Cachee De La Terre . BUCKS HARBOR (Pete Muller, USA, 2026) Highlights from this year’s Zurich Film Festival gala lineup include Peter Farrelly’s I Play Rocky , Beth de Araújo’s Josephine starring Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan, Possible Love , the new drama from acclaimed Korean director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning ), and Wicker , the sci-fi fantasy rom-com from directors Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson starring Alexander Skarsgård, Olivia Colman, and Elizabeth Debicki. Jordan Firstman’s Club Kid and Bunker with Javier Bardem and Penélope Cruz will also screen. Julianne Moore is set to be honored with the Golden Icon Award and will accept the accolade alongside Jesse Eisenberg, who directs her in his latest feature The Debut , a musical-comedy co-starring Paul Giamatti. John Turturro will be honored with the Golden Eye Award. He’s being recognized for his performance in Noah Segan’s The Only Living Pickpocket in New York , a project that is already garnering awards buzz . The 22nd Zurich Film Festival takes place from Sept. 24-Oct. 4. THR

articles.title: ‘Elf’ Movie to Come to Life With Immersive Experience at NYC’s Rockefeller Center (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All September 17, 2026 7:00am Will Ferrell in 'Elf.' New Line/courtesy Everett Collection Elf fans will have a unique way to spread Christmas cheer during this holiday season. The world of New Line Cinema’s beloved film Elf is set to come alive at HERO in New York City ‘s Rockefeller Center with The Elf Experience . The all-new immersive holiday adventure begins Nov. 14 from Warner Bros. Global Experiences and Fairview Portals. HERO, which is Rockefeller Center’s venue devoted to immersive storytelling, will transform into a storybook journey at the North Pole in honor of director Jon Favreau ‘s enduring 2003 movie that starred Will Ferrell as Buddy, a man raised by elves. The experience will involve immersive environments, interactive activities, photo opportunities and special treats, all inspired by the film itself. Related Stories Business Paramount Argues That the States Post a $1.88 Billion Bond to Cover Warner Bros. Bills TV 'New York: A Documentary Film' Returns to PBS With Two New Episodes on the 21st Century (Exclusive) Guests to The Elf Experience will meet one of Santa’s helpers before entering Papa Elf’s storybook and heading to the North Pole to learn about the life of an elf. The journey will include stops at the Candy Cane Forest, the Sea of Swirly Twirly Gumdrops, Santa’s Toy Workshop, the North Pole and ultimately New York City and Gimbels. The Elf Experience will offer a range of merchandise, such as apparel, accessories, toys, treats and artist collaborations. “We’ve assembled a group of artists that worked on the original film, as well as new ones who were inspired by it,” says Favreau, filmmaker and founder of Fairview Portals. “Miniature work, forced perspective, zoetrope and animatronics were all implemented to create a unique and handcrafted experience to capture the spirit of the film.” Elf Tickets are now available online for The Elf Experience , with prices starting at $45 for adults and $35 for children. It opens to the public on Saturday, Nov. 14. Adds Warner Bros. Discovery president of global experiences and worldwide studio operations Simon Robinson, “Watching Elf has become a holiday tradition for millions of fans, and Rockefeller Center is synonymous with the holidays in New York City. Bringing the two together gives fans from New York and around the world an entirely new way to immerse themselves in the Elf story. Together with Fairview Portals, it is a privilege to bring the humor, heart and Christmas cheer of Elf to life in this state-of-the-art experience . “ THR

articles.title: MLW Finally Gets Its Tubi Deal (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All September 17, 2026 7:00am Major League Wrestling's flagship series 'MLW Fusion' is headed to Tubi. MLW At long last, MLW ( Major League Wrestling ) is headed to Tubi under a new deal. Starting tonight, Thursday, Sept. 17 at 8 p.m. ET, the pro-wrestling promotion’s flagship series MLW Fusion will stream (for free) live on the on-demand/FAST platform. News episodes will premiere each Thursday in the same time slot. This was actually the deal that was meant to happen five years ago. At the time, however, WWE allegedly pressured Tubi into canceling the deal, leveraging its relationship with Tubi-owner Fox — WWE’s SmackDown aired on the broadcast network back then. The done deal was undone the night before I was set to exclusively report it. WWE and MLW settled out of court, with the former paying the latter $20 million. Related Stories Movies 'Resident Evil' Review: Zach Cregger Gives a Fatigued Franchise an Exhilarating Shot in the Arm Movies Zach Cregger's 'Resident Evil': First Reactions From the Premiere MLW has undergone some significant changes since then. For starters, actor Paul Walter Hauser has joined Court Bauer and Bryan Walsh as executive producer; additionally, Major League Wrestling signed with Artists First for representation in March 2025. And in fall 2025, MLW partnered with Danny McBride’s Don Gato Tequila and moved its headquarters from New York to Charleston, South Carolina. Tubi has 110 million monthly active users. MLW Fusion was relaunched in May 2026; the company’s pay-per-view events are now distributed by Live Nation’s Veeps. MLW Fusion episodes are also available on Veeps and NJPW World. “Wrestling should be easy to find and free to watch,” said Bauer, the founder and CEO of Major League Wrestling. “We built MLW around that, no paywalls, no subscription barriers, nothing standing between a fan and the show, and Tubi shares that same fan-first philosophy at scale. Starting Sept. 17, Tubi’s 110 million monthly active users have a front row seat on Thursday nights to the hardest hitting hour in pro wrestling, and it won’t cost a dime.” MLW Fusion “serves up a distinctive brand of pro wrestling, blending cutting-edge, new-era wrestling with the grit, colorful characters and throwback flavor of ’rasslin,” the company says. “Built around big fights, heated rivalries, championship stakes and an anything-can-happen attitude, Fusion brings a rowdy, hard-hitting edge to the modern wrestling landscape. MLW will also continue to produce live special events alongside the weekly series.” THR

articles.title: ‘The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd’ Review: Amanda Seyfried and Scoot McNairy Bring Raw Intensity to Tim Blake Nelson’s Death Row Drama
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By David Rooney Plus Icon David Rooney Chief Film Critic DavidCRooney1 Follow Sign Up View All September 17, 2026 7:03am Amanda Seyfried in 'The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd.' Benoit Soler One of the principal takeaways from Tim Blake Nelson ’s bruising drama set in and around a maximum-security Oklahoma prison, The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd , is how infrequently we get to see Scoot McNairy in a meaty lead role that gives the reliably great character actor real complexity to chew on. McNairy plays a death row inmate who forms a connection with the equally compelling Amanda Seyfried ’s creative writing teacher, a woman stuck in an abusive marriage and grasping to find a way out. There’s ambiguity in both characters’ choices, making for a tough film that refuses to provide easy answers. Related Stories Movies 'Re/Pair' Review: David Schwimmer, W. Kamau Bell and Van Jones Lead Pragmatic Doc About the Past and Present of Black-Jewish Relations Movies THR Returns to TIFF With Editorial Portrait Studio, Video Lounge and Live 'Awards Chatter' Recording With Penélope Cruz Nelson took 12 years to get the project made, and that labor-of-love aspect shows in the soulfulness and meticulous care the writer-director brings to this unsettling story of violence begetting violence, based on actual events. He gathers what seems a hand-picked cast of excellent actors to breathe texture and authenticity into a drama that’s not an easy watch but should find an appreciative audience on streaming platforms. The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd The Bottom Line Grim but riveting. Venue : Toronto International Film Festival (Gala Presentations) Cast : Amanda Seyfried, Scoot McNairy, Missi Pyle, Devyn Tyler, Elizabeth Marvel, Tim Blake Nelson, Grant Harvey, William Jackson Harper, Wunmi Mosaku Director-screenwriter : Tim Blake Nelson 2 hours 1 minute Nelson doesn’t shy away from the horrific brutality at the heart of the film but nor does he sensationalize it in the interest of amping up the material into a crime thriller. The movie is notable for its thoughtful approach to themes more often explored via heightened emotions. Nelson’s measured handle on the drama gives it an imposing gravity. The seemingly counterintuitive backing of a delicate, predominantly acoustic guitar score by Henry Nelson and Will Curry places the film in the American heartland and signals from the start that the focus will be more psychological than action-driven. Seyfried plays Karen, recently returned to her hometown to be near her father, who has dementia and has been placed in an elder-care facility, which she has to pay for given that her brother is in prison. With high school teaching positions in short supply, she takes a spot teaching a group of a dozen or so inmates at a men’s prison, starting them off with a Hemingway story. Karen encourages the students to write something personal and is surprised to get back a beautifully shaped piece of prose from Wilson, recounting a childhood episode when he was hunting squirrels in the woods and the complicated way it made him feel about the act of killing. Nelson, who also appears as the prison warden, builds the film along three parallel timelines, detailing Karen’s prison classes, which become a strange kind of respite from her miserable time at home with Kenneth (Grant Harvey), her deadbeat drunk of a husband; Wilson’s escape with two other men and the shocking incident that adds a handful more deaths to the grisly murder conviction that put him away; and the ticking clock as senior state prison warden Joan Gardner ( Missi Pyle ) oversees preparations for the execution of an inmate by lethal injection, to be supervised by a specialized medic ( Elizabeth Marvel ). This ambitious tripartite structure comes with strengths and weaknesses. It gives the drama a disturbing sense of human beings’ capability for heartless violence, keeps us on edge and shakes up our perspective by intercutting sympathetic scenes with chilling ones. But it also makes for an initial challenge in figuring out where the three timelines sit in relation to each other. This is somewhat detrimental to the development of Karen, since cutting back and forth interrupts the flow of her epistolary relationship with Wilson, whose stories morph into intimate letters. Seyfried has no trouble putting across the desperation of a woman in an unendurable marriage, but the script rushes through the escalation of her exchanges with Wilson, making it harder to buy the degree to which she is willing to compromise herself by becoming an accomplice in his escape plan. Of course, the sad phenomenon of women falling under the spell of incarcerated men is well-documented, but some audiences might find themselves thinking Karen is too smart to be pulled in so deep. McNairy leans into the enigmatic side of Wilson. He has the voice of a richly expressive writer, implying sensitivity and humanity alongside his unquestionable intelligence, but also the coiled danger and volatility of an unrepentantly calculating killer. Did he court Karen’s complicity from the start or did the plan coalesce in stages once the unexplained bruises and cuts on her face pointed to violence at home, exposing her loneliness and vulnerability? Putting his lean and sinewy physicality to disquieting use, McNairy makes Wilson both unreadable and coldly transparent, giving him equal parts menace and magnetism. The most harrowing scenes follow an innocent family, John Lawson ( William Jackson Harper ), his wife Jane (Devyn Tyler) and their two sweet young kids. Jane’s belief in forgiveness crashes up against the far less categorical reality of a vicious world when the Lawsons are dropped into a situation of extreme terror. Harper and Tyler’s performances are heartstopping. There’s expert work also from Pyle as a careworn law enforcement officer unable to remain indifferent to the taking of another life in the the name of the law. A terrific scene in which Joan unburdens herself of troubling thoughts resonates throughout the execution, which Nelson makes the effective choice to show in unflinchingly clinical detail. Like other death row dramas including Clemency , Just Mercy and Dead Man Walking , this film questions whether there’s really that big a difference between murderous cruelty and state-sanctioned capital punishment. The one disappointment of the superb ensemble is that Sinners standout Wunmi Mosaku is given too little to do as a supportive friend to Karen, who takes her in when she’s forced to flee from Kenneth. But this is nonetheless a fascinatingly dark and uncompromising film that reaffirms Nelson’s standing as a vital force in American independent filmmaking for more than three decades. Full credits Venue: Toronto International Film Festival (Gala Presentations) Production companies: Co-Created Media, V42, Red Barn Films, in association with QWGmire, Story Mill Entertainment Cast: Amanda Seyfried, Scoot McNairy, Missi Pyle, Devyn Tyler, Elizabeth Marvel, Tim Blake Nelson, Grant Harvey, William Jackson Harper, Wunmi Mosaku Director-screenwriter: Tim Blake Nelson Producers: Tim Blake Nelson, Julie Buck, Ryan Bartecki, Billy Hines, Miles David Romney Executive producers: Hal Widlansky, Bob Bookman, Jeffrey Cole, Christopher Hines, GaryLevinsohn, Steven Sims, Molly C. Quinn, Matthew M. articles.title: Dolly Parton Posthumously Accepts Americana Award in Newly Released Video Recorded Before Her Death: ‘Just Know That I Will Always Love You’
articles.full_text: Sep 17, 2026 5:10am PT Dolly Parton Posthumously Accepts Americana Award in Newly Released Video Recorded Before Her Death: ‘Just Know That I Will Always Love You’ By Chris Willman Plus Icon Chris Willman Senior Music Writer and Chief Music Critic ChrisWillman Latest Dolly Parton Posthumously Accepts Americana Award in Newly Released Video Recorded Before Her Death: ‘Just Know That I Will Always Love You’ 2 hours ago Tom Petty’s Original Heartbreakers to Reunite for First Time in Decades for Americana Awards, Fronted by Chris Stapleton; Boxed Set of ’70s Rarities Coming 22 hours ago Sheryl Crow Serenaded by Olivia Rodrigo, Chris Stapleton, Jason Isbell and Other Stars at BMI Troubadour Tribute in Nashville 2 days ago See All Courtesy Dolly Parton Estate Some attendees at the Americana Music Honors & Awards might have assumed that the lifetime achievement award for Dolly Parton was something that the Americana Music Association had come up with to honor her in the immediate wake of her death. So a gasp went up from the crowd at the Ryman Auditorium Wednesday night when the lights went down midway through the ceremony and Parton appeared on a big screen to accept the award in what was intended to be in absentia, and would up being posthumous. It wasn’t said when Parton filmed the video, but it was assumed to have been during the summer, which made it all the more startling to see the 80-year-old superstar looking as relaxed, lively and vivacious as she had at any point in recent years. The video acceptance speech was preceded by an introduction from Emmylou Harris , and followed by a tribute performance given by Brandi Carlile and the supergroup trio of I’m With Her (Sarah Jarosz, Aoife O’Donoan and Sara Watkins), singing one of Parton’s most personal signature songs, the autobiographical “Coat of Many Colors.” (Watch video of that performance below.) In the video, Parton says ,”Well, hey, it’s Dolly, and I am so honored to receive the Lifetime Achievement Award from the Americana Music Association. I mean, roots music, or what is now called Americana music, is what I grew up playing back in the Smoky Mountains. It’s that same music that drew me back to East Tennessee back in 1997 to write and record my album ‘Hungry Again.’ “And that project really opened the door to a series of bluegrass and acoustic albums that changed the course of my career in so many ways. Now, new fans discovered these albums, new Americana music communities embraced them, and now, looking back at it all, I see this era of my career as a musical renaissance of sorts.” She concluded, “And I want to thank everybody at the AMA for recognizing me with this award. It’s a great honor, truly. And just know that I will always love you.” Parton receiving the lifetime achievement award was announced just this month, but obviously long in the works. The existence of the acceptance speech was a surprise to the audience, as was the musical performance that followed. On the red carpet, Carlile told Variety , “Dolly’s being honored this year, and that makes me feel really good to be able to be there and bear witness to that.” In her introductory speech, Harris — who collaborated with Parton on the hit “Trio” album, along with Linda Ronstadt — explored her legacy. “Just a few weeks ago, something utterly unthinkable happened: Dolly Parton left our world. But over her time here, this tiny, extraordinary woman made it a better, brighter and kinder place,” Harris said to applause. “One of the many pearls — Dolly would call them rhinestones — of wisdom she imparted was her four-part motto: dream more, learn more, care more, be more,” Harris continued. “Dolly was more from the very start. More than the odds anyone gave her growing up in poverty in Locust Ridge, Tennessee, the fourth of 12 children. More than the precocious 10-year-old who sang on a local TV show. More tha just another pretty woman moving to Nashville with her guitar. And certainly more than the ‘dumb blonde’ she sang about, but never was. “In 1967, Dolly got a good start on her big dream when she landed a gig as the girl singer with Porter Wagoner. All right, remember those? Their duets were a hit on the show and on the charts, but Dolly was nobody’s sidekick. She wanted more and she deserved more, and she set out to get it, always, always, on her own terms. And we all know what happened when Dolly set her sights on something. She didn’t just succeed, she expanded the borders of what a musician could be. “She was a country star, then a pop star, then a global icon. She was one of our all-time greatest songwriters, but she shined just as brightly on stage. She lit up the TV screen and then she lit up the movie screen. Her stunningly beautiful, pure mountain voice could make us cry and then crack us up with a well aimed, sometimes bawdy joke. “There was nothing Dolly couldn’t do, and so she did it. She opened Dollywood, a theme part that continues to provide a real economic boost to the area she grew up in… She created a relief fund that helped hundreds of families get back on her feet after the wildfires ravaged east TN a decade ago. well all remember those. And she saved lives all over the world by funding research that helped lead to a COVID vaccine. Yeah, man, she did that. Closest to her heart was her Imagination Library. it’s given out more than 300 million free books just so far, and that’s showing kids all over the country that they can dream more and be more.” Saying goodbye before the video rolled, “Farewell, Dolly, godspeed, and thank you for everything.” Wednesday’s show had several emotional tributes to the dearly departed. As announced on the morning of the show, six members of Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers — original members Mike Campbell, Benmont Tench, Ron Blair and Stan Lynch — reunited in honor of the group’s 50th anniversary, for a lifetime achievement honor. Two additional latter-day members, Steve Ferrone and Scott Thurston, also appeared. The show opened with Chris Stapleton fronting the band for three numbers, “American Girl,” “Breakdown” and “You Wreck Me.” Related Stories Zack Snyder Wants You to Know He’s No Fascist: ‘I Made the Gayest Movie Ever Made’ At the end of the three-and-a-half-hour program, much of the show’s performing cast and winners reemerged on stage for the finale, a tribute to the late Raul Malo of the Mavericks. articles.title: BBC, Bobby Prod, Folivari, Gao Shan Pictures Honored by Europe’s Animation Industry at Cartoon Forum
articles.full_text: Sep 17, 2026 5:30am PT BBC, Bobby Prod, Folivari, Gao Shan Pictures Honored by Europe’s Animation Industry at Cartoon Forum The four major players respectively were saluted as broadcaster, investor/distributor and producer of the year, with Gao Shan bringing home the very first Ecoprod Cartoon Tributes for its commitment to sustainability in animation. By Kevin Giraud Plus Icon Kevin Giraud Latest BBC, Bobby Prod, Folivari, Gao Shan Pictures Honored by Europe’s Animation Industry at Cartoon Forum 2 hours ago Upcoming Canadian Animated Series Shine At Cartoon Forum 2026 1 day ago Heartfelt, Rare Animated Belgian Feature ‘Juul’ Headlines Studio 100 Film’s Expanding Slate at TIFF Market 3 days ago See All 'The Broos,' Courtesy of Bobby Prod Cartoon Forum , the leading co-production event in Europe for animated series, has unveiled the winners of this year’s Cartoon Tributes, recognizing the dedication and creativity of key players in the European animation industry. Chosen by the event’s attendees gathered in Toulouse, the winners in the three established categories (Producer, Broadcaster and Investor/Distributor of the Year) were celebrated today as the Forum slowly comes to a close after three days of intense pitching sessions, networking and debates around the state of European animated TV industry. Related Stories 'Like ‘Amores Perros,’ I Hope My Film Will Also Transcend Time in Some Way,’ Says Gael García Bernal of His Third Directorial Outing, ‘Hombre al Agua’ Water Crisis Documentary 'Every Living Thing' Sets Toronto Market Debut, Adds VIBE as Strategic Partner (EXCLUSIVE) This year, the Producer of the Year went to Bobby Prod (France), who presented “The Broos” back in 2024 at Cartoon Forum. Now streaming on ARTE France, the series (which originated on social media before being developed as an animated series in co-production with ARTE) highlights the potential of digital-first storytelling to reach wider audiences, with creators and communities deeply tied together. Popular on Variety An approach that’s been at the heart of Bobby Prod for more than 15 years, as the studio built its strong identity around irreverent humour, creative freedom and bold storytelling. From bringing known IPs to life with “Creatures Commandos” or “Dead Cells,” Bobby Prod and sister company Bobbypills are now expanding into their own originals IPs with French hit queer animated feature “ Jim Queen ” now being presented at TIFF, and Jordan Firstman announced as lead voice cast. France’s Folivari International takes home the Investor/Distributor of the Year award. Two year since its creation by Folivari, the independent sales agency carefully built its distinctive slate blending in-house titles and third-party acquisitions, with hit series such as “Samuel,” and buzzy titles currently in production and/or development, such as “Pil’s Adventures,” “Ted & Paula’s Tadpole Journey,” “Nino Dino” and “The Baker Street Four,” all presented at Cartoon Forum. BBC , UK’s public-service broadcaster and a major player in the global economy of animated TV series, received the Broadcaster of the Year award, emphasizing the enduring ties between European animation and the post-Brexit United Kingdom. With its children’s services CBeebies and CBBC catering respectively to preschool and school-age audiences, BBC remains a major commissioner and co-producer of children’s animation, with a strong focus on original content and partnerships with independent production companies. A long-standing presence at Cartoon Forum, BBC boarded several European series to its slate after their Forum pitches, including “Duck & Frog,” “Maddie + Triggs,” “Piggy Builders,” “Pablo” and “Dungeons & Kittens.” This year’s Tributes also introduced a fourth category, the Ecoprod-Cartoon Tribute, honoring a European animation production company or initiative that has made a significant contribution to advancing sustainability in the sector. Presented in partnership with Ecoprod, a French non-profit organisation supporting the audiovisual industry’s environmental transition, the new award featured three nominees, with the winner selected by Ecoprod in recognition of its commitment to sustainability across its operations, production methods and storytelling. The very first Ecoprod-Cartoon Forum Tribute went to French, Réunion Island-based Gao Shan Pictures , a 2D and 3D animation service studio and production company creating bold, distinctive and meaningful films for international audiences with sustainability at its core. A stance that is reflected both in the stories it chooses and in the way they are produced, with credits including “ In Waves ,” “The Smurfs,” “Jim Queen” and “Allah is Not Obliged.” At Cartoon Forum 2026, Gao Shan Pictures presented “The Roots of My Hair,” a 2D animated series for teenagers aged 12 to 15 adapted from the eponymous best-selling graphic novel. This year, all nominees had strong ties to Cartoon Forum, having participated in the event both to pitch their projects and to connect with the European animation industry. Companies from the Czech Republic, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, Spain and Sweden were also among this year’s nominees. Created in 1990 to boost the co-production and distribution of European animation across television and new media platforms, Cartoon Forum has since helped more than a 1,000 1,053 animation series obtain financing, totaling more than €3.83 billion ($4.39B). articles.full_text: Sep 17, 2026 6:02am PT Nex Playground Gaming Console Maker Raises More Than $150 Million in Funding, Niantic’s Jeff Shouger Joins as CFO By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest Nex Playground Gaming Console Maker Raises More Than $150 Million in Funding, Niantic’s Jeff Shouger Joins as CFO 47 minutes ago Overwolf Ads Launches ‘In-Game Audience Map’ Product for Brands to Identify What Their Customers Play Across More Than 5,000 Video Games (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago How Competitive ‘Pokémon’ Inspired Author Ava Reid’s New Dystopian YA Series ‘Winterveil’ 2 days ago See All Nex Nex , the company behind the popular family gaming console Nex Playground , has secured more than $150 million in new financing to support expansion across retail distribution and help grow its content ecosystem with major gaming and entertainment partners. According to Nex, the company plans to roll out “connected play,” which will allow families to play together on its fitness-centric gaming consoles across households and distances. Led by CEO David Lee, Nex also plans to expand across Europe and Asia, following its recent expansion into Canada, the U.K. and the Republic of Ireland. Nex will move into Germany later this year, with Japan and Korea planned for 2027. Popular on Variety Related Stories Zack Snyder Wants You to Know He’s No Fascist: ‘I Made the Gayest Movie Ever Made’ Nex Playground ‘s current lineup consists of 60 games, including globally recognized franchises and characters such as “Bluey,” Barbie, “Kung Fu Panda” and “Peppa Pig,” with experiences spanning music, sports, fitness, party and learning. The slate will continue to grow this fall and holiday season with “NFL Flag,” “Dude Perfect Trickshot Challenge,” “PAC-MAN” with Bandai Namco Entertainment and more. The late-stage funding comes in the same year that Nex Playground crossed more than one million units sold, with the system now distributed across more than 7,000 U.S. retail locations, including Costco, Sam’s Club, Target, Walmart and Best Buy. Nex’s subscriber base has grown sevenfold over the past 18 months and is approaching 1 million subscribers, a milestone the company expects to surpass by year-end. This new round of financing includes a Series E led by Baillie Gifford and BAI Capital, with participation from NBA Investments, Logitech, Medici Capital Partners, and the Raine Group, alongside a new credit facility with JPMorgan. Additionally, Nex has brought on Niantic vet Jeff Shouger as its chief financial officer and set Shouger and gaming and technology industry veteran Bing Gordon as new members of the company’s board of directors. “Families have timeless needs: to move, grow, connect, and have fun. The response to Nex Playground has shown us that active play can serve those needs at a meaningful scale,” Lee said. “We are building Nex to be a 100-year company. This investment gives us the resources to bring active play to millions more families around the world, and Jeff and Bing bring extraordinary experience building enduring gaming and technology companies. I’m thrilled to have them with us for this next chapter.” Jessica Chastain to Star in New Netflix Drama Series ‘The Retrievals’ Loading comments... articles.title: CookUnity Serves Gourmet Meals in New York City Bodegas With Spicy Promotional Recipe
articles.full_text: Sep 17, 2026 6:20am PT CookUnity Serves Gourmet Meals in New York City Bodegas With Spicy Promotional Recipe By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest CookUnity Serves Gourmet Meals in New York City Bodegas With Spicy Promotional Recipe 32 minutes ago CNBC Bolsters Staff Devoted to DTC, Streaming 24 hours ago ‘60 Minutes’ Season Debut Sees 21% Drop in Ratings: Is NFL or CBS News to Blame? 2 days ago See All Courtesy of CookUnity How do you get consumers to pick one subscription food-delivery service over another? Perhaps by serving up something a little different on the marketing front. CookUnity launched in 2016, with the premise of tweaking the recipe in the increasingly crowded business of serving meals to harried consumers who have little time to cook or prepare dinner. The independent company offers meals designed by top chefs such as Esther Choi, Jose Garces, and Marcus Samuelsson. Related Stories Zack Snyder Wants You to Know He’s No Fascist: ‘I Made the Gayest Movie Ever Made’ Its latest promotional effort aims to burnish its offerings to every New Yorker. On Thursday eight chefs set up shop – literally – at five local bodegas, delis or corner stores, serving up signature dishes for free to anyone who might walk in. John DeLucie, for example, grilled up rack of lamb, while Andrew Rea, also known as Babish, offered spicy chili-garlic noodles and Guinness shepherd’s pie. Popular on Variety “There are a lot of other providers of meals and subscription programs throughout the country,” acknowledges Michael Baruch, CookUnity’s head of brand. But the company believes it has a notable distinction that puts high quality dishes from celebrated chiefs in the hands of people who might ordinarily might not be able to sample them. “We don’t make any food. What we do is partner with the best chefs in the world,” he says, who take part because CookUnity’s distribution allows them to forge connections with customers not in the immediate vicinity of their restaurants. “Bodegas and delis and corner stores are part fo the cultural fabric of New York,” Baruch adds. Putting the chefs in these well-visited locations “provides access to individuals and communication with the chefs at a level people wouldn’t ordinarily have access to.” The global food subscription market size was valued at $6.19 billion in 2025, according to Fortune Business Insights, and is projected to grow to $14.4 billion in 2032, up from $6.74 billion in 2026. North American consumers create the biggest demand for such services. Chefs will also be handing out complete meals under seal that people can take home and eat later and offer “little bites” at the bodegas that can be sampled. Guests can also scratch a bodega-style lottery ticket for a chance to win free CookUnity meals for a year and additional prizes including special dining experiences at participating chefs’ restaurants. The promotion will, hopefully “give bodega owners a day off,” says Baruch, and “create some energy in these stores” that will get consumers to sample new foods and forge different connections with chefs. They will also promote appearances, he says, on their own social channels. Jessica Chastain to Star in New Netflix Drama Series ‘The Retrievals’ Loading comments... articles.full_text: Sep 17, 2026 6:53am PT Former Disney Star Debby Ryan Suffered ‘Life-Altering Brain Injury’ After Multiple Concussions: ‘Some Things Did Not Come Back’ By Zack Sharf Plus Icon Zack Sharf Digital News Director ZSharf Latest Matthew Lillard Says ‘I Feel Ashamed’ for Acting in ‘Scream 7’ After Melissa Barrera Got Fired: ‘I Blew That. I’m on the Wrong Side of History’ 16 hours ago ‘The Wire’ and ‘It’ Actor James Ransone Was Excluded From Emmys and Oscars In Memoriam Tributes; His Wife Says ‘It’s Simply Not Right’ 23 hours ago ‘Resident Evil’ First Reactions: Zach Cregger’s Zombie Horror Is ‘Gloriously Gory’ and One of ‘The Best Video Game Adaptations’ Ever 1 day ago See All Getty Images for Film Independen Debby Ryan , the former Disney Channel star who broke out on the network’s “Suite Life on Deck” before fronting her own series “ Jessie ,” revealed during an interview on “Mythical Kitchen’s Last Meals” (via People ) that she suffered a “life-altering brain injury a few years ago” after a long history of battling migraines. The brain injury included “sustained shaking over a minute of time” and resulted in “pre-incident Debby and post-incident Debby,” the actor said. Related Stories Zack Snyder Wants You to Know He’s No Fascist: ‘I Made the Gayest Movie Ever Made’ “I had a pretty crazy life-altering brain injury a few years ago, and I was out of commission for like six months, and I went to this neurological rehab for like six months,” Ryan revealed, noting her symptoms continued to worsen until she tried a “fringe science treatment” to help get her “back online but there are some things that just did not come back.” Popular on Variety The brain injury occurred after years spent dealing with “hellish” migraines. Ryan referred to herself as a “migraine warrior,” adding: “Quite often the world is really loud and too bright. A lot is going on. After the fifth concussion, the brain injury made things significantly worse.” “Quite often I can see better and think better with my eyes closed,” she continued about her condition. “The visual data I am taking in can be so distracting and so loud. The migraines were significantly worsened by that. If there is a thing that can make things really singular, I like that. I feel really fortunate that I have an amazing team of people around me who sort of reminded me who I am and was and also held a lot of space for that to change, potentially permanently, and love me through that.” Ryan rose debuted as Bailey Pickett on “The Suite Life on Deck” in 2008 alongside headliners Dylan and Cole Sprouse. She then fronted her own Disney Channel series, “Jessie,” in 2011 opposite Peyton List and Cameron Boyce. The show ran for four seasons and 98 episodes between 2011 and 2015.
