articles.title: Ozzy Osbourne and Black Sabbath’s Final Concert Film Sets October Release Date
articles.full_text: Sep 16, 2026 7:00am PT Ozzy Osbourne and Black Sabbath’s Final Concert Film Sets October Release Date By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest ‘70 Up’ Producer on How the Series Survived Six Decades and Became the ‘Definitive Longitudinal Documentary’: ‘To See a Whole Life Change in Front of You Is a Mindf—’ 23 hours ago How British Comedy Show ‘Mock the Week’ Found New Life on TLC After BBC Cancellation: ‘Absence Makes the Heart Grow Fonder’ 2 days ago ‘Sunday in the Park With George’ London Revival Canceled After Ariana Grande, Jonathan Bailey Exit 2 days ago See All Ross Halfin The long-awaited film of Ozzy Osbourne and Black Sabbath ‘s final concert has finally set a release date for later this year. The movie, now titled “Ozzy & Black Sabbath: Back to the Beginning,” will bow in theaters worldwide on Oct. 28. It is directed by Ben Wainwright-Pearce, who also helmed “Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour” for Disney+, with the press release promising a “fully immersive audio-visual experience.” Related Stories Seth Green Says He Was Never Invited Back for the Canceled 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer' Reboot Filmed just 17 days before Osbourne died , the concert in Birmingham, U.K. functioned as both a homecoming and farewell for the heavy metal legend, who performed a solo set as well as playing with original Black Sabbath members Tony Iommi, Geezer Butler and Bill Ward for the first time in 20 years. Popular on Variety “’Back to the Beginning’ came about because I asked Ozzy what would really make him happy,” Sharon Osbourne, Ozzy’s wife and manager, said in a statement. “And he said the only thing that would make him happy was if he could perform again and say goodbye to his fans. That’s all he wanted to do. He wanted to say goodbye and thank you.” Osbourne died on July 22, 2025 following a yearslong struggle with Parkinson’s disease. The concert, which was hosted by Jason Momoa, also saw an array of other metal and alternative artists performing throughout the event, including Disturbed’s David Draiman, Halestorm, Travis Barker, Steven Tyler of Aerosmith, Slayer, Pantera, Tool and Alice in Chains. 42,000 people attended the event in person at Birmingham’s Villa Park stadium on July 5 last year with another 3 million watching via a paid livestream. Tim van Someren directed the live concert, which was produced by Jim Parsons, Jamie Silk and Dan Seliger. Trafalgar Releasing are distributing the film, which was produced by Mercury Studios. Tickets are set to go on sale on Sept. 24 via backtothebeginning.com . “Ozzy Osbourne and Black Sabbath’s Back to the Beginning concert was a landmark cultural moment,” said Marc Allenby, CEO of Trafalgar Releasing. “Bringing it to cinemas worldwide is an opportunity to further cement Ozzy’s legacy and impact. We are really looking forward to giving fans around the world a chance to experience this final celebration of Ozzy and Black Sabbath together on the big screen.” Shudder Nabs U.S. Rights to ‘Bloody Tennis’ and Horror Film Grabs Buyers in Other Major Territories Ahead of Locarno World Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) ‘V/H/S/MIXTAPE’ Set at Shudder; Ninth Chapter of Horror Anthology Features RZA, Ernest Dickerson, Flying Lotus and More (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Season 35 Premiere Recap: The Men Take The Lead In First Of Two-Night Kick Off & Someone Goes Home Already
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Season 35 Premiere Recap: The Men Take The Lead In First Of Two-Night Kick Off & Someone Goes Home Already Emmys Producers Dish On Taylor Swift ‘SVU’ Sketch (Including The Easter Eggs), Mariska Hargitay’s Hosting Chops, Dolly Parton Tribute & More Sally Field Reflects On Filming ‘Remarkably Bright Creatures’ In Canada: “Let’s Keep Our Neighbors Close” — Emmys Backstage View All September 15, 2026 6:59pm 'Dancing With The Stars' Season 35 ABC SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from night one of the Season 35 premiere of Dancing with the Stars . Back like they never left! The ballroom at CBS Television City was once again glittering with celebrities on Tuesday night to kick off Season 35 of Dancing with the Stars. There are 16 contestants vying for the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy at the top of the season, and ABC opted for a two-night premiere that split the dances between Tuesday and Wednesday nights. On the first night, only the male celebrities performed. The ladies will take the floor on Wednesday night. Related Stories News 'American Idol' Moving Production To Georgia As ABC Series Becomes Latest To Leave California News 'Dancing With The Stars' Pro Emma Slater Pulls Out Stops By Performing With Savannah Bananas Ahead Of Tuesday's Premiere Unfortunately, things did not go over without a hitch. The party was interrupted by some tech issues, with voting going down online in the middle of the show. They threw out the ABC.com votes mid-premiere and relied solely on text votes, which have their own wrinkle this year since there’s two contestants who share the same name. Voters will need to specify Conner L. or Connor W. in their text votes, and they won’t count if they don’t, according to hosts Afonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough. What could go wrong there? Watch on Deadline While this week’s results might be questionable, the show must go on. Here’s how things shook out on night one. Savannah Bananas midfielder Jackson Olson with Emma Slater. The baseball player kicked things off with a cha cha to “Wannabe” by the Spice Girls — and it’s clear that Slater is reveling in being paired with a younger partner this season. In the package before the dance, she said it’s the first time she’s ever worked with a celeb in their 20s, and admits there were less “limitations” working with Olson.The energetic routine was a nice introduction to Olson, and the judges ate it up. “The ballroom is back!” judge Derek Hough said. “Jackson, my man, you are a natural born performer.” BUT! Hough also warned that the judges are going to be pretty tough with their scores this season, and Olson has plenty of room for improvement in the technique department. SCORE: 15 out of 30 Reality star Tyler Cameron with Sharna Burgess. The Bachelor alum was the first of many reality stars to take the dance floor over the next two days, dancing a tango. The former college football player says he did take some dance classes in college, but he’s got some brushing up to do. After a multi-year hiatus from the show, Burgess pleased the judges with her first routine with Cameron. “Tyler, what’s going on here? I have to say, I’m very pleasantly surprised. I mean, look at him. He looks like a tank…you can move, man,” Bruno Tonioli complimented. SCORE: 17 out of 30 Reality star Conner Leavitt with Adele Zaikman. These two stepped onto the ballroom floor with something to prove Tuesday night, what with newcomer Zaikman as the winner of DWTS: The Next Pro and Leavitt married to Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt, who took the ballroom by storm last season and leveraged the exposure to launch a Broadway run on Chicago . They danced a salsa to “Whoomp! (There It Is)” by Tag Team, putting Zaikman in her element as a Latin expert and taking Leavitt straight out of his. Carrie Ann Inaba called the routine “a little chaotic,” but overall, the judges loved the enthusiasm. SCORE: 12 out of 30 Late-night sidekick Guillermo Rodriguez with Witney Carson. Season 34 champ Carson is back on the ballroom floor with a much different contestant this year. She’s guiding Jimmy Kimmel’s right-hand man Rodriguez through the competition, and they started off with a cha cha. Carson, who is impressively competing pregnant this year, tried to disguise her partner’s lack of technique by leaning into Rodriguez’s charm, reminding why he’s spent decades at Kimmel’s side on late night. It only kind of worked. “Listen, was the technique there? No. Was the effort there? Absolutely,” Hough said. “We can’t be having heel leads in the cha cha.” Regardless, the audience clearly responded to Rodriguez’s “spicy” performance, chanting his name when he finished. There were even boos when the judges issued their (probably rightful) rating. SCORE: 10 out of 30 Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach. Julianne Hough kind of botched his introduction, but Frech still made a great impression on his first night as his rehearsal package gave audiences a glimpse of what he’s working through this season as an above-the-knee amputee in the competition. He and Karagach had to make some accommodations to take on the tango, but boy, did they deliver. The judges loved the fiery routine to Kelly Clarkson’s “Since U Been Gone,” and so did the crowd. “What really impressed me, you really looked like a leading man,” Tonioli said. SCORE: 20 out 30 Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold. The second Connor of the night showcased his personality with a cha cha to “I Like It, I Love It” by Tim McGraw. Of the group, Wood has some of the least dance experience, so it appears Arnold may have her work cut out for her this season. But what he lacks in technique, he makes up for in his sincerity. On the bright side, Inaba says he didn’t give her “the ick” when he made a wrong move. A for effort! No comment on the person riding a bedazzled mechanical bull in the background for the entire number. SCORE: 16 out of 30 Musician Taylor Hanson with Britt Stewart. The middle Hanson brother is back on stage after spending years “avoiding dancing.” He says he’s uncomfortable performing without an instrument in tow, but Stewart tells him to think of her as his new “safety blanket.” Having gone from avoiding all dancing to taking on the quickstep night one, Derek Hough assures him he should feel proud, despite the flaws. Tonioli agreed. Now, he needs to work on his frame. “Don’t tighten up,” Tonioli said. SCORE: 16 out of 30 Actor Harry Shum Jr. with Jenna Johnson. The Glee and Grey’s Anatomy actor closed out the night one with yet another cha cha. Johnson took advantage of Shum’s freestyle and hip-hop experience, though, and his prior performance chops on Glee to deliver a performance full of personality and charm. And, well, they absolutely saved the best for last. Those two lit up the ballroom floor with an “emergency disco” that had Tonioli in a fit. “The chemistry between you two is off the charts. Sharp as a scalpel,” he said. SCORE: 21 out of 30 (the highest score of the night!) So, who goes home? Sadly, after just one dance, Conner Leavitt and Adele Zaikman are sent packing. Well, they’ll be back in the ballroom at least once more for tomorrow’s ‘live afterparty’ with Season 34 winner Robert Irwin and whomever among the women is voted off on night two. articles.title: ‘Possible Love’ DoP Kim Ji-yong, ‘The Blue Road’ Director Han Jun-hee & WETA FX’s Kimball Thurston Among Speakers For Netflix ‘Creative Asia’ At BIFF
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz ‘Possible Love’ DoP Kim Ji-yong, ‘The Blue Road’ Director Han Jun-hee & WETA FX’s Kimball Thurston Among Speakers For Netflix ‘Creative Asia’ At BIFF Goodfellas Boards World Sales On Kamila Andini’s ‘Four Seasons In Java’ Ahead Of Toronto Premiere Finecut Scores Sales On Trio Of Titles Starring Members Of K-Pop Groups NCT, Fifty Fifty & The Boyz View All September 15, 2026 7:14pm Busan International Film Festival Busan International Film Festival Netflix has announced that speakers including Possible Love DoP Kim Ji-yong, The Blue Road director Han Jun-hee and WETA FX’s CTO Kimball Thurston will join the streamer’s Creative Asia programme at this year’s Busan International Film Festival (BIFF). Ji-yong will deliver a masterclass on how he and Possible Love director Lee Chang-dong shaped the visual world of the film, which just scored the Grand Jury Prize in Venice and is Korea’s official section for the Oscars. Han Jun-hee, whose credits also include D.P. and Weak Hero Class , is hosting a masterclass entitled “Making Unexpected Stories Resonate” about turning unexpected, even uncomfortable, subjects into stories that capture the world’s attention. Related Stories News Alix Earle's Reality Series 'Earle Meets World' Finds More Viewers In Week Two News 'The Murder Of JonBenét Ramsey' Gets December Release Date On Netflix & First-Look Photo Of Melissa McCarthy & Clive Owen As Girl's Parents Creative Asia will also feature a masterclass on “Location and Storytelling”, bringing together perspectives from Lauren Cooper of Location Managers Guild International, Perfect Days producer Reiko Kunieda and Sung Q Lee, Senior Director, APAC Production at Netflix. Watch on Deadline WETA FX’s chief technology officer Kimball Thurston is one of the speakers on an industry panel about using AI in filmmaking – “AI in Filmmaking: New Tools, New Possibilities” – along with Sung Q Lee and Korean director Kang Yun-sung ( Run To The West , The Outlaws ). Another industry panel entitled “New Voices in Filmmaking: What’s Ahead” will examine small- to medium-budget filmmaking and features speakers including Namkoong Sun ( Love Untangled ) and Wi Eun-kyoung and Son Gwang-min, co-directors of My Aunt . The programme also includes two workshops: “The Art and Archetypes of Cinematic Storytelling”, led by Netflix’s Director, Content Acquisition, Christopher Mack, is aimed at writers and breaks down what makes a pilot compelling and the structural choices that keep audiences watching. Led by Netflix’s Director, Creative Strategy, “Understanding the Buyer’s Perspective” looks at what motivates greenlight decisions, how a show gets chosen for financing, and what kind of script or story stays in the imagination after a pitch ends. Designed to support the region’s next generation of creators, the programme has been devised by Netflix in partnership with BIFF, the Asian Film Commissions Network (AFCNet) and the Motion Picture Association (MPA). It will take place on October 10 at Dongseo University Centum Campus. BIFF is running October 6-15 at the Busan Cinema Center and locations across Busan, with the Asian Contents & Film Market taking place at BEXCO October 10-13. articles.title: Fired ‘Shrinking’ Crew Member Accuses Warner Bros TV Of Doing Nothing Over Sexual Harassment By EP; Being Scapegoated After Complaining
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Fired ‘Shrinking’ Crew Member Accuses Warner Bros TV Of Doing Nothing Over Sexual Harassment By EP; Being Scapegoated After Complaining So Not A Shocker! Trump Weighs In For David Ellison & Paramount Over $1.88B Bond Battle With States No Death Penalty For Nick Reiner, L.A. DA Announces View All September 15, 2026 7:33pm Jason Segel and Harrison Ford in 'Shrinking' Apple TV+ Despite 10 nominations, Shrinking came up short at the Emmys on Monday, but the Warner Bros Television produced show may be taking centerstage in court soon. A longtime Key Second Assistant Director on the Jason Segel and Harrison Ford starring series says she was abruptly fired after a long day of shooting on July 10 by Executive Producer Kip Kroeger because of so-called “different needs of production.” In her seven claim compliant filed today in L.A. Superior Court against WBTV, Shrinking EP/director Randall Winston and others, Mindy Tessa McKoin doesn’t buy it. Related Stories News Emmy TV Ratings Down 10% From Last Year News Amazon In Talks To Take Over Emmys TV Deal As the document from attorney Avi Gholian exclaims of the industry vet’s multi-season Shrinking stint: “no performance deficiency, misconduct. or business rationale was identified then or anytime thereafter.” Watch on Deadline Filing earlier today with the California Civil Rights Department before going to the LASC docket, McKoin alleges the real reason she was canned was because of reporting an intentional “sexual abuse” by Winston at the June 22, 2024 Shrinking Season 2 wrap party, She says it was because of that and because of her raising a stink about of “inaccurate time records and pay statements.” Production and WBTV problems that Loot and Young Sheldon alum McKoin and her lawyers assert resulted in zero “corrective action” on the former and a lot of her Shrinking bosses not making a “big deal” about the former. McKoin says the CAA-repped Winston subjected her “to unwelcome, severe harassment because of her sex, including by grabbing and groping her breast without her consent at a work-related function in the presence of a coworker” at the 2024 party. “Such conduct was sufficiently severe to alter the conditions of Plaintiff employment and to create a hostile, intimidating, and offensive working environment.” An environment made all the worse by WBTV doing nothing about it, according to the plaintiff. While the sexual harassment and sexual battery claims sit on the top of McKoin’s allegations, it is the pay and timecard tampering of sorts that takes up the bulk of Tuesday’s unspecified damages seeking filing. In terms of retaliation, McKoin insists she made “bona fide complaints, both orally and in writing, that she was owed unpaid wages and that her time records had been unlawfully altered, and otherwise engaged in conduct protected by the Labor Code, including on or about May 26, May 28, June I0, June 11, June 19, and July I, 2026.” Her filing adds: “Warner Bros. discharged Plaintiff on July 10, 2026 – within 90 days of each of these instances of protected activities. “ “ As a direct and proximate result of Warner Bros.’ violation of Labor Code …Plaintiff has suffered and continues to suffer lost wages and work benefits and other actual consequential, and incidental financial losses. as well as emotional distress. humiliation, mental anguish, and anxiety in an amount to be proven at trial.” WBTV had no comment this evening when contacted by Deadline about the complaint and the allegations McKoin makes. Representatives for the multi-Emmy nominated Winston did no response when Deadline reached out about the claims against their client. articles.title: Seriesly Berlin Crowns ‘Hands Up’, Music Drama Featuring Israeli & Palestinian Characters
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Seriesly Berlin Crowns ‘Hands Up’, Music Drama Featuring Israeli & Palestinian Characters True Crime Remains The Red Hot TV Doc Genre, Ampere Data Shows PBS Buys Dutch Dementia Doc ‘Human Forever’, Which Follows “The Greta Thunberg Of Healthcare” View All September 15, 2026 11:21pm Creatives behind 'Hands Up' with the Writers Award jury after win Seriesly Berlin Seriesly Berlin kept up its reputation for backing complex TV series with its latest batch of award winners. Hands Up , a music drama series pitch from the U.S. focused on an Israeli musician and a Palestinian singer brought together in Berlin’s hip-hop scene was the winner of the Writers’ Pitch Award last night at a ceremony near the Fotografiska in Germany’s capital. The pitch was a popular winner, with the jury unanimous on the victor and several people we spoke to agreeing on the choice. The audience cheered wildly as the announcement was made. Related Stories News True Crime Remains The Red Hot TV Doc Genre, Ampere Data Shows News Seriesly Berlin Unveils Full Line-Up With Sessions On 'Krank Berlin', Creative Tensions & Co-Productions “ Hands Up has all the ingredients to be a great series: a clear central conflict, extraordinary characters, and even great music,” said the Seriesly Berlin jury in a statement. “It is a perfect example of a hyper local premise that can serve as a metaphor, touching audiences around the world. This story shows us that creative collaboration can bridge impossible borders, providing a path to mutual understanding in troubled times.” Watch on Deadline Coming from Neta Weiner, Samira Saraya and Michal Cooper Keren and borne out of the U.S., the story follows Israeli musician Geva and Palestinian singer Manal, who join together for a high-stakes collaboration set up by Petra, a former music industry figure who sees in their volatile chemistry a chance for a comeback of her own. As their music gains traction, their growing fame soon turns dangerous, and they are caught between political pressure, family expectations and ongoing public scrutiny, forcing them to risk relationships, their future and even their lives for the freedom to be heard. Palestinian artist, actress and filmmaker Saraya and Jewish rapper, musician and actor Weiner have worked across music, theater and screen as activists whose work explores identity, politics, and resistance. They were members of a Palestinian-Jewish hip-hop group and founders of a cultural education initiative. Israeli screenwriter and showrunner Keren has worked on shows for HBO Go, Canal+, Disney, Rai, Nickelodeon and Netflix. The show beat of pitches from Ireland, Germany, Serbia and the UK to win the Writers Pitch award, and takes home a €1,000 ($1,150) prize. Elsewhere, Latvian drama The Man Behind a Mask ( Cilvēks Maskā ) won the Co-Pro Pitch Award and landed a €25,000 post-production services prize. The show, from creator Anna Kalnina and producer Serge Serpuhovs, follows celebrated Soviet reconstructive surgeon Nikolay, who pioneers groundbreaking procedures, including the USSR’s first sex reassignment surgery, until the KGB blackmails him into espionage. Per the snyopsis, “His missions take him across Europe and beyond, where each medical breakthrough becomes a covert operation. Torn between his calling as a healer and his role as a spy, Nikolay is forced to betray patients, outwit intelligence agencies, and confront impossible moral choices. In the end, he survives, but returns home forever changed, having lost both his innocence and his faith in the regime.” The jury said it was “an engaging story about power and vulnerabilities, set in an original arena and based on true events that uses spy thriller elements to create a highly entertaining show for an international audience with the potential to run for multiple seasons.” The SteinbrennerMüller Award, which is handed out by Berlin-based PR firm SteinbrennerMüller Kommunkation to a German show with the best potential to connect with audiences, went to Hannah Doose’s I Am God ( Ich Bin Gott ). The show follows eight middle-aged people in midlife who come together at a spiritual festival on the German-Polish border. Amid cacao ceremonies, breathwork and psychedelic rituals, relationships begin to unravel, families drift apart and old wounds resurface, as the festival organizers ignore warnings of an approaching tornado. “The premise is a very clear promise of entertainment – world-building set in a nature reserve on the border between Germany and Poland,” said a rep from SteinbrennerMüller. “ I Am God explores social issues in a light-hearted yet relevant way through exaggeration. “This closed setting allows for the creation of characters who reflect all facets of society and with whom a wide audience can identify, combined with plenty of fun. Hovering over it all is the looming threat of an approaching tornado, which could wipe out all those ‘first world problems’ in an instant.” Mayana FIlms is the producer, with Doose writing alongside Nicolas Chevaillier and Sarah Schill. Chevaillier and Zorana Mušikić are the producers. The Seriesly Berlin conference ends today. articles.title: Cate Blanchett To Attend Tokyo Film Festival With Displacement Film Fund Shorts
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Oscars: Spain Selects ‘La Bola Negra’ For International Feature Film Race Cate Blanchett To Attend Tokyo Film Festival With Displacement Film Fund Shorts Screamfest To Open With ‘The Night Driver’ Starring Josh Lucas, David Arquette & Alyssa Milano View All September 16, 2026 12:31am Cate Blanchett speaks on stage during the Cannes Film Festival Teresa Suarez/Pool/Getty Images Cate Blanchett will attend this year’s Tokyo Film Festival with a series of short films supported by her Displacement Film Fund . TIFF will screen five short works produced with support from the Displacement Film Fund, of which Japanese brand Uniqlo is a founding partner. Following the film screenings, there will be a Q&A session with director Mohammad Rasoulof, director Shahrbanoo Sadat ( Super Afghan Gym ), and Blanchett. The screenings will take place the same week that Blanchett is to be honored in Tokyo with the festival’s Praemium Imperiale Award. “I am privileged to have the opportunity to share the inaugural short films supported through the Displacement Film Fund with audiences at Tokyo International Film Festival,” Blanchett said in a statement. Related Stories News Breaking Baz: Léa Seydoux Talks 'Gentle Monster's "Complexity" And "Contradictions" & Why She Wants To Take More Risks -- Telluride Film Festival Festivals Tokyo Film Festival To Open With 'Sukiyaki' & Close With 'Colony'; 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Set As Centerpiece Film “In a world where conflict and persecution are driving displacement and division, cinematic storytelling has a vital role to play in connecting with the experiences of others. Being displaced shouldn’t mean filmmakers abandon their creativity; in fact, their stories may feel even more urgent.” Watch on Deadline The 2026 Tokyo Film Festival will run from October 26 to November 4. Scroll down to see the short projects. 5 Short Films Supported by the Displacement Film Fund Allies in Exile (40 min., United Kingdom/Syria) Dir: Hasan Kattan Two Syrian filmmakers with a past shaped by war document the trauma of waiting for asylum, using friendship and storytelling to survive exile. Rotation (12 min., Ukraine/Turkey) Dir: Maryna Er Gorbach “Rotation” is a therapeutic hypnosis ritual experienced by a young Ukrainian woman who shifted from civilian life to military service. Sense of Water (39 min., Iran/Germany) Dir: Mohammad Rasoulof In the chill of exile, an Iranian writer confronts a foreign language. Super Afghan Gym (14 min., Germany) Dir: Shahrbanoo Sadat In a gym in downtown Kabul, a group of housewives gathers during the only hour of the day reserved for women. articles.title: Disney Seeking Next Big K-Pop Hit After Striking Ten-Project Deal With Kakao
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Hunting Gary Glitter’: Netflix Unveils Trailer & Launch Date For Doc About Race To Expose Serial Sex Abuser Bill Nighy Playing Socially-Challenged Literary Titan In Richard Curtis’ Debut Audio Sitcom Disney Seeking Next Big K-Pop Hit After Striking Ten-Project Deal With Kakao View All September 16, 2026 1:09am 'Kpop Demon Hunters' Netflix Could Disney be about to unearth the next big K-pop hit? Disney Korea has struck a deal with Kakao Entertainment to launch what they are calling a “K-culture fund” and is aiming to pursue around 10 projects over the medium to long term. The pair will “collaborate on projects that bring together K-pop IP and Disney’s stories and characters,” they saiid, “aiming to take the K-IP ecosystem to the next level and create new opportunities on the global stage.” Disney and Kakao stressed that the “K-culture fund” still needs to be ironed out, but they hope to do it. Neither company put a figure on the fund. Related Stories News Finecut Scores Sales On Trio Of Titles Starring Members Of K-Pop Groups NCT, Fifty Fifty & The Boyz Late Night TV Jimmy Kimmel "Play-Acting" Over James Talarico Interview & FCC Threats, White House Claims Disney is a major player in Korea, with hits including Moving, its first original show in the region. It streams a number of K-pop movies and docs including ones focused on giants like BTS. Watch on Deadline Founded in 2021, Kakao Entertainment is an offshoot of Korean media giant Kakao, owning agencies, production companies and entertainment arms. In coming together, Disney and Kakao are clearly looking at the runaway success of KPop Demon Hunters , made by Sony and shown to the world on Netflix. The animated musical about rival K-pop bands who live double lives as demon hunters was undoubtedly the biggest hit of last year and has had a major impact on K-culture. “K-pop today has evolved into a global cultural phenomenon shaping trends across areas including fashion, beauty, and lifestyle,” a spokesperson for Kakao Entertainment said. “Through this partnership, we look forward to bringing K-pop artists and music together with Disney’s stories – which have been loved around the world for generations – and expanding them into new worlds. articles.title: Jodie Whittaker To Star As Hotshot Media Lawyer In ITV Drama ‘In Contempt’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Seriesly Berlin Crowns ‘Hands Up’, Music Drama Featuring Israeli & Palestinian Characters True Crime Remains The Red Hot TV Doc Genre, Ampere Data Shows PBS Buys Dutch Dementia Doc ‘Human Forever’, Which Follows “The Greta Thunberg Of Healthcare” View All September 16, 2026 1:30am Jodie Whittaker Pip in London for CLD Communications EXCLUSIVE: Jodie Whittaker ‘s next starring role will be a hotshot media lawyer in ITV drama In Contempt . Ahead of her role in Hulu pilot Chicks and a part in the London-set Only Murders in the Building Season 6, Whittaker will star in the “high-stakes” legal drama as barrister Olivia Savareid. The character’s top-drawer advocacy skills have built her a career defending people’s reputations and engaging in multi-million pound litigation to prevent their names from being destroyed on social media, but the series will see the tables turned on her. Related Stories News International Revenues Of $2.1B Boost British TV Makers, Census Finds, As Pact Warns BBC Must Avoid "Managed Decline" News Tom Jones Claims He Has Been Fired From 'The Voice UK' Because Of "Financial Difficulty" Sherlock and Dracula maker Hartswood Films is producing in association with its parent, ITV Studios (ITVS), with the show airing in the UK on ITV and STV and on streamers ITVX and STV Player. ITVS has international distribution rights. Watch on Deadline Steve Thompson ( Sherlock ) is the writer, with Sue Vertue and Steven Moffat the executive producers. Ed Bazalgette ( The Last Kingdom ) is the director and Lawrence Till ( Douglas is Cancelled ) the producer. ITV’s Director of Drama, Polly Hill, who commissioned the show is also overseeing production for the broadcaster. In Contempt establishes Olivia’s challenging working relationship with veteran news director Greg Dalman, who edits a London daily newspaper prone to pushing the boundaries of what can be published. With a reputation for taking no prisoners, Greg has the capability of acting recklessly if he believes it’s in the public interest, and and as his legal counsel, Olivia, must summon all her skills and expertise to keep him out of libel court. She is also the mother of 15-year-old daughter, but when an explosive situation erupts at work, she makes a crucial misjudgement and Olivia’s own reputation is suddenly on the line. “There’s always been a voracious appetite for what happens behind the scenes before news stories are published,” said ITV’s Hill. “Steve has created a gripping and thought-provoking series and I’m thrilled Jodie Whittaker has agreed to play ‘hotshot’ lawyer Olivia Savereid. I have no doubt In Contempt will captivate our audience, as it’s a really timely story for ITV to be telling.” Whittaker, known for leading Doctor Who and ITV drama Broadchurch , said of her role as Savareid. “This is an amazing character in a world I haven’t explored before. Steve Thompson’s writing is an absolute joy to work with and I’m so excited to be embarking on this adventure with such a brilliant creative team at Hartswood Films and ITV.” Vertue said she had been seeking to work with Thompson again since BBC series Sherlock , but that “it was never the right time or the right idea” until now. “Then one day he sat down and said, “In the modern world, if you want to kill someone, you don’t use a gun – you destroy their reputation,’ and so began In Contempt . “A whirlwind drama of cancellation, online poison and media law, where there’s less than 12 hours to stop a headline that could detonate someone’s life. This is the story of now, and this is the series for today. I’m delighted to be working with ITV again and to bring to screen Steve Thompson’s most explosive and personal drama yet.” Thompson called the show “a signature piece for me”, adding: “It unpacks the challenging relationship between the media and the law – between the freedom of the press and people’s right to privacy. In a world where all of us are surfing the net, hungry for the latest gossip, this drama takes us behind the curtain and shows us the lawyers who are in the vanguard of that fight.” In Contempt will begin filming in London in the fall with further casting coming closer to production commencing. articles.title: Bill Nighy Playing Socially-Challenged Literary Titan In Richard Curtis’ Debut Audio Sitcom
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Hunting Gary Glitter’: Netflix Unveils Trailer & Launch Date For Doc About Race To Expose Serial Sex Abuser Bill Nighy Playing Socially-Challenged Literary Titan In Richard Curtis’ Debut Audio Sitcom Disney Seeking Next Big K-Pop Hit After Striking Ten-Project Deal With Kakao View All September 16, 2026 2:00am Richard Curtis (left) and Bill Nighy Rich Hardcastle / Aliona Adrianova EXCLUSIVE: Richard Curtis is returning to the sitcom game, this time through audio. The Vicar of Dibley, Blackadder and Mr Bean writer-director is making Greatest Living Writer for BBC Radio 4 starring Bill Nighy , Nicola Walker, Nick Mohammed, Jim Broadbent, Meera Syal and Traitors star Madelyn Smedley. It is Curtis’ first sitcom in nearly 20 years and his first for audio. Launching on Boxing Day on Radio 4 and as a BBC Sounds box-set two weeks prior, the series centers on John Westlake (Nighy), a literary titan whose towering genius has earned him global reverence, lifelong indulgence, and absolutely no useful social skills. As those around him absorb the blast radius of his genius, the series plays with creativity, legacy, literary celebrity, family, and the uncomfortable truth that being good at writing does not necessarily make you good at being a pleasant person. The character draws comparisons with the iconic Billy Mack, who Nighy played with aplomb in Love Actually. Related Stories News 'The Celebrity Traitors' Trailer Offers First Glimpse Of Players Including Bella Ramsey & Maya Jama: "We're In Game Mode Now" News 'Killing Eve' Origin Story 'Honey' To World Premiere At MIPCOM Curtis is an Oscar-nominated British screen legend whose movie credits include Notting Hill and Four Weddings and a Funeral. Watch on Deadline His last TV sitcom was The Vicar of Dibley, which concluded on the BBC in 2007. He has recently turned to animation: writing and producing Netflix’s That Christmas in 2024 and now producing Not Alone for Universal. Curtis said: “I’m loving working in this tight 15” minute format for the BBC – writing for performers I know and love – and writing something that’s about the creative world I have such direct experience of, as it crashes into family dynamics.” Script editor Emma Freud added: “Of all his writing, this is the closest Richard has written to his life, his world, his home and his experiences. It’s been a joy to see the scripts flowing out of him – I’ve never seen him write so fast or enjoy the process as much. He isn’t the brute at the centre of this comedy – but that brute is, I think, how he would secretly like to behave if he could. Which he can’t.” Goldhawk Productions ‘ Greatest Living Writer is produced by Emma Hearn, John Scott Dryden and Alex Hollands and script edited by Freud. It comes on a BBC audio slate that includes pilots from Nish Kumar and Jake Bhardwaj, along with stand-up and quiz shows. articles.title: ‘Hunting Gary Glitter’: Netflix Unveils Trailer & Launch Date For Doc About Race To Expose Serial Sex Abuser
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Hunting Gary Glitter’: Netflix Unveils Trailer & Launch Date For Doc About Race To Expose Serial Sex Abuser Bill Nighy Playing Socially-Challenged Literary Titan In Richard Curtis’ Debut Audio Sitcom Disney Seeking Next Big K-Pop Hit After Striking Ten-Project Deal With Kakao View All September 16, 2026 2:45am Trailer has dropped for Netflix ‘s Hunting Gary Glitter , the former pop superstar who was exposed as a serial child abuser. Check it out above. Launching October 14, the doc follows the pursuit of journalists alongside the survivors who speak out, charting Glitter’s 1997 conviction, through to his years on the run, and eventual incarceration. This string of dogged journalists chase the fugitive pop star across the globe — from Cuba to Cambodia to Vietnam — determined to expose the child sexual abuse he concealed behind decades of chart-topping fame. Real name Paul Francis Gadd, Glitter was a pop sensation in the 1970s and 1980s but was convicted in 1999 of downloading child sexual abuse material and of many more offences over the following years, along with being deported from several countries. He was most recently charged with further historical sex offences. Watch on Deadline Netflix’s doc is its latest big UK true crime series and comes from Voltage TV , with Sam Starbuck and Sanjay Singhal producing the three-parter. Netflix has previously shone a light on serial sex abuser Jimmy Savile via its Jimmy Savile: A British Horror Story doc. articles.title: Islamic Republic State Media Attacks Venice Prize-Winner Lelah Marzban Over Women’s Rights Speech
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Islamic Republic State Media Attacks Venice Prize-Winner Lelah Marzban Over Women’s Rights Speech The Coven Boards French Legalized Cannibalism Horror ‘Sunnyside’ As Filming Begins Venice Winner ‘Woman Unknown’ Unveils New Deals Including France In Wake Of Golden Lion Victory View All September 16, 2026 4:18am Laleh Marzban poses with the Orizzonti Best Actress Award for Falling House Andreas Rentz/Getty Images Laleh Marzban, who won Best Actress in Venice Film Festival’s Orizzonti sidebar, has become the subject of a harsh smear campaign by Islamic Republic state media over comments in her acceptance speech dedicating the prize to the women of Iran . One TV station channel, aligned with the Basij, the paramilitary volunteer militia within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), accused Marzban of turning her back on Iran, while other Islamic Regime-backed channels have accused her of treason and suggested the Ministry of Culture should ban her from returning to Iran. The Iranian actress Marzban was feted for her performance in Mohsen Gharaei’s drama Falling House (Mogareb), revolving around three generations of women in an economically fragile family, living under the thumb of the prison guard father. Related Stories News Iranian Director Mohsen Gharaei Talks Navigating Censors To Bring Prophetic Drama ‘Falling House’ To Fruition – Venice News Venice Winner ‘Woman Unknown’ Unveils New Deals Including France In Wake Of Golden Lion Victory Marzban plays the lead female role of the oldest daughter who the father locks-up on discovering her plans to leave Iran to pursue dreams of becoming a model, appearing on screen both with and without a hijab. Watch on Deadline The film’s director Gharaei told Deadline prior its world premiere in Venice that he had written the first draft in 2018 but that the 2022 Woman Life Freedom protests had given him fresh impetus to get the production off the ground. Sparked by the death in police custody on September 16, 2022 of Mahsa Amini, following her arrest for not wearing her hijab correctly, the protests saw hundreds of thousands of Iranian women and men take to the streets in Iran to call for an end to the draconian Islamic Republic rules around female dress codes and conduct. At the Venice Film Festival awards ceremony on Saturday evening, a tearful Marzban acknowledged that Iran and its people were going through “the hardest days” and dedicated her award to all Iranian women. “I dedicate my award to the women of my country who have paid the highest price for the smallest freedoms,” she said. “These women today carry dreams, courage and hope, and I believe that one day the wish of all of us will come true.” Iranian actress Zhila Sadeghi, who is known for her affiliation with Republic of Iran’s state broadcaster (IRIB), attacked Marzban for not dedicating her speech rather to the children killed in a U.S. missile strike on an elementary school in Minab on the February 28. She said that Marzban had betrayed Iran, adding “curse the ones who let you have a role in a film ever again”. Marzban, whose credits include the 2023 Iranian Oscar submission The Night Guardian , has never been at odds with the Islamic Regime before. Marzban was asked by Deadline at the Venice Orizzonti winners press conference how she thought the film would be received in Iran given that it challenged the government and its patriarchal system. “This question is very important for me as an actress, and as all other women in Iran, whether they be doctors, artists, whatever profession women can perform, we can only make one step at the time, one step towards our objective,’ she said. “If we give our small contribution, maybe we will reach our objective. I have made my small part. I have given my contribution. I really hope many other people can make small steps towards our common objective.” TV Ratings, Review, Winners, Snubs & Surprises, Scorecards; More Casey Bloys Celebrates HBO’s 21 Emmy Wins, Gives Updates On 2027 Slate Trump’s DOJ Backs Company In Battle Over Antitrust Suit’s $1.88B Bond Robert De Niro In Talks To Play Tommy Lasorda In Skydance Sports’ ‘Tommy & Me’ Read More About: Comments

articles.title: House Lawmakers Launch Movies, Music, Entertainment & Sports Caucus
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted House Lawmakers Launch Movies, Music, Entertainment & Sports Caucus Donald Trump Says Kennedy Center Will Close Immediately And No Renovations Will Take Place Unless His Name Is Restored To Facade Film & TV Coalition Presses For Quick Action On Federal Incentive; Lawmakers Plan Announcement This Week, GOP Senator Said To Back Proposal View All September 16, 2026 5:00am Al Drago/Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: A group of House lawmakers is launching a new caucus focused on the economic and cultural impact of movies, music, entertainment and sports. The Movies, Music, Entertainment & Sports (MoMEntS) Caucus is being launched by Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA), whose district includes Culver City, and she will co-chair it along with Rep. María Elvira Salazar (R-FL) and Troy Carter (D-LA). Kamlager-Dove said in a statement, “America’s creative and entertainment sectors are economic powerhouses, generating more than $1 trillion each year and supporting over five million good-paying jobs. Yet for far too long, Congress has failed to give these industries and the workers and creators who power them the attention and support they deserve.” Related Stories Ratings '60 Minutes' Season Premiere Averages 7.94 Million Viewers, A Falloff From Last Year's Debut News Donald Trump Says Kennedy Center Will Close Immediately And No Renovations Will Take Place Unless His Name Is Restored To Facade The caucus comes amid an industry push for the establishment of a federal film and TV tax incentive as a way to address the flight of production to other countries. Watch on Deadline The caucus will have a broader focus than TV and film, and also include broadcasting; music; sports and live entertainment; fashion and beauty; gaming, esports, and interactive media; streaming and digital platforms; content creators and the influencer economy; literary and publishing; and visual and performing arts, organizers said. Salazar said in a statement that the caucus “will bring lawmakers and creative industries together to better understand the challenges they face, protect creative rights, and keep American talent and innovation leading on the world stage.” Carter said the caucus “provides a critical opportunity for us to prioritize America’s creative and entertainment industries, which contribute so much to our nation’s history, economy, and culture.” The caucus also will focus on innovation, competition, and responsible platform practices, among other aims. Other members of the caucus include Rep. Joe Wilson (R-SC), Rep. André Carson (D-IN), Rep. Gilbert R. Cisneros, Jr. (D-CA), Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-FL), and Rep. Ted W. Lieu (D-CA). Among those praising the formation of the caucus were Recording Academy President Harvey Mason Jr., TKO Group Chief Legal Officer Riché McKnight, TikTok USDS Joint Venture”s head of public policy Nicole Nason and Kathryn Busby, head of orginal programming at Starz. Congress also has a Creative Rights Caucus, focused on copyrights, First Amendment rights and intellectual property rights. It is co-chaired in the House by Rep. Judy Chu (D-CA) and Rep. Laurel Lee (R-FL), and in the Senate by Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC) and Sen. Mazie Hirono (D-HI). Rep. Laura Friedman (D-CA) and Rep. Brian Jack (R-GA) appeared on a press call on Tuesday to call for a federal film incentive, telling reporters that legislation is being drafted. President Donald Trump announced his support for a federal film incentive earlier this month. articles.title: HBO Max Unveils Medical Drama In France Following Success Of ‘The Pitt’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Hunting Gary Glitter’: Netflix Unveils Trailer & Launch Date For Doc About Race To Expose Serial Sex Abuser Bill Nighy Playing Socially-Challenged Literary Titan In Richard Curtis’ Debut Audio Sitcom Disney Seeking Next Big K-Pop Hit After Striking Ten-Project Deal With Kakao View All September 16, 2026 5:28am Noah Wyle, Sepideh Moafi HBOMAX Earlier this year, HBO Max content boss Sarah Aubrey told us her team wanted to replicate the success of Emmy-winner The Pitt around the world, and France appears to be one of the first destinations. Unveiled today at La Rochelle Fiction Festival, HBO Max is making Rush [working title], a medical drama set in Paris following a close-knit group of mobile medical teams. They race against time and their personal battles to save lives, bringing emergency medicine to street corners, metro carriages, private homes and iconic landmarks – where every call is a crisis, every decision has consequences, and every moment is a chance for human connection. Related Stories Books Everything We Know About Season 2 Of HBO's 'Harry Potter' TV Series So Far News 'Harry Potter' TV Series Due To Hit HBO Christmas 2026: Everything We Know About The Cast, Who's Creating It, What J.K. Rowling Says & More The show is created and written by Nils-Antoine Sambuc ( Belphégor , In Treatment FR, Soleil Noir ), and co-written by Gaëlle Bellan, Maya Haffar, and Maxime Crupeaux, with Neal Baer ( ER ) as EP. Watch on Deadline Rush has shades of The Pitt, which swept the Emmys on Monday night including another win for lead Noah Wyle and is preparing a third season. Aubrey told us in March that HBO Max was developing medical dramas in both France and Italy, with no word yet on the Italian one. “To me that’s the model to emulate: Take a genre and a set of characters audiences feel very familiar with and want in their homes every week, and overlay that with a creator who is really excited to tell a specific story authentically,” she said at Series Mania. “Then you get something special that is also popular.” HBO Max is also making Bodycam [working title] in France, a thriller/horror following two beat cops who shoot an unarmed teenager, wounding him. They decide to cover it up, but the teen has disappeared with one of their bodycams, which captured the incident. As they race to recover the incriminating footage, a string of strange attacks starts tearing through the local Police force until an officer goes missing. This one comes from Timothée Hochet ( Lost Media , Calls ) and Benjamin Adam ( Privilèges , L’Opéra ), with the collaboration of Mehdi Ouahab, and is co-written by Hélène Faure and Maxime Berthémy. At La Rochelle, Clémentine Bobin, Director of Original Scripted Production for HBO Max France, said: “Our slate of local series is built around a simple belief, stemming from the deep HBO legacy: the most compelling stories offer bold takes on familiar narratives and genres, take risks, champion strong voices, and offer a distinctive perspective on the world.” “Following the launch of French Original Privilèges and Paolo this year, Rush and Bodycam continue to build on that ambition. Both are driven by a strong creative vision, each embracing a familiar genre as a toolbox to tell unique, engaging and deeply contemporary stories.” Outside of the U.S., France is one of HBO Max’s most crucial territories and the team has been commissioning local fare for a number of years. articles.title: Country Music Association Sets Two-Hour Live Special In Tribute To Dolly Parton At ABC
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise Country Music Association Sets Two-Hour Live Special In Tribute To Dolly Parton At ABC Carol Kane, Fiona Gubelmann & Marco Grazzini To Headline ‘An Angel In My Stocking’ Movie At Hallmark Channel ‘The Diplomat’ Season 4 Trailer: Keri Russell Confronts “Over The Line” White House View All September 16, 2026 5:30am Dolly Parton Miller Mobley/NBC via Getty Images The Country Music Association will honor Dolly Parton with CMA Presents I Will Always Love You: A Celebration of Dolly Parton , a live two-hour special set to air Wednesday, Oct. 21 at 9 pm on ABC and Disney+ internationally, available next day on Hulu. Produced by CMA, the special will be filmed live at Belmont University’s Fisher Center for the Performing Arts in Nashville as part of a continuing strategic partnership between CMA and the university. As described by the CMA, “the special will be a joyful, emotional celebration of the artist, songwriter, entertainer, humanitarian and entrepreneur whose music and generosity carried her from the mountains of east Tennessee into the hearts of generations around the world, told through performances, archival footage and personal stories that trace her extraordinary journey to becoming one of the most beloved entertainers and philanthropists in American history.” Related Stories News Emmy TV Review: Host Mariska Hargitay Let Down By Skits, Script & Taylor Swift Cameo Way Below 'Law & Order: SVU' Star's Pay Grade News Reba McEntire & Sally Field Honor Dolly Parton At Emmys: "If There Are Truly Angels On Earth, We Have Just Lost One" Parton died following a brief battle with cancer on August 25. She was 80. Watch on Deadline Belmont University and Parton previously teamed on the 2025 world premiere of Dolly: A True Original Musical at the Fisher Center and the launch of Dolly U, an immersive educational partnership designed to connect students with hands-on opportunities in entertainment, media and creative industries. “Dolly Parton belonged to the whole world, but she was born of this industry, and this industry owes her a debt of gratitude that words alone cannot repay,” said Sarah Trahern, CMA CEO. “As the organization built to serve and celebrate Country Music, honoring her legacy is not just an opportunity, it is our responsibility. This special is our way of saying thank you, on behalf of every artist, industry member and fan who found a piece of themselves in her music.” Robert Deaton serves as the project’s executive producer. Dolly gave Country Music its heart, and giving some of that heart back to her is an incredible honor,” said Deaton. “My hope is simply that we do right by her story, her music and the people who love her, so that this evening feels like the tribute my friend deserves.” “Dolly Parton’s impact extends far beyond music, said Dr. Greg Jones, President of Belmont University. “She represents creativity, generosity, entrepreneurial spirit and a commitment to lifting others up, qualities that have inspired generations and resonate deeply with Belmont’s mission. It was an honor for Belmont to partner with Dolly through the launch of Dolly U and the world premiere of her musical at the Fisher Center. Now, it is a privilege to welcome artists, friends and fans from around the world to celebrate her extraordinary life and legacy from this stage in Nashville, honoring a woman whose love for Tennessee was woven into everything she did.” In conjunction with the special, CMA and Belmont University will make a donation from proceeds to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library , continuing a legacy that gives millions of children the gift of a free book each month. In addition, Disney is supporting Imagination Library to further its mission of inspiring children to imagine their possibilities. Additional details about the special, including performers, tickets and additional partners, will be announced in the coming weeks. articles.title: Patricio Guzmán Dies: Documentarian Who Chronicled Chile’s Turbulent Modern History Was 85
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Islamic Republic State Media Attacks Venice Prize-Winner Lelah Marzban Over Women’s Rights Speech The Coven Boards French Legalized Cannibalism Horror ‘Sunnyside’ As Filming Begins Venice Winner ‘Woman Unknown’ Unveils New Deals Including France In Wake Of Golden Lion Victory View All September 16, 2026 5:34am Patricio Guzman at the Berlin Film Festival in 2015 Andreas Rentz/Getty Images Chilean documentary-maker Patricio Guzmán, whose landmark documentaries included The Battle of Chile a nd Cannes prize-winner The Cordillera of Dreams, died in Paris on September 15. He was 85. Guzmán, who was born in the Chilean capital of Santiago on August 11, 1941, has been hailed as one of Latin America’s most important non-fiction directors. His landmark works include the three-part 1975-79 The Battle of Chile: The Struggle of an Unarmed People , chronicling the final year of socialist President Salvador Allende; the 1973 coup d’état which put General Augusto Pinochet in power, and resistance in the early days of the latter’s dictatorship. Related Stories News Jeremy Thomas Dies: Legendary UK Producer Of 'The Last Emperor' & 'Crash' Was 77 News Richard O'Sullivan Dies: British Sitcom Star Known For 'Man About The House' & 'Robin's Nest' Was 82 Guzmán left Chile in the 1960s to study Official Cinema School (Escuela Oficial de Cinematografía, or EOC) in Madrid. He returned home in 1971 where Allende’s government appointed him head of documentary at state cinema company Chile Films. He was chronicling the work of the socialist government when the coup broke out. Watch on Deadline The filmmaker left the country in the wake of the coup after being arrested and detained briefly. He settled in Madrid and then Paris, only returning to Chile sporadically to film, when the political situation permitted. Guzmán’s more recent credits include a trilogy reflecting on the legacy of his country’s 40-year military dictatorship: Nostalgia for the Light (2010), The Pearl Button (2015), which won Berlin’s Silver Bear for Best Screenplay, and The Cordillera of Dreams (2019), which won the Golden Eye documentary prize at the Cannes Film Festival. For his final documentary – the 2022 work My Imaginary Country – Guzmán explored his native country’s contemporary politics and the youth-led popular protests that erupted in Chile in 2019 around democracy and social equality. Sheindlin – Judge Judy to millions – announced this morning that she is retiring “from in front of the camera” after 30 years of passing judgements that were often caustic, usually funny and always final. Appearing on ABC’s Good Morning America today with her son Adam Levy, lawyer and now presiding judge of TV’s new Adam’s Law show, Sheindlin said she is stepping away from her own show to focus on behind-the-scenes work including her position as executive producer of her son’s program. “I’m retiring from in front of the camera,” Sheindlin said. Asked by GMA hosts Lara Spencer and Sam Champion why now, Sheindlin said, “First of all, he was ready,” referring to her son. Related Stories News 'Judge Judy' Celebrates 30th Anniversary In CBS Primetime Special With Steven Spielberg, Samuel L. Jackson & More News 'Drew Barrymore Show', Judy Sheindlin's New 'Adam's Law', 'Hot Bench' & More Get Fall Premiere Dates “And, you know,” she continued, “I’ve aged pretty well over the years, reasonably – I look better than my grandmother did at my age, which didn’t take a lot – but it’s time for me to…take the message and put it in a little bit of a different form.” Watch on Deadline Sheindlin emphasized that she wasn’t retiring completely and would remain active in an off-screen manner. Levy’s program Adam’s Law was created by Sheindlin and premiered September 14 in national syndication through CBS Media Ventures. Sheindlin’s original program, Judge Judy , premiered in 1996 and stopped filming new episodes in 2021 (though reruns remain in syndication and on streaming networks such as Pluto TV.) Her follow-up series, the Amazon Prime spinoff Judy Justice , is expected to air its final episode on October 22, according to The New York Times. A 90-minute 30-year anniversary special, Judge Judy: Unfiltered, Unforgettable , will air on Tuesday, September 22 (8-9:30 p.m. ET/PT) on CBS and stream live on Paramount+ (Premium) and next day. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Judge Judy Retiring From TV Screen After 30 Years ‘Spring Awakening’ Revival Sets Principal Cast Including ‘John Proctor Is The Villain’s Amalia Yoo Rosie O’Donnell To Join Broadway’s ‘Rocky Horror Show’ As Temporary Fill-In For Rachel Dratch View All September 16, 2026 6:55am Christiani Pitts and Sam Tutty in 'Two Strangers (Carry A Cake Across New York)' Matthew Murphy Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) , the modest, two-person musical that charmed critics last season and scored eight Tony Award nominations, will play its final performance on Sunday, November 29. At the time of its closing, Two Strangers will have played 21 previews and 428 performances at the Longacre Theatre. The First National Tour of the show will launch in Providence, RI., with an expected start date in fall of 2027. Written and composed by Jim Barne and Kit Buchan, and directed and choreographed by Tim Jackson, Two Strangers stars Sam Tutty and Christiani Pitts (both Tony noninated) as two young strangers who meet when he is visiting New York (from England) for the wedding of a father he never met. Pitts plays the bride’s sister, and in opposites attract style the two bond, sometimes reluctantly, as they carry out the wedding task described in the title. Related Stories News Rosie O'Donnell To Join Broadway's 'Rocky Horror Show' As Temporary Fill-In For Rachel Dratch News 'Chicago' Sells Out With Arrival Of Ex-Cowboys Cheerleader Reece Weaver - Broadway Box Office While the musical received favorable reviews and solid word of mouth, it did not become a major hit at the box office. In recent weeks attendance at the show was typically on the lower end of the Broadway grosses roster: Last week, attendance was at 70% of capacity at the Longacre, with a middling gross of $519,236.
