articles.title: Filmmaker Tatiana Huezo Named Guest Of Honor For 39th Edition Of International Documentary Festival Amsterdam
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News ‘Widow’s Bay’ & ‘The Pitt’ Take Top Series Emmys As Matthew Rhys & Jean Smart Make History: Full Winners List Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Filmmaker Tatiana Huezo Named Guest Of Honor For 39th Edition Of International Documentary Festival Amsterdam Bleecker Street Moves Up ‘Musk’ Doc Theatrical Release Due To Overwhelming Demand ‘My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile’ Trailer: Brave Russian Women Journalists Flee Tyranny In Film From Julia Loktev, EPs Meryl Streep, Laura Poitras View All September 15, 2026 6:00am Filmmaker Tatiana Huezo Courtesy of IDFA IDFA , the world’s largest documentary film festival, has named filmmaker Tatiana Huezo as its 2026 guest of honor, a distinction that puts the Salvadoran Mexican director in the company of previous honorees Laura Poitras, Johan Grimonprez, Wang Bing, and 2025 guest of honor Susana de Sousa Dias . Huezo’s films include The Tiniest Place (2011), The Echo (2023), and her fiction debut, Prayers for the Stolen (2021). IDFA will present a complete retrospective of her work, including several short films and as part of the honor, Huezo will curate a personal Top 10 film selection, “taking her interest in cinematography as a starting point to explore how the camera shapes our perception of reality.” An extended conversation with Huezo will be the centerpiece Talk of the 2026 edition of IDFA. Related Stories News Oscar Documentary Contender 'House Of Hope' Secures North American Distribution News Fondazione Prada Film Fund Unveils First Grants: Tatiana Huezo, Apichatpong Weerasethakul & Levan Akin Among First Recipients “Born in El Salvador and raised in Mexico, Huezo has developed a distinctive body of work that moves between documentary and fiction, exploring how the violent consequences of organized crime and political turmoil shape the intimate lives of local families and communities,” IDFA writes in a release. “Her cinema is rooted in close observation and shaped by a highly attentive visual and sonic language—allowing memories and experience to surface through atmosphere and deeply personal stories.” Watch on Deadline ‘Once Upon a Time in Harlem’: Sitting (L-R) Thomas Harvey, William Patterson, John Henrik Clarke, Mrs. J.B. Matthews and Louise Patterson; Standing (L-R)): Ernest Chrichlow, Romare Bearden and Ida Mae Cullen Neon/Greaves Productions On Tuesday, IDFA also announced its 2026 Spotlight will focus on William Greaves, the late American filmmaker who deployed “sharp observation of social and political life” to explore Black history and culture. Earlier this year, the Sundance Film Festival premiered Once Upon a Time in Harlem , a documentary project conceived and filmed by William Greaves in 1972 that was completed more than 50 years later by his son, David Greaves, and granddaughter Liani Greaves. As part of the Spotlight program, IDFA will screen Once Upon a Time in Harlem , and the “cult classic Symbiopsychotaxiplasm: Take One (1971) [where William Greaves] turns a fiction shoot in Central Park into a self-reflexive study of a film crew in revolt.” Also on the bill is The Fight [The William Greaves Director’s Cut] (1973), which captures “the charged atmosphere surrounding the Joe Frazier–Muhammad Ali championship bout.” The 39 th edition of IDFA takes place in Amsterdam from Nov. 12-22, under the artistic direction of Isabel Arrate Fernández . The festival also shared details on the 20 th edition of IDFA DocLab, as well as its Dead Angle program. “ Dead Angle is IDFA’s multi-year focus program that uses documentary cinema to reveal what remains outside our direct field of vision,” the festival writes. “Following Borders (2024) and Institutions (2025), the program closes with the theme Common Ground, exploring the many ways people come together—from extraordinary acts of solidarity and collective resistance to the everyday life of communities and quintessential function of public space. “Several confirmed titles explore solidarity in times of crisis. Shinsuke Ogawa’s landmark film The Battle Front for the Liberation of Japan – Summer in Sanrizuka (1968) documents farmers and student protestors banding together to resist the expansion of Tokyo’s Narita Airport. “Barbara Kopple’s Oscar-winning American Dream (1990) poignantly portrays the unequal struggle between labor and capital in a prolonged strike in a meat packing plant in Minnesota. “Elsewhere, the program highlights everyday forms of connection. The Warsaw sidewalk becomes the stage in Paweł Łoziński’s The Balcony Movie , where his filming of casual encounters with passersby from his balcony becomes an intimate portrait of neighborhood and community. José Luis Guerín’s Work in Progress (2001) shows how gentrification not only reshapes a bustling Barcelona neighbourhood, but fractures the histories and relationships embedded in them. Everybody to Kenmure Street (2026) by Felipe Bustos Sierra captures a captivating account of collective resistance, when hundreds of Glasgow residents protested and prevented the deportation of two of their neighbors.” IDFA notes, “Together, the [Dead Angle] program invites audiences to reflect on the act of finding common ground—a gesture of humanity and hope in dark times.” The full selection will be confirmed on October 13. IDFA DocLab: Shared Realities Celebrating its 20th edition, IDFA DocLab looks back on two decades of pioneering interactive and immersive documentary art, “while decisively turning toward the next 20 years. What began as an experiment in 2007, has grown into a leading platform for the exploration of where digital art and critical reflection on technology meet. Presented under the theme Shared Realities, the anniversary program reflects on DocLab’s history and traces plans to resurface formative archival works, while venturing forward to ask: which realities do we want to experience together in the future? “The theme echoes this year’s launch of a new, eponymous international consortium, Shared Realities, that brings together artists, researchers, academic partners, venues, and cultural organizations to investigate new ways of creating, presenting, and sustaining immersive art. IDFA DocLab returns with an exhibition in de Brakke Grond, ARTIS-Planetarium, Droog, and Tobacco Theatre, with a diverse lineup of interdisciplinary immersive art and anniversary highlights to be revealed in the coming weeks.” The full IDFA DocLab selection will be announced in October. articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News ‘Widow’s Bay’ & ‘The Pitt’ Take Top Series Emmys As Matthew Rhys & Jean Smart Make History: Full Winners List Read the full story By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Jeremy Thomas Tributes: Figures From Across The Industry Remember Legendary UK Producer Of ‘The Last Emperor’ & ‘Crash’ Former Israeli Prime Minister Takes Aim At Yuval Abraham And Rachel Szor’s ‘NAZA’ Justin Trudeau Launching Production Company At TIFF View All September 15, 2026 6:11am Jim Caviezel in Dark Horse Go Up Entertainment Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the leading opposition candidate in Brazil’s upcoming presidential election, is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering tied to the financing of a film about his father, the country’s disgraced former President Jair Bolsonaro . A Brazilian Supreme Court judge unsealed court documents related to the case late last week. The documents revealed that the investigation was opened in July 2026. Justice Flávio Dino, a Jair Bolsonaro appointee, said in his ruling that there was a credible hypothesis that a sophisticated scheme was executed by the involved parties to divert funds from the public purse to pay for the production of Dark Horse . Local police have seized documents from the film’s production company and Mário Frias, who served as Brazil’s Secretary of Culture under Jair Bolsonaro, according to AP, which first reported the story. Frias is accused of sending around 2 million reais ($400,000) to a nonprofit linked to the film. The judge said last week that there are strong allegations that Frias played a central role within the alleged criminal network. Frias has denied all wrongdoing. Related Stories News Director Of Jair Bolsonaro Biopic Starring Jim Caviezel Says Film Is About "Power, Media, And Faith Under Fire" Casting Biopic Of Jair Bolsonaro In Works Starring Jim Caviezel As Incarcerated Ex-Brazilian President “I never allocated any congressional budget funds to finance or benefit the production of the film in any way,” Frias said Sunday in a statement. Watch on Deadline Flávio Bolsonaro has also denied any wrongdoing. “It is very positive that the documents are unsealed,” he told journalists at an event. “I want transparency in everything. I will only confirm what I always said. There’s nothing wrong about the movie.” Jair Bolsonaro was Brazilian president between 2019 and 2023. The so-called “Trump of the tropics” is currently serving a 27-year prison sentence for leading a criminal conspiracy to stop his rival, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, from taking power. Dark Horse stars American actor Jim Caviezel and tells Jair Bolsonaro’s life story. Co-starring opposite Caviezel in Dark Horse are Esai Morales, Lynn Collins, Camille Guaty, and Jeffrey Vincent Parise. Producers are Karina Ferreira and Michael Davis for Go Up Entertainment, and Ryan O’Quinn. The film’s screenplay was written by Mark Nowrasteh and Cyrus Nowrasteh from a story by Frias. Deadline has reached out to the production for comment. articles.title: ‘Annie’ Sets 2027 Broadway Return With ‘Oh, Mary!’ Director Sam Pinkleton
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News ‘Widow’s Bay’ & ‘The Pitt’ Take Top Series Emmys As Matthew Rhys & Jean Smart Make History: Full Winners List Read the full story By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Mariska Hargitay Opens The Emmys With Help From Jalen Brunson, Jean Smart & A Nicole Kidman Commercial Andrew Scott To Star In Film Version Of Simon Stephens Stage Play ‘Sea Wall’ Gary Myers Dies: NASCAR Driver, Patriarch Of Racing Family Was 76 View All September 15, 2026 6:25am Sam Pinkleton with vintage 'Annie' signage Cue all the “sun will come out” references: Annie , the beloved Tony-winning musical that gave us the song “Tomorrow” and provided generations of child actors the chance to play plucky orphans, will return to Broadway in a 2027 50th Anniversary production to be directed by Oh, Mary! ‘s Sam Pinkleton . The production is planned for fall 2027, say producers Michael Alden and Hal Luftig, Cathy Dantchik, & Kevin Connor for Halcyon Theatricals. Casting and a production timeline for the revival will be announced later. “If you ask any of my closest friends what I love more than anything on the planet, everyone will have the same answer: Annie ,” said Pinkleton, who also directed the current hit revival The Rocky Horror Show . “ Annie is everything I love about New York City: gutsy, fearless, and funny as hell. It’s a perfectly constructed musical comedy that my collaborators and I will run toward with joy and abandon – with open hearts and total adoration for this legendary show that has made generations fall in love with musicals.” Related Stories Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More News 'Oh, Mary!' Live Capture Starring Cole Escola To Debut On HBO & HBO Max In 2027 Annie , featuring music by Charles Strouse, lyrics by Martin Charnin, and a book by Thomas Meehan, premiered at the Goodspeed Opera House in 1976 before a pre-Broadway engagement at the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C. The musical opened on Broadway at the Alvin Theatre (now the Neil Simon Theatre) on April 21, 1977. Watch on Deadline In addition to “Tomorrow,” with its famous opening line “The sun’ll come out tomorrow,” the musical included such songs as “It’s the Hard-Knock Life” and “Easy Street.” In its original run, Annie was nominated for 11 Tony Awards, winning seven, including Best Musical, Best Original Score, Best Book of a Musical, Best Actress in a Musical (Dorothy Loudon), Best Choreography, Best Scenic Design, and Best Costume Design. The show made a star of young Andrea McArdle, who originated the title role, and would provide early career opportunities for any number of fledgling performers including Sarah Jessica Parker. In a joint statement, the producers said, “Half a century after a fearless redheaded orphan first walked onto a Broadway stage and sang that the sun would come out tomorrow, that promise continues to inspire audiences around the world, and will do so again.” The families of the musical’s creators also weighed in on the new production. “Fifty years ago, our father, Martin Charnin, had an idea: that a little redheaded girl who refused to give up might have something to say to the world,” said the Charnin family. “Today, we believe the true measure of a legacy is carrying it forward – so the work continues to inspire new generations. Randy and Sasha Charnin are deeply honored to help bring Annie home to Broadway, where she can once again share her timeless message of hope, joy, and optimism. Annie was never about yesterday. It was always about tomorrow.” The family of Thomas Meehan, the Tony Award-winning book writer, said, “ Annie is performed somewhere in the world virtually every moment of every day—from elementary-school auditoriums to regional theaters and major international stages. But Broadway will always be home. Annie is, at its core, a New York story: spirited, tough, funny and full of possibility. This isn’t a revival; it’s a homecoming.” The family of Charles Strouse, the Tony Award-winning composer and creator of the musical score, said, “We take enormous pride in the place Annie’s music has earned in the hearts of generations. These songs have become so familiar that it is easy to forget how much power they still hold—and how much joy they still inspire. We cannot wait to hear this extraordinary score ringing out on Broadway once again.” Emmy Analysis & Scorecards: Apple & ‘Widow’s Bay’ Break Records & Lead Night Sets Emmy Records With Comedy & Drama Acting Wins In Same Night Emmy Review: Mariska Hargitay Let Down By Bits Below Her ‘L&O: SVU’ Pay Grade Gallery Of The Best Looks From The 78th Primetime Emmys Read More About: 1 Comments

EXCLUSIVE: Cameron Cowperthwaite ( Fallout ) and Patricia De Leon ( The Cleaning Lady ) have completed production on Charred Remains of Heaven , an independent feature fully financed by the estate of former UCLA Film School Dean Robert “Bob” Rosen. Sundance alum Christopher Bradley ( Billy’s Hollywood Screen Kiss ) wrote and directed the film, and lead creative producer Michael J. Shoel of Ariztical Entertainment ( Eating Out franchise) packaged it. Veteran casting directors Michael Testa and Lisa Ystrom cast the film. The wider ensemble also includes Robert Pine ( CHiPS ), Mark Povinelli ( GOAT ), and Jeffrey Vincent Parise ( The Rookie ). Related Stories News Hammond Emmys Analysis: A Record Setting Night As The Once Repetitive Academy Proves They Like To Shake Things Up Cancellations and Renewals 'Slow Horses' Renewed For Season 8 At Apple TV The film’s narrative is said to blend paranormal horror and magical realism amid a high-stakes military takeover of Los Angeles. Watch on Deadline “What makes this project so compelling is its chilling, quiet exploration of institutional trauma,” Shoel said. “Much like The Handmaid’s Tale , the story uses a heightened alternative world to examine how easily authoritarianism can seep into ordinary civilian life.” Rosen was the longtime Dean of the UCLA School of Theater, Film and Television. He passed away in 2024, at the age of 84. He also co-founded Outfest and was co-creator of the Sundance Collection at UCLA. In 2008, Rosen received The Film Foundation’s John Huston Award from Martin Scorsese at the DGA Honors. Bradley, who shared a lifelong friendship with Rosen after meeting through UCLA’s MFA film program, shot the film on Rosen’s 4,000-square-foot Sunset Boulevard-style mansion before its sale this fall. One hundred percent of the proceeds from the sale will be permanently endowed as an ongoing grant to provide critical housing support for UCLA film preservation students. “Bob Rosen spent his life building the foundations of the independent film community. To shepherd a project that serves as his final legacy and directly funds the future of UCLA filmmakers is an immense honor,” Shoel said. Bradley added: “To bring this specific vision to life under the banner of Bob’s final wish, and to do so inside the very walls he lived in, makes this a deeply meaningful and creative milestone for everyone involved.” Emmy Analysis & Scorecards: Apple & ‘Widow’s Bay’ Break Records & Lead Night Sets Emmy Records With Comedy & Drama Acting Wins In Same Night Emmy Review: Mariska Hargitay Let Down By Bits Below Her ‘L&O: SVU’ Pay Grade Gallery Of The Best Looks From The 78th Primetime Emmys Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Hammond Emmys Analysis: A Record Setting Night As The Once Repetitive Academy Proves They Like To Shake Things Up
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News ‘Widow’s Bay’ & ‘The Pitt’ Take Top Series Emmys As Matthew Rhys & Jean Smart Make History: Full Winners List Read the full story By Pete Hammond Pete Hammond Awards Columnist/Chief Film Critic @DeadlinePete More Stories By Pete Emmys: What You Didn’t See On TV; Tom Holland, Zendaya, Charlie Hunnam, Nicole Kidman & More Toronto Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline’s Reviews ‘The Life And Deaths Of Wilson Shedd’ Review: Amanda Seyfried’s Complex Portrayal Enriches Tim Blake Nelson’s Downbeat Prison Picture – Toronto Film Festival View All September 15, 2026 7:00am Widow's Bay at the 78th Emmy Awards PMC The simple way to sum up Monday night’s Emmy Awards is, as we’ve seen in the past few years, there may be 24,000+ voters in the Television Academy membership but they only watch a handful of shows, and that membership has grown increasingly fickle as the Emmys near 80. To paraphrase a famous Oscar acceptance speech of Sally Field ‘s (who won her fourth Emmy last night) ‘if they like you, they really really like you’. It seems like we are writing the same headlines year after year as Emmy keeps breaking its own records. In 2023 The Bear broke the record for most wins for a comedy series with 10. The following year winning 11 it broke its own record even without winning again for Best Comedy Series. That went to Hacks winning its first and only Best Comedy Series Emmy. But the record setting achievement of The Bear was eclipsed the very next year in 2025 when The Studio took home 12 wins setting another new record for a Comedy Series, but it didn’t last long for Apple to crow about that one, since last night yet another freshman Apple series, Widow’s Bay set a new Comedy Series record with 13 wins as it was anointed the new Comedy champ based on just its first seven episodes that didn’t even debut until near the end of the season on April 29. Related Stories News Apple Takes Victory Lap After Emmy Bonanza: "You Can't Predict These Things" News Chuck Norris, 'Buffy The Vampire Slayer's Nicholas Brendon Among Those Skipped By Emmys In Memoriam Stephen Root, Matthew Rhys and Kate O’Flynn in ‘Widow’s Bay’ Apple TV The debut was so late that the final three episodes of the series weren’t even eligible for this season’s May 31 eligibility cutoff, but the show clearly and quickly found a loyal audience in the industry and was front of mind when ballots were being filled out. Ironically with 13 wins (including 4 for actors) out of 19 nominations, that nomination total was behind early front runner Hacks which itself broke the record of 24 noms in its fifth and final season, beating by one the shared record holders of 23 for The Bear and The Studio (it only cashed in with two wins for Editing and Jean Smart’s personal record run). Watch on Deadline So voters absolutely have been showing they really like to honor shiny new toys in the comedy categories and are willing to go to the wall and just check off one for everything. In recent years this has been a definite trend. Gone are the days of the same old-same old when Frasier, Modern Family, Veep would win repeatedly. Since 2018 only Ted Lasso (yet another Apple show) managed even a back to back win (for its first two seasons in the category in 2021 and 2022). Otherwise that has not been the rule anymore, as it has been a succession of newbies not previously registering in the Emmy comedy series races from The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel (2018); Fleabag ‘s second season (2019); Schitt’s Creek’s sixth season (2020); The Bear’s first season (2023); Hacks third season (2024); The Studio’s first season (2025); and now in 2026 Widow’s Bay’s first season, well most of it. Voters discover something or finally discover something, instantly smother it with statuettes, and then move on. This is not your father’s predictable Emmys anymore, at least in this category. Rhea Seehorn and Vince Gilligan attend the Governor’s Gala during the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards at Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Emma McIntyre/GA/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images) The staleness of seeing the same shows awarded year after year is definitely wearing off. Yes, The Pitt won in Drama Series for its second consecutive year but it still feels like fresh blood (sorry), and voters made room for other new drama series in awarding Emmys to Vince Gilligan and Rhea Seehorn for Pluribus ( six overall for the first season show); Tom Pelphrey in Task; Allison Janney gaining The Diplomat’s first ever Emmy; and, slowly but surely, the sublime Slow Horses for directing. In the Limited Series/Anthology category many were expecting front runner Beef, which was returning to category with an all new season, to win on name value and comfort alone but, after dominating in its first go-round in 2023, voters apparently felt a bit of ‘been there, done that’ and awarded seven Emmys to quirkily original DTS St Louis, again indicating they are looking for something fresh and different. They like to discover things, even at the last minute like Widow’s Bay, or in the second season of Fleabag or sixth season of Schitt’s Creek after previously not even acknowledging those shows even existed. ‘DTF St. Louis’ HBO Max This lively Emmy ceremony (nicely hosted by Mariska Hargitay who had some very amusing bits), which from my vantage point in the Peacock Theatre, actually had some other pleasing fresh moments revealed when the envelopes were opened. None was better than the unexpected win from the aforementioned Sally Field, so great at 79 in Remarkably Bright Creatures to become the oldest winner ever in a Limited Series/ Television Movie category that hasn’t awarded a single television movie performance over limited series turns since Julianne Moore in Game Change 14 years ago. “This wasn’t supposed to happen,” the veteran star now in her 62nd year in the business said of the predicton markets. But it did. The Academy can bring in new blood, but its nice to know we still can recognize a truly worthy legend every now and then. Sally Field at the 2026 Emmys Photo by Kevin Winter/Getty Images The Traitors, an exception to the new rule, won Best Reality Series for the third year in a row cementing itself as the kind of perennial winner in the category Ru Paul’s Drag Race and The Amazing Race used to dominate year after year. It looks like voters in this category do like the same old same old. That would be true in the ever-changing Variety Series category as well except Late Show With Stephen Colbert won its second consecutive Emmy ever shaking up a category that had mostly been won this century by either Last Week Tonight With John Oliver or The Daily Show . Of course to do it Colbert had to go and get canceled. Next year it probably goes back to Oliver or Daily Show. But the trend is clear, Emmy voters (yes I am one of them) may indeed be only watching a handful of shows, maybe overwhelmed by all the content, but when they happen on to one they want to see like Widow’s Bay apparently there is no record that can’t be reset. articles.title: Tom Cruise Pokes Fun At His Self-Serious Persona In Rare Feature Interview: “I Don’t Know What To Say. I Am Intense”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News ‘Widow’s Bay’ & ‘The Pitt’ Take Top Series Emmys As Matthew Rhys & Jean Smart Make History: Full Winners List Read the full story By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Jeremy Thomas Tributes: Figures From Across The Industry Remember Legendary UK Producer Of ‘The Last Emperor’ & ‘Crash’ Former Israeli Prime Minister Takes Aim At Yuval Abraham And Rachel Szor’s ‘NAZA’ Justin Trudeau Launching Production Company At TIFF View All September 15, 2026 7:05am Tom Cruise Gabe Ginsberg/Getty Images “I don’t know what to say. I am intense,” Tom Cruise concluded in a rare sit-down video interview published today by GQ Magazine . The veteran actor was speaking with the magazine as he gears up for the release of Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Digger next month. During the conversation, Cruise was asked about the lessons he learned early in his career as an actor. “I had to learn early. I was living in many different schools, and it taught me about human behavior, about life, but it’s a journey. So movies are—this is about humanity,” Cruise told the magazine . Related Stories Trailers New 'Digger' Trailer Reveals More Of Tom Cruise's Crusty Oil Baron, A Role That Took The Actor 40 Years To Prepare News Tom Cruise Backs Paramount's 30-Movies-A-Year Promise In WBD Merger: "I Think It's Awesome" “I have nothing against cable or TV or Netflix. I think it’s great. Create jobs and everything. But what I like about cinema is it is all of us coming together in a room and sharing an experience. I say, ‘Understand the tools, then go create what you want to create.’ When I’m working with people, I’m not afraid to, as I’m acting, look foolish to do it. It’s like: That’s not what this is about. It’s finding our tone, finding these tools together and having an experience.” Watch on Deadline Cruise added: “And look, I work hard, and people that work with me, they know. I expect a lot, and I’m up-front about it. It’s like: The rumors are true. And do you want this?’” Cruise was asked if that is truly his pitch to potential collaborators, to which he responded: “Yes.” “We’re there. I’m like, ‘Trust me, the rumors are true. I’ll be here before you. What experience do you want?’ And I’m very open. It’s not like we don’t have a plan. We have scripts, we have plans, we’re going through it,” he said. “But I also feel that level of responsibility for—I guess, for everyone. Even when I was a kid, they were like, Oh, come on, Tom. You’re so intense. I’m like, I don’t know what to say. I am intense. I got a very good sense of humor about it, but it was like: When I’m interested in something, I want to learn it. I want to understand it. And you want to blast through the confusion and kind of build up that ability.” Warner Bros. will release Digger in cinemas worldwide on October 2. The film stars Cruise as an oil baron named Digger Rockwell who is charged with saving the day to avert an environmental catastrophe that he caused in the first place. Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg and Jesse Plemons also star. articles.title: WME’s Sleek New Headquarters Give Agents Every Reason to Come to the Office (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Oren Peleg Plus Icon Oren Peleg View All September 14, 2026 6:30am The lobby of WME’s new Beverly Hills headquarters as realized by the interior design firm Gensler. Eric Laignel Photography Richard Weitz, co-chairman of the WME group, is standing in the lobby of the agency’s new Beverly Hills headquarters on a recent afternoon. The space suddenly swells with agents, assistants, clients and others shuffling through for lunch. Some people split off to sit for a meal at 1898 — the plush new lobby restaurant operated by Wolfgang Puck that has taken over for Jack & Ben’s — while others grab something light from the café and huddle inside the many wood-and-velvet booths taking up the center of the lobby, creating what is effectively the office’s new town square. Weitz watches as people come together to eat, chat and even just throw a quick “hey, nice to see you.” He believes work-from-home arrangements aren’t suited to WME’s business. Representation always has been about relationships, he says. Hollywood, in other words, is an in-person job. “Even though the industry is changing, there are two things you can’t replace: community and collaboration,” explains Weitz. So when he and Christian Muirhead became co-chairmen of the storied agency in 2022, they made it a priority to renovate the headquarters to foster more face-to-face interaction. They asked global design firm Gensler to reimagine WME’s aging offices along Camden Drive, which hadn’t had a refresh in more than two decades. “WME had been in this building for such a long time, and every time some other tenant moved out, they took over the space,” explains Brian Barry, Gensler’s design director, who led the renovation. As a result, the agency’s 10 floors were a Frankensteined amalgamation of styles flattened out by white paint and a vague Y2K futurism aesthetic: “It was all kind of cohesive, but not really.” Eric Laignel Photography Eric Laignel Photography Over four years, Barry transformed the headquarters by replacing the sterility of the white paint with layers of organic materials (rich woods, brass, leather) and designing smaller, human-centric spaces where agents and clients could meet. A large, state-of-the-art listening lounge was built on the seventh floor so musicians could play new work for their team in a comfortable, modern setting. On the ground floor, the Chaplin Theater provides a similar experience for such WME filmmaker clients as Christopher Nolan, Ryan Coogler and Maggie Gyllenhaal. “We wanted every creative environment in the building to support the work at the highest level,” says Weitz. Adds Muirhead: “We spend our days working with people who obsess over every detail of their craft. It only felt right to create spaces that meet that same standard.” Across the office floors, emphasis was placed on functionality. “The agents and their assistants have a very unique, very direct relationship,” says Barry. “So we created a sort of town hall on every floor with conference rooms and the improved pantries as a central destination.” Eric Laignel Photography The main design elements for these office spaces are the nearly 400 artworks hand-selected and supplied by Creative Arts Partners, whom WME had discovered after they supplied the artwork for Kevin Hart’s offices at HartBeat. “Our goal was, how do we put together a collection as creative as the amazing talent that WME represents?” explains Brian Ludlow, co-founder and CEO of Creative Arts Partners. The result is a beautiful array of original paintings, photography and even sculptural works that pepper the offices with names like Petra Cortright and Spencer Lewis. It’s been years of disruption and change for WME, from the pandemic to the WGA and SAG strikes and the four-year construction of the office itself. Now, Weitz says he’s excited to have everyone back in the new office. Eric Laignel Photography This story appeared in the Sept. 9 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

articles.title: Six Years After Starring Father Died Soon After TIFF Short Premiere, ‘Strong Son’ Director Returns With Grief Drama
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All September 14, 2026 6:45am Mandeep-Sodhi, Amrit-Parbhakar in Strong Son Markus Henkel Director Ian Bawa’s debut feature, Strong Son, explores the irony of a South Asian bodybuilder bulking up at a local gym just as his mental health goes downhill, and all while he cares at home for his strong-willed elderly father who is seeing his own physical health markedly weaken. And much as the movie’s main character, Harvey Singh, played by Mandeep Sodhi, becomes emotionally broken due to his father’s outdated idea about how a real man must act – hide your emotions, don’t appear powerless and get married – Bawa himself has pushed the limits of his own storytelling vulnerability as a director to capture his real-life grief over the loss of both his parents. Related Stories Movies 'Seventeen' Director Justin Ducharme Talks Portraying Struggling Sex Workers as BFFs in Gritty Vancouver Movies Zack Snyder's 'The Last Photograph': First Reactions “The feature itself is as truthful as a narrative and a personal narrative, without being a documentary,” Bawa tells The Hollywood Reporter ahead of a world premiere for Strong Son at the Toronto Film Festival. His feature, in fact, expands on a 2020 short film, also called Strong Son , that featured Bawa’s real-life father, Jagdeep Singh Bawa, as a South Asian father giving advice to his son as he trains at a local gym, with the mantra, “My son is very strong.” That 3-minute film, shot on Super 8, world premiered at TIFF during a pandemic-era festival online, and with Bawa, buoyed by his festival success and his father at his side, already having a feature adaptation in mind. But only three weeks later, after the first look in Toronto, Bawa’s father died from a sudden heart attack. And that shock death followed his mother, Pritam Bawa, passing away in 2007 after a battle with breast cancer and 36 years of marriage. “All of a sudden, my life blew up in the other way, where it was embarrassing, this movie, because it felt like people were pitying me and in my head I was dealing with grief rather than working on the feature,” Bawa recalled. The Winnipeg-based filmmakers explored his grief in another 2024 short film, My Son Went Quiet and other short films. But his first feature, Strong Son , captures the strained relationship between Harvey and his father after moving back into the family home, only to battle severe panic attacks and crying fits as he feels the strain of being a parental caregiver. And Harvey faces his overbearing father’s disappointment most glaringly with the public humiliation of an emotional breakdown while taking part in an amateur wrestling match the bodybuilder entered to prove his physical strength. Bawa says most every scene in Strong Son , and much of the dialogue, was taken directly from his personal experience caring for his father over the 10 years before his death, as the feature thematically explores toxic masculinity in South Asian culture. “Those words were spoken to me, as my Dad told me to stop crying, you’re acting like a woman, you’re acting like your mother. It’s one of the weird trauma moments that sit with you,” he explains. Another source material is the original emergency phone call Bawa in real life made to paramedics on discovering his father in heart arrest, which is recreated in Strong Son the feature. “It’s all real, from the true 911 call. I have this stuff, what else am I going to do with it? And it’s his legacy at this point – no one’s going to remember my Dad, except me,” he explains. At the same time, the sparse filmmaking style behind Strong Son — which combines stationary shots in quiet moments between Harvey and his father at home, with action-driven scenes set in the local gym – springs in part from the lead Sodhi being a bodybuilder-turned-actor since leaving India for Canada in 2011. And Amrit Parbhakar as Jagdeep Singh only came on board for his first film lead role just one week before Bawa started production on the low-budget indie, and after an earlier actor set to play Harvey’s father dropped out. Another hurdle was Parbhakar having gone blind two years before Strong Son was shot, which called for improvisation between director and lead actor on set during rehearsals and faking an eye line when the camera, handled by cinematographer and producer Markus Henkel, rolled. “We shot backwards. We’d start with close-ups of everyone, then do his (Parbhakar) last,” as a third assistant helped him learn lines phonetically as in effect his personal assistant. Another irony about Bawa as a filmmaker as his personal story is now ready for the world to see coming out of TIFF is he claims to be useless at talking about his inner feelings and emotions to his therapist. “I’m an extrovert. I do like to talk, but I’m really bad at therapy,” he insists. Bawa hopes his feature, as it explores family grief and intergenerational connection, does resonate with audiences. As for what’s next for the Canadian filmmaker after his debut feature premieres in Toronto, Bawa has a couple of scripts on the go, including a horror pic. The other is a dark comedy about a South Asian man who is balding and has wrinkles as he ages, and so decides to kidnap his illegitimate son to take him to Mexico for a skin and hair transplant. “Whatever the next one is, it has to be extremely different. Because that’s my rule in life. You have to pivot and try new things. Otherwise, what am I doing? I’m not going to learn anything,” Bawa says. THR

articles.title: The 37 Top L.A. Real Estate Brokers of 2026
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Hadley Meares Plus Icon Hadley Meares Contributor hadleymeares Follow Sign Up View All September 14, 2026 7:00am $47M 410 Trousdale Place, in Beverly Hills, listed by Aaron Kirman of Christie’s. Mike Kelley Amid wildfires and global uncertainty, L.A.’s top real estate agents honored on THR ‘s annual Power Brokers list have been facing strong headwinds. “It is definitely a buyer’s market right now,” say Jack Harris and Michael Fahimian. “We believe this is the bottom of the market, and it is only up from here.” Others aren’t so sure. “Sellers who think their homes are worth what they were offered (but didn’t take) during the pandemic or last year when we had a huge influx of fire victims looking to relocate need to readjust to the current market,” says realtor Juliette Hohnen. Related Stories News Nicolas Cage's Malibu Mansion Damaged by Massive Sinkhole Amid Coastal Erosion Lifestyle Did Jeff Bezos Just Buy a $200 Million Condo in Beverly Hills? These agents powered through the challenges — a few even outperformed 2025 — thanks to social media, innovative partnerships and a love of the game. Josh, Matt and Heather Altman and Jacob Greene Courtesy of Subject (4) The Altman Brothers Team DOUGLAS ELLIMAN Reality stars Josh, Matt and Heather Altman and Jacob Greene had another epic year, with more than $1 billion in deals from July 2025 to July 2026. Among the highlights were the local-record-breaking sale of a $25 million mansion in the coveted Encino neighborhood of Royal Oaks. They also hold the co-listing to the $39.8 million Hollywood Hills mansion built for Full House creator Jeff Franklin. “Good product that is priced correctly is selling,” Josh says. “I think we’ll continue to see buyers move quickly and aggressively for the right properties.” Cindy Ambuehl Courtesy of Subject Cindy Ambuehl CHRISTIE’S INTERNATIONAL REAL ESTATE SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA It was another stellar year for former actor Ambuehl, who totaled $355.9 million in sales year-to-year. Her standout deals included the $25 million sale of David E. Kelley and Michelle Pfeiffer’s Pacific Palisades estate; representing Kevin Nealon (also in the Palisades); and the sale of a Frank Gehry-designed Santa Monica home to Jason Blum. Ambuehl is heartened by the continuing recovery of the Palisades and Malibu. “There is real momentum returning to the Westside,” she says. “You can feel people becoming excited about the future of these communities again.” Santiago Arana Courtesy of Subject Santiago Arana THE AGENCY Known as the ultimate closer, Arana continues to be a major player in the market. In May, he represented Kamala Harris and Doug Emhoff in their purchase of an $8.15 million beach house in Point Dume, Malibu. “I genuinely believe this is one of the best times to be a buyer in Los Angeles,” he says. “The city is due for a strong comeback, and when that happens, these opportunities will be gone.” Rochelle Atlas Maize Courtesy of Subject Rochelle Atlas Maize NOURMAND AND ASSOCIATES Claiming more than $3.5 billion in career sales, Atlas Maize is known for her innovative media campaigns. Big closings this year included the $22.5 million sale of the historic “Roxbury Estate” in Beverly Hills, the onetime home of Casablanca director Michael Curtiz. “A million page views are wonderful,” she says. “One qualified buyer is better.” $4M Hollyridge House — 2356 Hollyridge Drive — listed by Rochelle Atlas Maize of Nourmand & Associates. Courtesy of Nourmand and Assoc. Ernie Carswell Courtesy of Subject Ernie Carswell SOTHEBY’S INTERNATIONAL REALTY After a messy split with Douglas Elliman, Carswell is thrilled that his team has found a new home at Sotheby’s. “I’ve learned the value of a true international company within our industry,” he says. With famous clients including the Chandler family and the late Raquel Welch, he now holds the co-listing for Angelina Jolie’s famed “Cecil B. DeMille Estate” in Los Feliz, on sale for $29.8 million. Jordan Cohen Courtesy of Subject Jordan Cohen REMAX Ranked the No. 1 ReMax agent worldwide, Cohen has long been known for his work with such A-list actors as Sylvester Stallone and more than 150 pro athletes, among them Reggie Miller, Shaquille O’Neal, Pete Sampras and Pau Gasol. He kept up his streak in 2026, scoring a big win with a major NBA star. “Selling Anthony Davis’ home in Bel-Air for $32 million was my most noteworthy sale for 2026 so far,” he says. Chris Cortazzo Courtesy of Subject Chris Cortazzo COMPASS With $815 million in sales from July 2025 to July 2026, Malibu ace Cortazzo has been at the front lines of the area’s post-fire recovery. He now holds the listing to the storied $90 million Point Dume Mediterranean mansion featured on The O.C. “Fortunately, we don’t have the ULA [mansion] tax in Malibu,” he says. “That has been a real advantage for our market, particularly at the luxury level.” Drew Fenton Courtesy of Subject Drew Fenton CAROLWOOD ESTATES With $9 billion in career sales, Fenton has attracted a starry clientele that includes Anthony Russo, James Packer, Eva Chow, Nick Candy and the estate of Bob Newhart. In May, he held the list on “The Peak,” a residential lot in Beverly Hills that sold for $31.8 million. Sally Forster Jones Courtesy of Subject Sally Forster Jones COMPASS Forster Jones counts among her clients Candy Spelling, Barbra Streisand and Chrissy Teigen and John Legend. Notable sales include a new Ramtin Ray Nosrati-designed Brentwood home for $24.38 million. In November, she became the recipient of the inaugural Compass Lifetime Achievement Award, given by Compass SoCal, for her years of success and contribution to the Los Angeles real estate industry. $100M La Fin, at 1200 Bel Air Road, listed by Sally Forster Jones of Compass. Courtesy of Compass Tomer Fridman Courtesy of Subject Tomer Fridman BEVERLY HILLS ESTATES Known as “Hollywood’s agent of record,” Fridman is the Kardashian-Jenner family’s go-to broker. He recently held the co-listing for Lori Loughlin and Mossimo Giannulli’s Hidden Hills estate that sold for $12.6 million. His portfolio reads like a map of trophy properties in Los Angeles, including 620 Arkell Drive in Beverly Hills, sold at $100 million, and Bel-Air’s La Fin, which brought $99.95 million. “The most sophisticated buyers don’t necessarily want the biggest house,” says Fridman, who recently left Christie’s for Beverly Hills Estates. “They want the house that is a home in every sense of the word.” Carl Gambino Courtesy of Subject Carl Gambino COMPASS As the Gambino Group continues its global expansion, it is hardly abandoning its L.A. base of operations. Major sales include the former Beverly Hills estate of Michael Caine and, later, Ricky Martin, which closed in December for $35 million. He also repped the buyer of Bruce Willis’ former $41.25 million Benedict Canyon estate. “Professionally, this has been my most successful year yet,” he says, “but what I’m most proud of is the team we’ve built.” Ginger Glass Courtesy of Subject Ginger Glass COMPASS With clients including Kylie Jenner, Mark Wahlberg, Jennifer Lopez, Cameron Diaz and Benji Madden, the THR list mainstay continues to find new ways to excel. “The most exciting evolution has been mastering target marketing and creative deal structuring,” says Glass, who notched $502.1 million in sales last year. “Helping clients secure great deals and build equity despite broader economic shifts has been incredibly rewarding.” Neyshia Go Courtesy of Subject Neyshia Go SOTHEBY’S INTERNATIONAL REALTY With $1 billion in career sales, Go runs The Go Group, Sotheby’s No. 1 realty team in SoCal. Specializing in new development and investment opportunities, her team oversees the marketing for the 44-floor Park Elm Residences at Century Plaza, where they have sold $45 million worth of properties in the past nine months. “I believe the market will continue to be defined by nuances that affect each of the individual neighborhoods in Los Angeles,” she says. Jon Grauman Courtesy of Subject Jon Grauman RESIDENT GROUP In 2025, the former Buying Beverly Hills star left The Agency to form the boutique brokerage Resident Group with Lauren Grauman and Adam Rosenfeld. They’ve emerged on the scene with a bang. In April, Grauman and Rosenfeld, alongside Bennett Bidwell, repped Guess CEO Carlos Alberini and his wife, Andrea, in their sale of Bruce Willis’ former Benedict Canyon mansion for $41.25 million. Jack Harris & Michael Fahimian Courtesy of Subject (2) Jack Harris & Michael Fahimian THE BEVERLY HILLS ESTATES The super team of Harris and Fahimian had another blockbuster year, accumulating a total transaction volume of $872 million. The duo now holds the most expensive listing in the world: the $400 million, 39-bedroom Chalon Estate in Bel-Air. “Wellness is the number one priority right now,” the duo told THR . “A great gym, sauna, steam room, cold and hot plunge and a dedicated recovery area are huge bonuses.” James Harris Courtesy of Subject James Harris CAROLWOOD ESTATES Now the head of Harris & Partners inside Carolwood, Million Dollar Listing’ s Harris has said goodbye to his longtime partnership with David Parnes. In April, he sold Lizzo’s Beverly Hills estate for $11.2 million. With $275 million in deals in the past six months, he also successfully repped the seller of the $10.35 million Sherman Oaks abode purchased by Macaulay Culkin and Brenda Song. Clients include Rihanna and A$AP Rocky, Robbie Williams and James Corden. “Today’s luxury buyer,” he notes, “wants a home that’s ready to enjoy from day one.” Juliette Hohnen Courtesy of Subject Juliette Hohnen DOUGLAS ELLIMAN The Hollywood insider and former MTV VJ continues to rake in marquee sales in today’s overloaded market. With a celebrity roster that includes Rami Malek, Emilia Clarke, Maria Bello, Chris Weitz, Elijah Wood, Sonya Walger and Dan O’Shannon, Hohnen maintains a keen read on the zeitgeist. “The biggest amenity in L.A. right now is a mahjong room,” she says. “I’ve been playing for a few years, and it gives me great joy to see a room devoted to mahjong!” Marci Kays & Jonathan Mogharrabi Courtesy of Subject (2) Marci Kays & Jonathan Mogharrabi CAROLWOOD ESTATES In August 2025, Kays and Mogharrabi represented Brad Pitt in his purchase of David Keuning’s Outpost Estates enclave for $12 million and sold Pitt’s “Steel House” to Austin Butler for $5.2 million. In February, they also repped Fear of God founder Jerry Lorenzo’s sale of his Los Feliz home for $8.6 million. Says Mogharrabi, “It’s been exciting to see these neighborhoods continue to evolve and reach new levels.” Aaron Kirman Courtesy of Subject Aaron Kirman CHRISTIE’S INTERNATIONAL REAL ESTATE SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA Since Kirman launched Christie’s SoCal operation in 2022, it has scaled to more than 300 agents across multiple offices. Three years later, it hit $4.2 billion in total sales volume. Kirman scored $912 million in sales from July 2025 to July 2026, including the recent $47 million sale of the Beverly Hills brutalist estate of Oakley founder James Jannard, which is tied for the highest-priced sale in Beverly Hills this year. He also sold a Beverly Hills home once owned by Mark Wahlberg for $22 million. Craig Knizek Courtesy of Subject Craig Knizek THE AGENCY Knizek has generated more than $1.2 billion in career sales. In February, he represented Macaulay Culkin and Brenda Song in the off-market sale of their Toluca Lake estate for $14.25 million. He also represented the buyer of Lori Loughlin and Mossimo Giannulli’s $12.65 million Hidden Hills estate and sold the residence of legendary songwriters Alan and Marilyn Bergman. “As state housing laws encourage greater density, luxury is defined by personal space,” Knizek says. Weston Littlefield & Alex Howe Courtesy of Subject (2) Weston Littlefield & Alex Howe CHRISTIE’S INTERNATIONAL REAL ESTATE SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA Littlefield and Howe helped spur post-fire redevelopment in August 2025, representing a foreign investor in acquiring nine oceanfront lots on Malibu’s La Costa Beach for more than $65 million. Their clients include Restoration Hardware CEO Gary Friedman, Saw franchise producer Oren Koules and, reportedly, Kristen Wiig. “There really isn’t another market quite like Los Angeles, because every neighborhood has its own identity,” Littlefield says. Linda May Courtesy of Subject Linda May CAROLWOOD ESTATES The venerable broker remains at the top of her game. This year, she held the co-listing on Tom Cruise’s former Beverly Hills estate, which billionaire financier Leon Black sold for $47 million in March in an off-market deal. In July, she made history selling the penthouse in West Hollywood’s Sierra Towers for a record-breaking $36 million. “The market has definitely slowed compared to the frenzy we experienced a few years ago, and buyers are taking more time to make decisions,” she says. “They’re thoughtful, selective and expect value. That said, the very best properties continue to stand apart.” Gina Michelle & George Ouzounian Courtesy of Subject (2) Gina Michelle & George Ouzounian THE AGENCY Michelle and Ouzounian have helped make the Valley a Hollywood hotspot. Celebrity clients include actor Daniel Wu and dancer Allison Holker. “We’re seeing buyers become much less tied to where they previously lived,” the team told THR . “Three of our recent sales in Encino were purchased by families relocating from the Westside and Newport Beach because they found they could get significantly more without sacrificing the Southern California lifestyle.” $13M 15834 High Knoll Road in Encino, listed by Gina Michelle & George Ouzounian of The Agency. Courtesy of the Agency Jade Mills Courtesy of Subject Jade Mills COLDWELL BANKER “Every market presents opportunities,” says Mills. “It has been especially meaningful to continue helping clients achieve exceptional results in this more selective and more difficult market.” With more than $9 billion in career sales, she continues to make big deals. In March, Mills sold the Beverly Hills mansion of former Windsor Healthcare CEO Lee Samson for $30.3 million. Michael & Myra Nourmand Courtesy of Subject (2) Michael & Myra Nourmand NOURMAND AND ASSOCIATES This year, the mother-and-son team brokered the sales of the former Malibu home of Barry Manilow and, later, Pink for $13.75 million and Tom Petty’s storied Malibu estate, which went for $11.2 million. “Not only was the property reminiscent of the Huntington Gardens,” Myra says of Petty’s place, “but it still had Tom Petty’s personality throughout, including his pre-wired studio. It was a piece of history that you could step inside.” David Offer Courtesy of Subject David Offer BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY “While there are still some buyers out there, they are not feeling any great sense of urgency; and as a result, they are moving cautiously and slowly,” says the veteran broker, who boasts career sales of more than $4.8 billion. “But now that the stock market has recovered nicely, the war is hopefully winding down and the summer is soon behind us, I am hopeful that market activity will pick up.” Jason Oppenheim Courtesy of Subject Jason Oppenheim THE OPPENHEIM GROUP Selling Sunset star Oppenheim remains one of the most visible brokers in Los Angeles. Last fall, he sold Bella Thorne’s Topanga Canyon home for $4 million. He now holds the co-listing of the $88 million Bel-Air contemporary megamansion developed by Michael Chen’s Luxford Group. David Parnes Courtesy of Subject David Parnes CAROLWOOD ESTATES This is Parnes’ first time on the list since splitting with partner James Harris. With $140 million in sales in the past six months, he seems to be handling the breakup well. His standout deals include the August 2025 sale of a $23 million Bird Street mansion featured in Entourage and Kevin Williamson’s Beverly Hills Post Office Estate for $21 million. “From a design perspective, we’re seeing a move away from homes that feel like museums,” he says. “Natural stone, warmer woods and homes with character are replacing the ultra-minimalist look that dominated for years.” Lea Porter Courtesy of Subject Lea Porter THE BEVERLY HILLS ESTATES In only four and a half years since returning to luxury real estate, Porter has surpassed $1 billion in sales. In April, she sold Daphna Ziman’s historic Beverly Hills Tudor-style estate once owned by Harry Warner for $27.25 million alongside co-listers Jade Mills and Joyce Rey. “A particular highlight has been representing the longtime Beverly Hills estate of Pat Boone,” she says of the past year. Kurt Rappaport Courtesy of Subject Kurt Rappaport WESTSIDE ESTATE AGENCY The elusive King of Hollywood Brokers had another banner year with more than $1 billion in sales. An agent for celebrities including David Geffen, David Ellison, Tom Brady and Beyoncé and Jay-Z, in May he held the listing for producer Joe Roth’s Beverly Hills estate, which went for $21.5 million. Joyce Rey Courtesy of Subject Joyce Rey COLDWELL BANKER The grande dame of Los Angeles real estate made her very first sale in 1974 — no less prestigious a property than the estate of Christina Onassis. More than 50 years later, the “billionaire’s broker” still loves what she does. “Every listing and client I work with excites me,” she says. Rey currently holds the co-listing (alongside Jade Mills) to Joni Mitchell’s former $26.99 million Malibu beach house. The Shevin Team Courtesy of Subject (3) The Shevin Team DOUGLAS ELLIMAN It is a family affair for The Shevin Team, which is composed of Marc Shevin and his daughters, Sara and Hanna. Best known for their work in Hidden Hills and Calabasas, they have repped celebrities including Kris Jenner, Kim Kardashian, Jennifer Lopez, Kaley Cuoco, Reggie Miller and Keyshawn Johnson. “Our dad has represented some area families for decades, and now we’re helping their adult children buy homes,” Sarah and Hanna said in a joint statement. F. Ron Smith & David Berg Courtesy of Subject (2) F. Ron Smith & David Berg COMPASS “The real estate market is currently in a standoff,” says Berg. “Buyers want a price that hedges against the economy. Sellers think their house is the exception to the economy. Everybody’s waiting for the other person to blink.” This stalemate hasn’t stopped the duo from having another successful year, with a sales volume of $645 million to prove it. “Social media has made it very easy to look like a top producer without being one,” Smith says. “Sellers figured that out, and now the first question we get in a listing appointment isn’t about marketing, it’s, ‘How many homes did you actually sell last year?’ That’s a healthy change.” Mauricio Umansky Courtesy of Subject The Umansky Team THE AGENCY Mauricio Umansky has built his team around his family, including his daughters, Farrah and Alexia, and dad, Eduardo. Since Umansky founded The Agency in 2011, it has grown into a global brand, but Umansky’s heart remains in L.A. “The weather here in Los Angeles allows for year-round indoor/outdoor living, which makes for very innovative architecture,” he says. $13.3M The Meadow House, at 2 Rumsen Trace in Carmel, listed by the Umansky Team at The Agency. Manny Espinoza Shauna Walters & Nicole Plaxen Courtesy of Subject (2) Shauna Walters & Nicole Plaxen SOTHEBY’S INTERNATIONAL REALTY With $1 billion in career sales, the duo has among the most impressive celebrity clientele in the business. They closed four transactions for Anthony Hopkins in the past year alone and represented Skechers founder Robert Greenberg in his record-setting purchase of the Melhill Estate in Brentwood for $53 million. “There’s something incredibly powerful about being able to meet someone over lunch in Beverly Hills and put together a deal that simply couldn’t happen the same way anywhere else,” Plaxen says. $25M 1000 The Strand, in Manhattan Beach, listed by Walters & Plaxen of Sotheby’s. Gavin Cater Shelton Wilder Courtesy of Subject Shelton Wilder CHRISTIE’S INTERNATIONAL REAL ESTATE SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA Wilder is the CEO of The Shelton Wilder Group at Christie’s International Real Estate Southern California, where she leads one of the few all-women luxury teams in Los Angeles. With an appearance on Shark Tank, a digital footprint of nearly 50,000 followers and a successful podcast, Wilder Possibilities, she has found innovative ways to build her brand and empower other female entrepreneurs. “We live in a digital-first world, and if you’re a ‘secret’ agent, you’re missing opportunities every single day,” she says. Brayden & Rayni Williams Courtesy of Subject (2) Brayden & Rayni Williams THE BEVERLY HILLS ESTATES Although the two are no longer romantically involved, the colorful duo’s professional life keeps swinging, with $1.6 billion in sales in 2025. Trusted by clients including Jennifer Lopez, Selena Gomez and Angelina Jolie, they have accrued $19 billion in career sales. The Williamses now hold the co-listing to Ardie Tavangarian’s $135 million Villa Siena and represented the mystery buyer who snapped up Joe Roth’s Beverly Hills midcentury modern for $21 million. *** Best of the Best: The 2026 L.A. Power Broker Awards The sixth annual THR Los Angeles Power Broker Awards, presented as always by The Society Group, will take place Sept. 16.
