articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Jon Cohen Named President Of Lipovsky & Stein’s Wonderlab Banner Comedian Mojo Brookzz Bringing Debut Special ‘I Know You Lying’ To Netflix In October ‘The Family Stone’ Sequel Set At Searchlight With Claire Danes, Rachel McAdams, Sarah Jessica Parker & Many More Returning View All September 14, 2026 7:00am John Cohen, Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein Courtesy/Getty Jon Cohen has joined Wonderlab , the newly launched production company of Final Destination: Bloodlines helmers Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein , as President. Cohen comes over from J.J. Abrams’ Bad Robot, where he most recently served as Head of Film. “We are so incredibly excited to launch Wonderlab with Jon,” Lipovsky and Stein said. “During his time at Bad Robot, Jon had a discerning eye for discovering some of the brightest genre filmmakers and writers and empowering them to make smart, original movies that connect with audiences. From our first conversations, Jon blew us away with his intelligence and deep creative insights about how to craft great stories. He shares our love of making unique and elevated films that are also incredibly fun and entertaining, and his collaborative nature is a perfect fit for the iterative way we plan to develop new movies at Wonderlab.” Related Stories News Zach Lipovsky And Adam B. Stein Ink First-Look Deal At Sony, Set 'Metal Gear Solid' Movie News 'Final Destination Bloodlines' Duo Zach Lipovsky & Adam B. Stein To Direct Animated 'Venom' Movie For Sony During his tenure at Bad Robot, Cohen produced a wide-ranging slate of features, including 10 Cloverfield Lane as co-producer, The Cloverfield Paradox and Overlord as executive producer. He was also a producer on Lou for Netflix, The End of Oak Street for Warner Bros., and the upcoming J.T. Mollner/Brie Larson film Skeletons , which Sony is set to release in 2027. Watch on Deadline Originally from Highland Park, Illinois, Cohen held executive positions at The Donners Company and Davis Entertainment before joining Bad Robot. “I couldn’t be more thrilled to be joining forces with Zach and Adam, and to be on the ground floor of what they’re creating with Wonderlab,” said Cohen. “I’ve admired the guys’ filmmaking for a while, and their FINAL DESTINATION: BLOODLINES was the sort of clever, impeccably made and wildly entertaining genre movie that so many aspire to create but very few can. As I’ve gotten to know them better, I’ve only grown more impressed with their ambition, work ethic, taste, story sense and talent, and how it’s all fused to an incredibly collaborative process and mindset that makes everyone who works with them long to work with them again. Cohen continued, “I’m very grateful to them for this opportunity, and to Sony Pictures for the faith they’ve placed in Wonderlab, and I look forward to making thrilling, surprising and emotionally resonant genre movies with this group for years to come.” Under a first-look deal with Sony Pictures that has the company developing projects across all of their film labels, Wonderlab projects announced so far include an animated Venom movie for Sony Pictures Animation; video game adaptation Metal Gear Solid ; and The Earthling , based on the Jonathan Marty short story, with the latter two projects being developed for Columbia Pictures. Founders Lipovsky and Stein broke out as the directors of New Line’s Final Destination: Bloodlines , which is now the highest-grossing film in its franchise at around $317 million worldwide. The films above are just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to their slate, which also includes a sequel to their 2018 sci-fi thriller Freaks , Warner Bros./Amblin’s Gremlins 3 , Universal/Amblin’s Long Lost , Paramount’s The Traveler , and more. “Wonderlab’s mission is to make movies using an iterative process that surrounds our creators with candid feedback from test audiences and other filmmakers,” Stein and Lipovsky stated. “It’s a process we’ve built over many years to make sure a film is the best it can be. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Gustavo Dudamel Takes New York Philharmonic Baton With Help From Lizzo, Liev Schreiber & More After Helping ‘Coyote Vs. Acme’ To Strong Opening, Legion M Expands Film Fund On 25th Anniversary Of 9/11, NY1 Anchor Pat Kiernan On “Putting Yourself Back In That Moment” View All September 14, 2026 7:49am William Franklyn-Miller in 'Young Washington' Angel Studios Angel Studios says its membership program has surpassed 3 million paying members, doubling its level of a year ago. The company, which went public last year, is known for releasing what it calls “values-based” films and TV series. It has promoted to Wall Street the unique role played by the Angel Guild membership plan, which not only provides a recurring revenue source but also creates essentially a giant-scale focus group. Projects are fostered by Guild members, who then weigh in at various stages of a project’s life cycle, reading scripts and viewing test screenings. Related Stories News Gossip Goblin AI Feature 'Gods Don't Give Gifts' Poised To Make Next Leap From YouTube To Big Screen News Is Neon Lining Up UK Distribution? - The Dish Angel burst onto the scene in 2023 when it released Sound of Freedom , an unheralded action movie about child trafficking that became a left-field blockbuster, grossing more than $250 million worldwide. Neal Harmon , the company’s co-founder and CEO, told Deadline in June the Guild had reached 2.4 million members. At the time of that interview, Angel’s historical actioner Young Washington was having its world premiere at the Tribeca Festival. The film wound up grossing $47 million, spawning a sequel. Watch on Deadline Angel’s theatrical slate continues with Runner , an action thriller starring Owen Wilson and Alan Ritchson, with upcoming theatrical releases also including Angel and the Badman , Drummer Boy , Hershey and Zero A.D. On the series front, the company plans new seasons of The Wingfeather Saga, Homestead and Testament . While Angel shares are well below their price at the IPO in September 2025, they have risen more than 20% over the past week, to about $5.50. articles.title: Donald Trump Says There Already Are Enough Guardrails Around AI
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted ‘60 Minutes’ Debuts New Season With A Pentagon Exclusive And Hidden-Camera Exposé Amid Plenty Of Scrutiny Of The Show Itself FCC Chairman Brendan Carr Accuses James Talarico Of Running A “Hoax” With Jimmy Kimmel Sit-Down; YouTube Interview Nears 7 Million Views Anthropic CEO Calls For Slowing Down AI Development, Warns Of “Swarm” Taking Over Internet In 6-12 Months View All September 14, 2026 7:54am Donald Trump Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images Amid the increasing alarm over AI ‘s supercharged capabilities, Donald Trump rejected calls for new regulation, saying that there already are guardrails in place. In a Truth Social post on Monday, Trump wrote, “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades! The Trump Administration has stopped AI ‘people’ from doing bad, or potentially bad, ‘things,’ like Dario ( Anthropic !), who is now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’ – and we will continue to do so! We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies! There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so. Conspiracy Theorists, Treasonists, Traitors, and Leakers, BEWARE!” Related Stories News '60 Minutes' Debuts New Season With A Pentagon Exclusive And Hidden-Camera Exposé Amid Plenty Of Scrutiny Of The Show Itself News FCC Chairman Brendan Carr Accuses James Talarico Of Running A "Hoax" With Jimmy Kimmel Sit-Down; YouTube Interview Nears 7 Million Views On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei posted an essay in which he called for slowing down AI development, warning that a “swarm” of AI agents could be capable of taking over the internet in 6-12 months. Watch on Deadline He wrote, “Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it’s my worry that in 6–12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet (potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage), and that the scale of damage would continue to increase from there if AI becomes more powerful without the necessary guardrails.” Amodei called on AI companies to commit to third-party evaluators “to verify adherence to safety practices and commitments, report incidents, and help assess the alignment of not just completed AI models but training pipelines and processes.” Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, and Elon Musk, founder of SpaceXAI, signalled agreement with Amodei. Amodei also called on governments to coordinate on safety standards. Trump, though, has warned of a slowdown in AI development ceding the technological arms race to China. articles.title: Moveria Film Acquires ‘No Money No Honey,’ Documentary Set For Imminent Premiere At Camden International Film Festival
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Midnight Madness! A Caped Canadian Prime Minister Stars In ‘Ladies And Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney’ – Toronto Film Festival ‘NAZA’ Review: Israeli Military Accused Of Depraved Indifference To Palestinian Life, Using AI To Kill In Gaza – Venice Film Festival ‘Black Sunflowers’ First Look: Ukraine’s Youth Live Life On The Edge In Propulsive Doc From EP Sean Penn – Toronto Film Festival View All September 14, 2026 8:00am 'No Money No Honey' Mimbre Films/Moveria Film EXCLUSIVE: Moveria Film has acquired international sales rights to No Money No Honey ahead of the documentary’s world premiere at the Camden International Film Festival in Maine. Moveria describes the film directed by Nicole Costa as “a vibrant story of friendship, migration, joy, and resilience” centering on Máxima Mauricio (she/he), “an Argentine non-binary sex worker in New York.” Daniela Camino of Mimbre Films produces along with Costa. No Money No Honey revisits personal VHS tapes recorded by Mauricio between 1991 and 2004, according to a synopsis. “Interweaving this vibrant archival material with post-pandemic 4K footage, the film opens a fluid portal into Máxima’s memory—confronting a childhood marked by abuse and neglect while longing for her golden days across Buenos Aires, Miami, and New York.” Related Stories Documentary Points North Institute Announces 2026 Artist Programs And Points North Forum Ahead of Camden Film Festival Documentary 22nd Camden Film Festival To Showcase New Work By Documentary's Leading Lights: Gibney, Kopple, Oppenheimer, Chin, Vasarhelyi, Poitras & More Lucas Besnard and Yasmin Porangaba negotiated the sales rights deal on behalf of Moveria Film, with producer Daniela Camino representing Mimbre Films. Watch on Deadline Moveria Films “What really drew us to No Money No Honey was the intimacy of Máxima’s story and the way the film brings us directly into her world,” said Lucas Besnard of Paris-based Moveria Film. “I was struck by the contrast between the VHS footage of her past—with all the energy, glamour, friends, and parties—and her life in New York in 2020. Having lived in New York myself, I connected with this side of the city. Máxima is incredibly endearing, and through her story, you get a sense of a queer community and a reality that deserves to be seen and better understood. That’s what made us want to bring the film into Moveria’s catalogue.” Ceskary Avitia of Moveria Film added, “Coming from Mexico, I know how much prejudice surrounds sex work and trans identity. What drew me to this film is that it doesn’t try to convince you of anything; it just asks you to listen to Máxima’s own voice and to the VHS tapes she filmed of her life. Through her archive, someone’s story opens up into an entire community—her friends, their world, and their shared history of trauma and resilience. Nicole Costa gives voice to a community rarely heard on screen, and everyone deserves the chance to tell their own story.” Mimbre Films In a statement, producer Daniela Camino of Mimbre Films commented, “Working with Moveria has been a turning point for No Money No Honey ’s international debut. Their experience and personalized approach are just what a film like ours needed. We are truly confident we will reach audiences around the globe.” No Money No Honey is programmed in Cinematic Vision Award competition at CIFF, the prestigious all-documentary festival that runs Sept. 17-20 in mid-coast Maine. The acquisition expands Moveria’s slate of “bold, auteur-driven international cinema,” according to a release. Founded in 2025, Moveria is an independent production, international distribution, and cultural mediation company “born from a collaboration between tech developers Arnaud Schoenher and Tristan de Oliveira and arts and culture professionals Ceskary Avitia and Isotta Tassoni… Moveria Film merges custom digital tools—including modeling, automation, and optimization—with traditional film production and distribution frameworks, bringing a novel approach to cinema grounded in dialogue across diverse fields to foster new creative experiences, fresh perspectives, and bold narratives about the world around us.” No Money No Honey , running time 80 minutes, is directed by Nicole Costa and written by Costa, Daniela Camino, and Melisa Miranda. Daniela Camino and Costa produced the film. The cast includes Máxima Mauricio Rodas, Sebastian Quiencke a.k.a. La Baronesa Ditra, Antonia Martinez, Nellie Benittez, Mila Miller, Darius M. articles.title: Pluto Film Boards ‘Ida’ Star Agata Trzebuchowska’s Horror Feature ‘Sick’ Ahead Of Fantastic Fest Premiere + First Teaser
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Well Go USA Entertainment Acquires ‘The Optimist’ For Digital Release On November 17 Canada’s Precious Metal Productions & Black Fawn Distribution Strike Genre Slate Deal – TIFF Beta Cinema Posts Fresh Deals For Trudie Styler’s ‘Up Against It’ Ahead Of TIFF Debut View All September 14, 2026 8:09am Sick Maciej Edelman EXCLUSIVE: Pluto Film has boarded sales for Agata Trzebuchowska’s horror feature Sick ahead of its world premiere at Fantastic Fest in Austin in September, which will be followed by its European debut at the Sitges Film Festival . The unsettling film about the horrors of growing up is the feature directorial debut of Polish director, screenwriter and actress Agata Trzebuchowska, who is best known internationally for her lead performance in Paweł Pawlikowski’s 2015 Oscar winner Ida . Patryk Sielecki and Adrianna Rędzia at Warsaw-based Lumisenta lead produce, while the cast features stars Konrad Kąkol, Katarzyna Łubik, Monika Niemczyk, Julian Świeżewski, and Eliza Rycembel. Related Stories News Firebook Entertainment Signals Move Into Production As First Movie 'Every Heavy Thing' Heads To Sitges News 'Disforia' Trailer: Spanish Horror-Thriller World Premieres At Austin's Fantastic Fest Set against the backdrop of the summer holidays, Sick revolves around sixteen-year-old Maks (Kąkol) and his older sister Emma (Łubik) who are sent to the Polish countryside to care for their ailing grandmother. Watch on Deadline Trapped together in the heavy, stifling isolation of the summer heat, the siblings’ bond begins to shift into something unsettling and difficult to define. As tensions rise and boundaries begin to blur, their grandmother’s frail presence takes on an increasingly disturbing quality, turning a once-idyllic summer into a haunting passage into adulthood. “We are very happy that Sick has found its home at Pluto Film. From our first conversations, we felt that they understood both the film’s provocative nature and the tenderness hidden beneath its genre elements,” said Lumisenta’s Patryk Sielecki. “The world premiere at Fantastic Fest and the European premiere at Sitges are an exciting beginning for the film, bringing it to audiences open to bold and unconventional stories. At the same time, we believe Sick can resonate beyond the genre circuit, as it is ultimately a deeply emotional story about adolescence, desire and dependence, centered on a relationship that crosses every possible boundary.” Pluto Film MD Daniela Cölle praised Trzebuchowska’s bold reinvention of the classic coming-of-age summer tale. “Agata Trzebuchowska has created an atmospheric and unsettling horror film that transforms the oppressive calmness of a summer into a powerful psychological landscape. Rather than coming-of-age story, Sick is the horror of growing up, exploring the fear, confusion, and loss of certainty that accompany the passage into adulthood.” Trzebuchowska shot to fame for her performance in Ida , as a young woman on the verge of taking her vows as a nun, after being scouted in a café by director Małgorzata Szumowska who knew her friend Pawlikowski was struggling to find the right person for the role. Trzebuchowska has eschewed mainstream fame since to forge her own path as a screenwriter and director. Sick follows short films including the Sundance-selected Heat and Vacancy , which also travelled the festival circuit stopping off at Go Short and Flickers’ Rhode Island International Film Festival. She also continues to act and was recently seen in Pete Ohs’ Erupcja alongside Charli XCX, Lena Góra and Will Madden. Sick will premiere in the New Wave sidebar of the Fantastic Fest running from September 17 to 24, 2026.
