articles.title: Paramount Argues States’ Antitrust Suit Will ‘Collapse Under Scrutiny’
articles.full_text: Sep 11, 2026 9:16pm PT Paramount Argues States’ Antitrust Suit Will ‘Collapse Under Scrutiny’ By Gene Maddaus Plus Icon Gene Maddaus Senior Media Writer @GeneMaddaus Latest Paramount Argues States’ Antitrust Suit Will ‘Collapse Under Scrutiny’ 8 hours ago Court to Hold Paramount-Warner Bros. Settlement Conference in Late October 17 hours ago Dan Schneider Loses ‘Quiet on Set’ Defamation Suit on Appeal 2 days ago See All Getty Images Paramount’s lawyers filed a legal response to the states’ antitrust lawsuit against the Warner Bros. Discovery merger on Friday, sketching out arguments and defenses it may use at a trial next March. Among other defenses, Paramount’s lawyers said they may claim that the coalition of 12 states lacks the authority to regulate the merger, “which is vested in the U.S. Department of Justice.” However, states do have the authority to bring claims alleging harms caused by conduct violative of federal antitrust law. Related Stories Bruno Dumont’s Cannes Movie 'Red Rocks' Sells to North America (EXCLUSIVE) Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit 'Congo Boy' (EXCLUSIVE) Paramount also noted that Cinema United, the trade group for theater chains, has called for a settlement. Popular on Variety “Day by day, the weak case against this Merger gets even weaker,” the company argued, adding that it also plans to challenge the states’ market definitions. “Plaintiffs’ case amounts to a series of attempted shortcuts and assumptions that collapse under scrutiny.” California led the state coalition in suing to block the merger in July, arguing that the deal will create unlawful concentration in the basic cable market and in the wide-release and blockbuster theatrical markets. The DOJ had earlier approved the merger , issuing a memo laying out its reasoning for why the deal should be allowed to go forward. States typically work with the DOJ in antitrust cases, but under the Trump administration California and several others have often charted their own course. Paramount has repeatedly argued that the deal will be pro-competitive, and will result in more movies and TV shows. In its answer to the complaint , the company denied the states’ allegations — a requisite formality to establish a legal controversy. The company also added a few pages of argument, alleging that the states’ case ignores the broader context of an industry in rapid transition to streaming. “The way audiences consume content is changing rapidly. Streaming services now have greater viewership than movie theaters and cable television,” Paramount argues. “Plaintiffs’ case depends on ignoring this reality. It involves a series of gerrymandered markets based on cherry-picked data from the past. The alleged markets are not the product of sound economic analysis or current market realities. They have been invented for one purpose and one purpose only: to trigger a presumption — any presumption, no matter how weak — in the hopes the Court will look no further.” The Writers Guild of America has filed its own lawsuit arguing that the merger will reduce the marketplace for writers’ work. That case is set to be heard alongside the states’ challenge at trial on March 2, 2027. Paramount has agreed not to close the deal until a ruling is issued after the trial — though it is asking the court to require the plaintiffs to post a $1.88 billion bond as the price of continuing the litigation. A judge is set to hear arguments on that request on Sept. 24. Meanwhile, a court will hold a two-day settlement conference in the antitrust case with the parties in late October. That’s a standard part of civil procedure and does not indicate whether a deal is in the offing. articles.title: Gary Oldman Predicts HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ Series Will Be ‘More Satisfying’ for Fans Than the Movies
articles.full_text: Sep 11, 2026 10:54pm PT Gary Oldman Predicts HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ Series Will Be ‘More Satisfying’ for Fans Than the Movies By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Gary Oldman Predicts HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ Series Will Be ‘More Satisfying’ for Fans Than the Movies 6 hours ago Streaming Prices Continue to Balloon: Is ‘Streamflation’ at a Breaking Point? 17 hours ago Maria Bartiromo Says ‘More to Come’ in First Comments After Shock Fox News Exit: ‘I Am So Grateful for the Outpouring of Love’ 18 hours ago See All Getty Images Gary Oldman , who played Sirius Black in four “ Harry Potter ” movies, said he believes HBO’s forthcoming TV series adaptation set in the Wizarding World will be a bigger crowd-pleaser than the Warner Bros. films. That’s because the movies were significantly abridged from J.K. Rowling’s original books, whereas HBO’s “Harry Potter” is including far more of the source material, the British actor said in a recent interview with EW. Related Stories Bruno Dumont’s Cannes Movie 'Red Rocks' Sells to North America (EXCLUSIVE) Wim-Wenders Produced 'I'll Be Gone in June' Bought for North America After Cannes Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) “We had to cut a lot [for the ‘Harry Potter’ movies], and still we could only get the films down to, like, three hours,” Oldman said, adding that “a lot of character detail was sacrificed” in the process. “I believe [the HBO series is] gonna do it pretty much word-for-word, which I think, as a viewer, would be more satisfying.” Popular on Variety Oldman has previously opined that Sirius Black, a character he loves, did not get enough screen time in the movies . “He wasn’t in it enough. He turned up and then he went through the veil,” Oldman told IndieWire in 2024. Oldman’s Black first appeared in 2004’s “Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban,” but he had only cameos in “Goblet of Fire” and “Deathly Hallows Part 2″ and a brief appearance in “Order of the Phoenix” before his character is killed off. That said, Oldman told EW he is “proud” and “grateful” to have been part of the “Harry Potter” films “because it is such a phenomenon, the like of which I don’t think you’re ever gonna see again.” “When you think of that initial cast, someone in the story who doesn’t get a lot of credit anymore is [director] Chris Columbus, who set the world up and cast it,” he said. “We were extraordinarily lucky to have those people come back again, and again, and again, and literally grow into those roles.” Oldman will next appear in Season 6 of Apple TV’s “Slow Horses,” which premieres Sept. 16 . Season 1 of HBO’s “Harry Potter” TV show has wrapped and will premiere on HBO and HBO Max on Dec. 25. The second season, which will be based on the second book in Rowling’s beloved fantasy series, is currently in pre-production at Leavesden Studios outside London. HBO has not announced casting for the role of Sirius Black in the series to this point. The cast of HBO’s “Harry Potter” series includes Dominic McLaughlin in the title role alongside Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley; John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore; Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall; Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape; Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid; Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom; and Lox Pratt as Draco Malfoy. Meanwhile, Oldman once said that his performance as Sirius Black in the movies was “mediocre ,” but he later clarified that he didn’t mean to “disparage anyone out there who are fans of ‘Harry Potter’ and the films and the character who I think is much beloved.” “What I meant by that is, as any artist or any actor or painter, you are always hypercritical of your own work,” he told Variety in 2024. “If you’re not, and you’re satisfied with what you’re doing, that would be death to me. If I watched a performance of myself and thought, ‘My God, I’m fantastic in this,’ that would be a sad day.” Three Films, and a Second Oscar? articles.title: ‘Totém’ Director Lila Avilés Wraps Production on ‘Cábula,’ Releases First Look (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 12, 2026 3:40am PT ‘Totém’ Director Lila Avilés Wraps Production on ‘Cábula,’ Releases First Look (EXCLUSIVE) By Christopher Vourlias Plus Icon Christopher Vourlias Latest ‘Totém’ Director Lila Avilés Wraps Production on ‘Cábula,’ Releases First Look (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Global Africa Hub at TIFF Market Seeks to Boost Visibility — and Deals — for African Filmmakers in Toronto: ‘It’s Our Moment’ 24 hours ago Telekom Srbija’s Content Head on Blueprint for Turning Serbian Production Powerhouse Into Global Player 2 days ago See All Courtesy Cuadernos de Cine Mexican filmmaker Lila Avilés (“Totém”) has wrapped production on her next feature film, “Cábula,” and shared an exclusive first-look image with Variety. The director presented the film during the Venice Gap-Financing Market , which took place from Sept. 4 – 6. Set in the fictional Mexican town of Mexicalpan, “Cábula” follows Toña, a dedicated and deeply compassionate teacher who is committed to nurturing her students’ creativity. When an invitation to represent their community takes Toña and her class to the capital, they encounter an absurd group of elites determined to appropriate and exploit their customs. But despite a series of challenges and betrayals, Toña reaffirms her calling and her belief in the transformative power of education. Related Stories Bruno Dumont’s Cannes Movie 'Red Rocks' Sells to North America (EXCLUSIVE) Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit 'Congo Boy' (EXCLUSIVE) Written by Avilés and Miguel Vasallo, “Cábula” is produced by Nicolás Celis (one of the producers of multi-Oscar winner “Roma”) for Cuadernos de Cine, the Mexico City-based shingle founded by Celis in 2008 and a sister company to production powerhouse Pimienta Films. It’s co-produced by Maria Zamora of Elastica Films and stars Teresita Sánchez, Gabriela Cartol and Montserrat Marañón. Popular on Variety The film marks Avilés’ long-awaited follow-up to “Totém,” which wowed audiences as well as the jurors at the 2023 Berlinale, where it won the Ecumenical Prize. Variety ’s Peter Debruge praised the “intimate, emotionally rich” drama, singling out the director’s “generous, open-ended style” in what he described as a “multilayered follow-up to ‘The Chambermaid.’” That film, which marked Avilés’ auspicious debut, premiered at the Toronto Film Festival in 2018, where it won the Ariel First Feature Film Award. According to a director’s statement provided to Variety , Avilés’ latest “uses comedy as resistance against a cruel, dehumanizing world… [and] explores humor as an escape valve and a collective mirror to question power, rebuilding the social fabric through vulnerability, tenderness and irreverence. At its heart is a tribute to education. In a country of minimal budgets, underpaid teachers become anonymous heroes.” Utilizing a mix of seasoned professional actors and fresh local talents, “Cábula” stars Teresita Sánchez, the veteran Mexican actress who featured in both “The Chambermaid” and “Totém.” Speaking to Variety from Mexico City, Avilés referred to Sánchez as her “muse,” comparing her to Federico Fellini’s wife, Giulietta Messina. “She has that energy that can make you cry, can make you laugh,” said the director. “She’s a magic woman. She has that power.” Avilés described Sánchez as a natural fit for the role of Toña, a woman whose “quiet, nurturing presence serves as an intimate moral counterweight to the surrounding chaos.” “She’s a woman that hears, she’s a woman that sees, but most of all, she’s a woman that feels,” said the director. “She’s really connected to her students, to her vocation — her calling. She’s super enthusiastic. She wants to [create] a real transformation in her students.” Avilés’ third feature builds on her already formidable catalog, twice representing Mexico in the Oscar race for best international feature film. Creatively, she said, all three films exist on a continuum, with one project leading naturally to the next. “When I started to do ‘The Chambermaid,’ I already had ‘Totém’ in my heart. While I was doing ‘Totém,’ I knew I wanted to do ‘Cábula,’” she said. “Sometimes we have stories, and those stories go out [into the world]. It’s that persistence of stories that…are not in the mind, but in the heart.” A former actress who directed theater before venturing into filmmaking, Avilés has been praised as part of the new wave of female directors shaping Mexican cinema. Celis echoed that, heralding the self-taught filmmaker as a “visionary.” “It is a true privilege to team up with a visionary like Lila Avilés, especially at a time when championing such genuine auteur voices is so challenging,” said Celis. “After admiring the beautiful and intimate journey that was ‘Tótem,’ we are thrilled to begin our collaboration with ‘Cábula.’” Octavia Spencer and Hannah Waddingham Are Badass Besties in Prime Video’s Middling Action Dramedy ‘Ride or Die’: TV Review Prime Video’s Stunning Drama ‘Sterling Point’ Elevates the YA Genre Beyond the Mundane: TV Review Loading comments... articles.title: ‘Dau’ Review: Ilya Khrzhanovsky’s Vast Cinematic Experiment in Historical World-Building Remains More Impressive From a Distance
articles.full_text: Sep 12, 2026 3:49am PT ‘Dau’ Review: Ilya Khrzhanovsky’s Vast Cinematic Experiment in Historical World-Building Remains More Impressive From a Distance The heftiest feature film to emerge so far from the 20-year multidisciplinary DAU project follows four decades in the life of a Greek-born physicist at odds with the Soviet state. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest ‘Dau’ Review: Ilya Khrzhanovsky’s Vast Cinematic Experiment in Historical World-Building Remains More Impressive From a Distance 2 hours ago ‘Stuffed’ Review: Jodie Comer and Harry Melling Sing the Body Eccentric in an Odd, and Oddly Touching, Taxidermy Musical 2 days ago ‘Company’ Review: Casey Affleck’s Latest Directorial Effort Isn’t What It Initially Appears to Be, but Isn’t Very Interesting Either Way 3 days ago See All Venice Film Festival More than six years after Ilya Khrzhanovsky premiered “ DAU . Natasha” and “DAU. Degeneration” at the Berlin Film Festival — right before the global COVID lockdown — to a politely muted reception and limited distributor interest, you might think the moment has passed for another missive from the DAU Cinematic Universe. Turns out, however, that you can’t keep a good immersive multidisciplinary art project dau. Or even a flawed and ethically questionable one: Allegations of physical and psychological abuse on the sprawling set of this years-long undertaking have surfaced prominently, but not enough to deter the Venice Film Festival from programming “Dau” — seemingly, as implied by the back-to-basics title, Khrzhanovsky’s attempt to extract a quintessential dramatic epic from untold reams of material — in its main competition. Related Stories Bruno Dumont’s Cannes Movie 'Red Rocks' Sells to North America (EXCLUSIVE) Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit 'Congo Boy' (EXCLUSIVE) The ethics of that decision are further fodder for debate, though festival brass have defended the film on political grounds. Certainly, you can argue that Khrzhanovsky’s overarching thesis, with its heavy focus on the grim tools of Russian state oppression and imperialism through history, has gained in timeliness since we last checked in on the DAU project, before Putin’s invasion of Ukraine. The other question to ask, however, is whether “Dau” is such an undeniable artistic accomplishment as to merit all this back and forth — and on that, the jury is out. Popular on Variety Weighing in at just over 200 minutes (not including the quarter-hour interval bisecting its Venice presentation), and spanning four decades in the life of a physicist involved in the Soviet atom-bomb project, the film certainly announces itself as a grave and major work. But beneath the impressive, sometimes seizure-threatening sound and fury of its formal construction, “Dau” feels dramatically and rhetorically thin: It plays as an avant-garde counterpart to such American films as “Oppenheimer” and “The Brutalist” (whose Oscar-winning DP, Lol Crawley, is one of three credited here), which likewise portrayed the social and ideological turmoil of a historical era through the portrait of a single tortured man. The man in this case remains something of a cypher to the last. The character is inspired by Lev Landau, a leading Soviet theoretical physicist who won a Nobel Prize in 1962, and whose achievements included calculating the dynamics of the first Soviet thermonuclear bomb. Landau’s own life story is eventual enough to sustain a conventional biopic, though of course “conventional” is not part of Khrzhanovsky’s mission. The film’s fictionalized protagonist, known only as Dau, is Greek-born, and played with gangly, wild-eyed physicality by the Greek-Russian musician Teodor Currentzis — whether or not Dau’s nationality was dictated by the casting, we never really learn the backstory of what brought him to the Soviet Union. He is, however, effectively marked as an outsider from the off, beginning with his eccentric appearance and dress — for the first half of the film’s extensive timeline, he’s consistently clad in glaring red velvet against the sober neutrals of the men around him. He’s introduced in 1928, striding with purpose down the heaving, filthy, vermin-infested streets of Leningrad in a grimily kaleidoscopic sequence barely tamed from the dizzily cacophonous montage of disconnected imagery — bodies, blackboard calculations, archival shreds of war and strife — that begins (and bookends) the film. It’s a vivid establishment of time and place, but we immediately lurch forward to mid-1930s Kharkiv, where we get better acquainted with Dau as a young rebel scientist thumbing his nose at the military industry that would like to employ him — arguing to his uniformed would-be recruiters that the job of the physicist is to discover new spaces, not defend existing territories. It’s the kind of principled stance that can only be beaten out of him by the state, but there’s plenty of time for that yet. The Kharkiv years also see him meet young working-class woman Nora (Radmila Shegoleva), cuing a marriage that will also be significantly corrupted in the hours to come. In the late 1930s, facing a choice between cooperation or consignment to a penal colony, he’s finally absorbed into a state scientific research institute in Moscow, where the rest of the film bitterly unfolds — a semi-surreal, oppressively over-scaled place that steadily consumes his mind, his principles and his freedom, under the unforgiving surveillance of government interrogator Azhippo (Vladimir Azhippo). What release he can find comes via a parade of extramarital affairs that progressively darken the mood of his domestic life — a holding pattern of misery that indeed holds through the film’s second half. Rather than opening up as a character, Dau recedes from us as time ticks by: His gradual ruin illuminates little that the film hasn’t already made obvious about the living nightmare of this milieu. Compensation come in a proliferation of visually and sonically startling setpieces that mostly serve to show off the unhinged dedication of the DAU project’s literal world-building. One fairly ordinary dialogue scene takes place atop an expansive steel grate suspended in mid-air; another at the foot of a gargantuan state sculpture surrounded by extras walking, for reasons unknown, at a perfect 45-degree angle; when Dau is violently attacked in the street, it’s against a mountain of cabbages scaled and loudly peeled by oblivious scavengers. As a sheer feat of production design and crowd choreography, then, “Dau” is occasionally jaw-dropping, though it still offers only a glimpse of the huge, mad artistic and practical undertaking that DAU is — conceived as a kind of quasi-“Truman Show”-style experiment in which participants lived and worked full-time on a 24/7 set spanning 12,000 square meters. None of the fictional DAU films set within this colossal recreation can be as interesting as the wider view, and “Dau,” for all its grandiose ambition, is no exception. Khrzhanovsky himself has described the films as mere trailers for the larger project; it would take a more hybrid form of cinema to capture the scope and folly of what has been achieved. ‘Dau’ Review: Ilya Khrzhanovsky’s Vast Cinematic Experiment in Historical World-Building Remains More Impressive From a Distance Reviewed at Venice Film Festival (Competition), Sept. 6, 2026. Running time: 202 MIN. Production: (Germany-France-Sweden) A Phenomen Berlin Filmproduktions, Essential Films, Société Parisienne de Production, Plattform Produktion production. (World sales: Producers: Ilya Khrzhanovsky, Philippe Bober, Leonid Lebedev. Co-producers: Susanne Mariann, Solal Coutard, Svetlana Dragayeva, Erik Hemmendorf. Crew: Director: Ilya Khrzhanovsky. Screenplay: Khrzhanovsky, with Susanne Marian, Vladimir Sorokin, Ilia Permiakov. Camera: Jürgen Jürges, Manuel Alberto Claro, Lol Crawley. Editors: Ilia Permiakov, Rob Myers. With: Teodor Currentzis, Radmila Shegoleva, Anatoly Vasiliev, Vladimir Azhippo, Dmitri Tcherniakov, Dmitry Cheglakov, Demyan Kudryavtsev, Maria Nafpliotou, Ekaterina Andreeva, Victoriia Skytska, Konstantin Leshan, Ekaterina Pachkovskaya, Alexey Blinov, Aleksey Trifonov, Peteris Kimelis, Nikita Nekrasov, Alexander Migdal, David Gross, Carlo Rovelli, James Fallon, Peter Sellars, Daniil Ishmatov, Yuriy Alekseev, Pavel Gordienko, Vladimir Yermolenko, Nikolay Voronov, Carsten Höller, Marina Abramović, Romeo Castellucci. articles.title: First Clip of ‘Club Kid’ Star Jordan Firstman as U.S. Voice Cast Lead in Cannes Breakout ‘Jim Queen’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 12, 2026 4:18am PT First Clip of ‘Club Kid’ Star Jordan Firstman as U.S. Voice Cast Lead in Cannes Breakout ‘Jim Queen’ (EXCLUSIVE) Global Constellation is screening the English-language version to North American buyers at TIFF By Marta Balaga Plus Icon Marta Balaga Latest Hans Petter Moland Talks ‘Epic Love Story’ That Defined the Nation as Norway’s Oscar Submission ‘Growth of the Soil’ Debuts Trailer: ‘It Resonates with All of Us’ (EXCLUSIVE) 23 hours ago ‘Krux’ Director Tony Vahl Combines Practical Magic With Post-WWII Taboo: ‘A Belief Can Help You – or It Can Destroy You” 1 day ago ‘Viva Carmen’ Reveals Clip Featuring Singer Silvia Pérez Cruz – and Brand New Song – Ahead of North American Premiere at TIFF (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Jordan Firstman, 'Jim Queen' Courtesy of Global Constellation Jordan Firstman , fresh off directorial debut “ Club Kid ” – acquired by A24 for release this November – leads the English-language voice cast of “ Jim Queen .” Variety reveals the exclusive first clip here: The animated comedy, directed by Marco Nguyen and Nicolas Athané, premiered at Cannes to rave reviews . Variety ’s Guy Lodge called it a “hilarious rare shot of broad comedy that plays like a queer ‘South Park’ on literal steroids.” Related Stories Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit 'Congo Boy' (EXCLUSIVE) Bruno Dumont’s Cannes Movie 'Red Rocks' Sells to North America (EXCLUSIVE) “Club Kid,” which Firstman starred in, wrote and produced, also took Cannes by storm, sparking a bidding war . Popular on Variety He’s currently in production on Season 2 of the hit HBO series “I Love LA,” and has also starred in FX’s “English Teacher” and Mubi’s “Rotting in the Sun.” He’s represented by UTA, The Lede Company and Frankfurt Kurnit Klein & Selz. Firstman is joined by Mateo Lane , currently on his third international stand-up tour, “We Gotta Catch Up!” Most recently, Lane made his Broadway debut as Billy Flynn in “Chicago” at New York’s Ambassador Theatre, the longest-running American musical in Broadway history. Nicole Byer (“Nailed It!”), John Cameron Mitchell (“Hedwig and the Angry Inch”), Bob the Drag Queen (“We’re Here,” “RuPaul’s Drag Race”) and Wendie Malick (“Shrinking”) round out the cast. M’saada Nia and Wolfie Trausch lead casting and recording of the English language version of the film, while Moby and Lindsay Hick’s Little Walnut is producing the English-language version alongside Bobbypills. Global Constellation is privately screening the English-language version, featuring the U.S. voice cast, to North American buyers at TIFF over the weekend, as U.S. distribution rights are currently in negotiation. Following its buzzy Cannes premiere – which Thierry Frémaux hailed as “one of the most beautiful in the festival’s history in terms of atmosphere, comparable to what ‘The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert’ once was” – the film was released in French theaters by The Jokers Films on June 17, debuting at #3 at the box office – behind only “Toy Story 5” and “Backrooms.” To date, “Jim Queen” is edging close to 400,000 admissions and $3 million at the French box office, and is rolling out theatrically across more than 25 international territories in the months ahead. U.S. distribution rights remain available and are currently in negotiation. Produced by Bobbypills founder David Alric and Arthur Delabays, “Jim Queen” starts when Heterosis, a mysterious virus that turns gay men straight, sweeps through the Parisian gay scene. Jim, the six-packed sovereign of the Gym Queens, goes from Pride royalty to social outcast. With only Lucien, a freshly out twink with more heart than abs, still by his side, Jim must race to find a cure before the disease erases the community that once worshipped him. Co-written with Simon Balteaux and Brice Chevillard, “Jim Queen” is produced by Bobbypills, one of Europe’s leading adult animation studios. It’s behind James Gunn’s “Creature Commandos,” the first television series and first official chapter of the DC Universe, for DC Studios and Warner Bros. Animation. Its credits also include “Captain Laserhawk: A Blood Dragon Remix,” produced with Ubisoft Film & Television for Netflix, as well as the adult animated series “Crisis Jung” and “Vermin,” both streaming on Netflix. “Let’s face it – gay guys are obsessed with the way we look. It can be tough in this world, because you have to be in shape and you have to be young. I’m 43, and guys look at me differently,” Balteaux told Variety back in May . “I used to be a Gym Queen myself. Now, I’m going to be a Daddy. It’s the next step, so I’m making fun of myself too. Although I’ll still go to the gym tomorrow.” Nguyen added: “There’s a lot of toxic masculinity in the gay community, too. You think it’s enough to say you’re gay, only to realize you don’t fit the standards because you weigh too much. It was very liberating to write this, and to write these jokes, because we talked about what we’ve experienced.” Co-produced by Umedia (“The Count of Monte Cristo,” “Night of the Zoopocalypse”), it’s executive produced by Moby and Lindsay Hicks for Little Walnut in the U.S., and Katarzyna Janiak and Jacek Świgost for Timeless Studios, Arthur Cohen for Momentum Entertainment, and Fabien Westerhoff for Global Constellation. “I guess we made a political film, but it’s also because laughter can be a weapon,” said Balteaux. “We’re very lucky – we live in a country where ‘Jim Queen’ could be made. But we still think of those in Senegal and trans people, also in the U.S. Maybe it will lighten their reality a little.” Prime Video’s Stunning Drama ‘Sterling Point’ Elevates the YA Genre Beyond the Mundane: TV Review Octavia Spencer and Hannah Waddingham Are Badass Besties in Prime Video’s Middling Action Dramedy ‘Ride or Die’: TV Review Loading comments... articles.title: ‘On Behalf of My Son’ Director Gabriel Martins on Black Brazilian Representation in His Films: ‘It’s a Life Project To Me, Not Just Cinema’
articles.full_text: Sep 12, 2026 5:01am PT ‘On Behalf of My Son’ Director Gabriel Martins on Black Brazilian Representation in His Films: ‘It’s a Life Project To Me, Not Just Cinema’ The powerful drama about guilt and reconciliation, having its world premiere at Toronto, is the biggest international hope this year from a Brazilian director By Rafa Sales Ross Plus Icon Rafa Sales Ross Guest Contributor Latest Toronto Premiere of ‘Le Faux Soir’ Crowns Great Year for Walloon Cinema, Built on Belgian Region’s Creative Freedom, Can Do Attitude 23 hours ago Ellen Burstyn Says Method Actors Today ‘Don’t Know Anything and Just Make a Lot of Noise’ 4 days ago ‘September 5’ Director Tim Fehlbaum Working on a ‘Historical Film’ Set in Berlin as Swiss Filmmakers Take on Challenges and Opportunities of Shooting in English 6 days ago See All Courtesy of Denise dos Santos/Netflix In 2022, Gabriel Martins made waves at the Sundance Film Festival with “Mars One,” a sprawling ensemble drama chronicling the life of a Black Brazilian family. At that time, the industry was still wrestling with what a post-pandemic future would look like and, despite “Mars One” having a strong festival run, Martins struggled to secure financing for his follow-up. Four years later, with Netflix on board, the director returns to a major festival with “ On Behalf of My Son ,” world premiering in the prestigious Platform section of the Toronto Film Festival , then heading to San Sebastián, where it plays in competition. Related Stories Bruno Dumont’s Cannes Movie 'Red Rocks' Sells to North America (EXCLUSIVE) Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit 'Congo Boy' (EXCLUSIVE) The drama reunites Martins with Rejane Faria, who seesaws between the visceral and the poised in her embodiment of Vicentina, the mother of a bus driver who apparently killed himself and dozens of passengers in a planned suicide crash. As the woman begins to pull at the complicated threads that made up her son’s psyche on the days leading up to the accident, she decides to contact the victims’ families and apologize on behalf of Wesley. “On Behalf of My Son” is produced by Martins’ Filmes de Plástico for Netflix Brazil , and stars Maíra Azevedo, Renato Novaes, Karine Telles, Giovanna Heliodoro, Thalma de Freitas, and Grace Passô. Popular on Variety Speaking with Variety ahead of the film’s premiere in Toronto, Martins notes how “Mars One” came out at a time when “Brazilian cinema was trying to recover” not only from the impact of COVID-19 but also from the major budget cuts for culture and political instability under the Bolsonaro government. “This partnership with Netflix came at a very important moment,” he notes. “‘On Behalf of My Son’ was an older project than ‘Mars,’ a project I’ve tried to make possible for many years, but it was very complex,” he goes on. “We needed several locations, a large ensemble; the theme was dense… I think the film comes at a very opportune time. We were ready, as a production company, to make a film this big and make it the best it could be. Those were four years of maturing and making the most of all the doors ‘Mars One’ opened to us.” Having Netflix’s support gave Martins a much more robust budget and the possibility to deliver a film that remains intimate and heartfelt while also displaying a higher production value – including a memorable crash scene. “Netflix arrived as a partner at a time when the idea was already consolidated, and we had a very strong script,” he says of what the streamer thought of balancing the two. “What you see onscreen was already very clear to us, and they came into the project wanting to support this idea of working on a story that would challenge the audience but was also universal.” Higia Ikeda, director of films at Netflix Brazil, echoes that thought: “Netflix is proud to partner with visionary storytellers like Gabriel Martins. It’s amazing to see how such a particular Brazilian story can connect with audiences across different cultures.” “‘On Behalf of My Son’ is a true testament to how sophisticated and diverse Brazilian cinema has become,” she adds. “Through its reflection on grief, solitude, forgiveness, and how life’s encounters shape us, the film invites us all to appreciate the power of human connection. We’re proud to partner with a unique Brazilian production company like Filmes de Plástico to bring such a sensitive and powerful story to the world.” Courtesy of Denise dos Santos/Netflix But the film could have ten times its budget and still not work without a central performance as powerful as Faria’s, who is almost unrecognizable onscreen. The duo first met in 2013, when the actress was working with Maurílio Martins, one of the founding members of Filmes de Plástico, on the short film “Quinze.” “My understanding of cinema came from working with them. I left that film and made some more, learned some more, and eventually reunited with Gabriel in ‘Mars One’ and now ‘On Behalf of My Son.’” “Vicentina was a major challenge, something completely different from anything I had done before,” she adds. “Gabriel didn’t write the character for me, as I was too young for it when he wrote it, but since the film took a decade to get made, I inched a little closer to her in age, and our relationship also narrowed. He knew I could make it work and get her to the place he wanted. I gave all of myself to the role; I became a completely different person.” Faria credits the “trust” Martins had in her, as well as his sharp direction, with the success of her performance. “We achieved something great and very new when compared to the work we’ve done before. I had a great desire to see a different side of myself, and this character, who required a lot of makeup and had completely different body language, allowed me to step out of myself.” With “Mars One,” Martins became the first-ever Black director to be chosen by Brazil to represent the country at the Oscars. With “On Behalf of My Son,” the director once again brings a large Black ensemble to the screen, showcasing the strength of Black creatives in a country that still struggles with representation despite having the second-largest Black population in the world, and the largest outside of Africa. Martins cast the film himself, saying it is one of the things that “makes him the happiest” about the project. “I love watching these people; it was incredible to be on set with these people, and putting them in the spotlight is aggrandizing,” he continues. “It’s a life project, not just cinema to me. It’s a project that involves wanting to see a better world, and that goes through directing people’s gaze to these stories, to interesting people. It makes me want to shoot more and more. Arriving at such a major festival, a festival that has a lot of influence, with this cast, is a great life experience for me.” Faria emphasizes that working with such a diverse cast “becomes bigger than the film.” “To have the film play [in Toronto], to see the impact on everyone who’s involved makes me so happy, and amplifies the political aspect of it, too.” “The political comes alongside my well-being and that of all involved,” she goes on. “ We were very, very happy with how we made the film, and we yearned to have our peers with us. When Gabriel offers the opportunity of having a majorly Black ensemble, he turns a desire we have all had for so long into a real possibility: the desire not to walk alone. To not experience success alone, but to bring others with you. Opening these doors is so important. It is a major step, and it says a lot about not only what we have already achieved but what we are yet to achieve.” “On Behalf of My Son” will open in select cinemas in Brazil Nov. 5, arriving on Netflix globally Nov. 20. articles.title: Maisie Williams Thriller ‘Ignition’ Bought by Saban for North America (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 12, 2026 5:15am PT Maisie Williams Thriller ‘Ignition’ Bought by Saban for North America (EXCLUSIVE) By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest Jeremy Thomas, Legendary British Producer and Oscar Winner, Dies at 77 3 minutes ago Liam Neeson on the ‘Rage’ Behind ‘The Lost Children of Tuam’ and Turning Producer for First Time to Tell Story of Irish Scandal 20 minutes ago Maisie Williams Thriller ‘Ignition’ Bought by Saban for North America (EXCLUSIVE) 30 minutes ago See All Maisie Williams in 'Ignition,' copyright NBF Studio 1. “Ignition,” the upcoming high-concept thriller led by Emmy-nominated “Game of Thrones” star Maisie Williams , has been acquired for North America. WestEnd Films — which launched the film in Cannes — has closed a domestic deal with Saban on the film, directed by Emmy-nominated filmmaker James Erskine (“Copa 71,” “Billie,” “Sachin: A Billion Dreams”). The deal comes following international sales including U.K. (Signature Entertainment), Spain (Twelve Oaks), Portugal (NOS), the Middle East (Falcon Films), CIS & Baltics (Arna Media), Eastern Europe and Israel (Forum Film). Related Stories Bruno Dumont’s Cannes Movie 'Red Rocks' Sells to North America (EXCLUSIVE) Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit 'Congo Boy' (EXCLUSIVE) Currently in post-production, “Ignition” sees Williams — currently on screens in “Practical Magic 2” — play a woman whose drive to London is thrown into chaos when an anonymous caller informs her that a bomb has been planted in her car. Trapped and cut off from any outside help, she’s forced to follow the terrorist’s instructions, her every move watched, with no choice but to deliver the ticking bomb to its target — the Royal Albert Hall. As the clock counts down, she must use all her wits to survive and, as the synopsis describes, “uncover why she has been entangled in this elaborate terror plot.” Popular on Variety The film co-stars BAFTA nominee Rory Kinnear (“No Time to Die,” “The Diplomat”) and Lovi Poe (“Bad Man,” “Seasons”). “Ignition” — which was filmed using real locations and on live roads using remotely operated multi-camera systems — was produced by Victoria Gregory (“Maiden,” “Man on Wire”), Erskine, Sean Sorensen (“Black and Blue,” “Worth”), Adriel Thomas, Jason Maza (“Twist,” “10×10”) and Mark Stewart (“Heist,” “Escape Plan”). The deal was negotiated by Maya Amsellem, managing director at WestEnd Films, on behalf of the filmmakers, and Bill Bromiley, vice chairman of Saban Films. “Maisie’s performance leaves you on edge, brilliantly bringing to life James Erskine’s terrific script,” said Bromiley. “We are proud to be a part of it, and to be working with Maya and the team at WestEnd.” Added Maya Amsellem: “We’re delighted to have Saban on board for ‘Ignition.’ They immediately understood James’s bold vision and the film’s strong commercial potential. It’s a gripping thriller with a fantastic lead performance from Maisie, and we’re excited for North American audiences to experience it.” WestEnd, which acquired the film under WeLove, its label dedicated to promoting female-driven stories and championing female talent, will continue international sales at TIFF . “Ignition” was produced by New Black Films under its New Bright Films label, together with Playhouse Pictures, Sharp House and in association with Royal Viking Entertainment, Epic EV Studios, Vectorscope Films and C’est Lovi Productions. Executive producers include Williams, Michael Safai, Montgomery Blencowe, Jon Levin (“All The Empty Rooms”), Randy Jones Toll (“Roofman”), Steven J. Toll (“Roofman”), Ian Sharp and Pat Wintersgill. articles.title: Liam Neeson on the ‘Rage’ Behind ‘The Lost Children of Tuam’ and Turning Producer for First Time to Tell Story of Irish Scandal
articles.full_text: Sep 12, 2026 5:25am PT Liam Neeson on the ‘Rage’ Behind ‘The Lost Children of Tuam’ and Turning Producer for First Time to Tell Story of Irish Scandal Directed by Frank Berry, the powerful drama details the tireless work of local historian Catherine Corless that helped uncover a secret mass grave at a mother-and-baby home. By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest New James Bond Movie: First Draft of the Script Is Done, Says Steven Knight 20 hours ago ‘SNL U.K.’ Cast on Wanting ‘Bigger Swings and Some Sex Sketches’ in Season 2, Bloody Backstage Mishaps and if Jack Shep’s Princess Diana Will Return 21 hours ago ‘Everybody Wants to F— Me’ Director on Poking Satirical Fun at Performative, Arthouse-Loving Nice Guys and Casting Taron Egerton to Play One 1 day ago See All Liam Neeson was in his home in upstate New York in late 2017 when he was sent a link to a New York Times article about a shameful episode in Ireland’s history. Almost a decade on and he tells Variety he’s “still coming to terms with my reaction to it.” The piece, written by Dan Barry, laid bare the shocking revelations from a Catholic home for mothers and babies in County Galway on Ireland’s West Coast, where over the course of several decades until the early 1960s almost 800 infants and children had been buried in unmarked graves, unceremoniously dumped in a sewage tank and forgotten about. Related Stories Bruno Dumont’s Cannes Movie 'Red Rocks' Sells to North America (EXCLUSIVE) Wim-Wenders Produced 'I'll Be Gone in June' Bought for North America After Cannes Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) At the center of the article was Catherine Corless, an amateur local historian whose tireless dedication and unwavering sense of moral justice, often in the face of indifference (and, in the case of the Catholic Church, resistance), would help bring the appalling story to light. Corless’ work had already sparked national fury in Ireland, but Barry’s words would bring it to a wider, international audience, including one of the Emerald Isle’s most famous stars. Popular on Variety “There certainly was a growing rage, an embarrassment,” says Neeson on his first thoughts after reading the article. “I was brought up a Catholic. I was an altar boy for a bunch of years, and I was kind of staggered by it. And, for the first time in my professional life, I remember thinking: ‘Whatever my celebrity status is in this business, I want this story to be shown to more people.” So “viscerally struck” was Neeson that he decided to take a leap from his prolific on-screen career (he passed 100 film credits a few yearsa go) and turn producer for the first time, optioning the article for what would become “The Lost Children of Tuam” (the same name as the article), which now screens in Toronto having had its world premiere on home soil at the Galway Film Fleidh. “I just had to respond to it a some way,” he says. Directing from a script by Rebecca Lenkiewicz (“She Said”) is acclaimed Irish filmmaker Frank Berry , best known for “Michael Inside” and, more recently, “Aisha.” “When I saw those films, I thought — this is the man to tell this story,” says Neeson, who would also bring on board producers including frequent collaborator Jules Daly and Irish powerhouse Element Pictures. “Frank wonderfully eavesdrops with his camera and allows the story to breathe. And especially with this, you do not want to highlight the horror. You just let the story breathe, and the horror will reveal itself.” Frank Berry while filming ‘The Lost Children of Tuam’ Berry may have been brought onto the film a few years after Neeson acquired the rights to the article, but says he was instantly “aware of the immense responsibility” involved. “There’s a lot of people in Ireland and throughout the world who are affected by religious institutions, so that was on our minds every single step of the way. How would survivors feel when they’re watching this scene or when they’re listening to this dialog?,” he says. “But we started at the very beginning at the core of the of the film, which is this amazing character in Catherine Corliss, and we let Catherine lead us.” Speaking at “The Lost Children of Tuam” world premiere in Galway, where she was the star attraction, Corliss — portrayed by Monica Dolan in the film — told the audience about first hearing that Neeson was interested in speaking to her. “And she said she nearly fell off her chair,” says Berry. Neeson would eventually go to meet Corliss in her home (“I did not arrive by helicopter,” he notes). “And I had a wonderful afternoon just listening to her, assuring her this would come to the screen and for her to please exercise extraordinary patience,” he says. “I said: ‘Schindler’s List’ took over 10 years.'” “The Lost Children of Tuam” would take almost 8 1/2 years. But it was wait everyone was prepared to make to get it right. Much of the film was shot in on location in and around the town of Tuam itself — “it was very important for us to be authentic,” says Berry — where the director met a number of survivors of the home. Some of them would go on to appear as extras (Neeson says that, beyond a period where “it was in my head for about 10 seconds,” there was never any question about him starring on screen). “As with all my films, it’s really important to have lived experience at every part of the process,” says Berry. “It keeps conversations alive and fresh all the time.” Monica Dolan plays Catherine Corless in ‘The Lost Children of Tuam’ But it wasn’t just those who had connections to that particular home who were drawn to the project and wanted to get involved. “There’s so many religious institutions in Ireland that have hurt people, and that pain is is very, very palpable in Irish society,” says Berry. “From Mother and Baby Homes but also the secondary school system, even up into the 80s, and the Magdalene Laundries, which were open until the 90s.” As he notes: “There are survivors everywhere — and that’s why we made the film, and that’s why what Catherine’s doing, is so important. A lot of that pain is is hidden in Ireland and there’s a lot of wounds in Ireland that need air.” For Corless, her devotion to the story and her support for the film came with on core goal: to excavate the area around the home, to have the children reburied respectfully and for them to be remembered. “So this is this film is part of that journey, and that’s the goal she’s looking at. And she’ll rest when that happens,” says Berry. For Neeson, who asserts that “The Lost Children of Tuam” may be his solitary producer credit, he cites a a line from someone else to underline the importance of Corless’ work. “As the wonderful late Irish journalist, Con Houlihan, once said regarding mortality and memory, ‘to be forgotten is to die twice.'” Oscar Predictions: Supporting Actress — Is This the Year of Penélope Cruz? articles.title: Jeremy Thomas, Legendary British Producer and Oscar Winner, Dies at 77
articles.full_text: Sep 12, 2026 5:42am PT Jeremy Thomas, Legendary British Producer and Oscar Winner, Dies at 77 By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest Liam Neeson on the ‘Rage’ Behind ‘The Lost Children of Tuam’ and Turning Producer for First Time to Tell Story of Irish Scandal 18 minutes ago Maisie Williams Thriller ‘Ignition’ Bought by Saban for North America (EXCLUSIVE) 28 minutes ago New James Bond Movie: First Draft of the Script Is Done, Says Steven Knight 20 hours ago See All Getty Images for BFI Jeremy Thomas , one of the film industry’s most highly respected independent producers with a body of work spanning more than half a century, has died. He was 77 years old. Across his career, Thomas — who founded the Recorded Picture Company and later Hanway Films — helped bring to life more than 80 features, championing the work of both international cinema and daring auteur filmmakers in the process. Related Stories Bruno Dumont’s Cannes Movie 'Red Rocks' Sells to North America (EXCLUSIVE) Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit 'Congo Boy' (EXCLUSIVE) Among numerous accolades and awards, Thomas won a best picture Oscar for Bernardo Bertolucci’s “The Last Emperor” in 1988. Popular on Variety Within his vast library of films, Thomas also produced Jonathan Glazer’s debut feature “Sexy Beast,” David Cronbenberg “Crash,” Christopher Hampton’s “A Dangerous Method” and Nagisa Oshima’s “Merry Christmas Mr. Lawrence.” Other directors he collaborated with, many across multiple films, would include Jim Jarmusch, Takashi Miike, Werner Herzog, Terry Gilliam, Richard Linklater, Karel Reisz, Phillip Noyce, David Mackenzie, Jerzy Skolimowski, Ben Wheatley and Wim Wenders. Most recently, Thomas produced Herzog’s “Bucking Fastard,” starring Rooney and Kate Mara, which premiered at the Venice Film Festival last week. Meanwhile, at the current Toronto Film Festival, his latest collaboration with Miike,”Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo,” is due to world premiere on Sep 14. In 2006 Thomas received a European Film Award for Outstanding European Achievement in World Cinema. In 2021, Thomas came to Cannes as the subject of Mark Cousins’ documentary “The Storms of Jeremy Thomas,” recounting his numerous trips to the festival and work as a producer. He recently appeared in Luca Guadagnino’s documentary “Joie De Vivre,” which also premiered in Venice, about the cinema, art, and life of Bertolucci. The son of director Ralph Thomas (who directed many “Doctor” films) and nephew of Gerald Thomas (who directed all of the “Carry On” films), Thomas was born in London in 1949. He began working in the industry immediately after leaving school, helping in the cutting rooms for films including “The Harder They Come” and “Family Life,” eventually rising to edit Ken Loach’s 1973 TV short “A Misfortune.” While he originally wanted to be a director, Thomas shifted to producing, with his first producer credit being the 1976 feature “Mad Dog Morgan,” which he made in Australia for director Phillipe Mora. He later returned to the U.K. and produced Skolimowski’s 1978 horror “The Shout,” the first for his newly-launched Recorded Pictures Company banner. The film went to Cannes, where it competed for the Palme d’Or and won the Grand Prix de Jury prize. articles.title: was canceled by Netflix after two seasons
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Minka Kelly Reacts To ‘Ransom Canyon’s Cancellation After “Two Beautiful Seasons” Noah Reid To Headline ‘Sheriff Country’ Medical Spinoff With Guest Starring Role On CBS Cop Drama ‘Ransom Canyon’ Canceled By Netflix After 2 Seasons View All September 10, 2026 5:43pm L-R: Josh Duhamel as Staten and Minka Kelly as Quinn in Episode 203 of 'Ransom Canyon' Season 2 Jeff Neumann/Netflix EXCLUSIVE : Staten and Quinn will be staying together forever as Netflix has opted not to proceed with a third season of the Texas romantic drama Ransom Canyon starring Josh Duhamel and Minka Kelly . The decision comes a month and a half after Season 2 was released on July 23. Ransom Canyon , an adaptation of the Jodi Thomas novels, already was on borrowed time. Related Stories Recaps ‘Ransom Canyon’ Showrunner Breaks Down Season 2: Grift, Love Triangles, Surprise Pregnancy & Ending That Is “Launch Of Next Story” For Possible Season 3 Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Cancellations Photo Gallery: Series Ending This Year & Beyond After a respectable but not massive viewership for Season 1, the series found itself somewhat on the bubble last year. It was eventually renewed for Season 2 more than two months after the premiere with a reduced order (eight episodes vs. 10) and a creative overhaul that included a supporting cast shakeup. With the storyline reset and other major changes, I hear the second installment was creatively better received internally. But, following a similar trajectory as many Netflix sophomore shows recently, Ransom Canyon returned down , logging 4.1 million views for its first week of release, off 43% from its Season 1 opening week, which collected 7.2 million views. Watch on Deadline The drama managed to bring its first season back into Netflix’s Top 10 for a week, which is important to the streamer, but the new installment fell off the Top 10 after only three weeks vs. four for Season 1. With Netflix weighing cost vs. performance for its renewal decisions, the Season 2 viewership likely was not enough to secure another season for a show that has considerable budget given its marquee-name leads. One of the things for which Ransom Canyon will be remembered is that Kelly stood her ground and asked for pay parity with Duhamel when she was offered the co-lead opposite him in 2022. It was a bold move amid a post-pandemic, post-peak TV industry contraction but it paid off — as Deadline reported last year , while she did not achieve full parity, Kelly came close to it and praised Netflix for their response to her request. Other sophomore Netflix series this year with similar or bigger year-to-year premiere week viewership slides that have managed to secure third seasons include Running Point (-43%), The Four Seasons (-63%) and several shows that had been renewed ahead of their Season 2 debuts including The Gentlemen (-45%), Avatar: The Last Airbender (-59%) and A Good Girl’s Guide To Murder (-76%). Netflix series to recently score a renewal also include Tires, My Life With the Walter Boys, Free Bert and Big Mistakes. Ransom Canyon follows childhood friends-turned-star-crossed lovers Staten Kirkland (Duhamel) and Quinn O’Grady (Kelly) who never seem to be able to get their timing right. The duo were tested again in the second season with Quinn getting briefly engaged to someone else but by the end, unlike the Season 1 finale which saw Staten and Quinn split up, they were in a good place — and very much together. In fact, as opposed as Season 1, the Season 2 closer of Random Canyon did not have any jaw-dropping cliffhangers, which would bring some consolation to fans who had invested in the series and its characters for two seasons. The finale did set up a potential love triangle for Ellie (Marianly Tejada) and a possible larger Season 3 presence for Staten’s half-brother Levi, played by Steve Howey, who deserved more than the single scene he was in. In Season 2 of Ransom Canyon , the titular Texas town hangs in the balance as ranching dynasties unravel, hearts switch allegiances and the overall future of small town culture built on ranching and agriculture comes under scrutiny. April Blair served as showrunner, creator and executive producer. articles.title: Amy Ryan Joins Emilia Jones In Netflix Drama Series ‘The Retrievals’ From Molly Smith Metzler
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Minka Kelly Reacts To ‘Ransom Canyon’s Cancellation After “Two Beautiful Seasons” Noah Reid To Headline ‘Sheriff Country’ Medical Spinoff With Guest Starring Role On CBS Cop Drama ‘Ransom Canyon’ Canceled By Netflix After 2 Seasons View All September 11, 2026 3:10pm Amy Ryan Ali Smith EXCLUSIVE : Amy Ryan ( Birdman ) is set to star opposite Emilia Jones in The Retrievals , Netflix ‘s third series from Maid and Sirens creator/executive producer Molly Smith Metzler . Inspired by the Peabody-winning NYT podcast by Susan Burton, The Retrievals follows an unlikely community of IVF patients who come together to crusade against Yale University after they are operated on without anesthesia–because a nurse stole their fentanyl. Ryan will play Carla Russo, a veteran nurse at Yale Fertility Center who pleads guilty to diverting vast amounts of fentanyl and diluting it with saline, forcing many patients to endure egg retrieval surgery without anesthesia. Related Stories Ratings 'The Gentlemen' Season 2 Loses Half A Million Viewers In The UK Cancellations and Renewals 'Ransom Canyon' Canceled By Netflix After 2 Seasons Jones plays Gabby Clemente, one of Carla’s victims who leads a groundbreaking legal battle against Yale University. Watch on Deadline Metzler is writer and showrunner. She executive produces via her Quiet Coyote banner alongside her Maid and Sirens collaborators Colin McKenna and LuckyChap. Serving as exec producers for LuckyChap are Dani Gorin, Tom Ackerley, and Margot Robbie. Additional executive producers include Caitlin Roper for The New York Times, and podcast write Burton. Also reuniting with Metzler is Lila Neugebauer, who directed one episode each of Maid and Sirens . She will direct the pilot episode of The Retrievals and executive produce. Thismarks the first series regular role for Ryan, an Oscar nominee for Gone Baby Gone . In TV, she is known for her major recurring roles on HBO’s The Wire, NBC’s The Office, Hulu’s Only Murders In the Building and, most recently, Season 1 of Apple TV’s Sugar. She will next be seen in Tom McCarthy’s A Statement , which will premiere at the New York Film Festival. articles.title: Curry Barker Initially Planned To Get Tattoos If ‘Obsession’ Opened To $20M; Inde Navarrette Has Plans To Direct – TIFF
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Curry Barker Initially Planned To Get Tattoos If ‘Obsession’ Opened To $20M; Inde Navarrette Has Plans To Direct – TIFF United Artists, Amazon MGM & Steven Spielberg’s ‘Mandela Catalogue’ Sets Summer 2028 Release Warner Bros’ Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy On Gen-Z Resurge, Credibility With Filmmakers & Embracing The Unknown – Toronto View All September 11, 2026 3:57pm Curry Barker And Inde Navarrette Getty Images “All we can hope for is that it sustains” That’s what Curry Barker was first told by his reps and those around him about the domestic box office prospects for his horror pic Obsession . He wasn’t expecting too much. Then the horror romance wound up making more than Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu , $512.6M to $345.5M at the global box office. In a sit-down at TIFF with his leading Obsession star Inde Navarrette, moderated by the fest’s Midnight Madness programmer Peter Kuplowsky, the duo reminisced how their lives have changed over the last year following the pic’s world premiere at TIFF where it was snatched up by Focus Features for $15M. The first change they noticed was an upgrade in their flight and hotel this year versus last when they arrived as a pure indie ( Obsession was financed by Capstone for $750K). Related Stories Reviews Toronto Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline's Reviews Reviews 'Faith' Review: Erin Doherty Is Heartbreaking As A Mother On The Brink In Paul Andrew Williams' Soulful Supernatural Drama - Toronto Film Festival However, had Obsession opened to $20M, Barker shared there was a plan for him and his reps to get tattoos. Watch on Deadline “It didn’t (do that). It made $17M. So we’re like ‘Ok, I guess we’re not getting the tattoos…still really cool’,” he said, “And then the next weekend it made $27M. It was like ‘Holy shit!’ That’s unheard of for it to go up!.” Interesting backstory, Barker had Obsession tested and the audience was quite unhappy with Bear (Michael Johnston) and his handling of off-the-rails g.f. Nikki (Navarrette), who he put a love-binding toxic spell on. “People were saying that they were frustrated with Bear and they didn’t understand why he doesn’t just try to do more to fix it (the spell.” “They were like ‘Why isn’t he going back to the crystal shop? Why isn’t he doing more research and trying to fix it?’ We got an overwhelming amount of people wanting us to do that,” said the filmmaker. “Then I was like ‘Oh, wait, that’s not what I want to do. I don’t want to try and fix it. It’s way more interesting that there’s a passivity in his character. He’s what I would call a passive antagonist,” explained Barker. “So, it became clear to me that the way to fix the movie was not to make Bear try and fix it sooner, but to actually make it even more clear to the audience that he wants to make it work. That’s the thing that he becomes active on trying to make this work,” said Barker. Barker thus had reshoots, which he praised his financier for; those additional resources proved to the filmmaker that his backers had complete faith in his vision. In regards to his how his career changed: Barker no longer gets ‘Nos’ when he heads into pitch meetings. Before Obsession, he would constantly come up with new ideas which were shot down. Now, the response he gets is, “‘Curry, what is it you want to do?'” shared the director. “It’s a little more challenging, he added, “I can pitch anything.” In terms of Navarrette’s streak, she recently appeared at D23 where it was announced she’s playing Rogue in the Marvel Studio’s revival of X-Men. “Everything has changed for me, I’m now in rooms I could never even imagine,” said Navarrette about her life post TIFF 2025, “I’m pitching my own projects and am hopefully can produce and direct my own stuff.” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Conjuring $30M U.S.; NFL Week 1 To Impact Holdovers Company & State AGs Set Antitrust Suit Settlement Talks For October Noah Reid To Headline CBS’ ‘Sheriff Country’ Medical Spinoff, Will Guest On Cop Show ‘Onwards And Sideways’ Chat; ‘Girl Group’, ‘River’, ‘Stuffed’ Reviews; WB Chiefs Read More About: 2 Comments

articles.title: Russell Crowe Charms 1,400-Strong Venice Audience With ‘What Love Builds’ Doc Charting His Musical Career
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Russell Crowe Charms 1,400-Strong Venice Audience With ‘What Love Builds’ Doc Charting His Musical Career ‘Before The War’, ‘Our Share Of Sand’ Scoop Top Venice Critics’ Week Prizes Venice Parallel Section Giornate Degli Autori Unveils 2026 Winners View All September 11, 2026 5:10pm Russell Crowe and Alberto Barbera at the What Love Builds world premiere at the Venice Film Festival Vittorio Zunino Celotto/Getty Images Russell Crowe enjoyed an enthusiastic response to his bio-doc meets concert film What Love Builds as it premiered Out of Competition to a 1,400-strong crowd at the Venice Film Festival on Friday evening. The documentary sets out to show that music has been part of Crowes’s life long before he decided to move to Sydney from New Zealand in the late 1980s to pursue an acting career, busking on the streets initially to make ends meet. It charts Crowe’s early musical endeavours from his teen years performing at an Auckland music hall under the stage name of Russ Le Roq, to his 415 performances as Eddie/Dr Scott in a New Zealand production of The Rocky Horror Show . Related Stories News International Insider: European TV In Peril; Venice & TIFF Latest; Mercedes Ron Interview Festivals 'Before The War', 'Our Share Of Sand' Scoop Top Venice Critics' Week Prizes Crowe delves into the creation of his first major band 30 Odd Foot of Grunts in 1992; its prophetic The Photograph Kills EP , and his abrupt decision to disband it as his acting career took off and he felt his fame was muddying the waters. He suggested a pushy offer verging on the vampiric from then Sony head Tommy Mottola to sign the band had been the final straw. Watch on Deadline In an example of how his love of music has fed into his acting, Crowe reveals how a line in Gladiator from his character Maximus in which he tells Emperor Marcus Aurelius that he has been away for “2 years, 264 days, and this morning” had been written at his request and taken inspiration from the “It’s been seven hours and 15 days” lyric in Prince’s track Nothing Compares 2 U. Later, he recounts how on 2010 Robin Hood , he had been able to influence the casting of the merry men to bring in actors who were also musicians. These would include Scott Grimes who would go on to become an occasional member of his current band Indoor Garden Party alongside the likes of Les Misérables actress Samantha Barks and Canadian folk rock musician Alan Doyle. Crowe also digs into lows of his career such as his arrest in New York in 2005 for assault for throwing a telephone at a hotel employee; “the pain” of being pursued by paparazzi, to whom he says he is ironically also grateful for capturing some of his favorite pictures of him with his children, or the ridiculing of his work as a musician and songwriter as his fame took off. Footage from the band’s performances intercut throughout film had the Venice audience clapping as if in a concert, with a cover version by Crowe of Dire Straits’ Romeo and Juliet causing the Sala Darsena theater to erupt into full-scale applause. Russell Crowe breaks into huge smile as 1,400-strong crowd claps to the beat of closing credits of bio-doc come concert film ‘What Love Builds’ at Venice Film Festival pic.twitter.com/zEO5ho8WNa — Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 11, 2026 As the credits rolled at the end, spectators clapped to the beat of the final track while a visibly happy Crowe laughed and smiled at the reaction. Crowe, who wrote, directed and produced the documentary, told a press conference earlier that it had been 15 years in the making. “I thought it might take me a year, but as I was doing it, things would come up that I was going to be doing shortly with the music, so I kept waiting for that, and the next thing, and the next thing. By the time we sat down to cut it we had an extensive 18 feet of film,” he said. “It was massive undertaking to try to chip away at the narrative, but I knew what my intention was, and my intention was to answer the question I get asked probably most and that is to define the difference between music and acting. The film attempts to explain the two things are completely intertwined for me,” he said. Crowe said Venice had been his target festival for the documentary and revealed he had contacted Italian director Gabriele Muccino, who directed him in Fathers & Daughters , to help connect him with Artistic Director Alberto Barbera. “As we’re coming towards the end of the cut, I said out loud, the most amazing thing would be if I could get to screen this in Venice. I’ve been to a lot of film festivals, but the most fun film festival is Venice, and there’s depth in the appreciation of the audience,” he said. “I couldn’t have had a better result as a filmmaker. This thing was just extremely personal, and this is the absolute perfect place.” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Conjuring $30M U.S.; NFL Week 1 To Impact Holdovers Company & State AGs Set Antitrust Suit Settlement Talks For October Noah Reid To Headline CBS’ ‘Sheriff Country’ Medical Spinoff, Will Guest On Cop Show ‘Onwards And Sideways’ Chat; ‘Girl Group’, ‘River’, ‘Stuffed’ Reviews; WB Chiefs Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Girl Group’ Review: Rebel Wilson’s Musical Comedy Is Fun Spiritual Sequel To ‘Pitch Perfect’ — Toronto Film Festival
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Toronto Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline’s Reviews ‘Girl Group’ Review: Rebel Wilson’s Musical Comedy Is Fun Spiritual Sequel To ‘Pitch Perfect’ — Toronto Film Festival ‘River’ Review: Joshua Giuliano Makes Directorial Debut With Tragic Family Drama Wrapped In Atmospheric Slasher — Toronto Film Festival View All September 11, 2026 5:11pm 'Girl Group' Future Artists Entertainment/Live Nation Studios Nearly 15 years after first stealing audiences’ funny bones as Fat Amy, Rebel Wilson has provided a new generation with a musical comedy that will have fans laughing and singing along just the same. In Girl Group , co-written and directed by Wilson, the Australian multihyphenate stars as popstar Tassie Young, who found fame with her four best friends when they were discovered at a talent show in 1996. Related Stories Festivals The Obsession For The Next ‘Obsession’ At TIFF: Festival Hot List Includes Pics For Sale With Cynthia Erivo, Chase Infiniti, The Maras, Dave Bautista & More Reviews Toronto Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline’s Reviews But with Tassie’s party girl ways forcing her out of the group in 2006, she finds out her former bandmates are having a reunion tour in the present and don’t want her back. After a DUI arrest, Tassie is forced to teach music to a group of teen girls at East Hollywood Community Center, where she discovers their talent and helps them prepare for an audition with a major label. Watch on Deadline Wilson hits all the right comedic notes as both star and director, complemented by hilarious performances from an ensemble that includes Jennifer Coolidge as her manager, Randall Park as the community center’s director and Derry Girls alum Jamie-Lee O’Donnell as a rival coach with her own girl group. The movie is also stacked with cameos from the likes of the Spice Girls’ Mel C, Pussycat Dolls’ Nicole Scherzinger, Sally Hawkins, Chris Colfer and more. With fun choreographed covers of Spice Girls, Destiny’s Child, Billie Eilish, Chappell Roan and others, the ensemble of newcomers puts their talent on full display, in addition to keeping up with their seasoned co-stars’ comedic chops. With an addictively enjoyable film like Girl Group that blends heart and humor, Wilson has returned to her roots to provide a fun, character-driven musical comedy that is sure to appeal to anyone who couldn’t stop singing “Cups (When I’m Gone)” for the majority of 2011. articles.title: ‘The View’s Sunny Hostin Defends AI As “New Art Form” Amid “Gatekeeping In Hollywood Around Black & Brown Creative Content”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Ocean Way Festival Canceled In Santa Monica Due To Beach Erosion & “Can No Longer Be Safely Held As Planned” Gary Oldman Says HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ TV Series Will Be “More Satisfying” Than The Movies ‘The View’s Sunny Hostin Defends AI As “New Art Form” Amid “Gatekeeping In Hollywood Around Black & Brown Creative Content” View All September 11, 2026 6:52pm (L-R) Joy Behar, Sunny Hostin and Alyssa Farah Griffin Sunny Hostin received pushback from her co-hosts on The View as she defended the use of AI in Hollywood. Hostin, who recently licensed her name and likeness to AI company Fountain 0, argued that generative AI should be considered a “new art form,” noting that it can help the entertainment industry show more Black and Brown representation. “I partnered with this company because I’ve written a trilogy, and for six years I’ve tried to get my films or my stories made into series and films, and the gatekeeping in Hollywood around Black and Brown creative content is insane,” the former prosecutor said. “I cannot get New York Times best-selling books onto the screen to tell diverse stories to diverse communities.” Related Stories News ‘The View’ Season 30 Cast Photos & Guests Set For ABC Talk Show News ‘The View’s Whoopi Goldberg Shuts Down Audience Boos At Ted Cruz Mention: “We Don’t Jell With Them Always, But We Are Respectful” She continued, “With AI, that cuts out the gatekeeping. You get to make your film. You get to have a director … It’s a way to go to a streamer and say, ‘Here’s the product. Will you license it? Will you show it?’ It’s a way, I think, to get Black and Brown stories told.” Watch on Deadline Joy Behar noted that with AI, “real people are not working,” and Hostin added, “The real people are not getting jobs in Hollywood. Black and Brown actors are not getting the jobs.” Alyssa Farah Griffin jumped on Behar’s point and said, “I worry you’re closing the doors to those roles being played by Black and Brown actors and being replaced by AI.” “That would be great if the studios would not gatekeep and allow the stories to be told,” Hostin replied. Griffin also said generative AI is “pulling from intellectual property of all the existing actors out there,” and they aren’t getting residuals for it. One thing that’s for sure is that the AI “train has left the station,” as Hostin said, who added, “This is something that’s here. It’s not going away, and I think that there are going to be enormous benefits.” Ana Navarro asked Hostin whether she felt any ethical issues with working with an AI company, and Hostin said she “thought about it a lot” before signing away her likeness. “I think that diverse stories need to be told,” Hostin said before Behar interjected to say, “We’ve said that already. I’m saying that those same people that you’re worried about are now out of work.” Hostin defended that point, saying, “I’m not the person putting them out of work because the studios just won’t make these projects.” Behar then said, “Force them to do it rather than have a robot replace Black people in movies.” Hostin closed out the topic, saying, “I don’t think it’s ever going to take away the arts. I think it’s a different art form.” Watch the full exchange from The View in the video below. ‘Practical Magic 2’ Conjuring $30M U.S.; NFL Week 1 To Impact Holdovers Company & State AGs Set Antitrust Suit Settlement Talks For October Noah Reid To Headline CBS’ ‘Sheriff Country’ Medical Spinoff, Will Guest On Cop Show ‘Onwards And Sideways’ Chat; ‘Girl Group’, ‘River’, ‘Stuffed’ Reviews; WB Chiefs Read More About: 7 Comments

articles.title: Gary Oldman Says HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ TV Series Will Be “More Satisfying” Than The Movies
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Ocean Way Festival Canceled In Santa Monica Due To Beach Erosion & “Can No Longer Be Safely Held As Planned” Gary Oldman Says HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ TV Series Will Be “More Satisfying” Than The Movies ‘The View’s Sunny Hostin Defends AI As “New Art Form” Amid “Gatekeeping In Hollywood Around Black & Brown Creative Content” View All September 11, 2026 8:30pm Gary Oldman and Daniel Radcliffe in 'Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix' Warner Bros. Gary Oldman is weighing in on the HBO adaptation of the Harry Potter saga and says one key difference from the films will make it “more satisfying” for fans. In a new interview, the actor who played Sirius Black across multiple movies in the Harry Potter universe revealed why he thinks the TV series will have an advantage over the films. “We had to cut a lot, and still we could only get the films down to, like, three hours,” Oldman told Entertainment Weekly . “I believe [the TV series is] gonna do it pretty much word-for-word, which I think, as a viewer, would be more satisfying.” Related Stories News Gary Oldman Reveals Jack Lowden's Response To His Bond Comments News Gary Oldman Clarifies James Bond Comments: "I Do Not Know, But I'm Hoping It's Jack" Oldman, who first appeared in the films in 2004’s Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, said that “a lot of character detail was sacrificed,” which the series could develop further. Watch on Deadline The actor said he was “grateful” to be part of the Harry Potter franchise, calling it a “phenomenon,” and added, “I don’t think you’re ever gonna see again.” “When you think of that initial cast, someone in the story who doesn’t get a lot of credit anymore is Chris Columbus, who set the world up and cast it,” he said. “We were extraordinarily lucky to have those people come back again, and again, and again, and literally grow into those roles.” Oldman would reprise his Sirius Black role with a cameo in 2005’s Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire . He then appeared in 2007’s Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix . The actor’s last appearance was a cameo in 2011’s Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows — Part 2 . The Harry Potter series will debut in Christmas 2026 on HBO and stream on HBO Max. Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone ‘s logline reads, “There is nothing special about Harry Potter – or so his Aunt Petunia tells him. But when a mysterious letter of admission to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry arrives, it opens the door to a hidden world of magic, friendship and adventure. Yet behind Hogwarts’ enchanted walls lie dark secrets. Harry must find the courage to prove himself against the darkest wizard of all.” The series stars Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape, Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid, Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom, Lox Pratt as Draco Malfoy, Leo Earley as Seamus Finnigan, Elijah Oshin as Dean Thomas, Tristan Harland as Fred Weasley, Gabriel Harland as George Weasley, Ruari Spooner as Percy Weasley, Alessia Leoni as Parvati Patil, Sienna Moosah as Lavender Brown, Finn Stephens as Vincent Crabbe, William Nash as Gregory Goyle, Warwick Davis as Filius Flitwick and Sirine Saba as Pomona Sprout. ‘Practical Magic 2’ Conjuring $30M U.S.; NFL Week 1 To Impact Holdovers Company & State AGs Set Antitrust Suit Settlement Talks For October Noah Reid To Headline CBS’ ‘Sheriff Country’ Medical Spinoff, Will Guest On Cop Show ‘Onwards And Sideways’ Chat; ‘Girl Group’, ‘River’, ‘Stuffed’ Reviews; WB Chiefs Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Ocean Way Festival Canceled In Santa Monica Due To Beach Erosion & “Can No Longer Be Safely Held As Planned”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Ocean Way Festival Canceled In Santa Monica Due To Beach Erosion & “Can No Longer Be Safely Held As Planned” Gary Oldman Says HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ TV Series Will Be “More Satisfying” Than The Movies ‘The View’s Sunny Hostin Defends AI As “New Art Form” Amid “Gatekeeping In Hollywood Around Black & Brown Creative Content” View All September 11, 2026 8:55pm Ocean Way Festival Getty Images Ocean Way Festival has been canceled because of beach erosion caused by Hurricane Marie. The two-day festival was scheduled for Saturday, September 26, and Sunday, September 27, with headliners The Killers and Olivia Dean, along with artists like Jack White, Sublime, Alvvays, Khruangbin, Durand Jones & The Indications, and Hiatus Kaiyote. “Due to the impacts of Hurricane Marie, the City of Santa Monica has canceled the inaugural Ocean Way Festival,” event organizers said in a statement on Friday, September 11. “Storm surf and runoff has caused significant beach erosion and the festival can no longer be safely held as planned.” Related Stories News Gary Oldman Says HBO's 'Harry Potter' TV Series Will Be "More Satisfying" Than The Movies News 'The View's Sunny Hostin Defends AI As "New Art Form" Amid "Gatekeeping In Hollywood Around Black & Brown Creative Content" The statement also noted that “plans are already underway to bring the festival to Santa Monica in 2027,” adding, “Refunds are being processed automatically, and no further action is required on your part. Please allow a few business days for the refund to appear in your account. Thank you for your support. See you soon.” Watch on Deadline Other artists scheduled to appear included SG Lewis, 54 Ultra, Hot Chip DJs, DJ Harvey, Austin Millz, Vandelux, Heidi Lawden, Blond:ish, Poolside, Carlita, Good Neighbours, Coco & Breezy, Nala, and Erez. Ocean Way Festival is not the first L.A.-area festival canceled this year. In August, the inaugural LA Jazz Festival was canceled and postponed until 2027, citing “last-minute public safety and municipal costs associated with the final permitting” of the event, according to a statement NBC4 shared. The jazz festival included “Jazz on the Beach” concerts at Dockweiler Beach and featured musical performances by John Legend, Janelle Monáe, Parliament Funkadelic featuring George Clinton, Charlie Wilson, Raphael Saadiq, Original Koffee, Terrace Martin, Poncho Sanchez, among others. ‘Practical Magic 2’ Conjuring $30M U.S.; NFL Week 1 To Impact Holdovers Company & State AGs Set Antitrust Suit Settlement Talks For October Noah Reid To Headline CBS’ ‘Sheriff Country’ Medical Spinoff, Will Guest On Cop Show ‘Onwards And Sideways’ Chat; ‘Girl Group’, ‘River’, ‘Stuffed’ Reviews; WB Chiefs Read More About: 3 Comments
