Zurich Film Festival/Summit EXCLUSIVE : The Zurich Summit (September 25 to 27) has revealed its second batch of speakers including Oscar winner Edward Berger ( Conclave ), Oscar nominee Robbie Brenner ( Barbie ), Constantin Film CEO Oliver Berben; and Komplizen producer Janine Jackowski ( Sentimental Value ). Also joining will be director-influencer Zack London, better known as the face of the YouTube/Instagram generative AI filmmaking team Gossip Goblin; and Transcontinental Entertainment Studios CEO/Zurich Film Festival President Martin Moszkowicz. They join existing speakers including Backrooms director Kane Parsons, AMPAS CEO Bill Kramer , Candle Media founder Kevin Mayer, Mediawan Pictures CEO Elisabeth d’Arvieu, and MUBI CEO Efe Cakarel. Related Stories News Zurich Summit: Kane Parsons, Kevin Mayer, Efe Cakarel & Eline Van Der Velden Among Speakers News International Insider: AI's First 'Actress'; Deadline Studio In Zurich; Insight From Iberseries The newly revealed speakers will join panels exploring the box office resurgence, AI, creator economy, YouTube, TikTok, and this edition’s Game Changer, Glen Basner. Watch on Deadline As the official media partner for the Summit (which is the flagship industry event of the Zurich Film Festival), Deadline covers and moderates panels, hosts the Deadline Studio for executive interviews, and provides on-the-ground reporting. Berger said of the Summit and Basner’s award: “I feel truly honored to have been asked to moderate this year’s Zurich Summit Game Changer Award conversation with its very deserving recipient, Glen Basner. I have had the immense pleasure to meet Glen on my first job in the film industry more than thirty years ago. Many moons later we graduated from colleagues to partners on Conclav e which was just pure joy. As a longtime admirer of the Zurich Film Festival, it is especially meaningful to return after having screened my previous three films there — and to have attended in person with Ralph Fiennes and Colin Farrell to present Conclave and Ballad Of A Small Player , respectively. As a Swiss citizen, I always love coming back to Switzerland, and especially to the ZFF. I’m excited to sit down with Glen, a true game changer whom I have admired and respected for many years, and perhaps elicit a few secrets out of him along the way. I know we have a lot to learn from him.” CAA Media Finance’s Roeg Sutherland, a longtime supporter of the event, commented on the Summit and this year’s Game Changer: “The Summit is such a well-curated gathering and plays a pivotal role in the global film financing marketplace. Glen possesses a rare ability to fuse a world-class creative sensibility with sharp strategic thinking, all driven by a genuine love of cinema. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BBC Stokes Anger By Curbing Cab Rides For Night Shift Workers… As Senior Managers Spend $17,000 On Taxis In Three Months Pierce Brosnan Says Tom Hardy ‘MobLand’ Feud Was “Storm In A Teacup” Channel 4 To Combine Drama & Comedy Teams Under Historic Jobs Cull View All September 11, 2026 3:40am 'The Gentlemen' Season 2 Netflix The blaze of Meghan Markle -shaped publicity around The Gentlemen appears to have done little for the show’s UK ratings, according to official figures. Season 2 of Guy Ritchie ‘s glossy crime drama premiered on September 3 on Netflix and, after seven days of streaming, the first episode was watched by 3 million British viewers. The Gentlemen ‘s viewing figures dropped around 15% from Season 1’s debut episode, which was streamed by an audience of 3.5 million in March 2024. Deadline’s Katie Campione reported that The Gentlemen scored 6.7 million streams in its first four days of availability. articles.title: Quiver Distribution Takes U.S. For Jérémy Comte’s Ghana & Canada-Set Drama ‘Paradise’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie John Trengove’s ‘The Smell Of Apples’ Sells To France Ahead Of TIFF Debut Gaza Doc ‘NAZA’ Gets 25-Minute Venice Ovation, Setting New A-List Festival Record As Palestinian Flags Fly In Sala Grande ‘Le Faux Soir’ Trailer: Arieh Worthalter & Mélanie Thierry Star In WW2 Belgian Resistance “Media Hack” Drama – TIFF View All September 11, 2026 5:00am Paradise Entract Studios, EMA Films, Constellation Productions EXCLUSIVE: Quiver Distribution has acquired U.S. rights to Oscar-nominated Canadian director Jérémy Comte film feature Paradise . The Canada -France- Ghana co-production had its world premiere in the Panorama section of the Berlinale earlier this year. Quiver is planning to release the film in the U.S. this winter. WME and Global Constellation , a Vuelta company, negotiated the deal on behalf of the filmmakers. The transatlantic drama thriller revolves around two teenagers living thousands miles apart, one on the streets of Accra in Ghana, the other in a Quebec suburb, whose lives become unexpectedly intertwined through their searches for the truth about their absent fathers. Related Stories Executives 'Murdoch Mysteries' Maker Shaftesbury Hires Nataline Rodrigues In Creative Push News Shailene Woodley Wins First Emmy For 'Paradise', Gives Shoutout To Her Mom In Ghana, Kojo is drawn into a world of street gangs and deception following his father’s disappearance at sea. Meanwhile in Quebec, Tony discovers his mother’s relationship with a mysterious sailor who may hold the key to finding the father he has never met. Watch on Deadline The film marks the feature debut of Canadian filmmaker Jérémy Comte, whose acclaimed short FAUVE was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film and won the Special Jury Prize at Sundance. “In Paradise, Jérémy Comte reveals the extraordinary power of human connection, with a rare balance of intimacy and expansive scope,” said Quiver Co-Presidents Berry Meyerowitz and Jeff Sackman. “We are thrilled to partner with this wonderful team and to introduce this stunning and sure-to-be memorable feature to U.S. audiences.” “Jérémy has crafted a deeply cinematic and emotionally resonant debut that crosses continents. We are thrilled to partner with Quiver to bring Paradise to U.S. audiences.” said Fabien Westerhoff at Global Constellation. Comte first made waves with Fauve which was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film and won the Special Jury Prize at Sundance. He recently wrapped principal photography on his second feature , Eléo & Nova , produced by Roger Frappier ( The Power of the Dog ). The survival drama follows four siblings left alone in a remote Canadian country house as a heatwave, power outage and mysterious lights turn their newfound freedom into something increasingly unsettling. Global Constellation handles international sales, with the film set to be submitted for festival consideration in 2027. Paradise is written by Comte and Will Niava and stars Daniel Atsu Hukporti, Joey Boivin-Desmeules and Évelyne de la Chenelière. The film is produced by Tim Ringuette of Entract Studios, Anne-Marie Gélinas of EMAfilms and Westerhoff under the banner of Constellation Productions, with Noah Segal and Christina Piovesan of Elevation Pictures. Global Constellation handles international sales. Elevation Pictures is releasing the film in Canada, while Tandem Films released the film theatrically in France in August. ‘Practical Magic 2’ Weaves $3.5 Million In Thursday Previews Trudeau Company; Reviews For ‘Being Heumann’, ‘The Housewife’; Photos Netflix Cancels Josh Duhamel-Minka Kelly Series After Two Seasons ‘Muppet Show’ Special Got Viewership & Emmys – Where’s The Disney+ Series Order? articles.title: Justin Trudeau Launching Production Company At TIFF
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac ‘Minotaur’ & ‘De Gaulle’ Among Five Titles Included In France’s International Oscar Shortlist Gaza Doc ‘NAZA’ Gets 25-Minute Venice Ovation, Setting New A-List Festival Record As Palestinian Flags Fly In Sala Grande ‘All Of A Sudden’ Trailer: Ryusuke Hamaguchi Returns With Parisian Drama That Japan Submitted To The Oscars View All September 11, 2026 5:36am Justin Trudeau DAVE CHAN/AFP via Getty Images Former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau is launching a production company with his former Chief of Staff Katie Telford, and it will be called Hope & Hard Work. The pair will officially launch the company at this year’s Toronto Film Festival. They will be repped by 3 Arts. In their official announcement, Trudeau and Telford have described the company as a “multidisciplinary media and entertainment enterprise dedicated to developing and producing engaging stories across film, television, audio and live experiences.” Related Stories Festivals John Trengove's 'The Smell Of Apples' Sells To France Ahead Of TIFF Debut Festivals Toronto Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline's Reviews The company is currently developing a slate of projects, including an adaptation of Perry Chafe’s Closer by Sea, from writer and producer Perry Chafe ( Republic of Doyle). Trudeau and Telford will also serve as executive producers on Detective Aunty , an adaptation of novelist Uzma Jalaluddin’s book, which has been optioned by Neshama Entertainment and producer Todd Berger. Watch on Deadline “At a time when the world can feel increasingly divided, we believe in the power of great storytelling to bring people closer,” Trudeau and Katie Telford said in a statement announcing their company. “In building Hope & Hard Work, we are finding stories that evoke empathy and understanding that can reach audiences in transformative ways; stories that transcend our own beliefs, and help us see the world through someone else’s eyes, and remind us of what we share. The projects we are working on reflect this ambition, and we are excited to bring these stories to the screen.” The full slate of Hope & Hard Work projects can be found below: CLOSER BY SEA by Perry Chafe – Series From the writer and producer of the hit TV shows Republic of Doyle and Son of a Critch , a poignant coming-of-age debut novel about the mysterious disappearance of a young girl and the fragility of childhood bonds, set against the backdrop of a small island community adapting to an ever-changing landscape. DETECTIVE AUNTY by Uzma Jalaluddin – Series Produced by Neshama Entertainment and Todd Berger with Trudeau and Telford as executive producers, Detective Aunty by Uzma Jalaluddin is a witty, warm-hearted cozy mystery about Kausar Khan, a widowed South Asian mother who returns to Toronto after her daughter is accused of murder. Convinced of her innocence, Kausar puts her keen observational skills—and talent for getting people to talk—to work, uncovering secrets, lies and betrayals within the close-knit community she once called home. LE COLLÈGE written by Jessie Gabe ( North of North , Workin’ Moms , Mr. D ) and Shebli Zarghami ( North of North , Late Bloomer , Kim’s Convenience ) – Original Series At Montreal’s most prestigious private high school, two codependent best friends navigate relationships, class and identity among the city’s elite. Set against Montreal’s unique culture and layered history, their coming-of-age story is distinctly local—and universally relatable. POWER MOVES by Leesa Ronald – Series A sharp, witty rivals-to-lovers romantic comedy set in the high-stakes world of politics and media. Ambitious political adviser Millsy Hatton is focused on getting her boss re-elected—until persistent journalist Archie Cohen threatens to derail both her campaign strategy and carefully controlled life. As professional rivalry turns into undeniable attraction, Millsy is forced to reconsider what she’s willing to sacrifice for success. BACKCHANNELS (Working title) – Series Based on the book The Right Hand: Conversations with the Chiefs of Staff to the World’s Most Powerful People by Phoebe Saintilan-Stocks, and in development with Phoebe’s twin sister Chloe Saintilan, Backchannels is a fast-paced scripted series that follows the life and work of a new Chief of Staff as they learn to navigate the environment of politics and power. articles.title: Ben Silverman, Emmanuelle Chriqui, Keshet & More On Advisory Board Of New Platform Connecting Jewish Creators With Investors — TIFF Market
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Zurich Summit: Edward Berger, Robbie Brenner, Oliver Berben, Janine Jackowski, Martin Moszkowicz & More Join Swiss Conference Lineup Noah Schnapp, David Mazouz & Seu Jorge Leading Thriller ‘Stealing From Pablo’; Myriad Launching For TIFF Market Odeya Rush, Annarah Cymone & Neela Jolene Join Justin Long & Iris Apatow In Killer Bee Movie ‘Stung’, Filming Wraps View All September 11, 2026 5:54am Shooq Shooq EXCLUSIVE : Former NBC Co-Chairman Ben Silverman, Micah Green (CEO of 30 West), Tanya Cohen (Co-CEO of Made by Us), actress Emmanuelle Chriqui ( Entourage ), producer Anthony Bregman ( Eternal Sunshine Of The Spotless Mind ) and Keshet International are among the advisory board members of new platform Shooq , which aims to connect Jewish creators with investors keen to accelerate Jewish storytelling. The group, overseen by veteran producers Ari Pinchot and Jonathan Rubenstein, is aiming to help finance film, TV, podcasts and digital media that “strengthen Jewish identity, combat antisemitism and bring top level Jewish stories to global audiences”. Related Stories News 'R.L. Stine's Pumpkinhead 2' Launches At TIFF Market, Details Revealed With Cassandra Peterson AKA 'Elvira Mistress Of The Dark' Joining Cast News Justin Trudeau Launching Production Company At TIFF Named after the Hebrew word for marketplace and launching this week during the Toronto Film Festival and market, the group aims to connect creators with investors, media funds, studios, foundations, philanthropists, and mission-driven funding partners. Watch on Deadline According to its founders, the platform already features narrative features, TV series, podcasts and social media video content. Funders are being sought to finance development, production and marketing with each project curated by the Shooq platform to match it with an appropriate financier. Unlike crowdfunding platforms, Shooq isn’t designed to raise or manage funds directly, but more as a matchmaking platform with funders creating profiles outlining their investment interests, requirements, preferred genres, funding ranges, and areas of focus. When a project aligns with those criteria, Shooq facilitates a direct introduction between the creators and the potential funder. Any investment or grant discussions take place directly between the parties. Funders can also showcase their own projects for additional funding. According to the founders, the site already features funders from the investment and philanthropic arenas. Shooq is also offering funders access to industry consultants and “optional reporting tools and impact metrics for mission-driven funders seeking to measure their project’s cultural and social outcomes”. Participation is free and funders can participate anonymously, depending on their preference. Founders Pinchot and Rubenstein produced the Roast of Anti-Semitism comedy show in LA and run the Jewish Writers Institute with the Maimonides Fund. “Great stories shape culture,” said Pinchot. “Many investors and philanthropists have been eager to support meaningful [Jewish] media but lacked both a trusted way to curate projects and an efficient mechanism and/or the means to fully finance them. Shooq is the solution.” Jonathan Rubenstein added: “We can’t afford to keep competing with one another for the same limited resources. We need to come together under one roof, pool our resources, and give our best [Jewish] storytellers the support they need to get impactful projects made to reach audiences around the world. That is what Shooq is designed to do.” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Weaves $3.5 Million In Thursday Previews Trudeau Company; Reviews For ‘Being Heumann’, ‘The Housewife’; Photos Netflix Cancels Josh Duhamel-Minka Kelly Series After Two Seasons ‘Muppet Show’ Special Got Viewership & Emmys – Where’s The Disney+ Series Order? articles.title: Jimmy Kimmel’s Interview With James Talarico Heading to YouTube to Avoid FCC Hassle
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content THR + Sportico: The Sports Issue Uniting the biggest names in Hollywood with the athletic stars they admire most close By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All September 10, 2026 2:48am From left: Jimmy Kimmel, James Talarico and Brendan Carr. Kevin Winter/Getty Images; Rick Kern/Getty Images for Vox Media; Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Jimmy Kimmel ‘s planned Thursday interview with James Talarico will not be aired on the ABC broadcast of Jimmy Kimmel Live! and will instead stream on the late-night show’s YouTube channel. Kimmel made the announcement during his monologue on Wednesday’s episode of his late-night show. Discussing the Texas Senate race, Kimmel said that he would interview Democratic candidate Talarico on Thursday “under unusual circumstances,” and then alluded to ABC’s ongoing issues with the Federal Communications Commission. “You know, for a lot of years, for the whole 20-plus years of our show, in fact, I’ve been interviewing Americans who are running for office with no problem at all, just like Letterman did, Leno did, Arsenio, etc. etc., I’ve interviewed a lot of political candidates. From Hilary Clinton to Ted Cruz to Donald Trump,” Kimmel said. “I interviewed Donald Trump when he was running for president in 2015, and at that time, when he was the one sitting next to me, he seemed to have no problem with the idea of talk show hosts interviewing candidates. In fact, he was very eager to come back for another interview, which he did just before he became the nominee in 2016. But for some reason, and I can’t seem to figure out what that reason is, something has changed.” Related Stories TV No Decisions Made on 'Jimmy Kimmel Live!' Future TV Adele Zaikman on Winning 'DWTS: The Next Pro' and Daniella Karagach's Advice for Season 35 “Now that [Trump is] president, his FCC has threatened me, threatened our show, threatened our network, ABC, our affiliates [and] our local stations based on simple traditional editorial decisions, guest bookings, it would seem, [that] they don’t like,” Kimmel added, referring to ABC’s ongoing battle with the FCC and in particular with the agency’s chair Brendan Carr . In September 2025, in the aftermath of the assassination of Charlie Kirk, Carr condemned Kimmel for comments he made during one of his monologues about Kirk’s death, and the FCC chair intimated that regulatory action or license reviews for ABC affiliates could happen if Kimmel wasn’t made to apologize. After Kimmel was temporarily suspended over the matter, a firestorm engulfed ABC’s owner, Disney. Kimmel became a cause celebre in Hollywood and he was eventually reinstated but that didn’t stop the FCC from continuing to target ABC, Jimmy Kimmel Live! and the daytime talk show The View over claims they didn’t meet the agency’s equal time requirements . In August this year, ABC said it was suing the FCC over the agency’s efforts to challenge its broadcast licenses and the content of The View , saying that it is a free speech violation by the Trump administration. On Wednesday, Kimmel confessed that ABC’s ongoing issues with the FCC meant that the Talarico interview would instead air online. “Out of consideration for our local stations, especially our ABC affiliates in Texas who would have to deal with this nonsense, my interview tomorrow with James Terico will not air on television. It will be posted on YouTube instead. It will not be on TV. So if you want to learn about a candidate for the Senate tomorrow, you will have to go to the Jimmy Kimmel Live! YouTube channel, where you will see it in its entirety. And thank goodness we have that because in the America we live in right now, that is the best that we can do until November.” The latest brouhaha between Jimmy Kimmel Live! and the FCC comes amid speculation that the late night show may come to an end in 2027. On Tuesday, Page Six reported that the long-running ABC talk show would end next year. A source close to Kimmel denied to The Hollywood Reporter there was any truth to the report. This also isn’t the first time an interview with Talarico has caused such consternation on late-night television. In February, Stephen Colbert, the host of the now-ended Late Show , revealed on air that lawyers for CBS blocked him from interviewing Talarico on broadcast, citing the FCC’s new guidance for political candidates on talk shows. The Late Show ran the Talarico interview on its YouTube channel, where it has been viewed 9.5 million times. THR

articles.title: Nat Geo May Have Its Most Beautiful Wildlife Series Yet With ‘Africa Earth’s Wild Home’ — Watch Trailer (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content THR + Sportico: The Sports Issue Uniting the biggest names in Hollywood with the athletic stars they admire most close By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All September 10, 2026 5:00am A fennec fox in the sand dunes of the Sahara desert on 'Africa: Earth's Wild Home.' National Geographic Bless the black rain frogs down in Africa. National Geographic series Africa Earth’s Wild Home has captured the elusive amphibians — and other species — on camera for television for the first time ever. As gross as frogs are, the whole thing looks gorgeous. The Hollywood Reporter can exclusively unveil the trailer for Africa Earth’s Wild Home (below) as well as its premiere date, Oct. 2 at 8 p.m. ET (on National Geographic Channel; it will be available to stream the next day on Disney+ and Hulu). Related Stories Business Nat Geo Turns to Creators in Fresh Digital Push (Exclusive) TV Ryan Reynolds Celebrates Nature's Losers in Nat Geo's 'Underdogs' Trailer (Exclusive) Wunmi Mosaku ( Sinners , Loki , Lovecraft Country ) executive produced and narrated Africa Earth’s Wild Home . The seven-part event series, presented by Rolex, uses “cutting-edge CGI to unearth the deep history and forces that shaped Africa’s natural worlds,” Nat Geo says. Africa Earth’s Wild Home is the beginning of the cable network’s “ambitious multi-year franchise that will document our planet continent by continent, at a moment when that planet is changing faster than ever.” The series took four years to film across nearly 30 countries. In addition to the black rain frog, Africa Earth’s Wild Home also captured hyenas in the Congo hunting elephants at night — bet you haven’t seen that before. There’s also footage of a rare wild African black panther as well as chimpanzees using unique tools to fish for algae. The monkeys sound like they’re about a decade from beginning us. Each episode of Africa Earth’s Wild Home concludes with an “Explorer Spotlight” featuring the scientists, photographers and National Geographic Explorers behind the discoveries — among them are Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorers Steve Boyes, Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka, Matt Shirley and Ingi Agnarsson. (Nat Geo and Rolex have collabed on conservation for more than 70 years.) The event series’ finale switches focus from the wildlife to the humans fighting to protect it. “Africa is home to some of the planet’s most spectacular wildlife and dramatic landscapes, and Africa Earth’s Wild Home captures them through breathtaking, blue-chip landmark natural history storytelling,” said Courteney Monroe, president, National Geographic. “Across seven extraordinary episodes, the series reveals never-before-seen behaviors, explores the forces that shaped the continent and celebrates the remarkable ways life adapts and thrives. It also shines a light on the National Geographic Explorers, scientists and conservationists whose groundbreaking work continues to deepen our understanding of Africa and help safeguard its wild future.” Africa Earth’s Wild Home is produced by BBC Studios Natural History Unit for National Geographic. For BBC Studios NHU, Simon Blakeney is the executive producer. For National Geographic, Pam Caragol is the executive producer, Janet Han Vissering is senior vice president of Production and Development, and Tom McDonald is executive vice president of National Geographic Content. Watch the trailer, below: THR

articles.title: Oscars: Australia Picks ‘First Light’ as International Feature Contender (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content THR + Sportico: The Sports Issue Uniting the biggest names in Hollywood with the athletic stars they admire most close By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All September 10, 2026 5:18am 'First Light' Clou Media Productions Australia has selected James J Robinson’s feature debut First Light as its official submission for the Best International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards, The Hollywood Reporter has learned exclusively. The first-ever Filipino-Australian co-production, First Light is the first Tagalog-language film ever submitted by Australia for the Oscars . The drama follows an elderly nun (played by Brilliante Mendoza regular Ruby Ruiz), whose life has been shaped by discipline, service and belief, who, after a young construction worker dies under suspicious circumstances, gets drawn into a world of crime and corruption. Maricel Soriano, Rez Cortez and Kidlat Tahimik co-star. Related Stories TV 'RuPaul's Drag Race UK' Dropped by BBC Movies Mercedes Ron Discusses Prime Video's New YA Romantic Thriller 'Drawn Together' and What's Next for Her Explaining their decision, the Australian Oscar selection committee called First Light “a meditative work about an aging woman who questions her faith as her world begins to crumble around her, leaving an indelible mark.” Robinson’s feature, they said, was “an impressive debut that is a shining example of Australian filmmaking.” First Light was produced by Gabrielle Pearson of Majella Productions and Christelle Lou Dychangco and Jane Pe Aguirre of Clou Media Productions. The film was released in cinemas in the Philippines by Clou Media Productions, and in Australian cinemas by Bonsai Films. Independent Entertainment are handling international sales. Robinson, a photographer-turned-director, brought his feature debut to the Melbourne Film Festival last year before traveling to Marrakech and the International Film Festival Rotterdam. First Light has been critically-well received, but, lacking a platform at one of the top-tier A-list fests, the film has been largely overlooked in the awards conversation so far. First Light is Australia’s eighteenth submission in the Best International Feature Film category. Only one Australian film, Bentley Dean and Martin Butler’s Tanna (2015) has ever been nominated for the Best International Feature Oscar. To date, no Australian film has ever won. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences will announce the 15 films on the best international feature film shortlist on Dec. 15. The five nominees will be announced Jan. 21, 2027. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony will take place on March 14, 2027. THR
