Jack Quaid isn’t giving up his acting career, but the “Boys” star jokes he’s on his way to becoming a supermodel now that he stars in the Fall 2026 campaign for menswear brand Bonobos. “I guess I can add that to the résumé,” he cracks. The campaign is an episodic video series featuring Quaid in an office setting, where he manages to keep himself — and the Bonobos clothing he’s wearing — together even when thrown some curveballs. Related Stories Arte France’s ‘Tax Me (If You Can)’ Sells to Multiple Territories: ‘Getting Rich People to Talk About Money Was Tough,’ Says Director (EXCLUSIVE) Stefano Knuchel Premieres Final Chapter in 20-Year Hugo Pratt Trilogy With ‘Hugo in Venice’ “I’ve been a fan of the brand for a while now,” Quaid tells me. “I remember wearing a lot of their stuff in the earlier days when they had a brick-and-mortar store near me in L.A. HR keeps rejecting it but that’s what people call me around here because I wear these — the Weekday Warriors,” he says as the camera pans to his pants. “Great-fitting, no-worries work pant. No wrinkles, no hassles.” He goes on to brag that he got others in the office to wear the $119 pants. “But out there,” he says, looking out a window, “there are guys walking around in bad-fitting wrinkly pants that were a ‘great deal’ online — not on my watch.” Future episodes will center on the Weekday Warrior Dress Shirt, Jetsetter Dress Shirt, Everyday Oxford Shirt, Unconstructed Blazer and Knit Blazer. Real Bonobos employees are also featured in the campaign. Quaid admits he wasn’t always one to think about fashion too much. “I’ve come a long way,” he says. “Starting out in like high school, middle school, everything was like a graphic tee with a ‘Family Guy’ quote on it. Nothing against ‘Family Guy,’ but when all of your shirts have a ‘Family Guy’ quote on it, it’s time to maybe have something more basic.” But now, Quaid says, “I consider myself pretty fashionable. I still hang out with a lot of the people I went to high school with, and they’re like, ‘Hey, you dress a lot better than you used to. articles.title: ‘Why Did I Get Married Again?’ Review: Taraji P. Henson Joins the Gang for a Tyler Perry Sequel That Sells the Next Generation Short
articles.full_text: Sep 10, 2026 6:04am PT ‘Why Did I Get Married Again?’ Review: Taraji P. Henson Joins the Gang for a Tyler Perry Sequel That Sells the Next Generation Short Arriving 16 years after 'Why Did I Get Married Too?,' this Netflix release spends too much time reminding viewers why they should be invested in the franchise. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest ‘Company’ Review: Casey Affleck’s Latest Directorial Effort Isn’t What It Initially Appears to Be, but Isn’t Very Interesting Either Way 17 hours ago ‘Bunker’ Review: Javier Bardem and Penélope Cruz Are Brilliant in Florian Zeller’s Riveting, Slightly Overstated Thriller of Isolation and Invasion 2 days ago ‘The Spiral’ Review: Paolo Strippoli’s Lurid Faustian Tragedy Shores Up His Reputation as Italy’s New Horror Virtuoso 3 days ago See All ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection It’s been nearly 20 years since “Why Did I Get Married?”, the original Tyler Perry movie that first introduced these characters and their variously troubled relationships — and 16 years since the sequel to that film, “Why Did I Get Married Too?”. So it feels only normal, at the start of this latest outing for the gang, that we should be treated to some fairly heavy exposition. “ Why Did I Get Married Again ?” certainly doesn’t stint on it: As the film begins, we catch up with fiery Angela ( Tasha Smith ) and her husband Marcus ( Michael Jai White ), a now somewhat cowed figure who has quit his womanizing in practice but kept the macho attitude. The pair are preparing to host a dinner ahead of the marriage of their daughter Jasmine (Armani Greer) to football player Wesley (Everett Osborne), who happens to be the son of their friend Roselyn ( Taraji P. Henson , new to the franchise but treated by all and sundry as if she had been part of the adventure all along). Related Stories How Did the Emmys’ Documentary Category Get So Star-Studded? 'Widow's Bay,' 'DTF: St. Louis' and 'Spider-Noir' — Despite Its Cancellation — Dominate Creative Arts Emmys Night 2 Winners (FULL LIST) Tasha and Marcus have of course invited their old friends from the first two films, Shelley (Jill Scott) and Troy (Lamman Rucker), and Diane (Sharon Leal) and Terry (Tyler Perry), who all have children of their own, in their early twenties. Meanwhile, Shelley’s old troublemaker ex, Mike (Richard T. Jones), turns up for some reason, this time dating a much younger woman who happens to be the ex of Angela and Marcus’s son Marcus Jr. (Da’Vinchi). It seems like an overly convoluted set-up — not least because the younger generation don’t bring much to the film apart from narrative developments that reflect the older generation back to them. So, Marcus Jr. is a hot-headed skirt-chaser like his old man, and Diane and Terry fret that their son T.J. (Jaden Michael) may conversely be a little mild. The film is fundamentally uninterested in the younger people as characters, however, which gives it a strange flavor: The kids constantly provide the (rather thin) action, and the older lot then argue, worry or wryly chuckle about these events, saying things like, “Marcus Jr. is just like you used to be, Marcus.” That is to say, the film’s exposition-speak continues long after its opening scenes, permanently relating to the audience what is happening, who is who, and why it concerns the franchise’s veteran characters. That doesn’t make for very enjoyable watching, and it compounds a tonal problem raised by the multi-generational approach: Where the older characters are cheerfully upfront and confrontational about their problems, the younger people have grown up in a world that sees things differently, and therefore appear bland. You have to feel sorry for Marcus Jr., portrayed as the lone bad egg among the dreary new set, whose greatest sin is trying to get with his spoken-for ex-girlfriend a couple of times, only to get a furious dressing-down from Angela in front of everybody. A lightly macho tone prevails, even as Perry writes a handful of quite sensitive scenes for his female characters, such as Shelley’s fears about her aging mother, or Roselyn’s anguish about her son rejecting her. That leads to a curious scene in which Marcus somehow bests the insanely buff Wesley at weightlifting, which seems like nothing so much as wish-fulfillment — and to an even more curious treatment of the character of T.J., who appears to be written as homosexual without this ever being stated. Stranded in a no-man’s land where everybody deplores toxic masculinity but the guys still need to be given something to do, the film doesn’t manage to contrive any actual fun. Popular on Variety Netflix money oozes from every pore of “Why Did I Get Married Again?,” most visibly when the gang head to Lake Como for the nuptials. The ladies duly appear at brunch in a variety of chic ensembles and statement jewelry, and the wedding itself is suitably plush, but all of this merely adds to the film’s strange detachment from reality — an overstuffed chamber-piece with a tenuous connection to actual life and concerns. Among the performers, Smith rules the roost as the no-nonsense Angela, and Jones acquits himself tolerably on comic relief duties as the pathetic Mike. Henson, apparently acting in another film entirely, gives us a character unable to submit to true love in the face of her perceived duties; alone of all the actors, she gets close to something truthful, but that still sits quite uncomfortably with the ambient tone of woolly half-jokes and that’s-life sermonizing. That spirit finds its most naked expression in a drably conceived scene toward the film’s conclusion, in which the older characters gather in a semi-circle to literally explain everything to the younger generation (who are also seated in a semi-circle). Everybody takes turns to speak their hard truth or life lesson or warm expression of love. A wedding dance scene — interspersed with bloopers to remind you that you have been watching a comedy — caps off proceedings with something like relief, the assignment finally completed. ‘Why Did I Get Married Again?’ Review: Taraji P. articles.title: Amazon’s AWS Now Lets Streamers Deliver up to 11 Live Feeds on One Screen
articles.full_text: Sep 10, 2026 6:18am PT Amazon’s AWS Now Lets Streamers Deliver up to 11 Live Feeds on One Screen By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Trump White House Pulls Down Tetris-Like Game, in Which You Had to Stop a ‘Zombie Siege’ at Mexican Border, After Company’s Copyright Threat 13 hours ago How Netflix Will Use Apple’s iPhone Duo to Deliver a ‘Big-Screen Feeling’ 17 hours ago Newly Discovered Plant-Eating Insects Named After Taylor Swift 19 hours ago See All Courtesy of AWS Personalized multiview livestreams — the ability to watch multiple video feeds on one screen — have become a popular and much-requested feature by customers, particularly for sports. Now AWS , Amazon ‘s cloud-services division, is launching a new service that will let streamers deliver up to 11 feeds in a single personalized channel. On Thursday, AWS took the wraps off new capabilities in its suite of video services: per-viewer dynamic multiview, AI-generated metadata generation to facilitate monetization opportunities based on what’s happening on screen, and automated backfill of unfilled ad inventory. AWS is showcasing the new capabilities at IBC 2026, running Sept. 11-14 in Amsterdam. Related Stories How 'The Pitt' Production Designer Expanded the Emergency Room for Season 2 Martin Short Gets Honest: What It’s Like to Be All Over the Emmy Race, Thanks to Three Very Different Projects The new capabilities will make it possible to deliver “truly personalized live TV,” said Samira Bakhtiar, general manager of telco, media, entertainment, games and sports at AWS. “AWS helped build the streaming era. Now we’re helping to build the intelligence era. Every frame of live video is personalized and understood.” Popular on Variety The new AWS Elemental MediaPackage Dynamic Multiview lets viewers choose their own multi-camera layout from a single set of encoded sources, delivered to any device over standard HTTP Live Streaming (HLS) or Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH) — without per-layout encoding costs India’s JioHotstar is already using the AWS multiview feature to present quad-view features for its coverage of Indian Premier League (IPL) cricket matches. “AWS Elemental MediaPackage Multiview lets us deliver multiple synchronized camera angles within a single stream, putting our subscribers in control of how they experience live sports,” Akash Saxena, CTO of JioHotstar, said in a statement. “The server-side composition approach scales this premium experience to over 100 million viewers without multiplying origin complexity or CDN costs, giving us a true differentiator in India’s competitive OTT landscape.” AWS says that existing approaches to implementing multiview features have forced trade-offs. For example, tiled encoding limits reach to High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC)-capable devices, while client-side compositing demands custom software development kits for each device. Server-side compositing requires pre-encoding every layout combination (each costing as much as a new channel). By contrast, AWS MediaPackage Dynamic Multiview stitches multi-camera and multi-feed layouts on demand from encoded sources, delivered as a single adaptive bitrate stream through HLS or DASH. Sources encode one time through AWS Elemental MediaLive. Then, Elemental MediaPackage assembles layouts in the compressed domain with no reencoding. The output reaches more than 95% of consumer devices with a single digital rights management (DRM) key and requires no SDK, per-device builds, or new vendors, according to AWS. Also being introduced by AWS is Elemental Inference Contextual Metadata, which uses AI to extract metadata from live video in real time. That can then be used to power personalized video experiences and contextual ad decisioning. In addition, the AWS Elemental MediaTailor Yield Optimization capability provides automated backfill of unfilled ad inventory using Amazon Publisher Services (APS) demand, aimed a maximizing ad revenue. The new suite of capabilities also includes AWS Elemental MediaTailor Low-Latency Ad Insertion, which provides personalized ad insertion to low-latency streams using Apple’s HLS interstitials. According to AWS, its cloud services are used by streaming services to nearly 2 billion customers worldwide. Media companies that use AWS include Fox, Amazon MGM Studios, Disney, HBO, NBCUniversal, Sony and Netflix. articles.title: Kayleigh Llewellyn Adapting Sarah Waters Novel ‘The Paying Guests’ For BBC Studios Fiction
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Royal Period Drama ‘Queen Silvia’ To Get World Premiere Screening At MIPCOM Cannes Channel 4 To Combine Drama & Comedy Teams Under Historic Jobs Cull Kayleigh Llewellyn Adapting Sarah Waters Novel ‘The Paying Guests’ For BBC Studios Fiction View All September 10, 2026 2:56am Kayleigh Llewellyn and Sarah Waters Getty, Charlie Hopkinson EXCLUSIVE: Every book in the canon of British author Sarah Waters has been adapted for screen – except one. That’s about to change. Deadline understands BBC Studios Fiction has optioned The Paying Guests , the 2014 book about a 1922 love affair that turns into a twisting crime thriller. We hear In My Skin and Killing Eve writer Kayleigh Llewellyn , who is penning the upcoming BBC series The Dream Lands , is attached to adapt it as a series. No network or streamer is attached at this stage. Here’s the plotline: “Set in London in 1922, The Paying Guests follows Frances Wray and her mother as they take in married lodgers Lilian and Leonard Barber. What begins as a clandestine, intoxicating love affair between Frances and Lilian spirals into a twisting crime thriller, culminating in a brutal murder and a nail‑biting court case.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News BBC Studios Launches High-End Drama Label Led By 'Good Omens' EP Josh Cole News 'Bridgerton's Queen Charlotte Boards BBC's 'The Dream Lands' Waters, who has been shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize and Women’s Prize For Fiction, is one of the most adapted authors working today. Previous adaptations of her books include BBC series Tipping the Velvet and Fingersmith , Andrew Davies’ Affinity , BBC telemovie The Night Watch and Lenny Abrahamson’s feature The Little Stranger . Fingersmith was also the inspiration for Park Chan‑wook’s The Handmaiden . The Paying Guests will join a BBC Studios Fiction slate that includes the upcoming third season of Jimmy McGovern drama Time , which is set in a Young Offenders Institution and stars David Tennant and Siobhan Finneran. BBC Studios Fiction was created last year, as we revealed at the time, with BBC Studios Comedy boss Josh Cole at the top as Chief Creative Officer. The label sits alongside BBC Studios Drama Productions, which makes long-running, continuing and returning series such as Casualty and Silent Witness . Other labels include Trying maker BBC Studios Comedy, Baby Reindeer producer Clerkenwell, Sherwood maker House, Firebird Pictures ( Wahala ), Lookout Point ( Pride and Prejudice ), Baby Cow ( Changing Ends ) and Killing Eve producer Sid Gentle. articles.title: Channel 4 To Merge Unscripted Units, Slashing Commissioning Roles In Half
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Channel 4 To Combine Drama & Comedy Teams Under Historic Jobs Cull Channel 4 To Merge Unscripted Units, Slashing Commissioning Roles In Half ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race UK’ Canceled By BBC Amid “Financial Pressures” View All September 10, 2026 3:30am 'The Great British Bake Off' Channel 4 / Love Productions / Mel Lehmann Channel 4 is planning a significant overhaul of three unscripted commissioning departments as part of the biggest jobs cull in its 43-year history. The British network announced on Wednesday that it would cut 340 jobs — around 28% of its workforce — before the end of the year, with details emerging about where the axe will fall. Channel 4 is planning to merge three of its biggest unscripted units: Documentaries and factual entertainment; reality and entertainment; and specialist factual. These teams are responsible for shows including The Great British Bake Off , Married at First Sight , 24 Hours in Police Custody, and The Piano . Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Channel 4 Confirms Plans To Cut More Than A Quarter Of Its Workforce News International Revenues Of $2.1B Boost British TV Makers, Census Finds, As Pact Warns BBC Must Avoid "Managed Decline" The changes, first reported by Broadcast, will mean around half of commissioning roles are at risk. One source estimated that 16 jobs will become seven. Some people are being offered voluntary redundancy. Channel 4 declined to comment beyond Wednesday’s statement about the layoffs. Channel 4 CEO Priya Dogra said the cuts were aimed at reducing management layers, removing duplication and simplifying decision-making. A person familiar with the changes said they were communicated internally in a “ruthless” way, with staff being told that if they received an email at a certain time, it would inform them that their job was at risk. Insiders are describing the jobs cull as a “watershed” moment for Channel 4, as it grapples with unprecedented competition for viewers and pressure on advertising revenue. Dogra said: “These decisions have not been taken lightly, but I strongly believe they are necessary to create a simpler, more focused and more sustainable Channel 4 that can invest a greater proportion of revenues into distinctive content, back British creativity and deliver impact for audiences long into the future.” Historic Job Cull Will See Mergers In Unscripted & Scripted Divisions Interview With Oscar Winners About Bombshell New Gaza Doc; Reviews ‘Practical Magic 2’ Looks To Cast Post-Summer Spell With $58M-$63M: Preview ‘Charlie’s Angels’ & ‘Buffy’ Reunions In Play As First Presenters Are Revealed Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Blockbuster Summer Pushed UK Cinema Admissions To Pre-Pandemic High In August
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Paul Mescal, Tracy Letts & Uzo Aduba Among Names Set For National Theatre Productions In 2027 John Malkovich Cancels 2027 Tel Aviv Show & Says Producers Fabricated Quotes About The Performance Damilola Orimogunje On Making Venice Giornate History & Prioritizing African Distribution With His Sophomore Feature ‘Dear Ajayi’ View All September 10, 2026 3:45am Matt Damon, Charlize Theron in 'The Odyssey' Universal Cinema admissions across the UK in August surpassed 17 million, a 56 per cent increase on the same month in 2025, according to new figures collected by the UK Cinema Association. The official figures for August were 17,000,838. That makes August 2026 the second-biggest month since the pandemic and the biggest August since 2018. The largest post-pandemic month is still July 2023, thanks to the Barbenheimer craze. The bulk of these admissions can be attributed to the summer’s two massive box office hits, Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey, which has hit £89m in the UK, and Spider-Man: Brand New Day , which has a £77m cume in the UK. Related Stories News Imax Tops $600M In Q3 Box Office So Far On 'The Odyssey'; CEO Shrugs Off Industry M&A - "Our Primary Relationships Are With Filmmakers" News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Pushes Summer To Record $4.76B; Universal Wins Season With $1.23B - Labor Day Box Office Update The UK figures are in line with bumper numbers across Europe. Earlier this week, Gower Street and the International Union of Cinemas reported that box office stats across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) increased 88% year-on-year as the global box office passed $4 billion. Watch on Deadline In August, France recorded 19.9 million admissions, the best figure recorded in the country during August since monthly records began in 1980 and twice the level of the same month in 2025. In Italy , cinemas enjoyed their best-ever June-August period, with 20.8 million admissions and €162.3 million in box office receipts. That is the strongest August ever recorded in the country. Gower Street also reported significant year-on-year increases across markets, including Spain (+71%) and the Netherlands (+77%). UNIC ’s report similarly credited international blockbusters such as Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey for the big summer figures, alongside successful local productions, including the French two-part drama De Gaulle, the German comedy Steckerlsfischfiasko , and the Spanish family franchise Tadeo Jones 4 . articles.title: ‘No Other Land’ Co-Directors Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor Lift Lid On New Bombshell Doc ‘Naza’ Exposing Israel’s Deliberate Targeting Of Civilian Homes In Gaza – Venice
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Ellen Burstyn Talks Working Into 90s with Starring Role In Unexpected Love Story ‘Place To Be’; Pays Tribute To Gloria Steinem – Venice First Behind-The Scenes Look Reveals Isabelle Huppert As Crime Boss In Yann Demange’s London-Set ‘Lineage’ LevelK Posts U.S. & Euro Sales Haul For Karlovy Vary Prizewinner ‘The Guest’ View All September 10, 2026 4:10am Naza The Guardian/JW Films Oscar-winning Israeli directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor hit the Venice Film Festival on Thursday with bombshell late competition addition Naza . Based on interviews with 24 Israeli intelligence officers and soldiers, the documentary exposes the AI, phone surveillance and crude points-based systems deployed by the Israeli military in Gaza to decide targets, Hamas-related or otherwise, and then take them out in their homes regardless of whether children and other family members are likely to be killed in the strike as well. The title Naza is taken from the Israeli military’s Hebrew acronym to describe each individual that could die when tallying up an estimated death-toll ahead of a strike. Related Stories News Elon Musk Embarks On Vicious Rant About "Bitter Old Man" Alex Gibney & Threatens To Sue Over 'Musk' Documentary Festivals 'DAU': First Teaser From Ilya Khrzhanovsky's Epic Venice Competition Title The film also contains allegations that Israel is systematically destroying homes in Gaza to create a wasteland that will prevent Palestinians from ever returning, and also deliberately taking out figures from civil society such as journalists and medical staff. Watch on Deadline It follows and builds on Abraham and Szor’s No Other Land , winner of the Best Documentary Academy Award in 2025, co-directed with Palestinian filmmakers Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal, documenting Israeli army-backed efforts to erase the West Bank Palestinian villages of Masafer Yatta, while painting a wider picture of Israeli occupation. “Our film is showing that the basic targeting unit of the Israeli targeting systems is a family home in Gaza,” Abraham told Deadline ahead of the world premiere. “That’s how it operates. Every building in Gaza, every home in Gaza has a number. The system is designed to locate targets. When they are in civilian spaces, when they go back home, that is one of, for me, one of the most striking revelations of the film. A revelation, of course, that I think should have been known to people by the fact that they should have listened to Palestinians in Gaza who are saying it. But to hear it from the inside for me was quite striking.” The world premiere comes amid growing condemnation of Israel’s military campaign in the Palestinian territory – sparked by Hamas’s slaughter of 1,200 people in Southern Israel on October 7, 2023 – which has since killed more than 73,000 people and injured close to 175,000 others, while destroying key infrastructure and 90% of homes. The film is based on investigative reporting carried out by Abraham in the wake of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks and the launch of Israel’s retaliatory military campaign on October 27 of that same year, the findings of which were previously published by The Guardian, which is a producer on the film, and Israeli news outlets +972 and Local Call. “I had spent time already before October 7 with +972 magazine and Local Call, and later with The Guardian, investigating the Israeli military, the Israeli targeting systems, Israel’s reliance on AI, on big data and mass surveillance of Palestinians,” he said, explaining how he had managed to connect with the interviewees in the film through a network built across years. Co-director Szor, who is also cinematographer on the film, kept a low media profile during the festival run and awards campaign for No Other Land , but joins Abraham in the interviews for Naza in Venice. “It’s true with No Other Land , I was not vocal, it’s just my personality,” said Szor, when quizzed on how their partnership works. “As directors, we just talk about everything, what exactly are we looking for; the questions that need to be asked… the structure, what story we will tell, and then, cinematically, where will we film the interviews and what else will we show beyond the interviews,” she explained. The anonymous silhouetted testimonies at the heart of the film are framed as rooftop interviews against the nighttime skyline of Tel Aviv, which aside from being one of the most liberal cities in the world is also the beating heart of Israel’s military apparatus and home to its HaKirya HQ. The physical appearances and voices of the interviewees have been altered to hide their identities. “As you can imagine, we went through a very rigorous process with The Guardian’s investigations desk which is an expert in that field… we’ve taken extraordinary measures,” said Abraham of the efforts to protect his sources, adding the aim was also to ensure the interviews did not come over as “robotic” as a result. “That was important for us because we wanted the testimonies to land and to be impactful,” he explains, highlighting that the anonymized interviewees are real people and not actors voicing transcripts. The testimonies are chilling, with multiple interviewees explaining they are part of a system that they are powerless to challenge, evoking unspoken references to Adolf Eichman, who managed the logistics of the Holocaust, and Hannah Arendt’s coverage of his trial in Jerusalem in which she coined the phrase “banality of evil”. “It’s something that came up from some of the soldiers themselves. It’s one of the things that surprised me. Of course, I think about Second World War and the Holocaust, and I think our obligation is to draw universal lessons from that, because when we say never again, how can we say that if we are not drawing the universal lessons, the universal opposition to dehumanization, to turning people into numbers,” said Abraham. “I was surprised how much soldiers themselves sometimes, not all of them, but some of them, spoke about it too. I mean we have a soldier in the film who talks about how after being involved in the killing of so many civilians and seeing their humanity kind of evaporate, he thought about German society in the 30s and the 40s. He felt he could understand something about that, that he couldn’t understand before.” “To me, in a world where so many people use the memory of the Holocaust in a way to justify what is happening in Gaza, and it is important to think about how can we draw from that period of time to oppose dehumanization, to oppose killing, no matter who the person is being killed, and that’s not to say that it’s the same, but it is to say that we are finding these similarities that exist throughout many cases of genocide.” In between the interview segments, the documentary cuts to footage of the aftermath of Israeli strikes in Gaza as family members desperately try to dig out victims from underneath collapsed buildings, as well as shots into Tel Aviv homes as people serenely go about their lives in the evening. Asked if this was meant as a deliberate parallel between the lives of people living in Tel Aviv and those in Gaza, some 40 miles to the south, Abraham says it goes beyond that and is more a comment on Israel’s bombing of civilian homes on the basis of intelligence that a person of interest is present. “Our film shows, it could have been someone selected by AI, it would have been someone who the army decides is somehow related to Hamas, it could have been someone that they targeted for other reasons, the mere fact they are physically present in a building, where there is no military activity, justifies bombing the building and killing everyone inside,” said Abraham. “If you apply these kinds of standards to any place in the world, and especially Tel Aviv, that gives you an endless stream of justifications to bomb pretty much any civilian building, any shopping mall, any cinema… Houses are not bombed because Hamas are firing rockets from them, which is what we’ve consistently heard from intelligence officers. The houses are bombed because it’s easier to bomb people and to find them when they go home to sleep at night.” Asked on how he got military personnel to speak so candidly, Abraham suggests he filled a void, with his quest helped by the lack of coverage of what was going on in Gaza in Israel’s mainstream media. “Mainstream Israeli media is totally uninterested in asking these questions, in asking soldiers about the actions that they’ve done, which have contributed to the mass killing of Palestinian civilians. A polite way to say it, would be to say that they ignored the atrocities in Gaza. But if I’m being honest, it’s not that they ignored it; it’s that they very often created the justification and normalized very genocidal, very scary ideas about the population in Gaza, and I really think they bear some of the responsibility for what happens,” he said. “When you operate as an Israeli journalist in a space where the majority of the mainstream kind of legacy Israeli media are not asking these questions, then you have an advantage because when you start asking these questions, then slowly… you find the answers,” he continued. Abraham says mainstream channels could equally connect with the subjects in his film, and confirm the revelations in Naza, but suggests they will not because in his view they are “complicit in the killing”. Digging into that allegation he suggests that while a handful of Israeli news outlets such as Haaretz and +972 Magazine have been critical of the military campaign in Gaza they are the exception to the rule. “The majority of the society watches the TV channels: Channel 13, Channel 12, Channel 11,” said Abraham, citing Israeli research into local TV coverage of the military campaign in Gaza. “In the first six months of the onslaught in Gaza, this period of time when about 10,000 children are being killed by Israel, Channel 12, the mainstream Israeli channel, dedicated less than 0.5% of its news items and news coverage to talk about the civilian casualties in Gaza… there are journalists far more talented than us in Israel that have been asking these questions, but the majority of the media has ignored, justified, incited, and therefore is partially responsible, I think, for the killing in Gaza.” As the film debuts in Venice both directors hope the exploration of Abraham’s previously published findings will travel wider on the big screen. “There is something different about seeing it on screen and seeing people talking about it from reading it, so hopefully it will have a big impact. It will reach more people. I think we’re also using our privileges because we’ve done No Other Land , and it reached Oscar. That also was for us just a motivation to make another film because we hope that it will reach a big stage,” said Szor. “It’s weird to be in a festival with this kind of film, which is so heavy and on such a hard topic, but it’s very important to show it in the biggest stage there is.” Historic Job Cull Will See Mergers In Unscripted & Scripted Divisions Interview With Oscar Winners About Bombshell New Gaza Doc; Reviews ‘Practical Magic 2’ Looks To Cast Post-Summer Spell With $58M-$63M: Preview ‘Charlie’s Angels’ & ‘Buffy’ Reunions In Play As First Presenters Are Revealed Read More About: Comments

articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Wicked’ & ‘Wicked: For Good’ Live-To-Film Concerts To Kick Off 2027 Tour In San Francisco & New York ‘Disclosure Day’ Release Date Set At Peacock Anthropic Researcher Jacob Coxon Resigns, Warns AI Industry Is “Gambling With Our Lives” View All April 30, 2026 7:26am John Legend Alberto Rodriguez/Variety via Getty Images UPDATE, with production dates : Imitation of Life , the new musical with a book by Lynn Nottage , music and lyrics by John Legend , and direction by Liesl Tommy will begin performances on Wednesday, September 9, at The Griffin Theater at The Shed Off Broadway . A co-production of The Shed and National Black Theatre, Imitation of Life will play a strictly limited four- week presentation engagement through Sunday, October 4. In the announcement today, the production was described as The Shed’s “first major step in nurturing and developing a new American musical. The musical will be performed with full cast and live orchestra. Related Stories News Alex Winter Bringing Arthur Miller's 'Incident At Vichy' Revival To Off Broadway Next Year News Sophia Anne Caruso To Star In Duncan Sheik's 'Memoirs Of Amorous Gentlemen' Stage Musical Adaptation Additional details including casting, design and creative team members will be announced at a later date. Watch on Deadline PREVIOUS, February 12: A new stage adaptation of the Fannie Hurst novel Imitation of Life , featuring music and lyrics by Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony Award winner John Legend and a book by Pulitzer Prize winner Lynn Nottage, will premiere at the Off Broadway venue The Shed this coming fall, producers announced today. Liesl Tommy ( Eclipsed ) will direct. The Shed staging at its Griffin Theater is a co-production with National Black Theatre. Additional details for the limited engagement including casting, design and creative teams and production dates will be announced at later. The musical is based on both the 1933 novel and the famed 1934 and 1959 Universal Pictures adaptations. The ’33 film directed by John M. Stahl starred Claudette Colbert, Louise Beavers, Fredi Washington and Rochelle Hudson; Douglas Sirk’s 1959 version starred Lana Turner, Juanita Moore, Sandra Dee and Susan Kohner. The synopsis: “ Imitation of Life follows two single mothers, one Black and one White, as well as their daughters, who build a shared life while each strives for success and love in a society divided by race and class. Set across the vibrant backdrop of 1920s Atlantic City and 1930s New York, this new, profoundly moving musical explores themes of identity, the American Dream, and what we leave for future generations.” In a joint statement, Nottage, Legend and Tommy said today: “Originally published in 1933, novelist Fannie Hurst’s Imitation of Life tells the story of two women, one Black and one white, struggling to raise their daughters in a world shaped by inequalities. While the novel’s narrative is very much a product of its time, its themes of race, class, and gender in America continue to resonate today. As artists, we are drawn to Imitation of Life ’s enduring emotional power and its potential to be reimagined in ways that feel both contemporary and urgent. It has been a profound joy to collaborate on bringing this story to the stage, and we are thrilled to premiere this musical at The Shed, where we look forward to sharing the beautiful and deeply moving journey of Delilah and Peola Johnston with audiences.” The project marks Legend’s first major musical stage endeavor as a composer. He was a producer on both Ain’t Too Proud in 2019 and Jitney in 2017, and contributed the song “(I Guess I) Miss You” to SpongeBob SquarePants in 2017. articles.title: Channel 4 To Combine Drama & Comedy Teams Under Historic Jobs Cull
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter , Jesse Whittock September 10, 2026 4:40am Brenda Blethyn in Channel 4 series 'A Woman of Substance' Banijay Rights/The Forge/Channel 4 EXCLUSIVE : Channel 4 will merge its drama and comedy commissioning units as the UK network seeks to cut its workforce by more than a quarter over the coming months. Channel 4 will create a new scripted commissioning team, which sources said would more closely resemble the set-up at major U.S. networks and streamers. Film4 will not be part of the changes. Channel 4 is putting around half of commissioning roles at risk, though it is not clear exactly how jobs will be impacted in the drama and comedy teams. The network will close a total of 340 jobs before the end of the year, which is equivalent to 28% of its workforce. It is the biggest round of layoffs in Channel 4’s 43-year history. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Channel 4 To Merge Unscripted Units, Slashing Commissioning Roles In Half News Channel 4 Confirms Plans To Cut More Than A Quarter Of Its Workforce Channel 4’s new scripted unit will be responsible for shows including A Woman of Substance , Big Boys , and Derry Girls . Drama commissioning is led by interim chief Gwawr Lloyd following Ollie Madden’s departure to Netflix last year. Channel 4 comedy is overseen by Charlie Perkins. The change mirrors work in unscripted , where Channel 4 is planning to bring together three units: Documentaries and factual entertainment; reality and entertainment; and specialist factual. “It makes sense after being resisted for years,” said a respected drama producer. A second producer added that there is increasing cross-pollination between the genres, with writers like Succession and Peep Show creator Jesse Armstrong occupying a space somewhere between comedy and drama. Channel 4 declined to comment beyond Wednesday’s statement about the layoffs. CEO Priya Dogra said the cuts were aimed at putting more money on screen by reducing management layers, removing duplication and simplifying decision-making. A person familiar with the changes said they were communicated internally in a “ruthless” way, with staff being told that if they received an email at a certain time, it would inform them that their job was at risk. Insiders are describing the jobs cull as a “watershed” moment for Channel 4, as it grapples with unprecedented competition for viewers and pressure on advertising revenue. Dogra said: “These decisions have not been taken lightly, but I strongly believe they are necessary to create a simpler, more focused and more sustainable Channel 4 that can invest a greater proportion of revenues into distinctive content, back British creativity and deliver impact for audiences long into the future.” Historic Job Cull Will See Mergers In Unscripted & Scripted Divisions Interview With Oscar Winners About Bombshell New Gaza Doc; Reviews ‘Practical Magic 2’ Looks To Cast Post-Summer Spell With $58M-$63M: Preview ‘Charlie’s Angels’ & ‘Buffy’ Reunions In Play As First Presenters Are Revealed Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Final Fantasy VII Revelation’ Game Director Naoki Hamaguchi On Taking Risks With Beloved Characters: “One Wrong Decision” Could Get Him “Shouted At”; Teases TV Show Potential
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Destiny Jackson Destiny Jackson Crafts Editor, Awards @DestinyDreadful More Stories By Destiny ‘Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival’ Video Game Devs On Making The Franchise “Nobly Provocative” In The Modern Age ‘Saw: Genesis’ Creative Director Talks Multiplayer Build, Expanding The ‘Saw’ Mythology & Putting Players Through The Wringer Emmys Night 2 Craft Awards Predict Smooth Sailing For ‘Widow’s Bay’ Alongside Celebrating ‘The Pitt’ & ‘DTF St. Louis’ View All September 10, 2026 5:00am Final Fantasy VII Revelation Square Enix Looks like those seven seconds are coming to an end. At Gamescom 2026, Final Fantasy VII Revelation offered a glimpse at the enormous final chapter of Square Enix ’s remake trilogy, which concludes Cloud and his activist friends’ journey as they race against time to stop Sephiroth, who is close to attaining god status in his quest to harm the planet. The preview dropped us into Chapter 4 aboard Cid’s iconic Highwind aerial ship with Yuffie, Barret, Cait Sith and Vincent, as the group explores the islands for resources or makes a beeline for Wutai, which has been significantly expanded for the finale. Meanwhile, Tifa and an unwell Cloud remain separated from the group, leaving the rest of the party to chart their own course through a world that has grown considerably since Rebirth . Related Stories News Mory Sacko Prepares 'Food Samurai' For Disney+ North America News 'Kane Chronicles' Live-Action Series In Development At Disney+ For Square Enix game director Naoki Hamaguchi , who has guided the project through Final Fantasy VII Remake and Rebirth , that expansion is one of the biggest challenges—and opportunities—of the finale. The Highwind opens the skies, while flying chocobos and parachuting offer new ways to traverse familiar territory. Junon bears the brunt of Weapons’ attacks in defense of the planet, parts of Gongaga have been flooded, and the grasslands look remarkably different from above. Watch on Deadline After Remake ’s more linear structure and Rebirth ’s open-world expansion, Revelation takes that scale to a planet-wide level. Hamaguchi said the Highwind provides “a feeling that no other open-world game gives,” while Mai and the game’s side content help guide players through the sprawling landscape without making exploration too stressful. During the timed playthrough (and despite all the exploratory distractions), I caught a hopeful glimpse of a finale geared towards delving deeper into the lore of its iconic cast of characters. Hamaguchi told Deadline that the team painstakingly cemented Vincent and Yuffie into irrevocable mainstays while also giving Zack (not available in my preview) an increasingly important role in the trilogy’s larger time-boggling mystery. Below, Deadline spoke further with Hamaguchi about bringing the ambitious remake project to its conclusion, expanding its world and characters, Cloud’s emotional journey, and whether Final Fantasy VII could eventually leap to television. DEADLINE: This is it. You’re in the process of finalizing one of the biggest remake projects of a legendary game for Square Enix. What is the general vibe and emotionality going through your minds right now at headquarters? NAOKI HAMAGUCHI: As you say, it is a legendary game. It’s so well-loved by so many people out there, with really high expectations, and I’m remaking that. And in doing the final work, it’s really setting in that we’re about to release the climax. There’s a feeling of great satisfaction, and I’m feeling that now. I can still remember when we put out Final Fantasy VII Rebirth ; the big challenge with that game was that we wanted to take that classic Final Fantasy feel and bring it into an open-world structure. And I think we felt that we did that really well, and thankfully, there was a very positive reaction to that. So, with Revelation , what we’ve tried to do is take that even further and expand out. And it sits on a planet-level open world, with verticality, and the whole environment is now available for adventure. And I’m very confident that we’ve done that. And really, there’s no open world out there at this scale in any other game. Final Fantasy VII Revelation Square Enix DEADLINE: With that said, I know Final Fantasy VII Remake faced backlash for being too linear. Then Rebirth opened up a lot as you’ve stated. And now this one’s even bigger. Are you worried about an unwieldy narrative or fans’ response to this? HAMAGUCHI: Whatever kind of game you’re making, you can have 100 people and show them the game; you’re never going to get anything where all 100 of them like it. There’ll always be someone who doesn’t like it, who complains about it. You can’t reduce those voices to nothing, so we don’t even try. What’s important is that you have a solid concept and do your best to achieve it. With Revelation , I really am confident that we managed to do that. So, again, you guys played the demos and had this experience, but that feeling of just the size of the world and that scale of open world, when you get up in the Highwind and you set out into the skies, I don’t think there’s any other open-world game out there that will give you that feeling. So, I want to share that feeling with as many people as possible and show what we’ve achieved here. DEADLINE: Does this mean we can expect the chicken with the tin can in Gongaga to appear again? HAMAGUCHI: No, I was thinking about what to do with that for a long time. We’ve taken a slightly different approach [laughs]. But we’ve got a lot of quests like that, with that distinctive Final Fantasy humor in it. Look forward to loads of that. Final Fantasy VII Revelation Square Enix DEADLINE: Who was the character you understood more by the end of the game’s journey? HAMAGUCHI: Vincent and Yuffie because they were two characters in the original who were optional characters. And because of that, they weren’t featured within the main story as strongly as all the other cast. So, as a very conscious decision for the Remake series, they’ve been made compulsory parts of the team, and they’ve really been fleshed out more and given the background and the deeper dive into them as characters. So, I think those are probably the two the fans will appreciate most and that have been fleshed out the most. Also, Zack is the other one because he plays a very interesting role in the story’s setup. He gives the impression of, “Well, this is the [game] differences, this is what is going on.” Similarly to Rebirth , in terms of showing not telling, he will also have a role like that in Revelation . So players can very much expect to see a lot more of Zack and dig even deeper into him. He plays a very massive part in this last finale of the series. DEADLINE: Which character then was the most difficult to flesh out and bring to the forefront? HAMAGUCHI: That’s a tough question. In some ways, Zack was quite a difficult one. Because first of all, he’s quite well covered in terms of background material from the compilation. There’s a lot of information about him where he features quite heavily, so there’s stuff we have to include. And at the same time, the way he’s used in the story, he’s part of that very special metaphysical phenomenon that’s going on. So, how he’s portrayed in that, and how he interacts with others and the environment, have to be handled very carefully so that we don’t give too much away. Getting that balance right with Zack was hard, especially in adding more detail about him. But thinking about this question again, and all the characters, they’ve got really dedicated fans. You make one wrong decision for any of them, I’m probably going to get shouted at by a lot of people [laughs]. So, I think picking one as more difficult than the others is quite difficult in itself. DEADLINE: In the preview’s Chapter 4, Cloud is already suffering from mako poisoning. But it was interesting to me that Mai mentions the Lifesprings may be involved in restoring or improving his mental state? What can you tell us about this new development? My boy is suffering. HAMAGUCHI: So first of all, everyone wants to enjoy that in the game. I want you to enjoy that in the game. The best way to experience that is by not telling you. I can’t tell you [laughs]. But what I will tell you is that, like in any film, any really good film, you’ll get the rhythm of things, the ups and downs of the story and how [the story] progresses like that. And in terms of that rhythm in Revelation , that was one of the areas we put so much care and attention into the story of how Cloud finds himself and recovers and gets his sanity back. Some of the voice actors have said in interviews that there’s so much emotional payback in that scene, and everyone’s going to have so many complicated emotions about the really beautiful scene. And it was the English voice actors who said that if you didn’t cry in Rebirth , you’re going to cry in Revelation . So that’s why I really wanted people [at the demos] to see and experience that as soon as possible. Final Fantasy VII Revelation Square Enix DEADLINE: Looking ahead to 2027, it’s going to be a big year for Square Enix between Kingdom Hearts IV and Final Fantasy VII Revelation . But I’m thinking more specifically about Tetsuya Nomura going to D23 and the announcement of the Kingdom Hearts animated series for Disney+ . Does Final Fantasy VII lend itself to a TV series adaptation? HAMAGUCHI: In terms of Square Enix and 2027, our President, Takashi Kiryu, says that next year is the big fight back for us, where everything turns around. And obviously, between Final Fantasy VII Revelation and Kingdom Hearts IV , those are massive titles that are going to push that. And both are being developed in my own studio, Creative Studio 1. So yeah, I’m really pumped up now for that. That’s really all on my watch now, so I’m going to be the guy who’s pushing all that forward. But in terms of adaptations, even a live-action adaptation or an animated adaptation, we’re always thinking that these properties, things like, again, Kingdom Hearts , Final Fantasy VII … not just Final Fantasy VII , even just Remake . Across all of the Final Fantasy properties and IPs, we’re always looking for the best way to bring them to the audience and for opportunities like this with them. So yeah, it’s definitely a possibility. We want to be very proactive in looking into opportunities like that. Final Fantasy VII Revelation will release on April 8, 2027 simultaneously on PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, Steam and Epic Games. articles.title: Royal Period Drama ‘Queen Silvia’ To Get World Premiere Screening At MIPCOM Cannes
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Channel 4 To Combine Drama & Comedy Teams Under Historic Jobs Cull Kayleigh Llewellyn Adapting Sarah Waters Novel ‘The Paying Guests’ For BBC Studios Fiction ‘Love Island’ Star Arabella Chi Signs With Rizzo The Agency View All September 10, 2026 5:03am 'Queen Silvia' Becker Films, Amazon, Joyn, Pyjama Pictures EXCLUSIVE: Queen Silvia , the Prime Video and ProSiebenSat.1 period drama, will have a world premiere at MIPCOM Cannes. The Pyjama Pictures and Unlimited Stories drama, inspired by the real-life romance of Sweden’s Queen Silvia and King Carl Gustaf, will screen on Tuesday, October 13 at 6pm local time at the Grand Auditorium at the Palais des Festivals. It will be open to the public with English and French subtitles. Per the show synopsis, the audience will discover “the remarkable story of a young German woman whose chance encounter with Sweden’s future king would change the course of both their lives – and ultimately see her become not only Queen of Sweden, but one of Europe’s most recognizable and enduring royal icons.” Related Stories News 'Maxton Hall' Uses Amazon AI Technology To Sync Actors' Lips With Human-Dubbed Audio Books International Disruptors: 'My Fault' Author Mercedes Ron On Building A Romance Empire, Taking Her IP To Hollywood & Hopes For Fourth 'Culpables' Adaptation Queen Silvia is set across Munich, Stockholm and the French Riviera, and follows German-Brazilian interpreter Silvia Sommerlath (Alicia von Rittberg) and Sweden’s young Crown Prince, Carl Gustaf (Edvin Endre), from their first meeting until their engagement four years later. Their paths cross during the 1972 Olympic Games in Munich, and what begins as an unexpected romance develops into an impossible love that must navigate public scrutiny, royal tradition, and the expectations of the Swedish monarchy. Watch on Deadline The screening of the first episode will be followed by a Q&A featuring von Rittberg ( Charité ), Endre ( Eddie the Eagle ), showrunner Carsten Kelber, director Miguel Alexandre ( Sisi ) and Beta Film ’s Justus Riesenkampff. We revealed news of the show back in March, with Prime Video on board for rights in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and the Nordics and Nordics and German free-TV broadcaster SAT.1 also attached, with Beta handling international sales. The director, Alexandre, also co-wrote the screenplay together with Lisa Hofer ( Black Island ), with the pair serving as head writers, alongside Pauline Wolff ( Stockholm Requiem ). Exec producers are Tina Ermuth, Frank Buchs, Kelber, Emil Wiklund, Manya Lutz-Moneim and Riesenkampff. Pia Lüke, Tim Bahalou, and Frida Wallman are the producers, and Jallo Faber is the director of photography. The series is supported by German Motion Picture Fund, Medienboard Berlin Brandenburg, and FilmFörderung Bayern. “This love story is relevant and one of a kind, and, surprise, it does not follow a Cinderella narrative,” said Kelber, who leads the SevenOne.Studios-owned Pyjama alongside Buchs. “Instead, it has a very modern take on relationship and marriage – depicting the lead character Queen Silvia who was way ahead of her time. And here we are, half a century later, which best describes how epic this couple is.” Justus Riesenkampff, EVP Nordics & Benelux for Beta added: “ Queen Silvia is ultimately a story about love and identity – about a young woman entering a royal world she never sought to be part of, staying true to herself and ultimately winning the hearts of a nation.” “The premiere will give audiences in Cannes the opportunity to experience this highly anticipated new drama on the big screen, while also showcasing the series to the international television community gathered at the market,” said Lucy Smith, Director of MIPCOM Cannes . “We’re particularly pleased to open the screening to the public, bringing this compelling royal story to audiences both within and beyond the MIPCOM Cannes delegate community.” Historic Job Cull Will See Mergers In Unscripted & Scripted Divisions Interview With Oscar Winners About Bombshell New Gaza Doc; Reviews ‘Practical Magic 2’ Looks To Cast Post-Summer Spell With $58M-$63M: Preview ‘Charlie’s Angels’ & ‘Buffy’ Reunions In Play As First Presenters Are Revealed Read More About: Comments

In Europe, it has been acquired for Benelux (September Film Distribution), France Nour Films, Greece (Cinobo), Italy (I Wonder Pictures), UK and Ireland (Altitude), Spain (Filmin, Elastica), Germany and Austria (PIFFL), Hungary (Mozinet Ltd) and Poland ( Cinobo), while Aardwolf has taken rights for Airlines. Watch on Deadline The film is adapted from Sarah Leavitt’s graphic memoir Tangles: A Story About Alzheimer’s, My Mother and Me , retelling her experiences after her feisty, beloved mother developed Alzheimer’s. It follows her family’s bewilderment as the mother’s personality inexplicably begins to change ahead of a diagnosis. Sarah then puts her life as an activist and artist in 1990s San Francisco on hold to return to her small hometown to spend time with mother as her mind fragments. The film – featuring Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Seth Rogen, Abbi Jacobson and Samira Wiley in voice cast, enjoyed a buzzy world premiere as a Special Screening in Cannes , and also went on to play in Annecy . It is produced by Vicky Patel, Steve Barnett and Alan Powell of Monarch Media; Rogen, Evan Goldberg, James Weaver, Alex McAtee and Madeline Blair of Point Grey Pictures; Ross Murray, Teresa Toews through director Nelson and Jay Grandin’s Giant Ant Films; Lauren Miller Rogen, Jen Ray and Sophie Hoegh through LYLAS Pictures; and Louis-Dreyfus. Charades is handing international sales, with CAA Media Finance , and they are co-repping North American and Global sales. articles.title: ‘& Juliet’ To Close In January After Four Years On Broadway
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Wicked’ & ‘Wicked: For Good’ Live-To-Film Concerts To Kick Off 2027 Tour In San Francisco & New York ‘Disclosure Day’ Release Date Set At Peacock Anthropic Researcher Jacob Coxon Resigns, Warns AI Industry Is “Gambling With Our Lives” View All September 10, 2026 6:00am '& Juliet' on Broadway Matthew Murphy & Juliet , the Broadway dance-pop jukebox musical that imagines Shakespeare’s Romeo and Juliet if Juliet hadn’t ended it all after Romeo, will play its final performance on Sunday, January 3, 2027, more than four years after it opened at the Stephen Sondheim Theatre. At its closing, the musical will have played 1,723 regular performances and 20 preview performances, making it one of the 50 longest-running Broadway musicals of all time. Nominated for nine Tony Awards including Best Musical, & Juliet was created by David West Read and features a playlist of hit songs from writer-producer Max Martin including “Since U Been Gone,” “Roar,” “I Want It That Way,” “Confident,” and more. The production is directed by Luke Sheppard with choreography by Jennifer Weber. Related Stories News 'Harry Potter And The Cursed Child' Posts Big Gain As Summer Slips Away - Broadway Box Office News Julia Roberts, Paul Rudd & Sarah Paulson Set Broadway Return In Bess Wohl's 'Small Mouth Sounds' From Producers Scott Rudin & Barry Diller After opening on Broadway on November 17, 2022, & Juliet broke multiple box office records at the Stephen Sondheim Theatre, recouping its $17 million capitalization in 2024, the first new musical of its season to do so. Producers say the production has grossed more than $175 million. Watch on Deadline Last week, & Juliet took in $779,070, a decent amount if not a match for the $1 million-plus grosses of its peak years. Attendance was at about 90% of the Sondheim’s capacity. The Broadway production’s long success though has spurred tours that have played in 73 US cities, nine countries and four continents, producers said. The show currently stars Gianna Harris as ‘Juliet,’ Paulo Szot and Joey Fatone as ‘Lance,’ Alison Luff as ‘Anne,’ Corey Mach as ‘Shakespeare,’ Michael Iván Carrier as ‘May,’ Chrissy Metz as ‘Angélique,’ Ben Jackson Walker as ‘Romeo,’ and Makai Hernandez as ‘François.’ “From the very beginning, & Juliet has been winning over audiences and critics alike, shattering every stereotype about jukebox musicals to deliver a smart, funny, heartfelt story – all while sparking true joy in everyone who sees it,” producers Theresa Steele Page and Eva Price said. “We’re incredibly proud of the run we’ve had on Broadway, and the story of inclusion, acceptance and second chances we’ve been able to share with more than 1.5 million people in our four years on Broadway.” & Juliet is produced on Broadway by Max Martin, Tim Headington, Theresa Steele Page, Jenny Petersson, Martin Dodd and Eva Price. articles.title: Adrienne Warren To Star In ‘Imitation Of Life’ Off Broadway Musical With John Legend Score
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Wicked’ & ‘Wicked: For Good’ Live-To-Film Concerts To Kick Off 2027 Tour In San Francisco & New York ‘Disclosure Day’ Release Date Set At Peacock Anthropic Researcher Jacob Coxon Resigns, Warns AI Industry Is “Gambling With Our Lives” View All September 10, 2026 6:00am Adrienne Warren Production Adrienne Warren is set to star in the previously announced Off Broadway musical adaptation of Imitation of Life , the Fannie Hurst novel that spawned two classic Hollywood films. Warren will play Delilah, the role played by Louise Beavers in the 1934 film and by Juanita Moore in Douglas Sirk’s 1959 remake (the character was called Annie in that version). The musical features a book by two-time Pulitzer Prize winner Lynn Nottage, an original score by EGOT winner John Legend and direction by double Tony nominee Whitney White (taking over for the previously announced Liesl Tommy, who remains a producer). Related Stories News Alex Winter Bringing Arthur Miller's 'Incident At Vichy' Revival To Off Broadway Next Year News Sophia Anne Caruso To Star In Duncan Sheik's 'Memoirs Of Amorous Gentlemen' Stage Musical Adaptation The world premiere, six-week limited engagement through January 3, 2027, is set to begin previews on Saturday, November 21, at The Griffin Theater at The Shed. Opening night is Thursday, December 3. Watch on Deadline “It is truly an honor to join this incredible team in bringing Imitation of Life to the stage,” Warren, a Tony winner for her starring role in Broadway’s Tina: The Tina Turner Musical , said in a statement. “Over the years, developing the role of Delilah has become a highlight of my career. She is a character I have grown to love deeply, and I cannot wait to share her with audiences.” Said Legend, “ Imitation of Life tells a deeply emotional story of a remarkable woman’s journey, and I’m thrilled to know that Adrienne Warren will bring Delilah to life. Adrienne is an incredibly gifted performer who brings heart, humanity and radiance to every character she plays. I’m so excited that the world will hear her magnificent voice on the first musical that I’ve composed.” First published in 1933, Hurst’s novel, set in the 1920s and ’30s, tells the stories of two single mothers -one Black, one white – and their daughters as all four build a life together. A central conflict in the story arises when housekeeper Delilah’s daughter attempts to “pass” as white, with the musical addressing such issues as race, identity, motherhood, ambition and belonging. Additional casting, as well as design and creative team members will be announced at a later date. A co-production of The Shed and National Black Theatre, the new musical is produced by National Black Theatre, Universal Theatrical Group, Sue Wagner, John Johnson, Get Lifted Film Co., Crocodile Eyes, LD Entertainment and The Shed. articles.title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Musical Parody Recoups Off Broadway Investment, Extends Run
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Wicked’ & ‘Wicked: For Good’ Live-To-Film Concerts To Kick Off 2027 Tour In San Francisco & New York ‘Disclosure Day’ Release Date Set At Peacock Anthropic Researcher Jacob Coxon Resigns, Warns AI Industry Is “Gambling With Our Lives” View All September 10, 2026 6:00am Jay Armstrong Johnson and Jimin Moon in 'Heated Rivalry: The Unauthorized Musical Parody' Courtesy Production Heated Rivalry: The Unauthorized Musical Parody , Dylan MarcAurele’s buzzy Off Broadway show that began performances at the smallish The Culture Club venue last May, has recouped its initial half-million-dollar investment in its first 13 weeks, producers announced today, adding that the engagement will be extended for a third time. Originally scheduled for an eight-week run at the 174-seat venue – which, prior to this show had been dark for more than a year – the musical is now set to play through Sunday, January 17, 2027. (A previous extension had put the closing date in November.) Related Stories News Alex Winter Bringing Arthur Miller's 'Incident At Vichy' Revival To Off Broadway Next Year News Sophia Anne Caruso To Star In Duncan Sheik's 'Memoirs Of Amorous Gentlemen' Stage Musical Adaptation Producer Alan Kliffer announced the recoupment and latest extension today. Watch on Deadline In a statement, Kliffer and General Manager Christian Palomares said, “This is an extraordinary moment in today’s theatre landscape, especially so for a musical parody about gay hockey players from Canada. Focusing on strong word-of-mouth and moving with deliberate speed in all steps allowed us to grow the show from a fan phenomenon into a musical with its own credibility, and everything since has built on those initial strategies. “This happy moment for our team,” they continued, “is another strong proof point for investing in Off Broadway and redefining what musical parodies can do.” The musical, inspired by the hit TV show that streams on HBO Max, began previews at The Culture Club on Tuesday, May 12, opening on May 26. Prior to The Culture Club engagement, the show was unveiled in eight concert presentations in February and March at the Laurie Beechman Theater and The Bell House. The parody’s approach to the original material is nicely captured in the official synopsis: “ Heated Rivalry: The Unauthorized Musical Parody follows starry-eyed golden boy Shane Hollander on his journey from power center to power bottom. Relive all of the moments from the show that made you wet (with tears) up close on the small-stage by an incredible cast of Broadway actors who thought they were auditioning to be in Season 2. Sporting a bop-infused score, scene-stealing cameos by characters like ‘Rose Landry’ and ‘Ilya’s Ass,’ and time jumps absolutely no one can keep track of, audiences will find themselves hot, bothered, and probably saying, ‘….Girl!'” The current cast features Jay Armstrong Johnson as ‘Ilya Rozanov’ and Troy Iwata as ‘Shane Hollander’ (Jimin Moon originated that role), with Ryann Redmond, Cherry Torres and Ryan Duncan rounding out the ensemble. As previously announced, current company member Shelby Acosta will assume the role of ‘Shane’s Mom & Others’ from Torres beginning Thursday, September 10. The creative team for Heated Rivalry: The Unauthorized Musical Parody includes MarcAurele (Book, Music, Lyrics and Orchestrations), Alan Kliffer (Direction), Brooke & Tiffany Engen (Choreography), Mateo Chavez Lewis (Music Direction), Sully Ross (Scenic Design), Brendan McCann (Costume Design), Devin Cameron (Lighting Design), Germán Martinez (Sound Design), and Ann James (Intimacy Coordinator/Sensitivity Specialist). An original cast album will be released by Center Stage Records on September 18. Heated Rivalry: The Unauthorized Musical Parody is produced by Klif Entertainment and Executive Producer Christian Palomares. articles.title: Alicia Keys, Yeonjun & Others Join Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean For Hugh Jackman-Hosted 2026 Global Citizen Festival In NYC
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Adrienne Warren To Star In ‘Imitation Of Life’ Off Broadway Musical With John Legend Score ‘& Juliet’ To Close In January After Four Years On Broadway ‘Wicked’ & ‘Wicked: For Good’ Live-To-Film Concerts To Kick Off 2027 Tour In San Francisco & New York View All September 10, 2026 6:10am Hugh Jackman at 2025 Global Citizen Festival in Central Park Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Global Citizen UPDATE: Alicia Keys & friends, Victoria Monét, Yeonjun, and Yoshiki have joined the lineup for this year’s Global Citizen Festival . Taking place on September 26 in Central Park, they join previously announced performers Ms. Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean , Lenny Kravitz, John Legend,Lainey Wilson, Shaboozey and Tomorrow X Together. Additionally, Bill Nye, IZA, Jordan Fisher, Katie Couric, Lais Ribeiro, Marcus Samuelsson, Naomi Watanabe, Nomzamo Mbatha, PJ Sin Suela, and Vladimir Duthiers will make appearances, with more names to be announced in the coming weeks. PREVIOUS, August 13: The 2026 Global Citizen Festival in New York’s Central Park next month will feature a line-up including Ms. Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean celebrating the 30th anniversary of Fugees’ album The Score, Lenny Kravitz, John Legend, Lainey Wilson, Shaboozey, and Tomorrow X Together. Related Stories Acquisitions Sony Pictures Circling Ridley Scott's 'Treasure Island' Package Starring Hugh Jackman News Hugh Jackman Hopes Next Wolverine Actor "Makes It Their Own": "I'm Not Going To Say Anything" Taking place on Central Park’s Great Lawn on Saturday, September 26, the festival will be hosted by Hugh Jackman , and feature appearances by Rachel Brosnahan and Gayle King, with more to be announced in the coming weeks. Watch on Deadline The line-up was announced today by Global Citizen, considered the world’s largest movement to end extreme poverty. Following the success of the first-ever FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show, which was produced by Global Citizen and helped raise $60 million for the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, this year’s festival will raise awareness for what the organization says are three core issues perpetuating cycles of extreme poverty across the world. The goals as stated are to create opportunities for 2 million children to go to school, support 1.5 million smallholder farmers, and provide electricity for 2.5 million homes. Tickets to the Global Citizen Festival are free and can be secured by visiting the Global Citizen app and earning points by completing “action journeys” related to the core issues. Points can be redeemed by entering the free ticket lottery or making a $25 charitable donation to instantly secure a ticket. Funds raised will go to New York City’s City Parks Foundation to support their youth education programming and parks initiatives across all five boroughs, as well as to organizations helping those experiencing homelessness across the city. “It’s time to gather once again on the Great Lawn, in the middle of New York City, to tell the world an end to extreme poverty is possible,” said Jackman, Global Citizen Ambassador, in a statement. articles.title: EST N8 Picks Up Manila-Set Crime Thriller ‘Jaguar’ With Elijah Canlas, David Call, Sid Lucero & Gabby Padilla
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Chinese Distributor Hishow Adds ‘Josephine’, ‘Ah Girl’ & ‘Rec’ Franchise To We Love Cinema Release Slate Tokyo Gap Financing Market Unveils 24 Projects & Partnership With Canada’s Frontières Herman Yau’s Audience Award-Winner ‘We’re Nothing At All’ Sold To Blacklight Global For U.S. Release View All September 10, 2026 6:16am Jaguar EST N8 EXCLUSIVE: EST N8 has acquired worldwide rights to Jaguar , a Manila-set crime thriller from director Dean Colin Marcial, a Berlinale Talents Lab alumnus whose work has screened at Toronto, SXSW, Tribeca and Sitges film festivals. The ensemble cast is led by award-winning Filipino actor Elijah Canlas – known for indie breakout hits Kalel, 15 and Sunshine – along with U.S. actor David Call ( Tiny Furniture ; James White ), Sid Lucero (Lav Diaz’s Norte, The End of History ) and Cinemalaya Best Actress winner Gabby Padilla ( Kono Basho ). Also featuring in the cast are Ruby Ruiz, who starred in Prime Video series Expats , Soliman Cruz ( To The North ), Venice best actor winner John Arcilla ( On The Job 2: The Missing 8 ) and Isabel Sandoval ( Lingua Franca ). The film also marks the feature acting debut of Dilaw Obero, the frontman for Filipino rock band Dilaw . Watch on Deadline Related Stories News EST N8 Takes Worldwide Rights To Bangladeshi Rotterdam Winner 'Master' News EST N8 Appoints JP Villanueva As EVP Of Acquisitions & Global Distribution The film follows a young security guard in Manila who accidentally witnesses a high-profile murder involving an American movie star. Described as a combination of Filipino genre cinema with American indie grit, the film explores themes including class, power and corruption. Supported by Purin Pictures and Film London, and winner of the Mocha Chai Laboratories Post-Production Grant at the QCinema Project Market, the film is produced by Braden Friedman ( Little Accidents ), Bam Manlongat ( Under Parallel Skies ) and Marcial. Executive producers include A/Vantage Pictures founder Jason Michael Berman, whose credits include Spike Lee’s Highest 2 Lowest and Ben Affleck’s Air ; Galileo Mondol ( The Creator ) and veteran Filipino producer Moira Lang ( The Blossoming of Maximo Oliveros , Norte, The End of History ). EST N8 will launch international sales on the title at the upcoming Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) Market. The deal for worldwide rights was brokered by Sophie Shi for EST N8, and Bianca Grimshaw with Rebecca Theodore at Granderson Des Rochers LLP on behalf of the filmmakers. “I was just blessed to work with an amazing cast and director that always collaborated to elevate the scenes in the film,” said Canlas, who won several Best Actor awards for his role in Jun Robles Lana’s Kalel, 15 and stood out in Antoinette Jadaone’s social drama Sunshine . “I feel like audiences are craving for unique and fresh ways of telling a story and that’s what we aimed for with Jaguar : a film that follows an ordinary Filipino worker that spirals into unknown territory.” Sophie Changhui Shi, EST N8 Head of Studios, said: “ Jaguar hits the sweet spot for international distributors – it’s an auteur-driven crime story with visceral genre elements and an exceptional festival pedigree that showcases the extraordinary creative energy coming out of Southeast Asian cinema right now.” “Dean Colin Marcial and his team have crafted a story deeply rooted in the local atmosphere while possessing universal tension, further elevating high-concept Asian genre cinema on the world stage. We are thrilled to introduce this raw, electric thriller to global buyers at TIFF.” Marcial noted: “We set out to shoot an incendiary crime story that’s a snapshot of present-day Manila – the bleeding edge of east & west. Sophie and the rest of the EST N8 team share our vision for the film and are champions of the emerging SEA New Wave.” Jason Michael Berman said: “I really believe Jaguar announces Dean as a great new talent. It’s also a genuinely cross-cultural film – pairing a prolific American actor with some of the biggest Filipino stars, and standing as a terrific U.S.-Philippines co-production. “Partnering with the team at EST N8 to launch Jaguar on the international stage at TIFF ensures that this collision of indie filmmaking and Filipino genre reaches the wide global audience it was made for.” The international sales push and global rollout strategy for Jaguar will be led by EST N8 executives Jan Paul Villanueva (EVP, Acquisitions & Global Distribution), Cathy Ni (Head of Sales) and Shams Pasha (Sales & Marketing Executive). EST N8’s TIFF Market slate also inclues B-EST Pictures’ Thai horror debut Tame , Chan Chun-hao’s Taiwanese thriller Dead End , Rezwan Shahriar Sumit’s IFFR Big Screen Award winner Master , and Tetsuya Mariko’s Dear Stranger , starring Hidetoshi Nishijima and Gwei Lun-Mei. articles.title: ‘Le Faux Soir’ Trailer: Arieh Worthalter & Mélanie Thierry Star In WW2 Belgian Resistance “Media Hack” Drama – TIFF
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie ‘No Other Land’ Co-Directors Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor Lift Lid On New Bombshell Doc ‘Naza’ Exposing Israel’s Deliberate Targeting Of Civilian Homes In Gaza – Venice Ellen Burstyn Talks Working Into 90s with Starring Role In Unexpected Love Story ‘Place To Be’; Pays Tribute To Gloria Steinem – Venice First Behind-The Scenes Look Reveals Isabelle Huppert As Crime Boss In Yann Demange’s London-Set ‘Lineage’ View All September 10, 2026 6:26am EXCLUSIVE: Michaël R. Roskam‘s ensemble World War Two Belgian resistance drama Le Faux Soir world premieres as a Special Presentation in Toronto this weekend, before heading to San Sebastian as the closing film, and Deadline can unveil the trailer. Set in Belgium in November 1943, the drama is inspired by the events surrounding daily newspaper Le Soir, which became a vehicle for Nazi Germany propaganda following its invasion of the country in 1940, resulting in it being nicknamed “Le Soir Volé” (The Stolen Soir). In the world’s “first media hack”, a group of Resistance fighters hatch a wild but dangerous plan to print a fake edition of Le Soir, packed with articles mocking the occupier. Related Stories News Oscar-Hopeful 'Tangles' Sells Wide For Charades Ahead Of North American Premiere In Toronto News Netflix Snaps Up Australian Doc Series '2.6 Seconds: Death In The Outback' Ahead Of TIFF Bow Arieh Worthalter ( The Goldman Case ) leads a cast also featuring Mélanie Thierry ( Da 5 Bloods , Memoir of War ), Karim Leklou (Beating Hearts , Jim’s Story ), Mara Taquin ( The Mohicans , On the Edge ), Bouli Lanners ( Nobody Has to Know , The Night of the 12th ), Julien Frison ( The Night of the 12th) and François Damiens ( Dog on Trial, La Famille Belier ). Watch on Deadline The production marks Roskam’s first feature film since Racer and the Bird , which played as a Special Presentation in Toronto in 2017, with credits in between including Apple+ drama Golden Globe-nominated Black Bird, with Taron Egerton, Paul Walter Hauser and Greg Kinnear. Le Faux Soir is produced by Jean-Yves Roubin and Cassandre Warnauts at Belgium’s Frakas Productions; Alice Girard and Vincent Maraval at French production combo Goodfellas /Rectangle Productions; and Roskam’s Harbor Men Pictures; in association with Anonymous Federation et Rossel (Bernard Marchant). Cinéart has taken Benelux rights. Goodfellas is handling international sales.
