articles.title: Longstanding Franchises, Distinctive New IPs Help French Animation Industry Weather Market Slowdown
articles.full_text: Sep 8, 2026 5:12am PT Longstanding Franchises, Distinctive New IPs Help French Animation Industry Weather Market Slowdown Family-viewing, IP branch-out and bold creative-driven endeavors power Xilam, Mediawan Kids & Family and the whole French animation sector at Unifrance Rendez-Vous. By Kevin Giraud Plus Icon Kevin Giraud Latest MIAM! Distribution Expands Slate, Strengthens Partnerships With French Indie Producers, Unveiled at Unifrance Rendez-Vous (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Female-Driven, Premium Period Dramas Spearhead Latest French Fiction Revolution 1 day ago Cartoon Forum Unveils Tribute Nominees, Introduces New Sustainability Award Ahead of 2026 Edition 6 days ago See All From left to right: 'Witch Detectives,' 'Chickies,' 'Astro Boy Reboot,' 'Submarine Jim'. Credits Mediawan Kids & Family, Xilam Animation Of the numerous formats impacted by budget cuts and labor shortage in the entertainment industry, animation ranks high in that rather bleak list. Yet for French production companies, distributors and sales agent who are gathering at the Unifrance Rendez-vous in Normandy’s Le Havre, hope is still a word with 24 animated fps. For Mediawan Kids & Family global partnerships and new business director Marie Lassalle, there’s strength in unity. “Sure, the market is pushing the entire sector to be more selective and to diversify its models (international co-productions, multiple financing sources, earlier consideration of rights and distribution channels as well as a greater focus on formats and production costs), but the answer can’t be solely economic. French creatives must continue to focus on their strengths, expertise, and the uniqueness of their universes.” Related Stories Wim Wenders Clarifies His Stance on Filmmakers' Role in Politics After Berlin Controversy: 'We Are the Opposite of Politicians ... We Are the Antidote' ‘Witch Detectives’ Credits Mediawan Kids & Family To Lassalle’s point, Mediawan brings “Witch Detectives” to the Rendez-Vous. A high-end, 26 half-hour episode 3D-series featuring three inseparable BFF trainee witches, the show is a pan-European new IP, co-produced by Method Animation (part of Mediawan Group) and Toonz Media Group with TF1, Super RTL, BBC and Rai already on board. A perfect illustration on how strong international partnerships can power ambitious projects, all the while retaining their French flavor. Popular on Variety For Xilam Animation , the answer to the current shifts comes from both legacy franchises (“Zig & Sharko” and “Oggy and the Cockroaches” have both sold worldwide) and strong original new IPs, such as preschool hit “Piggy Builders” and the laugh-out-loud comedy series “Submarine Jim,” headlining Xilam’s slate at the Rendez-Vous. “We’re also looking forward to launching our spin-off series ‘Chickies’ at the market,” adds Safaa Benazzouz, EVP Distribution at Xilam. “Derivated from our hit YouTube series ‘Where’s Chicky,’ which has reached reached billions of views thanks to our extensive, digital-driven distribution strategy. Today, making a digital hit requires both linear and digital exposure. But even if preschool is, to my opinion, the most competitive area, animation is ranking high in the total consumption on YouTube and streaming platforms, so there’s no shortage of demand.” Lassalle also identifies family viewing as a very significant trend. “Content that brings children and parents together meets a genuine demand from the audience, and often has a long lifespan. At Mediawan, we therefore look for projects with multiple layers of interpretation, accessible to younger audiences while also engaging the whole family.” While Xilam prefers still to target settled demographics (preschool, kids, YA) on both linear and non-linear programming, Benazzouz acknowledges the ongoing nostalgia trend for content from the 1980/90s that adults love to watch again, sometimes with their kids. “It does create a cross-generational viewing experience for the whole family, and this should be considered when producing animated series today.” The “Astro Boy” reboot, arriving in 2027 on Mediawan’s catalog and produced by Method Animation, and Shibuya International along with Tezuka Productions, is a particularly representative IP in this regard. According to Lassalle, it will introduce this iconic universe to a new generation, while also appealing to parents who grew up with the character. “In our distribution catalog, ‘Ulysses 31’ also illustrates the enduring power of these worlds that continue to resonate with multiple generations.” Beyond these well-known, solid legacy IPs, new concepts are also on the radar of both executives. “We look for concepts that are easy to identify, yet rich enough to last,” explains Lassalle. “Projects with a strong world, well-developed characters, and a compelling narrative.” The ability to make them travel easily while maintaining their unique creative vision is also key. With Madbox, Mediawan is currently developing “Pocket Champs” (a French video game IP with 72 million players) into a transmedia franchise designed to grow with its community, with a YouTube-first launch in 2027. “Digital development and the ability to leverage IP for new uses will be crucial in the near future,” she adds. “YouTube hits like ‘ Miraculous Chibi’ demonstrate the power of short formats designed for global platforms. For us, the challenge is to have a balanced catalog capable of appealing to diverse audiences, uses, and distribution models.” Credits Xilam Animation The same goes for Xilam. Over the years, the company grew its production studios to cover all animation techniques from 2D hand-drawn to full CG animation capabilities. “In terms of sales, we need and want to have a strong variety of formats and techniques,” underlines Benazzouz. “Which in turn allows us to have at least one programme in each category to present for every client. High-quality production, matched with character-driven new IPs with original design and strong humour, is what makes our programming really stand out.” Remaining agile while maintaining high editorial and production standards seems to be the answer to navigating these shifting tides. And both companies are hungry for more, as they head to the Rendez-vous, with Mipcom just around the corner. “Our integrated model, from development to production and distribution, allows us to support projects over the long term and fully realize their international potential,” concludes Lassalle. “And the recent launch of Wonderland Junior TV is a concrete example of that strategy: We are creating a free, reliable, and family-friendly destination in the U.S., which enhances the visibility of premium European content to new audiences.” With more than 1,700 episodes, Wonderland Junior TV is not only Mediawan’s own effort. Major European partners are on board as well, including Xilam, pushing French high-end, unique animation series beyond its borders. articles.title: MIAM! Distribution Expands Slate, Strengthens Partnerships With French Indie Producers, Unveiled at Unifrance Rendez-Vous (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 8, 2026 5:14am PT MIAM! Distribution Expands Slate, Strengthens Partnerships With French Indie Producers, Unveiled at Unifrance Rendez-Vous (EXCLUSIVE) Along with its three newly acquired titles – 'Sevens,' 'Queerstory,' 'Dad & Me,' MIAM! announced new collaborations with indie producers Have a Nice Day Films, Les Astronautes, Hauteville Productions and Girelle Production By Kevin Giraud Plus Icon Kevin Giraud Latest MIAM! Distribution Expands Slate, Strengthens Partnerships With French Indie Producers, Unveiled at Unifrance Rendez-Vous (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Female-Driven, Premium Period Dramas Spearhead Latest French Fiction Revolution 1 day ago Cartoon Forum Unveils Tribute Nominees, Introduces New Sustainability Award Ahead of 2026 Edition 6 days ago See All From left to right, 'Sevens,' 'Queerstory,' 'Dad & Me' Courtesy of MIAM! Distribution As Unifrance Rendez-Vous kicked out yesterday and with its sales team attending, MIAM! Distribution unveiled earlier today the acquisition of two new animated TV series and a 52-minute TV special, the latest addition to a carefully curated catalogue marked by MIAM! distribution’s editorial ambition: to champion distinctive creative voices and stories, rooted in the lived experiences of their creator. Spanning three different target groups and three distinct formats, these productions fully embody MIAM!’s commitment to accompany stories that matter. With universal, impactful themes resonate with audiences worldwide. Related Stories Wim Wenders Clarifies His Stance on Filmmakers' Role in Politics After Berlin Controversy: 'We Are the Opposite of Politicians ... We Are the Antidote' “Our acquisition strategy is driven by a desire to work with independent producers and creators who bring distinctive voices and fresh perspectives, says Hanna Mouchez, CEO of MIAM! Distribution. “Through these three projects, we explore themes that are central to our editorial vision: identity and belonging, diversity and representation, and the confidence to find your own place in the world.” Popular on Variety Sevens Inspired by the real-life journey of French international rugby player (and co-creator of the series) Séraphine Okemba, “ Sevens ” is a 13×22-minutes character-driven kids’ series celebrating female sport, powered by Girelle Production. As Rose, an average middle-school girl, decides to launch a female rugby sports team at her school, she and the girls joining her begin to build powerful bonds of friendship, solidarity and sisterhood. “Rugby is a sport built on values,” adds Okemba. “Within a team, players learn solidarity, mutual support and trust in yourself and others. They learn to trust themselves, and to trust others.” This collective adventure is the heart of “Sevens,” centering on how sport can empower young people, build confidence, proving that strength, courage and leadership have no gender. Currently in development with France Télévisions, with an expected delivery by the end of 2028, the show is co-directed by Guillaume Lorin, award-winning director of the TV special “Vanille,” and Vinnie Ann Bose, director of the César-nominated short “Suliamani.” Queerstory A bold young adults 20×6-minutes doc series bringing forgotten queer myths to the spotlight, “ Queerstory ” blends humor, documented historical sources and experts’ takes to share queer tales whose voices have too often been erased from history. From the truth behind Thor’s hammer and the goddess Amaterasu to Princess Badoure from One Thousand and One Nights, the show restores these legends to their rightful place in our collective memory. Driven by the distinctive voice of its creator Iris Miské and blending rough-edged graphic design with bold pop-culture references, the series combines sharp pacing, clever punchlines and compelling storytelling, inviting a broad audience to rediscover history through fresh, inclusive perspectives. “Queer people have always existed, all around the world,” hammers Miské. “In these times where LGBTQIA+ identities are globally threatened, ‘Queerstory’ builds a bridge between the past and the present, giving life to our queer ancestors, and arguments to fight bigotry.” The series will be delivered in May 2027 by Hauteville Productions and is set to premiere on Slash, France Télévisions’ digital platform dedicated to young adults audiences. Dad&Me A 52-minute coming-of-age TV special produced by Have a Nice Day Films and Les Astronautes, “Dad & Me” follows Alyona and her father Fiodor as they leave their Russian village to settle in Paris. On her very first day at school, Alyona cannot understand a single word of French, making friendship seem impossible. But when a rap competition unexpectedly brings her together with two classmates, she gradually finds her place between two cultures and discovers a new way to express herself. With her father by her side, every challenge can become an adventure. “Whatever your age, you always need courage to build a new life in a new country, town, or even neighborhood,” recalls director Olesya Shchukina who adapts her own childhood story with this special. ” “I wanted to talk about this experience and its complexity, so both kids and adults could relate.” Currently in production, “Dad & Me” is supported by a broad alliance of French funds, including Pictanovo, CICLIC, Région Sud, Procirep, France’s CNC National Film Board and French distributor Les Films du Préau. The special will be delivered in July 2027, and premiere on France Télévisions. These three productions join a catalogue of 33 programs handled by MIAM! Distribution, the international distribution and licensing division of MIAM! group, which also oversees licensing & merchandising rights of MIAM! animation’s original IPs. Founded in 2016, the group develops and distributes ambitious stories and experiences for children, families and young adults, such as “Edmond and Lucy,” “The Tinies,” and “Goat Girl,” with a strong focus on artistic originality, technological innovation and sustainable production models. articles.title: Tom Jones Alleges ‘The Voice U.K.’ Fired Him at 86 Years Old Due to ‘Financial Difficulty With Insurance’
articles.full_text: Sep 8, 2026 5:57am PT Tom Jones Alleges ‘The Voice U.K.’ Fired Him at 86 Years Old Due to ‘Financial Difficulty With Insurance’ By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest Tom Jones Alleges ‘The Voice U.K.’ Fired Him at 86 Years Old Due to ‘Financial Difficulty With Insurance’ 5 minutes ago BBC News Anchor Maryam Moshiri Reveals Blood Cancer Diagnosis 22 hours ago ‘SNL U.K.’ Adds Freddie Meredith to Cast 1 day ago See All Getty Singer Tom Jones has claimed he was fired as a judge from singing competition show “ The Voice U.K.” due to “financial difficulty with insurance.” “To be clear, I did not want to leave ‘The Voice’ as I love the show and really appreciate the audience,” Jones posted on social media. “ ITV made this decision — obviously a while ago, and I was told just recently. The reason given is because of a financial difficulty with insurance.” Related Stories Wim Wenders Clarifies His Stance on Filmmakers' Role in Politics After Berlin Controversy: 'We Are the Opposite of Politicians ... We Are the Antidote' “They now say in the press they wanted to ‘refresh’ the show, and with a new coaching line-up there wouldn’t be a chair for me,” he continued. “They are offering a much-reduced role where I would make an appearance but without being actually involved from the start, and I’m not thrilled about that. So the only thing I know right now, is that there’s never a good time to fire an 86-year-old who’s still pretty good at his job.” Popular on Variety Jones, best known for hits such as “It’s Not Unusual,” has appeared on the show almost continuously since its inception in 2012, when it first aired on the BBC as a competitor to ITV’s “The X-Factor.” He spent three years on the coaching panel before taking a break and then rejoined when the show moved from the BBC to ITV in 2017. “The Voice U.K.” is currently produced by Lifted Entertainment, a subsidiary of ITV Studios. After almost a decade on ITV’s version of “The Voice U.K.,” rumors emerged over the weekend that Jones would not be rejoining the next season, prompting him to make his statement. Variety has contacted ITV for comment. Jones is currently appearing on Season 9 of “The Voice U.K.,” which launched on Aug. 22 and is airing every Saturday on ITV. The other coaches include will.i.am, Sir Tom Jones, Tom Fletcher, Danny Jones and Kelly Rowland. Will.I.Am posted a series of crying emojis under the Instagram post while other artists expressed their support, such as AnneMarie who wrote “I love you.” Season 4 contestant Karl Loxley also replied, saying: “The best thing about being on The Voice was getting the chance to work with you @realsirtomjones . An absolute legend and a true gentleman. The Voice won’t be the same without you. articles.title: Penélope Cruz Says It Would Be ‘Very Contradictory’ to Star in ‘Bunker’ and Refuse to Talk About Politics: It ‘Involves So Many Aspects of Where the World Is Right Now’
articles.full_text: Sep 8, 2026 6:17am PT Penélope Cruz Says It Would Be ‘Very Contradictory’ to Star in ‘Bunker’ and Refuse to Talk About Politics: It ‘Involves So Many Aspects of Where the World Is Right Now’ By Ellise Shafer , Rebecca Rubin Michael Buckner Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem have proven that they aren’t afraid to speak out about politics, with the power couple being especially vocal about their support of Palestine. It was inevitable that the topic would come up at the Venice Film Festival press conference for their new film “ Bunker ,” which also doesn’t dance around timely issues. Directed by Florian Zeller, they star as a husband and wife whose 17-year marriage begins to unravel after Bardem’s character, an architect, agrees to build a survivalist bunker for a tech billionaire. Related Stories Wim Wenders Clarifies His Stance on Filmmakers' Role in Politics After Berlin Controversy: 'We Are the Opposite of Politicians ... We Are the Antidote' Asked about their choice to speak up about politics as actors, Cruz pointed out that it would be “very contradictory” not to do so while starring in a movie like “Bunker.” Popular on Variety “We don’t have to agree with our characters, we don’t have to agree sometimes with the story, but this involves so many aspects of where the world is right now — things that affect all of us, future generations,” Cruz said. “There are so many things in this film that it would be really contradictory to then be here and say, ‘Oh, I don’t wan to talk about that.’ It’s impossible. And that’s why a situation like [this press conference] is sometimes more scary than, I don’t know how many weeks of shooting that we did. But still, I don’t think it would make sense to say, ‘I don’t talk about politics.'” Bardem added that it “doesn’t matter if you’re an artist, an actor, a plumber, a taxi driver, you have the right to expose your truth on what you think is important.” “Obviously I have more resources to do it than a taxi driver, because I have this thing [the mic] and I have you guys listening to me. So the responsibility is a different one,” he continued. “And that’s what I think is important, to have a responsibility towards the world that we live in and I don’t take it for granted. But artistically speaking, this movie speaks about that, about how much we’re willing to see, feel, welcome the other, or fear based on what we imagine, our pre-judgments, our fears. Based on that, how much are we going to isolate and criminalize the other? And I don’t know the answer, but it’s a good question.” Zeller wrote and directed “Bunker,” which also stars Paul Dano, Patrick Schwarzenegger and Stephen Graham. The movie marks his return to Venice, where his prior film “The Son,” starring Hugh Jackman, competed for the Golden Lion in 2022. An acclaimed playwright, Zeller made his feature directorial debut with 2020’s “The Father,” which won Oscars for Anthony Hopkins and for adapted screenplay. The director has cited Stanley Kubrick’s “Eyes Wide Shut” as a key inspiration for “Bunker.” Like Kubrick, who cast then-married Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman as partners on the verse of unraveling, Zeller described wanting to blend “fiction and reality” by spotlighting a real couple. Although Barden and Cruz have appeared in many movies together over the years, including “Jamón Jamón,” “Vicky Cristina Barcelona” and “Everybody Knows,” Zeller said he was intrigued that they had never played long-wed spouses. “I loved ‘Eyes Wide Shut,’ this ambivalent proposition presented to the audience where you’re not quite sure what you’re being invited to watch,” Zeller told Variety . “Is it fiction? Is it another version of fiction? Where is the line between reality and fiction? That permeability between reality and fiction seemed to me a truly fascinating project.” Asked about what it was like to work together on “Bunker” and if they ever argue about work, Bardem said they “are very good at either creating fiction or reality, otherwise we would not survive in this job.” He then joked, “And if we do argue? No, no never.” Cruz laughed and added, “I know you for more than 30 years, imagine if we’d never had an argument.” On a more sincere note, Cruz said: “We both really love this profession, but it’s true that there is a good balance in terms of how much you are speaking about work. Obviously if you are preparing a movie together, that is going to be very present in the conversations. But we haven’t done this very often. Naturally, it has appeared like, every five years.” Cruz continued that working with Zeller made them both feel comforted throughout the filming process. “We knew we were going to be protected in that way, in terms of having someone in the middle who is inviting you not to bring anything from your personal life, but you are going to bring yourself and everything you have experienced in your life,” she said. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are said to be “surprised” that King Charles III communicated his desire for them to remain non-working members of the royal family after they initially left the UK in 2020. In a letter sent on behalf of the King on Monday, senior Palace official Lord Chamberlain said: “It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of the sovereign, and are no longer working members of the Royal Family.” Related Stories News BBC Rejects Complaints It Aired "Too Much" Coverage Of Harry & Meghan's UK Return Casting Netflix On Meghan Markle Being Cast In 'The Gentlemen': "All Bets Are Off" In a coordinated briefing to UK media on Tuesday, a person close to Harry and Meghan said the couple “were a little surprised not to have been told about this in advance.” Royal sources told BBC News that Prince Harry and Markle were made aware of the letter before it was made public. The Lord Chamberlain’s letter continued: “Any specific questions from official and state organizations about the courtesies which should be extended to the Duke and Duchess, and particularly where recourse to public funds may be required, should be directed to Buckingham Palace.” On Prince Harry and Markle’s security arrangements, the letter added: “Any operational security issues should continue to be directed to the relevant police authorities.” Deadline reported on Monday that BBC News’ coverage of Harry and Markle‘s decision to move back to the UK prompted viewer complaints. The BBC revealed that audience members contacted the UK broadcaster to raise concerns that it was dedicating “too much” airtime to the Duke and Duchess of Sussex. The BBC did not disclose how many complaints it received from disgruntled viewers, but rejected the concerns in a notice published on its website . “We believe our approach to this story was proportionate, offering legitimate analysis of the different implications,” the BBC said. articles.title: Alex Gibney Encountered “Tremendous Sense Of Fear”  While Researching ‘Musk’;  Praises “Brave People” Like Ashley St. Clair For Agreeing To Talk
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow , Nada Aboul Kheir September 8, 2026 4:27am Ashley St. Clair, Alex Gibney and Zoë Schiffer attend the 'Musk photocall at the 83rd Venice Film Festival Kate Green/Getty Images Oscar-winning director Alex Gibney told a Venice Film Festival press conference on Tuesday that he came up against a “tremendous sense of fear” as he canvassed for interviewees his new bombshell documentary Musk about controversial tech tycoon Elon Musk. “There was a tremendous sense of fear of talking, really almost existential fear, both among people who were his critics, people who were his business colleagues and people who are his friends,” he said. “I talked to you know many, many, many, many people who, except for some of the brave people here with me here, declined to speak.” Related Stories News 'Company': First Footage Revealed For Casey Affleck's Venice Drama Featuring His Two Sons Documentary 'Musk' Teaser-Trailer: World's Richest Man Called "Chaotic, Capricious," "Manifestly Cruel And Selfish" In Damning Alex Gibney Doc He suggested that the documentary had intersected previous works such as the Oscar-nominated Enron: The Smartest Guys in the Room , or his 2019 Elizabeth Holmes exposé The Inventor: Out for Blood in Silicon Valley . Watch on Deadline “What I discovered was that the story of Musk was not, in a way, a new tech story. Though there’s much about it that is tech, but… his story is really the story of an old wine in a new bottle. His story turns out to be the story of the confidence man, the stock pumper, his wealth and power comes from inflated stock, and so I had told that story before with Enron and with Elizabeth Holmes, and so it was a story that was oddly familiar to me,” said Gibney. Gibney was joined at the press conference by Musk interviewees Ashley St. Clair, Elon Musk’s ex-partner and the mother of one of his children, and journalist and writer Zoë Schiffer, author of the 2024 book ‘Extremely Hardcore: Inside Elon Musk’s Twitter’. Asked why the had agreed to participate in the film, St. Clair brought up a previously reported $40M NDA offer she received from Musk after their relationship ended. “When you’re offered something like that, it really causes a debate in your head about what your speech means and how valuable that is, and why do they want to offer me this amount of money to not speak?,” she said. “And I believe Alex spoke to it a little bit about Elon’s unreality, and he does complicated relationships generally, but his most complicated relationship is with the truth. And so, I think most importantly, I want to set the example for my kids that you should never take being materially comfortable over speaking the truth.” View this post on Instagram Schiffer said her involvement chimed with her own work as a journalist who has covered Musk in depth, suggesting it was easier to find people who would talk further down the chain in “Musk Inc”. “His empire is that he has a lot of loyalty at the upper echelons of his company. He stacks the boards with friends and colleagues, but at the lower levels he doesn’t do a lot to engender a ton of loyalty toward him,” she said. “He treats people pretty harshly, and particularly when he’s coming into a new organization like USDS or Twitter. I think there’s a feeling that it’s a sort of takeover, and people who were there previously feel like something really wrong is happening, and those people were quite quite willing to talk. Overnight the production released a first trailer giving a taste of the film, with soundbites describing Musk as “chaotic”, “capricious” , “manifestly cruel”, “a nuke” and “a “fascist” Musk had yet to respond to the trailer by the time the press conference kicked off at 12.30pm CET (3am PT), having pre-emptively fired off a post on X on about Gibney and the documentary last week. His social posts over the past 24 hour have focused instead on showing support for the victory of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in elections Germany’s eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt over the weekend. A German journalist commented on the fact that AfD politicians had thanked Musk for his supported in the wake of their party’s victory, while had congratulated them, and asked for Gibney’s view on the tech tycoon’s influence on politics outside of the U.S. “I hope I show in the film that he’s involved in right-wing political parties all over the globe, in Germany, in the United Kingdom, in Brazil, in Turkey,” said the director. “I think there are a number of reasons for that. That seems to be his ideology at the moment, but in addition to that, many of these right-wing governments tend to be more pliable. It’s easier to buy the results you want from administrations that are utterly corrupt and venal and have no sense of restraint or internal checks and balances. So yeah, I think he’s pursuing a global right-wing agenda, both for ideological and I think for very practical and monetary reasons.” Trump Admin Attacks UK Plan To Boost BBC Content On YouTube Apple TV & HBO Max Set Primetime Showdown After Early Wins; Winners List; More U.S. Summer Record In Play As Spidey No. 1; ‘Odyssey’ Wins Global Battle Surprise Movie ‘You Can See Everything’ Reviewed; More Pics In Focus Read More About: Comments

articles.title: BBC Strike Threat Rises As Matt Brittin Laments “Disappointing” Decision By Unions To Reject Improved Pay Offer
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Tom Jones Claims He Has Been Fired From ‘The Voice UK’ Because Of “Financial Difficulty” BBC Strike Threat Rises As Matt Brittin Laments “Disappointing” Decision By Unions To Reject Improved Pay Offer Harry & Meghan Briefing War Breaks Out Within Days Of UK Return; Couple “Surprised” By King Charles Edict View All September 8, 2026 4:47am BBC boss Matt Brittin BBC EXCLUSIVE : BBC boss Matt Brittin has revealed that unions have rejected an improved employee pay offer, increasing the likelihood of a mass staff walkout at the British broadcaster. In an internal town hall briefing, Brittin said the BBC had revised its pay increase offer from 1% to an average of 2.1%, but this was dismissed by unions, including the National Union of Journalists. “That was disappointing,” Brittin said. “I understand the cost of living and the pressures that people are under, but [I’m] just disappointed because people want clarity and we want to be able to give the pay rise.” Related Stories News BBC Rejects Complaints It Aired "Too Much" Coverage Of Harry & Meghan's UK Return News Richard Osman Appears To Confirm 'The Celebrity Traitors' Premiere Date Amid Talk That Season 2 Was "Intense" To Film The BBC director general said the pay talks had been a “pretty difficult process for everyone” and he acknowledged that industrial action was a possibility. Watch on Deadline Brittin said low earners would benefit most from the remuneration offer (some employees will get a 2.5% raise), while members of the BBC’s top leadership team will not receive a pay rise. He added that the BBC was making the offer in the context of cutting costs by £500 million ($675 million), while at the same time having no certainty over its future funding amid charter renewal talks with the government. Brittin said a 1% pay rise was equivalent to 180 jobs. “That’s where we’re in a tight situation on savings. How do we get the right balance between helping people progress with the cost of living, but also managing the size and shape of the BBC for the future.” BBC News presenter Adam Fleming, who was hosting the staff Q&A with Brittin, asked: “Do you think that people who want a bigger pay rise are putting their colleagues’ jobs at risk?” Brittin responded: “I understand completely why people want to be paid in a world of cost of living increases and so on. But yeah, that’s the choice that you have to make at a management level. To award more, you’re going to have to find the money from elsewhere. The cupboard is bare. There isn’t a cash reserve that we can draw on here. So that’s the kind of trade-off that we’re having to look at.” The former Google executive, who earns £565,000 running the BBC, said talks with unions would continue. He added that some union leaders were in favor of approving the 2.1% offer, but “different people have got different opinions.” Brittin said more details on BBC cuts would be announced in the coming weeks. The corporation’s £500M target expands on a previous savings goal worth £1.5 billion. The bigger picture behind the cuts is that 94% of the UK population use the BBC every month, but fewer than 80% pay the £180 annual licence fee. The BBC is attempting to bridge this gap. articles.title: ‘Musk’ Review: World’s Richest Man, And His Digital Avatar, Thrashed In Damning Alex Gibney Doc – Venice Film Festival
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew The Talk Of Telluride: Secret Screening Of Elizabeth Holmes Documentary ‘You Can See Everything’ ‘Musk’ Teaser-Trailer: World’s Richest Man Called “Chaotic, Capricious,” “Manifestly Cruel And Selfish” In Damning Alex Gibney Doc Director Pawo Choyning Dorji, Cellist Yo-Yo Ma Team On ‘A Song For The Snow Lion’ Set In Himalayas Of Bhutan – Telluride Film Festival View All September 8, 2026 5:05am 'Musk' Courtesy Bleecker Street What sort of billionaire criticizes another billionaire for giving tons of money to charity? The same kind of billionaire who would gleefully gut USAID, calling it a “criminal organization,” a move that has cost hundreds of thousands of lives, according to multiple estimates. What kind of entrepreneur falsely claims to have founded Tesla, when it was really two other men? The same kind of man who would claim to have held his dying infant in his arms, when it was actually his wife who did (a wife he later dumped). That’s the Elon Musk portrayed in the documentary Musk , which just held its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival . Related Stories News Alex Gibney Encountered "Tremendous Sense Of Fear Of Talking" As He Researched Bombshell Doc 'Musk'- Venice Documentary 'Musk' Teaser-Trailer: World's Richest Man Called "Chaotic, Capricious," "Manifestly Cruel And Selfish" In Damning Alex Gibney Doc The film depicts the world’s richest man as petty, narcissistic, megalomaniacal, cruel, detached from humans at a personal level (including various ex-partners and many of his children) while purporting to want to save humanity by colonizing Mars. A real prince. Musk , in my view, gives Elon the takedown he richly deserves. Watch on Deadline Elon Musk leaps on stage with then Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump in 2024. JIM WATSON/AFP via Getty Images At 225 minutes, some will deem it too long a haul, but I found the film engrossing from the start and a necessary length to confront Musk’s immense impact on contemporary life and politics, sprawling businesses, and complex personal life. The documentary’s most brazen and innovative technique is to turn Musk into a CGI avatar, enthroned in the purple glow of a digital background, eerily mouthing words that, as the film says, Elon has said in real life. He’s dressed in a tough guy leather jacket, dispensing self-justification and deep thoughts like, “I wanna be out there exploring the stars… I just want to know what’s going on.” He also speculates that we humans might be in a simulation created by some other being (to my mind a bizarre flight of fancy which subtly gives him license to ignore suffering on Earth. Hey, if we’re just characters in some grand intelligence’s video game, why be bothered by what happens to individuals even on a mass scale?). ‘Musk’ director Alex Gibney Courtesy of DOC NYC Gibney, who has applied investigative rigor to Enron, Scientology, Casino Jack Abramoff and other targets in previous films, digs particularly deep into Tesla and its safety claims associated with self-driving technology. The documentary asserts Musk has vastly overstated the capacities of Tesla vehicles, dazzling 60 Minutes ’ Lesley Stahl and other journalists with displays of his electric cars proceeding under their own guidance, while hiding a frightening reality. It explores cases of Tesla owners who let the car do the driving, only to die in accidents or kill others on the road (like a 2019 incident in Florida when a Tesla S model ran through a T-intersection, killing 22-year-old Naibel Benevides Leon and injuring her boyfriend). The film suggests Tesla lied about not being able to access data from its vehicle that struck Leon. Experts in the film also say Tesla has lied about the true range of its vehicle batteries and that it fraudulently promised to create a network of roadside ports where drivers could easily swap batteries, extending range (this dodge allegedly allowed Tesla to pocket millions in government subsidies predicated on the viability of the program). More darkly, Musk implies Elon wants the vast data a Tesla can accumulate on its owners to feed his AI ambitions. The documentary spends considerable time exploring Musk’s checkered romantic relationships, including with Justine Musk, his first wife who bore him six children (including the ill-fated Nevada, the boy who died at 10 weeks old from sudden infant death syndrome). He has rejected his trans daughter Vivian, one of his kids by Justine. The “pro-natalist” Musk has also sired three kids with the singer Grimes (aka Claire Elise Boucher), a baby mama relationship that has also soured. L-R tech journalist Zoë Schiffer, director Alex Gibney, and Ashley St. Clair attend the photocall of ‘Musk’ at the Venice Film Festival on September 8, 2026. Tiziana FABI / AFP via Getty Images One of the most absorbing parts of the film involves Ashley St. Clair, the conservative influencer, who bore a son by Musk in 2024. She chillingly describes encounters with Jared Birchall, a man often described as Musk’s fixer/enforcer, charged with muscling people like St. Clair under control. She refused to accept a financial settlement after her split with Musk that would have required her to sign a non-disclosure agreement; in lieu of an NDA, she freely speaks with the filmmaker about Musk in very unflattering terms. St. Clair was involved with Musk during the time of the 2024 presidential election when Musk, as we all saw, threw his arms around Donald Trump and leveraged his vast wealth to help get Trump reelected. In the film’s most sensational claim, St. Clair says Musk told her he would exploit “an anomaly in the matrix” to affect the outcome of the race, citing his access to space lasers – an apparent reference to his network of Starlink satellites. Gibney lets it hang that Musk might have nefariously determined the winner of the presidency. I found this less than completely convincing, though I would love to see definitive proof. Musk , to my mind, is most successful at painting a psychological portrait of the multi-billionaire. Musk’s father, Errol Musk, is interviewed in the film and relates a telling incident in which the family drove by the scene of a man who being resuscitated by the side of the road. Errol stopped the car and he recounts how Elon, then a boy, kept reading his comic book, completely ignoring the life-and-death drama in front of him. His childhood in South Africa is explored, one where the potential for violence in the country’s Apartheid era seems to have traumatized young Elon. He comes to Silicon Valley in his 20s and in short order has made millions from startups, including Zip2 (a kind of digital yellow pages), and X.com (not to be confused with his later acquisition, Twitter), a financial services and internet bank that merged with PayPal. In interviews back then, Musk comes off as awkward, a geek in pleated khakis with a receding hairline and uneven teeth. Before long, his wealth and his hair would expand, and the teeth would be straightened. This insecure Musk dwells within the adult who craves constant attention through his social media platform and reacts with fury to perceived slights (the film suggests Musk turned on Democrats in part because President Biden didn’t invite Tesla to an electric vehicle exhibition at the White House). Donald Trump and Elon Musk, speak in the Oval Office of the White House on May 30, 2025. Getty All this leads to Trump 2.0 when the reelected president handed vast power to Musk by appointing him chief of “DOGE,” the spurious Department of Government Efficiency. There, Musk’s disturbing lack of empathy would glory in slashing jobs and spending, including on the vital USAID. The full catastrophe of DOGE hasn’t been written, but Musk goes some way in exposing its arbitrary nature, grotesquely inflated claims of cost-cutting and utter failure as Trump negated any savings by handing a gigantic tax cut to the wealthy, ballooning the national debt. Most sinister of all, the documentary suggests Musk’s real goal in getting into the White House was to access data on all Americans, once again to feed his pernicious AI dreams. The Musk of this film is unscrupulous, power-hungry, and narcissistic, the child of a distant, difficult father. No wonder he and Trump bonded – until they didn’t, but then they did again, realizing they needed each other: Trump to get access to that colossal wealth and Musk to avoid government investigations into his enterprises and to maintain access to the federal piggybank and untold troves of data. Alex Gibney has made a lot of vital documentaries. This is his most important. In a statement posted on Instagram, the Welsh singer alleged that he was removed from his coaching role on The Voice because of a “financial difficulty with insurance.” Jones did not elaborate on the issue, but suggested that it was wrong of ITV to brief that he was removed from the show because of a creative refresh. View this post on Instagram “They are offering a much-reduced role where I would make an appearance but without being actually involved from the start, and I’m not thrilled about that,” Jones said. The Sun added that Will.i.am and Kelly Rowland will return as coaches. Stacey Solomon and Alesha Dixon will take over hosting duties from Emma Willis, who is now presenting Strictly Come Dancing . ITV has been approached for comment. Jones has been a coach on The Voice since its first season on the BBC in 2012. Season 14 is currently on air. Jones’ acts have won the series three times in those 14 years. articles.title: Casey Affleck On ‘Company’: “I Was Responding In Part To Raging Conflicts In The World, And To Things Inside Myself” — Venice
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas ‘Company’: First Footage Revealed For Casey Affleck’s Venice Drama Featuring His Two Sons Telluride’s Surprise Movie Sparks Industry Guessing Game As Studio Buyer Emerges; Update With A Winner — The Dish Venice Film Festival Chief Alberto Barbera On Oscar Chances, Why Gaza Doc ‘NAZA’ Is Playing So Late & Why He’s Confident U.S. Studios Will Return View All September 8, 2026 5:41am Indiana Affleck, Emily Alyn Lind, Scoot McNairy, Casey Affleck, Adelaide Clemens, Nick Nolte and Caylee Cowan at the "Company" photocall at The 83rd Venice International Film Festival on September 08, 2026 in Venice, Italy. Getty Casey Affleck ‘s Venice Film Festival Competition drama Company is launching on the Lido today. Affleck was flanked at the film’s press conference by Adelaide Clemens, Scoot McNairy, Emily Alyn Lind, actress-producer Caylee Cowan — Affleck’s partner — and 85 year-old screen legend Nick Nolte. Affleck told the assembled journalists that actor Ben Mendelsohn, who also stars in the film, had arrived with the team in Venice but had to return home to be with his father who is unwell. The film also introduces Affleck’s son Atticus for the first time on screen and marks the second feature for his son Indiana. Both were seated in the front row but Affleck said he wanted to play ‘father’ and not have them exposed to questions today. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Reviews Venice Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline's Reviews News Ellen Burstyn Talks Future Direction Of U.S. As She Receives Venice Career Award: "I Pray My Country Finds Its White Line" Described as “a meditation on grief, vengeance, forgiveness, and the quiet acts of compassion that can heal even the deepest wounds”, the gothic drama is set over a single night in 1975 when a wintry holiday gathering is interrupted by a mysterious woman who recounts a tale from decades before. Oscar winner Affleck responded to a question about whether the film was an expression of anger about global conflicts: “It’s not explicitly a political movie. But I’m not impervious to the to the world around me, so I was responding in part to all of the sort of raging conflicts in the world, and to things inside myself. And what do we do with the the stuff in our life? All of us, not just me or someone over there or people living next door to me, but everyone, with the injuries and insults that we experience, the harm that has caused us, the pain and suffering, the injustice that we feel that makes us so angry and want to lash out and fight back. Is there another way to process those feelings? Is there another way? And and there’s no answer that’s given. I was I was just exploring those those questions.” He continued: “Chekhov said that art isn’t supposed to provide answers. It’s just supposed to formulate the problem. The metaphor he used was that the courts are there to formulate the problem, and the jury solves it. And I think the same is true for for art and for movies. What we’re doing is sort of formulating the problem. We’re not trying to to solve it or even really suggest a solution.” One journalist lamented to Affleck that it had been years since she had last seen him at the Venice Film Festival with Manchester By The Sea [Affleck was last at the festival in 2022 with Dreamin’ Wild ], and she wanted to know why he hadn’t been back since and what he had learnt about himself in that time: “Let’s see”, he responded. “I’m 51, so I was 41, and my kids grew up, and I went through COVID and divorce and a million things, and I took all of that stuff…You know, the good thing about being an artist, the best thing maybe, is that you can take all of the hardest experiences in your life and put it into your work, and it just makes you better if you’re willing to face it all, be honest about it all, and show vulnerably with those feelings, and allow for the fact that you might not be able to really fully understand them, but you’re willing to put them into what you’re making.” He continued: “It’s a blessing, and for me, it’s the only way that I can understand what’s happening in my own life. Sometimes I’ll see movies from five years ago and I think, ‘Oh wow, that’s what that was about. I had no idea. I didn’t know that is what I was going through at that time. That is what was on my mind.’ Because we go through our lives thinking about picking the kids up or making lunch or buying the groceries, but there’s this other stuff that’s churning deep, deep, deep down, and that’s the stuff that comes out when you’re making something. And then there you see it on the screen. You think, ‘oh, I guess that’s me’. So I think someday I’ll look back on this movie and I’ll say, ‘that’s me, and I’ll have a better understanding of what the last 10 years have been like.’ Unsaid was also the challenging period following the movie I’m Still Here , which led to Affleck having to settle two lawsuits out of court, and his name being pulled into the MeToo debate. He pulled out of presenting an Oscar at the 2018 ceremony and hasn’t been nominated by the Academy since his win for Manchester By The Sea in 2016. Affleck was asked at one stage why he cast his kids in his new film and whether he had to drag them “kicking and screaming” to do it: “That’s not inaccurate,” he explained. “Neither one of them really wanted to be a part of this production. I think that they grew up around it and had some interest in it and a sort of innate understanding of what it was, like I did. My dad worked in the theater for many years, and so it’s passed down, I suppose, which is a really nice thing, and they were willing to be a part of this. The casting process was pretty conventional. We just hired a great casting director, Avy Kaufman, who I’ve worked with before, but I couldn’t find people. I was sitting around the house doing read throughs of this script over and over, and and I would have my two kids read the younger and older teens, and and they were fantastic. I got to the point where I was there in pre-production and they were willing to show up and do it…they were amazing and it made it the best professional experience of my life by far because I got to go to work every day with my kids and hang around and I would do it over and over again if I could. I don’t think that they will let me but I I’m gonna try.” The multi-hyphenate was also asked why the film was dedicated to his parents. He explained that he had lost both parents this year and didn’t get a chance to show it to them, which he had wanted to do. Affleck went on to say that Venice was his favorite place to show movies and that being a part of the Venice launch of The Assassination Of Jesse James was probably his favorite festival experience. The full synopsis for the movie reads: “On a winter night in 1975, a mysterious woman named Evelyn arrives uninvited at a holiday gathering and tells the story of Tom, an aging hermit who rescues a stranded actress during a Colorado blizzard in 1953. To pass the night, the actress recounts an older tale of a farming couple who take in a troubled young drifter as a series of grisly murders spreads fear across the frontier.” Affleck co-wrote the script with Ron Hansen. Producers include Steven Schneider and Roy Lee via Spooky Features, Catherine Caylee Cowan, Dan Lawler, Affleck, Sean Patrick O’Reilly, K. Asher Levin, Enzo Marc, and Anthony Katagas. Executive producers include Ben Ross via Image Nation Studios, Rami Yasin for Spooky Pictures, Ronnie Exley and Jeremy Ross via Rabbits Black, Ron McLeod, Dr. Terence Chan, Brian Meng, and Maria Breese for 3:33 Creative Productions, and Jonathan Miller. It has been seven years since Affleck’s sophomore directorial outing, Light Of My Life . articles.title: John Turturro To Receive Zurich Film Festival’s Golden Eye Award
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana ‘Coming Of Age’: First Look At Josh Appignanesi’s Upcoming Comedy About “The Power Of Aging” Amelia Dimoldenberg’s Hit YouTube Series ‘Chicken Shop Date’ To End After 12-Year Run ‘Art Sex Music’: First Look At Caroline Catz’s Doc About British Artist & Musician Cosey Fanni Tutti View All September 8, 2026 6:00am John Turturro Primož Koros John Turturro is set to receive the Golden Eye Award at the Zurich Film Festival , which kicks off later this month. The Emmy award-winning actor-writer-director will be feted for his performance in The Only Living Pickpocket in New York , written and directed by Noah Segan. Turturro will touch down in Zurich to accept the award in person on September 26 and will also participate in a Zurich Film Festival Masters session on September 27. In The Only Living Pickpocket in New York , Turturro stars as Harry, a seasoned pickpocket whose carefully controlled life is thrown into turmoil when a job goes wrong, setting off a tense chain of events that unfolds over the course of 36 hours. Set against the streets of New York, the film combines the momentum and suspense of a crime thriller with a character-driven story about a man confronting the choices that have shaped his life. Related Stories News Julianne Moore To Receive Zurich's Golden Icon Award Festivals Zurich Bolsters Position As Awards Circuit Stop-Off As 'Bunker', 'Club Kid' & 'Adult Supervision' Join Gala Lineup Turturro’s career spans more than four decades, working with a range of filmmakers such as Spike Lee, Joel and Ethan Coen, Martin Scorsese, Robert Redford, Robert De Niro, Nanni Moretti and Pedro Almodóvar. His breakthrough roles in Lee’s films Do the Right Thing and Jungle Fever firmly established him as a distinctive actor of his generation. Watch on Deadline Turturro has been a frequent collaborator with the Coen brothers, appearing in films such as Miller’s Crossing , Barton Fink , O Brother, Where Art Thou? and The Big Lebowski , in which he created the iconic character Jesus Quintana. For his lead performance in Barton Fink , he won the Best Actor Award at the 1991 Cannes Film Festival and the David di Donatello Award. Further credits include Francesco Rosi’s The Truce , Redford’s Quiz Show , Scorsese’s The Color of Money and Di Niro’s The Good Shepherd as well as Almodóvar’s The Room Next Door , Matt Reeves The Batman , Mr. Deeds , Anger Management and Transformers He later reprised his role as Quintana in The Jesus Rolls , which he wrote, directed and starred in. Turturro received the Camera D’Or Award at the Cannes Film Festival for Mac , his directorial debut. His other films as a writer and director include Illuminata , Romance & Cigarettes , Passione and Fading Gigolo . His TV work has seen him earn an Emmy for his guest appearance on Monk and he was nominated for an Emmy, Golden Globe and SAG Award for his performance as criminal attorney John Stone in HBO’s The Night Of . Further TV credits include The Plot Against America , Mr. & Mrs. Smith and Severance , the latter of which he received Primetime Emmy nominations for both seasons. Yesterday, ZFF announced that it would also be honoring Zurich-born actress Elisabeth Baume-Schneider with a Golden Eye Award, making her the youngest actress to receive the award. Baume-Schneider is featured in two films at this year’s festival – Eurotrash and animated film De Rägebogefisch . The 22 nd Zurich Film Festival takes place September 24 – October 4, 2026. articles.title: ‘Murdoch Mysteries’ Maker Shaftesbury Hires Nataline Rodrigues In Creative Push
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Mory Sacko Prepares ‘Food Samurai’ For Disney+ North America Vertical Video Studio LoveHit Launches With Adaptations Of Literary Classics Starring Microdrama Regulars & Eric Roberts Steve Callaghan’s ‘Trivia Night Mysteries’ Cozy Crime Franchise Expands With Two Movies View All September 8, 2026 6:00am Nataline Rodrigues Shaftesbury EXCLUSIVE: Canada ‘s Shaftesbury is supercharging its creative team. The Murdoch Mysteries maker has hired former Rogers content director Nataline Rodrigues in a VP role and promoted Susan Alexander to the same level. Both execs be VP, Creative Content, with the latter upped from her Senior Director post. Rodrigues will work on Shaftesbury’s primetime shows in development and production, and led on efforts in the comedy space. Rodrigues will report to Christina Jennings, Shaftesbury’s Chairman and President. She joins from her own company, Grit & Grace Entertainment, and prior to that was Director of Original Content at Rogers Sports & Media, where she oversaw development, production and acquisition for the likes of Citytv, OMNI, FX and Viceland. There she commissioned the long-running Hudson & Rex , and her other credits include Related Stories Politics Apple May Soon Join Google In Renaming Lake Ontario After Donald Trump's Executive Order News Owner Of 'Heated Rivalry' Cottage Did "Soul Searching" Before Agreeing To Season 2: "I'm A Private Guy" “Nataline brings a rare combination of creative instinct and business savvy, and we are delighted to have her experience in our company,” said Jennings. “Expanding Shaftesbury’s comedy slate, which Nataline will focus on, marks an exciting new direction for us.” Watch on Deadline Shaftesbury is among Canada’s biggest independent producers by volume, with Murdoch Mysteries in its twentieth season and Hudson & Rex in its tenth, and comedy shows such as Crave’s upcoming comedy series Slo Pitch , Irish-Canadian co-pro and the latest installment of Hell Motel . “We are fortunate to have a robust primetime slate, but we need to expand,” said Jennings, who founded Shaftesbury in 1987. “The team of Christina Fon [VP of Strategic Partnerships & Scripted Content], Susan Alexander and Nataline Rodrigues gives Shaftesbury an exceptional creative leadership group to champion new stories and the people behind them.” Rodrigues added: “I look forward to advancing its creative ambition, championing bold ideas and nurturing talent as we build on its impressive legacy as a leading force in Canadian independent production.” Trump Admin Attacks UK Plan To Boost BBC Content On YouTube Apple TV & HBO Max Set Primetime Showdown After Early Wins; Winners List; More U.S. Summer Record In Play As Spidey No. 1; ‘Odyssey’ Wins Global Battle Surprise Movie ‘You Can See Everything’ Reviewed; More Pics In Focus Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ’60 Minutes’ Gives A Peek At Story Lineup For Season Premiere Following Tumultuous Revamp
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Matt Gutman Dropped From Former ABC News Field Producer’s Wrongful Termination Lawsuit; Disney, ABC Remain As Defendants History Is Paramount: As The Last Warner Bros Merger Trial Proved, A Legal Victory Is No Guarantee Of A Happy Ending In Latest Threat Of Regulatory Retaliation, Donald Trump Says He’ll Report NBC News’ Kristen Welker To FCC For “Rebuke Or Punishment” View All September 8, 2026 6:16am Norah O'Donnell interviews Air Froce officer whose plane was shot down over Iran. The season premiere of 60 Minutes on Sunday will feature Norah O’Donnell’s interview with the the weapon systems officer whose plane was struck down in Iran, leading to a successful rescue operation. The newsmagazine will be starting its 59th season with plenty of scrutiny: It’s the first original broadcast since a tumultuous revamp earlier this year. The network ousted executive producer Tanya Simon and brought in Nick Bilton to succeed her, while correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega were dropped and, sharply criticizing the changes in an all-staff meeting with Bilton, Scott Pelley was fired. The three correspondents have all claimed political interference in their stories, something that the network has denied. Related Stories Legal Matt Gutman Dropped From Former ABC News Field Producer's Wrongful Termination Lawsuit; Disney, ABC Remain As Defendants News Norah O'Donnell Claps Back At Bari Weiss Critics After 'CBS Mornings' Return: "This Is So Silly. Just Watch Our Show" Under CBS News editor in chief Bari Weiss , the show has brought in Ross Douthat, a former New York Times columnist, as a correspondent, and upped O’Donnell’s role on the broadcast. Those joining as contributors include Gianna Toboni, former senior correspondent at Vice News, who is also a CBS News national correspondent; Sebastian Junger; Ariel Levy, a staff writer at The New Yorker; and Trevor Phillips, who is also senior global affairs correspondent for the network. Watch on Deadline It's time for 60 Minutes. ⏱️ The new season starts this Sunday, Sept. 13. pic.twitter.com/Tol7VBWwaY — 60 Minutes (@60Minutes) September 8, 2026 O’Donnell’s segment will feature interviews with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth; General Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and Admiral Brad Cooper, the operational commander of the war with Iran. In the interview, the officer is identified by the call sign Dude Four Four Bravo. Another segment, from correspondent Jon Wertheim, will be a look at the Los Angeles Rams. Wertheim, Lesley Stahl and Bill Whitaker chose to remain with the show. 60 Minutes also leans more heavily in film-like narrative in a trailer for O’Donnell’s interview.
