articles.title: ‘Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing’ Review: A Handsome Ode to an Oft-Disrespected Sport
articles.full_text: Sep 7, 2026 4:50am PT ‘Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing’ Review: A Handsome Ode to an Oft-Disrespected Sport Erik Shirai's ESPN-produced Venice premiere follows a year in the lives of several men at ascending and descending stages of their relatively short sumo careers. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest ‘Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing’ Review: A Handsome Ode to an Oft-Disrespected Sport 3 hours ago ‘Agata the Writer’ Review: Mia Wasikowska Plays an Author Adrift and Short of Ideas, in a Sly, Witty Film With Plenty 20 hours ago ‘Chronovisor’ Review: An Eerie, Fiendishly Clever Mystery for Lovers of Libraries and the Storied Smell of Old Books 2 days ago See All ESPN Films The title of “ Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing ” is the closest that Erik Shirai ‘s documentary comes to a joke at the expense of its subject: sumo wrestling, the Japanese sport largely known in the western world for the ample size and minimal clothing of its practitioners, and not an awful lot beyond that. In all other respects, however, this stately, artfully produced film aims to act as a corrective to such cheap, culturally insensitive perceptions. Examining as it does the motivations and ambitions of a number of sumo wrestlers, from grand masters to rising stars, through a solemnly respectful lens, the doc finds humanity and even beauty in what can all too easily be comically framed on screen. Related Stories Telluride’s Julie Huntsinger on Her 20 Years Leading the Festival, Chasing ‘Digger’ and ‘Dune 3’ and a ‘True TBA’ Film Hidden Until Patrons Walk Into the Theater Telluride Festival Lineup: 'The Debut,' 'Elsinore' and 'Tender Loving Care' Set for Premieres, Tributes for John Malkovich, Sandra Hüller and Andrew Haigh Indeed, the approach of Japanese-American docmaker Shirai (who previously probed a very different Japanese institution in his popular 2015 doc “The Birth of Saké”) is so respectful as to feel a touch sanitized: smoothed-out and simplified for the benefit of Western viewers, to whose perspective the film is mostly tailored. More unsavory aspects of the sport — including controversies over hazing and match-fixing, not to mention its ongoing exclusion of women from competition and ceremonies — are swept aside, while the compelling fact of its declining popularity in Japan is only passingly addressed. Only before the closing credits roll is it revealed how few yokozuna (the name given to men achieving the highest rank in sumo) this century have been homegrown, as Mongolia and the U.S. step into the breach. Popular on Variety Shedding more light on such matters would provide a richer context for the film’s reverent celebration of sumo tradition, but many viewers will still find it an illuminating and exquisitely mounted study, ennobling the sport with the sheer, studied splendor of its imagery, captured alternately in atmospherically high-contrast monochrome and tea-stained sepia tones. Produced by ESPN Films, it will doubtless find a dedicated broadcast and streaming viewership following its premiere as the opening film of Venice’s audience-oriented Spotlight competition. Early on, the camera observes a group of rookie wrestlers, training at the Tokyo stable of 62-year-old Master Sakaigawa, as they collectively recite a pledge to the sport: “We shall uphold our responsibility and duty to to sumo; we shall uphold a strong heart, kindness and courage.” This is followed by a droll shot of trainees all putting their freshly laundered thongs out to dry: For all its earnestness, the film is not without offhand humor. In the house of Sakaigawa, we meet Hiradoumi, a 24-year-old upstart tipped for big things in the ring (or dohyō , to use its proper term), and a great hope for continued Japanese representation in the sport’s top tier. In the same stable, and younger still, is teenager Yonezawaryu, still learning the ropes, and battling doubts over his long-term commitment to sumo after witnessing firsthand the extreme, potentially fatal, physical toll it takes on the body. At the opposite end of the career scale is Mongolian-born Terunofuji, who at the time of filming was the only practicing yokozuna in sumo, a 10-time title winner considering retirement after 14 years in the sport, five of them at the very top. He is spoken of as a veteran, positively godly in status, though he’s only 33 years old. Age, however, doesn’t mean quite what it does to civilians in a realm where so much transformational strain is placed on the body, and Terunofuji’s is beginning to fail him. “By doing sumo, I’m cutting my lifespan by 10 to 20 years,” he frankly admits, before likening the travails of the professional wrestler to those of a soldier going to war. He’s now married with a son — it’s hard not to wonder if, at the end of his reign, he thinks it was all worth it. It’s one of a few questions that this handsome, sober documentary is too polite to ask. But it does convey the grand, challenging physicality of sumo, which to many of its students qualifies as an answer in itself. There’s also a thoughtful focus here on the pain and labor that goes into building and maintaining these extraordinary bodies — shot, by Shirai and fellow DP Hiroshi Hara, in awed chiaroscuro portraits that line up with the men’s view of themselves as warriors of a kind, leaving far behind many racist, cartoonish depictions of yore. ‘Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing’ Review: A Handsome Ode to an Oft-Disrespected Sport Reviewed at Soho Screening Rooms, London, Aug. 13, 2026. In Venice Film Festival (Spotlight). Running time: 99 MIN. Production: (Documentary — Japan-U.S.-Denmark-U.K.) An ESPN Films presentation of a Rise Films production in association with Real Lava, Generation11. Producers: Teddy Leifer, Sam Stankey, Sigrid Dyekjaer, Yusuke Kamata, Erik Shirai, Carolyn Hepburn. Executive producers: Heather Anderson, Marsha Cooke, Brian Lockhart, Burke Magnus. Crew: Director: Erik Shirai. Camera: Shirai, Hiroshi Hara. Editor: Frederick Shanahan. Music: Rutger Hoedemaekers. articles.title: Studio TF1 Smashes Doc Records With ‘Leon Marchand: Beyond Gold,’ Rolls Out ‘Surface’
articles.full_text: Sep 7, 2026 4:57am PT Studio TF1 Smashes Doc Records With ‘Leon Marchand: Beyond Gold,’ Rolls Out ‘Surface’ By Ed Meza Plus Icon Ed Meza @edmezavar Latest Studio TF1 Smashes Doc Records With ‘Leon Marchand: Beyond Gold,’ Rolls Out ‘Surface’ 3 hours ago France TV Distribution Unveils Female-Led Actioners in Le Havre Lineup 5 hours ago France’s Halley Production Boards Thriller ‘Carro Seco,’ About Killer Who Targets Unscrupulous Barcelona Real Estate Speculators (EXCLUSIVE) 6 hours ago See All 'Leon Marchand: Beyond Gold' (Courtesy of Quad Lab/Clox Production/France Télévisions) Studio TF1 is celebrating recent successes at home and abroad with Sacha Vucinic and Xavier Marchand’s sports documentary “ Leon Marchand : Beyond Gold” and Slimane-Baptiste Berhoun’s mystery drama “ Surface .” While the doc series on French Olympic swimming champion Leon Marchand and his life in the wake of four gold-medal wins at the Paris Olympics has scored record viewing results for France TV, “Surface” has proved a hot seller across Europe and in the U.S. Related Stories Telluride’s Julie Huntsinger on Her 20 Years Leading the Festival, Chasing ‘Digger’ and ‘Dune 3’ and a ‘True TBA’ Film Hidden Until Patrons Walk Into the Theater Meet Topic, the Indie Studio Dominating the Festival Circuit With ‘The Debut,’ ‘Club Kid,’ ‘Wicker’ Offering an intimate look at the young Marchand over the year following his Olympic victories, “Leon Marchand: Beyond Gold” goes beyond the medals to explore his identity, ambition and life as he copes with sudden fame, pursues engineering studies and navigates personal growth at age 22. Popular on Variety Setting an all-time documentary record for France TV, the three-part series drew 2.3 million average views per episode when it premiered on the france.tv platform in July followed by 1.6 million viewers on France 2 during its Sept. 1 TV premiere and a total of more than 13 million views across social media, including more than 1 million views on YouTube. ‘Surface’ Baptiste Langinier/France Télévisions/Quad Drama On the scripted front, Studio TF1’s hit mystery drama “Surface,” which premiered last year at Canneseries and went on to become a major hit on France TV’s streaming platform, has found enthusiastic buyers abroad. Based on the bestselling novel by Olivier Norek and produced by Quad Drama for France TV, the show has sold to MHz Choice in the U.S., the BBC in the U.K., AMC Global Media in Spain, Vodafone for Greece, Blue Play for French-speaking Switzerland and to Moment in a deal covering airlines and cruise ships. Also presented last year at the Unifrance Rendez-Vous in Le Havre, the six-part series follows Parisian police captain Noémie Chastain, who is visiting a remote town to assess a police station’s possible closure while recovering from a traumatic facial injury. When the discovery of a child’s remains leads to the reopening a 20-year-old missing person’s case, Chastain decides to lead the investigation herself, in the process uncovering dark secrets that impact both her and the town. articles.title: ‘Plaza Catedral’ Director Abner Benaim, Chile’s Daniela Vega and Alfredo Castro Board Fiction Series ‘School of the Americas’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 7, 2026 4:57am PT ‘Plaza Catedral’ Director Abner Benaim, Chile’s Daniela Vega and Alfredo Castro Board Fiction Series ‘School of the Americas’ (EXCLUSIVE) The project has been selected for the Co-Production and Financing Forum at Madrid-based confab Iberseries & Platino Industria which takes place Sept. 29-Oct. 2 By Anna Marie de la Fuente Plus Icon Anna Marie de la Fuente @adelafuente1 Latest ‘Plaza Catedral’ Director Abner Benaim, Chile’s Daniela Vega and Alfredo Castro Board Fiction Series ‘School of the Americas’ (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago ‘Strawberry and Chocolate’ Star Jorge Perugorría and Brazil’s Thiago Lacerda Lead Havana-Set ‘Hotel Nacional’ (EXCLUSIVE) 7 hours ago Mexico’s Venice Queer Lion Contender ‘Tijuana, Todavía’ Trains a Spotlight on the Plight of Gay Refugees Fleeing Persecution 2 days ago See All 'School of the Americas' Courtesy of La Panda and Seedling Media Panama’s Abner Benaim has boarded as a co-director of the fiction series “School of the Americas” (“Escuela de las Américas”), which will star two of Chile’s most internationally renowned thespians: Daniela Vega , who headed the Oscar-winning “A Fantastic Woman,) and Alfredo Castro , a Pablo Larrain regular who’s also starred in a slew of Latin American projects. The project has been selected for the Co-Production and Financing Forum at Madrid-based confab Iberseries & Platino Industria which takes place Sept. 29-Oct. 2. Related Stories Meet Topic, the Indie Studio Dominating the Festival Circuit With ‘The Debut,’ ‘Club Kid,’ ‘Wicker’ Jordan Firstman's 'Club Kid' Hits Telluride, and Colleen Camp Could Be Its Secret Oscar Weapon Benaim was an obvious addition to the project given its subject matter and setting. “School of the Americas” begins with an exhumation at the site of the 1983 El Jazmín massacre, which yields a graduation photograph of four commandos with their faces scratched out and a pendant stamped Fort Gulick, the U.S. military base in the Panama Canal Zone, site of the infamous U.S. Army School of the Americas. Popular on Variety Panamanian-American human rights investigator Inés Vega recognizes the massacre’s signature: counterinsurgency doctrine taught at the School. When someone tries to kill her, the cold case turns personal. Tracking four graduates across three continents, she uncovers what the School really taught – and who is still protecting its legacy. Benaim joins co-director Oscar Godoy who also has close ties to Larraín, having been first AD on Larraín’s “The Count,” “The Club,” “Neruda,” “No” and “Tony Manero.” Godoy was recently second unit director on Fabula ’s “Someone Has to Know,” which ranked among Netflix’s global top ten for non-English-language series. His feature “Ulysses” screened at a string of festivals, starting with the San Sebastián Film Fest and culminating at Chile’s Santiago Film Fest (Sanfic) where it won Best Chilean Film. Benaim, Panama’s most internationally renowned filmmaker, has represented his country three times at the Oscars, starting with his documentary “Invasion,” about the U.S. 1989 invasion of Panama, followed by “Yo No Me Llamo Rubén Blades” and “Plaza Catedral,” the latter making the Academy shortlist and earning Benaim a Premios Platino nomination for screenplay. His debut feature “Chance” remains the highest-grossing Panamanian film ever released. Its producers Seedling Media Productions (Panama) and La Panda Productions (U.S./Spain) are targeting 2028 for principal photography to begin, provided all the financing is in place. “The School of the Americas was a real school, located in the Panama Canal Zone; for half a century, it taught officers from across Latin America. We are not making a series about monsters — monsters are an alibi. We are making one about a curriculum: the fact that this was written down, graded and taught, and the men who graduated went home and became somebody’s father. Violence isn’t born. It’s taught,” said La Panda’s Guillermo Escalona, co-creator and executive producer alongside Brittany DeVries of Seedling Media. Escalona, a Spanish-American screenwriter-producer based in Los Angeles, co-founder of La Panda Productions, is the co-creator and co-writer, along with Rhayuela’s Federico Durán, of the late Colombian filmmaker Jaime Osorio Márquez ’s posthumous feature “The Awakening.” The supernatural action thriller was completed by Durán and José Luis Rugeles (“Alias Maria” “Rebellion”) after the director’s death following which it world-premiered at the Guadalajara International Film Festival in April, with Latido Films handling sales. Based in Panama, Seedling Media Productions, founded in 2013 by DeVries, has a varied list of credits that include fiction and documentary features. Among them are crime thriller “Chacalería,” “I Really Love My Husband,” shot in Panama and premiered at SXSW in 2025 and documentaries “Dear Panamá,” “A World Without Orphans” and “Lost Kites,” winner of the Best Documentary Feature at the London Independent Film Awards. Currently, Seedling is producing “Against No One” (“Denuncia Contra Nadie”), a co-production with Guatemala supported by the Ibermedia Co-Production Fund. articles.title: Festival Leaders Confront Growing Political Pressure at Lumiere Summit: ‘We Don’t Judge Artists by Their Passport’
articles.full_text: Sep 7, 2026 5:09am PT Festival Leaders Confront Growing Political Pressure at Lumiere Summit: ‘We Don’t Judge Artists by Their Passport’ By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Festival Leaders Confront Growing Political Pressure at Lumiere Summit: ‘We Don’t Judge Artists by Their Passport’ 2 hours ago Screen Industries Adopt Five Thematic Declarations at Lumiere Summit, Setting Terms on AI, Piracy, Gender, Education and the Environment 5 hours ago France and Korea Launch $1.16 Billion Screen Industry Financing Partnership at Lumiere Summit 5 hours ago See All Naman Ramachandran Political pressure on film and television festivals emerged as a defining theme of a panel discussion Monday at the Lumière Summit in Saint-Paul-de-Vence, France, with Séries Mania general director Laurence Herszberg issuing the session’s most direct call for protection of programming autonomy. “We don’t judge artists by their passport, we judge them by their works,” Herszberg said. Related Stories Meet Topic, the Indie Studio Dominating the Festival Circuit With ‘The Debut,’ ‘Club Kid,’ ‘Wicker’ ‘The Idiot(s)’ Review: Dostoevsky Is an Endearing Drunken Fool in This Rambunctious, Tonally Off-Kilter Two-Hander The panel, titled “Easy to Criticize, Impossible to Replace: Rethinking the Festival” and moderated by Rajendra Roy, chief curator of film at MoMA, brought together festival chiefs from Berlin, Cannes, Toronto, San Sebastián, Annecy, Mumbai, Durban, the Red Sea and South by Southwest. It covered three areas: audiences and community, how festivals relate to the media, and the mounting economic and political strains on festival leadership. Herszberg was direct on the political pressure facing her and her peers. “We feel more and more under pressure from different groups,” she said. “They might be politicians, they might be just people who disagree with the representation of some countries.” As general director of Séries Mania – a free-access festival with 1,500 seats – she said controlling who walks through the door is not possible. “We have to be protected, and we still have to go on and fight for the artists,” Herszberg said. Popular on Variety Cameron Bailey, chief executive of the Toronto Film Festival, which launches its first formal market this year, echoed the sentiment. “Filmmakers are not their nations, and shouldn’t be treated as such by anyone,” Bailey said. He recalled joining TIFF as a programmer in 1990, “at a time when festivals felt like a completely free and open space.” Bailey pointed to TIFF’s Next Wave youth program – now 15 years old – as a long-term investment in building young audiences. “‘Obsession’ became one of the biggest sales at a film festival in a long, long time,” Bailey said, noting that Next Wave participants had championed the title. On the rationale for TIFF’s new market, Bailey said: “The market is also part of that ecosystem – I mean, a terrible way to put it would be that it’s the fertilizer of the ecosystem, but really, it’s what feeds” a constant supply of ambitious films. Berlinale festival director Tricia Tuttle, whose event drew 450,000 admissions last year, and was at the eye of a political storm, put audience development at the center of her contribution. “The answer for me to all of these challenges is to really think about audiences,” Tuttle said, adding that reaching people who are not yet passionate cinemagoers matters as much as serving those who are. Cannes president Iris Knobloch pointed to the breadth of her festival’s annual gathering – 40,000 accredited participants from 140 countries, with over 4,000 journalists in attendance. “For me, that is the real shining light on films and the talent all over the world,” Knobloch said. Faisal Baltyuor, chief executive of the Red Sea Film Foundation, said his organization’s last edition sold out every screening. “We have a lot of creative talents that need that boost to make it to the international stage,” Baltyuor said, noting that 11 films the Foundation supported appeared in Venice and eight were heading to Toronto. On the festival-press relationship, Peter Debruge – now director of the South by Southwest Film & TV Festival after a 20-year tenure at Variety , the last ten as chief critic – put the case for studio films serving discovery. “The studio-level films are the sizzle that brings the attention, the press, and the audiences to the discoveries,” Debruge said. Maialen Beloki, deputy director of San Sebastián, pointed to shrinking press resources as a structural problem. “Each year, media send less and less critics to the festival,” Beloki said. She added that the race to break news online carries its own cost. “We are losing our capacity to talk about the films with some time and with some respect,” Beloki said. Shivendra Singh Dungarpur, founding director of the Film Heritage Foundation and director of the MAMI Festival in Mumbai, said his screenings of restored films regularly attract between 1,000 and 1,400 people and that all MAMI events are free of charge. “I believe that a film festival has to be for everyone,” Dungarpur said. He described the MAMI Independent outreach initiative that partnered with a major cinema chain to bring independent films to cities across India ahead of the festival proper. Mickaël Marin, from the Annecy Animation Film Festival, said that since his appointment in 2018 he has worked to open Annecy to general audiences beyond its traditional professional base, including through a permanent exhibition space that opened last June. “We have a worldwide community of animation coming here in Annecy, from the school, from the student, up to the platform,” Marin said. Magdalene Reddy, director of the Durban FilmMart Institute, said the core challenge in Africa is not finding audiences but reaching them in the absence of sufficient cinema infrastructure. “For us, engaging with audiences is really going into the community,” Reddy said. When moderator Roy closed the session by asking whether festivals could survive without the American industry – demanding a yes or no – Reddy was the only panelist to answer no, while noting that her focus remains squarely on African content. articles.title: ‘Imperium’ Review: Sergei Loznitsa Brings Together Nearly Three Hours of Italian Footage From the Early 1970s Covering the Vastness of the USSR
articles.full_text: Sep 7, 2026 5:15am PT ‘Imperium’ Review: Sergei Loznitsa Brings Together Nearly Three Hours of Italian Footage From the Early 1970s Covering the Vastness of the USSR Journeying from Moscow to the Soviet Far East and then back west, this sprawling documentary shows a multicultural nation stubbornly resistant to Politburo attempts at homogeneity. By Jay Weissberg Plus Icon Jay Weissberg Latest ‘It Will Happen Tonight’ Review: Louis Garrel and Jasmine Trinca Follow Each Other Through the Years In a Light and Predictable Romcom 2 days ago ‘The City of the Living’ Review: A Superbly Acted and Heartbreakingly Real Story Based on a Real Event That Shook Rome to Its Core 3 days ago ‘Al Baraneya’ Review: Cinema Verité Doesn’t Get More Naturalistic Than Egyptian Director Ashgan El-Hamus’ Impressive Debut 3 days ago See All Essential Filmproduktion, Kino Produzioni, Société Parisienne de Production, Studio Uljana Kim In the early 1970s, Italian film crews spread out across the USSR, capturing a vast, multicultural empire few had ever seen in such diversity. From urban commuters to village fêtes, Baku trawlers to Siberian reindeer herders, the cameramen aimed to capture the Soviet polity at a time when Westerners had a gray, monolithic image of what lay behind the Iron Curtain. Granted official permission, they managed to resist any push towards propaganda, even finding ways to slyly critique a system that proclaimed regional autonomy but controlled everything from the Kremlin. While planned as a monumental, multi-chapter TV series, only a few episodes wound up being broadcast on Italian TV, just once, following which the endeavor lay forgotten in the archives. If ever there was a project for Sergei Loznitsa , this was it. Related Stories Nathan Fielder Drops Weird Trailer for Secret Elizabeth Holmes Doc ‘You Can See Everything’ Meet Topic, the Indie Studio Dominating the Festival Circuit With ‘The Debut,’ ‘Club Kid,’ ‘Wicker’ In “ Imperium ,” working with 60 hours of 16mm, the master documentarian organizes this journey along geographic lines, starting in Moscow and heading east, then doubling back through “the Stans” and the Baltic republics until ending in what was then Leningrad. As with Loznitsa’s past films of this type, some snippets of conversation and music have been added, but otherwise the footage has simply been restored and edited together. What’s revealed is an immense state whose distinct regions still managed to hold onto unique traditions, notwithstanding an incessant centralized proclamation of unity. Popular on Variety While “Imperium” can be engrossing, its nearly three-hour running time is felt more than in Loznitsa masterpieces like “Maidan” and “State Funeral.” Perhaps that’s because in those films, one feels the force of history pushing us forward, inexorably heading to a watershed moment whose impact continues to resonate across the decades. With “Imperium,” the motivation is clear yet the concept is more diffuse. It’s also a film which will likely resonate best with those of us old enough to recall how the Soviet Union was discussed in the West at the time, a decade before Ronald Reagan’s “Evil Empire” remark — which simply gave a reductivist Star Wars moniker to the anti-communist propaganda suffusing American-driven global discourse since the end of the Second World War. For Loznitsa, of course, his interest is inside the country rather than how it was perceived from abroad, though it will be impossible for most audiences to separate the two. The film kicks off with a classic parade in Red Square for the 24th Congress of the Central Committee of the Communist Party, with banners touting the same slogans from the previous forty years about production targets being met ahead of schedule. Next comes the GUM department store and window displays with tuxedos, shiny patent leather shoes and beaded handbags, making us wonder who in early 1970s Moscow was buying such luxury goods. Commercialized religion makes its first appearance with a lively trade in Christmas decorations, one of many reminders that despite an official policy of atheism, certain traditions were allowed to persist. (Vladimir Putin, of course, has done an even better job in harnessing religion to his oligarchic dictatorship.) From the capital the footage moves east, where consumer goods are far more difficult to obtain. In Suzdal, an old woman washes clothes in an ice hole; shots of Vladimir show a town seemingly unchanged from pre-Revolutionary days; further south, residents come out for a winter carnival whose roots must date long before Leninism arrived. As the cameramen spread east, local customs become stronger: Bactrian camel races near the Mongolian border, reindeer sleds in the Sakha Republic. It’s here in Siberia where the footage most forcefully critiques Soviet policy, as a group of young Caucasian Russians (in classic 1970s fashion) play guitar and sing Russian songs, the local Yakut population looking on from the sidelines, discontented observers of this not-so-subtle form of colonialism. The greatest takeaway from “Imperium” is just how stubbornly resistant centuries-old traditions were to the Soviet push towards uniformity. People still attended mosques in Bukhara and churches in Etchmiadzin, they held on to ways of life that had not been collectivized by Stalinist dictates. Today, however, rampant capitalism and the internet have changed Russia’s social landscape far more than anything Lenin or Brezhnev could have imagined, turning stubbornly multicultural populations that boldly resisted homogeneity into consumers looking West for their acquisitions. It’s interesting to imagine what might have happened had Italian TV screened the majority of these films upon release. A sense of what life was really like in the Soviet Union was hard to come by then — in the U.S., a 1977 National Geographic publication “Journey Across Russia: The Soviet Union Today” was the first populist corrective to the sense of a uniform society of collectivized proletariat. Italy, with its strong communist party, had a different problem, too often refusing to acknowledge Politburo abuses. An interesting companion piece to “Imperium” would be Federico Ferrone and Michele Manzolini’s 2013 documentary “The Train to Moscow: A Journey to Utopia,” also consisting of found footage but earlier, when a party supporter from Emilia Romagna discovered that life in the USSR wasn’t all solidarity and freedom. At the time, his Italian colleagues censored his revelations. All empires peddle utopias, but why do so many people believe them? ‘Imperium’ Review: Sergei Loznitsa Brings Together Nearly Three Hours of Italian Footage From the Early 1970s Covering the Vastness of the USSR Reviewed at Venice Film Festival (Venice Open - Documentary), Sept. 5, 2026. articles.title: Ellen Burstyn Cries as She Gets Venice Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement: ‘It’s One Thing to Win an Oscar, Tony or Emmy — All of Which I’ve Won. But This Is a Lot’
articles.full_text: Sep 7, 2026 6:50am PT Ellen Burstyn Cries as She Gets Venice Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement: ‘It’s One Thing to Win an Oscar, Tony or Emmy — All of Which I’ve Won. But This Is a Lot’ By Rebecca Rubin Plus Icon Rebecca Rubin Senior Film and Media Reporter rebeccaarubin Latest ‘Possible Love’ Cast Sobs as Lee Chang-dong’s Epic Embraced at Venice With 6-Minute Standing Ovation 21 hours ago Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Remains No. 1 in Sixth Weekend, Nears ‘Avengers: Endgame’ All-Time Domestic Record 21 hours ago Robert Pattinson Kisses Suki Waterhouse as ‘Primetime’ Rocks Venice With 7-Minute Standing Ovation 2 days ago See All Getty Images Maggie Gyllenhaal delivered a message on behalf of Ellen Burstyn before the 93-year-old acting legend took the stage at the Venice Film Festival to receive the prestigious Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement. “Ellen asked me to let you know that she recently took a fall,” Gyllenhaal said from the podium. “She’s OK, but she is moving more slowly — which is fine because it’ll give us more time to clap.” Related Stories ‘The Idiot(s)’ Review: Dostoevsky Is an Endearing Drunken Fool in This Rambunctious, Tonally Off-Kilter Two-Hander How John Malkovich’s 30-Year Oscar Drought Could Finally End With ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Indeed, the room burst into applause as Burstyn, clad in a vibrant yellow gown, sauntered onto the stage with a walker. Burstyn cried and wiped away her tears with a tissue as she was greeted with a heartfelt, minutes-long standing ovation. Popular on Variety “You’re making me cry!” she said, which did little to stop the enthusiastic applause. “You’re overwhelming me, you know! I don’t know how to recover from that generous greeting.” Burstyn has achieved a lot in her seven-decade career in Hollywood, which she was quick to remind the crowd, but she puts the Venice award among the top honors. “You can’t imagine how meaningful this is to me It’s one thing to win an Oscar, a Tony or an Emmy — all of which I’ve won,” she said. “But this … it’s a lot.” Since she learned she’d receive the Golden Lion, she said, she’s been reflecting on her life — and what it means to get a career tribute. “At 93, it means you have a far about of lifetime to look back on,” she said. “I thought, maybe it’s not just a record of what you’ve accomplished, but what you’ve learned.” During her speech, she recalled that while shooting Martin Scorsese’s 1974 drama “Alice Doesn’t Live Here Anymore,” she was required to film a nighttime driving scene while the director and the cinematographer were blocking her view of the street. “I couldn’t see the side of the road; I could go off and kill all of us,” Burstyn said. “But then I noticed, this is a two-way road. There’s a white line in the middle of the road, and I can see that. So all I have to do is look up to the left, and follow the white line. And that’s how I managed to not kill Martin Scorsese.” She then drew a parallel between the funny story and the fraught state of the U.S. right now, saying: “I wanted to close out saying how deeply appreciative I am of this Golden Lion and I hope — no, pray — that my own country will find its own white line.” Burstyn was awarded the Golden Lion on Monday afternoon during the premiere of Gyllenhaal’s short film “Flesh Impact.” Taika Waititi, Pamela Anderson and Murray Bartlett, her co-stars in “Place to Be,” a comedic drama that premieres Wednesday on the Lido, attended the ceremony. The trio were among the first to lead another standing ovation when Burstyn exited the stage and went to sit in the audience. Dedicated to Marilyn Monroe on what would be her 100th birthday, the 20-minute-long “Flesh Impact” portrays Dakota Johnson as the actress at the height of her fame and Burstyn as the version of Monroe the world never got to see. The star died on Aug. 4, 1962 at age 36 from an acute barbiturate overdose. The short’s title, “Flesh Impact,” comes from a phrase once used to describe the aura of Monroe — “that she looked so real and luminous on camera that viewers felt they could touch her through the screen,” according to the synopsis. Prior to the ceremony, Burstyn sat on Monday morning for a press conference and spoke about a fleeting encounter with Monroe way back when. “We never met. We saw each other once. We went to a nightclub, and she was sitting across from me,” Burstyn recalled. “And of course, I was enchanted by just looking at her. She was such a magical creature. And then she looked at me and nodded at me. And I was very early in my career, and I thought, was I just recognized by Marilyn Monroe?” She had another connection to Monroe, through Ralph Roberts, an actor-turned-masseur to the stars. “Ralph Roberts, who had been Marilyn’s masseur, and not only that, but her confidant, he had lots of stories to tell me about Marilyn,” Burstyn said. “So I used to get my massages and hear Marilyn’s stories. My favorite one was that her whole persona was a construction.” Burstyn was asked if she had any other memorable encounters with other Hollywood luminaries, to which she responded, “When I met Marlon Brando briefly, and I almost fainted. That was pretty spectacular.” Then, she cracked, “I can’t think of anyone else — it mustn’t have impressed me too much.” She also recalled the early career advice she received from Bette Davis, who was 24 years her senior. “I had just become known,” Burstyn said. “I was new, but famous. I met [Davis] and she said, ‘Let me tell you one thing, honey. At the beginning of your illustrious career, the only thing that’s important is your work. Anybody that tries to get in the way of you and your work, they’re your enemy. You know what you say to them? ‘You are my enemy.’ I said, “Thank you, Mrs. Davis…” Burstyn has two movies at Venice, the other being Kornél Mundruczó’s quirky drama “Place to Be,” which premieres on Wednesday. She stars in “Place to Be” alongside Waititi, Anderson, Édgar Ramírez, Lena Waithe and Bartlett. Mundruczó and Burstyn previously collaborated on “Pieces of a Woman,” which premiered on the Lido in 2020. Burstyn, who is still acting as a nonagenarian, described her rationale for saying “yes” to projects. “When I get a script, I sit down and read it — and if it makes me laugh, that’s good. If it makes me cry, that’s good. If it makes me laugh and cry, that’s terrific,” she said. “By the time I finish the script, I have to feel moved in some way to say, ‘I want to do this.'” As Burstyn mentioned in her Golden Lion Speech, she is one of the few performers to achieve the Triple Crown of Acting, earning an Oscar for “Alice Doesn’t Live Here Anymore” and a Tony for “Same Time, Next Year” in 1975, and two Emmys for “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” and “Political Animals” in 2009 and 2013, respectively. Over her 60-year career in Hollywood, Burstyn has received dozens of nominations for films and television shows including “The Exorcist,” “The Last Picture Show,” “Requiem for a Dream” and “House of Cards.” Burstyn believes roles for women in entertainment have changed “enormously” over the decades. She added that although the industry is “not quite 50-50” in terms of parity, “they’re close.” “When I first started working, which was 150 years ago, there were no women on set. No women crew. No women directing. It was all men,” she said. “If a woman was on set, it meant she was an actress. And then slowly, thanks to blessed Gloria Steinem, who just died, the consciousness started to be changed.” Starz’s U.K.-Set Boxing Crime Drama ‘Fightland’ Is a Knockout: TV Review Loading comments... articles.title: BBC News Anchor Maryam Moshiri Reveals Blood Cancer Diagnosis
articles.full_text: Sep 7, 2026 7:42am PT BBC News Anchor Maryam Moshiri Reveals Blood Cancer Diagnosis By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest ‘SNL U.K.’ Adds Freddie Meredith to Cast 4 hours ago ‘Fauda’ Creator Calls Mark Ruffalo a ‘Rare Combination’ of ‘Stupid’ and ‘Ignorant’ After His Viral Statement on Paramount: ‘Do You Understand What It Means, “Genocide”?’ 3 days ago ‘Game of Thrones’ Creator George R.R. Martin Confirms Play ‘The Mad King’ Will Transfer to London 3 days ago See All BBC BBC News anchor Maryam Moshiri has revealed she has been diagnosed with incurable blood cancer. The anchor, who joined the BBC in 2003, has covered events ranging from the Pope’s funeral to the Iran war since being diagnosed with Polycythaemia vera (PV) two years ago. Moshiri went public with her diagnosis Monday in an interview with The Times of London. “I was working 14-hour days, constantly on air, constantly having to think on my feet, and holding it together, despite the fact that I had this chronic tiredness and fatigue,” she told the newspaper. “When you’re doing live news, you have this rush of adrenaline, and you just have to get on with it.” Related Stories Telluride Festival Lineup: 'The Debut,' 'Elsinore' and 'Tender Loving Care' Set for Premieres, Tributes for John Malkovich, Sandra Hüller and Andrew Haigh Telluride’s Julie Huntsinger on Her 20 Years Leading the Festival, Chasing ‘Digger’ and ‘Dune 3’ and a ‘True TBA’ Film Hidden Until Patrons Walk Into the Theater Although the cancer itself is not deadly, PV results in the overproduction of red blood cells, causing the blood to thicken and potentially leading to blood clots, heart attacks and strokes. It requires lifelong treatment, much of which is physically gruelling. Popular on Variety “It is going to be there till the day I die,” Moshiri said of her diagnosis. “A big part of this disease is having to get on with life.” Among the treatments Moshiri has endured are twice-monthly venesections, where doctors remove blood through a vein, which she said was exhausting and left her feeling “extremely unwell.” Despite that, she travelled to Rome for two weeks last year to cover the death of Pope Francis. On her return she underwent an immunotherapy treatment which resulted in “horrendous” side effects. She eventually switched to a different drug. Moshri, who also has three children, decided to go public with her diagnosis in order to back a campaign by charity Blood Cancer U.K. called “Here for This,” which highlights the time sufferers miss with loved ones due to their treatment. She is also determined to continue working. “I love what I do. I love being where the story is,” she told The Times. “I don’t want to allow blood cancer to stop me from doing my work.” Starz’s U.K.-Set Boxing Crime Drama ‘Fightland’ Is a Knockout: TV Review Loading comments... articles.title: Gaza Cinema Academy Launches At Venice Film Festival To Help Gazans Tell Their Own Stories
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Gaza Cinema Academy Launches At Venice Film Festival To Help Gazans Tell Their Own Stories ‘A Good Little Soldier’ Trailer: Alba Rohrwacher & Vincent Lindon Co-Star In Stéphane Brizé’s Venice Contender Exploring Toxic Corporate Culture Netflix Officially Confirms ‘The Inbetweeners’ Reunion Movie As Production Kicks Off With First Look At Original Cast In Reprised Roles View All September 7, 2026 2:10am Ezzaldeen Shalh (c) with students on Gaza Filmmaking Diploma course Gaza Cinema Academy The official launch of the Gaza Cinema Academy was announced at the Venice Film Festival on Monday, as the humanitarian crisis in the Palestinian territory continues to dominate global news. The initiative – co-founded by Palestinian filmmakers Ezzaldeen Shalh and Mai Masri – aims to establish a sustainable space for film education, training and production in the Gaza Strip. Gaza-based director and film academic Shalh is known for works such as The Dry Spring , The Other World and Love and Bread as well as for spearheading the Gaza International Women’s Film Festival. Related Stories News 'A Good Little Soldier' Trailer: Alba Rohrwacher & Vincent Lindon Co-Star In Stéphane Brizé's Venice Contender Exploring Toxic Corporate Culture News May El-Toukhy Stops Venice Competition Screening Of 'Woman Unknown' Over Subtitle Snafu; Film Goes On To Garner 7 1/2-Minute Ovation “In Gaza, cinema is not merely an art form; it is a means of preserving memory, reclaiming our right to shape our own image, and giving a new generation the tools to tell its own story,” he said. Watch on Deadline The launch was accompanied by a short film showing Shalh in the classroom with aspiring female filmmakers talking about their desire to bring their stories to the big screen. Palestinian film and TV heavyweights Annemarie Jacir , Hiam Abbass and Saleh Bakri have gotten behind the initiative, with Egyptian comedian and filmmaker Ramy Youssef, Tunisian The Voice of Hind Rajab director Kaouther Ben Hania , who is in Venice this year as a member of the jury; Italian producer Graziella Bildesheim, and Alaa Karkouti, cofounder of Cairo-based film promotion and talent company Mad Solutions, also lending their support. The official launch of the academy is the next step in a process that began in 2024 with the development of the Gaza Filmmaking Diploma, a nine-month theoretical and practical filmmaking training which welcomed its first intake of 25 young Palestinian women in March 2026. The academy is also working to develop a filmmaking degree accredited by Al-Quds Open University, the main higher education institute for Palestinians, with the aim of establishing a sustainable academic pathway for film education in the Gaza Strip. Palestinian cinema pioneer Masri is best known for her 2015 feature 3000 Nights , which premiered in Toronto and the played numerous festivals worldwide. “Supporting a new generation of filmmakers in Gaza means giving them a space to express their reality, memory and dreams. We believe that creativity and cinema can empower, preserve human memory, and build bridges that transcend borders,” she said. Shalh invited film and cultural institutions, festivals, film funds, production companies, filmmakers and related organizations around the world to build partnerships with the Academy, to exchanging expertise, provide resources and professional opportunities. “We want the Academy to open a window for young people and women in Gaza to learn, create and make their own films, and for their voices and images to reach the world. We invite our partners in institutions, universities and the international film community to be part of building this space,” he said. articles.title: BBC News Presenter Maryam Moshiri Reveals She Has Incurable Blood Cancer
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Piers Morgan Launches ‘Football Uncensored’ On YouTube After World Cup Series Scored 60M Views BBC Rejects Complaints It Aired “Too Much” Coverage Of Harry & Meghan’s UK Return BBC News Presenter Maryam Moshiri Reveals She Has Incurable Blood Cancer View All September 7, 2026 2:23am BBC News channel presenter Maryam Moshiri BBC News Maryam Moshiri , one of the BBC’s most seasoned news presenters, has revealed that she has been diagnosed with blood cancer. In interviews with BBC News and The Times of London , Moshiri said that she is living with polycythaemia vera, a rare but treatable blood cancer. Moshiri, 49, was diagnosed in November 2024 after her doctor was “fastidious” about blood tests. Moshiri said she “mostly” had no symptoms, though the condition can cause headaches, confusion, dizziness, and blurred vision. Polycythaemia vera is manageable with treatment. Moshiri has received “debilitating” rounds of venesection, which involves bloodletting. She has also received immunotherapy. Related Stories News Deborah Turness Resurfaces With Studio At Independent Talent Group News BBC To Test Streaming News Channel Live On YouTube Outside Of UK The cancer can thicken the blood, increasing the risk of developing blood clots that can lead to strokes, heart attacks, or deep vein thrombosis. Watch on Deadline “It’s been two years since my diagnosis and I’ve felt that I’ve started to understand the disease a lot better and the way it affects my life. I’ve got a handle on it to a degree now, so I felt it was really important to raise awareness,” Moshiri told BBC News. On the venesection treatment, she said: “In about a space of five months, I had venesection seven or eight times. So you can imagine my iron levels hit the floor and I felt even more exhausted. “After a while, I started feeling extremely unwell and tired. I started losing my hair, I got itchy all over my body, but the main symptom was fatigue.” She continued: “It’s the kind of fatigue that is not like I’m just tired and I didn’t get a good night’s sleep, you feel like someone has removed your battery completely, and however much sleep you get makes no difference.” Moshiri has continued to work over the past two years, traveling overseas to anchor BBC News, including spending time in Qatar at the start of the U.S.-Israel war with Iran. “Even though I feel the best I have in two years, I don’t know how I’m going to be in six months, one year, two years,” she said. “People with PV have a higher chance of stroke, heart attack or DVT, so it’s something I always have to be aware of and make sure I mitigate.” Netflix Confirms Third ‘Inbetweeners’ Movie; First Look At Cast ‘Possible Love’ Rave Reaction; ‘Woman Unknown’ Snafu; Reviews; Photos Nights 1-2 Full Winners List; Rob Reiner Posthumous Win; Red Carpet Pix Surprise Movie ‘You Can See Everything’ Reviewed; More Pics In Focus Read More About: 1 Comments

The BBC revealed that audience members contacted the UK broadcaster to raise concerns that it was dedicating “too much” airtime to the Duke and Duchess of Sussex. The BBC did not disclose how many complaints it received from disgruntled viewers, but rejected the concerns in a notice published on its website . “We believe our approach to this story was proportionate, offering legitimate analysis of the different implications,” the BBC said. We gave appropriate scrutiny to these issues, reflecting the context in which they occur.” Coverage was fueled by speculation that Markle was returning to the UK to pursue an acting opportunity. Meredith, who is also a comedian, is coming off his Edinburgh Fringe debut show Need a Light? , which was nominated for a Best Newcomer Award. He will now join an ensemble also including Hammed Animashaun, Ayoade Bamgboye, Larry Dean, Celeste Dring, George Fouracres, Ania Magliano, Annabel Marlow, Al Nash, Jack Shep, Emma Sidi and Paddy Young. Meredith said it was a “no brainer” to join SNL UK , calling it, “The most iconic comedy show,” and adding: “It will undoubtedly inform everything I do for the rest of my career and I can’t wait for the experience.” Related Stories News Jeff Goldblum To Host Season 2 Premiere Of 'Saturday Night Live UK' News Sky Commits To Future Of 'Saturday Night Live UK': "We're In This For The Long Run" As announced last week, Jeff Goldblum will present the first episode of SNL UK Season 2 on Sky this Saturday (September 12), with CMAT the musical guest. Five more episodes will follow weekly until October 24 before a midseason break and a return in “early 2027.” Watch on Deadline Season 1 hosts included Tina Fey, Hannah Waddingham, and Nicola Coughlan. SNL UK is produced by Universal Television Alternative Studio’s UK production team and Broadway Video. Lorne Michaels serves as executive producer. James Longman is lead producer. Sky unscripted chief Phil Edgar-Jones told delegates at the recent Edinburgh Television Festival that the British remake of the iconic U.S. sketch show could continue beyond the second season . “We’re in this for the long run, and we’re super proud of it, and super proud of the team,” Edgar-Jones said, adding that he was pleased to have proved the social media “naysayers” wrong – referencing the general feeling from the British public and TV industry prior to the show’s launch that Season 1 would fail. articles.title: France & Korea Pledge $1.16B For Global Screen Industries At South Of France Cinema Summit
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Gaza Cinema Academy Launches At Venice Film Festival To Help Gazans Tell Their Own Stories ‘A Good Little Soldier’ Trailer: Alba Rohrwacher & Vincent Lindon Co-Star In Stéphane Brizé’s Venice Contender Exploring Toxic Corporate Culture Netflix Officially Confirms ‘The Inbetweeners’ Reunion Movie As Production Kicks Off With First Look At Original Cast In Reprised Roles View All September 7, 2026 6:08am France's President Emmanuel Macron (R) welcomes South Korea's President Lee Jae-myung at the "Lumière Summit" meeting on the future of cinema and the moving-image industry at the Maeght Foundation in Saint-Paul-de-Vence, AFP via Getty Images France and Korea pledged to invest 1 billion euros ($1.16 billion) in the global screen industries from 2027 to 2031, in a cornerstone announcement of President Emmanuel Macron’s Lumière Summit devoted to the future of the moving image unfolding in the South of France on Monday. Korean President Lee Jae Myung, who is on a four-day state visit to France and is co-hosting the global cinema meeting, joined Macron in announcing the funding. He said his country, which has been at the forefront of the global cross-border content boom with shows such as Squid Games and multi-Oscar winner Parasite , would take the lead “in producing content which resonates with humanity and transcends borders and language barriers.” Related Stories News Lee Chang-dong On His Eight-Year Hiatus & Confident Return With Venice Competition Title 'Possible Love' News Jean-Paul Rappeneau Dies: 'Cyrano de Bergerac' Director Was 94 The heads of state said other countries were welcome to join the partnership on the proviso they signed up for its commitments to human creativity, copyright protection and cultural diversity. Watch on Deadline The unveiling of the funding kicked off the Lumière Summit in Saint Paul-de-Vence, which is famous for its associations with artists such as Marc Chagall, Henri Matisse, and Pablo Picasso. The one day summit, taking its name from the French film pioneers Auguste and Louis Lumière, has gathered more than 200 high-profile figures from the world of cinema with announced guests including George Clooney, fresh from his Lifetime Achievement Award spree at the Venice Film Festival; Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos, NBCUniversal Entertainment Chairperson Donna Langley and CAA head Bryan Lourd among many more. Local industry figures in attendance include Mediawan co-founder Pierre-Antoine Capton, Canal+ Group CEO Maxime Saada and Cannes Film Festival Director Thierry Frémaux. articles.title: Colin Morgan & Katie Leung To Narrate BBC Studios Gothic Horror Podcast Drama ‘The Haunted Library’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Vertical Video Studio LoveHit Launches With Adaptations Of Literary Classics Starring Microdrama Regulars & Eric Roberts Steve Callaghan’s ‘Trivia Night Mysteries’ Cozy Crime Franchise Expands With Two Movies Colin Morgan & Katie Leung To Narrate BBC Studios Gothic Horror Podcast Drama ‘The Haunted Library’ View All September 7, 2026 6:45am Katie Leung and Colin Morgan will narrate 'The Haunted Library' BBC Studios EXCLUSIVE: Colin Morgan ( Merlin ) and Katie Leung ( Harry Potter ) will narrate The Haunted Library , a podcast about based around classic horror stories. The concept is for the pair to read titles from a fictional Gothic library, the doors to which open on September 21, with BBC Studios Audio producing and funding the series, which will comprise versions of stories from Edgar Allan Poe, Bram Stoker, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, Algernon Blackwood, M.R. James and more. Two episodes will launch each week on major podcast providers and BBC Sounds , the BBC’s audio platform. Subscribers to The Haunted Library Plus on Apple Podcasts will get early access and ad-free listens. Related Stories News Jon Ronson Culture Wars Series 'Things Fell Apart' Returns For Third Season On BBC - This Time Exploring David Vs. Goliath Stories News Jordan Stephens To Replace Lily Allen As Miquita Oliver's Permanent Co-Host For 'Miss Me?'; Hit Podcast Exits BBC Sounds Robert Louis Stevenson’s The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde will launch the series, with Morgan and Leung narrating the likes of Frankenstein , The Turn of the Screw , The Picture of Dorian Gray , Carmilla and The Invisible Man . Watch on Deadline “I’ve always been drawn to stories that explore the darker corners of the imagination, and it’s been a real pleasure to spend time with so many of the great works of Gothic literature,” said Morgan. “These are stories that have endured for generations, but there’s something particularly powerful about hearing them told aloud. I hope The Haunted Library gives listeners the chance to lose themselves in these extraordinary worlds and perhaps discover a few stories they haven’t encountered before.” “There’s something irresistible about the idea of a mysterious library filled with stories that have frightened and fascinated readers for centuries,” added Leung. “I love the atmosphere of The Haunted Library and the way it draws you into this strange, spooky world. I’m delighted to be joining Colin to bring these incredible stories to life.” Lydia Shamah, Creative Director, Fiction, at BBC Studio Audio said Morgan and Leung’s “exquisite narration perfectly captures the atmosphere of these classic tales which have remained so vivid in our collective imagination,” and added: “These stories are the foundations on which all subsequent horror – in literature and on film – has been built. And we can’t wait for listeners to discover how Colin and Katie have brought them to life in such a fresh and immersive way.” Netflix Confirms Third ‘Inbetweeners’ Movie; First Look At Cast ‘Possible Love’ Rave Reaction; ‘Woman Unknown’ Snafu; Reviews; Photos Nights 1-2 Full Winners List; Rob Reiner Posthumous Win; Red Carpet Pix Surprise Movie ‘You Can See Everything’ Reviewed; More Pics In Focus Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Piers Morgan Launches ‘Football Uncensored’ On YouTube After World Cup Series Scored 60M Views
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BBC News Presenter Maryam Moshiri Reveals She Has Incurable Blood Cancer Gary Oldman Claims James Bond Has Been Cast, As He Backs Jack Lowden To Play 007 Richard Osman Appears To Confirm ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ Premiere Date Amid Talk That Season 2 Was “Intense” To Film View All September 7, 2026 6:59am Piers Morgan and co-host Simon Jordan Uncensored EXCLUSIVE : Piers Morgan is turning his FIFA World Cup show into a permanent series. The British journalist is launching the weekly series Football Uncensored , expanding a roster of YouTube shows that includes Piers Morgan Uncensored and The Royals Uncensored . Morgan will co-host Football Uncensored with Simon Jordan , the former owner of Premier League club Crystal Palace and TalkSport pundit. Episode one will premiere on Monday. Alongside John Terry, Morgan and Jordan hosted World Cup Uncensored over the summer, which Uncensored said scored 60M streams across all social platforms over its 12 episodes. Related Stories News Piers Morgan Backed By Liz Murdoch As Part Of $27M Raise For Uncensored Venture News Piers Morgan's 'World Cup Uncensored' & 'The Royals Uncensored' Spin-offs Heading To Paramount's 5 Morgan said: “I can’t wait to kick off. Simon is a great sparring partner and we both love an on-air tear-up, so watch out for fireworks. But we are also passionate about football and we want everyone who shares that passion to be part of the Uncensored experience. Simply put, we aim to make Football Uncensored the most followed and most talked-about football debate show on the planet. Watch on Deadline “The response over the summer to our World Cup Uncensored show was phenomenal, with nearly a million views of our last episode, dwarfing any other online show audience during the tournament. We’ll carry on that momentum.” Morgan’s boast about 500,000 views appears to be a dig at rivals, including the well-resourced show The Rest is Football, hosted by Morgan’s friend Gary Lineker. The Rest is Football averaged more than 100,000 viewers on Netflix, which the streamer felt was enough to continue streaming the series into the Premier League season. Jordan added: “It strikes me in sports broadcasting that a lot of the conversations lack clarity, insight or courage. They are formulaic, one-dimensional and not very bold… I don’t suffer from those afflictions and my ethos of discuss, debate and resolve, teamed with my deep, real-world understanding of the business of sport, provides a real opportunity for this project of ours to dominate the sport’s media landscape.” In June, Morgan completed a $27M raise for his growing YouTube empire. Among those backing the former CNN anchor was Elisabeth Murdoch. Rashida Jones, the former MS NOW chief, serves as CEO of Uncensored. articles.title: Paul Thomas Anderson’s Cameron Winter Concert Film Joins London Film Festival Lineup As Mubi Acquires World Rights
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Paul Thomas Anderson’s Cameron Winter Concert Film Joins London Film Festival Lineup As Mubi Acquires World Rights Lee Chang-Dong’s ‘Possible Love’ Earns 6.5-Minute Ovation At Venice World Premiere A24’s ‘Primetime’, Starring Robert Pattinson As Chris Hansen, Lands 9-Minute Ovation At Venice World Premiere View All September 7, 2026 7:00am 'Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall' Mubi The London Film Festival has made several additions to this year’s lineup, including the concert film Paul Thomas Anderson shot at Carnegie Hall last year with Geese frontman Cameron Winter . Mubi has now also acquired global rights outside of North America to the film. Scroll down for the full list of LFF additions. Officially titled Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall, the film was shot during Winter’s sold-out solo run at Carnegie Hall in December 2025. Images of Anderson roaming around the concert venue with a large 35mm camera were shared widely on social media sites at the time. Filmmaker Bennie Safdie was also seen lurking at the shows with a camera. The Good Time filmmaker has now been listed as a producer on the project alongside Sara Murphy, Erica Frauman and Maggie Ambrose. Related Stories News London Film Festival Lineup: Ava DuVernay's '14th' & Boots Riley's 'I Love Boosters' Among Headline Titles -- Full List Festivals Hirokazu Kore-eda, Carol Morley & Lili Horvát In Competition At London Film Festival The concert film will screen as part of LFF’s Create strand. It will be the UK premiere. The film will drop on Mubi in 2027. Janus/Criterion are releasing the film in North America. Watch on Deadline The LFF has also added a series of new screen talks. Javier Bardem and Robert Eggers will now also participate in screen talks. Bardem has two films that will screen at the LFF: The Beloved and Bunker . Eggers is set to debut his latest feature, Werwulf , on New Year’s Day. This year’s LFF will run from October 7 to 18. The festival will open with the European Premiere of Simon Stone’s Elsinore , starring Andrew Scott, and close with the UK Premiere of Jesse Eisenberg’s The Debut . Other highlight titles include Ava DuVernay’s 14th, which will screen in the festival’s Special Presentations strand. The film details how the tenets of the 14th Amendment, ratified post-Civil War, are now under systematic attack. Other titles in the Special Presentations strand include a new restoration of Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger’s Gone To Earth and The Trip To The Northern Lights , the latest instalment in Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon’s travel comedy series. Michael Winterbottom has directed the series. NEW ADDITIONS TO THE PROGRAMME: ARTIFICIAL Sunday 11 October 21:00 and Friday 16 October 11:30 at the Southbank Centre’s Royal Festival Hall, Thursday 15 October 15:30 at Vue West End Director Luca Guadagnino. Screenwriter Simon Rich. Andrew Garfield, Yura Borisov, Monica Barbaro, Cooper Hoffman, Jason Schwartzman, Chris O’Dowd with Ike Barinholtz and Mark Rylance. USA-Italy 2026. 140min. Courtesy of NEON. Language English Luca Guadagnino returns to the Festival with his fascinating and of-the-moment origin story of Open AI and its co-founder, Sam Altman. Artificial homes in on the rise of Open AI and the tumultuous period that saw Altman ousted as CEO of his own company. Andrew Garfield has rarely been better in his portrayal of the tech entrepreneur, with an impressive cast joining him. Writer Simon Rich and Guadagnino ( Queer , LFF 2024; After the Hunt , LFF 2025) centre the human drama and ethical conundrums facing the creators of this life-changing technology. Screening as part of our GALA strand. CAMERON WINTER AT CARNEGIE HALL Wednesday 7 October 18:30 at Prince Charles Cinema and Thursday 8 October 15:00 at BFI Southbank Director Paul Thomas Anderson. With Cameron Winter. USA 2026. 71 min. Courtesy of MUBI. Language English. ‘One Battle After Another’ director Paul Thomas Anderson creates an intimate document of Geese frontman Cameron Winter’s solo piano performance at the legendary New York concert hall. In December 2025, Paul Thomas Anderson collaborated with fellow filmmaker Benny Safdie on a multi-perspective and multi-format recording of Winter’s solo performance. The warm hues capture the feeling in the room, including audience reactions, to create an immersive cinematic experience for those of us who couldn’t be there. It’s a rapturous celebration of live performance, whose appeal should reach far beyond the band and Winter’s existing fan base. Screening as part of our CREATE strand. EVEREST: THE OTHER SIDE Saturday 10 October 12:45 at Vue West End and Tuesday 13 October 18:20 at BFI Southbank Director Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi, Jimmy Chin. With Jim Morrison, Hilaree Nelson. USA 2026.113min. Courtesy of Walt Disney Studios. Language English This intimate portrait from the directors of Oscar winner Free Solo follows a mountaineering couple with a shared passion and ambition for the near-impossible. Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin once again show their passion for individuals who push themselves to the limits of human endurance. Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson share a dream of becoming the first to successfully climb up and ski down the north face of Everest – a feat that prompts concern among friends and family. The resulting film is a compelling and moving portrait of perseverance. Screening as part of our JOURNEY strand. JOY OF JOYS Sunday 11 October 13:45 Vue West End Director Jonathan Glazer. With Olivia Rodrigo, Arctic Monkeys. UK 2026. 38min. With some English subtitles Devised by Mica Levi and Jonathan Glazer, and seen through young eyes, Joy of Joys transforms the making of War Child’s record HELP(2) into something tender and playful. At Abbey Road, London schoolchildren film recording sessions with artists including Olivia Rodrigo, Arctic Monkeys and Jarvis Cocker – their small digital cameras capturing the music with curiosity and wonder. Meanwhile, children in Gaza, Sudan, Ukraine and Yemen record fragments of their daily lives. Moving between these images, the film finds in music a form of witness and refuge, and in childhood, a spirit of play and joy that persists amid catastrophe. Screening as part of our CREATE strand. PRIMETIME Sunday 11 October 18:00 at BFI IMAX Director Lance Oppenheim. Screenwriter Ajon Singh. With Robert Pattinson, Merritt Wever, and Anna Faris. USA 2026. 107min. Courtesy of A24. Language English. Contains Flashing images. Robert Pattinson continues his run of astonishing 2026 performances as he portrays the To Catch a Predator presenter Chris Hansen in this vivid and propulsive drama. It’s 2006 and despite its unconventional methods, To Catch a Predator is a US TV hit. When executives decide to move the show to a primetime slot, Hansen and his production team must up the ante to keep their audience, no matter the cost. Merritt Weaver and Skyler Gisondo also impress in this absorbing narrative feature debut from documentary filmmaker Lance Oppenheim. Screening as part of our THRILL strand. MISTY GREEN Monday 12 October 18:30 at Vue West End and Sunday 18 October 18:15 at BFI Southbank Director-Screenwriter Chris Rock. With Rosalind Eleazar, Adam Driver, Daniel Kaluuya USA 2026. 104min. Courtesy of A24 Films. Language English. Contains flashing images Chris Rock turns his eye to contemporary Hollywood in this biting comedy, in which a washed-up actress attempts to turn her life around in the course of a week. Misty Green used to be a somebody. These days, she’s barely scraping by. But when an old acquaintance re-enters her life, it looks like she might finally have the chance to start afresh. However, when the biggest obstacle is yourself, rebooting your life is not always so easy. Rosalind Eleazar is magnetic as Misty, and is joined by an all-star cast including Rock, Daniel Kaluuya and Adam Driver. Screening as part of our JOURNEY strand. INHERIT Friday 9 October 20:50 at Curzon Soho and Saturday 10 October 11:10 at Prince Charles Cinema Director Banjong Pisanthanakun. Screenwriter Banjong Pisanthanakun, Thamsatid Charoenrittichai, Chantavit Dhanasevi. With Davika Hoorne, Baipor Thitiya Jirapornsilp, Sinjai Plengpanich. Thailand 2026. 129min. Courtesy of Barunson E&A. Language Thai. A rich Thai family falls apart with the arrival of a distant relative in Banjong Pisanthanakun’s (The Medium, LFF 2021) gripping and unpredictable new horror. Grandma Woranart is full of surprises. She claims to be 80 but has the face of a beautiful young woman. That turns out to be the tip of the iceberg, as family secrets are gradually revealed, and it becomes all too apparent that something sinister lurks inside this seemingly benign relative. Featuring a magnetic performance by Davika Hoorne (A Useful Ghost), Inherit thrills as much as it chills. Screening this film as part of our CULT strand. JAVIER BARDEM SCREEN TALK Sunday 11 October 10:30 at Curzon Soho We welcome Javier Bardem to the Festival, whose Screen Talk accompanies his stunning performances in Gala entries The Beloved and Bunker. One of the most accomplished actors of his generation, Javier Bardem first gained attention with roles in Bigas Luna’s Jamón Jamón and Golden Balls. He followed it with an outstanding performance in Pedro Almodóvar’s thriller, Live Flesh. Further acclaim and international roles followed, with lead performances in Julian Schnabel’s Before Night Falls, for which he received his first Academy Award nomination, and John Malkovich’s The Dancer Upstairs, as well as a scene-stealing cameo in Michael Mann’s Collateral. His moving performance in Alejandro Amenábar’s The Sea Inside saw him win the fourth of his seven Goya awards, while his portrayal of a ruthless, sociopathic killer in the Coen Brothers’ No Country for Old Men brought him an Oscar, BAFTA and Golden Globe. He changed tack to play the charming object of desire for two American tourists in Vicky Cristina Barcelona, and followed it with a Cannes-winning performance as a dying man haunted by ghosts from the past in Alejandro González Iñárritu’s emotionally raw Biutiful. Bardem received another Oscar and Golden Globe nomination for his role in Aaron Sorkin’s Being The Ricardos, and was Emmy, SAG and Golden Globe-nominated as José Menendez in Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story. Over the last two decades, Javier Bardem has worked with Terrence Malick, Sam Mendes, Ridley Scott, Darren Aronofsky, Ryan Murphy, Josph Kosinski, and Denis Villeneuve. He played Silva, one of the most captivating Bond villains, in Skyfall, was terrifying as Max Cady in the serial adaptation of Cape Fear and will return to our screens in December as Stilgar in the much-anticipated third part of the Dune trilogy. ROBERT EGGERS SCREEN TALK Sunday 11 October, 17:30 VUE West End In advance of the New Years Day 2027 opening of Werwulf, we welcome writer-director-producer Robert Eggers to this Screen Talk to discuss his career. A master storyteller whose five features all unfold before the 20th century and revel in a world of myths, legends, folk tales and gothic atmosphere, Robert Eggers is one of the 21st century’s most distinctive filmmakers. Initially displaying an interest in theatre – where his vision for Nosferatu first began – he soon moved from experimental and street theatre to film, developing the story for his feature debut The Witch. Immersing himself in the early 17th century, he wrote a script with dialogue and a dialect as close to that era as he could achieve – an element of his process that would continue through all his subsequent work. The Witch proved an outlier among contemporary horror films and paved the way for his visually striking and boldly original sophomore feature, The Lighthouse. That saw Willem Dafoe and Robert Pattinson as two 19th-century lighthouse keepers gradually driven mad. The Northman, Robert Eggers’ first collaboration with Icelandic novelist Sjón, marked a significant increase in scale, as it detailed a Viking warrior’s trail of destruction as he avenges his murdered father. No less ambitious, Eggers’ take on F.W. Murnau’s Nosferatu is a gruesomely beautiful tale of tortured love and bloodlust, receiving four Oscar® and five BAFTA nominations. He returns with his most visceral and haunting experience yet, upcoming Werwulf, once again co-written with Sjón, a harrowing tale of devotion, damnation and the devil within. We welcome him to this Screen Talk to discuss these films and his vision of the world. articles.title: Steve Callaghan’s ‘Trivia Night Mysteries’ Cozy Crime Franchise Expands With Two Movies
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘SNL UK’ Adds Comedian & ‘Big Boys’ Actor Freddie Meredith To Season 2 Cast Dori Media Wants Buyers To Hunt ‘New Love’ At MIPCOM Dvizhon Studios Launches With Sex Education Series ‘The First Time’ A Featuring Puppet Presenter, Ukraine War Veteran & Social Media Star Tumazar View All September 7, 2026 7:00am Trivia Night Mysteries and Steve Callaghan (center) Nicely Entertainment EXCLUSIVE: There’s no question about it, Steve Callaghan ‘s Trivia Night Mysteries is expanding. The Nicely Entertainment -produced cozy crime franchise has wrapped production on its second and third instalments, Fit for a Murder and A Fatal Lesson , with stars Morgan Bradley ( The Christmas Recipe Files ) and Alex Trumble ( A Scottosh Christmas Secret ) reuniting in the lead roles as amateur sleuth Sara Keane and lawyer Reid Taggart, respectively. Emmy-nominated Family Guy writer Callaghan has written the new TV movies, which Nicely says combines clever whodunits, character-driven humor, small-town charm, and the flirtatious chemistry between Sara and Reid.” Vincenzo Conrorio directs the new instalments. Related Stories Acquisitions Romance 'Bee My Love' Scores U.S. & Canada TV Deals For Precious Metal Prods & Good Soldier Films News Former 'Family Guy' Showrunner Steve Callaghan Pens 'Trivia Night Mysteries'; Shoot Wraps With Morgan Bradley & Alex Trumble Starring The first movie in the franchise, Trivia Night Mysteries: A Question of Murder , makes its TV and streaming premiere in 2027. With production complete Fit for a Murder and A Fatal Lesson are expected to be completed and released in later next year, with pre-production on subsequent instalments already underway. Watch on Deadline “I conceived of the premise, world, and central characters of Trivia Night Mysteries by combining my lifelong love of whodunnits with my experience writing and hosting weekly Zoom trivia quizzes as a personal hobby I took upon myself to help friends stay connected during the pandemic lockdown,” said Callaghan. “Now seeing my initial concept grow into an ongoing series of multiple movies has been incredibly rewarding, and I’m enormously thrilled and grateful that my two leads, Sara and Reid, will be continuing their crime-solving and romantic adventures.” “ Trivia Night Mysteries has all the ingredients of a marquee feel-good franchise: brilliant writing, magnetic characters, genuine heart, and clever whodunits that leave audiences constantly guessing,” added Vanessa Shapiro, founder and CEO of Nicely. “Successfully wrapping production on both movies number two and number three speaks volumes about the momentum behind this property. We fully believe in the international appeal of these stories, and we can’t wait to bring these next chapters to fans around the world.” Today’s news comes ahead of MIPCOM in Cannes next month, where Nicely and its competitors will be shopping their latest wares to international buyers. The Trivia Night Mysteries series follows freelance fact-checker and team trivia champion Keane, whose exceptional trivia knowledge and instinct for finding the right answer make her an unlikely but highly effective amateur detective. She works closely with charming, new-to-town lawyer Taggart, who becomes her increasingly close partner in crime-solving. In Trivia Night Mysteries: Fit for a Murder , Keane is hired for a fact-checking job on a series of articles about women’s health for a national fitness magazine, only to discover her editor’s body, apparently having been strangled. As she begins to investigate, she needs to piece together the editor’s final days to unmask the killer. Trivia Night Mysteries: A Fatal Lesson will see Keane attends an auction fundraiser for the school where her mother serves as Vice Principal, only for the school superintendent to be pushed to his death. Keane, Taggart and the rest of the trivia team dig into the administrator’s backstory to reveal the murderer’s motive and identity. Shapiro and Scott Kirkpatrick, EVP of Distribution and Co-Productions at Nicely, serve as executive producers on the Trivia Night Mysteries movie series, with Callaghan another EP and the showrunner. Focused on feel-good entertainment, Nicely makes cozy mysteries such as The Abigail Mysteries for Great American Family and Great American Pure Flix and The Christmas Recipe Files for QVC+, which also starred Bradley. It also makes Crossroad Springs , which has been renewed for a second season by Great American Media. Callaghan remains a writer and executive producer for Family Guy , having worked on the series since its inception and spending nearly seven seasons as its showrunner. He was also a writer, executive producer and showrunner for American Dad! and has written for CBS’ Yes, Dear and MTV’s 3-South . Callaghan is repped by Yorn Levine Barnes.
