articles.title: Maureen Lipman Tells “Cowardly” Co-Star To “Grow Up” After He Quit Play Over Her Pro-Israel Views
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Jasmine Jobson Teases Details About Netflix’s ‘Top Boy’ Spin-Off Series ‘Jaq’: “She’s Going Down A Crazy Rabbit Hole” Maureen Lipman Tells “Cowardly” Co-Star To “Grow Up” After He Quit Play Over Her Pro-Israel Views ‘Entourage’ Creator Doug Ellin Denies Debi Mazar’s “Disgusting” Claim About Being Fat-Shamed On HBO Series After Giving Birth View All September 2, 2026 2:00am Maureen Lipman Getty Maureen Lipman , the BAFTA-nominated actress known for her work in The Pianist , has hit out at co-star Gerard McCarthy after he quit their Soho Theatre play over her pro-Israel stance. Lipman and McCarthy were due to share a stage in Stan Zimmerman’s Right Before I Go on September 5, but McCarthy walked away from the project citing Lipman’s political views. In an Instagram post, McCarthy said: “Because of views she has publicly and repeatedly expressed regarding Israel and Palestine, I did not feel comfortable personally promoting her involvement. Related Stories News Maureen Lipman Attacks BAFTA "Numbskulls" Over Gender-Neutral Award Engravings News UK March Against Antisemitism Attended By Maureen Lipman, Eddie Marsan, Boris Johnson “I did not ask for her casting to be reconsidered or expect anyone else to share my position. I simply chose not to use my own platform to promote someone whose political views are at odds with my own.” Watch on Deadline View this post on Instagram Responding in The Times of London , Lipman described McCarthy as “cowardly” for quitting the play without speaking to her directly. She said his Instagram post was “virtue-signalling” and called on the actor, who has appeared in The Fall , to “grow up.” “I am asking for him to have the courage to face me and tell me what he thinks it is I should do, or think, or say,” she said. “I would like to reassure him that I will not be arriving with a star of David on my forehead, nor am I trying to argue him out of his point of view. “He has to wake up and smell the grass. I have worked with actors for 60 years who often don’t share my politics. I don’t ask them, and they don’t ask me.” Lipman added that McCarthy’s position was curious given it came just weeks after he attended the opening night of Richmond Theatre’s production of Allegra , in which the Olivier Award-winning actress was the lead. McCarthy posed for a photo in front of a poster featuring Lipman’s name in large print. Gerard McCarthy “I would love to know what has changed in the last six weeks. Has he become radicalised, and by whom?” Lipman said. “I am at a loss, but I would like to extend the olive branch and get a proper understanding of his problem with me. “I am simply a working woman of a certain age who believes that the state of Israel should be allowed to exist. I am an actor, not a politician. There is very little I can do to influence (Israeli prime minister) Bibi Netanyahu, nor would I want to.” McCarthy has been approached for comment. Lipman, 80, supports Israel’s right to exist and defend itself, and has previously been critical of artists who publicly back Palestine without mentioning Hamas. articles.title: ‘Bunker’: Watch Javier Bardem & Penélope Cruz In Florian Zeller’s Venice-Bound Psychological Thriller
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana Cynthia Erivo, Andrew Scott, Ava DuVernay, Jesse Eisenberg & More Set For London Film Festival Screen Talks Program Tom Hiddleston Thriller ‘Tenzing’ To Open Zurich Film Festival Marketing Executive Kevin Harrington Launches New Entertainment Agency Patrick Patrick View All September 2, 2026 2:17am EXCLUSIVE : Here’s an exclusive clip from Florian Zeller’s upcoming Venice competition title Bunker starring Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem . The psychological thriller, which Zeller wrote, produced and directed, follows the emotional and moral challenges faced by a couple in an increasingly uncertain world. Bardem plays Miguel, a successful London architect, who considers a prestigious offer to build a survivalist bunker for a tech billionaire. The project causes his wife Sofia (Cruz) to question their relationship of 17 years as they are drawn deeper into a life of extreme wealth, paranoia and fear. The intrusion of an unsettling neighbor becomes another source of anxiety. Related Stories Festivals Zurich Bolsters Position As Awards Circuit Stop-Off As 'Bunker', 'Club Kid' & 'Adult Supervision' Join Gala Lineup Documentary First Look At 'Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing,' Documentary With Rare Access To Giants Of The Ring - Venice Film Festival Additional cast include Stephen Graham ( Adolescence ), Paul Dano ( There Will Be Blood ) and Patrick Schwarzenegger ( The White Lotus ). The French-Spanish co-production is produced by Federica Sainte-Rose, Zeller for Blue Morning Pictures, Fernando Bovaira and Simon de Santiago of MOD Producciones and Alice Dawson. Pathé’s Ardavan Safaee and Mediawan’s Pierre-Antoine Capton serve as co-producers. Earlier this year, Sony Pictures Classics acquired North American, Southeast Asian and worldwide airline rights (excluding France) for the title. The film continues SPC’s relationship with Zeller that dates back to the release of his first film, Oscar winner The Father , and his second film The Son . FilmNation Entertainment is handling international sales on the film while CAA Media Finance and WME repped domestic rights. Pathé is set to distribute the film in France, Switzerland and West Africa. Bunker is set to world premiere In Competition at the Venice International Film Festival on September 8. Check out the clip above. articles.title: Jean-Paul Rappeneau Dies: ‘Cyrano de Bergerac’ Director Was 94
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Venice Jury Head Maggie Gyllenhaal Calls For Empathy In Politically Charged Times; Addresses Dearth Of Women In Competition: “It’s A Systemic Problem” Jean-Paul Rappeneau Dies: ‘Cyrano de Bergerac’ Director Was 94 Ukrainian Drama ‘Camouflage’ Set Sales With MMM Films – Venice View All September 2, 2026 2:22am Jean-Paul Rappeneau at Romy Schneider Exhibition At La Cinematheque In Paris in 2023 Getty Images French director and screenwriter Jean-Paul Rappeneau , who was best known internationally for the 1990 Oscar-nominated drama Cyrano de Bergerac , died on September 2 his family has announced. He was 94. Born on April 8, 1932 in the town of Auxerre in central France , Rappeneau’s career spanned more than 50 years of French cinema history. His early screenwriting credits include Louis Malle’s Zazie in the Metro ((1960)and A Very Private Affair (1962) as well as Philippe de Broca’s classic thriller That Man From Rio starring Jean-Paul Belmondo. Related Stories News Donald Trump Pays Tribute To Dolly Parton, Says He's Lowering U.S. Flags To Honor Entertainer News Saudi Arabia To Invest $7 Billion In Three Theme Parks Near Paris He broke into feature film directing in 1966 with A Matter of Resistance , a romantic comedy set on the eve of France’s World War Two liberation starring Catherine Deneuve. Watch on Deadline The pair would work together again on his 1975 film Le Sauvage , co-starring Yves Montand as a man living a solitary on a Caribbean island who becomes entangled with a runaway bride. Other directorial credits include All Fired Up (1982) and Horseman on the Roof (1995). He is best known internationally, however, for his big screen adaptation of Edmond Rostand’s 1897 stage play Cyrano de Bergerac starring Gerard Depardieu in the titular role. After world premiering in 1990 in Cannes, where Depardieu won Best Actor, the film enjoyed a buzzy awards season garnering five nominations in the lead up to the 63rd Academy Awards, including for Best Actor and Best Foreign Language Film. It missed out on both prizes, but won Best Costume Design for Franca Squarciapino. Rappeneau’s last feature-length directorial credit was the comedy drama Families starring Mathieu Amalric as a Shanghai-based French financier who returns home to find the family mansion is being sold off. articles.title: ‘Kill Jackie’: Catherine Zeta-Jones Is On The Run In Prime Video & AMC+’s Pulsating Thriller Series; Launch Date Set
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse David Oyelowo & Nate Parker’s Mansa Studios Debuts Slate Of TikTok Microdramas ‘Kill Jackie’: Catherine Zeta-Jones Is On The Run In Prime Video & AMC+’s Pulsating Thriller Series; Launch Date Set ‘Gunsmoke & Mirrors’, Drama Series About Danish Criminal Turned American Frontier Hero Chris Madsen, In The Works View All September 2, 2026 3:00am Buckle up for a global thrill ride. Catherine Zeta-Jones is on the run in the first trailer for action series Kill Jackie . Zeta-Jones is is seen shooting shotguns, taking out home-raiding assassins with guns hidden in artwork and charting a private aircraft as her character, former drug smuggler Jackie Price, attempts to evade The Seven Demons, a squad of the world’s most terrifying hired hitmen. There’s even a nod to 28 Days Later , with Zeta-Jones hobbling across a deserted Westminster Bridge in London wearing blue hospital scrubs, just like Cillian Murphy’s Jim in the 2002 horror movie. Watch the full trailer above. Related Stories Casting Alex Kingston, Iain Glen & Sean Pertwee Among 7 Cast In Prime Video's Ray Winstone Action-Comedy Series 'Danger Money' News Prime Video Sets Premiere Date For Third & Final Season Of 'Maxton Hall' The trailer comes as distributor Fremantle revealed that Stan in Australia, Yes in Israel, Sky TV in New Zealand, Sky Italia in Italy and Globoplay in Brazil have acquired the show. Prime Video was the orginal buyer, taking it for the UK, Ireland, Netherlands, Turkey, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg and Canada, with AMC+ snapping up U.S. rights. Watch on Deadline In further news, Prime Video, AMC+ and Stan have announced a October premiere date with the other territories announcing soon. Based on Sunday Times bestselling author Nick Harkaway ‘s acclaimed novel The Price You Pay , the eight-part series follows Zeta-Jones as Jackie Price, a former international drug smuggler whose carefully constructed new life is thrown into chaos when a team of elite assassins is sent to kill her. The show comes from creative talent behind Killing Eve and Gangs of London , and stars Zeta-Jones ( Chicago , Wednesday ) alongside Daniel Ings ( A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The Gentlemen ), Sidse Babett Knudsen ( Prime Target , Borgen ), Bill Paterson ( Fleabag , Criminal Justice ), Ron Perlman ( Hellboy ), Óscar Jaenada ( Rambo V , Cantinflas ) and Hattie Hook ( Of An Age , Ten Pound Poms ) among others. Also cast are Darci Shaw ( A Thousand Blows , This City is Ours ), Raff Law ( Masters of The Air , Triton ), Enzo Cilenti ( Black Mirror , The Crown ), Christine Adams ( Hijack , Malice ), Julian Rhind-Tutt ( Britannia , Napoleon ), Karlis Arnolds Avots ( Soviet Jeans , Lovable ), Set Sjöstrand ( The Wheel of Time , Valhalla ), Tadashi Ito ( Society of the Snow , The Platform 2 ), Sebastian Armesto ( Gangs of London , A Small Light ), Julian Barratt ( The Mighty Boosh , The Great ), Gavin Spokes ( House of The Dragon , Slow Horses ), Jonathan Cake ( And Just Like That , Camping ) and Bamshad Abedi-Amin ( A Town Called Malice , The Last Kingdom ). Fremantle and Steel Springs Pictures are the co-producers, with Conor Keane, Tom Butterworth ( Gangs of London ), Peter Lawson ( John Wick ) and Damon Thomas ( Killing Eve ) the co-creators. Butterworth is the writer and showrunner and Keane co-wrote the TV adaptation and is an associate producer. Harkaway was an executive consultant. Executive producers are Lawson and Jose Agustin Valdes for Steel Springs, Butterworth, Damon Thomas, Zeta-Jones, Rebecca Dundon, Dante Di Loreto and Jeffrey Levine. The lead director is Damon Thomas. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac London Film Festival Lineup: Ava DuVernay’s ‘14th’ & Boots Riley’s ‘I Love Boosters’ Among Headline Titles — Full List Julianne Moore To Receive Zurich’s Golden Icon Award Indie Media Outfit Alexander Opens Film Arm With Kevin Chan, Hamish Moseley On Board And ‘Ben’imana’ Set As First Release View All September 2, 2026 3:00am 14th. The sitting Librarian of Congress Carla Hayden with filmmaker Ava DuVernay in Washington, DC in January 2025. Cr. Paul Garnes/Netflix © 2026 The full 2026 London Film Festival lineup has been confirmed, with Ava DuVernay’s latest feature documentary, 14th, and Boots Riley’s I Love Boosters among the headline titles. This year’s LFF will run from October 7 to 18. The festival will open with the European Premiere of Simon Stone’s Elsinore , starring Andrew Scott, and close with the UK Premiere of Jesse Eisenberg’s The Debut . DuVernay’s 14th will screen in the festival’s Special Presentations strand. The film details how the tenets of the 14th Amendment, ratified post-Civil War, are now under systematic attack. Other titles in the Special Presentations strand include a new restoration of Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger’s Gone To Earth and The Trip To The Northern Lights , the latest instalment in Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon’s travel comedy series. Michael Winterbottom has directed the series. Related Stories Festivals Hirokazu Kore-eda, Carol Morley & Lili Horvát In Competition At London Film Festival Festivals 'Hamnet' & 'The Beatles' Producer Pippa Harris & 'The Zone Of Interest' Producer James Wilson To Headline LFF's Industry Forum Boots Riley’s I Love Boosters travels to London for its first screenings this side of the pond almost six months after its U.S. release. The film will screen as one of the festival’s Headline Galas. Other Headline Gala titles include Jordan Firstman’s Club Kid , Cristian Mungiu’s Fjord , and Taika Waititi’s Klara and The Sun adaptation. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Baz Bamigboye Baz Bamigboye Columnist/International Editor At Large @BazBam More Stories By Baz Breaking Baz: Broadway’s Intoxicating ‘Buena Vista Social Club’ Musical Eyes London Transfer In 2027, Say Producers Orin Wolf & Barbara Broccoli Breaking Baz: ‘MobLand’s Joanne Froggatt In Advanced Talks To Play Quaker Leader In MGM+’s ‘The Magnificent Seven’ Remake Breaking Baz: Hammer’s ‘Horror Of Dracula’ Starring Christopher Lee Is Ready To Sink Its Teeth Into Audiences At Halloween With Censored Scenes Restored – Exclusive Interview View All September 2, 2026 3:00am (L to R) Guy Pearce as Murdoch and Jack OConnell as Lamb in Ink. Anthony Dickenson The Sun sure shone for me. “Get on the bloody Concorde with Jerry!” The Sun’s news editor barked when I rang in the old-fashioned way from a call box at JFK. It was 1982. When I queried how to pay for the hefty cost of a seat on an Air France supersonic jet to Charles de Gaulle airport in Paris, I was told, “Pick up the pre-paid ticket from the desk and get on the bloody plane.” The ‘Jerry’ in question was Jerry Hall. She was dating Mick Jagger but had entered into a brief fling with racing tycoon Robert Sangster, who was a big noise back then. Related Stories Festivals Zurich Bolsters Position As Awards Circuit Stop-Off As 'Bunker', 'Club Kid' & 'Adult Supervision' Join Gala Lineup News Guy Pearce Gives 'Priscilla, Queen Of The Desert 2' Filming Update My Sun colleagues back at the paper’s Fleet Street office had just discovered that Jagger was planning to reunite with Hall, the glamorous cover girl and catwalk star, in Paris. My task was to accompany her on the flight and get her to talk. Even a simple “hello” or “piss off” from her was worth a thousand words to the paper. Watch on Deadline John Kay, The Sun’s then-chief reporter, used to say that whatever words a subject uttered was copy. You could, in theory, write, ”Jerry Hall spoke for the first time today, amid her reunion with Rolling Stones front man Mick Jagger, following her brief liaison with millionaire playboy Robert Sangster…” And that’s how it went down. Legendary photographer Arthur Edwards was waiting to snap a photo as Jerry exited customs. She ran into Jagger’s arms as he cooed, ”Hello babe.” It was all so easy-peasy. I was The Sun’s U.S. correspondent based in Manhattan. After that perfect airport rapprochement, Edwards and I tailed them to Jagger’s chateau near Amboise in the Loire Valley. I had a travel bag with a change of clothes but it was freezing. I swiftly purchased a double-breasted wool and camel hair Burberry overcoat (on expenses — thank you, Rupert Murdoch) which, amazingly, I still have. It’s not in bad nick and it’s perfect for walking the dogs on winter weekends. The aforementioned tale and other crazy memories came flooding back as I watched Danny Boyle ’s scorching new movie Ink , which opens the Venice Film Festival on the Lido on Wednesday. Jack O’Connell as Larry Lamb in ‘Ink’ Anthony Dickenson The film is a sort of origin story for the tabloid papers as we know them today. Jack O’Connell ( Sinners, 28 Years Later ) stars as Larry Lamb, a then-little-known, Yorkshire-born news executive on the U.K.’s biggest selling daily paper, the Daily Mirror. The business-savvy Murdoch approaches Lamb with a plan to relaunch a rival to the Mirror: The Sun newspaper, a middling broadsheet he’s bought for a pittance from Hugh Cudlipp’s IPC publishing group. And this mission suits Lamb just fine, because IPC also owns the Daily Mirror, and Lamb is out for revenge against his employers for not promoting him. Lamb gamely assembles a team of brilliant misfits and The Sun relaunches as a tabloid in November, 1969. O’Connell is superb as the brilliant newspaper tactician Lamb. It’s a huge performance, even Shakespearean in stature, as glory turns to tragedy. In the stage version of Ink , written by James Graham , which premiered in London in 2017, the role of Murdoch was played by Bertie Carvel ( Dalgiesh , Doctor Foster ) and he was magnificent. But for this film incarnation of Graham’s story, Boyle wanted an Australian to portray the man labelled the ‘Dirty Digger’. And Guy Pearce cracks it as the Aussie who beat the Brits at their own game of publishing. Doyle’s ‘big three’ cast is rounded out by Claire Foy ( The Crown, Women Talking ), who is ferociously good as Jules, an amalgam of the group of women Lamb gathered for plumb posts on the Sun. Claire Foy as Jules Davies in ‘Ink’ Anthony Dickenson Boyle introduced Foy to former newspaper editor and columnist Eve Pollard (who happens to be the mother of The Traitors host Claudia Winkleman). “Claire loved her biting wit and modeled herself primarily on Eve and other pioneering Sun women, such as Joyce Hopkirk, who went from being the paper’s first women’s editor to editor of the U.K. Cosmopolitan,” Boyle tells me when we get on the phone to discuss the film. He took Graham’s award-winning play of the same name and spun it into cinema art. “It’s cracking the Magnificent Seven of it. Assembling a bunch of people. They were the underdogs, and Larry and Rupert turned them into all-stars,” Boyle says. The Sun soared. Within months, it was outselling the Mirror and in its heyday, the paper sold four million copies a day. The runaway hit paper was laced with stories about the shenanigans of stars, politicians, footballers, Page 3 girls (back then, topless female models were on every issue’s opening spread), horoscopes, sport, female-aimed features and serializations of books about matters of sex — all with pithy, attention-grabbing headlines, saucy graphics and photos. The paper absolutely revolutionized daily newspaper habits. “It’s taken us to where we are now with the internet,” Boyle says, adding, “we can’t complain about it because we bought it. No one forced us to.” Brian Gleeson, Patrick Kennedy, Claire Foy, Christopher Fulford and Blake Harrison in ‘Ink’ Anthony Dickenson In Darkest Hour , for which Gary Oldman won a Best Actor Oscar for his portrayal of wartime leader Winston Churchill, the great statesman is seen riding on the London Underground — a bit of poetic license. But Murdoch actually did ride around on the tube, checking out which newspapers were being read. “It’s true,” Boyle says. “Back then, he wasn’t the household name he is now. He blended in.” And it was such scenes as this that allowed Boyle and Graham to turn a stage-bound story into a big-screen tale. Boyle studied film adaptations of Peter Shaffer’s Amadeus , which was turned into an Oscar-winning Best Picture by Miloš Forman, and Christopher Hampton’s Les liaisons dangereuses , from which filmmaker Stephen Frears created Dangerous Liaisons , which won three Oscar trophies and was nominated for Best Film. “I looked at them because these two films were based on stage plays but in the hands of Forman and Frears they became pure cinema,” Boyle says. Boyle says he’s in such awe of Frears ( The Queen, The Grifters, Philomena ) that he and others are encouraging the British Film Institute to honor Frears with a “big BFI season” of his movies. Guy Pearce as Murdoch and Jack O’Connell as Lamb in ‘Ink’ Anthony Dickenson When Kelvin MacKenzie took over as The Sun’s editor in 1981, he hired me away from the Evening Standard to become The Sun’s show business and general reporter in London. I covered riots in Brixton, South London, and when there was unrest in Liverpool, MacKenzie ordered teams of reporters to cover the mayhem. But covering movie and rock stars was my main beat. One time, I showed up at Elizabeth Taylor’s pad in Chelsea and handed her a bouquet of flowers. She was huge news in those days. By then, Richard Burton was divorced from Taylor and married to Sally Burton, but still, he turned up for Taylor’s 50th birthday celebrations. So, of course, I followed him. It turned out he was staying at the Dorchester Hotel, where I somehow managed to persuade him to let me inside his suite. As he poured out his heart about “darling Elizabeth” (and poured booze down his throat), I would excuse myself to the bathroom every fifteen minutes to write up notes on the crinkly, hard loo paper. Not to boast (OK, I will), but the resulting spread brought me job offers from rival papers. So, Murdoch and MacKenzie dispatched me to New York to keep the poachers at bay. Talk about fun on the Sun! I had the time of my life! “Joan Collins has a cold. She’s in Los Angeles. Take her flowers and get an interview.” Director Danny Boyle and Jack O’Connell as Lamb on the set of ‘Ink’ Nick Wall “Rod Stewart’s living it up in Hollywood. Go see him.” One day, the instruction came: “Randy Andy (the former Prince Andrew) is on a plane with model Koo Stark bound for Barbados. They’re headed for Mustique, and the Daily Express is with them. Go and join them.” “The local authorities won’t let me stay on the island,” I wailed. “Charter a yacht!” came the reply. But I was also told to share said yacht with rival journalists to cover the costs, mind you. Every morning, we’d row or swim to Basil’s Bar, where we were allowed to avail ourselves of his food and drink, for a price. Island security would corral us at Basil’s. However, a few of us would slope off to try and interact with the prince and his starlet. My photographer Matthew Ford and the Daily Mail’s snapper Peter Carrette were arrested. When we tried to bail them out of jail, Carrette managed to covertly pass me his roll of film. By rights it belonged to the Mail. But I had it, so they had to share. The resulting photo that ran in The Sun of a bare-chested Andrew was headlined Me Tarzan, You Koo. The escapade cost thousands of dollars. The Sun’s managing editor was livid. He still approved my expenses. There were many other such jolly outings in the Caribbean, South America and across the U.S., all with the aim of filling column inches with showbiz and a few actual hard news stories. The thing about The Sun was, they had a crack team of reporters and editing staff who would turn your turn your copy into gold. People used to ask if I was ever embarrassed about working on The Sun. I wasn’t. When I accompanied Andrew from Barbados back to London, a TV newsman interviewed me after I landed at Heathrow and asked me to justify the time and money spent chasing the prince and the showgirl. I simply replied that “I was enjoying myself.” A year or so later, the Daily Mail’s editor David English was in Manhattan. He came a-courting and I switched papers. My days in The Sun were over. Guy Pearce as Murdoch in ‘Ink’ Anthony Dickenson The best movies set in the newspaper world are mostly American ones. Boyle cites Billy Wilder’s Ace in the Hole . And, of course, there’s Alexander Mackendrick’s Sweet Smell of Success , Howard Hawks’ His Girl Friday , Alan J. Pakula’s All the President’s Men and Tom McCarthy’s Spotlight . The only British movie that springs to mind is Val Guest’s The Day the Earth Caught Fire — and now there’s Boyle’s Ink . It joins that list because it’s a portrait of Britain that also reflects aspects of our society now, for good and bad. In Graham’s play Ink , it was Carvel’s larger than life portrayal of Murdoch that seemed to dominate the piece. Graham tells me that Boyle “wanted to slightly tilt the balance” towards what “I think was the surprise in the play — that everyone assumed they were coming to watch a biography of Murdoch, and that Murdoch is the agent of all this change. I think what delighted Danny was the idea that actually no, it’s Larry Lamb, this guy you’ve never heard of, who who drove a lot of those most radical changes and built a lot of what would become the template for modern day populist sensational news. Danny really delights in that.” Boyle says that he was initially apprehensive about seeking out Carvel to play the Mirror’s owner Hugh Cudlipp. “I loved the play and I remembered when I saw Bertie do it, that theater is a celebration of live performance. But for the film, I wanted Bertie to flex different muscles as Cudlipp. I thought he’d kill me when I approached him about Cudlipp. And he did go, ‘Oh, f–k, really?’ But when I explained that I wanted an Australian for Murdoch he understood what I was saying and took Cudlipp and captures him.” But it’s O’Connell’s Lamb that’s at the heart of the film. Boyle thought of Al Pacino in The Godfather Part II when he was working on the script with Graham. “You see Pacino’s Michael Corleone shut out the people closest to him and Lamb does that in Ink . Jack does that. His desire to create this newspaper makes him lose his soul,” Boyle says. Graham notes that what’s liberating for him is “you know everybody has strong feelings about The Sun in particular, and Murdoch’s empire more generally. What’s liberating for us, I guess, is by going back to the beginning, you don’t have to worry about the politics of the now in painting too much on that. You’re basically going, this is how the newspaper was built. This is how it started. Isn’t it quite surprising, actually, that a lot of the people who built it were working class outsiders, often from the north and around the country — a group of people trying to make the news less pompous and less earnest, and make it fun.” But of course, now we’re in an era where everything has changed. 24 hour news and commentary taking over from the facts has only escalated, but also, social media and AI and the platforms in which we share information now are all about engagement. It’s all about distraction and engagement and activation rather than what people might need to hear, or what the boring truth is. And that is worrying. “I think I’m terrified and worried about all those things,” Graham says. And going back to the surprising origins of in The Sun in the 1960s has made him see that the state of how we get our news now is “more urgent than ever.” Ink has its U.S. theatrical release on December 11, U.K. theatrical through StudioCanal is January 8 and it’s on Netflix in the U.S. from January 8. articles.title: ‘Miraculous’ Studio Founder Jeremy Zag To Receive Deadline’s French TV Disruptor Award At The Unifrance Rendez-Vous
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Audible’s ‘Harry Potter’ Full-Cast Audiobooks Conjure Over 5M Sales ‘Sopranos’ Alums Michael Imperioli & Steve Schirripa Reunite For 9/11 Mob Audio Drama ‘UnderGround Zero’ From iHeartPodcasts & Thoroughbred Prime Video Sets Premiere Date For Third & Final Season Of ‘Maxton Hall’ View All September 2, 2026 3:00am Jeremy Zag Zag, Unifrance Jeremy Zag will receive Deadline’s 2026 French TV Disruptor Award. Zag founded the iconic Zag Entertainment banner in 2009 and it went on to become a leading international animation studio, responsible for shows including global hit Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir . France has traditionally had a dynamic animation sector and Zag has been in the vanguard. A producer, director, writer, and composer for both film and TV, Zag will receive his French TV Disruptor Award at the Unifrance Rendez-Vous event, which is the largest market of the year dedicated to buying and selling French-language programming. It is appropriate, given Zag’s shows have traveled far and wide and are on streaming platforms and channels around the world. Related Stories News Unifrance Rendez-Vous In Paris Unfolds Amid Complex Time For French Films As Local Indie Biz Internationalizes News International Insider: Banijay & All3 Cozy Up; Indian Box Office Record; Unifrance Rendez-Vous Review Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir Zag Zag is a co-creator of Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir alongside Thomas Astruc and Nathanaël Bronn. It follows two Parisian teens who transform into the titular superheroes to fight supervillains and baddies. As well as multiple seasons of the show and TV specials, there has been a successful feature adaptation. Other Zag shows include Ghostforce , Zak Storm and Power Players . Watch on Deadline In 2024, Zag partnered with French super-indie Mediawan to create Miraculous Corp, a joint venture to handle – and expand – the Miraculous franchise. Zag will sit down with Deadline at the Rendez-Vous to discuss the business, and his approach to building animation franchises and connecting with younger audiences. He follows in the footsteps of Fanny Herrero ( Call My Agent! ), who received last year’s French TV Disruptor Award. The award will be presented to Zag at the closing cocktail reception at the Rendez-Vous, which is a glitzy affair held at the historic Montivilliers Abbey and hosted by Hervé Morin, President of the Normandy Region. Deadline’s Disruptors strand is well established with a renowned annual Cannes Disruptors magazine and International Disruptors column. The French TV Disruptor Award is in recognition of Zag’s contribution to the world of TV. articles.title: Jasmine Jobson Teases Details About Netflix’s ‘Top Boy’ Spin-Off Series ‘Jaq’: “She’s Going Down A Crazy Rabbit Hole”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Jasmine Jobson Teases Details About Netflix’s ‘Top Boy’ Spin-Off Series ‘Jaq’: “She’s Going Down A Crazy Rabbit Hole” Maureen Lipman Tells “Cowardly” Co-Star To “Grow Up” After He Quit Play Over Her Pro-Israel Views ‘Entourage’ Creator Doug Ellin Denies Debi Mazar’s “Disgusting” Claim About Being Fat-Shamed On HBO Series After Giving Birth View All September 2, 2026 3:34am Jasmine Jobson as Jaq in 'Top Boy' Ali Painter/Netflix © 2022 EXCLUSIVE : Jasmine Jobson has said that Netflix ‘s Top Boy spin-off series about her character Jaq Lawrence will be an “insane” addition to the world created by Ronan Bennett. Netflix announced last week that Jobson would reprise her role for the six-part series, which will be a sequel to Top Boy after the drama concluded in 2023. Working titled Jaq , the show will shoot next year and is part of a wider expansion of the Top Boy universe, with Barry Keoghan returning as Irish mobster Jonny McGee in prequel Jonny Boy . Related Stories News 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Extended Preview Is Netflix's Most-Watched Weekly Title News Netflix Signs Global Deal For British True Crime Podcast 'Outlore With Eleanor Neale' In an interview with Deadline, Jobson said Jaq will pick up five years after the events of the final season of Top Boy , in which Jaq tried to get out of the Summerhouse drug game. Watch on Deadline The character is living in a seaside town when someone close to her goes missing, pulling her back into a world she attempted to escape. “She’s definitely going down a very crazy rabbit hole, and I can’t confirm or deny who, what, or whatever’s going on, but all I can say is that it is going to be insane,” Jobson said. “She’s in a completely different environment. So when all of this is kicking off, it’s really drawing her back into a whole heap of craziness that I don’t know if she’s 100% prepared for. She’s just got to figure it out. We know she’s good at figuring things out.” Jobson won a BAFTA TV Award for her portrayal of Jaq. Soon after collecting the prize, she told Deadline that she was not prepared to relinquish the character and was open to a spin-off series. Two years on and Jobson’s ambition has become a reality. She has worked closely with writer Ryan Calais Cameron to create Jaq and will serve as an executive producer on the drama. Cameron has written episodes of Boarders and The Flatshare , but Jaq will be his biggest screen project to date. Jobson “fell in love with his writing” after watching his play Afronauts . Jasmie Jobson “He’s very passionate about Jaq’s character arc and storyline. The ideas he was bringing to the table [were amazing]. It’s very raw, edgy, current, and relevant,” Jobson said. “Once we started putting things together, it just looked so great. It was undeniable.” The actress continued: “Jaq is my baby. There’s a lot of myself that I put into Jaq, like her loyalty and compassion. So when Top Boy ended, naturally I was like, ‘No guys, we’ve got so many more stories to tell.'” Jaq’s executive producers are Charles Steel and Alasdair Flind for Cowboy Films; Bennett for Easter Partisan Films; Calais Cameron and Jobson; Aubrey Drake Graham and Adel “Future” Nur for DreamCrew Entertainment; Maverick Carter and Jamal Henderson for SpringHill Studios, a Fulwell Entertainment label. Next up for Jobson is In The Shadows , her boxing biopic feature about Ramla Ali, who made history as the first non-track and field athlete to compete for Somalia in the Olympic Games. The pic is part of the London Film Festival line-up. Jobson will also return in Season 2 of Paramount+ series MobLand as Zosia. Season 3 is yet to be officially greenlit, but a writers’ room has opened for the Tom Hardy show. Asked if she will be part of MobLand Season 3, Jobson said: “I would love to, but we’ll see. I mean, I haven’t seen any scripts or anything like that yet, so we’re just waiting and seeing.” Baz Bamigboye Looks Back On Tabloid Life With ‘Ink’s Danny Boyle & James Graham Alexander Opens Film Arm With Kevin Chan & Hamish Moseley On Board Tom Cruise Backs WBD Deal & CEO’s Vow Of 30 Pics A Year: “It’s Awesome” Taneo Sebastian Cast In Don Josephus Raphael Eblahan’s ‘Hum’ Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Venice Jury Head Maggie Gyllenhaal Calls For Empathy In Politically Charged Times; Addresses Dearth Of Women In Competition: “It’s A Systemic Problem”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow , Nada Aboul Kheir September 2, 2026 3:40am VENICE, ITALY - SEPTEMBER 02: Jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal attends the Jury Photocall Getty Images Venice Film Festival jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal called for empathy at the opening press conference for the 83rd edition on Wednesday, which gets underway against politically charged times. Asked whether cinema should be political, Gyllenhaal replied that filmmakers and spectators needed to be open to all types of filmmakers and stories. “To me, the answer has something to do with empathy. I think that film allows an opening into an opportunity to find empathy inside of ourselves. Personally, I don’t believe that there is any subject or any filmmaker that shouldn’t be heard,” he said. Related Stories Festivals 'Bunker': Watch Javier Bardem & Penélope Cruz In Florian Zeller's Venice-Bound Psychological Thriller News Ukrainian Drama 'Camouflage' Set Sales With MMM Films - Venice “I think we can challenge ourselves to hear stories about the most corrupt, the most perverse people, because it opens up the opportunity to find empathy for those people, and even to look at the ways in which we might have a little bad guy inside us, a little perversity inside us, a little corruption inside us. Fight it as we might.” Watch on Deadline “I think that if movies really are an honest look into other people’s experience, that they are fundamentally unavoidable. unavoidably political, as well as a lot of other things.” #VeniceFilmFestival jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal on whether films should be political: "If movies really are an honest look into other people's experience, then they are fundamentally, unavoidably political" pic.twitter.com/G7zbvJ37XX — Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 2, 2026 Gyllenhaal is joined in the jury this year by Tunisian The Voice of Hind Rajab director and screenwriter Kaouther Ben Hania ; English composer and artist Daniel Blumberg , Italian professor Francesco Casetti, French director and screenwriter Xavier Giannoli , the Afghan director and screenwriter Shahrbanoo Sadat , and the Hong Kong director and producer Johnnie To . They did not take to the stage with Gyllenhaal, who was instead joined by the jury heads for the festival’s other competitive sections, Valérie Donzelli for the Orizzonti and Carolina Cavalli for the Luigi De Laurentiis “Lion of the Future” award for a debut film. Dearth of women Many of the questions focused on the fact that there are just two female directors in the main competition. Gyllenhaal joked that it was proof that male directors were better than female ones before going into the subject in more depth. “There’s a systemic problem,” she said. She added that it was harder for women to get their films financed but also suggested there was another fundamental reason preventing female directors from breaking through. #VeniceFilmFestival president Maggie Gyllenhaal addresses the lack of female directors in this year's main competition and the systemic problem within the industry: "It's much harder for women to get their films financed" pic.twitter.com/0qgey2x4Rx — Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 2, 2026 “Could it be possible that the things that women, having had a different experience of being alive in the world. Want to make movies about are not always deemed high art. Who decides what’s good? Who decides what’s valuable?”. articles.title: George Clooney Slams Pete Hegseth Over Canadian Cadet Post; Voices Support For Mark Ruffalo & Muses On Paramount-Warner Bros Merger – Venice
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow , Nada Aboul Kheir September 2, 2026 4:40am VENICE, ITALY - SEPTEMBER 02: George Clooney attends the Golden Lion For Lifetime Achievement Photocall during the 83rd Venice International Film Festival at Palazzo del Casino on September 02, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Vittorio Zunino Celotto/Getty Images) George Clooney mixed gravity and laughter as he landed at the Venice Film Festival on Wednesday to receive a Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement at the opening ceremony this evening. The actor, director and producer was put through his paces at a press conference preceding the honor on a wide range of topics from U.S. politics to climate change, the role of the press, Mark Ruffalo , the Paramount-Warner Bros merger, studio shying away from festivals and whether he plans to return to the director’s chair. On the latter, Clooney, who has nine feature and two TV series directorial credits to his name including Good Night, and Good Luck and most recently, The Boys in the Boat , revealed he had put directing aside for now in favor of acting because of fatherhood. Related Stories News Venice Jury Head Maggie Gyllenhaal Calls For Empathy In Politically Charged Times; Addresses Dearth Of Women In Competition: "It's A Systemic Problem" Festivals 'Bunker': Watch Javier Bardem & Penélope Cruz In Florian Zeller's Venice-Bound Psychological Thriller “The only reason I’m not directing, which I love doing, is because I have two nine-year-old kids, and in order for me to spend time with them, I can’t,” he said. Watch on Deadline “You know, if I act in a movie, it’s three months, and I can go and come and go and come back. When you direct a movie, it’s a year, wherever you are, and there’s no traveling back and forth, so I can’t do that anymore. The last thing I did was this play last year on Broadway, and that took away that took us all away for a period of time. And I can’t really pull the kids out of school anymore, so I’m really happy doing this. It’s fun to be an actor again. I’m enjoying it, actually.” A smiley George Clooney arrives to the #VeniceFilmFestival press conference room and asks journalists “How are you?” in Italian. Clooney will receive the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement at the Opening Ceremony tonight pic.twitter.com/3Bl8Df7mqT — Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 2, 2026 Unsurprisingly, Clooney also found himself being quizzed about U.S. politics and the direction of his country under President Donald Trump. “I’m always very optimistic about things,” he said. “We’re at a moment in time that’s unfortunate… that’s an understatement. I do believe that we’re going to get through all of this. I’m old enough to have been through 1968 in the states when every city in the United States was set on fire, and we lost Martin Luther King and Bobby Kennedy in the same year. There was tons of violence. The capital was surrounded with tanks. We’ve had some other difficult times, but this is one of them,” he said. He suggested the midterm elections for the U.S. House of Representatives in November could set the tone for a change of political direction in the U.S.. “There’s a great word, kakistocracy, which is a country run by the least qualified people. I think maybe we have a kakistocracy right now, but we’ll get through it, and we will have an election in November that should be a check and balance, and then in 2028, with any luck, we’ll have some restoration into some normalcy.” Clooney slammed what he called “the idea of cruelty” at the heart of the current administration, reserving special criticism for U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and his recent post deriding women and Canada’s cadet program. “You see what the Secretary of Defense just tweeted out a picture about women in the military in Canada, and you’re going, ‘What’s wrong with you? Where’s the sense of decency in all of this?’ And I’m ashamed of all of that, but we will get through it, and we will we will come out better on the other side.” Clooney was asked for his view on the ongoing furore around Mark Ruffalo who has been accused of antisemitism in relation to his criticism of the Paramount-WBD merger. “I support Mark Ruffalo’s ability to speak freely… I believe in free speech even when I completely disagree with it. That’s important, right? In fact, it’s part of how a democracy works. There are going to be people tonight in the room that are going to disagree with most everything I say or stand for. Fair enough. That’s how it’s supposed to be. We’re supposed to argue these things out and come to a conclusion based on the information that we take in,” he said. “I will always support Mark Ruffalo’s ability to speak freely. I like him. He’s a good man.” George Clooney says “I support Mark Ruffalo’s ability to speak freely” at the #VeniceFilmFestival . This comes after Ruffalo was accused of antisemitism by a Paramount spokesperson for highlighting the Ellison family’s connection to the Israeli state and its military apparatus pic.twitter.com/rRDle1lANX — Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 2, 2026 On the Paramount-Warner Bros., Clooney said he had yet to understand how the deal could be brought over the line but that overall he was concerned about its implications. “There’s so many issues involved… it doesn’t matter how much money you have; it’s going to be very tricky to do. So, my opinion on the merger is I always worry whenever big companies are consolidating because it usually means a lot of people lose their jobs. That’s the truth, but we’ll see,” he said. He also noted that the merger comes at a time when the film industry is already going through major changes due to AI. “We’re going through a revolution in our industry… AI is going to be a very big part of this industry. It’s going to hurt us in a lot of ways. If you’re a visual effects supervisor, you’re going to have trouble coming up because… a lot of jobs are going to be taken away, probably about 30% of the jobs. I don’t know what the real number is, but there’s going to be a big number of jobs going to be taken away, and we’re kind of on our back foot on it. We’re not taking the lead on it. People are just now starting to, so it’s going to be a complicated time in our industry, and so we’re going to have to find ways to survive.” George Clooney on the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger at the #VeniceFilmFestival : “I don’t see how it financially ends up making sense for the people who are trying to do it. I’m always worried whenever one big company swallows up another big company” pic.twitter.com/s6GHQ7nGPK — Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 2, 2026 On a lighter note, Venice regular Clooney also talked about his long-time love of the festival and the city, which he said was also special in his heart as the place where he married wife Amal Clooney in 2014. Asked on his plans for the evening after the ceremony he replied to laughter, “I’m going to drink”, before adding he was hoping to get in an intimate dinner with his wife. “We’re going to go out to dinner… you know this is a town where you ride, you take the boat underneath some little tiny arches, and suddenly you’re in the middle of a a restaurant that has four tables, and the the guy who runs it comes out and sits with you… it’s just a really optimistic, beautiful place, and we’re gonna go find a fun place to have dinner, my wife and I. She’s gonna be wearing a very nice dress, so we’ll have to be careful where we go.” Baz Bamigboye Looks Back On Tabloid Life With ‘Ink’s Danny Boyle & James Graham Alexander Opens Film Arm With Kevin Chan & Hamish Moseley On Board Tom Cruise Backs WBD Deal & CEO’s Vow Of 30 Pics A Year: “It’s Awesome” Taneo Sebastian Cast In Don Josephus Raphael Eblahan’s ‘Hum’ Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Hanway Boards Luca Guadagnino’s Bernardo Bertolucci Doc ‘Joie De Vivre’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac London Film Festival Lineup: Ava DuVernay’s ‘14th’ & Boots Riley’s ‘I Love Boosters’ Among Headline Titles — Full List Julianne Moore To Receive Zurich’s Golden Icon Award Indie Media Outfit Alexander Opens Film Arm With Kevin Chan, Hamish Moseley On Board And ‘Ben’imana’ Set As First Release View All September 2, 2026 5:00am Luca Guadagnino in ‘Joie De Vivre’. Hanway. Hanway Films has boarded Luca Guadagnino ‘s Bernardo Bertolucci documentary Joie De Vivre , which debuts at this year’s Venice Film Festival. Guadagnino’s 7-hour Director’s Cut will screen in two parts at Venice: the first on 8th September and the second on the 9th. Guadagnino will receive the Cartier Glory to the Filmmaker Award before the first screening. The documentary explores Bertolucci’s work, including: 1900, The Conformist, Last Tango in Paris, La Luna, Me and You, The Sheltering Sky and The Last Emperor . It features discussions with a range of interviewees, including filmmakers (Martin Scorsese, James Gray, David Cronenberg, Alfonso Cuarón); actors (Debra Winger, Margot Robbie); screenwriter Francesca Maneri; producer Jeremy Thomas; and critics and cinephiles, including Murielle Joudet, Armond White and Mark Cousins. Related Stories News Drew Starkey Stays Mum On Potential 'American Psycho' Casting, But Teases: "The Script Is Amazing" News Luca Guadagnino To Receive Filmmaker Award At Venice Film Festival Joie de Vivre is produced by MeMo Films, the production company co-founded in 2010 by entrepreneur and fashion designer Gabriele Moratti and distributor and film producer Francesco Melzi d’Eril. MeMo Films has collaborated with Guadagnino on films such as Call Me by Your Name and Suspiria . Watch on Deadline Joie De Vivre is Guadagnino’s second nonfiction piece on the Last Tango in Paris filmmaker, following the 2013 essay film Bernardo Bertolucci, which he produced using filmed interviews given by The Last Emperor Oscar winner over the course of 50 years. Guadagnino has described Joie de Vivre as a “very personal movie” that features conversations with filmmakers across the world about Bertolucci. Discussing the film during his lineup announcement, Venice head Alberto Barbera described Joie de Vivre as an “extraordinary documentary that will keep you “hooked to your chair” despite the 435-minute runtime. articles.title: Hot Docs Promotes Diana Sanchez, Hires Mara Gourd-Mercado As Festival Seeks To “Future-Proof” Itself
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Doc Talk Podcast Goes Live With Director Poh Si Teng And Physicians Of ‘American Doctor’ Watch ‘One In A Million’ Trailer, Oscar Contender That Follows Incredible Journey Of Syrian Girl Across Tumultuous Decade Points North Institute Announces 2026 Artist Programs And Points North Forum Ahead of Camden Film Festival View All September 2, 2026 5:00am Diana Sanchez (left) and Mara Gourd-Mercado Courtesy of Dewey Chang/Oliver Harding Hot Docs , the world-class documentary film festival in Toronto, has announced some major personnel moves – elevating Diana Sanchez to president and bringing in Mara Gourd-Mercado to succeed Sanchez as executive director. Gourd-Mercado, currently head of industry at CPH:DOX in Copenhagen, will report to Sanchez in her new role, which begins October 19. As president, Sanchez will “concentrate on the organization’s strategic direction — artistic oversight, government relations, business development, and major financial partnerships — while safeguarding Hot Docs’ long-term health and stability,” according to a release. Related Stories News Oscar Documentary Contender 'House Of Hope' Secures North American Distribution Documentary West Bank-Set 'House Of Hope,' 'Saigon Story: Two Shootings In The Forest Kingdom' Among Big Winners At Hot Docs The nonprofit Hot Docs, which will celebrate its 34 th edition next year, also announced that Julie Bristow will serve as chair of the organization’s board of directors, while Aaron Zeghers will serve as vice-chair. Watch on Deadline Courtesy of Hot Docs Sanchez tells Deadline the moves are part of “creating a really solid foundation” for Hot Docs, “future-proofing the organization… But the proof will be in the pudding.” In a statement, Bristow, the board chair, praised “the phenomenal work [Sanchez] has done to stabilize and elevate Hot Docs. As we look to the future, this enhanced executive leadership team enables Diana to focus on what matters most: taking Hot Docs to the next level while ensuring it is financially secure, resilient, and nimble.” Just two years ago, before Sanchez’s arrival as executive director, Hot Docs warned it might go under as it faced a financial crisis emerging from the pandemic, a time of enormous challenge for many festivals including Sundance and Montreal’s Just For Laughs. It temporarily shut down its Hot Docs Ted Rogers Cinema and laid off some staff. The 2024 turmoil extended beyond the financial into board governance and artistic operations. Shortly before that year’s festival,10 programmers abruptly left, followed quickly by the resignation of then-Artistic Director Hussain Currimbhoy. Two board members also resigned in the middle of that year’s event. Sanchez says Hot Docs is on the right track, and pointed to a successful 2026 edition, which ran from April 23 to May 3. Mathew Tsang/Getty Images “I think last festival was a real indication, and I think great example of what Hot Docs can deliver,” Sanchez observes. “That’s what I told my team… ‘Let’s just make something great. And then there’ll be word of mouth and people will want to come.’ You can’t do it backwards. You actually have to work on what you’re delivering first, and then that’s when people are going to come back.” To foster stability and growth, she says, “You look at your revenue mix and one of the things I’d like to do is focus on earned revenue, more on that for the coming years. And that’s what I mean by future proofing. It’s like creating these great programs, diversifying our revenue mix, bringing people back by offering something that’s really exciting, being very intentional about what we are actually putting on — ‘You have to live within your means’ kind of thing. So, this year we did the Forum in our cinema, which was great, and people love that experience. And we had a great little delegate lounge close by that was really an intimate space… where people could meet, go and grab coffee. Making it easy for the industry to meet and do business I think is also top of mind.” Hot Docs From her perspective at CPH:DOX, Gourd-Mercado says she saw a renewed appreciation this year for the importance of Hot Docs. “You see the excitement of the people that were there at the [2026] edition. I think that it’s going to only build for the coming editions,” she says, expressing enthusiasm for joining Hot Docs “to participate in building activities and to building a festival where people are going to be excited to go.” As executive director, per the news release, “Gourd-Mercado will lead day-to-day operations and fiscal management of the organization and the festival, including festival and industry fundraising, with an additional focus on industry programming, including a revitalized Hot Docs Forum, and ties with the Francophone doc community in Canada and abroad.” As an Argentinian Canadian and native of Montreal who grew up speaking French, Gourd-Mercado is well situated not only to connect with Canada’s Francophone community, but with documentary makers throughout the Americas as well. “We want to make sure that we are showcasing stories that speak to the moment that we are in now, and that’s globally, not only locally,” notes Gourd-Mercado. “The Americas and Latin America and South America have a lot of great documentary makers. When you look at an event like Conecta in Chile or you look at BAM [Bogotá Audiovisual Market] in Bogotá [Colombia], you can see the incredible amount of projects that are coming out of those regions and those storytellers. And I think it’s our duty as international festivals to also showcase them.” Gourd-Mercado, Sanchez, and Isabel Arrate Fernández – IDFA’s artistic director, who is the child of Chilean political exiles – are among leaders in the documentary festival space who bring international experience and ties to Latin America to their work. “I oversaw Latin American cinema at TIFF for many years. And I was a founding artistic director of the Panama Film Festival,” Sanchez notes. “I also worked with the Los Angeles Latino Film Festival, a wonderful festival as well, every June. There is a very strong tradition of documentary filmmaking from Latin America that’s really informed a lot of my work. And we want to bring in this international experience into Hot Docs as well. We have that kind of vision, which is I think very exciting.” Sanchez’s appointment as Hot Docs president is effective immediately. The 2027 edition of Hot Docs, set for April 23-May 2, is sure to feature a lineup of world premieres and acclaimed documentaries from around the globe. Along with programming a first-class lineup, Sanchez says there’s another dimension to the festival-going experience that she and her colleagues intend to bear in mind. “If you’re a great host, people will also want to come back,” she affirms, “and we’re putting a lot of effort into that.” Baz Bamigboye Looks Back On Tabloid Life With ‘Ink’s Danny Boyle & James Graham Alexander Opens Film Arm With Kevin Chan & Hamish Moseley On Board Tom Cruise Backs WBD Deal & CEO’s Vow Of 30 Pics A Year: “It’s Awesome” Taneo Sebastian Cast In Don Josephus Raphael Eblahan’s ‘Hum’ Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘East Of Eden’ Trailer: Evil Lurks “Cloaked In Goodness” In Zoe Kazan’s Limited Series Take On John Steinbeck’s Novel
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez , Katie Campione September 2, 2026 5:30am The full trailer for Netflix’s East of Eden limited series adaptation has arrived. Zoe Kazan ’s take on John Steinbeck’s classic 1952 novel will premiere on Netflix October 1. Related Stories News Upcoming Florence Pugh Projects: From ‘East of Eden’ To ‘Dune 3’ Books Everything We Know About Netflix’s ‘East of Eden’ Series So Far “I believe there are monsters born in this world to human parents. A monster is a variation from the accepted normal,” Florence Pugh’s Cathy Ames says in the beginning of the clip. A child may be born perfect, but without kindness or conscience. The show will explore the multigenerational saga of the Trask family, focusing new attention on its indelible antihero, Cathy Ames (Pugh), who shows up to the Trask brothers’ home bloody and crawling, disrupting the brotherhood between Christopher Abbott ’s Adam Trask and Mike Faist ’s Charles Trask, descended from Cyrus Trask (Tracy Letts). Watch on Deadline “Can you tell me your name?” Adam asks her upon her refreshment. “You may call me Cathy,” she replies. Adam thinks Cathy, “brightens the whole house” despite not having left her room much. Charles worries for his brother, claiming “A girl like that doesn’t just fall out of the sky. She’s going to tear you to pieces, and I don’t want to watch it.” L-R: Florence Pugh as Cathy Ames and Christopher Abbott as Adam Trask in ‘East of Eden’ Kirsty Griffin/Netflix Adam proposes marriage to Cathy, promising protection and happiness. “Evil is not always apparent at first glance,” Cathy continues narrating. “It can come cloaked in goodness, or beauty, or love. The heart of our oldest stories.” Here she hints at the ties to the Biblical tale of Cain and Abel, which serves as a framework for East of Eden . The series also stars Martha Plimpton as Faye; Ciarán Hinds as Samuel Hamilton; Joseph Zada as Cal Trask; Joe Anders as Aron Trask and Hoon Lee as Lee. Later on in the trailer, Adam is advised not to leave his and Cathy’s twin boys (Zada and Anders) fatherless when they are already without a mother. L-R: Joe Anders as Aaron Trask and Joseph Zada as Cal Trask in ‘East of Eden’ Courtesy of Netflix “I fear father damned us to the wrong fates,” Faist’s voiceover says, calling back to the boys’ childhood raised by Cyrus. East of Eden hails from co-studios Fifth Season and Anonymous Content. The series was filmed across multiple locations in New Zealand. Kazan wrote the screen adaptation of the novel, which was previously turned into a 1955 movie directed by her grandfather, Elia Kazan. She serves as co-showrunner alongside Jeb Stuart. The two and Pugh executive produce alongside Garth Davis, who directs episodes 1-4; Laure de Clermont-Tonnerre, who directs episodes 5-7; Antoine Douiahy; and Zack Hayden. Nearly four years after the limited series starring Florence Pugh was first announced , Netflix unveiled the first trailer for the seven-episode epic during its upfront presentation on Wednesday, May 13. The series was then teased to launch in fall 2026. Watch the teaser trailer below, and scroll on to find more new photos from the show. articles.title: David Oyelowo & Nate Parker’s Mansa Studios Debuts Slate Of TikTok Microdramas
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘Gunsmoke & Mirrors’, Drama Series About Danish Criminal Turned American Frontier Hero Chris Madsen, In The Works Clíodhna O’Sullivan’s Romantasy Novel ‘Her Hidden Fire’ Getting YA Series Adaptation With Great Island Attached Kevin Hart’s Hartbeat To House Vertical Originals On Microdrama Platform aTwist View All September 2, 2026 6:00am 'I Married the King of the Streets', 'The Love Contract' and 'My Twin Sister Stole My Man' Mansa Studios EXCLUSIVE: David Oyelowo and Nate Parker ‘s Mansa Studios is turning to TikTok for its latest slate of microdramas. The company is launching three vertical shows direct via the TikTok Minis platform. These are My Twin Sister Stole My Man , a relationship-driven drama about betrayal, identity and the complicated ties that bind family together; I Married the King of the Streets, a “high-stakes romance in which love, loyalty and power collide within a dangerous world”; and The Love Contract , which follows a “contract relationship that becomes increasingly complicated when a carefully arranged agreement begins to turn into something real.” Related Stories News Kevin Hart's Hartbeat To House Vertical Originals On Microdrama Platform aTwist News ReelShort Strikes Microdrama Deal With Indonesian Streamer Vidio For 200 Catalogue Titles & Co-Production Of New Shows “Mansa was created to ensure that culturally rich stories can reach audiences wherever they are,” said Oyelowo. “As viewing habits evolve, we are embracing new formats and platforms that allow us to remain connected to our audience while creating meaningful opportunities for diverse storytellers and talent.” Watch on Deadline The launches come following “months of collaboration with TikTok’s team,” according to Mansa’s bosses, and marks the first time Mansa shows have launched on the platform. “TikTok has become the most influential platform in the world for entertainment discovery, making it an ideal home for stories designed to capture audiences immediately and keep them coming back,” said the CAA-repped Parker, co-founder and CEO of Mansa. “Bringing multiple original projects to viewers at once allows us to continue expanding the possibilities of culturally resonant, mobile-first storytelling.” Mansa has been investing in vertical entertainment through 2026. Earlier this year, it announced a slate of 10 original microdrama series spanning romance, drama and other genres. Actor-producers Oyelowo and Parker have turned Mansa as the first microdrama service dedicated to Black stories. It originally launched as an ad-supported streaming platform highlighting Black content for a global audience, and still develops TV and film content alongside microdramas. It also has a theatrical deal with AMC Theatres, which earlier this year gave the long-delayed thriller Newborn a domestic release . Oyelowo, who has been nominated for Golden Globes and Emmys, is know for his role as Martin Luther King Jr. in Selma , while Parker wrote, directed and starred in Sundance favorite The Birth of a Nation .
