articles.title: ‘The Varnell Hill Show’ Review: Tommy Davidson in Paramount+’s Amiable Throwback of a ‘Martin’ Spinoff
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Angie Han Plus Icon Angie Han Television Critic ajhan Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 12:00am Tommy Davidson as Varnell Hill in 'The Varnell Hill Show.' Paramount+ “I got just one question for you: Did you miss me?” So goes the catchphrase for Varnell Hill ( Tommy Davidson ), the late-night talk show host who first graced our screens in Martin some 30-odd years ago. I’ll leave you to determine how much you personally have been longing to revisit a character who, for all his vivid personality, only ever appeared in two episodes of that earlier series. But hearing that line again in his new spinoff, Paramount+’s The Varnell Hill Show , it feels easy enough to answer in the affirmative. If the workplace comedy works better as a reminder of times gone by than a breath of fresh air, it nonetheless makes for a pleasantly nostalgic time. Related Stories TV 'Martin' Spinoff 'The Varnell Hill Show' Sets Premiere Date Movies Dave Chappelle Pitches Eddie Murphy on Joining Potential 'Chappelle's Show' Reboot at AFI Gala The Varnell Hill Show The Bottom Line More nostalgic than fresh, for better or worse. Airdate: Tuesday, Sept. 1 (Paramount+) Cast: Tommy Davidson, Wendy Raquel Robinson, Chris Williams, Nick Cafero, Emmanuel Hudson, Kym Whitley Creators: Kevin G. Boyd, Sherri McGee McCovey, Bentley Kyle Evans Despite its connection to Martin , no real knowledge of the earlier show is required to watch this one. Aside from a few passing references (“My cousin from Detroit told me to tell you, “Wazzup?”), creators Kevin G. Boyd, Sherri McGee McCovey and Bentley Kyle Evans rarely bring up past events or characters; even Martin star and creator (and Varnell Hill executive producer) Martin Lawrence guest stars only as a completely different character. As for Varnell, not much seems to be different for the self-described “one-time radio king, two-time ex-husband — soon to be three — and eight-time Soul Train Awards presenter.” He’s still an outgoing, egotistical personality, and still played by Davidson with loads of charisma and a knack for big but precise physical comedy. He’s still hosting the same old talk show to the same old, now rapidly aging audience. His most loyal aides, yes-man/bestie Tre (Chris Williams) and assistant Kym (Kym Whitley), are ones who’ve been with him for ages. But change is coming for Varnell, whether he likes it or not. (He very much does not.) The network CEO who once championed him has been pushed out, replaced by the useless nepo baby son (Nick Cafero’s Jonah) who despises Varnell precisely because the old man adored him. Jonah’s plan to oust Varnell involves installing an ambitious new executive producer (Wendy Raquel Robinson’s Rachel) ostensibly to help boost ratings, but in actuality to annoy Varnell into quitting over creative differences. Despite the season primarily revolving around the efforts to freshen up the talk show for a wider (i.e., younger) demographic, not much about The Varnell Hill Show reads as particularly modern, for better or for worse. Its format — multi-cam, laugh-tracked, with the occasional fourth-wall-breaking aside — is one that would have been in vogue when Martin originally aired. It’s done quite well (and of the supporting cast, Robinson and Whitley, both veterans of sitcoms from that era, seem so at home that you’d think they’d been on this brand-new show for years already), but whether that makes it feel hoary or comforting will probably depend on whether you grew up watching similar series. Its storylines tend to stick to well-trod territory: Varnell not understanding social media, Varnell trying to seem younger, Varnell accidentally getting high on pot brownies. Even a multi-episode arc featuring a Gen Z comic who seems primed to supplant Varnell as the network’s new darling betrays little understanding of who Marshay (Brittney Ayona Clemons) is beyond “younger than Varnell.” Its jokes are occasionally stale — sometimes in ways that seem appropriate for the characters (of course Varnell is the sort of guy who’d drop a Kato Kaelin reference three decades after the O.J. trial) and sometimes in ways that suggest The Varnell Hill Show itself might benefit from some fresher blood behind the scenes (it makes no sense that a Millennial hypebeast-type writer would describe Moo Deng as a top comedy trend in 2026). The inconsistency can make it difficult to tell exactly what the vibe of Varnell’s program is meant to be. In one episode, Varnell goes viral for an accidentally live-streamed rant complaining of being treated by top brass like “a TikTok Bojangles” and declaring that, “When I speak my truth, it’s aggressive” — a slightly confusing statement given that what we’ve seen of his public persona up to that point is so easygoing that earlier that day, he’d been boasting of how many grandmas fall asleep to him. (“And a lot of them don’t wake up,” Jonah snarks in response.) Still, there’s an earnestness to the series that makes it easy to vibe with. The challenges faced by a Black host and his mostly Black staff in trying to create something that feels good and authentic at a company run by white men, at least one of whom is hell-bent on ruining them, is an intermittently important theme throughout the eight-part season. And there’s an element of wish fulfillment in seeing Varnell and Rachel and their colleagues triumph by, for example, giving a MAGA-era Kanye West stand-in the takedown he deserves (even if, again, the real-life reference feels a few years old). Then there’s the endless rotation of celebrities playing themselves. Varnell’s show might be fictional, but the show about his show actually does function as a way to spotlight Black talents across the industry. Doug E. Fresh is the program’s bandleader, while the likes of Damon Wayans and Matt Barnes come through as talk show guests and Kirk Franklin and Omarion as musical guests. In one of the comic highlights of the season, Deon Cole, Mike Epps, Lavell Crawford and Miss Pat play themselves as friends of Varnell’s who’ve been invited to roast him for an anniversary special; the chemistry that flows from the segment really does have the joyous, unfiltered feel of old friends just trying to crack each other up. Ironically, or perhaps appropriately, the most glaring issue with the series, aside from its old-timey-ness, likely would have been less of one in the 1990s: the fact that there simply doesn’t seem to be enough of it. Like so many first seasons, The Varnell Hill Show ’s has the feel of a newcomer trying out everything it can to see what sticks. But at just eight half-hour episodes, it simply doesn’t have time to figure out what to do with supporting ensemble members like AJ (Emmanuel Hudson), Varnell’s dopey social media manager of a nephew, or flesh out ones like hopelessly square head writer Thad (Neil Brown Jr.) and his staff. If Paramount+ is putting its weight behind this amiable throwback of a series, it might as well go all the way and give it another dozen or 20 episodes to find its most fully realized self. THR

articles.title: ‘Love Island USA’ Season 8 Reunion Sees Fiery Islander Confrontations, Tear-Filled Moments and More
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 12:25am 'Love Island USA' season eight reunion. Christine Bartolucci/Peacock Logo text Nothing was off limits at Peacock ‘s Love Island USA season eight reunion that saw the winners, fan-favorite Islanders and bombshells reunite to unpack some of the season’s biggest and most drama-filled moments. Ariana Madix and Andy Cohen co-hosted the reunion special that aired Monday night and was filmed in front of a live studio audience in Los Angeles. The reunion featured winners Trinity and Bryce , as well as finalists Aniya and Carl, Kayda and Zach, and Melanie and Sincere. However, the other OG Islanders and bombshells from the latest season were also in attendance to help stir the night’s drama. Related Stories TV 'Love Island USA' Returns for Season 8 Reunion: When and Where to Watch Online TV 'Love Island USA' Renewed for Season 9, Peacock Drops Season 8 Reunion Teaser After showing never-before-seen videos of the finalists when they first got their phones back and saw America’s reaction in July following the season eight finale, Madix and Cohen didn’t waste any time diving right in. The night also featured a classic Kenzie split, Trinity and Bryce talking about life outside the villa, Islanders’ reactions to fan comments, the couples revealing who’s still together post- Love Island USA and more. Below, The Hollywood Reporter unpacks the season’s eighth reunion’s most memorable moments. And if you want to relive all the season’s jaw-dropping moments , check out THR ‘s coverage and interviews here . Aniya, Tierra and KC Squash Any Beef Following one of the season’s most dramatic moments, when KC left Aniya single after he chose to couple up with Casa Amor bombshell Titi, leading to a fiery confrontation between the Islanders, a surprising friendship later developed on the show between Titi and Aniya. However, comments Titi and KC made on their Aftersun episode after being dumped from the villa left Aniya confused about where their dynamic stood. “I feel like at the moment I had no beef with Titi at all,” Aniya said. “It was more the situation with KC and what happened. Honestly, I was kind of like taken aback a little bit when you’re on Aftersun , you were like, ‘Oh, I’m not going to be friends with anyone outside of this, really.’ Why did you say that?” Titi then took a moment to clarify her past comment. “I didn’t say I want to be friends with anyone . I said I didn’t want to be friends with everyone , and that wasn’t regarding you,” she said before asking, “Is there a reason why you felt that was directed towards you?” “I was kind of really thrown off with the whole Aftersun [episode], especially with both of you guys,” Aniya replied. “I feel like we’ve been on good terms, and then KC proceeded to say, ‘Oh, Aniya’s fragile,’ and I feel like you just contradicted the whole apology that we had in there. I haven’t spoken badly on you guys at all, so it really hurt my feelings a little bit.” KC also took the opportunity to apologize to Aniya over his “fragile” remark. “I could have said a different word,” he said. “I would hate for you to think I have anything against you, you know what I mean? I think we’re all left on good terms and that’s where I want to be.” Madix and Cohen on Love Island USA season eight reunion. Christine Bartolucci/Peacock Kenzie and Melanie Squabble Over Airtime Comment and “Non-Existent” Friendship Madix asked Kenzie to clarify her alleged comment on Sol’s Instagram live last month about Melanie having more airtime than everyone else. “After watching the show back, I did see that she did get a lot more airtime, but I would never talk shit about her,” Kenzie said. After Kenzie called out Melanie for rolling her eyes, she added, “This isn’t about you. It’s just the show and you did get more [air]time because you guys had more stuff going on in y’all’s relationship.” In response, Melanie said, “It just caught me off guard that everyone’s together and that it’s even a conversation. I have not done anything to you.” She also accused Kenzie of never being there for her throughout their time in the villa, despite Kenzie calling Melanie her best friend. “These girls [Trinity, Aniya and Kayda] were there for me,” Melanie said before sharing an example of Kenzie’s betrayal of their friendship. “There was a moment when me and Corbin got put together. You completely dipped on me. You did not talk to me. You didn’t even check up on me. I had to see my couple be with someone else. You did not care about me. I never had a chat with you. I didn’t pull you. You didn’t pull me.” After Madix pointed out that “it seems like this friendship is essentially non-existent” at the moment, the host asked if there’s a path forward for them. After Kenzie expressed through tears that she still loves Melanie, the latter also shared that “everything is fixable,” including their friendship. Sol and Melanie Get in Fiery Exchange: “Mama a Liar” After Cohen reminded the audience that Sol previously said on social media she wanted her fellow Islanders to “feel your wrath tonight,” he gave her an opportunity to share what’s on her mind. Sol was ultimately dumped from the villa earlier in the season after Sincere recoupled with Melanie. “Where do we start? When I first came in, I feel like you guys were welcoming the first day, and then I started talking to Sincere, and then the energy just got fucking weird in the house. And I was like, whoa, I don’t know what’s going on,” Sol said. “Also, me watching it back, I’m like, damn, y’all were objectifying my body and like just saying like a bunch of different stuff.” Melanie quickly chimed in, saying, “I am actually shocked about you.” “I am actually shocked because as soon as America put you and Sincere together, I’ve never once came at you crazy ever,” she continued. “In fact, I actually pulled you aside in Say Less, and I got to know you. I sat with you. We spoke about your dad. We spoke about your friendships. … I was so genuine.” Melanie also called out Sol for claiming on social media post-villa that she was pied more than twice during one of the challenges. “You didn’t. You’re a liar. Mama a liar,” Melanie stated. Despite Sol doubling down that she was pied more, Cohen later confirmed that she was in fact only pied by two boys during said challenge. Following a heated exchange between the two women, Melanie shouted, “You’re lying. You’re trying to build this victim’s story, but it’s not.” She also noted that “we tried” to befriend Sol in the villa. However, Sol angrily replied, “It’s not about you. It’s about me and my experience. She also maintained her stance that she felt the girls never genuinely wanted to be her friend. Love Island USA season eight reunion. Christine Bartolucci/Peacock Trinity Confronts Sol Over Her Remarks About Relationship With Bryce Despite Trinity and Bryce becoming the ultimate winners of Love Island USA season eight, Sol previously questioned their relationship while answering fan questions during an Instagram live. In response, Trinity took a moment during the reunion to confront Sol. “I didn’t like the way that you went on live and started talking about me and Bryce,” Trinity said. She was specifically frustrated with Sol claiming Bryce pulled Kayda for a chat four or five times in the villa, despite being coupled up with Trinity. However, he actually only asked to talk to Kayda once. “Y’all keep bringing up this one time where he pulled Kayda,” Trinity said. “There’s been times I wanted to talk to Corbin; I wanted to talk to Sean. Nobody bring that shit up.” Bryce also chimed in, adding, “Everyone’s saying it’s Couples Island and everyone’s closed off. But when I pull one person for a chat, and now, I don’t love my person.” After hearing Trinity and Bryce out, Sol apologized for her past comments. “I will say I worded that completely wrong,” she said. “I 100 percent apologize for that.” Which Couples Are Still Together Post-Show? In addition to all the season eight finalists still being together and continuing to grow their connections, Titi and KC, and Dylan and Kenzie are also still in relationships post-show. However, Parmida and Corbin’s romantic spark has since ended. As for why they’re no longer in a relationship, Corbin said, “Our chemistry together was fantastic. Our energy was 100 percent with each other. We’re compatible in some ways. It’s just coming out into the real world, we had some ups and downs. But as two people come together [and] come to an understanding, you know, two people just don’t work out.” Parmida added, “I just feel like a relationship right now is not what we need. Better as friends.” THR

articles.title: ‘Shadow Has Fallen’: Iwan Rheon, Brendan Coyle, Atandwa Kani Join ‘Has Fallen’ Season 3
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All September 1, 2026 12:35am 'Paris Has Fallen' Studiocanal Shadow Has Fallen , the third season of the Has Fallen franchise, is a go and has started filming. It follows Paris Has Fallen and the upcoming Apollo Has Fallen . It also continues the high-octane ambition of Gerard Butler’s Has Fallen film franchise. StudioCanal , Urban Myth Films, Millenium and G-Base said on Monday that filming has commenced, with the new season shooting in South Africa and the U.K. Ritu Arya (The Umbrella Academy, Polite Society) and Tewfik Jallab (Spiral, Dark Hearts) reprise their respective roles as fearless MI6 operative Zara Taylor and former French Secret Service agent Vincent Taleb. Related Stories Movies 'Club Kid,' 'Bunker' and Danny Boyle's 'Ink' Added to Zurich Film Festival Lineup Movies In 'Love Is the Monster,' Paulina García Is a Granny Facing Impossible Choices (Exclusive TIFF Trailer) Joining the cast for season 3 are Iwan Rheon (Game of Thrones, Misfits) , Brendan Coyle (Downton Abbey, Hit Point) and Atandwa Kani (Black Panther, Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom) . The new six-episode season (6 x 52’) is once again written by series creator Howard Overman ( War of The Worlds, Misfits, Hit Point ) who said: “There’s a scale to season 3 that we’ve been building towards since Paris Has Fallen .” He added: “ Shadow Has Fallen will see Vincent and Zara embark on their most demanding and morally challenging mission – a mission that takes them into the very heart of Southern Africa.” Marco Kreuzpaintner ( Bodies, The Lazarus Project ) and Alice Troughton ( The Living and The Dead, Cucumber, Dr Who ) are attached to direct. The show comes from producer Julian Murphy and executive producers Johnny Capps and Howard Overman for Urban Myth Films, M-K Kennedy and Daniel Gratton for StudioCanal, Gerard Butler and Alan Siegel for G-Base, as well as Avi Lerner, Jonathan Yunger and Yariv Lerner for Millennium. Following the Canal+ Group’s acquisition of African pay-TV giant MultiChoice Group, Shadow Has Fallen is the second production of scale that studio arm StudioCanal is bringing to South Africa as it wraps filming on Bill Condon’s feature film The Road Home starring Thabo Rametsi, Cynthia Erivo, Guy Pearce, Johnny Flynn and John Legend. “ Shadow Has Fallen is the next chapter of StudioCanal’s globally recognized franchise,” the company said Monday. “The series will draw on South Africa’s world-class cast (additional names to be announced), crews and creative talent, further showcasing the country’s capabilities on the global stage.” in THR

articles.title: In ‘Until the Day Ends,’ Two Serbs on Opposite Sides of a Deeply Divided Society Fall for Each Other (Exclusive Venice Trailer)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All September 1, 2026 1:45am 'Until the Day Ends' Courtesy of Venice Film Festival With her debut feature, the Serbian protest drama Until the Day Ends ( Do Kraja Dana ), Jelena Maksimović becomes the first female director from Serbia to bring a narrative feature to the official selection at the Venice Film Festival since Soja Jovanović’s Eagles Fly Early in 1966. That is likely to make for an emotional journey for the filmmaker to the festival, which just seems fitting. After all, an emotional, and intense, journey is also what the protagonists of her movie embark on. The film, set against anti-government protests by students and others in the country’s capital, Belgrade, will world premiere in the Horizons (Orrizonti) section of the 83rd edition of the Italian festival on Sept. 10. Serbia has experienced its largest wave of student protests and civil unrest in decades since the collapse of a railway station canopy killed 16 people in November 2024. Related Stories Movies 'Club Kid,' 'Bunker' and Danny Boyle's 'Ink' Added to Zurich Film Festival Lineup Movies In 'Love Is the Monster,' Paulina García Is a Granny Facing Impossible Choices (Exclusive TIFF Trailer) Until the Day Ends stars Lena Trifunović as Lena, an anarchist student, and Andrija Krivokapić as Stefan, a working-class youth with friends who are pro-government loyalists. Forget Romeo and Juliet! Set against the backdrop of the student protests in and around Belgrade, the two may be on opposite sides of a deeply divided society, but fall for each other. When a stone is thrown and hits a policeman, Stefan fears he is to blame, leading the duo to flee the city together, adding a road movie vibe to the film. Irina Hotomski, Stefan Tarabić and Miodrag Dragičević are also part of the cast. The director co-wrote Until the Day Ends with Olga Dimitrijevic and Ivan Salatic. Paul Spengemann ( Der Fleck ) is the cinematographer, and Jan Klemsche ( God Will Not Help ) the editor. Heretic is handling sales on the film. If the film sounds like one for you to explore, THR can now exclusively premiere a clip from it ahead of its Venice debut. Caution: things get tense here! But you were likely already expecting that. So let me get out of your way so you can watch the exclusive clip from Until the Day Ends . THR

articles.title: Ari Emanuel and His Brothers Donate $550,000 to Palestinian Doctor Training Program
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 2:25am Left to right: Zeke, Ari and Rahm Emanuel. Neilson Barnard/Getty Images for Klick Health; Amy Sussman/Getty Images; Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images Hollywood mogul Ari Emanuel and his brothers Zeke and Rahm have donated $550,000 towards a program to train Palestinian doctors from the West Bank at the Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center in Israel. eJewishPhilanthropy reported that the Emanuel brothers’ donation would go towards funding the training of pediatric doctors and nurses from An-Najah University Hospital in the West Bank city of Nablus in the hopes of establishing the first dedicated children’s hospital in that region. The donation was made via the non-profit Rozana and its American arm, Rozana USA. According to the organization, the donation is the largest private donation that Rozana USA has ever received. Related Stories Movies In 'Until the Day Ends,' Two Serbs on Opposite Sides of a Deeply Divided Society Fall for Each Other (Exclusive Venice Trailer) TV 'Shadow Has Fallen': Iwan Rheon, Brendan Coyle, Atandwa Kani Join 'Has Fallen' Season 3 The donation also comes in the wake of increased global concerns over healthcare services in the West Bank in the midst of increased attacks from Israeli settlers. Médecins Sans Frontières said that “Palestinians are struggling to access basic healthcare due to restrictions, insecurity, and systematic violence,” in Hebron and other places in the West Bank. “This contribution will ultimately provide much-needed, improved care for Palestinian children while leveraging the field of healthcare to build constructive, trusting relations between Israeli and Palestinian medical professionals, bridging the divide,” the Emanuel brothers said in statement that was shared with Rozana. Ari Emanuel is the billionaire executive chairman of WME Group, as well as CEO and executive chairman of TKO Group Holdings, which owns UFC and WWE. Zeke Emanuel is an oncologist and bioethicist and was a key advisor to the Obama administration on health policy. Rahm Emanuel was Obama’s White House chief of staff, the former U.S. ambassador to Japan, mayor of Chicago and a presumed 2028 Democratic presidential candidate. THR

articles.title: Andrew Scott, Cynthia Erivo, Jesse Eisenberg Among Star-Studded London Film Festival Screen Talk Slate
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 3:00am (L-R) Scott, Erivo, Eisenberg, Ali BFI London Film Festival This year’s BFI London Film Festival has unveiled a raft of talent set for its Screen Talks lineup, including Andrew Scott, star of Sherlock , Fleabag and, more recently, Pressure ; Cynthia Erivo, an Oscar nominee for her performance in Wicked , Social Network actor-turned-filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg ; and two-time Academy Award winner Mahershala Ali, best known for roles in Moonlight and Green Book . Also joining for a discussion — in which the creative reflects on their processes, influences and careers in depth in front of an audience at BFI Southbank in central London — are Oscar-nominated actor John Malkovich ( Being John Malkovich , Dangerous Liaisons ), U.S. filmmakers Sofia Coppola ( Lost in Translation , Marie Antoinette ), Ava DuVernay ( Selma , 13th ), Brad Bird ( The Incredibles , Ratatouille ) and James Gray ( Ad Astra , Paper Tiger ). Related Stories News Ari Emanuel and His Brothers Donate $550,000 to Palestinian Doctor Training Program Movies In 'Until the Day Ends,' Two Serbs on Opposite Sides of a Deeply Divided Society Fall for Each Other (Exclusive Venice Trailer) They’re scheduled for wide-ranging conversations alongside British actress Naomi Ackie ( Blink Twice , Mickey 17 ) and prolific director in the U.K. Danny Boyle ( Trainspotting , 28 Days Later ), whose event will take place in Manchester, marking the festival’s first Screen Talk outside of London. Among some of the projects they’ll be promoting are Scott’s London Film Festival opener Elsinore with Olivia Colman, Johnny Flynn, Billie Piper, Luke Thompson and Peter Mullan. The feature, written by BAFTA winner Stephen Beresford ( Pride ), is based on the life of Ian Charleson. It follows the actor’s final weeks before his death from AIDS, playing Hamlet at London’s National Theatre in the 1990s. Daniel Day-Lewis had abruptly pulled out mid-performance, forcing Charleson to step in. Eisenberg will likely cover his latest movie (and LFF closer ) The Debut with Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti. The film follows a shy woman who is unexpectedly cast in a local production of an original musical. Under the spell of the strong-willed and enigmatic director, she loses herself in the role and the high-stakes world of this community theatre production. The full lineup for the 70th BFI London Film Festival is coming in due course. The event runs Oct. 7-18 2026. THR

articles.title: Diane Von Furstenberg to Honor Jane Fonda in Venice; Tina Brown and Karlie Kloss to Present
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 3:00am Karlie Kloss Jane Fonda and Tina Brown Chad Salvador/WWD/Getty Images; Courtesy of Subject; Astrid Stawiarz/Getty Images Diane von Furstenberg has zeroed in on a roster of “extraordinary women” to honor at her 17th annual DVF Awards. Set to take place in Venice, Italy on Sept. 3, a date that coincides with this year’s Venice Film Festival , Furstenberg will fete Jane Fonda , Prime Minister of Barbados Mia Amor Mottley, Pulitzer Prize-winning photojournalist Lynsey Addario, Food4Education founder and CEO Wawira Njiru and author, advocate and survivor Gisèle Pelicot. Held at Teatro Carlo Goldoni, the ceremony will also feature media maven Tina Brown and Karlie Kloss as presenters with a performance by singers Noa and Mira Awad. Related Stories Movies Andrew Scott, Cynthia Erivo, Jesse Eisenberg Among Star-Studded London Film Festival Screen Talk Slate News Ari Emanuel and His Brothers Donate $550,000 to Palestinian Doctor Training Program “For the 17th year of the DVF Awards, I am excited to honor women who have the courage to fight, the strength to survive and the leadership to inspire,” said von Furstenberg in a statement. Von Furstenberg and the Diller-von Furstenberg Family Foundation launched the DVF Awards in 2010 as a way to spotlight and support “extraordinary women” dedicated to “transforming the lives of other women; women who have had the courage to fight, the strength to survive and the leadership to inspire.” Five trophies are handed out to women along with a grant to each honoree, a gift bestowed to their respective nonprofit organizations to help propel and support their work. This year’s lineup covers such causes as environmental protection, political leadership, frontline journalism, food and education and advocacy for survivors. The DVF Awards also come at a time of immense challenges globally across the political and social landscape. More about the event and Furstenberg’s empire can be found here . Diane von Furstenberg CREDIT: Portrait by Mireille Roobaert/Courtesy of Subject THR

articles.title: Netflix’s New Releases Coming in September 2026
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 4:00am From top left: 'Stavros Halkias: Uncle Stav,' 'Dang!,' NFL Melbourne Game, 'LEGO ONE PIECE,' 'Unabomber,' 'The Gentlemen,' 'Stranger Things: Tales From '85' and 'Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.' Netflix; Gregory Shamus/Getty Images The return Guy Ritchie’s hit comedy crime series The Gentlemen ; an animated Asian-American comedy from Andrew Law; the latest special from comedian-of-the-moment Stavros Halkias ; the much-hyped comeback of Aaron Donald as the NFL heads Down Under for the first-ever regular season game in Australia; a second season of animated tales from 1985 Hawkins, Indiana; the fourth chapter of Ryan Murphy’s Monster anthology series; a two-part Lego animated One Piece special; and Jacob Tremblay depicting the origin story of Unabomber are just some of the film and TV highlights hitting Netflix in September. Related Stories TV 'Tires' Renewed for Season 4 by Netflix TV 'Manifest' Spinoff 'Arrivals' Landing at Netflix In the midst of all the speculation on whether Meghan Markle will be joining season 3 of The Gentlemen , it would have been easy to forget that season 2 of the hit Guy Ritchie comedy crime series launches on Sept. 3. The logline for season 2 reads, “It’s been one year since Eddie and Susie joined forces to work together in Bobby’s criminal empire overseas. As they drive to expand their enterprise, the decisions Bobby is making seem to be increasingly unsound. Now Eddie and Susie must decide whether to take action or risk losing it all.” Theo James, Kaya Scodelario, Daniel Ings, Joely Richardson, Vinnie Jones, Giancarlo Esposito and Ray Winstone all return for the second season, with newcomers including Hugh Bonneville, Benjamin Clementine, Benedetta Porcaroli, Amra Mallassi, Tyler Conti and Chris Eubank Jr. Netflix continues its push into adult animated comedies with the launch of Dang! on Sept. 8. The terminally online will have picked up on the spirited debate the show inspired on social media when a trailer for the Andrew Law-created Asian-American project first dropped. Those who are lucky enough not to be brain-poisoned by internet chatter, maybe interested to know that the show “follows a brother and sister duo whose fun, messy lives in New York City are interrupted when their worst nightmare comes true: their high-achieving older sister shows up and wants to hang out with them.” It’s not much deeper than that, for better or worse. Poppy Liu, Andrew Law, Noël Wells and Stephanie Hsu provide the voices. Stavros Halkias is the comedian-of-the-moment and his fame is only likely to grow with his new Netflix special landing on Sept. 8. Halkias, the former Cumtown podcaster, current star of Netflix comedy Tires as well as scene stealer in films like Bugonia and Tony , is a new breed of standup that’s crude but empathetic, a refreshing change of pace from the Roganverse comics who seem to delight in punching down and being cruel for the sake of it. Uncle Stav is a followup to 2023’s hilarious Fat Rascal , and deals with Halkias becoming an uncle. Sept. 17 will see the debut of the next installment of Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan’s Emmy-winning anthology series Monster hits Netflix. The eight-episode fourth chapter, The Lizzie Borden Story , is series’ first female-led tale and will focus on the infamous 1892 axe murders of Borden’s father and stepmother in Fall River, Massachusetts. Ella Beatty stars as Lizzie and the stellar cast includes Charlie Hunnam, Vicky Krieps, Rebecca Hall, Billie Lourd, Jessica Barden and Sarah Paulson. Also on Sept. 17, we return to Hawkins once more for season 2 of Stranger Things: Tales From ’85. Unsurprisingly, the animated series hasn’t inspired the same level of fervor or expectation as the live-action Stranger Things show did, but there are still millions of fans out there to service with more tales of retro horrors from the Upside Down. The logline for season 2 reads, “With Valentine’s Day on the way, the gang must uncover the truth behind ghostly apparitions and a swarm of strange creatures causing chaos around town.” On Sept. 18, the NFL continues its quixotic attemtps to grow American Football around the world with its first-ever regular season game in Australia, dubbed the NFL Melbourne Game . That’s right, the land of hard-running and hard-hitting Aussie Rules, Rugby Union and Rugby League will host a game of the premiere ball-based stop-start contact sport where you wear full padding and helmets. Fair dinkum! Still, you have to at least try to get skeptical foreigners interested and the NFL is bringing out the big guns with the San Francisco 49ers taking on the L.A. Rams at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground. Adding extra spice to the occasion is that the game will likely be the first game back for NFL legend Aaron Donald. After two seasons away from the game, the former three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year has come out of retirement to rejoin the Rams and should play Down Under. Netflix’s major American feature release for September is the Janus Metz Pedersen-directed Unabomber , an origin story for the infamous domestic terrorist Ted Kaczynski. Based on true events, Jacob Tremblay plays the 16-year-old Harvard prodigy who is subjected to controversial psychological experiments by Professor Henry Murray (Russell Crowe) and his eventual transformation into the Unabomber. The film, which debuts on Sept. 25, seems to fit into bracket of modestly budgeted well acted projects that Netflix seems to be leaning into more recently. The cast also includes Shailene Woodley, Annabelle Wallis, Alexander Ludwig, Steven Ogg and Marc Menchaca. The Stranger Things universe maybe showing signs of exhaustion, but Netflix still has a ways to go to satiate the demand for One Piece -related projects. On Sept. 29, the streamer launches LEGO ONE PIECE , the two-part animated special that kinda speed runs the story of “the crew’s escapades across the East Blue and into the Grand Line.” The voice cast includes Iñaki Godoy (Luffy), Emily Rudd (Nami), Mackenyu (Zoro), Jacob Romero Gibson (Usopp), Taz Skylar (Sanji), Charithra Chandran (Wednesday/Nefertari Vivi), Mikaela Hoover (Tony Tony Chopper), Katey Sagal (Dr. Kureha), Jeff Ward (Buggy) and Callum Kerr (Smoker). Movies added to Netflix in September include 17 Again, About Time, Alien, Aliens, Antz, Battleship, Big Daddy, The Blues Brothers, The Boy Next Door, Conan the Barbarian, Cruel Intentions, Dragnet, The Flintstones, Gothika, Greta, Jarhead, Jaws, Jaws 2, Jaws 3, Jaws: The Revenge, Kick-Ass 2, Knocked Up, Liar Liar, Neighbors, Phantom Thread, Prom Night, Ready or Not, Resident Evil: Afterlife, Resident Evil: Extinction, Resident Evil: Retribution, The Rite, Scarface, Shark Tale, Sleepless in Seattle, Straight Outta Compton, T2 Trainspotting, The Texas Chainsaw Massacre, Uncle Buck and Unfriended . articles.title: Howard Stern Hands Over One SiriusXM Channel to Andy Cohen
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Caitlin Huston Plus Icon Caitlin Huston Business Writer hustonca Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 5:00am Howard Stern and Andy Cohen on Sirius XM Courtesy of Sirius XM Howard Stern is officially handing over one of his SiriusXM channels to Andy Cohen starting Sept. 1. The transition comes about one year after Stern and Cohen pranked listeners by having Cohen take over the airwaves and imply that Stern was fired and that Howard 100, Stern’s main channel, was now his own. The prank came amid rumors about Stern’s impending retirement and the cancellation of his show. This time, Stern is actually giving Cohen Channel 101, his second channel which hosted archival clips of his show, as he returns and transitions to only doing one show a week, rather than the typical two. Stern has also struck a deal with HBO Max to adapt his live SiriusXM show into streaming episodes for HBO Max. “Last year we pranked the world. We made everybody think that I was taking over Howard 100. It was the best morning. Now the carrot is being dangled that Radio Andy will be taking over 101. Is this a prank? Am I being pranked?” Cohen asks Stern in a new video released by SiriusXM. “No, you are not being pranked. And Andy has been gracious enough to take over 101. And I have one request: please continue the tradition of doing a lot of gay antics,” Stern says. On Sept. 14, Howard will also unveil a new lineup for his Howard 100 channel, which will include Wrap Up Wednesday , an expanded version of Howard’s Wrap Up Show hosted by Gary Dell’Abate and Jon Hein that previously ran on Howard 101. In the past, Cohen, who helms a SiriusXM radio empire, including hosting Andy Cohen Live, has been rumored to be the eventual successor for Stern. SiriusXM did not comment on that theory, but Cohen and Stern seemed to downplay the idea. “Any chance I could get 100, and you take 101?” Cohen asks in the video. “No, I’m not giving up 100,” Stern says. As part of the channel shakeup, Sebastian Maniscalco’s Comedy Radio will take over Cohen’s previous channel, 102, while Netflix is a Joke Radio will move to channel 105, which has been home to temporary or pop-up programming. SiriusXM did not comment on reported layoffs as part of Stern’s move to one show a week. THR

articles.title: Fewer Women Are Creating TV Shows Now Than They Were Nearly a Decade Ago, Study Finds
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 5:00am Rachel Sennott, creator and star of 'I Love LA' season one, which premiered in 2025. Kenny Laubbacher/HBO The number of women working as TV creators and directors on original U.S. shows airing on streaming services has declined, in addition to female characters in major roles, according to the latest “Boxed In” study released Tuesday. The report, which tracked over 2,500 characters and more than 3,600 behind-the-scenes credits during the 2025-26 television year, was penned by Dr. Martha Lauzen, executive director of the Center for the Study of Women in Television and Film at San Diego State University. She found that the amount of women creating shows across streaming plummeted from 36 percent in 2024-25 to 24 percent in 2025-26, which was a stark contrast to the increase the year prior (27 percent in 2023-24 to 36 percent in 2024-25). The new findings indicate that last year’s increases were a momentary surge, rather than the beginning of a positive trend. As for broadcast, women creators also declined slightly from 20 percent in 2024-25 to 19 percent in 2025-26. “The numbers of women creating shows on both platforms are now lower than they were almost a decade ago in 2017-18,” Lauzen said. When it came to the percentage of women directing streaming projects, the report found that number also dropped from 32 percent in 2024-25 to 22 percent in 2025-26, following the temporary increase after 2023-24 (23 percent). Women directing broadcast programs also dipped from 18 percent in 2024-25 to 16 percent in 2025-26. This new study follows a report from The Hollywood Reporter in June that spotlighted the lack of progress in women-held below-the-line positions after a behind-the-scenes video of Sydney Sweeney on the set of Euphoria season three started circulating on social media. At the time, fans were quick to point out that the majority of the crew members seen in the clip were men, while Sweeney was sitting in a suggestive pose. As for roles in front of the camera, the number of female characters in major roles also declined last year, per the study. For streaming, women comprised 44 percent of major characters in 2025-26, down from 49 percent in 2024-25, and on broadcast, females accounted for 46 percent of major characters, down slightly from 47 percent in 2024-25. The report also found that male characters continue to have an easier time aging on television compared to female characters. On both streaming and broadcast shows, the majority of women in speaking roles were in their 20s and 30s, while the majority of men were in their 30s and 40s. The number of female characters also experienced a steep decline as they aged from their 30s into their 40s, while their male counterparts didn’t experience a substantial drop until their 50s. “The emphasis on youth for the majority of female characters foregrounds their appearance, whereas males are able to credibly age into positions of personal and public power, normalizing the perception that men are naturally more powerful than women,” Lauzen added. “The fully-realized characters played by Kathy Bates on Matlock or Jean Smart on Hacks remain the exception, not the rule, for women on television.” The “Boxed In” report has monitored over 65,000 characters and more than 80,00 behind-the-scenes credits on original dramas, comedies and reality television programs over the last 27 years, starting in 1997-98. It aims to provide a comprehensive historical record of women’s representation and employment in television. THR

articles.title: Unifrance President Gilles Pélisson Discusses Industry Challenges, Winning Strategies Ahead of Rendez-Vous Market in Le Havre
articles.full_text: Sep 1, 2026 6:24am PT Unifrance President Gilles Pélisson Discusses Industry Challenges, Winning Strategies Ahead of Rendez-Vous Market in Le Havre 'Hyper-distribution' can be scary, but it is leading to real advantages and increasing the international reach of shows on a wide range of channels and platforms, Pélisson notes By Ed Meza Plus Icon Ed Meza @edmezavar Latest Unifrance President Gilles Pélisson Discusses Industry Challenges, Winning Strategies Ahead of Rendez-Vous Market in Le Havre 31 minutes ago Unifrance Rendez-Vous TV Mart Spotlights Ancient Rome, 19th Century Paris, Retired Spooks, Luchadores, Diplomatic Intrigue and Gaza 1 day ago Patricio Valladares Descends Into Hell With Horror Adaptation of Dante’s ‘Inferno’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 week ago See All The French audiovisual sector is gearing up for the Unifrance Rendez-Vous in Le Havre , not only France’s premiere TV programming market but also an industry confab offering a clear assessment of how business trends and global developments are reshaping the domestic playing field, from evolving distribution models to programming increasingly tailored for export. Speaking to Variety ahead of the event, which runs Sept. 7-10 in Normandy’s famed port city, Unifrance President Gilles Pélisson discusses the pressing issues facing French distributors and producers and the continuing strength of local content on the international market. Related Stories Netflix’s Latest Marketing Mash-Up Pairs Stella Artois With 'The Gentlemen' HBO Max Banks on Upcoming Genre Thriller ‘Mataviejitas: The Serial Killer’ (EXCLUSIVE) The changing landscape for French TV distribution in the wake of increasing consolidation and streaming dominance is one major topic du jour that is affecting industries across Europe. Popular on Variety Gilles Pélisson Courtesy of Nicolas Gouhier “French TV distribution is not immune to the turbulence of the international market, and there is real concern among French distributors,” Pélisson points out. “Some critical questions have emerged with everyone watching: What will be the future model of European public broadcasters, how much will the streamers continue to produce locally and buy new programs, and how will private free-to-air channels cope with a shrinking advertising market?” Nevertheless offering an upbeat take, Pélisson stresses that new content is still needed regardless. “This is why we are delighted to welcome once again around 130 buyers to Le Havre this year. We worked with our distributors in June to preview their expectations, and the message is clear: French production keeps offering exceptional diversity, with relevant content for every kind of buyer.” The changing distribution landscape has, in the face of streaming dominance, seen the rise of “hyper-distribution.” Discussing the strategy at last year’s Mipcom, Glance, the TV and video market intelligence division of French audience measurement company Médiamétrie, stated: “[T]he need to distribute content everywhere while collaborating with rivals often creates a winning strategy.” Pélisson agrees: “Hyper-distribution can be scary, yet it’s showing some true benefits. It can clearly expand reach: A hit like ‘ Miraculous ’ can be present simultaneously on a wide range of channels and platforms across many countries, more than what was possible or even thinkable a decade ago. But simple presence does not guarantee to be seen.” Indeed, when the same content is available everywhere simultaneously, “it can disappear into the catalogue just as easily as it can stand out,” Pélisson emphasizes. “This is why, alongside our sales data, Unifrance tracks not only where French programs are distributed but how they actually perform, with data such as audience market share or viewed hours.” Continued analysis and receiving as much data as possible from all players is therefore crucial, he adds. “Quality programs can only be made if there is money to produce them!” Turning to the international appetite for French content, the Unifrance chief notes that Europe remains its core market, “and where the momentum is the most solid.” Poland, in particular, has become a leading territory this year as the top country for broadcasts of French programs on linear channels, while Germany remains a leading territory “thanks to a rich offering on the streaming side.” Despite reports that global audiences are moving away from Hollywood content , Pélisson remains cautious. “Buyers are certainly more risk-averse and negotiations may take longer, which leads some players towards proven, well-known IP,” he explains. “Nevertheless, the appetite for a strong non-English alternative is real, and France is very well positioned to answer.” ‘Grizzy & the Lemmings’ Courtesy of Studio Hari He adds: “All genres travel well — that’s the strength of the French offering. Animation remains our flagship in terms of sheer volume on foreign linear channels, carried by evergreen franchises like ‘Miraculous’ and ‘Grizzy & the Lemmings.’” The story is different on streaming, however, where fiction leads the way and, in value terms, drama has become France’s leading export genre over the last two years. Documentary, meanwhile, remains “a strong, steady genre, with real festival and platform presence.” Looking at emerging markets, Pélisson points out that “it is more about volume than value: buyers are very price-sensitive and increasingly digital-driven, so animation and formats do well there.” Overall, animation leads the way in global sales, “with ‘Miraculous’ enjoying by far the widest international footprint of any French title, alongside strong travelers like ‘Grizzy & the Lemmings’ and the ‘ Totally Spies! ’ revival.” ‘The Bureau’ Courtesy of Federation Entertainment On the fiction side, Pélisson notes that older titles are still doing well abroad: Federation ’s hit espionage thriller “The Bureau” has continued its remarkable international journey, while series like Studio TF1 ’s profiler crime drama “Profilage” (“The Paris Murders”) and Film & Pictures’ mystery miniseries “Un Soupçon” (“The Black Widow”) have found substantial audiences on major channels and platforms across Europe. ‘Miyazaki: The Spirit of Nature’ Courtesy of Les Bons Clients Among documentary shows that have reached strong global audiences on streaming are Balanga’s “Miyazaki: The Spirit of Nature,” about Oscar-winning animator and filmmaker Hayao Miyazaki, and Netflix ’s “Tour de France.” Despite an increasingly challenging environment, animation remains France’s top audiovisual export due to a number key factors, Pélisson says. “French animation rests on sound foundations: world-class studios, a training pipeline which is the envy of the sector, and a catalogue of IP with real brand equity. “This being said, we have been seeing sales decline for a year now, for two main reasons. First, streamers — and French broadcasters too — are ordering fewer new projects and fewer new IPs. Secondly, the major streamers take a global approach when producing.” Pélisson points to Netfix’s “Asterix & Obelix: The Big Fight” as an example. “When a global streamer produces the series, the entire international value is folded into a single production figure that counts as financing for a French production, not as an export sale. This is exactly why data matters so much — the only way to know what a program is really worth, on an international basis, would be to separate the value of its national exposure from its international one. Therefore, part of our real international success simply does not appear in the figures, both on the sales and audiences sides.” Animation producers are likewise finding ways to better navigate the tougher market. “Producers are leaning into exactly what makes the sector resilient — building franchises rather than one-off titles, accelerating co-productions to share risk, and designing for both linear and streaming distribution from the outset,” Pélisson explains. ‘Robin Hood: Mischief in Sherwood’ Courtesy of Mediawan Kids & Family Among the new and returning shows that are dazzling audiences abroad are Banijay Kids & Family’s “ Totally Spies!” revival, which “has found a genuinely global audience”; and, from Mediawan Kids & Family, “Robin Hood: Mischief in Sherwood,” which “keeps expanding its territory count”, and the “Miraculous” universe, which “continues to extend across formats.” “The winning formula, Pélisson adds, “is a strong brand that can live across many windows at once — which is precisely where the market is heading.” American Film Market Expands With Launch of AFM House, Site of Its Innovation Hub William H. articles.title: Luca Guadagnino’s ‘Artificial’ to World Premiere at New York Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 1, 2026 6:40am PT Luca Guadagnino’s ‘Artificial’ to World Premiere at New York Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) By Rebecca Rubin Plus Icon Rebecca Rubin Senior Film and Media Reporter rebeccaarubin Latest Luca Guadagnino’s ‘Artificial’ to World Premiere at New York Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) 6 minutes ago Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Triumphs Again in Fourth Weekend With $39 Million, ‘Insidious 6’ Launches to $25 Million 1 week ago ‘The Odyssey’ Beats ‘Deadpool & Wolverine’ as Biggest R-Rated Movie of All Time With $1.35 Billion 2 weeks ago See All New York Film Festival audiences will be the first to see “ Artificial ,” director Luca Guadagnino ‘s movie about OpenAI founder Sam Altman. The buzzy drama, which Neon acquired after Amazon MGM dropped the nearly competed film , will host its world premiere on Oct. 5 at Lincoln Center’s Alice Tully Hall. Guadagnino and the cast, including Andrew Garfield, Monica Barbaro, Yura Borisov, Ike Barinholtz, Cooper Hoffman, Jason Schwartzman and Chris O’Dowd, are expected to attend. Related Stories 'Beef' Creator Lee Sung Jin on Abandoning His Tom Brady Heist Plot and the Finneas, Cailee Spaeny Emmy Snubs YouTube Creator Kevin Langue Is Bringing His Comedy Channels to Netflix “Artificial” stars Garfield as Altman and centers around the tumultuous time when the boss was controversially fired and then rehired by the AI giant. Barbaro plays Open AI’s chief technology officer Mira Murati, Borisov is the OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever who ousts Altman, and Barinholtz portrays Elon Musk. Producers on the movie include David Heyman, Jeffrey Clifford, Guadagnino, Jennifer Fox and Simon Rich. Popular on Variety “Artificial” became one of the buzziest films of the season after Amazon MGM announced in June that the movie would be “better served if it were released by a different studio.” The company’s decision to jettison the project raised more than a few eyebrows around town because it came just a few months after Amazon signed a major partnership with OpenAI, including a $50 billion investment. Plus, Altman attended the wedding of Amazon chief Jeff Bezos in 2025. Multiple studios, including Mubi and Focus, circled “Artificial” before it landed at Neon. “The most remarkable thing about Luca Guadagnino’s sly and sobering new film is that it finds the perfect tone to tell the story of how we arrived at the AI precipice,” says NYFF artistic director Dennis Lim. Artificial traces this trajectory with clear-eyed horror, dark humor, and a sense of existential urgency. If ever there was a movie for its moment, this is it.” Guadagnino’s history with NYFF includes “Call Me by Your Name,” which was a main slate selection, “Bones and All” and “Queer,” which were spotlight selections, and “After the Hunt,” which opened last year’s festival. The 64th edition of New York Film Festival, which takes place from Sept. 25 through Oct. 12, will also feature James Gray’s crime drama “Paper Tiger,” starring Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller; Ava DuVernay’s documentary “14th”; director Tony Gilroy’s music drama “Behemoth!” with Pedro Pascal, Olivia Wilde and Will Arnett; and Takashi Yamazaki’s kaiju sequel “Godzilla Minus Zero.” Emmy Rossum Says Years-Long ‘Shameless’ Pay Battle Only Ended in Season 8 After Salary Dispute Leaked to the Public: ‘It Was Resolved Within a Day’ American Film Market Expands With Launch of AFM House, Site of Its Innovation Hub William H. articles.title: Gal Gadot Says ‘Wonder Woman 3’ Getting Axed and Henry Cavill’s Superman Exit Were ‘Not Handled Elegantly’ by the Studio but ‘We’re All Adults and It’s All Good’
articles.full_text: Sep 1, 2026 6:48am PT Gal Gadot Says ‘Wonder Woman 3’ Getting Axed and Henry Cavill’s Superman Exit Were ‘Not Handled Elegantly’ by the Studio but ‘We’re All Adults and It’s All Good’ By Zack Sharf Plus Icon Zack Sharf Digital News Director ZSharf Latest Gal Gadot Defends Starring in Movie With AI Sets and Lighting Because ‘You’re Going to Work With It or Be Out of the Game’; Lawyers Spent 6 Months Ensuring AI Would Not Alter Actors 16 hours ago Mel Gibson Apologizes for Mocking Sign Language Interpreter as Backlash Grows: ‘Thoughtless Idiocy’ With ‘No Intended Maliciousness’ 20 hours ago John Galliano Cancels Met Gala and Exhibit for 2027 Amid Backlash Over Past Racism: ‘I Remain Deeply Sorry’ to the ‘Jewish and Asian Communities’ 1 day ago See All ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection Gal Gadot insists DC Studios bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran told her they would develop “ Wonder Woman 3″ with her returning in the title role after they took over the company and rebooted Zack Snyder’s DC Universe. When asked on the latest “Happy Sad Confused” podcast if Gunn and Safran ever told her they would be going in a different direction, Gadot responded: “They told me the opposite! They told me, ‘We’re going to do develop it with you. The third [movie]…'” Related Stories ‘The Gentlemen’ Officially Renewed for Season 3 as First Season 2 Trailer Drops: ‘I’m Looking Forward to Pushing the Boundaries Further,’ Guy Ritchie Says (EXCLUSIVE) Netflix Hires Warner Bros. Exec Katie Martin Kelley as Communications VP Back in 2023, Gadot claimed in interviews with ComicBook.com and Flaunt magazine that Gunn and Safran were interested in developing “Wonder Woman 3.” She told the later publication that she even met with the new heads of DC Studios and “what they told me, and I’m quoting: ‘You’re in the best hands. We’re going to develop “Wonder Woman 3″ with you. [We] love you as Wonder Woman— you’ve got nothing to worry about.’” Sources close to the situation exclusively told Variety at the time that “Wonder Woman 3” was not in development at DC Studios and that nothing was ever promised to Gadot regarding another sequel, nor was there any definitive discussion of Gadot’s Wonder Woman continuing with the new DC Universe. Popular on Variety Gadot originated the role of Wonder Woman in Zack Snyder’s DC Universe, debuting in “Batman v Superman : Dawn of Justice” before leading her own two standalone films: “Wonder Woman” and “Wonder Woman 1984.” Gadot’s Wonder Woman also appeared in “Justice League” and had cameos in DC films such as “Shazam! Fury of the Gods.” Her two standalone “Wonder Woman” films were directed by Patty Jenkins. The two were developing “Wonder Woman 3” together before Gunn and Safran were named the new heads of DC Studios. During her interview on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast, Gadot said she ultimately was not surprised when she got the boot from Wonder Woman because “I saw the way everybody else was handled. The Henry [Cavill] situation was not handled elegantly to say the least. Same with Patty [Jenkins]. It was not handled elegantly. We’re all adults and it’s all good. It’s not even about [James Gunn and Peter Safran]. They are there and they’re there to do what they believe in. It’s all good.” Henry Cavill ‘s return as Superman was officially announced in October 2024 after he returned as the Man of Steel in the “Black Adam” post-credits scene. The announcement was only two months before Gunn and Safran’s DC takeover was officially confirmed, and the duo did not have plans to bring Cavill’s Superman back. Instead, they rebooted “Superman” with David Corenswet. Jenkins, meanwhile, had been developing a third “Wonder Woman” to star Gadot when news broke in December 2022 that their “Wonder Woman 3” had fallen apart after Warner Bros. leadership passed on Jenkins’ treatment for the sequel. Jenkins publicly exited the project. The news hit shortly after James Gunn and Peter Safran took the reins of DC Studios, which led to speculation that Jenkins had rebuffed efforts to reshape “Wonder Woman 3” to fit into their DC Universe. “I never walked away,” Jenkins shared in a post on Twitter at the time. “I was open to considering anything asked of me. It was my understanding there was nothing I could do to move anything forward at this time. DC is obviously buried in changes they are having to make, so I understand these decisions are difficult right now.” Jenkins confirmed on the “Talking Pictures” podcast soon after that her experience with “Wonder Woman” was over “for the time being, easily forever.” “They aren’t interested in doing any ‘Wonder Woman’ for the time being,” Jenkins said. “It’s not an easy task, with what’s going on with DC. James Gunn and Peter Safran have to follow their own heart into their own plans. I don’t know what they are planning on doing or why, so I have sympathy for what a big job it is and they have to follow their heart and do what they’ve got planned.” With her time as Wonder Woman over, Gadot said on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast that she’d likely not return to the role even if the chance arose to make “Wonder Woman 3” again at the new DC Studios. “For me to go to do another Wonder Woman, I am not sure I would at this point in my life with four children and different schools and all of that,” Gadot said. “To check out from all of them for such a long period of time, it doesn’t work for my life anymore at this point.” Watch Gadot’s full interview on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast in the video below. articles.title: ‘Down the Arm of God’ Review: Caleb Landry Jones Finds That God’s House Isn’t a Home in a Stirring Social Drama
articles.full_text: Sep 1, 2026 6:58am PT ‘Down the Arm of God’ Review: Caleb Landry Jones Finds That God’s House Isn’t a Home in a Stirring Social Drama The actor-writer reteams with his 'To the Night' director Peter Brunner for a moving if slightly schematic story of a Texas priest battling small-town prejudice to help the unhoused. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest ‘Sacred Creatures’ Review: Slippery Canadian-Italian Satire Follows the Cult and Collapse of a Questionable Guru 17 hours ago ‘Call My Agent! The Movie’ Review: Love-Hate Energy Keeps the Gang Together in a Fast, Funny Feature-Length Return 2 days ago ‘Sea of Glass’ Review: A Widow’s Coastal Healing Retreat Turns Into a Stately, Moody Greek Tragedy 2 days ago See All Courtesy of Kinology A harvester of disease in “Antiviral,” a white supremacist in “Get Out,” mass murderer Martin Bryant in “Nitram,” Vlad the Impaler himself in “Dracula”: Caleb Landry Jones has carved such a niche for himself playing men not to be touched with a ten-foot pole that “ Down the Arm of God ” immediately stands out for casting the actor as a man of regular, common decency. The takeaway, however, from this affectingly earnest social drama is that decency is neither common nor regular in an increasingly divided, individualist America — something that Jones’ character, small-town Texas priest Nick, learns to his growing anguish. Related Stories Emilia Jones to Star in Netflix Series Adaptation of 'The Retrievals' Podcast Christian Metal Band Demon Hunter Sues Netflix Over 'KPop Demon Hunters,' Citing Trademark Infringement Reteaming the star with Austrian director Peter Brunner , “Down the Arm of God” presents an unsurprisingly skeptical outsider’s view of the land of the free in the MAGA era — its foundational democratic values compromised by desperate economic inequality and bitter ongoing conflicts of race and class. With a diverse ensemble mixing name actors and non-professionals, the film’s first half recalls documentary-infused observational drama in the mold of early Chloé Zhao, as it follows Nick’s efforts to engage with a homeless community on the edge of his parish. Popular on Variety The second, segueing into violently heated, politicized melodrama, is less convincing. But the whole thing is kept on track by the worn, steadfast integrity of Jones’ performance: It’s clear that the film, which he co-wrote with Brunner following their work together on 2018’s tense psychodrama “To the Night,” is a passion project for him, to the extent that his own father John has a fleeting but crucial cameo. Following its world premiere in Locarno’s audience-oriented Piazza Grande section, this French-American co-production (Jones’ “Dracula” director Luc Besson is among the producers) should secure arthouse distribution (or a streaming deal) on both sides of the Atlantic. Breakout potential may be curbed by its stolid, downbeat nature. Shooting in a widescreen format that gives ironic grandeur to a squat, featureless town in the Texas Panhandle, DP Peter Flinckenberg is attentive to the piercing, sometimes radiant winter light of the region in the harshest months of the year. There’s a sparse, severe beauty to its unremarkably suburban vistas, with their freeze-dried lawns and stripped, skeletal trees, but mostly you feel the face-slapping cold through the screen. It’s certainly what Nick first notices as a newcomer to the area, having been rather thanklessly assigned there by the Church; his congregation, consisting mostly of superficially polite but insular white Christian conservatives, isn’t all that warm either. But he’s young and keen and persistent, winning over at least some converts with his amiably straight-talking sermon style and his passionate, community-minded charity drives. On the latter front, he concentrates much effort on a settlement of homeless people barely surviving on the town fringes; they’re wary of his interest at first, but eventually accept his help, with idealistic young Black woman Raven (India Marie Cross, a superb discovery) emerging as their uncompromising leader. But Nick learns the limits of his parishioners’ charity when, as the frostiest temperatures set in, he advocates temporarily sheltering them in the town gymnasium or, failing that, the church itself. Met with a wall of combined NIMBYism and racially coded prejudice from the townspeople — with ultra-Aryan couple Anna (Mena Suvari) and Chris (Nick Stahl) his most hostile opponents — Nick overrides their will and moves the homeless into the house of God anyway. Cue an increasingly fraught war of words — and, eventually and inevitably, other very American weapons — in the congregation, with even the good preacher tiring of turning the other cheek. To begin with, Brunner and Jones’ script brims with patient, generous human interest, abetted by the director’s sure touch with actors of all abilities: Early scenes find hitherto separate demographics sizing each other up and marking out common ground. As it progresses, however, issues and characters alike grow more polarized, in ways that make the film persuasive as polemic — and as an eminently worthy PSA, concluding with a series of title cards about America’s wider homelessness crisis — but slightly less interesting as drama. Beset with inner demons and scarring family tragedy, Nick is a consistently compelling protagonist, but wants for an antagonist of equivalent nuance and complexity: He’d already be on the side of the angels even if the likes of Anna and Chris weren’t such flatly hateful stereotypes. Still, this urgent, moving film is very much a work of its fractious era, when the time taken to see your opponent’s side might come at the expense of someone more worthy of grace. ‘Down the Arm of God’ Review: Caleb Landry Jones Finds That God’s House Isn’t a Home in a Stirring Social Drama Reviewed online, Aug. 31, 2026. articles.title: Hershey Hopes Katseye Will Lure Younger Snackers to New Crème Bars
articles.full_text: Sep 1, 2026 7:00am PT Hershey Hopes Katseye Will Lure Younger Snackers to New Crème Bars By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest NBC Sends Football on Cross-Country Trip to Count Down to NFL Kickoff 1 hour ago Sony Aims to Connect Advertisers to PlayStation Users With Launch of ‘Live TV on PS5’ (EXCLUSIVE) 22 hours ago Antonia Hylton’s New MS NOW Weekend Show ‘The Assignment’ Debuts September 12 24 hours ago See All Courtesy of Hershey's At The Hershey Company, the candy is the star, but marketing executives at the chocolate titan have figured out a way for the sweets to share screen time with some notable guests. Katseye , the popular all-girl pop group, will have a significant role in a new ad campaign aimed at introducing new Hershey’s Crème Bars to consumers — and their appearance suggests marketers long attached to themes of nostalgia are willing to break some longstanding rules in a bid to get noticed in a crowded marketplace. Related Stories 'Top Boy' Prequel 'Jonny Boy' Starring Barry Keoghan, Jaq Spinoff With Jasmine Jobson Ordered at Netflix What's New on Netflix in September 2026 Hershey’s doesn’t need to do a lot to stand apart. The wrappers for its signature chocolate bar and Reese’s chocolate-and-peanut-butter candy are cultural icons. And yet, the company may need something differ to catch the attention of younger customers, says Stacy Taffet, the company’s chief growth and marketing officer, during a recent interview. Popular on Variety “There’s a lot of trust and nostalgia and emotional connection” tied to Hershey products, Taffet says. “But as we think about a younger cohort, in particular, Gen Z, teens, twenty-somethings, they love Hershey, but they also want to experiment with new flavors, different textures, more indulgent premium experiences.” The new Crème Bars, which come in flavors such as affogato and salted caramel, are meant to stand as something more indulgent, and an alliance with Katseye was seen as a way to nudge a consumer who might not put Hershey in the realm of fancier treats. To emphasize the luxurious nature of the new candy, Katseye sings its song “Pinky Up” in what appears to be the car of a New York subway, with bites of the treat spurring riders to dance and move. The campaign will turn up in streaming video, digital, in national TV, in streaming audio, in social media and on murals in Brooklyn and Los Angeles. Hershey is one of several big candy and snack-makers trying to cultivate younger crowds with new flavors and textures. Ferrara Candy Co., for example, has driven sales by transforming its decades-old Nerds from what were once fruity candy pebbles into candies that have new textures that give consumers a different sort of “mouth feel.” “We are starting to push the boundaries on where our categories can go, thinking about our innovation process,” says Taffet “We are using different types of tools, including AI and social listening to get further ahead of where the consumer is going.” In recent months, Hershey’s has introduced new flavors to Reese’s, including one that pairs the candy with Oreo cookies. The executive says an effort is afoot to enter the lives of a young generation that indulges in what she calls “selective splurging.” Younger consumers “are really intentional in how they spend their dollars. And if they’re going to spend money on something, it’s going to be for an experience that they think is special relative to other things they could spend their money on,” says Taffet. If there’s an extra dollar to be spent, it’s “going to go to something that’s a little bit more special and bring something new that they haven’t experienced before. That bar is high, but I think it’s inspiring us” to try new methods. articles.title: Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen Launches Out of Pocket Studios
articles.full_text: Sep 1, 2026 7:00am PT Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen Launches Out of Pocket Studios By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest NBC Sends Football on Cross-Country Trip to Count Down to NFL Kickoff 1 hour ago Sony Aims to Connect Advertisers to PlayStation Users With Launch of ‘Live TV on PS5’ (EXCLUSIVE) 22 hours ago Antonia Hylton’s New MS NOW Weekend Show ‘The Assignment’ Debuts September 12 24 hours ago See All Courtesy of Buffalo Bills Josh Allen is joining the ranks of athletes getting into content production. The Buffalo Bills quarterback is launching Out of Pocket NFL MVP and star quarterback of the Buffalo Bills, has announced the launch of Out of Pocket Studios , a media venture that will have him backing entertainment, commercial and experiential projects. Allen will serve as CEO of the new company and as an executive producer on all work. Related Stories 'You' Author Caroline Kepnes Sets Series Directorial Debut With Psychological Thriller 'The Attentionist' (EXCLUSIVE) 'Top Boy' Prequel 'Jonny Boy' Starring Barry Keoghan, Jaq Spinoff With Jasmine Jobson Ordered at Netflix The new production outlet builds on an alliance Allen struck Skydance Sports , part of Paramount Skydance, in January of last year. Lindsey Cohen, president of strategy and operations at Out of Pocket Studios, will oversee the company’s day-to-day operations. She previously served at Meadowlark Media and DAZN, and began her career at CAA. “Skydance Sports has given me a platform to turn the ideas I care most about into something real,” said Allen, in a prepared statement. “We’re excited to share what Out of Pocket Studios has created so far, and for everyone to see what we’re building from here.” Popular on Variety The new studio’s initial slate includes “America’s Tailgate,” a TV special slated to air Labor Day on Paramount’s CBS. The program, which will feature music and celebrities, is produced with Skydance Sports, EverWonder Studio, and Lost Tribe Studio, and is hosted by “CBS Mornings” anchor and “The NFL Today” studio analyst Nate Burleson, along with co-host Melanie Collins and correspondent Whitney Cummings. Allen makes an appearance as well. Also set to launch is “NFL Play Action,” a weekly football-analysis studio show is slated to debut on Paramount+ on September 9. The show is hosted by by Kyle Brandt and co-hosted by fitness instructor Ally Love. The pair offer a weekly cultural recap of NFL action in a program meant to spur family viewing. “The Buffalo Miracle” is directed by documentarian Ben Proudfoot and produced with Breakwater Studios and Skydance Sports,. The film captures the heroism of a McDonald’s manager in Buffalo who, during a deadly blizzard in 2022, opened the restaurant to stranded citizens on Christmas Eve. Other projects, including a comedy series conceived by Allen that has already been sold, is in the company’s content pipeline. Both Allen and Out of Pocket Studios are represented by CAA. articles.title: ‘La Bola Negra’ Trailer: Netflix’s Oscar Contender Is a Time-Bending Queer Epic That Won Best Director at Cannes
articles.full_text: Sep 1, 2026 7:00am PT ‘La Bola Negra’ Trailer: Netflix’s Oscar Contender Is a Time-Bending Queer Epic That Won Best Director at Cannes By Mya Copeland Plus Icon Mya Copeland Latest Everything We Know About ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ 4 days ago Hooters Restaurant Movie in the Works — Film News in Brief 4 days ago ‘Final Fantasy VII Revelation’ Gameplay Trailer Shows Weapons Destroying Planet in the Series’ Finale (Gaming News Roundup) 5 days ago See All 'La Bola Negra' Carla Oset/Netflix Netflix released the official trailer for “ La Bola Negra ” (“The Black Ball”), from directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi. Set in 1932, 1937 and 2017, the Spanish-language queer epic explores the interconnected lives of three gay men. The film is inspired by an unfinished work of the same name by Spanish poet and playwright Federico García Lorca and Alberto Conejero’s play “La Piedra Oscura” (“The Dark Stone”). Conejero co-wrote the screenplay with Calvo and Ambrossi, known collectively as Los Javis. Related Stories 'Who Has Time to Watch All This Crap?': Inside 10 Anonymous Emmy Ballots as Voting Officially Closes Netflix Teen Thriller 'The Body’ Sets November Release Date, Drops First Look Photos (TV News Roundup) The cast features Spanish musician Guitarricadelafuente (Álvaro Lafuente Calvo) in his acting debut as Sebastián, Carlos González as Alberto, Miguel Bernardeau as Rafael Rodríguez Rapún, Milo Quifes as Carlos, Lola Dueñas as Teresa, Penélope Cruz as Nené Romero, Glenn Close as Isabelle Durand, Julio Torres as Juan Pablo and Alberto Cortés as Federico García Lorca. Popular on Variety The film made its world premiere at Cannes in May, where Calvo and Ambrossi won the Best Director Award. It features an original song, “La Nieve,” written and performed by Guitarricadelafuente, and a score from Raül Refree. “La Bola Negra” is slated for a theatrical release in Spain on Sept. 25. Netflix won the bidding war for U.S. distribution rights following the film’s Cannes premiere and set a theatrical window starting Oct. 16 before a streaming debut on Dec. 2. This marks the longest theatrical window for a Netflix film, breaking the record previously held by 2019’s “Marriage Story” starring Scarlett Johansson and Adam Driver. “La Bola Negra” is a Movistar Plus+ Original Film in collaboration with Suma Content Films. Telefónica Audiovisual Digital and Los Esquiadores AIE produced the film. El Deseo and Le Pacte co-produced, with the participation of Atresmedia and CREA SGR. Watch the trailer below. articles.title: Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit ‘Congo Boy’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 1, 2026 7:02am PT Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit ‘Congo Boy’ (EXCLUSIVE) The film, inspired by Fariala's own experience as a young refugee, unspools at Toronto and is set for a 2027 U.S. release By Ed Meza Plus Icon Ed Meza @edmezavar Latest Unifrance Rendez-Vous TV Mart Spotlights Ancient Rome, 19th Century Paris, Retired Spooks, Luchadores, Diplomatic Intrigue and Gaza 1 day ago Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Boards Palestinian Art and Resistance Documentary ‘Freedom Theatre’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago Patricio Valladares Descends Into Hell With Horror Adaptation of Dante’s ‘Inferno’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 week ago See All 'Congo Boy' Courtesy of The Party Film Sales/Outsider Pictures Santa Monica-based Outsider Pictures has picked up Rafiki Fariala ’s award-winning Cannes title “ Congo Boy ” for the U.S. ahead of its North American premiere at Toronto. Courtesy of Makongo Films/Unité/Kiripifilms/Karta Film/Canal+ The film bowed in Cannes’ Un Certain Regard, where it won Bradley Fiomona the best actor prize for his role as 17-year-old Robert, whose family was forced to flee the Democratic Republic of Congo for the neighboring Central African Republic. With his parents are imprisoned, Robert does what he can to care for his four younger siblings while attending high school, hoping to get into medical school and finding musical success despite all the odds stacked against him. Related Stories Netflix Hires Warner Bros. Exec Katie Martin Kelley as Communications VP Rafael Nadal Docuseries ‘Rafa’: How a Local Setting, Language and Intimate Lensing Set the Primetime Emmy Contender Apart Variety’s Murtada Elfadl praised the film as a “stirring musical drama” that “beats with the rhythms of resilience.” Popular on Variety “Congo Boy” is set to play a number of fall festivals in the U.S. ahead of a planned release in the spring of 2027. “I will be releasing the film in as many cities as I can since the film deals with the hardships of life but also our dreams, and right now everyone can relate to that and the film is ultimately an upbeat audience friendly film,” Outsider Pictures founder and CEO Paul Hudson told Variety . The film’s story very much parallels that of Fariala’s life. A Congolese refugee who came to the Central African Republic as a child, “Congo Boy” is his story told through fiction, according to the director. “It’s the story of the year my parents went to prison — the year I found myself alone with four younger siblings and forced to find a way to survive. The year music became my lifeline. Everything that happens in the film really happened to me.” In telling his story, Fariala hoped to encourage audiences “to see refugees differently” and to illustrate that “there is a light at the end of the tunnel,” the director previously told Variety . A four-country co-production, “Congo Boy” is produced by Makongo Films, based in the Central African capital of Bangui, Unité in France, the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Kiripifilms and Karta Film in Italy. Paris-based The Party Film Sales is handling “Congo Boy” internationally. The film has sold across Europe and beyond, including such major territories as Germany and Austria, where it will be released by Immergute Filme, France via Jour2fête, and Brazil, where Ipecine is distributing. “Congo Boy” follows Fariala’s award-winning 2022 debut feature, “We, Students!” which bowed in Berlin. The documentary captures the everyday life of the director and his fellow students at the Central African Republic’s Bangui University.
